text: Weakly Supervised Object Localization (WSOL) aims to identify object regions in images using only image-level labels, which remains a challenging task due to the lack of precise localization information. This paper introduces a novel Dual-attention Guided Dropblock Module (DADM) to enhance the localization accuracy of WSOL models. The proposed approach integrates two key components: a channel-wise attention mechanism to emphasize discriminative features and a spatial attention mechanism to focus on salient object regions. Additionally, the Dropblock module is employed to prevent overfitting by randomly dropping contiguous regions during training, thereby improving the model's generalization capability. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, such as CUB-200-2011 and ILSVRC, demonstrate that DADM achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of localization accuracy and robustness. The results highlight the effectiveness of the dual-attention mechanism in guiding the model to focus on relevant object regions while mitigating background noise. This work contributes to advancing WSOL by providing a more reliable and interpretable framework for object localization, with potential applications in medical imaging, autonomous driving, and video surveillance. **Keywords**: Weakly Supervised Object Localization, Dual-attention Mechanism, Dropblock, Image Classification, Deep Learning.

Image harmonization aims to modify the color of the composited region with respect to the specific background. Previous works model this task as a pixel-wise image-to-image translation using UNet family structures. However, the model size and computational cost limit the performability of their models on edge devices and higher-resolution images. To this end, we propose a novel spatial-separated curve rendering network (S^2CRNet) for efficient and high-resolution image harmonization for the first time. In S^2CRNet, we firstly extract the spatial-separated embeddings from the thumbnails of the masked foreground and background individually. Then, we design a curve rendering module (CRM), which learns and combines the spatial-specific knowledge using linear layers to generate the parameters of the pixel-wise curve mapping in the foreground region. Finally, we directly render the original high-resolution images using the learned color curve. Besides, we also make two extensions of the proposed framework via the Cascaded-CRM and Semantic-CRM for cascaded refinement and semantic guidance, respectively. Experiments show that the proposed method reduces more than 90% parameters compared with previous methods but still achieves the state-of-the-art performance on both synthesized iHarmony4 and real-world DIH test set. Moreover, our method can work smoothly on higher resolution images in real-time which is more than 10\times faster than the existing methods. The code and pre-trained models will be made available and released at https://github.com/stefanLeong/S2CRNet.

Biện pháp đàm thoại đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc phát triển ngôn ngữ đối thoại cho trẻ từ 5 đến 6 tuổi thông qua các hoạt động học tập và vui chơi. Để kích thích khả năng giao tiếp, giáo viên và phụ huynh cần tạo môi trường tương tác tích cực, khuyến khích trẻ bày tỏ suy nghĩ, cảm xúc và đặt câu hỏi. Các hoạt động như kể chuyện, đóng kịch, thảo luận nhóm giúp trẻ rèn luyện kỹ năng nghe, nói và phản hồi. Việc sử dụng ngôn ngữ đơn giản, gần gũi cùng với sự kiên nhẫn lắng nghe sẽ tạo điều kiện để trẻ tự tin hơn trong giao tiếp. Bên cạnh đó, việc khen ngợi và động viên kịp thời cũng góp phần thúc đẩy sự phát triển ngôn ngữ một cách toàn diện.

This paper addresses the challenging problem of dense 3D object reconstruction from a single depth view, a crucial task in robotics, augmented reality, and computer vision. We propose a novel approach combining deep learning with geometric priors to infer complete 3D shapes from sparse and noisy depth data. Our method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict a dense volumetric representation of the object, guided by a shape completion network trained on a large dataset of 3D models. A key innovation is the integration of a surface normal consistency loss, encouraging geometrically plausible reconstructions even in areas with limited depth information. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy and completeness, particularly for objects with complex geometries and significant occlusions. The generated 3D models exhibit finer details and improved structural integrity. This work contributes a robust and efficient solution for single-view 3D reconstruction, enabling wider applications in real-world scenarios. **Keywords:** 3D reconstruction, depth completion, single-view reconstruction, deep learning, shape completion, computer vision.

**Abstract** This paper addresses the challenge of extracting meaningful patterns from heterogeneous multivariate time-series data with a focus on advancing home health telecare applications. The objective of the research is to develop an effective data mining framework capable of handling disparate sensor sources, variable sampling rates, and complex temporal relationships inherent in telecare environments. The proposed methodology integrates advanced preprocessing techniques for data synchronization and normalization, followed by the application of a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with attention mechanisms to model long-term dependencies and highlight critical health-related events. Experimental evaluation was performed using real-world telecare datasets collected from multiple health sensors deployed in smart home settings. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves the accuracy in detecting anomalies and recognizing patterns associated with patient well-being compared to traditional single-modality or univariate analysis techniques. The study's findings highlight the potential of multivariate time-series mining to enhance remote health monitoring, support early intervention, and personalize care for elderly and chronically ill individuals. Overall, this research contributes a robust and scalable solution for learning meaningful patterns from complex health data streams, paving the way for more intelligent and responsive home health telecare systems. **Keywords:** multivariate time-series, pattern mining, home health telecare, anomaly detection, deep learning, sensor data fusion, remote monitoring

This paper addresses the challenge of multi-label few-zero-shot learning, where a model must recognize multiple labels with limited or no training data. Our objective is to develop a novel approach that aggregates knowledge from multiple label graphs to improve the performance of few-zero-shot learning. We propose a method that constructs multiple label graphs, each representing a different relationship between labels, and then aggregates the knowledge from these graphs using a graph attention mechanism. Our approach enables the model to capture complex label relationships and adapt to new, unseen labels with minimal training data. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing few-zero-shot learning approaches, achieving significant improvements in label recognition accuracy. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a multi-label graph attention mechanism and the demonstration of its effectiveness in few-zero-shot learning scenarios. Our work has important implications for applications such as image and text classification, where multi-label recognition is crucial. Key keywords: few-zero-shot learning, multi-label classification, graph attention, label graphs, knowledge aggregation.

We present the Cosmology and Astrophysics with MachinE Learning Simulations (CAMELS) Multifield Dataset, CMD, a collection of hundreds of thousands of 2D maps and 3D grids containing many different properties of cosmic gas, dark matter, and stars from 2,000 distinct simulated universes at several cosmic times. The 2D maps and 3D grids represent cosmic regions that span \sim100 million light years and have been generated from thousands of state-of-the-art hydrodynamic and gravity-only N-body simulations from the CAMELS project. Designed to train machine learning models, CMD is the largest dataset of its kind containing more than 70 Terabytes of data. In this paper we describe CMD in detail and outline a few of its applications. We focus our attention on one such task, parameter inference, formulating the problems we face as a challenge to the community. We release all data and provide further technical details at https://camels-multifield-dataset.readthedocs.io.

This paper addresses the challenge of network clustering, with a specific focus on brain-network analysis, by introducing a novel approach based on Kernel-ARMA modeling and the Grassmannian framework. The objective is to develop a robust and scalable method for identifying meaningful clusters in complex network structures, particularly in the context of brain connectivity data. Traditional clustering techniques often struggle with high-dimensional and nonlinear network data, prompting the need for advanced methodologies. Our approach leverages Kernel-ARMA modeling to capture temporal dependencies and nonlinear relationships within network data, while the Grassmannian framework provides a geometric perspective for representing and comparing subspaces of network features. Together, these components enable efficient and interpretable clustering of brain networks. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world brain-network datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over existing techniques, achieving higher accuracy and computational efficiency. The findings highlight the potential of this approach for applications in neuroscience, such as identifying biomarkers for neurological disorders and understanding functional brain connectivity. This work contributes to the field by offering a mathematically grounded and scalable solution for network clustering, with broader implications for analyzing complex networks in other domains. **Keywords**: Network clustering, Kernel-ARMA modeling, Grassmannian, Brain networks, Nonlinear data analysis, High-dimensional data.

Monocular depth estimation is a challenging problem in computer vision due to the inherent scale ambiguity. This paper introduces LiDARTouch, a novel approach that leverages sparse LiDAR point clouds to guide monocular depth prediction. Our method uses a few-beam LiDAR sensor, significantly reducing the cost and power consumption compared to dense LiDAR systems, while still providing sufficient geometric constraints for accurate depth estimation. We propose a deep learning architecture that effectively fuses monocular image features with sparse LiDAR data through a cross-modal attention mechanism. This allows the network to learn the correlation between image cues and LiDAR measurements, enabling robust depth completion and scale recovery. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that LiDARTouch achieves state-of-the-art performance in monocular metric depth estimation with substantially fewer LiDAR beams. The proposed method shows significant promise for applications requiring accurate and cost-effective depth sensing, such as autonomous driving and robotics. Keywords: Depth Estimation, Monocular Vision, LiDAR, Sensor Fusion, Deep Learning.

Pedestrian detection is crucial for various applications, including autonomous driving and video surveillance. This paper introduces a novel scene-specific pedestrian detection framework leveraging parallel vision to enhance accuracy and robustness in complex environments. Our approach employs a dual-camera system mimicking human binocular vision to capture complementary scene information. We propose a parallel processing pipeline that integrates both RGB images and disparity maps for enhanced feature extraction. A scene-specific adaptive learning module is developed to fine-tune a Faster R-CNN model using data tailored to the target environment, mitigating the domain adaptation problem often encountered in real-world deployments. Experimental results on challenging pedestrian datasets demonstrate significant improvements in detection accuracy compared to state-of-the-art generic detectors and existing domain adaptation techniques. Specifically, we achieve a 15% increase in average precision in densely crowded scenes. This research offers a practical and efficient solution for robust pedestrian detection in scene-specific scenarios, paving the way for improved performance in real-world intelligent transportation systems. Keywords: Pedestrian Detection, Parallel Vision, Scene-Specific Learning, Domain Adaptation, Autonomous Driving.

MotivationThe motivation behind implementing a time filtering mechanism for individ ual providers is to enhance the overall experience for these providers. By allowingthem to specify their available time slots accurately, the application aims to prevent scheduling conflicts and optimize the appointment booking process. This fea ture is designed to ensure that customers can only choose appointments within the provider’s designated working hours, leading to better scheduling and increased customer satisfaction.

Trầm cảm ở sinh viên y khoa là một trong những vấn đề đáng lưu tâm, tuy nhiên chưa có nhiều nghiên cứu đánh giá tình trạng này ở Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu này nhằm xác định tỉ lệ có dấu hiệu trầm cảm ở sinh viên y đa khoa chính quy và các yếu tố liên quan. Nghiên cứu cắt ngang được thực hiện trên 358 sinh viên y đa khoa chính quy từ Y1 đến Y6 được chọn ngẫu nhiên tại Trường Đại học Y khoa Phạm Ngọc Thạch. Sử dụng thang đo CESD-20 (được chuẩn hóa tại Việt Nam với hệ số tin cậy Cronbach’s Alpha là 0,87) với mốc điểm CESD-20 22 là có dấu hiệu trầm cảm, và bộ câu hỏi về các yếu tố liên quan. Mô hình hồi quy logistic được sử dụng nhằm xác định mối liên hệ giữa các yếu tố với dấu hiệu trầm cảm. Kết quả: Sinh viên y đa khoa chính quy có dấu hiệu trầm cảm chiếm 49,2%. Các yếu tố có liên quan đến dấu hiệu trầm cảm trong mô hình hồi quy đa biến gồm: giới tính, kết thúc tình bạn, bất đồng hoặc gặp rắc rối với ba mẹ, thay đổi thói quen ăn uống, bỏ bữa ăn, học lực, áp lực từ việc học của bản thân, mục tiêu học tập. Số liệu cho thấy phần lớn sinh viên y đa khoa chính quy gặp nhiều vấn đề liên quan đến trầm cảm trong suốt thời gian học tập. Cần có sự quan tâm đúng mức đến sức khỏe tâm thần ở sinh viên, với những biện pháp hỗ trợ từ gia đình và nhà trường.

The accurate prediction of future Humphrey Visual Fields (HVF) is critical for early detection and management of progressive eye diseases such as glaucoma. This study proposes a novel deep learning-based approach to forecast future HVF measurements, leveraging historical patient data to predict visual field progression. A convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture is designed to capture spatial and temporal patterns in HVF data, integrating longitudinal measurements to enhance prediction accuracy. The model is trained and validated on a large dataset of HVF records, achieving superior performance compared to traditional statistical methods and existing machine learning models. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces prediction error and provides reliable estimates of future visual field loss. This work contributes to the field by introducing a robust, data-driven tool for early intervention in glaucoma management, with potential applications in clinical decision-making and personalized treatment planning. Keywords: Humphrey Visual Fields, deep learning, glaucoma, visual field prediction, convolutional neural networks.

Hình ảnh học cắt lớp vi tính (CT) đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc đánh giá và dự đoán nguy cơ xuất huyết phổi, một tai biến nghiêm trọng có thể xảy ra sau các thủ thuật y khoa. Các đặc điểm hình ảnh như kích thước, vị trí và mật độ của tổn thương phổi được phân tích kỹ lưỡng để xác định mối liên quan với nguy cơ xuất huyết. Nghiên cứu chỉ ra rằng những bệnh nhân có tổn thương phổi lớn, nằm gần mạch máu chính hoặc có mật độ không đồng nhất thường có nguy cơ cao hơn. Việc sử dụng CT giúp các bác sĩ can thiệp kịp thời, giảm thiểu biến chứng và cải thiện kết quả điều trị. Đây là công cụ hữu ích trong việc tối ưu hóa quy trình chăm sóc bệnh nhân, đặc biệt trong các trường hợp phức tạp.

State of the art machine learning algorithms are highly optimized to provide the optimal prediction possible, naturally resulting in complex models. While these models often outperform simpler more interpretable models by order of magnitudes, in terms of understanding the way the model functions, we are often facing a "black box". In this paper we suggest a simple method to interpret the behavior of any predictive model, both for regression and classification. Given a particular model, the information required to interpret it can be obtained by studying the partial derivatives of the model with respect to the input. We exemplify this insight by interpreting convolutional and multi-layer neural networks in the field of natural language processing.

Objective: Designing optimal deep neural network (DNN) architectures remains a time-consuming task that relies heavily on expert intuition. This paper proposes an automated approach to structure learning of DNNs by framing architecture search as a sequential decision process and applying Q-Learning to select and assemble network layers. Methods: We model each candidate network as a state in a Markov decision process and actions correspond to adding, modifying, or terminating layer configurations. A Q-Learning agent iteratively explores the space of possible architectures, using experience replay and ε-greedy exploration to balance discovery and exploitation. A reward function based on validation accuracy and model complexity guides the agent toward compact, high-performing designs. Results: Experiments on image classification benchmarks (CIFAR-10, MNIST) and a text classification task demonstrate that our Q-Learning–driven search consistently identifies architectures that match or exceed the accuracy of manually designed models while reducing parameter count by up to 30%. Compared with random search and genetic algorithms, our method converges 40% faster and yields more stable performance across repeated runs. Conclusion: By leveraging reinforcement learning for structure learning, we offer a scalable, generalizable framework that automates DNN design without extensive human intervention. This approach accelerates model development and can be extended to diverse domains, including speech recognition and time-series forecasting. Keywords: deep neural network, Q-Learning, architecture search, reinforcement learning, model optimization.

Gà nhiều ngón, một giống gà đặc biệt, đang được nuôi tại rừng quốc gia Xuân Sơn, Huế, nổi bật với những đặc điểm ngoại hình độc đáo và khả năng sản xuất ấn tượng. Giống gà này có bộ lông dày, màu sắc phong phú và đặc biệt là số lượng ngón chân nhiều hơn so với các giống gà thông thường, điều này không chỉ tạo nên sự khác biệt mà còn ảnh hưởng đến khả năng di chuyển và tìm kiếm thức ăn trong môi trường tự nhiên. Khả năng sinh sản của gà nhiều ngón cũng rất đáng chú ý, với tỷ lệ đẻ trứng cao và chất lượng trứng tốt, góp phần vào nguồn thực phẩm phong phú cho người dân địa phương. Việc nuôi dưỡng giống gà này không chỉ giúp bảo tồn nguồn gen quý mà còn tạo ra nguồn thu nhập ổn định cho các hộ gia đình trong khu vực, đồng thời thúc đẩy phát triển kinh tế bền vững tại rừng quốc gia.

Bệnh Kawasaki là một bệnh viêm mạch máu cấp tính thường gặp ở trẻ em, đặc biệt là trẻ dưới 5 tuổi. Bệnh được chia thành hai thể chính: thể điển hình và thể không điển hình. Thể điển hình có các triệu chứng rõ ràng như sốt cao kéo dài, phát ban, viêm kết mạc, sưng hạch bạch huyết, thay đổi ở miệng và lưỡi, cũng như sưng đỏ ở bàn tay và bàn chân. Trong khi đó, thể không điển hình thường có các triệu chứng không đầy đủ hoặc không rõ ràng, gây khó khăn trong chẩn đoán. Tại Bệnh viện Nhi Đồng 2, các nghiên cứu so sánh đặc điểm lâm sàng và cận lâm sàng giữa hai thể này cho thấy sự khác biệt đáng kể về mức độ nghiêm trọng và cách điều trị. Việc nhận biết sớm và chẩn đoán chính xác là yếu tố quan trọng giúp giảm thiểu nguy cơ biến chứng tim mạch, đặc biệt là viêm động mạch vành.

Graphene xoắn là một loại vật liệu mới được tạo ra bằng cách xoắn các lớp graphene lại với nhau. Điều này tạo ra một cấu trúc đặc biệt có thể được sử dụng trong các ứng dụng điện tử và quang học. Trong lĩnh vực đi-ốt siêu dẫn, graphene xoắn đã được chứng minh là có thể tăng cường hiệu suất và giảm thiểu tổn thất điện năng. Các nhà nghiên cứu đã sử dụng graphene xoắn để tạo ra các đi-ốt siêu dẫn mới có khả năng chuyển đổi điện năng thành ánh sáng với hiệu suất cao hơn. Điều này có thể dẫn đến sự phát triển của các thiết bị điện tử và quang học mới có khả năng hoạt động hiệu quả hơn và tiết kiệm năng lượng hơn. Sự phát triển của đi-ốt siêu dẫn dựa trên graphene xoắn cũng có thể mở ra các khả năng mới trong lĩnh vực công nghệ thông tin và truyền thông. Các đi-ốt siêu dẫn này có thể được sử dụng để tạo ra các thiết bị truyền thông nhanh chóng và an toàn hơn, giúp tăng cường khả năng kết nối và trao đổi thông tin trên toàn cầu. Tóm lại, graphene xoắn và đi-ốt siêu dẫn đang trở thành một trong những lĩnh vực nghiên cứu và phát triển mới mẻ và đầy hứa hẹn trong lĩnh vực vật liệu và công nghệ.

Nghiên cứu mới đây tập trung vào ảnh hưởng của Dao động nội mùa Biển Đông (BSISO) đến lượng mưa cực trị ở Việt Nam, một yếu tố quan trọng trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu. BSISO, một hiện tượng thời tiết đặc trưng của khu vực Biển Đông, có khả năng tác động đáng kể đến sự phân bố và cường độ mưa, đặc biệt là các sự kiện mưa lớn gây ra lũ lụt và thiên tai. Phân tích sâu về mối liên hệ giữa BSISO và mưa cực trị giúp cải thiện khả năng dự báo thời tiết, hỗ trợ công tác phòng chống thiên tai và quản lý nguồn nước hiệu quả hơn. Nghiên cứu này đóng góp vào sự hiểu biết toàn diện về các yếu tố khí hậu ảnh hưởng đến Việt Nam, từ đó đưa ra các giải pháp thích ứng và giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực của biến đổi khí hậu. Kết quả nghiên cứu có ý nghĩa quan trọng trong việc xây dựng các chiến lược phát triển bền vững và bảo vệ cộng đồng trước các rủi ro liên quan đến thời tiết cực đoan.

Airline crew pairing optimization is a critical and highly complex task in airline operations, involving the selection of feasible and cost-effective crew schedules that comply with regulatory, operational, and contractual constraints. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the scale and combinatorial nature of real-world instances, leading to suboptimal solutions or prohibitive computation times. This paper presents a novel machine learning-based approach to augment large-scale airline crew pairing optimization by learning combinatorial patterns from historical data. Our method leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture intricate relationships among flight legs and crew assignments, enabling the identification of promising substructures and variable reductions prior to optimization. We integrate the learned patterns into a branch-and-price framework, significantly reducing the solution space and improving computational efficiency. Experimental evaluations on industry-scale datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves up to 35% faster convergence and produces pairings with lower operational costs compared to state-of-the-art optimization techniques. The proposed framework showcases significant potential in real-world airline scheduling, offering robust scalability and adaptability to evolving operational requirements. Keywords: airline crew pairing, combinatorial optimization, machine learning, graph neural networks, branch-and-price, operational research.

Child trafficking is a severe global issue, and identifying locations where children are most vulnerable is critical for effective intervention. This paper introduces a novel machine learning pipeline designed to aid in the identification of schools from images potentially related to child trafficking. The pipeline integrates techniques from computer vision and machine learning to detect and analyze school-related features within images. We employ a pre-trained object detection model fine-tuned on a dataset of school buildings, playground equipment, and related objects. Detected objects are then fed into a classification model to predict the likelihood of an image containing a school environment. The performance of the pipeline was evaluated on a held-out dataset, demonstrating a significant improvement in accuracy compared to baseline methods. The proposed system offers a valuable tool for law enforcement and non-governmental organizations to prioritize investigations and allocate resources effectively, contributing to the fight against child trafficking. Keywords: Child Trafficking, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Object Detection, School Identification, Image Analysis.

In this study, we introduce a low cost method for generating descriptions from images containing novel objects. Generally, constructing a model, which can explain images with novel objects, is costly because of the following: (1) collecting a large amount of data for each category, and (2) retraining the entire system. If humans see a small number of novel objects, they are able to estimate their properties by associating their appearance with known objects. Accordingly, we propose a method that can explain images with novel objects without retraining using the word embeddings of the objects estimated from only a small number of image features of the objects. The method can be integrated with general image-captioning models. The experimental results show the effectiveness of our approach.

Generating images from scene graphs is a challenging task that attracted substantial interest recently. Prior works have approached this task by generating an intermediate layout description of the target image. However, the representation of each object in the layout was generated independently, which resulted in high overlap, low coverage, and an overall blurry layout. We propose a novel method that alleviates these issues by generating the entire layout description gradually to improve inter-object dependency. We empirically show on the COCO-STUFF dataset that our approach improves the quality of both the intermediate layout and the final image. Our approach improves the layout coverage by almost 20 points and drops object overlap to negligible amounts.

Autonomous learning of robotic skills can allow general-purpose robots to learn wide behavioral repertoires without requiring extensive manual engineering. However, robotic skill learning methods typically make one of several trade-offs to enable practical real-world learning, such as requiring manually designed policy or value function representations, initialization from human-provided demonstrations, instrumentation of the training environment, or extremely long training times. In this paper, we propose a new reinforcement learning algorithm for learning manipulation skills that can train general-purpose neural network policies with minimal human engineering, while still allowing for fast, efficient learning in stochastic environments. Our approach builds on the guided policy search (GPS) algorithm, which transforms the reinforcement learning problem into supervised learning from a computational teacher (without human demonstrations). In contrast to prior GPS methods, which require a consistent set of initial states to which the system must be reset after each episode, our approach can handle randomized initial states, allowing it to be used in environments where deterministic resets are impossible. We compare our method to existing policy search techniques in simulation, showing that it can train high-dimensional neural network policies with the same sample efficiency as prior GPS methods, and present real-world results on a PR2 robotic manipulator.

Accurate medical image segmentation is crucial for computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. This paper introduces an iterative deep convolutional encoder-decoder network designed to improve the precision and efficiency of medical image segmentation. The proposed network incorporates a novel iterative refinement module within a U-Net architecture, allowing for progressive error correction and feature enhancement. Specifically, the encoder extracts hierarchical features, while the decoder reconstructs the segmentation map through iterative feedback loops. Skip connections facilitate the transfer of fine-grained details from encoder to decoder, mitigating information loss. The iterative refinement module refines the segmentation output in each stage by attending to previously misclassified regions, leading to improved boundary delineation and reduced false positives. We evaluated our method on benchmark datasets of brain tumor and cardiac MRI images, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art segmentation techniques in terms of Dice score, Jaccard index, and Hausdorff distance. The iterative refinement strategy significantly enhances segmentation accuracy, particularly in challenging regions with ambiguous boundaries. This work provides a promising approach for medical image segmentation with potential applications in clinical decision support systems. **Keywords:** Medical Image Segmentation, Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, Encoder-Decoder, Iterative Refinement, U-Net.

Natural image matting is a fundamental challenge in computer vision, aiming to accurately extract foreground objects from images with complex backgrounds. This paper presents a deep learning-based approach for automatic natural image matting, addressing the limitations of traditional methods that often require user interaction or fail to generalize across diverse scenes. Our proposed framework leverages a novel encoder-decoder architecture with multi-scale feature fusion, enabling precise alpha matte estimation without manual guidance. The model is trained on a large-scale dataset with diverse foreground-background compositions, ensuring robustness across various real-world scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, achieving superior performance on benchmark datasets. The proposed approach also exhibits strong generalization capabilities, making it suitable for applications in image editing, video production, and augmented reality. This work contributes to advancing automatic image matting by introducing a scalable and efficient solution that eliminates the need for user intervention while maintaining high-quality results. **Keywords**: natural image matting, deep learning, encoder-decoder architecture, alpha matte estimation, computer vision, image editing.

Hybrid modeling, the combination of first principle and machine learning models, is an emerging research field that gathers more and more attention. Even if hybrid models produce formidable results for academic examples, there are still different technical challenges that hinder the use of hybrid modeling in real-world applications. By presenting NeuralFMUs, the fusion of a FMU, a numerical ODE solver and an ANN, we are paving the way for the use of a variety of first principle models from different modeling tools as parts of hybrid models. This contribution handles the hybrid modeling of a complex, real-world example: Starting with a simplified 1D-fluid model of the human cardiovascular system (arterial side), the aim is to learn neglected physical effects like arterial elasticity from data. We will show that the hybrid modeling process is more comfortable, needs less system knowledge and is therefore less error-prone compared to modeling solely based on first principle. Further, the resulting hybrid model has improved in computation performance, compared to a pure first principle white-box model, while still fulfilling the requirements regarding accuracy of the considered hemodynamic quantities. The use of the presented techniques is explained in a general manner and the considered use-case can serve as example for other modeling and simulation applications in and beyond the medical domain.

Traditional neural networks assume vectorial inputs as the network is arranged as layers of single line of computing units called neurons. This special structure requires the non-vectorial inputs such as matrices to be converted into vectors. This process can be problematic. Firstly, the spatial information among elements of the data may be lost during vectorisation. Secondly, the solution space becomes very large which demands very special treatments to the network parameters and high computational cost. To address these issues, we propose matrix neural networks (MatNet), which takes matrices directly as inputs. Each neuron senses summarised information through bilinear mapping from lower layer units in exactly the same way as the classic feed forward neural networks. Under this structure, back prorogation and gradient descent combination can be utilised to obtain network parameters efficiently. Furthermore, it can be conveniently extended for multimodal inputs. We apply MatNet to MNIST handwritten digits classification and image super resolution tasks to show its effectiveness. Without too much tweaking MatNet achieves comparable performance as the state-of-the-art methods in both tasks with considerably reduced complexity.

This paper introduces Regression Prior Networks (RPNs), a novel approach designed to enhance the robustness and interpretability of regression tasks in machine learning. The primary objective of this research is to address the limitations of traditional regression models, particularly in handling uncertainty estimation and out-of-distribution data. RPNs leverage probabilistic deep learning techniques to model prior distributions over regression parameters, enabling more accurate uncertainty quantification and improved generalization. The proposed method integrates a Bayesian framework with neural networks, allowing for flexible and scalable regression modeling. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that RPNs outperform conventional regression models in terms of predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration. Additionally, the framework provides interpretable insights into the underlying data distribution, making it suitable for applications in domains such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems. The key contribution of this work lies in its ability to combine the strengths of Bayesian inference and deep learning, offering a robust and interpretable solution for regression tasks. This research opens new avenues for developing reliable machine learning models in scenarios where uncertainty estimation and interpretability are critical. **Keywords**: Regression Prior Networks, uncertainty estimation, Bayesian deep learning, probabilistic modeling, interpretability, out-of-distribution detection.

This paper proposes a novel approach to explaining complex machine learning models for tabular data, inspired by the concept of attention mechanisms. The objective is to provide insights into how different features contribute to the predictions made by these models. Our method, dubbed "Attention-like Feature Explanation" (AFE), leverages a technique that assigns feature importance scores, similar to attention weights, to quantify the contribution of each feature to the model's output. We employ a combination of feature permutation and sensitivity analysis to generate these scores. The results show that AFE outperforms existing feature explanation methods in terms of accuracy and consistency, particularly for models trained on high-dimensional tabular data. Our approach has significant implications for model interpretability, transparency, and trustworthiness, enabling practitioners to better understand and refine their models. Key contributions include the introduction of attention-like mechanisms to tabular data explanation, improved feature importance estimation, and enhanced model interpretability. Relevant keywords: explainable AI, feature importance, attention mechanisms, tabular data, model interpretability.

Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) for 3D object detection aims to transfer knowledge from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain. Existing methods often suffer from noisy pseudo-labels generated on the target domain, hindering performance. This paper introduces ST3D++, a novel denoised self-training framework to address this issue. ST3D++ builds upon a self-training paradigm, incorporating a dynamic pseudo-label filtering mechanism based on both prediction confidence and feature consistency to reduce noise. Furthermore, we introduce a contextual regularization technique that leverages the relationships between objects to refine predictions, especially for challenging cases. We evaluate ST3D++ on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over state-of-the-art UDA methods for 3D object detection. Specifically, ST3D++ achieves superior performance in adapting across different LiDAR sensor configurations and environmental conditions. The results highlight the effectiveness of our denoised self-training approach in mitigating the impact of noisy labels and improving adaptation accuracy. Keywords: 3D Object Detection, Unsupervised Domain Adaptation, Self-training, Denoising, LiDAR, Point Cloud.

The increasing complexity of time series data in cloud computing environments necessitates efficient and scalable prediction algorithms to support real-time decision-making. This paper presents a novel periodicity-based parallel time series prediction algorithm designed to address the challenges of handling large-scale, high-frequency data streams in distributed systems. The proposed approach leverages periodicity detection techniques to identify recurring patterns in time series data, enabling more accurate and efficient predictions. By integrating parallel processing frameworks, the algorithm optimizes computational resources and reduces prediction latency, making it suitable for cloud-based applications. Experimental evaluations conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate that the algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of prediction accuracy and scalability. The results highlight its ability to handle dynamic workloads and adapt to varying data characteristics, making it a robust solution for time series forecasting in cloud environments. This research contributes to the advancement of scalable data analytics by providing a practical and innovative approach to time series prediction, with potential applications in areas such as resource allocation, anomaly detection, and predictive maintenance. **Keywords**: time series prediction, periodicity detection, parallel processing, cloud computing, scalability, distributed systems.

Object detection models typically require large annotated datasets and struggle to adapt to new object categories with limited data, posing significant challenges in dynamic real-world environments. This paper addresses these limitations by introducing a novel Incremental Few-Shot Object Detection framework, designed to efficiently learn new object classes from minimal labeled examples without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. Our approach integrates incremental learning techniques with few-shot learning paradigms to enable seamless and scalable model updates. The proposed method employs a meta-learning backbone for rapid feature adaptation, combined with a memory-based consolidation module to minimize catastrophic forgetting during the introduction of new categories. Extensive experiments on benchmark object detection datasets demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing methods in both detection accuracy and stability across incremental learning sessions. Furthermore, comparative analysis highlights the model’s ability to maintain high performance on previously learned classes while achieving robust detection on novel, low-sample categories. The results suggest significant advancements in practical applications such as robotics, surveillance, and autonomous systems where continuous learning from limited data is required. Keywords: few-shot learning, incremental learning, object detection, meta-learning, continual learning, computer vision.

Preserving the privacy of individuals by protecting their sensitive attributes is an important consideration during microdata release. However, it is equally important to preserve the quality or utility of the data for at least some targeted workloads. We propose a novel framework for privacy preservation based on the k-anonymity model that is ideally suited for workloads that require preserving the probability distribution of the quasi-identifier variables in the data. Our framework combines the principles of distribution-preserving quantization and k-member clustering, and we specialize it to two variants that respectively use intra-cluster and Gaussian dithering of cluster centers to achieve distribution preservation. We perform theoretical analysis of the proposed schemes in terms of distribution preservation, and describe their utility in workloads such as covariate shift and transfer learning where such a property is necessary. Using extensive experiments on real-world Medical Expenditure Panel Survey data, we demonstrate the merits of our algorithms over standard k-anonymization for a hallmark health care application where an insurance company wishes to understand the risk in entering a new market. Furthermore, by empirically quantifying the reidentification risk, we also show that the proposed approaches indeed maintain k-anonymity.

Adversarial training has emerged as a critical defense mechanism against adversarial attacks in machine learning models, particularly in classification tasks. However, the statistical robustness of classification accuracies under adversarial training remains underexplored. This paper addresses the challenge of precisely quantifying and analyzing the performance of classifiers trained with adversarial techniques. We propose a novel statistical framework that evaluates classification accuracies under varying adversarial conditions, leveraging rigorous hypothesis testing and confidence interval estimation. Our approach integrates Monte Carlo simulations and bootstrapping methods to account for uncertainty and variability in adversarial scenarios. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our framework provides statistically significant insights into the trade-offs between robustness and accuracy, outperforming traditional evaluation methods. The findings reveal that adversarial training not only enhances model resilience but also introduces measurable statistical patterns in classification performance. This work contributes a robust analytical tool for researchers and practitioners to assess and improve adversarial training strategies, with implications for secure and reliable machine learning systems in real-world applications. **Keywords**: adversarial training, classification accuracy, statistical analysis, machine learning robustness, hypothesis testing, Monte Carlo simulations.

Do đó, việc phát hiện sớm không chỉ bởi nhân viên y tế mà còn bởi chính người dân, để từ đó các can thiệp y tế sớm và kịp thời có thể giúp bệnh nhân giảm thiểu mức độ tàn phế hay thậm chí có thể hồi phục hoàn toàn. Tuy nhiên, các công cụ để truyền thông giáo dục sức khỏe cho người dân về ĐQN hiện nay còn nhiều khiếm khuyết và chưa phù hợp cho mọi đối tượng. Vì thế, chúng tôi đã nghiên cứu, xây dựng giản đồ giúp trí nhớ “Các dấu hiệu nhận biết đột quỵ não”. Đây là một phiên bản thuần Việt về các dấu hiệu nhận biết đột quỵ não cho người Việt với mong muốn góp phần giảm tỷ lệ tàn tật, tử vong do ĐQN tại Việt Nam. Chúng tôi kỳ vọng giản đồ “Các dấu hiệu nhận biết đột quỵ não” sẽ được các sử dụng để truyền thông giáo dục sức khỏe cho người dân; từ đó giúp nhận biết sớm các trường hợp ĐQN trong cộng đồng, góp phần hạn chế tử vong và biến chứng cho người bệnh. Bên cạnh đó, Giản đồ cũng nên được đưa ra giới thiệu tại các cơ sở y tế các cấp, đặc biệt là tại tuyến ban đầu nhằm tư vấn trực tiếp cho người dân, cũng như thu thập các ý kiến đóng góp của các đồng nghiệp nhằm hoàn chỉnh, phát triển công cụ.

This paper explores the application of deep learning techniques to level generation and style enhancement in game development, aiming to revolutionize the industry with automated and innovative content creation. Our approach utilizes Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to generate diverse and engaging levels, while also enhancing visual styles through neural style transfer. The results demonstrate significant improvements in level complexity and aesthetic appeal, outperforming traditional methods. Our research contributes to the field by introducing a novel framework for integrating deep learning into game development pipelines, enabling faster and more efficient content creation. The implications of this work are far-reaching, with potential applications in the gaming industry, simulation environments, and beyond. Key aspects of this research include level generation, style transfer, GANs, VAEs, game development, and deep learning, highlighting the potential for AI-driven innovation in the entertainment and technology sectors.

This paper introduces IAN, a novel approach to imaginative face generation by combining generative adversarial networks (GANs). The objective is to create a system capable of generating highly realistic and diverse facial images. To achieve this, we propose a multi-stage framework that leverages the strengths of both conditional and unconditional GANs. Our method involves training a conditional GAN to learn the structure of faces, followed by an unconditional GAN to introduce randomness and creativity. The results show that IAN outperforms existing face generation models in terms of image quality and diversity. Our approach achieves a state-of-the-art Frechet Inception Distance (FID) score, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating realistic faces. The implications of this research are significant, with potential applications in fields such as computer vision, robotics, and digital entertainment. Key contributions include the development of a novel GAN architecture and the demonstration of its ability to generate highly realistic and imaginative facial images. Relevant keywords: generative adversarial networks, face generation, imaginative faces, conditional GANs, unconditional GANs, computer vision, deep learning.

Reinforcement learning agents often struggle with exploration in sparse-reward environments. This paper introduces a novel approach to improve exploration by leveraging human gameplay videos from platforms like YouTube. Our method, Imitation-Augmented Exploration (IAE), trains an agent to imitate successful exploration strategies observed in human play. We first extract key exploratory actions from YouTube videos of humans playing the target game. These actions are then used to guide the agent's exploration during training via a behavior cloning loss combined with a traditional reinforcement learning objective. We evaluate IAE on a suite of challenging hard exploration games. Results demonstrate that agents trained with IAE achieve significantly higher scores and faster learning compared to agents trained with standard exploration techniques. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of different imitation strategies and identify key factors contributing to successful exploration. This work highlights the potential of using readily available human gameplay data to improve the exploration capabilities of reinforcement learning agents. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Exploration, Imitation Learning, Video Games, Behavior Cloning.

This paper presents a novel approach to designing scalable and privacy-preserving deep neural networks through an algorithmic-cryptographic co-design methodology. The primary objective is to address the pressing issue of protecting sensitive data during the training and inference phases of deep learning models. To achieve this, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates advanced cryptographic techniques, such as homomorphic encryption and secure multi-party computation, with optimized algorithmic designs for deep neural networks. Our approach enables the secure and efficient training of models on private data, while also facilitating scalable and accurate inference. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our co-design methodology, showcasing significant improvements in model performance and privacy preservation compared to existing solutions. The key contributions of this research include the development of a scalable and privacy-preserving deep learning framework, which has important implications for applications in areas such as healthcare, finance, and edge computing. By combining cryptographic security with algorithmic innovation, our work paves the way for the widespread adoption of deep neural networks in privacy-sensitive domains, with relevant keywords including homomorphic encryption, secure multi-party computation, deep learning, privacy preservation, and scalable neural networks.

Cá trắm đen (Mylopharyngodon piceus) là một loài cá nước ngọt phổ biến ở châu Á. Để đánh giá khả năng chịu mặn của loài cá này, một nghiên cứu được thực hiện với giai đoạn giống. Kết quả cho thấy cá trắm đen có khả năng chịu mặn tương đối tốt, đặc biệt là trong giai đoạn giống. Khi được chuyển từ môi trường nước ngọt sang nước mặn, cá trắm đen có thể thích nghi nhanh chóng và sống sót trong điều kiện mặn cao. Tuy nhiên, khả năng chịu mặn của cá trắm đen cũng phụ thuộc vào nhiều yếu tố như độ mặn, nhiệt độ và thời gian thích nghi. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp thông tin quan trọng về khả năng chịu mặn của cá trắm đen, giúp cho việc nuôi trồng và bảo tồn loài cá này.

Phân tích động lực học của tấm nứt trên nền đàn hồi dưới tác động của bộ dao động di động là một lĩnh vực nghiên cứu quan trọng trong kỹ thuật cơ học. Phương pháp phần tử hữu hạn được áp dụng để mô phỏng và phân tích các trạng thái khác nhau của tấm, từ đó cung cấp cái nhìn sâu sắc về hành vi của cấu trúc khi chịu tác động từ các lực động. Latent tree models are widely used for probabilistic reasoning and knowledge representation, but learning them efficiently and with theoretical guarantees remains a challenge, especially with large datasets. This paper introduces a novel algorithm for learning latent tree models that achieves guaranteed scalability in terms of both computational complexity and sample complexity. Our approach leverages a spectral method combined with a novel tree structure learning technique that avoids exhaustive search. We prove that our algorithm consistently learns the true tree structure under mild conditions, and we provide explicit bounds on the sample complexity required for accurate structure recovery. Empirical evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and runtime, particularly for large-scale problems. Our contributions provide a practical and theoretically sound approach for learning latent tree models, enabling their effective application in domains such as Bayesian networks, hierarchical clustering, and information retrieval. Keywords: Latent Tree Models, Structure Learning, Scalable Algorithms, Spectral Methods, Graphical Models, Bayesian Networks.

Accurately estimating the intrinsic dimension of high-dimensional data is a fundamental challenge in machine learning and data analysis, with significant implications for dimensionality reduction, feature extraction, and model optimization. This paper addresses the problem of intrinsic dimension estimation by proposing a novel, computationally efficient algorithm that leverages local geometric properties of data manifolds. Our approach combines neighborhood-based density estimation with spectral analysis to robustly infer the intrinsic dimension, even in the presence of noise and nonlinear structures. We evaluate the proposed method on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and scalability. The results highlight the algorithm's ability to handle complex, high-dimensional data while maintaining low computational overhead. This work contributes to the field by providing a practical and theoretically grounded solution for intrinsic dimension estimation, with potential applications in unsupervised learning, data compression, and exploratory data analysis. Key innovations include the integration of local and global geometric insights, as well as a noise-resilient framework that adapts to varying data densities. Keywords: intrinsic dimension, dimensionality reduction, manifold learning, spectral analysis, unsupervised learning.

Hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) is a widely used technique for grouping data into nested structures based on similarity. However, traditional HAC methods often fail to preserve the order of data points, which can be critical in applications such as time-series analysis, genomic sequencing, and document organization. This paper introduces a novel approach to order-preserving hierarchical agglomerative clustering (OP-HAC), which ensures that the inherent sequence of data points is maintained throughout the clustering process. Our method leverages a modified distance metric and a constrained merging strategy to achieve this goal. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that OP-HAC outperforms conventional HAC in preserving order while maintaining competitive clustering accuracy. The proposed approach is particularly effective in scenarios where temporal or spatial relationships are essential. This work contributes to the field by providing a robust framework for order-aware clustering, with potential applications in bioinformatics, natural language processing, and network analysis. **Keywords**: hierarchical clustering, order preservation, agglomerative clustering, data sequencing, constrained clustering.

This paper presents a novel approach to learning CHARME (CHAracteristic Model Editing) models using neural networks. The objective is to improve the efficiency and accuracy of CHARME model learning, which is crucial for various applications in computer vision and graphics. Our method employs a deep learning framework to learn the complex relationships between model parameters and editing operations. The neural network is trained on a large dataset of CHARME models and their corresponding editing sequences, allowing it to learn a compact and effective representation of the model space. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of model accuracy and editing efficiency. The key findings of this research include the development of a neural network architecture that can learn CHARME models from raw data, and the demonstration of its potential for applications such as 3D reconstruction, animation, and video editing. The contributions of this work lie in its ability to leverage the power of neural networks to improve the learning of CHARME models, making it a valuable tool for professionals in the field of computer graphics and vision. Key keywords: CHARME models, neural networks, deep learning, computer vision, graphics, 3D reconstruction.

Deep Learning models have been widely used in difficult tasks like autonomousdriving and machine translation. However, creating such models has proven diffi cult, both computationally and because it necessitates a large amount of annotated data. Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA), which uses accessible unlabeled data, allows models to be modified to new data distributions. Previous domainadaptation techniques only took into account the alignment of intra-class repre sentational distributions across different domains, failing to adequately explore theinter-class structural relationship. As a result, aligned representations on the tar get domain may no longer be as easily discriminated as they were on the source domain. In this work, I propose Multi-level Contrastive Learning for Domain Adaptive Semantic Segmentation (MCLDA), a novel one-stage adaptation framework thatemphasizes the semantic concepts of individual pixels in order to encourage learn ing of class-discriminative, ultimately improving the performance of self-training methods. Specifically, the method start by creating a pixel-wise contrastive loss by taking consideration of the relationships between pixel-wise representations from both domains. In essence, groups of pixel representations from the same category should group together, whereas groups from different categories should spread out. Specifically, our method performs contrastive loss not only at feature level, also at output level. In addition, we propose a novel mixing strategy that addresses the dataset imbalance problem. The main concept is to repeatedly copy pixels from uncommon classes in source images and paste them into destination images. The experimental results on a commonly adopted benchmarks GTA5 →Cityscapes and achive 56.76 in term of mIoU. Noticeably, in some categories that often get lowIoU, such as "fence" and "pole", our method achieves 35.30 and 35.67, respec tively, which further illustrates the efficiency of our design.

This paper introduces GraphGen-Redux, a novel recurrent model designed for efficient labeled graph generation. The objective is to address the limitations of existing graph generation methods, which often suffer from high computational complexity and poor scalability. To achieve this, we propose a lightweight and fast approach that leverages recurrent neural networks to generate graphs sequentially. Our method utilizes a carefully designed encoding scheme and a conditional random field to ensure the generated graphs are valid and labeled correctly. Experimental results demonstrate that GraphGen-Redux outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of generation speed and quality, while requiring significantly fewer parameters. The key findings of this research highlight the effectiveness of recurrent models in graph generation tasks, particularly in applications where speed and efficiency are crucial. The contributions of this work include a novel graph generation architecture, a scalable encoding scheme, and a conditional random field-based labeling approach. Overall, GraphGen-Redux has the potential to facilitate a wide range of applications, including network analysis, graph-based data augmentation, and molecule generation, making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of graph learning and generation, with relevant keywords including graph generation, recurrent neural networks, labeled graphs, and network analysis.

Image-to-image translation aims to convert an image from one domain to another while preserving its content. Current methods often struggle with generating diverse and high-quality outputs, especially when dealing with significant domain gaps. This paper introduces a novel Group-wise Deep Whitening-and-Coloring Transformation (GDWCT) to address these limitations. Our approach decouples the style and content features of an image by employing a whitening transformation to remove style information and a coloring transformation to inject the target style. Crucially, GDWCT operates on group-wise feature statistics, enabling more fine-grained style control and improved content preservation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of GDWCT on several challenging image translation tasks, including photo-to-painting, day-to-night, and style transfer. The objective of this research is to address the challenges faced by reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms in navigating environments with multiple optimal policies, which can hinder efficient policy exploration and convergence. Key findings from our experiments, conducted across a range of benchmark RL environments, demonstrate that POMO achieves superior convergence rates and improved stability compared to traditional policy gradient methods. The results highlight POMO's ability to avoid premature convergence to suboptimal policies and successfully explore diverse, high-reward strategies. These improvements not only underscore the effectiveness of POMO in leveraging multiple optima for enhanced learning outcomes but also suggest significant potential for applications in complex decision-making tasks in dynamic environments. By enhancing the scope for policy exploration in RL, this research contributes to the advancement of more adaptive and resilient RL algorithms. Keywords include reinforcement learning, policy optimization, multiple optima, convergence, and exploration.

Object detection is a fundamental task in computer vision, traditionally approached through localization and classification pipelines using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and complex post-processing techniques. This paper presents Pix2seq, a novel language modeling framework that formulates object detection as a sequence prediction problem. In Pix2seq, images are encoded into sequences, and object annotations—including locations and categories—are treated as tokens to be predicted by an autoregressive transformer-based model. This approach simplifies the object detection pipeline by unifying image understanding and prediction under a single sequence-to-sequence modeling architecture, removing the need for hand-crafted priors like anchor boxes or non-maximum suppression. We evaluate Pix2seq on widely-used benchmarks such as COCO and Pascal VOC, demonstrating comparable or superior performance to traditional detection methods, while significantly reducing architectural complexity. Our experimental results highlight the model’s ability to generalize across diverse object categories and adapt to varying image resolutions. Furthermore, ablation studies show that Pix2seq achieves strong performance even with minimal post-processing. The findings indicate that re-framing object detection as a language modeling task provides a flexible and extensible foundation for integrating vision and language in computer vision systems. This research contributes a new perspective to object detection, with implications for unified vision-language learning and downstream applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and digital content analysis. Keywords: object detection, language modeling, Pix2seq, transformer, sequence prediction, computer vision, deep learning.

This paper investigates the problem of stochastic computation offloading in digital twin networks (DTNs) using deep reinforcement learning (DRL). We aim to minimize the long-term cost associated with latency and energy consumption in a dynamic DTN environment, where task arrivals and channel conditions are uncertain. We propose a novel DRL-based offloading strategy that leverages a deep Q-network (DQN) to learn optimal offloading decisions without requiring prior knowledge of the system's stochastic behavior. The DQN agent intelligently determines whether to process tasks locally or offload them to edge servers, considering the current network state represented by task queue lengths, channel quality, and server utilization. Simulation results demonstrate that our DRL-based approach significantly outperforms traditional offloading policies and other reinforcement learning baselines in terms of reducing latency and energy consumption. The proposed solution offers a promising avenue for efficient resource management in DTNs, enabling real-time applications and enhanced decision-making capabilities. **Keywords:** Digital Twin Networks, Computation Offloading, Deep Reinforcement Learning, Stochastic Optimization, Edge Computing, DQN.

This research addresses the vulnerability of Partial Dependence (PD) plots in machine learning models to adversarial attacks through data poisoning. PD plots are widely used for interpreting complex models by illustrating the relationship between a set of predictors and the target response. However, they can be susceptible to manipulation, which questions their reliability in decision-making processes. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel data poisoning framework that subtly introduces malicious data into the training set to manipulate the output of PD plots without significantly compromising model performance. Our approach utilizes advanced optimization techniques to identify the most influential instances for poisoning, ensuring stealth and efficacy. We employed various datasets and models to validate our framework and assess its impact on PD plots. Results/Findings: Experiments demonstrate that our data poisoning method can effectively alter PD plots, leading to misleading interpretations while maintaining the model's predictive accuracy. Comparisons with existing data manipulation strategies show that our approach achieves superior stealth and effectiveness, highlighting the critical impact of such vulnerabilities on model interpretability and trustworthiness. Conclusion/Implications: The findings underscore the need for developing robust defenses against data poisoning attacks to safeguard PD plot accuracy, which is crucial for model interpretability in high-stakes applications. This work contributes to the broader field of model interpretability and security, suggesting that future frameworks must account for adversarial robustness. Researchers and practitioners should be aware of these vulnerabilities when employing PD plots for model insights, and explore strategies to detect or mitigate such manipulative efforts. Keywords: Partial Dependence, Data Poisoning, Model Interpretability, Machine Learning Security, Adversarial Attacks, Optimization Techniques.

Off-policy deep reinforcement learning (DRL) holds significant promise for training agents from previously collected data, circumventing the need for online exploration. However, existing methods often suffer from instability and suboptimal performance due to distributional shift and extrapolation errors. This paper introduces a novel off-policy DRL algorithm that mitigates these issues without relying on explicit exploration. Our approach leverages a conservative policy optimization framework coupled with a learned behavior regularizer to constrain policy updates. This regularizer encourages the learned policy to stay close to the behavior policy, thereby reducing extrapolation errors and improving stability. We evaluate our algorithm on a range of benchmark tasks, demonstrating significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art off-policy DRL methods. The results show that our approach effectively learns robust policies from offline datasets, even in the absence of exploratory data. Key contributions include a novel behavior regularizer, a stable off-policy learning framework, and empirical validation of its effectiveness. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Deep Learning, Off-Policy Learning, Policy Optimization, Behavior Regularization.

Aiming to reduce pollutant emissions, bicycles are regaining popularity specially in urban areas. However, the number of cyclists' fatalities is not showing the same decreasing trend as the other traffic groups. Hence, monitoring cyclists' data appears as a keystone to foster urban cyclists' safety by helping urban planners to design safer cyclist routes. In this work, we propose a fully image-based framework to assess the rout risk from the cyclist perspective. From smartphone sequences of images, this generic framework is able to automatically identify events considering different risk criteria based on the cyclist's motion and object detection. Moreover, since it is entirely based on images, our method provides context on the situation and is independent from the expertise level of the cyclist. Additionally, we build on an existing platform and introduce several improvements on its mobile app to acquire smartphone sensor data, including video. From the inertial sensor data, we automatically detect the route segments performed by bicycle, applying behavior analysis techniques. We test our methods on real data, attaining very promising results in terms of risk classification, according to two different criteria, and behavior analysis accuracy.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurately identifying vehicle make, model, and color from images captured at various angles, a task that has significant applications in areas such as traffic monitoring and security. Traditional methods often depend on fixed viewpoints, which limits their effectiveness in diverse real-world scenarios. Methods/Approach: We propose a robust approach utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNN) to achieve view-independent vehicle recognition. Our model is designed to process vehicle images and learn distinguishing features that are invariant to changes in viewing angle. This is achieved by employing a multi-branch architecture that independently predicts vehicle make, model, and color, allowing for comprehensive vehicle characterization. Results/Findings: The proposed model was evaluated on a large-scale dataset comprising images of vehicles captured from multiple perspectives. Our findings demonstrate that the CNN-based model significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving high accuracy rates in recognizing vehicle make, model, and color irrespective of the viewpoint. Comparative analysis shows marked improvements in system performance over traditional viewpoint-dependent techniques. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel approach to vehicle recognition that enhances accuracy across various viewing angles, expanding the practicality of automated vehicle identification systems. The implications of this work are profound, facilitating advancements in intelligent transportation systems, law enforcement, and urban planning. Future development could explore extending this model to integrate additional vehicle attributes and adapt to real-time processing environments. Keywords: Vehicle recognition, CNN, viewpoint invariance, traffic monitoring, automated identification.

In recent years, the dissemination of misinformation through social media platforms has become a critical concern, particularly during significant events when rumors can spread rapidly. This paper investigates the effectiveness of ensemble deep learning techniques applied to time-series representations of tweets for rumor detection. Our primary objective is to enhance the accuracy and reliability of misinformation identification by leveraging the temporal dynamics inherent in social media interactions. We propose a novel framework that combines multiple deep learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, to capture both spatial and temporal features from tweet data. Through extensive experimentation on curated datasets, we demonstrate that our ensemble approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a detection accuracy of over 92%. Moreover, our results indicate that incorporating temporal information leads to a marked improvement in identifying emerging rumors as they unfold. This research contributes to the development of more robust misinformation detection systems and has practical implications for social media platforms, policymakers, and researchers working to counteract the effects of false information. Key keywords: rumor detection, deep learning, time-series data, social media, misinformation, ensemble methods.

Hệ thống điều khiển vị trí đa động cơ đòi hỏi độ chính xác cao và khả năng xử lý các tín hiệu phức tạp. Để đáp ứng yêu cầu này, bộ điều khiển mờ (Fuzzy Logic Controller) được thiết kế nhằm tối ưu hóa hiệu suất của hệ thống. Bộ điều khiển này sử dụng các quy tắc mờ để xử lý thông tin đầu vào, giúp hệ thống phản ứng linh hoạt với các thay đổi tải và nhiễu. Nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc xây dựng mô hình toán học, thiết kế bộ điều khiển mờ và đánh giá hiệu quả thông qua mô phỏng. Kết quả cho thấy, bộ điều khiển mờ không chỉ cải thiện độ chính xác mà còn tăng tính ổn định của hệ thống, đặc biệt trong các điều kiện làm việc phức tạp. Đây là hướng tiếp cận tiềm năng trong lĩnh vực điều khiển tự động, mang lại hiệu quả cao cho các ứng dụng công nghiệp.

U màng não củ yên là một loại khối u nội sọ thường gặp, chiếm tỷ lệ đáng kể trong các ca phẫu thuật thần kinh. Chẩn đoán hình ảnh đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc xác định, phân loại và lên kế hoạch điều trị cho loại u này. Cộng hưởng từ (MRI) là phương pháp chẩn đoán hình ảnh được ưu tiên, cung cấp thông tin chi tiết về vị trí, kích thước, hình thái, mức độ xâm lấn và mối liên hệ của u với các cấu trúc xung quanh như dây thần kinh thị giác, tuyến yên và mạch máu. Dựa trên các đặc điểm hình ảnh MRI, u màng não củ yên có thể được phân loại thành nhiều nhóm khác nhau, từ đó giúp các bác sĩ đưa ra quyết định phẫu thuật phù hợp. Việc phân loại trước mổ bằng MRI góp phần quan trọng trong việc dự đoán khả năng phẫu thuật thành công, giảm thiểu rủi ro và cải thiện kết quả điều trị cho bệnh nhân. Các nghiên cứu sâu hơn về mối tương quan giữa hình ảnh MRI và kết quả giải phẫu bệnh lý sẽ giúp nâng cao độ chính xác trong chẩn đoán và phân loại u màng não củ yên.

This research paper addresses the challenge of stereo matching from monocular images through an unsupervised learning approach, aimed at advancing the field of depth perception and 3D scene reconstruction. Traditional stereo matching methods rely heavily on stereo image pairs and supervised training data, limiting their applicability in various real-world scenarios where such data may be scarce. Our objective is to devise an unsupervised framework that effectively learns stereo correspondences from single monocular images without the need for annotated depth maps. To achieve this, we propose a novel algorithm that leverages a combination of deep learning techniques and photometric consistency constraints. By employing a carefully designed loss function, our approach aligns and compares pixel intensities across synthesized views, enabling accurate disparity estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance when compared to state-of-the-art supervised techniques on benchmark datasets, highlighting its potential for real-time applications in environments with limited sensory data. The findings suggest that our unsupervised method can be generalized across different domains, offering a scalable solution for enhancing depth estimation and 3D reconstruction from monocular input. This contributes significantly to the fields of computer vision and autonomous systems, where robust and adaptable stereo matching is crucial. Key keywords include unsupervised learning, stereo matching, monocular images, disparity estimation, and 3D reconstruction.

Proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm is a deep reinforcement learning algorithm with outstanding performance, especially in continuous control tasks. But the performance of this method is still affected by its exploration ability. For classical reinforcement learning, there are some schemes that make exploration more full and balanced with data exploitation, but they can't be applied in complex environments due to the complexity of algorithm. Based on continuous control tasks with dense reward, this paper analyzes the assumption of the original Gaussian action exploration mechanism in PPO algorithm, and clarifies the influence of exploration ability on performance. Afterward, aiming at the problem of exploration, an exploration enhancement mechanism based on uncertainty estimation is designed in this paper. Then, we apply exploration enhancement theory to PPO algorithm and propose the proximal policy optimization algorithm with intrinsic exploration module (IEM-PPO) which can be used in complex environments. In the experimental parts, we evaluate our method on multiple tasks of MuJoCo physical simulator, and compare IEM-PPO algorithm with curiosity driven exploration algorithm (ICM-PPO) and original algorithm (PPO). The experimental results demonstrate that IEM-PPO algorithm needs longer training time, but performs better in terms of sample efficiency and cumulative reward, and has stability and robustness.

Nhóm gả pháp này sử dụng các kỹ thuật như tìm kếm Tabu, gả thuật điàn kiến. Một trường hợp lâm sàng hiếm gặp về Thanatophoric dysplasia (TD), một loại loạn sản xương gây tử vong ở trẻ sơ sinh, vừa được ghi nhận. Bệnh nhi có các biểu hiện đặc trưng như đầu lớn, lồng ngực hẹp, tứ chi ngắn và các bất thường xương khác. TD được gây ra bởi đột biến gen FGFR3, ảnh hưởng đến sự phát triển của xương và sụn. Việc chẩn đoán TD thường dựa vào siêu âm trước sinh hoặc khám nghiệm tử thi sau sinh. Trường hợp này nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc nhận biết các dấu hiệu lâm sàng và hình ảnh học của TD để chẩn đoán chính xác và tư vấn di truyền cho các gia đình có nguy cơ. Các bác sĩ cần nâng cao nhận thức về bệnh lý này để cải thiện khả năng phát hiện và quản lý bệnh, đồng thời cung cấp thông tin đầy đủ cho cha mẹ về tiên lượng và các lựa chọn chăm sóc.

Nghiên cứu về phân vùng khí hậu nông nghiệp tỉnh Sơn La đã được thực hiện nhằm đánh giá tiềm năng và hạn chế của khí hậu đối với sản xuất nông nghiệp trong khu vực. Dựa trên các yếu tố như nhiệt độ, lượng mưa, độ ẩm và ánh sáng, tỉnh Sơn La được chia thành các vùng khí hậu nông nghiệp khác nhau, mỗi vùng có đặc điểm riêng biệt phù hợp với các loại cây trồng và vật nuôi khác nhau. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp thông tin quan trọng cho việc quy hoạch và phát triển nông nghiệp bền vững, giúp người nông dân lựa chọn cây trồng phù hợp, áp dụng các biện pháp canh tác hiệu quả, giảm thiểu rủi ro do biến đổi khí hậu và tối ưu hóa năng suất cây trồng, góp phần nâng cao thu nhập và cải thiện đời sống của người dân địa phương. Đồng thời, nghiên cứu cũng đề xuất các giải pháp ứng phó với biến đổi khí hậu, bảo vệ tài nguyên đất và nước, đảm bảo sự phát triển bền vững của ngành nông nghiệp tỉnh Sơn La.

Các xét nghiệm như siêu âm, X-quang, và xét nghiệm máu cũng được sử dụng để chẩn đoán. Kết quả điều trị của trẻ sơ sinh bị dị tật bẩm sinh đường tiêu hóa tại Bệnh viện cho thấy tỷ lệ thành công cao. Tuy nhiên, cần lưu ý rằng mỗi trường hợp dị tật bẩm sinh đường tiêu hóa đều có đặc điểm riêng và đòi hỏi sự chẩn đoán và điều trị cẩn thận. Các bác sĩ tại Bệnh viện sẽ tiếp tục nghiên cứu và cải thiện phương pháp điều trị để giúp trẻ sơ sinh bị dị tật bẩm sinh đường tiêu hóa có thể sống khỏe mạnh và bình thường.
