This paper introduces a novel adaptive video super-resolution algorithm designed to enhance reconstruction quality while maintaining robustness against innovations, such as sudden scene changes and object occlusions. The proposed algorithm employs a dynamic filtering approach coupled with motion-compensated temporal filtering to leverage inter-frame redundancies effectively. An adaptive weighting scheme, based on local image statistics and motion vector reliability, mitigates artifacts introduced by inaccurate motion estimation, thereby improving robustness to innovations. Experimental results on a diverse set of benchmark video sequences demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) compared to state-of-the-art super-resolution methods, particularly in the presence of significant innovations. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have gained momentum for their ability to model image distributions. They learn to emulate the training set and that enables sampling from that domain and using the knowledge learned for useful applications. Several methods proposed enhancing GANs, including regularizing the loss with some feature matching. We seek to push GANs beyond the data in the training and try to explore unseen territory in the image manifold. We first propose a new regularizer for GAN based on K-nearest neighbor (K-NN) selective feature matching to a target set Y in high-level feature space, during the adversarial training of GAN on the base set X, and we call this novel model K-GAN. We show that minimizing the added term follows from cross-entropy minimization between the distributions of GAN and the set Y. Then, We introduce a cascaded framework for GANs that try to address the task of imagining a new distribution that combines the base set X and target set Y by cascading sampling GANs with translation GANs, and we dub the cascade of such GANs as the Imaginative Adversarial Network (IAN). We conduct an objective and subjective evaluation for different IAN setups in the addressed task and show some useful applications for these IANs, like manifold traversing and creative face generation for characters' design in movies or video games.

Facial Expression Recognition (FER) plays a crucial role in human-computer interaction. While Vision Transformers (ViTs) have shown promise in various vision tasks, their application to FER has been limited, often overlooking fine-grained local features critical for recognizing subtle expressions. This paper proposes a novel Vision Transformer architecture incorporating Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks to enhance the feature representation learning for FER. Our method, named SE-ViT, integrates SE blocks into the ViT architecture to adaptively recalibrate channel-wise feature responses, emphasizing informative facial regions and suppressing less relevant ones. We evaluate SE-ViT on several benchmark FER datasets, including AffectNet and FER-2013. Experimental results demonstrate that SE-ViT achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing existing CNN-based and ViT-based methods. Specifically, SE-ViT shows improved accuracy in recognizing expressions with subtle muscle movements. The results highlight the effectiveness of integrating channel attention mechanisms within ViTs for FER. The proposed SE-ViT architecture offers a promising approach to improve the accuracy and robustness of FER systems. Keywords: Facial Expression Recognition, Vision Transformer, Squeeze-and-Excitation, Channel Attention, Deep Learning.

Our experiments were conducted on a real-world ICU dataset, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method in identifying AMR acquisition with improved accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional approaches. The results highlight the potential of combining time series kernels and dimensionality reduction for early detection of AMR, offering actionable insights for clinical decision-making and infection control strategies. The paper addresses the critical need for explainable validation methods for machine learning (ML) models, focusing on their application in real-world scenarios. As ML models are increasingly integrated into practical applications, understanding their reliability and trustworthiness becomes paramount. Methods: We propose an innovative approach that combines online validation techniques with explainable AI frameworks to enhance the transparency and accountability of ML models. Our hybrid methodology employs a combination of real-time data monitoring, model performance tracking, and explainability mechanisms, such as interpretable visualization tools and feature importance analysis, to offer continuous insights into model operations and decision-making processes. Results: Experiments conducted across multiple datasets and application domains demonstrate the approach's efficacy. Our method not only improves validation accuracy but also provides intuitive explanations for model behaviors. Comparisons with traditional validation techniques highlight significant advancements in interpretability and user trust, reducing decision-making errors by 23% on average. Conclusion: This research contributes a novel framework for explainable online validation of ML models, bridging the gap between complex algorithmic performance and practical application needs. By facilitating deeper insights into model decision processes, our approach is positioned to support a wide range of industries seeking to leverage machine learning, from healthcare to finance. Keywords: Explainable AI, Machine Learning Validation, Real-time Monitoring, Model Interpretability, Practical Applications.

This paper introduces a novel real-time policy distillation framework for deep reinforcement learning (DRL) that addresses the challenge of deploying complex, computationally intensive policies in resource-constrained environments. Our approach, Real-time Distillation Network (RTDN), enables the transfer of knowledge from a sophisticated teacher policy to a compact student policy within a continuous learning loop. RTDN employs an asynchronous training scheme, allowing the student policy to learn online from the teacher's actions and experiences in real-time without interrupting the environment interaction. We evaluate RTDN on a set of challenging continuous control tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in student policy performance compared to offline distillation methods and traditional DRL algorithms. Specifically, RTDN achieves comparable performance to the teacher policy while reducing computational overhead by an average of 60%. The findings suggest that RTDN offers a promising solution for deploying high-performing DRL agents in real-world applications with limited computational resources. Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Policy Distillation, Real-time Learning, Knowledge Transfer, Continuous Control.

Phân tích ứng xử động khung phẳng bê tông cốt thép dưới tải trọng va chạm là một vấn đề quan trọng trong lĩnh vực xây dựng và cơ sở vật chất. Khung phẳng bê tông cốt thép là một cấu trúc phổ biến trong các công trình xây dựng, bao gồm các tòa nhà, cầu, và đường cao tốc. Khi xảy ra tải trọng va chạm, khung phẳng bê tông cốt thép phải có khả năng chống chịu và hấp thụ được lực va chạm để đảm bảo an toàn cho người và tài sản. Tuy nhiên, quá trình này cũng có thể gây ra các vấn đề về độ bền và ổn định của cấu trúc. Phân tích ứng xử động khung phẳng bê tông cốt thép dưới tải trọng va chạm bao gồm việc đánh giá khả năng chịu lực của cấu trúc, phân tích các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến độ bền và ổn định, và đề xuất các giải pháp để cải thiện khả năng chống chịu của cấu trúc. Quá trình phân tích này thường bao gồm các bước sau: - Xác định tải trọng va chạm và các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến độ bền và ổn định của cấu trúc. - Phân tích các tính chất cơ học của bê tông cốt thép, bao gồm độ cứng, độ dẻo, và khả năng chịu lực. - Sử dụng các mô hình toán học để mô tả và phân tích ứng xử động của khung phẳng bê tông cốt thép dưới tải trọng va chạm. - Đánh giá và phân tích kết quả phân tích để xác định khả năng chịu lực và ổn định của cấu trúc. Kết quả phân tích này sẽ giúp các kỹ sư và kiến trúc sư có thể đề xuất các giải pháp để cải thiện khả năng chống chịu của cấu trúc, bao gồm việc tăng cường độ bền của bê tông cốt thép, cải thiện thiết kế của cấu trúc, và thực hiện các biện pháp an toàn để giảm thiểu rủi ro.

Dự thảo Luật Phòng, chống rửa tiền (sửa đổi) hiện đang được xem xét nhằm hoàn thiện khuôn khổ pháp lý trong lĩnh vực này. Một số vấn đề quan trọng được đặt ra bao gồm việc mở rộng phạm vi đối tượng báo cáo, tăng cường các biện pháp nhận biết khách hàng và kiểm soát giao dịch, đặc biệt là các giao dịch liên quan đến công nghệ mới và tài sản ảo. Cần làm rõ hơn về trách nhiệm của các tổ chức tài chính và các ngành nghề kinh doanh phi tài chính có rủi ro cao trong việc phát hiện và báo cáo các giao dịch đáng ngờ. Bên cạnh đó, việc nâng cao hiệu quả hợp tác quốc tế trong phòng, chống rửa tiền cũng là một yếu tố then chốt. Dự thảo cần đảm bảo tính khả thi, phù hợp với thông lệ quốc tế, đồng thời đáp ứng yêu cầu thực tiễn của Việt Nam trong bối cảnh tội phạm rửa tiền ngày càng tinh vi và phức tạp. Việc sửa đổi luật này đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc bảo vệ sự ổn định của hệ thống tài chính và ngăn chặn các hoạt động phạm pháp.

Các u này thường được phát hiện trong những năm đầu đời khi đánh giá van hoặc tắc nghẽn dòng máu. Biểu hiện lâm sàng tùy thuộc vào vị trí, số lượng và kích thước u. U có thể gây ra rối loạn huyết động nghiêm trọng như tắc nghẽn đường ra thất trái hoặc gây rối loạn nhịp tim. Hơn 90 % u cơ vân đa ổ có dấu hiệu của phức hợp bệnh xơ củ. Phẫu thuật cắt bỏ khối u là phương pháp điều trị hiệu quả khi khối u lớn gây ra các biến chứng huyết động nặng hoặc rối loạn nhịp tim tái phát và kháng trị. Báo cáo ca: Bệnh nhân nam hơn 1 tháng tuổi được chẩn đoán u tim, tắc nghẽn đường ra thất trái bằng siêu âm tim và MRI tim. Bệnh nhân được phẫu thuật tim, và các khối u (bên dưới van động mạch chủ và ở bờ tiểu nhĩ phải) đã được cắt bỏ. Xét nghiệm mô bệnh học và hóa mô miễn dịch khẳng định là các u cơ vân. Bệnh nhân hồi phục tốt sau phẫu thuật. Ngoài ra, xét nghiệm sinh học phân tử cho thấy một đột biến trong gen TSC2. Kết luận: Chúng tôi trình bày trường hợp này để chia sẻ những phát hiện về u này với các đồng nghiệp. Mặc dù đây là một trường hợp hiếm được báo cáo, chúng tôi hy vọng báo cáo về u này và tổng quan tài liệu có thể nâng cao nhận thức về khối u ở tim.

This paper proposes a novel approach to signal processing by integrating variational models with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The objective is to develop a robust and flexible framework for processing signals on graph-structured data, which is common in various applications such as sensor networks, traffic forecasting, and recommendation systems. Our approach leverages the strengths of both variational inference and GNNs to learn effective representations of signals and capture complex relationships between nodes in the graph. We employ a variational autoencoder (VAE) framework to model the signal distribution, and a GNN to learn the graph topology and node relationships. The results show that our model outperforms existing methods in terms of signal reconstruction and prediction accuracy. The key contributions of this work include the development of a novel variational-GNN framework, which enables efficient and accurate signal processing on graph-structured data. Our approach has significant implications for various applications, including signal processing, graph analysis, and machine learning. Key keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Variational Autoencoders, Signal Processing, Graph-Structured Data.

Kết quả cho thấy vi khuẩn này có khả năng phân giải lân khó tan một cách hiệu quả, giúp giảm thiểu lượng chất thải và tạo ra sản phẩm hữu ích. Quá trình lên men chất thải là một phương pháp phổ biến để xử lý chất thải hữu cơ, nhưng nó cũng có thể tạo ra lượng lân khó tan. Lân khó tan là một loại chất thải có thể gây hại cho môi trường nếu không được xử lý đúng cách. Vì vậy, việc tìm kiếm phương pháp phân giải lân khó tan trở thành một vấn đề quan trọng. Vi khuẩn Bacillus được chọn để nghiên cứu vì chúng có khả năng phân giải lân khó tan một cách hiệu quả. Quá trình nghiên cứu cho thấy vi khuẩn này có thể phân giải lân khó tan thành các sản phẩm hữu ích như axit amin và các hợp chất hữu cơ khác. Đồng thời, nó cũng mở ra hướng nghiên cứu mới về việc sử dụng vi khuẩn để phân giải lân khó tan trong quá trình lên men chất thải.

Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy rằng Việt Nam đã đạt được sự hội nhập tài chính đáng kể, đặc biệt là trong lĩnh vực đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài và giao dịch chứng khoán. Sự hội nhập này đã mang lại nhiều lợi ích cho nền kinh tế Việt Nam, bao gồm tăng cường dòng vốn, cải thiện hiệu quả sản xuất và tăng trưởng kinh tế. Tuy nhiên, nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng vẫn còn nhiều thách thức cần được giải quyết để tăng cường sự hội nhập tài chính của Việt Nam. Các thách thức này bao gồm việc cải thiện hệ thống pháp luật, tăng cường minh bạch và bảo mật trong giao dịch tài chính, và phát triển các công cụ và công nghệ hỗ trợ cho quá trình hội nhập. Kết quả nghiên cứu này sẽ có giá trị cho các nhà hoạch định chính sách và các nhà đầu tư trong việc đánh giá và phát triển chiến lược hội nhập tài chính của Việt Nam.

This paper explores the concept of Third-Person Imitation Learning, a novel approach to learning from demonstrations where an agent learns to perform tasks by observing another agent's behavior. The objective is to develop a framework that enables efficient and effective learning in complex environments. Our method utilizes a combination of reinforcement learning and imitation learning techniques, allowing the agent to learn from both its own experiences and the observed behaviors of others. We evaluate our approach on a range of tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in learning speed and accuracy compared to traditional first-person imitation learning methods. The results show that our third-person imitation learning framework can learn complex behaviors and adapt to new situations, making it a promising approach for real-world applications such as robotics and autonomous systems. Key contributions include the introduction of a new perspective on imitation learning, the development of a scalable and efficient learning algorithm, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in various domains. Relevant keywords: imitation learning, reinforcement learning, third-person perspective, robotics, autonomous systems.

Contrastive representation learning aims to learn effective feature representations by maximizing the agreement between different views of the same data. However, directly maximizing mutual information (MI) between these views can lead to trivial solutions. To address this, we propose a novel approach, Decomposed Mutual Information Estimation (DeMI), which decomposes the overall MI into a set of more manageable, lower-dimensional MI components. This decomposition enables a more nuanced and stable estimation process. Our method employs a neural network architecture to estimate these decomposed MI components and guide the learning of feature representations. We evaluate DeMI on several benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, STL-10, and ImageNet, demonstrating significant improvements in downstream classification accuracy compared to existing contrastive learning methods. The results indicate that DeMI effectively prevents mode collapse and learns more robust and generalizable representations. Our key contributions lie in the MI decomposition strategy and its application to contrastive learning, offering a new perspective on information-theoretic representation learning. Keywords: Contrastive Learning, Mutual Information, Representation Learning, Deep Learning, Information Theory.

Time series classification (TSC) is a critical task in various domains, including finance, healthcare, and environmental monitoring, where accurate predictions depend on identifying patterns in sequential data. This paper explores the application of deep learning techniques to improve the performance and scalability of TSC. We propose a novel deep neural network architecture that integrates convolutional layers for feature extraction and recurrent layers for capturing temporal dependencies. The model is trained and evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior classification accuracy compared to traditional machine learning approaches and state-of-the-art methods. Our results highlight the effectiveness of combining spatial and temporal feature learning in handling complex time series data. The proposed approach achieves an average accuracy improvement of 5-10% across datasets, with significant reductions in computational complexity. This research contributes to advancing TSC by providing a robust, scalable solution that can be applied to real-world scenarios. Key implications include enhanced predictive capabilities for applications such as anomaly detection, forecasting, and decision support systems. Keywords: time series classification, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, temporal data analysis.

In recent years, the rise of machine learning and deep neural networks has heightened the focus on adversarial attacks, which pose significant threats to the security and reliability of AI systems. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive survey on universal adversarial attacks, examining their methodologies, effectiveness, and implications across various applications. We categorize existing attack strategies, highlighting techniques that generate perturbations applicable to multiple inputs, thus ensuring broad efficacy. Our analysis encompasses a wide range of experimental results showcasing the performance of these attacks in comparison to traditional localized methods. The findings reveal that universal adversarial attacks maintain a high success rate while requiring minimal computational resources, demonstrating their potential to exploit real-world vulnerabilities in AI models. We conclude by discussing the broader implications for cybersecurity and machine learning robustness, urging the need for enhanced defense mechanisms to mitigate these threats. This survey not only clarifies the current landscape of universal adversarial attacks but also sets the stage for future research in developing resilient AI systems. Keywords: adversarial attacks, universal attacks, machine learning security, deep learning, cybersecurity.

Tình trạng xơ hóa gan và nhiễm mỡ gan là những biến chứng nghiêm trọng thường gặp ở bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ không do rượu (NAFLD). NAFLD là một trong những bệnh lý gan phổ biến nhất hiện nay, đặc biệt ở những người có chỉ số khối cơ thể (BMI) cao. Khi lượng mỡ tích tụ quá mức trong gan, nó có thể dẫn đến viêm gan, xơ hóa và thậm chí là xơ gan nếu không được điều trị kịp thời. Xơ hóa gan là quá trình hình thành mô sẹo thay thế các tế bào gan khỏe mạnh, làm suy giảm chức năng gan. Các yếu tố nguy cơ bao gồm béo phì, tiểu đường, rối loạn lipid máu và lối sống ít vận động. Việc chẩn đoán sớm và can thiệp kịp thời thông qua thay đổi lối sống, giảm cân và điều trị y tế là chìa khóa để ngăn ngừa tiến triển của bệnh.

Công nghệ này tận dụng tín hiệu truyền hình số mặt đất (DVB-T) làm nguồn phát, giúp giảm chi phí và tăng tính linh hoạt so với radar chủ động truyền thống. Mục tiêu của nghiên cứu này là đánh giá và dự đoán chính xác lượng khí nhà kính được phát thải ra môi trường từ quá trình xử lý nước thải. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy rằng hệ thống xử lý nước thải sinh hoạt có thể phát thải khí nhà kính như CO2, CH4 và N2O. Các yếu tố như loại công nghệ xử lý, quy mô hệ thống và điều kiện môi trường có ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến lượng khí nhà kính được phát thải. Mô hình số được thiết lập dựa trên các phương trình hóa học và vật lý để mô tả quá trình xử lý nước thải và phát thải khí nhà kính. Kết quả tính toán của mô hình số cho thấy rằng lượng khí nhà kính được phát thải từ hệ thống xử lý nước thải sinh hoạt có thể giảm đáng kể khi áp dụng các công nghệ xử lý tiên tiến và hiệu quả. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp thông tin quan trọng cho các nhà quản lý và kỹ sư trong việc thiết kế và vận hành hệ thống xử lý nước thải sinh hoạt một cách hiệu quả và thân thiện với môi trường.

This paper explores novel learning methodologies for implicit generative models (IGMs), which offer flexible alternatives to explicit density estimation but pose challenges in parameter optimization. We introduce a variational approach that leverages adversarial training to approximate the intractable posterior distribution inherent in IGMs. Our method, Variational Implicit Generative Learning (VIGL), combines a variational autoencoder framework with a discriminator network to guide the generator towards regions of high data likelihood. VIGL overcomes limitations of traditional GAN-based training by providing a more stable and theoretically grounded learning objective. We demonstrate the efficacy of VIGL on several benchmark datasets, showing improvements in sample quality and mode coverage compared to existing IGM training techniques, including GANs and adversarial autoencoders. Empirical results indicate that VIGL achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Kernel Inception Distance (KID). This work offers a new perspective on learning in IGMs and provides a practical algorithm for generating high-quality samples from complex data distributions. Keywords: Implicit Generative Models, Variational Inference, Adversarial Training, GANs, Generative Models, Machine Learning.

Bên cạnh đó, việc áp dụng các biện pháp quản lý đàn khoa học, nâng cao năng suất sữa cũng góp phần giảm phát thải trên mỗi đơn vị sản phẩm. Việc triển khai đồng bộ các giải pháp này không chỉ giúp giảm phát thải khí nhà kính mà còn nâng cao hiệu quả kinh tế cho người chăn nuôi và hướng tới phát triển bền vững.

This paper addresses the correspondence problem on point sets, a fundamental challenge in computer vision and machine learning, by introducing a novel quantum computational approach. The objective is to efficiently establish correspondences between two point sets, enabling applications such as 3D reconstruction, object recognition, and tracking. Our method leverages the power of quantum computing to develop a quantum algorithm that solves the correspondence problem by representing point sets as quantum states and utilizing quantum parallelism to explore the solution space. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in computational efficiency and accuracy compared to classical methods, particularly for large-scale point sets. Key findings include the development of a quantum circuit architecture for point set representation and a quantum-inspired optimization technique for correspondence estimation. The implications of this research are substantial, enabling faster and more accurate solutions for correspondence problems, with potential applications in fields such as robotics, computer vision, and artificial intelligence. Keywords: quantum computing, correspondence problem, point sets, computer vision, machine learning, 3D reconstruction.

This paper addresses the challenge of semantic colorization in digital images, focusing on the accurate and context-aware assignment of colors to grayscale or pixelated inputs. The objective is to develop a robust framework that leverages semantic understanding to produce realistic and visually coherent colorized outputs. To achieve this, we propose a novel deep learning-based approach that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with semantic segmentation techniques. Our method utilizes a multi-stage pipeline, where semantic labels are first predicted to guide the colorization process, ensuring that colors are applied in a contextually meaningful manner. The model is trained on a diverse dataset of annotated images, enabling it to generalize across various domains and scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in colorization accuracy and visual quality compared to existing methods, particularly in complex scenes with multiple objects and textures. The proposed approach also exhibits enhanced robustness to pixelation artifacts, making it suitable for applications in image restoration and enhancement. This research contributes to the field of computer vision by introducing a semantically aware colorization framework that bridges the gap between low-level pixel manipulation and high-level contextual understanding. Potential applications include digital art, historical image restoration, and automated image processing pipelines. **Keywords**: semantic colorization, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, image restoration, semantic segmentation, pixelation.

Bệnh ngủ rũ tuýp 1 là hội chứng rối loạn thần kinh ảnh hưởng nghiêm trọng đến việc kiểm soát giấc ngủ, gây ra bởi sự suy giảm số lượng tế bào thần kinh tiết Orexin. Mặc dù có ý nghĩa quan trọng đối với khoa học và đời sống, các nghiên cứu về bệnh thần kinh nói chung và bệnh ngủ rũ nói riêng vẫn bị hạn chế bởi việc không thể tiếp cận nguồn mẫu từ não bộ người cũng như khó khăn trong việc nuôi cấy các dòng tế bào thần kinh. Với mục đích khắc phục rào cản này, chúng tôi tiến hành tạo tế bào thần kinh tiết Orexin-A từ tế bào gốc vạn năng cảm ứng (hiPSCs), sử dụng môi trường biệt hóa có bổ sung N-acetyl-D-mannosamine (ManNAc) và Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4). Chúng tôi đánh giá đặc tính các tế bào biệt hóa được bằng phương pháp nhuộm miễn dịch huỳnh quang, phản ứng real-time PCR và kỹ thuật ELISA cạnh tranh. Kết quả cho thấy, nghiên cứu đã tạo thành công dòng hiPSC mang những đặc trưng của tế bào gốc vạn năng. Tế bào thần kinh tiết Orexin-A tạo thành từ hiPSCs đã cho kết quả biểu hiện dương tính với NCAM1 và TUBB3, tăng biểu hiện gen hypocretin (HCRT) và có khả năng tiết Orexin-A. Dựa trên tiền đề này, tế bào thần kinh tiết Orexin-A được tạo ra sẽ là cơ sở cho việc xây dựng mô hình bệnh trên tế bào và các nghiên cứu sâu hơn về cơ chế các bệnh thần kinh liên quan.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning stochastic transition models in complex systems, a critical task for applications such as reinforcement learning, robotics, and decision-making under uncertainty. We propose a novel approach to approximate stochastic transition models using a combination of deep neural networks and probabilistic graphical models. Our method leverages structured representations to capture dependencies between system states and actions, enabling efficient learning of transition dynamics even in high-dimensional spaces. The proposed framework is evaluated on benchmark environments and real-world datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. Results indicate that our approach achieves a 15% improvement in model fidelity and reduces training time by 20% on average. The implications of this work extend to domains requiring robust decision-making under uncertainty, such as autonomous systems and dynamic resource allocation. This research contributes a scalable and interpretable solution for learning stochastic transition models, offering a significant step forward in modeling complex systems with uncertain dynamics. **Keywords**: stochastic transition models, deep learning, probabilistic graphical models, reinforcement learning, decision-making under uncertainty.

Cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán (DWI) là một kỹ thuật hình ảnh y học đầy hứa hẹn trong việc phân biệt giữa các khối u mô mềm cơ xương khớp lành tính và ác tính. DWI đo lường sự khuếch tán của các phân tử nước trong mô, từ đó cung cấp thông tin về cấu trúc tế bào và vi môi trường của khối u. Mặc dù DWI có tiềm năng cải thiện độ chính xác trong chẩn đoán phân biệt u mô mềm, nhưng vẫn cần nghiên cứu thêm để chuẩn hóa các giao thức và xác định các ngưỡng ADC tối ưu cho các loại khối u khác nhau.

The research addresses the challenge of extracting meaningful and discriminative features from medical images without requiring labeled data. This work focuses on enhancing the understanding and analysis of complex medical imagery through unsupervised learning, aiming to contribute to more efficient and scalable diagnostic tools. Methods/Approach: We present a novel unsupervised learning framework designed to learn local discriminative representations from medical images. The proposed approach leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and integrates contrastive learning to maximize the separation between image sub-regions. By transforming image structures into a latent space where similar patterns are clustered and distinct patterns are separated, our model builds a robust representation without the dependence on pre-existing image annotations. Results/Findings: Our experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that the model successfully discovers and isolates key diagnostic features, surpassing traditional unsupervised methods in both accuracy and efficiency. The approach achieves prominent performance gains in comparison with existing baseline models, particularly in scenarios where labeled data is scarce or completely unavailable. Moreover, the learned representations prove beneficial when transferred to downstream tasks such as image classification and anomaly detection. Conclusion/Implications: The study introduces a powerful unsupervised methodology for the discriminative analysis of medical images, offering significant advancements in the field of medical image processing. This unsupervised framework has the potential to be a game-changer in clinical settings, facilitating automated diagnosis and paving the way for healthcare systems with minimal human intervention. The insights gained from this work could significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of medical diagnostics, especially in resource-constrained environments. Keywords: unsupervised learning, medical images, local discriminative representation, convolutional neural networks, contrastive learning, feature extraction, image classification, anomaly detection.

This paper addresses the challenge of designing robust control systems by introducing a novel approach that combines alternating optimisation and quadrature techniques. The results show that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of robustness and computational efficiency, with key findings including significant reductions in control effort and improved disturbance rejection. The conclusion highlights the importance of this research in enabling the design of robust control systems for a wide range of applications, including process control, robotics, and autonomous systems. The novelty of our approach lies in its ability to balance exploration and exploitation in the optimisation process, making it a valuable contribution to the field of control systems. Key keywords: robust control, alternating optimisation, quadrature, uncertainty, non-linearity, control systems.

Abstract In the rapidly evolving field of logistics, efficient inventory management is crucial for minimizing costs and enhancing operational efficiency. Traditional methods of inventory rotation often lead to stock inefficiencies and increased waste, which are exacerbated in high-volume warehousing environments. This thesis addresses the need for a more systematic approach to inventory rotation through the implementation of Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology. The research aims to develop a comprehensive automated inventory system that enhances the accuracy of stock management, optimizes space utilization, and minimizes the risk of stock obsolescence. The primary objectives of this thesis include the design and implementation of an RFID-based inventory rotation system, which specifically targets issues related to manual tracking errors, retrieval inefficiencies, and inventory turnover rates. The methodology involves the integration of RFID tags, a centralized database, and a user-friendly interface that facilitates real-time tracking and management of inventory. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in inventory turnover rates and a reduction in stock discrepancies, ultimately leading to enhanced operational efficiency within logistics warehouses. Furthermore, this research contributes to the field by providing a scalable model for RFID automation in inventory management, offering practical insights for industry professionals seeking to streamline their warehousing processes. In conclusion, this thesis highlights the significance of adopting modern technologies such as RFID in inventory rotation practices. The findings pave the way for future studies to explore advanced analytics and machine learning integration, ultimately aiming to further optimize inventory strategies in logistics operations.

In the rapidly evolving landscape of adversarial machine learning, the challenge of creating robust and transparent attack methodologies remains critical. This paper addresses two key limitations in adversarial patch attacks: distributional shift and obtrusiveness. While existing patch-based attacks often fail to generalize across diverse datasets or require highly conspicuous modifications, we propose a novel framework that enhances both effectiveness and transparency. Our approach leverages adaptive patch generation techniques, integrating domain adaptation principles to mitigate distributional shifts, while employing perceptual loss functions to minimize visual obtrusiveness. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, we demonstrate that our method achieves superior attack success rates across varying data distributions, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches by up to 15%. Additionally, qualitative evaluations confirm that the generated patches are significantly less detectable by human observers, striking a balance between stealth and efficacy. The implications of this work extend to improving the robustness of machine learning models against real-world adversarial threats, while also raising awareness of the need for transparent and adaptive defense mechanisms. This research contributes to the broader discourse on trustworthy AI by addressing critical vulnerabilities in a manner that prioritizes both performance and practicality. **Keywords**: adversarial attacks, patch attacks, distributional shift, obtrusiveness, transparent AI, domain adaptation, perceptual loss.

This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing teaching strategies by proposing a learner-aware framework that leverages inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) integrated with explicit modeling of learner preferences and constraints. Traditional IRL techniques typically focus on recovering reward functions from observed behaviors, but often neglect individual differences in learner goals, prior knowledge, and practical limitations such as time or cognitive resources. Our approach formulates teaching as a collaborative process, where the teacher adapts instructions and demonstrations by inferring not only the underlying reward structure but also the unique preferences and constraints of each learner. We introduce a novel algorithm that jointly estimates learner-specific reward functions and constraint sets from limited interaction data. Experimental results across synthetic and real-world teaching scenarios demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms standard IRL-based teaching paradigms, yielding faster and more effective learner adaptation. The findings highlight the importance of personalized teaching and provide a foundation for intelligent tutoring systems that dynamically tailor content based on inferred learner profiles. Keywords: inverse reinforcement learning, learner modeling, teaching strategies, personalized education, preference learning, constraint-aware AI.

This paper proposes a novel approach for moving object detection by identifying contiguous outliers in low-rank representations. The objective is to effectively separate moving objects from the background in video sequences. Our method utilizes a robust low-rank matrix decomposition technique to model the background, and then detects moving objects by identifying contiguous outliers that do not fit the low-rank representation. The approach is validated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting moving objects in various scenarios. Experimental results show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness. The key contributions of this research include a new framework for moving object detection, improved handling of complex backgrounds, and enhanced robustness to noise and occlusions. This work has significant implications for applications such as surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and robotics, where accurate moving object detection is crucial. Key keywords: moving object detection, low-rank representation, robust matrix decomposition, computer vision, video analysis.

**Abstract** The rapid expansion of e-commerce platforms has intensified the demand for effective automated product question answering (QA) systems. This paper addresses the challenge by proposing a distantly supervised approach that leverages transformer-based models for e-commerce product QA, aiming to provide accurate and context-aware responses to user queries. Our method utilizes large-scale, weakly annotated data sourced from product descriptions, customer reviews, and previously answered questions, reducing reliance on expensive manually labeled datasets. We employ a pre-trained transformer model, further fine-tuned with distantly supervised signals, to capture nuanced semantic similarities between queries and product information. Through comprehensive experiments on a benchmark e-commerce QA dataset, our approach demonstrates significant improvements in answer relevance and precision compared to baseline models relying exclusively on labeled data or traditional information retrieval techniques. The results indicate that distantly supervised transformers can effectively generalize across diverse product categories and question types, offering scalable solutions for real-world e-commerce applications. This research contributes a novel framework for integrating distant supervision with transformer architectures, highlighting its practicality for large-scale, dynamic QA environments. Keywords: e-commerce, question answering, transformers, distant supervision, natural language processing, product information retrieval.

This paper presents a novel approach to continuous action reinforcement learning, leveraging a mixture of interpretable experts to improve learning efficiency and effectiveness. The objective is to develop an agent that can learn complex policies by combining the strengths of multiple specialized experts, each capturing distinct aspects of the environment. Our method employs a hierarchical framework, where a high-level controller selects and combines the outputs of a set of interpretable experts, allowing for flexible and adaptive decision-making. The experts are designed to be interpretable, enabling insights into the decision-making process and facilitating the incorporation of domain knowledge. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in several continuous control tasks, achieving improved sample efficiency and asymptotic performance. The key contributions of this work include the introduction of a novel expert mixture framework, the development of interpretable expert models, and the demonstration of significant performance gains in continuous action reinforcement learning. Our approach has potential applications in areas such as robotics, autonomous driving, and healthcare, where continuous action reinforcement learning can be used to improve decision-making and control. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, continuous action, interpretable experts, hierarchical control, decision-making.

Unsupervised domain adaptive object detection aims to adapt detectors from a labelled source domain to an unlabelled target domain. Most existing works take a two-stage strategy that first generates region proposals and then detects objects of interest, where adversarial learning is widely adopted to mitigate the inter-domain discrepancy in both stages. However, adversarial learning may impair the alignment of well-aligned samples as it merely aligns the global distributions across domains. To address this issue, we design an uncertainty-aware domain adaptation network (UaDAN) that introduces conditional adversarial learning to align well-aligned and poorly-aligned samples separately in different manners. Specifically, we design an uncertainty metric that assesses the alignment of each sample and adjusts the strength of adversarial learning for well-aligned and poorly-aligned samples adaptively. In addition, we exploit the uncertainty metric to achieve curriculum learning that first performs easier image-level alignment and then more difficult instance-level alignment progressively. Extensive experiments over four challenging domain adaptive object detection datasets show that UaDAN achieves superior performance as compared with state-of-the-art methods.

The research addresses the challenge of natural image matting, which involves accurately separating the foreground from the background in complex imagery. This task is essential for various applications in graphic design, augmented reality, and image editing. Methods/Approach: This study introduces a novel deep learning framework for automatic natural image matting. Leveraging advances in convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the proposed method integrates end-to-end learning mechanisms to predict alpha mattes directly from input images. Utilizing a multi-scale approach, the model captures intricate details and utilizes contextual information to improve matting accuracy. Results/Findings: The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deep automatic matting approach achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. Evaluations on standard benchmark datasets reveal significant improvements in the accuracy of foreground extraction, particularly in challenging scenarios involving fine structures and varying opacities. The system's robustness and computational efficiency make it suitable for real-time applications. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a potent solution to the field of image matting, pushing the boundaries of automation and precision. The deep learning system's ability to deliver high-quality mattes without manual input advances the possibilities for seamless integration into creative tools and real-time processing environments. Future work could explore further enhancements through data augmentation techniques and GAN-based architectures. Keywords: natural image matting, deep learning, CNN, alpha matte, image editing, real-time processing.

This paper addresses the challenge of partitioning data points into meaningful clusters by introducing a novel large-margin metric learning approach. Our method aims to learn a distance metric that maximizes the margin between different clusters while minimizing the intra-cluster variance, leading to improved partitioning accuracy. We formulate the metric learning problem as a semidefinite program with constraints that enforce large margins between clusters. We propose an efficient optimization algorithm based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to solve the resulting optimization problem. Empirical evaluation on several benchmark datasets demonstrates that our large-margin metric learning approach outperforms state-of-the-art metric learning methods and clustering algorithms in terms of clustering accuracy and normalized mutual information. The proposed method offers a robust and effective solution for various partitioning problems, including image segmentation and document clustering, by learning a discriminative distance metric that enhances cluster separability. **Keywords:** Metric learning, clustering, partitioning, large margin, semidefinite programming, ADMM.

Giá thể gốm kỹ thuật và phân chậm tan đang được nghiên cứu và ứng dụng trong việc trồng cây rau húng bạc hà (Mentha arvensis L.), mang lại hiệu quả cao trong canh tác nông nghiệp. Giá thể gốm kỹ thuật, với khả năng giữ ẩm và thoáng khí tốt, giúp cây phát triển bộ rễ khỏe mạnh, đồng thời cải thiện chất lượng đất trồng. Phân chậm tan, với cơ chế giải phóng dinh dưỡng từ từ, đảm bảo cây hấp thụ đủ chất dinh dưỡng trong thời gian dài, giảm thiểu việc bón phân nhiều lần. Kết hợp hai yếu tố này không chỉ nâng cao năng suất cây trồng mà còn góp phần bảo vệ môi trường, hạn chế ô nhiễm do dư thừa phân bón. Đây là hướng đi tiềm năng trong nông nghiệp bền vững, đặc biệt phù hợp với các loại cây gia vị như húng bạc hà.

Sau khi thực hiện rất nhiều thí nghiệm với dữ liệu nhân tạo, em thấy rằng để có thể cải thiện độ chính xác lên trên 90% là rất khó. Điều này nguyên nhân có thể do gia hạn học của mô hình hoặc do dữ liệu chưa đủ tốt gây ra. Để gả quyết gả thiết thứ nhất thì em sẽ phải tìm và nghiên cứu những mô hình mờ hơn, hiện đại hơn mô hình đang sử dụng hiện tại. Ngoài ra điểm tiện đánh giá và các kết quả đã thực hiện trước đây, em vẫn sử dụng mạng backbone là resnet 31. Để có thể cải thiện độ chính xác thì em có thể thử sử dụng những kiến trúc mạng backbone sâu hơn, nặng hơn điểm thử nghiệm. Còn đối với giả thiết thứ hai, em nghĩ chúng ta có thể tìm hiểu thêm những phương pháp sinh dữ liệu sử dụng mô hình sinh khác. Hiện tại những mô hình sinh như mô hình diffusion đang đạt được kết quả SOTA trên những tác vụ liên quan đến hình ảnh nên nếu có thờ gan thì em sẽ thử thêm những phương pháp đo điểm đưa vào trong đánh giá. Liên kết giữa hộ nông dân và doanh nghiệp trong sản xuất và tiêu thụ cà phê ở Tây Nguyên đang trở thành một yếu tố quan trọng trong việc nâng cao giá trị sản phẩm và phát triển bền vững. Khu vực Tây Nguyên, với điều kiện khí hậu và đất đai thuận lợi, là nơi sản xuất cà phê chủ lực của Việt Nam. Tuy nhiên, để tối ưu hóa quy trình sản xuất và tiêu thụ, việc thiết lập mối quan hệ chặt chẽ giữa nông dân và doanh nghiệp là cần thiết. Các doanh nghiệp có thể cung cấp kỹ thuật, giống cây trồng chất lượng và hỗ trợ tài chính, trong khi nông dân đảm bảo nguồn nguyên liệu ổn định và chất lượng. Sự hợp tác này không chỉ giúp nâng cao năng suất và chất lượng cà phê mà còn tạo ra những sản phẩm có giá trị gia tăng, đáp ứng nhu cầu thị trường trong và ngoài nước. Việc phát triển mô hình liên kết này sẽ góp phần thúc đẩy kinh tế địa phương và cải thiện đời sống của người nông dân.

Understanding the complex dynamics of neural activity is essential for advancements in neuroscience and the development of brain-inspired computational models. This paper addresses the challenge of perceiving neuron point processes in the presence of "unknown unknowns"—latent factors or unexpected variability not captured by standard models. We propose a novel data-driven framework that leverages advanced machine learning techniques to analyze and interpret spike train data, enabling robust detection and representation of neuronal events even in the presence of unmodeled uncertainties. Our method utilizes a hybrid approach combining unsupervised learning for anomaly identification with deep generative models to uncover hidden patterns in neuronal firing. Experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world neural datasets demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and resilience compared to traditional point process analysis methods, particularly when faced with previously uncharacterized disturbances or data noise. These findings suggest that our approach can enhance the reliability of neural signal interpretation and facilitate new insights in computational neuroscience. The work underscores the importance of data-driven perception, anomaly detection, and model adaptability in handling the complex, noisy, and often incomplete nature of neural recordings. Keywords: neuron point processes, data-driven analysis, unknown unknowns, spike train, machine learning, anomaly detection, computational neuroscience.

This paper explores the development of an adaptive teaching system that leverages student feedback to enhance the learning experience. The objective is to create a personalized education framework that adjusts its teaching strategies based on real-time student input. Our approach utilizes machine learning algorithms to analyze student feedback, identifying areas of improvement and optimizing the teaching methodology accordingly. The system integrates natural language processing to interpret and categorize student responses, enabling the adaptation of instructional materials and delivery methods. Results show significant improvements in student engagement and knowledge retention, with the adaptive system outperforming traditional teaching methods in comparative studies. The findings of this research contribute to the development of more effective and responsive educational technologies, highlighting the potential of student-centered feedback mechanisms to revolutionize the way we teach and learn. Key contributions include the design of a novel feedback-driven teaching framework and the demonstration of its efficacy in enhancing student outcomes, with implications for the broader adoption of adaptive learning systems in education.

This paper investigates the spectral properties of latent representations in deep learning models, aiming to uncover insights into their structural and functional characteristics. The objective is to analyze how latent spaces encode information and how their spectral decomposition can reveal underlying patterns relevant to model performance. We propose a novel approach that leverages spectral analysis techniques, including eigenvalue decomposition and Fourier transforms, to examine the latent representations generated by various neural network architectures. Our experiments focus on comparing the spectral signatures of latent spaces across different tasks, such as image classification and natural language processing, and explore their correlation with model generalization and robustness. Results demonstrate that latent representations exhibit distinct spectral patterns, which can be used to identify overfitting, improve model interpretability, and guide the design of more efficient architectures. The findings highlight the potential of spectral analysis as a tool for understanding and optimizing deep learning models, with implications for applications in computer vision, NLP, and beyond. Keywords: latent representations, spectral analysis, deep learning, eigenvalue decomposition, model interpretability.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc đánh giá các đặc điểm nông học và xác định gen mẫn cảm nhiệt độ của một số dòng giống cây trồng biến đổi gen (TGMS). This paper addresses the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning methods by introducing a novel algorithm, Greedy-GQ with Variance Reduction, aimed at improving the efficiency and effectiveness of policy evaluation in reinforcement learning environments. Methods/Approach: The proposed method leverages variance reduction techniques to enhance the Greedy-GQ algorithm, a widely recognized off-policy temporal-difference learning approach. The variance reduction is achieved through a carefully designed update rule that balances between bias and variance, leading to more stable and efficient learning. The finite-time analysis of the algorithm provides theoretical guarantees for the convergence and performance metrics, offering insights into its operational complexity. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the Greedy-GQ with Variance Reduction significantly outperforms traditional Greedy-GQ and other baseline methods in terms of convergence speed and accuracy. The variance reduction strategy effectively reduces the complexity of the learning process, yielding faster convergence in finite-time scenarios across various reinforcement learning tasks. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field by offering an advanced reinforcement learning approach that combines variance reduction techniques with established algorithms, resulting in improved learning performance and reduced computational demands. The Greedy-GQ with Variance Reduction is poised to offer practical benefits in real-world applications where efficient policy evaluation and decision-making are critical. Keywords: Greedy-GQ, variance reduction, finite-time analysis, reinforcement learning, policy evaluation, algorithm complexity.

Nghiên cứu về hành vi che giấu kiến thức của nhân viên ngân hàng tại Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh chỉ ra nhiều yếu tố tác động đáng kể. Môi trường làm việc độc hại, thiếu tin tưởng giữa các đồng nghiệp, và cảm giác bất công trong tổ chức là những nguyên nhân chính dẫn đến việc nhân viên cố tình giữ kín thông tin. Bên cạnh đó, áp lực công việc quá lớn, sự cạnh tranh không lành mạnh, và nỗi sợ bị đánh giá thấp cũng thúc đẩy hành vi này. Che giấu kiến thức gây ảnh hưởng tiêu cực đến hiệu quả hoạt động, khả năng đổi mới và sự gắn kết của nhân viên với ngân hàng. Do đó, các ngân hàng cần xây dựng văn hóa doanh nghiệp lành mạnh, tăng cường sự tin tưởng, đảm bảo công bằng trong đãi ngộ, và giảm áp lực công việc để hạn chế hành vi tiêu cực này, từ đó nâng cao năng lực cạnh tranh và phát triển bền vững.

In recent years, the task of segmenting foreground objects from background in a video, i.e. video object segmentation (VOS), has received considerable attention. In this paper, we propose a single end-to-end trainable deep neural network, convolutional gated recurrent Mask-RCNN, for tackling the semi-supervised VOS task. We take advantage of both the instance segmentation network (Mask-RCNN) and the visual memory module (Conv-GRU) to tackle the VOS task. The instance segmentation network predicts masks for instances, while the visual memory module learns to selectively propagate information for multiple instances simultaneously, which handles the appearance change, the variation of scale and pose and the occlusions between objects. After offline and online training under purely instance segmentation losses, our approach is able to achieve satisfactory results without any post-processing or synthetic video data augmentation. Experimental results on DAVIS 2016 dataset and DAVIS 2017 dataset have demonstrated the effectiveness of our method for video object segmentation task.

The purpose of this study is to investigate the impact of individual rater style on the uncertainty associated with deep learning models used for medical imaging segmentation. In medical imaging, accurate segmentation is critical for diagnostics and treatment planning, yet the inherent variability in manual annotations poses significant challenges in training robust and reliable models. Our approach involves analyzing the segmentation performance of deep learning models trained on datasets annotated by different raters, while quantifying the uncertainty using advanced uncertainty estimation techniques. We employed methods such as Monte Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensembles to capture both predictive uncertainty and model variance, revealing how individual rater styles contribute to the overall uncertainty in segmentation outcomes. Results demonstrate a notable variation in model performance based on rater-dependent annotations, highlighting the variability and potential biases introduced by individual rater styles. The findings underscore the importance of considering rater variability when developing and deploying deep learning models in medical imaging. Our work contributes to the field by providing insights into the critical relationship between manual annotation styles and deep learning model uncertainty, ultimately guiding improvements in model robustness. This research has profound implications for enhancing the accuracy and reliability of medical image segmentation, potentially leading to improved clinical decision-making and patient care. Key keywords include medical imaging, deep learning, uncertainty estimation, segmentation, and model robustness.

This paper introduces FIERY, a novel approach to predict future instances in bird's-eye view from surround monocular cameras. The objective is to forecast the trajectory of objects, such as pedestrians, cars, and cyclists, in a 3D environment, enabling enhanced autonomous driving capabilities. Our method leverages a combination of computer vision and machine learning techniques, utilizing a surround-view camera system to capture a 360-degree view of the environment. We propose a deep learning architecture that predicts future instances by learning spatial and temporal relationships between objects. The results show significant improvements in prediction accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods. Electrocardiogram (ECG) arrhythmia classification systems play a crucial role in automated diagnosis. However, the robustness of these systems against adversarial attacks remains largely unexplored. This paper investigates the vulnerability of ECG arrhythmia classifiers to adversarial examples by introducing ECGadv, a novel method for generating adversarial ECG signals. ECGadv leverages a generative adversarial network (GAN) to create imperceptible perturbations that, when added to genuine ECG signals, cause misclassification by state-of-the-art arrhythmia classification models. We demonstrate that ECGadv can successfully mislead deep learning-based classifiers with high success rates while maintaining clinically plausible ECG morphology, validated through expert physician review. Our findings reveal a significant security risk in current ECG analysis systems, highlighting the need for robust algorithm design and defenses against adversarial attacks in critical healthcare applications. This work contributes a practical method for evaluating and improving the security of ECG-based diagnostic tools. Keywords: ECG, adversarial attack, arrhythmia classification, deep learning, GAN, security, healthcare.

Pedestrian trajectory prediction is a critical component in the development of autonomous vehicles, intelligent surveillance systems, and crowd analysis applications. However, accurately forecasting human movement in dynamic and complex environments remains challenging due to the influence of contextual factors such as surrounding pedestrians, static obstacles, and environmental semantics. This paper presents a novel approach to pedestrian trajectory prediction by leveraging Context-Augmented Transformer Networks (CATN). The proposed model integrates transformer-based self-attention mechanisms with augmented contextual encodings, effectively capturing both spatial and temporal dependencies alongside rich environmental cues. Extensive experiments were conducted on benchmark trajectory datasets, demonstrating that our method outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness, particularly in highly interactive scenarios. The results show substantial improvements in trajectory consistency and adaptability to varying scene contexts. This research highlights the effectiveness of incorporating contextual information within transformer architectures, offering substantial advancements for real-world applications in autonomous navigation, crowd safety, and urban planning. Keywords: pedestrian trajectory prediction, transformer networks, context augmentation, autonomous vehicles, trajectory forecasting, intelligent surveillance.

This paper introduces MeInGame, a novel approach to generating a 3D game character face from a single 2D portrait image. The objective is to create a realistic and personalized game character face that captures the likeness of the input portrait. Our method utilizes a deep learning-based framework, combining the strengths of generative adversarial networks (GANs) and 3D reconstruction techniques. The approach involves training a GAN model to learn the mapping between 2D portraits and 3D face models, allowing for the generation of detailed and realistic 3D faces. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of MeInGame, showing significant improvements in face reconstruction accuracy and visual fidelity compared to existing methods. The proposed system has important implications for the gaming and entertainment industries, enabling the creation of personalized and engaging game characters. Key contributions include a novel GAN-based architecture, a large-scale dataset of 2D-3D face pairs, and a user-friendly interface for game developers and players. Relevant keywords: 3D face reconstruction, GANs, game character creation, portrait-based modeling, deep learning, computer vision.

The study investigates the development of a multi-modal representation learning framework aimed at enhancing the structuring of video advertisement content. This research addresses the challenge of effectively analyzing varied data modalities such as audio, text, and visuals to improve advertising content delivery and audience engagement. Methods/Approach: The proposed model integrates deep learning techniques with multi-modal representation learning to process and comprehend diverse media elements within video advertisements. This approach involves the utilization of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image data, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for text data, and a specific attention mechanism to align and fuse information from different modalities. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that the multi-modal representation learning framework significantly outperforms traditional single-modal strategies in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The system achieved a notable improvement in content structuring, enabling more coherent and appealing advertisements. Comparative analysis against existing frameworks showed advancements in recognition and categorization tasks within video ads. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field of content structuring by offering a robust framework that leverages multi-modal data for more effective video advertisement analysis. The findings imply potential applications in targeted marketing and personalized ad experiences, driving advancements in automated video content management. The novel integration of multi-modal representation learning underlines the significance of combining auditory, textual, and visual data to encapsulate the richness of video advertising content. Keywords: Multi-modal representation learning, video advertisement, deep learning, content structuring, CNN, RNN, multi-modal data fusion.

This paper addresses the challenge of reinforcement learning in parameterized action spaces, a complex environment where actions are defined by discrete and continuous parameters. Our objective is to develop hierarchical approaches that enhance learning efficiency and performance in such intricate settings. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that decomposes the parameterized action space into manageable subspaces. This involves creating a hierarchy of policies where a high-level policy selects among discrete actions while low-level policies fine-tune continuous parameters. The approach employs deep learning techniques to integrate both components effectively, optimizing policy networks through a combination of policy gradient methods and actor-critic models. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate that the hierarchical approach significantly improves learning speed and decision-making accuracy compared to traditional non-hierarchical reinforcement learning methods. Results show superior performance across various benchmark environments, highlighting the model's capability to generalize well in multi-dimensional action spaces. The framework also provides robustness against sparse reward scenarios, often a bottleneck in parameterized environments. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of hierarchical approaches in reinforcement learning for parameterized action spaces presents a substantial advancement, offering a scalable and flexible solution for complex decision-making tasks. This research contributes to expanding the applicability of reinforcement learning in diverse areas such as robotics, automated control, and gaming. Future work could explore the integration of transfer learning techniques to further boost adaptability and efficiency in more dynamic contexts. Keywords: hierarchical reinforcement learning, parameterized action spaces, deep learning, policy gradient, actor-critic, scalability, decision-making tasks.

Virus trải qua quá trình cấy truyền liên tục để theo dõi sự thay đổi trong khả năng gây bệnh và các đặc điểm di truyền. This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing convolutional neural networks (ConvNets) by introducing a dynamic filtering mechanism that leverages a large sampling field. The aim is to improve the adaptability and accuracy of ConvNets in processing complex datasets. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel dynamic filtering approach integrated into ConvNets, characterized by an adjustable sampling field. This mechanism enables the network to dynamically select relevant features from a broader context, enhancing spatial representations within the model. The method is validated through the implementation of modified convolutional layers that utilize these adaptive filters to balance computation and performance effectively. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations on standard image recognition benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed dynamic filtering with a large sampling field significantly outperforms traditional convolutional approaches. The results show improved classification accuracy and robustness, with notable performance gains observed on complex and high-resolution datasets. Additionally, our approach is computationally efficient, achieving these improvements without a substantial increase in processing time or resource consumption. Conclusion/Implications: The research introduces a significant advancement in ConvNets by incorporating a dynamic filtering strategy that adapts to varying spatial data contexts, enhancing feature extraction capabilities. This technique holds promise for broadening the applicability of ConvNets in real-world scenarios requiring precise pattern recognition and adaptive processing. Future applications could extend to various domains, including video analysis, medical imaging, and autonomous systems where efficient high-dimensional data processing is critical. Keywords: dynamic filtering, ConvNets, large sampling field, convolutional neural networks, feature extraction, image recognition, adaptive processing.

The TLS/SSL Security Tester allows users to evaluate the security of TLS/SSL configurations in their uploaded Android applications. By analyzing the protocols used, reviewing how certificates are validated, and scrutinizing encryption practices, it helps identify vulnerabilities such as weak cipher suites, obsolete protocol versions, and improper certificate validation. Detecting these flaws is crucial, as their presence could potentially expose apps to man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks or sensitive data breaches.

Coverage path planning is a well-studied problem in robotics in which a robot must plan a path that passes through every point in a given area repeatedly, usually with a uniform frequency. To address the scenario in which some points need to be visited more frequently than others, this problem has been extended to non-uniform coverage planning. This paper considers the variant of non-uniform coverage in which the robot does not know the distribution of relevant events beforehand and must nevertheless learn to maximize the rate of detecting events of interest. This continual area sweeping problem has been previously formalized in a way that makes strong assumptions about the environment, and to date only a greedy approach has been proposed. We generalize the continual area sweeping formulation to include fewer environmental constraints, and propose a novel approach based on reinforcement learning in a Semi-Markov Decision Process. This approach is evaluated in an abstract simulation and in a high fidelity Gazebo simulation. These evaluations show significant improvement upon the existing approach in general settings, which is especially relevant in the growing area of service robotics.

Quản lý nhà nước về kinh tế xanh trong lĩnh vực xây dựng tại Việt Nam đang chịu ảnh hưởng từ nhiều yếu tố quan trọng. This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently embedding point features in 3D data processing tasks, which is critical for various applications in computer vision and graphics. Traditional methods often suffer from computational inefficiencies and limitations in handling large-scale data due to their dependence on regular data structures. We propose a novel approach to overcome these limitations by introducing an Irregularly Tabulated Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Methods/Approach: Our approach leverages an irregular tabulation strategy within the MLP framework to accelerate the point feature embedding process. By bypassing the necessity for uniform data structures, the proposed method efficiently processes and embeds features from point clouds directly, utilizing a dynamic data handling process that adapts to the intrinsic characteristics of the data. This results in a more flexible and scalable embedding technique, tailored to overcome the innate irregularity of point cloud data. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our Irregularly Tabulated MLP outperforms conventional MLP-based embedding methods, achieving superior speed and accuracy in feature extraction from point clouds. Comparative analysis shows a significant reduction in computational time, while maintaining or even enhancing the quality of the embeddings, especially in scenarios dealing with high-density data points. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of an Irregularly Tabulated MLP provides a transformative advancement in the field of 3D data processing, presenting a promising solution for fast and accurate point feature embedding. This method not only enhances performance in existing applications but also opens avenues for efficient real-time processing in emerging technologies such as autonomous driving and augmented reality, where rapid and reliable point feature analysis is paramount. Keywords: Point Feature Embedding, Irregularly Tabulated MLP, 3D Data Processing, Point Clouds, Multilayer Perceptron, Computer Vision, Real-time Processing.

This study aims to develop an innovative approach for evaluating the depth of metal surface defects using eddy current testing (ECT) combined with deep residual convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed method utilizes ECT to capture high-resolution images of metal surfaces, which are then analyzed by a deep residual CNN to predict the depth of defects. The network is trained on a comprehensive dataset of ECT images with corresponding defect depth labels, enabling it to learn complex patterns and features associated with defect depth. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy and robustness in defect depth evaluation. The use of deep residual CNNs improves upon traditional ECT analysis methods, offering enhanced sensitivity and specificity in detecting and characterizing metal surface defects. This research contributes to the development of advanced non-destructive testing (NDT) techniques, with potential applications in industries such as aerospace, automotive, and energy. Key contributions include the integration of ECT with deep learning, improved defect depth evaluation, and enhanced NDT capabilities. Relevant keywords: eddy current testing, deep residual CNNs, metal surface defects, non-destructive testing, defect depth evaluation.

Neural networks play a crucial role in modern machine learning applications, yet their optimization processes are often plagued with challenges stemming from nondeterminism and instability. This paper aims to investigate the factors contributing to these issues and to propose methods to mitigate them, ensuring more reliable and consistent training outcomes. Methods/Approach: We explore the optimization dynamics of neural networks by examining factors such as initial weight distributions, learning rate schedules, and random seed dependencies. Utilizing a combination of theoretical analysis and empirical experiments, we scrutinize the variabilities introduced during the training process. Our approach also involves comparing various optimization algorithms, including stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and its variants, with a focus on mitigating instabilities. Results/Findings: Our study reveals significant insights into how minor changes in initial conditions can drastically affect model performance. Through extensive experimentation, we demonstrate that certain adjustments to the weight initialization and learning rate strategies can substantially reduce optimization variability. Our findings are validated across multiple neural network architectures and datasets, showing improved performance stability and reduced convergence times. Conclusion/Implications: The research advances our understanding of the inherent challenges in neural network optimization related to nondeterminism and instability. By identifying key factors and proposing practical mitigation strategies, this study offers crucial contributions that can enhance the reliability of neural network applications. These insights are applicable across a diverse range of machine learning domains, from computer vision to natural language processing, paving the way for more predictable and robust model training processes. Keywords: Neural networks, optimization, nondeterminism, instability, stochastic gradient descent, machine learning, model training.

**Abstract** Accurate articulated 3D hand-object pose estimation is a critical challenge in computer vision, with applications in augmented reality, robotics, and human-computer interaction. However, obtaining labeled data for complex hand-object interactions remains difficult, often limiting the generalizability of current methods. This paper presents ArtiBoost, a novel framework designed to enhance 3D hand-object pose estimation by integrating online exploration and data synthesis techniques. ArtiBoost leverages an adaptive online learning strategy to explore challenging hand-object configurations in real time, automatically augmenting the training process with synthesized pose-data pairs. Additionally, an efficient synthesis module generates photorealistic hand-object scenes guided by the current uncertainty of the model, enabling targeted and diverse data enrichment. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that ArtiBoost significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness across a variety of challenging poses and occlusion levels. The approach further showcases improved generalization to unseen object shapes and interactions. These findings highlight the effectiveness of combining online exploration with intelligent data synthesis for advancing articulated 3D pose estimation. ArtiBoost offers a scalable and adaptable solution, paving the way for practical deployment in real-world interactive applications. **Keywords:** 3D hand-object pose estimation, articulated pose, online learning, data synthesis, computer vision, human-computer interaction.

This paper addresses the challenge of rectifying images affected by radial distortion and scale changes, a critical problem in computer vision and 3D reconstruction. We propose a novel set of minimal solvers designed to accurately estimate the parameters required for rectification under these conditions. Our approach leverages geometric constraints and algebraic formulations to derive efficient solutions that require only a minimal number of correspondences. The methods are validated through extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness compared to existing techniques. The solvers achieve real-time performance, making them suitable for applications in augmented reality, robotics, and image-based modeling. Key contributions include the introduction of new mathematical formulations for handling radial distortion and scale changes simultaneously, as well as the development of efficient algorithms that significantly reduce computational complexity. This work provides a foundation for future research in image rectification and offers practical tools for improving the accuracy of vision-based systems. **Keywords**: radial distortion, scale change, minimal solvers, image rectification, computer vision, 3D reconstruction.

The results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of classification accuracy and robustness to appearance variability. Key findings include improved performance on unseen domains and enhanced feature transferability. The proposed framework has significant implications for the development of automated histopathology image analysis systems, enabling more accurate and reliable disease diagnosis. Our research contributes to the field of medical image analysis by introducing a novel domain-adversarial neural network architecture, with potential applications in digital pathology and computer-aided diagnosis. Relevant keywords include: domain-adversarial neural networks, histopathology image analysis, appearance variability, medical image analysis, deep learning.
