Scene text recognition (STR) presents a significant challenge due to the diverse textual content and varying environmental conditions in which text appears. This paper introduces MASTER, a Multi-Aspect Non-local Network designed to enhance accuracy and robustness in STR. Methods: MASTER leverages a novel architecture that integrates multi-aspect features and non-local operations to capture both global and local contextual information within scene images. The network employs an attention mechanism to refine text feature extraction and a sequence-to-sequence model to facilitate recognition, capitalizing on advancements in deep learning for improved performance in dynamic text recognition scenarios. Results: Experimental results demonstrate that MASTER achieves superior recognition accuracy across multiple benchmark datasets, outperforming existing state-of-the-art STR methods. The non-local network architecture allows for efficient feature learning, significantly reducing the error rate while maintaining a low computational overhead. Conclusion: The introduction of the MASTER network represents a significant step forward in STR technology, offering robust and scalable solutions for automatic text recognition in complex scenes. This advancement has wide-ranging applications, including autonomous navigation systems, augmented reality, and document digitization. The integration of multi-aspect non-local networks could serve as a foundational model for future research in scalable and efficient text recognition systems. Keywords: Scene Text Recognition, Non-local Network, Multi-Aspect Features, Attention Mechanism, Deep Learning, Autonomous Systems, Text Feature Extraction.

This paper investigates the "multiple manifold problem" encountered in deep learning, where high-dimensional data lie close to multiple lower-dimensional manifolds. We hypothesize that standard deep networks struggle to effectively disentangle and represent data distributed across these manifolds, leading to suboptimal generalization and feature extraction. To address this, we propose a novel deep network architecture incorporating manifold regularization techniques. Our approach leverages concepts from differential geometry to encourage the network to learn representations that respect the underlying manifold structure of the data. We evaluated our method on several benchmark datasets, including synthetic data designed to explicitly exhibit the multiple manifold problem, as well as real-world image and text datasets. Results demonstrate that our manifold-regularized deep networks consistently outperform standard architectures in terms of classification accuracy and representation learning, particularly when the data are known to lie on multiple manifolds. These findings suggest that explicitly accounting for manifold structure is crucial for effective deep learning, paving the way for more robust and generalizable AI models. Keywords: Deep Learning, Manifold Learning, Regularization, Representation Learning, Differential Geometry, Generalization.

Function is defined as the ensemble of tasks that enable the product to complete the designed purpose. Functional tools, such as functional modeling, offer decision guidance in the early phase of product design, where explicit design decisions are yet to be made. Function-based design data is often sparse and grounded in individual interpretation. As such, function-based design tools can benefit from automatic function classification to increase data fidelity and provide function representation models that enable function-based intelligent design agents. Function-based design data is commonly stored in manually generated design repositories. These design repositories are a collection of expert knowledge and interpretations of function in product design bounded by function-flow and component taxonomies. In this work, we represent a structured taxonomy-based design repository as assembly-flow graphs, then leverage a graph neural network (GNN) model to perform automatic function classification. We support automated function classification by learning from repository data to establish the ground truth of component function assignment. Experimental results show that our GNN model achieves a micro-average F-score of 0.832 for tier 1 (broad), 0.756 for tier 2, and 0.783 for tier 3 (specific) functions. Given the imbalance of data features, the results are encouraging. Our efforts in this paper can be a starting point for more sophisticated applications in knowledge-based CAD systems and Design-for-X consideration in function-based design.

The research focuses on addressing uncertainties in reinforcement learning environments and enhancing decision-making processes. Uncertainty-aware Model-based Policy Optimization explores the integration of uncertainty quantification into model-based reinforcement learning to optimize policy performance in dynamic settings. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel framework that incorporates Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) to model uncertainties within the environment and its transitions. The proposed method utilizes a Monte Carlo sampling approach to assess uncertainty in predicted outcomes and augment policy updates. This uncertainty quantification guides policy optimization, allowing the model to adaptively focus on reducing uncertainty in high-impact areas. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate significant improvements in policy performance and stability compared to traditional model-based approaches. The introduction of uncertainty awareness leads to better decision-making in environments characterized by stochastic dynamics. Performance metrics indicate a clear advantage in minimizing expected cumulative costs and achieving faster convergence to optimal policies, as verified through comparative studies on benchmark environments. Conclusion/Implications: The integration of uncertainty awareness in reinforcement learning strategies presents a pivotal advancement in adaptive decision-making processes. This approach provides a robust framework for enhancing policy effectiveness in uncertain environments, with potential applications extending to robotics, autonomous vehicles, and other domains requiring high levels of environmental interaction. Keywords: Uncertainty, Model-based Reinforcement Learning, Policy Optimization, Bayesian Neural Networks, Monte Carlo Sampling, Decision-making.

This paper addresses the challenge of unsupervised transfer learning by introducing an adaptive feature ranking approach. The objective is to enable effective knowledge transfer between domains with disparate distributions, without requiring labeled data in the target domain. Our method employs a novel ranking algorithm that dynamically selects and weights the most relevant features from the source domain, based on their transferability and relevance to the target domain. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised transfer learning methods, achieving significant improvements in feature adaptation and target task performance. The key findings highlight the importance of adaptive feature ranking in facilitating efficient domain adaptation. Our research contributes to the development of more robust and flexible transfer learning frameworks, with potential applications in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and recommender systems. Key keywords: unsupervised transfer learning, domain adaptation, feature ranking, adaptive learning, knowledge transfer.

This paper introduces the Monash University, UEA, UCR Time Series Extrinsic Regression Archive, a comprehensive repository of time series datasets designed to facilitate research in extrinsic regression. The objective of this archive is to provide a unified platform for evaluating and comparing the performance of various regression models on time series data. A novel approach was employed to curate and preprocess the datasets, incorporating techniques from data mining and feature engineering to enhance their quality and relevance. The archive comprises a diverse collection of time series datasets from various domains, including finance, climate, and energy. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the archive in evaluating state-of-the-art regression models, with key findings highlighting the importance of dataset diversity and feature extraction in achieving accurate predictions. The Monash University, UEA, UCR Time Series Extrinsic Regression Archive contributes to the field of time series analysis by providing a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners, enabling the development of more accurate and robust regression models. Key keywords: time series analysis, extrinsic regression, dataset archive, data mining, feature engineering.

To improve the performance of deep learning, mixup has been proposed to force the neural networks favoring simple linear behaviors in-between training samples. Performing mixup for transfer learning with pre-trained models however is not that simple, a high capacity pre-trained model with a large fully-connected (FC) layer could easily overfit to the target dataset even with samples-to-labels mixed up. In this work, we propose SMILE - Self-Distilled Mixup for EffIcient Transfer LEarning. With mixed images as inputs, SMILE regularizes the outputs of CNN feature extractors to learn from the mixed feature vectors of inputs (sample-to-feature mixup), in addition to the mixed labels. Specifically, SMILE incorporates a mean teacher, inherited from the pre-trained model, to provide the feature vectors of input samples in a self-distilling fashion, and mixes up the feature vectors accordingly via a novel triplet regularizer. The triple regularizer balances the mixup effects in both feature and label spaces while bounding the linearity in-between samples for pre-training tasks. Extensive experiments have been done to verify the performance improvement made by SMILE, in comparisons with a wide spectrum of transfer learning algorithms, including fine-tuning, L2-SP, DELTA, and RIFLE, even with mixup strategies combined. Ablation studies show that the vanilla sample-to-label mixup strategies could marginally increase the linearity in-between training samples but lack of generalizability, while SMILE significantly improve the mixup effects in both label and feature spaces with both training and testing datasets. The empirical observations backup our design intuition and purposes.

This paper addresses the challenge of change captioning, where the goal is to describe changes between two images taken from different viewpoints. Our objective is to develop a robust and efficient method for matching and describing changes in scenes despite significant viewpoint variations. To achieve this, we propose a novel Viewpoint-Adapted Matching Encoder (VAME) that leverages a transformer-based architecture to adaptively align features from different viewpoints. Our approach enables the model to focus on the essential changes between images, rather than being distracted by viewpoint-dependent features. Experimental results demonstrate that VAME outperforms state-of-the-art methods in change captioning tasks, particularly in scenarios with large viewpoint differences. The key findings of this research highlight the importance of viewpoint adaptation in change captioning and demonstrate the effectiveness of VAME in real-world applications, such as surveillance, robotics, and autonomous driving. Our contributions include a novel encoder architecture, a viewpoint-adapted matching mechanism, and a comprehensive evaluation framework for change captioning. Key keywords: change captioning, viewpoint adaptation, transformer, encoder, computer vision, image matching.

Phương pháp này cho phép so sánh và đánh giá các loại gạch dựa trên nhiều tiêu chí khác nhau như độ bền, giá thành, khả năng cách nhiệt và tính thẩm mỹ. Việc áp dụng SAW trong ngành xây dựng mở ra hướng đi mới cho việc lựa chọn vật liệu, góp phần nâng cao chất lượng công trình.

This study aims to develop a deep learning model for forecasting future Humphrey visual fields, addressing the critical need for early detection and monitoring of visual field progression in patients with glaucoma and other ocular diseases. Our approach utilizes a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, incorporating longitudinal visual field data and patient demographics to predict future visual field loss. The model is trained on a large dataset of patient records, leveraging techniques such as data augmentation and transfer learning to enhance performance. Results show that our model achieves high accuracy in predicting future visual field defects, outperforming traditional methods and demonstrating potential for clinical application. The key contributions of this research include the development of a robust and generalizable forecasting model, enabling early intervention and personalized treatment planning. This study highlights the potential of deep learning in ophthalmology, particularly in the context of visual field analysis, and paves the way for future research in AI-assisted disease diagnosis and monitoring, with relevant keywords including deep learning, visual field forecasting, glaucoma, ophthalmology, and convolutional neural networks.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have emerged as a powerful tool for generating synthetic data, with significant applications in time series analysis. This paper presents a comprehensive survey and taxonomy of GAN-based approaches for time series data, addressing the challenges and opportunities in this domain. The objective is to provide a structured overview of existing methods, highlighting their strengths and limitations. We systematically categorize GAN architectures and training strategies tailored for time series, including recurrent GANs, convolutional GANs, and hybrid models. Additionally, we evaluate their performance in tasks such as anomaly detection, forecasting, and data augmentation. Our findings reveal that GANs offer promising results in generating realistic time series data, but challenges such as mode collapse and training instability persist. The taxonomy proposed in this study serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners, enabling informed decisions when selecting and designing GAN-based solutions for time series applications. This work contributes to advancing the field by identifying key research directions and potential improvements in GAN architectures for time series analysis. **Keywords**: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), time series, anomaly detection, forecasting, data augmentation, taxonomy.

This paper addresses the problem of learning linear non-Gaussian graphical models with multidirected edges, a crucial task in understanding complex relationships between variables. Our objective is to develop an efficient method for estimating the structure of such models from observational data. We propose a novel approach that leverages a combination of independence tests and graph optimization techniques to identify the underlying graph structure. Our method utilizes a sparse representation of the graph and incorporates a robust estimation procedure to handle non-Gaussian noise. The results show that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and scalability, especially in high-dimensional settings. The key findings include the development of a new algorithm for learning multidirected graphical models and the demonstration of its effectiveness in various simulated and real-world datasets. Our research contributes to the advancement of graphical modeling and has important implications for applications in genetics, finance, and social network analysis, where complex relationships between variables are common. The proposed method has the potential to uncover new insights into the underlying mechanisms of complex systems, and its novelty lies in its ability to handle non-Gaussian data and multidirected edges, making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of machine learning and statistics. Key keywords: graphical models, non-Gaussian data, multidirected edges, structure learning, independence tests.

The increasing complexity of neural networks has led to significant challenges in achieving runtime efficiency, particularly in resource-constrained environments. This paper introduces *AntiDote*, a novel attention-based dynamic optimization framework designed to enhance the runtime efficiency of neural networks without compromising accuracy. The proposed approach leverages attention mechanisms to dynamically identify and prioritize critical computational paths during inference, enabling adaptive resource allocation and reducing redundant computations. We evaluate *AntiDote* on a diverse set of benchmark datasets and neural architectures, demonstrating significant improvements in inference speed and computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art optimization techniques. Experimental results show an average reduction of 30% in runtime latency while maintaining model accuracy within 1% of baseline performance. The framework is particularly effective for real-time applications, such as edge computing and mobile devices, where computational resources are limited. By integrating attention-based dynamic optimization, *AntiDote* offers a scalable and practical solution for deploying efficient neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This work contributes to the growing field of neural network optimization by introducing a lightweight, adaptive approach that bridges the gap between efficiency and performance. **Keywords**: neural network optimization, attention mechanisms, runtime efficiency, dynamic computation, edge computing, resource-constrained environments.

This paper proposes a novel approach to early time series classification using deep convolutional networks, with a focus on earliness-aware learning. The objective is to develop a model that can accurately classify time series data as early as possible, while minimizing unnecessary computations and improving real-time decision-making. Our approach utilizes a customized convolutional neural network architecture that incorporates earliness-aware loss functions and early exit mechanisms, allowing the model to adaptively determine the optimal classification time. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art early classification techniques, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of earliness-aware deep learning frameworks and the development of novel evaluation metrics for early time series classification. This study has important implications for real-time applications, such as anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and healthcare monitoring, where early and accurate classification is crucial. Key keywords: early time series classification, deep convolutional networks, earliness-aware learning, real-time decision-making, anomaly detection.

The paper addresses the challenge of improving predictive model robustness in the presence of adversarial examples, which are carefully crafted inputs designed to deceive models. We focus on the deterministic context, analyzing theoretical aspects and constraints associated with the application of adversarial training methods. Methods/Approach: Our approach involves a comprehensive theoretical examination of adversarial training techniques in deterministic settings. We develop mathematical models to rigorously assess the effectiveness of these methods, investigating their capacity to secure predictive tasks against adversarial interventions. This includes the evaluation of existing algorithms and their optimized variants to enhance model resilience under deterministic conditions. Results/Findings: The findings reveal critical insights into the capabilities and boundaries of adversarial training when applied to deterministic predictive models. While adversarial training can mitigate certain adversarial effects, our analysis identifies inherent limitations that constrain its effectiveness. We quantify these limitations and demonstrate scenarios where adversarial training may not provide sufficient robustness, highlighting the disparities between theoretical efficacy and practical application. Conclusion/Implications: Our theoretical analysis underscores the necessity of cautious application of adversarial training in deterministic scenarios, acknowledging its constrained efficacy. This research contributes valuable insights into the design of security-focused predictive models, suggesting that alternative or supplementary methods might be required to achieve desired robustness levels. The study sets the stage for future research aimed at overcoming the identified limitations and enhances understanding of adversarial training's theoretical foundations. Keywords: adversarial training, predictive tasks, deterministic models, theoretical analysis, model robustness, adversarial examples, limitations.

This paper introduces EGAD, a novel graph representation learning framework designed to enhance live video streaming events. The objective is to improve the accuracy of event detection and representation in real-time video streams. EGAD employs a self-attention mechanism to capture complex relationships between graph nodes, combined with knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge from pre-trained models. The approach leverages evolving graph structures to adapt to dynamic event patterns. Experimental results demonstrate that EGAD outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of event detection accuracy and efficiency. The key findings highlight the effectiveness of self-attention and knowledge distillation in graph representation learning for live video streaming events. This research contributes to the development of more accurate and efficient event detection systems, with potential applications in real-time content analysis and recommendation systems. The novelty of EGAD lies in its ability to evolve graph representations in real-time, making it suitable for live video streaming events. Key keywords: graph representation learning, self-attention, knowledge distillation, live video streaming, event detection, evolving graphs.

Image inpainting is a critical task in computer vision, aimed at restoring missing or corrupted regions of images. Traditional approaches often rely on spatial domain methods, which can struggle with complex patterns and textures. This paper explores a novel approach leveraging frequency domain priors to enhance inpainting performance. Methods: We propose a method that integrates frequency domain information as a prior in the inpainting process. The approach employs Fourier Transforms to identify and utilize the frequency components that characterize the intact regions of an image. An algorithm is then applied to guide the reconstruction of missing areas, ensuring consistency with these frequency priors. Results: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method significantly improves the quality of the inpainted images, achieving higher accuracy and visual appeal compared to state-of-the-art spatial domain techniques. Quantitative metrics such as PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) and SSIM (Structural Similarity Index) show notable enhancements when our frequency-based model is employed. Conclusion: The incorporation of frequency domain priors offers a powerful alternative to conventional image inpainting techniques. By focusing on frequency information, our approach effectively reconstructs complex patterns and textures, enhancing the fidelity and natural appearance of the inpainted regions. This study not only provides significant insights into the capabilities of frequency-based image processing but also opens avenues for further research in the application of frequency analysis in computer vision tasks. Keywords: Image inpainting, frequency domain, Fourier Transform, computer vision, PSNR, SSIM.

This paper introduces a novel deep ensemble multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach for optimizing air traffic control (ATC) operations. The primary objective is to enhance airspace efficiency by reducing flight delays and optimizing resource allocation, while maintaining safety standards. Our method combines deep reinforcement learning with an ensemble of agents, each trained independently using a shared reward structure and distinct exploration strategies. This ensemble promotes robustness and reduces the risk of converging to suboptimal policies. We evaluate our approach in a simulated ATC environment based on real-world air traffic patterns, comparing it against traditional single-agent and cooperative MARL algorithms. Results demonstrate that our deep ensemble MARL method achieves a 15% reduction in average flight delay and a 10% improvement in airspace throughput compared to benchmark methods. Furthermore, the ensemble approach exhibits greater resilience to unforeseen events such as weather disruptions. These findings highlight the potential of deep ensemble MARL for developing more efficient and adaptive ATC systems. Keywords: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, Air Traffic Control, Deep Learning, Ensemble Learning, Optimization, Aviation.

The Relation Extraction (RE) problem is a very important task in Information Extraction. Because of its effectiveness in extracting information from unstructured text, it is the key component of many NLP tasks, such as Information Retrieval , Question Answering and Knowledge Graph Construction . In particular, a relation extraction system is expected to classify the semantic relation between two entity mentions in the given context. To deal with this problem, many methods have been proposed and achieved remarkable results –. Nevertheless, a majority of previous RE studies only considered the traditional setting where the set of relations is pre-defined and fixed during the training and testing phases. This setting is not practical as new relations of interest might emerge during the deployment time of RE systems in practice, requiring the models to adapt their operation to accommodate new types. Therefore, Continual Relation Extraction was proposed, aiming to learn new relations from new coming data. Recently, CRE has attracted considerable attention in the literature – because of not only its appealing practical applications but also the challenging problems which come from both fields, Continual Learning, and Relation Extraction.

This paper introduces a novel approach for detecting gaze preferences in children using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), with the potential to aid in the early diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The objective is to develop a robust and automated method for analyzing visual attention patterns, a key indicator of ASD. Our method utilizes a CNN architecture trained on eye-tracking data collected during visual stimuli presentation. The CNN model learns to classify gaze patterns, distinguishing between neurotypical children and those with ASD, based on preferential looking behaviors. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed CNN-based approach, achieving a significant improvement in accuracy compared to traditional machine learning techniques for gaze preference analysis. These findings suggest that the developed system can serve as a valuable tool for clinicians in the early identification of children at risk for ASD, enabling timely intervention and support. Keywords: Autism Spectrum Disorder, Gaze Preference, Convolutional Neural Network, Eye-Tracking, Diagnostics, Visual Attention.

Video Object Segmentation (VOS) is a critical task in computer vision, aiming to accurately segment and track objects across video frames. This paper introduces **LIP (Learning Instance Propagation)**, a novel framework designed to enhance the performance of VOS by leveraging instance-level information propagation. The proposed approach addresses the challenges of occlusions, appearance changes, and complex object interactions in dynamic video sequences. LIP employs a dual-branch architecture that integrates spatial-temporal feature learning with instance-aware propagation mechanisms. The first branch focuses on capturing object-specific features, while the second branch propagates instance-level information across frames, ensuring robust tracking and segmentation. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, such as DAVIS and YouTube-VOS, demonstrate that LIP achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The framework also exhibits superior generalization capabilities, making it suitable for real-world applications such as autonomous driving, surveillance, and video editing. This work contributes a scalable and efficient solution to VOS, emphasizing the importance of instance-level learning for improving segmentation accuracy in complex video scenarios. **Keywords**: Video Object Segmentation, Instance Propagation, Deep Learning, Spatial-Temporal Modeling, Computer Vision.

The rapid growth in the size of neural networks has necessitated the development of more efficient algorithms for handling large vocabularies in tasks such as language modeling and machine translation. This paper addresses the computational challenges associated with softmax layers in such scenarios by introducing an optimized sampled softmax function within the TensorFlow framework. Methods/Approach: We present an enhanced sampled softmax technique that leverages TensorFlow's computational capabilities to reduce the complexity of large output layers, enabling quicker and more resource-efficient model training. Our approach integrates sampling strategies that approximate the full softmax while maintaining accuracy, and optimally utilizes TensorFlow’s parallel processing to expedite computations. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in both speed and memory usage without compromising the accuracy of the models. The proposed method shows superior performance when compared to traditional softmax implementations and existing sampling strategies, reducing training time by a substantial margin while preserving model quality. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of an efficient sampled softmax within TensorFlow enables practitioners to train large-scale language models more effectively, thus making high-performance deep learning more accessible for resource-constrained environments. This advancement could accelerate developments in AI-driven applications including speech recognition, natural language processing, and real-time translation systems. Keywords: sampled softmax, TensorFlow, neural networks, computational efficiency, large vocabulary, language modeling.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving kernel learning in machine learning models, particularly in the context of high-dimensional data and complex patterns. Traditional kernel methods often struggle with scalability and adaptability, limiting their effectiveness in modern applications. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel approach called Convolutional Spectral Kernel Learning (CSKL), which integrates convolutional operations with spectral techniques to enhance kernel flexibility and computational efficiency. The CSKL framework leverages spectral decomposition to approximate kernels in a low-dimensional space, while convolutional layers capture local dependencies and hierarchical features in the data. We evaluate the proposed method on benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in both accuracy and computational performance compared to conventional kernel methods. Experimental results show that CSKL achieves superior generalization capabilities, particularly in tasks involving image classification and signal processing. The key contribution of this work lies in its ability to combine the strengths of convolutional architectures with spectral kernel learning, offering a scalable and adaptable solution for complex data analysis. This research opens new avenues for applying advanced kernel methods in domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, and bioinformatics. **Keywords**: Kernel learning, convolutional methods, spectral decomposition, machine learning, high-dimensional data, scalability.

The sim-to-real transfer of robot learning has emerged as a critical challenge in deploying robotic systems in real-world environments. This paper addresses the problem of enabling robots to generalize learned behaviors from simulation to reality, particularly when dealing with variable-length inputs, such as sensor data or task-specific sequences. We propose a novel framework that leverages adaptive neural architectures and domain randomization techniques to bridge the gap between simulated and real-world dynamics. Our approach introduces a dynamic input processing mechanism capable of handling inputs of varying lengths, ensuring robust performance across diverse scenarios. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our method achieves significant improvements in transferability, outperforming existing approaches in terms of task success rates and adaptability. The results highlight the framework's ability to generalize across different environments and tasks, even with limited real-world training data. This research contributes to advancing the field of robot learning by providing a scalable solution for sim-to-real transfer, with potential applications in industrial automation, healthcare robotics, and autonomous systems. **Keywords**: sim-to-real transfer, robot learning, variable-length inputs, domain randomization, adaptive neural networks, robotics.

Molecule generation is a challenging open problem in cheminformatics. Currently, deep generative approaches addressing the challenge belong to two broad categories, differing in how molecules are represented. One approach encodes molecular graphs as strings of text, and learns their corresponding character-based language model. Another, more expressive, approach operates directly on the molecular graph. In this work, we address two limitations of the former: generation of invalid and duplicate molecules. To improve validity rates, we develop a language model for small molecular substructures called fragments, loosely inspired by the well-known paradigm of Fragment-Based Drug Design. In other words, we generate molecules fragment by fragment, instead of atom by atom. To improve uniqueness rates, we present a frequency-based masking strategy that helps generate molecules with infrequent fragments. We show experimentally that our model largely outperforms other language model-based competitors, reaching state-of-the-art performances typical of graph-based approaches. Moreover, generated molecules display molecular properties similar to those in the training sample, even in absence of explicit task-specific supervision.

This paper addresses the challenge of unsupervised domain adaptation in stereo matching, a crucial component in many computer vision applications such as autonomous driving and 3D scene reconstruction. The primary objective is to enhance the adaptability and accuracy of stereo matching algorithms when applied to new domains without manual re-calibration. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel geometry-aware framework for unsupervised domain adaptation in stereo matching. Our approach integrates geometric consistency constraints with disparity estimation, facilitating the transfer of knowledge from labeled synthetic datasets to unlabeled real-world data. The framework leverages a geometrically-guided self-supervised learning pipeline, optimizing the model's performance by enforcing structural robustness and reducing domain discrepancies. Results/Findings: The proposed method significantly improves stereo matching accuracy across various cross-domain scenarios, demonstrating superior performance over existing unsupervised domain adaptation methodologies. Extensive experiments reveal that our geometry-aware approach not only maintains high precision in disparity maps but also enhances the system's adaptability to different environmental conditions, such as variable lighting and scene complexities, achieving state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets. Conclusion/Implications: The findings of this research provide valuable insights into leveraging geometric cues for domain adaptation in stereo matching tasks. The integration of geometric consistency offers a promising avenue for improving cross-domain robustness, enabling more reliable 3D information gathering in diverse real-world applications. This work opens pathways for future research in geometry-aware learning strategies and their applications in other areas of computer vision. Keywords: stereo matching, unsupervised domain adaptation, geometry-aware, disparity estimation, computer vision, self-supervised learning.

Autonomous repair of deep-sea coral reefs is a recent proposed idea to support the oceans ecosystem in which is vital for commercial fishing, tourism and other species. This idea can be operated through using many small autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and swarm intelligence techniques to locate and replace chunks of coral which have been broken off, thus enabling re-growth and maintaining the habitat. The aim of this project is developing machine vision algorithms to enable an underwater robot to locate a coral reef and a chunk of coral on the seabed and prompt the robot to pick it up. Although there is no literature on this particular problem, related work on fish counting may give some insight into the problem. The technical challenges are principally due to the potential lack of clarity of the water and platform stabilization as well as spurious artifacts (rocks, fish, and crabs). We present an efficient sparse classification for coral species using supervised deep learning method called Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). We compute Weber Local Descriptor (WLD), Phase Congruency (PC), and Zero Component Analysis (ZCA) Whitening to extract shape and texture feature descriptors, which are employed to be supplementary channels (feature-based maps) besides basic spatial color channels (spatial-based maps) of coral input image, we also experiment state-of-art preprocessing underwater algorithms for image enhancement and color normalization and color conversion adjustment. Our proposed coral classification method is developed under MATLAB platform, and evaluated by two different coral datasets (University of California San Diego's Moorea Labeled Corals, and Heriot-Watt University's Atlantic Deep Sea).

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc phân lập và đánh giá ảnh hưởng của các loại muối dinh dưỡng, cụ thể là nitrat (NO₃⁻) và photphat (PO₄³⁻), lên sự phát triển của một số loài vi sinh vật hoặc thực vật. Kết quả cho thấy, nồng độ và tỷ lệ của các muối này có tác động đáng kể đến tốc độ sinh trưởng, quá trình trao đổi chất và khả năng hấp thụ dinh dưỡng. Nitrat đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc thúc đẩy quá trình tổng hợp protein, trong khi photphat lại ảnh hưởng đến sự hình thành năng lượng và cấu trúc tế bào. This paper proposes an innovative no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) approach, leveraging attention-driven mechanisms to evaluate the perceptual quality of images. The model is trained on a large dataset of images with diverse distortion types and levels. Experimental results demonstrate that our attention-driven NR-IQA approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving high correlation with human subjective scores. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of attention mechanisms in NR-IQA, enabling the model to adaptively weigh the importance of different image regions, and the development of a more robust and generalizable image quality assessment framework. This work has significant implications for various applications, including image and video processing, compression, and transmission. Generalization across environments is critical to the successful application of reinforcement learning algorithms to real-world challenges. In this paper, we consider the problem of learning abstractions that generalize in block MDPs, families of environments with a shared latent state space and dynamics structure over that latent space, but varying observations. We leverage tools from causal inference to propose a method of invariant prediction to learn model-irrelevance state abstractions (MISA) that generalize to novel observations in the multi-environment setting. We prove that for certain classes of environments, this approach outputs with high probability a state abstraction corresponding to the causal feature set with respect to the return. We further provide more general bounds on model error and generalization error in the multi-environment setting, in the process showing a connection between causal variable selection and the state abstraction framework for MDPs. We give empirical evidence that our methods work in both linear and nonlinear settings, attaining improved generalization over single- and multi-task baselines.

This paper introduces SaliencyMix, a novel data augmentation strategy that leverages saliency maps to guide the mixing of images, enhancing model regularization. The objective is to improve model generalization by focusing on the most relevant features of the input data. Our approach utilizes a saliency detection algorithm to identify critical regions in images and then applies a mixing strategy to combine these regions with other images, creating new, informative training samples. Experimental results demonstrate that SaliencyMix outperforms existing data augmentation techniques, leading to improved model performance and reduced overfitting. The key findings indicate that SaliencyMix enhances model robustness and accuracy, particularly in scenarios with limited training data. The proposed method has significant implications for deep learning applications, offering a simple yet effective way to regularize models and improve their ability to generalize to new, unseen data. By highlighting the importance of saliency-guided data augmentation, this research contributes to the development of more robust and accurate AI models, with potential applications in computer vision, image classification, and object detection. Key keywords: data augmentation, saliency maps, model regularization, deep learning, computer vision.

This paper introduces Manifold Topology Divergence, a novel framework for comparing the geometric and topological properties of data manifolds. The objective is to develop a robust method for assessing the similarity and differences between complex data distributions, which is crucial in various applications such as data analysis, machine learning, and computer vision. Our approach leverages advances in manifold learning and topological data analysis to define a divergence metric that captures the structural differences between data manifolds. The results show that our framework outperforms existing methods in comparing manifolds with varying degrees of complexity and noise. The key findings indicate that Manifold Topology Divergence can effectively identify subtle differences in data distributions, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks such as classification and clustering. The proposed framework has significant implications for understanding the geometric and topological properties of complex data, with potential applications in fields such as artificial intelligence, data science, and scientific computing. Key keywords: manifold learning, topological data analysis, data geometry, divergence metrics, machine learning, data comparison.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) aims to learn optimal policies from previously collected, static datasets without further environment interaction. This work addresses the challenge of partial coverage in offline RL, where the dataset may not fully represent the state-action space, leading to overestimation and poor generalization. We introduce a pessimistic model-based approach grounded in Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning theory. Our method constructs a lower-confidence bound on the model's predicted reward and transition dynamics. By optimizing policies with respect to this pessimistic model, we mitigate the risks associated with out-of-distribution actions. We derive novel PAC bounds demonstrating the sample complexity of learning near-optimal policies under partial coverage. Furthermore, we propose a practical algorithm based on posterior sampling, allowing for efficient exploration of the pessimistic model space. Empirical results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing offline RL methods in scenarios with limited data coverage. This work contributes to the theoretical understanding and practical development of robust offline RL algorithms. **Keywords:** Offline Reinforcement Learning, Pessimistic Planning, PAC Learning, Partial Coverage, Model-based RL, Posterior Sampling.

This paper investigates the problem of regret minimization in reinforcement learning (RL) using kernel-based methods. We focus on episodic RL with continuous state and action spaces, where the transition dynamics are unknown. We introduce a novel kernelized least-squares value iteration algorithm that leverages the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) to represent value functions. Our main contribution is deriving a finite-sample regret bound for the proposed algorithm. Specifically, we show that the cumulative regret scales sublinearly with the number of episodes, achieving a rate of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T})$, where $T$ is the total number of episodes. The analysis relies on carefully controlling the approximation error and the estimation error introduced by the kernel method. Furthermore, we provide theoretical insights into the impact of kernel choice on the regret performance. Empirical evaluations on benchmark RL environments demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm compared to existing kernel-based and non-kernel-based approaches. This work provides a theoretical foundation for the use of kernel methods in RL and offers a practical algorithm with provable regret guarantees. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Kernel Methods, Regret Bound, Value Iteration, RKHS.

Abstract: Visual Speech Recognition (VSR) has made significant advances with deep learning techniques, yet the challenge remains to recognize out-of-vocabulary or unseen words and phrases, particularly in low-resource scenarios. This paper addresses the problem of zero-shot learning in VSR—the ability to identify new classes that were absent during training—by harnessing the powerful generative capabilities of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). We propose a novel framework that employs GANs to synthesize realistic visual speech features for new, unseen classes using semantic class embeddings as guidance. The generated data is then integrated into a conventional VSR pipeline, enabling robust recognition of previously unobserved words or speakers. Experimental results on benchmark VSR datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly improves classification accuracy for unseen classes compared to traditional methods, while maintaining performance on known classes. The key contributions include an effective GAN-based data generation mechanism for zero-shot class augmentation and an end-to-end architecture seamlessly combining generative and discriminative models. This work highlights the potential of generative deep learning models to advance VSR systems towards more flexible, scalable, and generalizable recognition. Keywords: Visual Speech Recognition, Zero-shot Learning, Generative Adversarial Networks, Data Augmentation, Deep Learning.

The creation of large, labeled datasets is a significant bottleneck in training high-performing machine learning models, particularly in areas like image generation and manipulation. This paper introduces DatasetGAN, a novel framework designed to efficiently generate labeled data with minimal human effort. Our approach leverages the generative power of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) coupled with a user-friendly interface for specifying data characteristics. Instead of manually labeling individual samples, users interact with the GAN's latent space to define semantic attributes, effectively creating a labeled dataset by mapping latent vectors to corresponding labels. We demonstrate the efficacy of DatasetGAN in generating high-quality labeled data for various image domains. Experiments show that models trained on data synthesized using DatasetGAN achieve comparable or superior performance to those trained on manually labeled datasets, while significantly reducing human annotation time. This approach offers a promising avenue for democratizing access to labeled data and accelerating the development of data-hungry machine learning applications. Keywords: GAN, data augmentation, labeled data, synthetic data, machine learning, image generation, data efficiency.

This paper presents DatasetGAN, a novel framework designed to generate high-quality labeled datasets with minimal human annotation effort. Traditional supervised learning approaches are heavily dependent on large volumes of accurately labeled data, a process that is time-consuming and resource-intensive. DatasetGAN addresses this challenge by leveraging generative adversarial networks (GANs) to synthesize realistic images while simultaneously producing detailed semantic labels. The proposed approach integrates a small set of manually annotated examples and utilizes a segmentation network trained in tandem with the GAN to propagate labels to generated samples. Experimental evaluation across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrates that DatasetGAN-generated data significantly enhances the performance of downstream tasks, such as image classification and object segmentation, reducing the need for extensive manual labeling. Furthermore, qualitative and quantitative results show that DatasetGAN maintains high fidelity and consistency in both image quality and annotation accuracy. This work highlights the potential for DatasetGAN to streamline data preparation processes in machine learning pipelines, making it a valuable tool for applications in computer vision, AI model training, and large-scale data annotation. Key keywords: dataset generation, GAN, automatic labeling, semantic segmentation, data augmentation, computer vision.

This paper introduces a novel approach for image deblurring and super-resolution, leveraging adaptive sparse domain selection and adaptive regularization techniques. The objective is to enhance image quality by simultaneously reducing blur and increasing resolution. Our method adaptively selects relevant sparse domains based on local image characteristics, enabling efficient representation of image structures. Furthermore, we employ an adaptive regularization strategy that adjusts regularization parameters according to the local image content, effectively balancing noise suppression and detail preservation. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both quantitative metrics (PSNR and SSIM) and visual quality, particularly in handling complex blur kernels and significant upscaling factors. The adaptive nature of our method makes it robust to varying image conditions and blur types, offering significant improvements in image restoration performance. Keywords: Image Deblurring, Super-resolution, Sparse Representation, Adaptive Regularization, Image Restoration.

This research addresses the challenge of developing an energy-efficient locomotion strategy for snake-like robots, which can adaptively navigate varied terrain while minimizing energy consumption. The study explores the potential of deep reinforcement learning to optimize snake locomotion gaits, paving the way for advances in robotic efficiency and adaptability. Methods/Approach: Utilizing a deep reinforcement learning framework, the study employs a combination of neural network architectures and policy gradient methods to derive optimal gait patterns for snake robots. The approach is designed to iteratively refine motion strategies based on feedback from energy expenditure metrics and movement efficiency across simulated environments. Results/Findings: The proposed methodology successfully identified energy-saving gaits, demonstrating a significant reduction in energy consumption compared to traditional locomotion strategies. Experimental results reveal that the reinforcement learning-derived gait policy results in enhanced adaptability to varied terrains, including complex and dynamic surfaces. The findings confirm the viability of deep reinforcement learning as a powerful tool for optimizing robotic locomotion beyond preconceived motion patterns. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel solution for energy-efficient robotic locomotion by incorporating deep reinforcement learning into gait strategy development. The innovations presented are applicable to various robotic systems requiring energy-efficient movement solutions. The broader implications of the study suggest potential applications in search and rescue missions, planetary exploration, and environmental monitoring, where energy-efficient navigation is crucial. Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Snake Locomotion, Gait Policy, Energy Efficiency, Robotic Navigation.

The objective of this research is to address the challenge of developing efficient online learning algorithms for situations involving nonlinear dynamics. We introduce the Koopman Spectrum Nonlinear Regulator, a novel approach leveraging the Koopman operator theory to transform complex nonlinear systems into linear representations, enabling improved analytical tractability and control. Our method utilizes the Koopman spectrum to design a regulator capable of handling the intricacies of nonlinear dynamics more effectively than traditional techniques. The approach integrates these theoretical advancements into a pragmatic online learning framework, ensuring adaptability and resilience across diverse dynamic environments. The key findings of our study demonstrate that our proposed regulator outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of convergence speed and stability. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the system's theoretical foundation along with experimental validations, showcasing its robust performance in real-time applications. Our results further indicate significant enhancements in learning efficiency, asserting that the integration of Koopman theory into dynamic systems control fosters superior adaptability and precision. Conclusively, this research offers substantial contributions to the field of online learning for dynamic systems, presenting a scalable and efficient solution with promising implications for a variety of applications such as autonomous systems and robotics. The fusion of Koopman operator theory with online learning paradigms substantiates a stepping stone towards more intelligent and autonomous regulatory mechanisms. Key keywords include Koopman operator, nonlinear dynamics, online learning, system control, and adaptive algorithms.

This paper introduces a novel multi-task based lifelong learning approach, Regularize, Expand and Compress (REC), which leverages NonExpansive AutoML to efficiently adapt to continuously arriving tasks. The objective is to develop a flexible and scalable framework that can learn from a stream of tasks without requiring prior knowledge of the task sequence or suffering from catastrophic forgetting. Our approach combines regularization techniques to prevent overfitting, expansion methods to incorporate new tasks, and compression algorithms to retain essential knowledge. The REC framework is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its ability to outperform existing lifelong learning methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and adaptability. Key findings include improved performance on subsequent tasks, reduced forgetting of previously learned tasks, and enhanced robustness to task variability. The proposed REC approach contributes to the field of lifelong learning by providing a versatile and automated framework for multi-task learning, with potential applications in areas such as autonomous systems, recommender systems, and edge AI. Relevant keywords: lifelong learning, multi-task learning, AutoML, non-expansive learning, regularization, compression, edge AI.

This paper presents an end-to-end computer vision approach for multi-class classification of blood cells, aiming to assist in the diagnosis of various blood-related disorders. The objective is to develop a robust and accurate system that can automatically classify blood cells into different categories. Our approach utilizes a deep learning-based methodology, leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract features from blood cell images. The proposed system is trained on a large dataset of annotated blood cell images, achieving high accuracy and outperforming traditional machine learning methods. The results show a significant improvement in classification accuracy, with an overall accuracy of 95% across multiple classes. The key contributions of this research include the development of a novel CNN architecture and a comprehensive evaluation framework for blood cell classification. This study demonstrates the potential of computer vision-based diagnosis in hematology, enabling rapid and accurate analysis of blood cells. This paper addresses the critical challenge of dataset bias in the emerging field of visual emotion recognition. While deep learning models have shown promise in automatically inferring emotions from images, their performance is often hampered by biases present in existing datasets, leading to poor generalization across diverse visual contexts. This study investigates the impact of such biases, focusing on inherent correlations between specific visual attributes and emotion labels. We propose a novel debiasing framework based on adversarial learning, which aims to disentangle emotional content from confounding factors. Our approach incorporates a bias detector to identify and suppress spurious correlations during feature extraction. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in generalization performance compared to state-of-the-art models, particularly in cross-dataset validation scenarios. The results highlight the importance of addressing dataset bias in visual emotion recognition and provide a promising direction for developing more robust and reliable emotion-aware systems. Keywords: visual emotion recognition, dataset bias, adversarial learning, debiasing, deep learning, generalization.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing the robustness of graph neural networks against adversarial attacks. Our objective is to develop a novel defense strategy, termed Adversarial Immunization, which leverages the concept of certifiable robustness to protect graph models from malicious perturbations. We propose a unique approach that combines graph-based adversarial training with a certification mechanism, ensuring that the trained models are robust against a wide range of attacks. Our method utilizes a robust optimization framework to minimize the loss function while maximizing the certifiable robustness of the model. Experimental results demonstrate that our Adversarial Immunization approach outperforms existing defense methods, achieving state-of-the-art robustness on various graph benchmarks. The key findings of this research highlight the importance of certifiable robustness in graph neural networks and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving model resilience against adversarial attacks. This work contributes to the development of more secure and reliable graph-based AI systems, with potential applications in areas such as social network analysis, recommendation systems, and graph-based anomaly detection. Key keywords: graph neural networks, adversarial robustness, certifiable robustness, graph-based defense, robust optimization.

This paper addresses the challenge of precise object detection in densely packed scenes, a critical task in applications such as surveillance, autonomous driving, and industrial automation. In this paper, we address the problem of having characters with different scales in scene text recognition. We propose a novel scale aware feature encoder (SAFE) that is designed specifically for encoding characters with different scales. SAFE is composed of a multi-scale convolutional encoder and a scale attention network. The multi-scale convolutional encoder targets at extracting character features under multiple scales, and the scale attention network is responsible for selecting features from the most relevant scale(s). SAFE has two main advantages over the traditional single-CNN encoder used in current state-of-the-art text recognizers. First, it explicitly tackles the scale problem by extracting scale-invariant features from the characters. This allows the recognizer to put more effort in handling other challenges in scene text recognition, like those caused by view distortion and poor image quality. Second, it can transfer the learning of feature encoding across different character scales. This is particularly important when the training set has a very unbalanced distribution of character scales, as training with such a dataset will make the encoder biased towards extracting features from the predominant scale. To evaluate the effectiveness of SAFE, we design a simple text recognizer named scale-spatial attention network (S-SAN) that employs SAFE as its feature encoder, and carry out experiments on six public benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that S-SAN can achieve state-of-the-art (or, in some cases, extremely competitive) performance without any post-processing.

Video object detection on mobile devices presents significant challenges due to limited computational resources and power constraints. This paper introduces a novel approach to achieve high-performance video object detection on mobile platforms by optimizing both the detection model and the processing pipeline. Our method incorporates a lightweight yet effective object detection network based on MobileNetV3, coupled with a frame selection strategy that prioritizes frames containing motion and reduces redundant processing. We further employ quantization and model pruning techniques to minimize the model size and computational complexity. Experimental results on benchmark video datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves a significant improvement in frames per second (FPS) and energy efficiency compared to existing methods, while maintaining comparable detection accuracy. Specifically, our system achieves a 25% increase in FPS with a 15% reduction in energy consumption. These results indicate the feasibility of deploying high-performance video object detection systems on mobile devices. Keywords: Video Object Detection, Mobile Devices, Deep Learning, Model Optimization, Frame Selection, Energy Efficiency.

This paper presents a novel information-geometric approach to feature extraction and moment reconstruction in dynamical systems. The objective is to develop a framework that leverages geometric techniques to identify and extract relevant features from complex systems, enabling accurate reconstruction of moments and improved understanding of system behavior. Our approach employs a combination of differential geometry and information theory to analyze the underlying structure of dynamical systems, providing a unique perspective on feature extraction and moment reconstruction. The methodology involves the use of Riemannian metrics and geodesic equations to identify optimal feature sets, which are then used to reconstruct system moments. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in extracting relevant features and reconstructing moments in various dynamical systems, outperforming traditional methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed framework has significant implications for fields such as signal processing, control theory, and machine learning, and contributes to the development of more accurate and robust models of complex systems. Key contributions include the introduction of a geometric framework for feature extraction and moment reconstruction, and the demonstration of its potential in analyzing and understanding complex dynamical systems. Relevant keywords: information geometry, dynamical systems, feature extraction, moment reconstruction, Riemannian metrics, geodesic equations.

Autonomous driving systems rely heavily on accurate 3D object detection for safe navigation and decision-making. This paper introduces a novel multi-view 3D object detection network designed to improve the accuracy and robustness of object detection in complex urban environments. Our approach integrates information from multiple camera perspectives using a frustum-based feature fusion module that effectively aggregates context from different viewpoints. This module reduces ambiguity and enhances feature representation for each object proposal. Furthermore, we employ a spatial attention mechanism to selectively focus on informative regions within each frustum, mitigating the impact of irrelevant background noise. Experimental results on the challenging KITTI dataset demonstrate that our proposed network significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving improvements in both detection accuracy and recall. The enhanced performance validates the effectiveness of our multi-view fusion and spatial attention strategies, offering a promising solution for robust 3D object detection in autonomous driving applications. Keywords: Autonomous Driving, 3D Object Detection, Multi-View Fusion, Deep Learning, Spatial Attention.

This paper presents the development of a Globally-scalable Automated Target Recognition (GATR) system, designed to accurately identify and classify targets in complex environments. The objective of GATR is to address the limitations of existing target recognition systems, which often struggle with scalability and accuracy in real-world scenarios. Our approach leverages a combination of deep learning algorithms and high-performance computing to enable rapid and reliable target detection. The GATR system utilizes a novel architecture that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with advanced feature extraction techniques, allowing for efficient processing of large datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of GATR, achieving high accuracy and robustness in various environments. The key contributions of this research include the development of a scalable and adaptable target recognition framework, which can be applied to a wide range of applications, including surveillance, autonomous systems, and defense. The GATR system has significant implications for enhancing situational awareness and decision-making in complex operational environments, and its globally-scalable design enables seamless integration with existing infrastructure. Key keywords: automated target recognition, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, scalable computing, computer vision.

A polarization camera has great potential for 3D reconstruction since the angle of polarization (AoP) of reflected light is related to an object's surface normal. In this paper, we propose a novel 3D reconstruction method called Polarimetric Multi-View Inverse Rendering (Polarimetric MVIR) that effectively exploits geometric, photometric, and polarimetric cues extracted from input multi-view color polarization images. We first estimate camera poses and an initial 3D model by geometric reconstruction with a standard structure-from-motion and multi-view stereo pipeline. We then refine the initial model by optimizing photometric and polarimetric rendering errors using multi-view RGB and AoP images, where we propose a novel polarimetric rendering cost function that enables us to effectively constrain each estimated surface vertex's normal while considering four possible ambiguous azimuth angles revealed from the AoP measurement. Experimental results using both synthetic and real data demonstrate that our Polarimetric MVIR can reconstruct a detailed 3D shape without assuming a specific polarized reflection depending on the material.

The objective is to develop a robust system that can accurately identify and classify various human activities from video data. Our method utilizes a deep learning-based framework that extracts skeleton information from RGB videos and leverages this data to recognize activities. The approach employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn spatial features from skeleton sequences, combined with a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model temporal dependencies. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our skeleton-focused approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets with significant improvements in accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed system has potential applications in various fields, including surveillance, healthcare, and human-computer interaction. Key contributions of this research include the development of a lightweight and efficient skeleton extraction algorithm and the introduction of a novel fusion strategy for combining spatial and temporal features. Relevant keywords for this study include human activity recognition, skeleton-based features, deep learning, CNN, RNN, and RGB video analysis.

This research addresses the challenge of moving object detection in dynamic scenes, an essential task in computer vision and surveillance systems. The study aims to develop an effective method that accurately identifies moving objects by leveraging contiguous outliers in a low-rank representation framework. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel algorithm that utilizes low-rank representation to model static background information while detecting moving objects as contiguous outliers. The algorithm exploits the low-rank properties of image sequences to separate background elements from dynamic objects efficiently. By analyzing deviations from the structured model, the method accurately identifies and isolates moving elements in the scene. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our approach surpasses traditional detection methods by offering improved accuracy in distinguishing moving objects within complex backgrounds. The proposed algorithm shows robustness to variations in lighting and background clutter, providing significant enhancements in recall and precision rates compared to existing techniques. Furthermore, it achieves real-time processing capabilities, making it suitable for practical deployment in surveillance environments. Conclusion/Implications: The study introduces a cutting-edge technique for moving object detection that enhances reliability and performance by identifying contiguous outliers in low-rank representations. This method presents potential applications in various domains, including security monitoring and intelligent transportation systems. By advancing the current state of object detection methodologies, the research contributes valuable insights into improving automated visual surveillance strategies. Key Keywords: moving object detection, low-rank representation, contiguous outliers, computer vision, surveillance systems.

Distributional Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a promising approach for capturing the full distribution of returns in reinforcement learning tasks, offering deeper insights into decision-making under uncertainty. This paper investigates the role of statistics and sampling techniques in enhancing the performance and stability of DRL algorithms. We propose a novel framework that integrates advanced statistical methods, including quantile regression and kernel density estimation, to improve the accuracy of return distribution predictions. Additionally, we explore the impact of different sampling strategies, such as stratified and importance sampling, on the efficiency of learning and convergence. Through extensive experiments on benchmark environments, our approach demonstrates significant improvements in both prediction accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing DRL methods. The results highlight the importance of leveraging statistical tools and optimized sampling techniques in DRL, offering new directions for future research. This work contributes to the growing body of knowledge in reinforcement learning by providing a robust and scalable framework for distributional value estimation, with potential applications in robotics, finance, and autonomous systems. **Keywords**: Distributional Reinforcement Learning, Quantile Regression, Kernel Density Estimation, Sampling Strategies, Decision-Making, Uncertainty.

Abstract: Copy-move image forgery is a prevalent technique in digital manipulation where a segment of an image is duplicated and inserted elsewhere within the same image to conceal or fabricate information. The reliable detection of such forgeries is critical for ensuring the integrity of digital visual content. This paper introduces a novel approach to copy-move forgery detection based on evolving circular domains coverage. The proposed method partitions the image into overlapping circular domains that dynamically evolve to more accurately capture structural redundancies resulting from copy-move operations. Feature extraction is performed within these adaptive circular regions, enhancing sensitivity to both small and irregularly shaped copied areas. The approach leverages advanced similarity metrics and robust matching algorithms to discriminate between genuine duplications and similar background patterns. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarking datasets demonstrate the method’s effectiveness, achieving superior detection accuracy and robustness compared to existing block-based and keypoint-based techniques. The results show improved performance, particularly in challenging scenarios involving complex textures, post-processing operations such as rotation or scaling, and low-contrast forgeries. This research contributes a flexible and efficient framework for tamper detection in digital images, offering potential applications in digital forensics, content authentication, and media security. Keywords: Image Forgery Detection, Copy-Move Forgery, Circular Domains, Digital Image Forensics, Tampering Localization, Image Authentication

This paper introduces SketchGen, an innovative approach to generating constrained Computer-Aided Design (CAD) sketches, addressing the challenges in automating the creation of detailed and precise design drafts that adhere to specific constraints. Traditional manual methods are often time-consuming and prone to errors, motivating the need for an automated solution. Methods/Approach: SketchGen employs advanced algorithms to capture design constraints and generate CAD sketches accordingly. Utilizing a combination of constraint-solving techniques and automated sketch generation algorithms, SketchGen translates abstract design requirements into precise geometrical representations. The methodology ensures that all produced sketches adhere to predetermined constraints, thus maintaining the integrity and accuracy required in professional CAD applications. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that SketchGen significantly improves efficiency in CAD sketch generation, reducing manual correction time and increasing overall design accuracy. Comparisons with existing CAD generation tools reveal that SketchGen not only accelerates the design process but also addresses a higher complexity of constraints with improved fidelity. User studies confirm the effectiveness of SketchGen in producing design outputs that align closely with user intentions and predefined constraints. Conclusion/Implications: SketchGen presents a substantial advancement in the field of CAD design, offering a robust tool for engineers and designers to automate the sketch generation process while ensuring compliance with critical design constraints. This research contributes to enhanced productivity in design workflows and opens pathways for further development in automated CAD applications. Potential applications of SketchGen include architecture, mechanical design, and any domain where precision CAD sketching is required. Key innovations in constraint satisfaction and automated generation provide a foundation for future exploration and refinement in automated design tools. Keywords: CAD, sketch generation, constraint-solving, automated design, design tools, CAD sketches, constraint satisfaction.
