This study introduces the CAMELS Multifield Dataset, a novel resource developed to facilitate research in astrophysics by leveraging artificial intelligence for learning the Universe's fundamental parameters. The dataset aims to provide a comprehensive representation of the Universe's large-scale structure, addressing key challenges in cosmology and galaxy formation. Methods/Approach: The dataset integrates state-of-the-art AI techniques with simulations to model various aspects of the Universe. By utilizing advanced machine learning algorithms, including neural networks and probabilistic models, the dataset captures multifield data, encompassing a wide range of cosmological parameters and environmental conditions. This approach allows for scalable and efficient analysis of complex astrophysical phenomena. Results/Findings: Preliminary results demonstrate that models trained with the CAMELS Multifield Dataset exhibit improved accuracy in predicting fundamental cosmological parameters compared to existing datasets. The integration of multifield data significantly enhances the precision of parameter estimation and model training, providing new insights into the underlying physics of the Universe's structure and evolution. Conclusion/Implications: The CAMELS Multifield Dataset represents a significant advancement in the application of artificial intelligence to cosmology, offering a robust tool for the scientific community. This dataset not only improves the accuracy of astrophysical simulations but also opens up new avenues for research in understanding the Universe's fundamental properties. Its implications extend to practical applications in observing and interpreting cosmological data, reinforcing the role of AI as a transformative tool in the field of astrophysics. Keywords: CAMELS, multifield dataset, cosmology, artificial intelligence, machine learning, galaxy formation, universe's parameters, astrophysical simulations.

Nghiên cứu về bướu tuyến mang tai tập trung vào việc sử dụng siêu âm để phân biệt giữa các khối u lành tính và ác tính. Siêu âm, một kỹ thuật chẩn đoán hình ảnh không xâm lấn, được đánh giá cao nhờ khả năng cung cấp thông tin chi tiết về cấu trúc và đặc điểm của khối u. Các đặc điểm siêu âm như kích thước, hình dạng, đường bờ, cấu trúc bên trong, sự hiện diện của vôi hóa và mạch máu được phân tích kỹ lưỡng. Kết quả cho thấy một số đặc điểm nhất định có liên quan mật thiết đến khả năng ác tính, bao gồm đường bờ không đều, cấu trúc không đồng nhất, và sự tăng sinh mạch máu bất thường. Tuy nhiên, không có đặc điểm đơn lẻ nào có thể xác định chắc chắn bản chất của khối u. Do đó, việc kết hợp nhiều yếu tố siêu âm và so sánh với các phương pháp chẩn đoán khác như sinh thiết đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc đưa ra quyết định điều trị phù hợp, giúp bác sĩ đưa ra đánh giá toàn diện và chính xác hơn về nguy cơ ác tính của bướu tuyến mang tai.

Trong bối cảnh chuyển đổi số diễn ra mạnh mẽ, việc đảm bảo an toàn và bảo mật cho các giao dịch điện tử trở nên vô cùng quan trọng. Ký số từ xa (Remote Signing) nổi lên như một giải pháp ưu việt, cho phép người dùng ký tài liệu số một cách an toàn và tiện lợi từ mọi nơi, mọi lúc, mà không cần đến các thiết bị lưu trữ khóa bí mật truyền thống như USB Token. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc xây dựng một hệ thống ký số nội bộ sử dụng công nghệ ký số từ xa, đáp ứng nhu cầu xác thực và bảo vệ tính toàn vẹn của các văn bản, hồ sơ trong một tổ chức. Hệ thống được thiết kế để tích hợp với các ứng dụng và quy trình nghiệp vụ hiện có, tạo thành một môi trường làm việc số khép kín và an toàn. Quá trình xây dựng hệ thống bao gồm việc lựa chọn các thuật toán mã hóa phù hợp, thiết kế kiến trúc hệ thống đảm bảo tính bảo mật và khả năng mở rộng, cũng như phát triển các giao diện lập trình ứng dụng (API) cho phép các ứng dụng khác tương tác với hệ thống ký số. Đặc biệt, nghiên cứu này đi sâu vào việc xây dựng module quản lý khóa bí mật tập trung, tuân thủ các tiêu chuẩn bảo mật quốc tế như chuẩn HSM (Hardware Security Module), đảm bảo an toàn tuyệt đối cho khóa bí mật của người dùng. Bên cạnh đó, hệ thống cũng được trang bị các cơ chế xác thực mạnh mẽ, như xác thực đa yếu tố (Multi-Factor Authentication), nhằm ngăn chặn các truy cập trái phép. Kết quả của nghiên cứu là một hệ thống ký số từ xa hoàn chỉnh, có khả năng đáp ứng các yêu cầu về bảo mật, tính toàn vẹn và khả năng xác thực của các giao dịch điện tử trong môi trường nội bộ. Hệ thống này không chỉ giúp nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động của tổ chức mà còn góp phần giảm thiểu rủi ro pháp lý liên quan đến các giao dịch điện tử. Hơn nữa, việc triển khai hệ thống ký số nội bộ còn giúp tổ chức chủ động hơn trong việc quản lý và kiểm soát các hoạt động ký số, đồng thời giảm sự phụ thuộc vào các nhà cung cấp dịch vụ bên ngoài. Cuối cùng, nghiên cứu này cũng đề xuất các hướng phát triển tiếp theo cho hệ thống, bao gồm việc tích hợp với các công nghệ mới như blockchain để tăng cường tính minh bạch và không thể chối bỏ của các giao dịch điện tử.

Vốn đầu tư gián tiếp nước ngoài (FII) đóng vai trò quan trọng trong thúc đẩy tăng trưởng kinh tế ở các quốc gia đang phát triển. Dòng vốn này có thể giúp các nước này tiếp cận nguồn tài chính cần thiết để đầu tư vào cơ sở hạ tầng, công nghệ và nguồn nhân lực, từ đó nâng cao năng suất và năng lực cạnh tranh. Tuy nhiên, FII cũng tiềm ẩn những rủi ro nhất định, bao gồm tính biến động cao và khả năng gây ra các cuộc khủng hoảng tài chính. Các nhà hoạch định chính sách cần có các biện pháp quản lý hiệu quả để tối đa hóa lợi ích và giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực của FII. Điều này bao gồm việc xây dựng một môi trường kinh tế vĩ mô ổn định, tăng cường giám sát hệ thống tài chính và phát triển các công cụ phòng ngừa rủi ro. Bên cạnh đó, việc thu hút và sử dụng hiệu quả FII đòi hỏi các quốc gia đang phát triển phải cải thiện chất lượng thể chế, nâng cao năng lực quản lý và tạo ra một môi trường đầu tư minh bạch và hấp dẫn.

Deep face recognition has achieved remarkable success, yet challenges remain in disentangling appearance and geometric features to improve robustness and generalization. This paper addresses the problem of enhancing face recognition performance by explicitly separating appearance-based attributes (e.g., texture, lighting) from geometric structures (e.g., pose, shape). We propose a novel framework that leverages disentangled representation learning to isolate these two critical components. Our approach employs a dual-branch neural network architecture, where one branch focuses on encoding appearance features, while the other captures geometric information. A disentanglement loss function is introduced to ensure minimal overlap between the two feature spaces, enabling more discriminative and interpretable representations. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art face recognition models, particularly in scenarios with significant pose variations and lighting changes. The results highlight the importance of disentangling appearance and geometry for robust face recognition. This work contributes a scalable and effective solution for improving deep face recognition systems, with potential applications in security, surveillance, and human-computer interaction. **Keywords**: Deep face recognition, disentangled representation, appearance features, geometric features, neural networks, pose invariance.

Objective: Real-time perception in autonomous systems is often hampered by the latency incurred when waiting for complete LiDAR sweeps before performing object detection. StrObe addresses this bottleneck by detecting objects on-the-fly directly from incoming LiDAR packets, significantly reducing end-to-end detection delay. Methods: We introduce a streaming pipeline that processes each 3D LiDAR packet as soon as it arrives. A lightweight packet-level feature extractor encodes partial point clouds into compact representations. These per-packet features are incrementally aggregated using a temporal fusion module, which maintains spatial coherence across packets. A detection head built on a modified voxel-based network then produces bounding-box predictions in real time. The entire architecture is optimized for low-latency inference on embedded GPUs. Results: Evaluated on the KITTI and nuScenes benchmarks, StrObe achieves comparable mean average precision to state-of-the-art offline detectors (within 2.5% mAP) while lowering average detection latency by 40–60%. In end-to-end tests, our system processes 10 ms LiDAR packets with under 15 ms delay per packet, enabling >20 Hz update rates. Compared to full-sweep methods, StrObe reduces the perception-to-action loop by up to 50 ms. Conclusion: By shifting object detection to the packet level, StrObe offers a practical, low-latency solution for safety-critical real-time applications in autonomous driving and robotics. Its modular design supports integration with diverse LiDAR sensors and downstream planning modules. Keywords: LiDAR streaming, real-time object detection, packet-level processing, temporal fusion, autonomous driving.

This research addresses the challenge of optimizing molecular structures by developing a novel approach that translates one molecular graph to another. The goal is to enhance molecular properties while maintaining essential structural integrity, thereby aiding in the efficient design of pharmaceuticals and materials. Methods/Approach: We propose a multimodal graph-to-graph translation model that leverages advanced graph neural networks (GNNs) to process and transform molecular graphs. The model integrates text data, structural information, and other relevant multimodal input to effectively learn and generalize the relationship between different molecular configurations. This approach incorporates a robust training regime with a focus on preserving crucial chemical properties. Results/Findings: Our model demonstrates significant improvements in molecular optimization tasks, outperforming traditional methods in terms of computational efficiency and optimization success rates. Key findings reveal that the multimodal approach provides greater accuracy in predicting optimal molecular configurations, as validated through multiple benchmark datasets showcasing improved stability and reactivity. Conclusion/Implications: The study introduces a groundbreaking multimodal graph-based framework that contributes to the field of molecular optimization by offering a potent tool for drug discovery and material innovation. This work paves the way for future exploration of multimodal learning in molecular sciences, highlighting potential applications in chemical synthesis and biotechnology development. The unique integration of multimodal data and graph translation offers a promising direction for computational chemistry and material science. Keywords: molecular optimization, graph-to-graph translation, graph neural networks, multimodal learning, pharmaceutical design, computational chemistry.

Zero-shot learning (ZSL) aims to recognize unseen classes by transferring knowledge from seen classes through semantic descriptions. This paper addresses the challenge of effectively leveraging class descriptions to improve ZSL performance. We propose a novel class description regularization (CDR) method that enforces consistency between predicted and provided class descriptions during training. Our approach utilizes a regularization term based on a similarity measure between predicted class embeddings generated by a deep neural network and the given textual descriptions, guiding the model to learn a more aligned feature space. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CDR significantly improves ZSL accuracy compared to existing methods. Specifically, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard ZSL benchmarks and generalized ZSL settings. The findings indicate that explicitly regularizing the learned feature space with class descriptions enhances the transferability of knowledge to unseen classes. This work contributes a simple yet effective regularization technique that can be readily integrated into existing ZSL frameworks, advancing the state-of-the-art in zero-shot recognition. Keywords: Zero-shot learning, class descriptions, regularization, semantic embedding, knowledge transfer, machine learning.

Đặt vấn đề: Điều dưỡng (ĐD) đóng vai trò chính trong phòng ngừa tổn thương do tỳ đè (TTDTĐ). Giảm tỷ lệ TTDTĐ là mục tiêu quan trọng trong chiến lược đảm bảo an toàn người bệnh (ATNB). Các chương trình đào tạo (CTĐT) quản lý TTDTĐ giúp ĐD đạt kiến thức, thực hành và thái độ cao hơn đáng kể so với các điều dưỡng không được đào tạo hoặc so với thời điểm trước đào tạo. Nghiên cứu được thực hiện nhằm xác định kiến thức, thực hành quản lý TTDTĐ của ĐD trước CTĐT, sau CTĐT và 2 tháng sau CTĐT. Đối tượng - Phương pháp: Thực hiện nghiên cứu bán can thiệp, đánh giá kiến thức và thực hành quản lý TTDTĐ trên 32 ĐD làm việc tại Khoa Hồi sức tích cực và Khoa Thần kinh, Bệnh viện Đại học Y dược Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh (BV ĐHYD) trước và sau chương trình đào tạo. This paper presents comprehensive datasets designed for the tasks of sheep identity recognition, age estimation, and weight prediction, addressing critical needs in modern livestock management and animal husbandry. The objective of this research is to facilitate the development and benchmarking of intelligent computer vision systems that enable accurate identification and biometric analysis of sheep using non-invasive image and annotation data. The datasets consist of high-resolution visual records from diverse sheep populations, labeled with unique identity markers, verified age information, and precise weight measurements. Advanced data acquisition protocols were employed to ensure consistency, quality, and variability under real-world farm conditions. The utility and effectiveness of the datasets are evaluated through baseline experiments employing state-of-the-art deep learning models for facial recognition, regression-based age estimation, and weight prediction. Results demonstrate notable improvements in recognition accuracy and estimation precision compared to existing resources, supporting robust model training and transfer learning applications. This work provides a valuable open resource for academic researchers and industry practitioners, enabling data-driven approaches to livestock monitoring, breeding selection, and welfare assessment. Keywords: sheep recognition, biometric analysis, age estimation, weight prediction, livestock datasets, computer vision, deep learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning and planning in complex action spaces, a crucial problem in the realm of artificial intelligence and robotics. Our focus is on developing strategies that enable efficient decision-making in environments characterized by vast and intricate sets of potential actions. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative framework combining reinforcement learning with advanced search algorithms to navigate these expansive action spaces effectively. By integrating a hierarchical learning structure with model-based planning, our approach allows for dynamic adaptation and optimization. Key components of our framework include a novel policy network design specifically tailored to manage high-dimensional action spaces and an adaptive learning mechanism that enhances exploration and exploitation balance. Results/Findings: Our experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to existing methods. The framework was tested across a range of complex simulated environments, showcasing its ability to scale efficiently and maintain robust performance. Compared with traditional approaches, our model achieved notably higher reward metrics and reduced computation times, confirming its effectiveness in managing complex action dynamics. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field by offering a scalable solution that enhances both the learning and planning phases in high-dimensional action landscapes. The proposed framework holds potential for applications in advanced AI systems, robotics, and autonomous agents requiring real-time decision-making capabilities. Our findings suggest a promising direction for future research in expanding the capabilities of AI systems to handle even more complex tasks with heightened efficiency and effectiveness. Keywords: complex action spaces, reinforcement learning, hierarchical learning, model-based planning, decision-making, AI, robotics.

The study aims to address the challenge of unsupervised action recognition by introducing a novel framework that leverages augmented skeleton-based contrastive action learning. Traditional methods often rely on labeled datasets, limiting scalability and applicability in real-world scenarios. Methods/Approach: We propose a Momentum Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network that enhances unsupervised learning through contrastive techniques. By integrating augmented skeleton data, our model captures rich temporal and spatial features of human actions. The use of a momentum update mechanism in LSTM networks facilitates robust and efficient learning of action dynamics without requiring labeled data. Results/Findings: Our approach demonstrates superior performance in action recognition tasks compared to existing unsupervised models. Extensive experiments on benchmark skeleton action datasets highlight the effectiveness of our method in accurately classifying actions. The results showcase improvements in recognition accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency, underscoring the robustness of the momentum LSTM in handling diverse and complex movement patterns. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides a significant contribution to the field of action recognition by presenting an innovative unsupervised learning technique that can be widely applicable to various human-computer interaction and surveillance systems. The use of augmented skeleton data with momentum LSTM opens new avenues for developing scalable, efficient, and adaptable action recognition systems in diverse environments. Key keywords include unsupervised learning, action recognition, augmented skeleton, momentum LSTM, and contrastive learning.

Đặt vấn đề: Bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ không do rượu (Non - alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease: NAFLD) là bệnh lý gan mạn phổ biến trên thế giới với tỉ lệ hiện mắc là gần 30%. Nhiều nghiên cứu đã chứng minh có mối liên hệ giữa NAFLD và gia tăng độ dày lớp nội trung mạc động mạch cảnh (ĐDLNTMĐMC). Từ đó, góp phần gián tiếp chứng minh được sự liên quan giữa NAFLD và các yếu tố nguy cơ tim mạch. Trên thế giới, đây là một vấn đề tương đối mới và hiện vẫn còn nhiều nghiên cứu đang thực hiện. Ở Việt Nam, mới chỉ có một vài đề tài về sự liên quan của NAFLD với bệnh tim mạch. Chính vì vậy, chúng tôi quyết định thực hiện đề tài “Liên quan giữa nhiễm mỡ và xơ hóa gan với độ dày lớp nội trung mạc động mạch cảnh ở bệnh nhân bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ không do rượu” để góp phần làm sáng tỏ vấn đề trên. Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang thực hiện tại phòng khám đa khoa trường đại học Y Khoa Phạm Ngọc Thạch và phòng khám Hòa Hảo từ 01/2020 đến 6/2020. Bệnh nhân có gan nhiễm mỡ trên siêu âm thỏa tiêu chuẩn nghiên cứu được thực hiện đo FibroScan và đo ĐDLNTMĐMC. Xử lý số liệu bằng phần mềm SPSS 20. Kết quả: Nghiên cứu khảo sát được 145 bệnh nhân từ tháng 01/2020 đến tháng 6/2020. Qua phương pháp đo Fibroscan-CAP và đo ĐDLNTMĐMC, chúng tôi ghi nhận được giá trị trung bình của ĐDLNTMĐMC ở hai bên của bốn mức độ nhiễm mỡ gan đều là 0,6mm và của bốn mức độ xơ hóa gan đều là 0,6 mm, riêng F3 là 0,7mm. Không có mối tương quan thuận giữa chỉ số nhiễm mỡ gan và xơ hóa gan trên Fibroscan-Cap với ĐDLNTMĐMC. Kết luận: Giá trị trung bình của ĐDLNTMĐMC ở hai bên của bốn mức độ nhiễm mỡ gan trên Fibroscan-CAP là gần bằng nhau, không có sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thống kê và không có sự liên quan giữa chỉ số nhiễm mỡ gan và xơ hóa gan trên Fibroscan-CAP với ĐDLNTMĐMC.

Gaze estimation, a critical task in human-computer interaction and computer vision, often relies on large-scale labeled datasets, which are costly and time-consuming to acquire. This paper introduces *GazeGAN*, a novel unpaired adversarial image generation framework designed to address the challenge of limited labeled data for gaze estimation. Unlike traditional methods that require paired training data, GazeGAN leverages unsupervised learning to generate synthetic gaze images that preserve the structural and semantic features of real-world gaze data. The proposed framework integrates a generative adversarial network (GAN) with a gaze-specific feature extractor, enabling the generation of high-quality, domain-consistent images without the need for explicit supervision. Experimental results demonstrate that GazeGAN significantly improves gaze estimation accuracy when used for data augmentation, outperforming existing methods on benchmark datasets. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robustness across diverse environments and lighting conditions, showcasing its potential for real-world applications. This work contributes a scalable and efficient solution to the gaze estimation problem, reducing dependency on labeled datasets and advancing the state-of-the-art in unpaired image generation for computer vision tasks. **Keywords**: Gaze estimation, GAN, unpaired image generation, adversarial learning, data augmentation, computer vision.

This paper provides a comprehensive review of the early classification of time series data, an area of increasing interest due to its potential to enable timely decision-making across various domains such as healthcare, finance, and industry. The objective is to summarize current methodologies and assess their applications and effectiveness. Methods/Approach: The paper systematically categorizes existing approaches for early time series classification, including probabilistic models, machine learning algorithms, and hybrid techniques. Recent advances and innovations are highlighted, focusing on algorithms that enhance prediction accuracy while minimizing the length of time series required for reliable early classification. Results/Findings: The review identifies key patterns and trends in the literature, noting improvements in computational efficiency and prediction performance. Detailed comparisons of existing methods are presented, with performance metrics such as accuracy, speed, and computational cost systematically evaluated across various datasets and scenarios. The findings indicate a significant increase in the deployment of deep learning techniques, which offer promising results but also highlight challenges such as data scarcity and interpretability. Conclusion/Implications: This study contributes by synthesizing knowledge from diverse techniques and applications, offering insights into the trade-offs and challenges associated with early time series classification. The review underscores the importance of continuing research into hybrid models and the integration of domain knowledge to enhance early classification accuracy. The implications for real-time applications and the potential for these technologies to advance predictive analytics in critical sectors are discussed. Key Keywords: early classification, time series, machine learning, deep learning, predictive analytics, hybrid models.

Sleep staging is a crucial component in diagnosing and managing sleep disorders. However, current automated systems often lack interpretability, posing challenges for medical practitioners who rely on expert guidelines. This research introduces SLEEPER, an innovative framework designed to enhance interpretability in sleep staging by leveraging prototypes derived from expert rules. Methods/Approach: SLEEPER employs a hybrid model combining machine learning techniques with domain-specific knowledge encapsulated in expert-drafted rules. The framework develops representative prototypes that align with traditional sleep staging criteria, facilitating a transparent decision-making process. These prototypes act as reference points that correspond to well-defined sleep stages, ensuring alignment with medical expert expectations. Results/Findings: Our evaluations demonstrate that SLEEPER achieves a significant balance between accuracy and interpretability, matching the performance of state-of-the-art machine learning models while providing clear insights into its decision processes. Comparative studies show that SLEEPER's ability to explain its predictions outperforms existing black-box algorithms, making it a superior choice for clinical applications. Conclusion/Implications: SLEEPER advances the field of automated sleep staging by integrating interpretability at its core, providing a viable solution for healthcare providers who require transparent models. The framework's prototype-based approach ensures that its decisions remain traceable and in accordance with established medical guidelines, fostering trust and facilitating its implementation in clinical settings. Future work could expand SLEEPER's adaptability to other domains requiring interpretable artificial intelligence solutions. Keywords: Sleep staging, interpretable machine learning, expert rules, prototypes, automated diagnosis, healthcare AI.

Estimating causal effects from observational data is a fundamental challenge across various scientific disciplines. This paper introduces Graph Intervention Networks (GIN), a novel framework that leverages graph neural networks to model and estimate causal effects under complex causal structures. GIN learns node representations that encode both observational and interventional distributions, enabling accurate estimation of treatment effects even in the presence of confounding. The proposed method employs a specialized graph neural network architecture coupled with an intervention module to simulate counterfactual outcomes. We evaluate GIN on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art causal effect estimation methods. Results show that GIN achieves significant improvements in accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios with high-dimensional data and complex causal dependencies. The framework provides a valuable tool for researchers seeking to understand and quantify causal relationships from observational data. Key words: Causal Inference, Causal Effect Estimation, Graph Neural Networks, Intervention, Counterfactual Reasoning, Observational Data.

This paper introduces Graph-SIM, a novel graph-based approach for spatiotemporal interaction modelling to predict pedestrian actions. The objective is to improve the accuracy of predicting pedestrian behavior in complex scenarios by capturing the interactions between pedestrians, vehicles, and infrastructure. Our method utilizes a graph neural network to model the dynamic relationships between entities in a scene, incorporating both spatial and temporal information. The results show that Graph-SIM outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in predicting pedestrian actions, achieving a significant reduction in error rate. The key contributions of this research include the development of a graph-based framework for spatiotemporal interaction modelling and the demonstration of its effectiveness in pedestrian action prediction. This work has important implications for autonomous vehicles, smart cities, and surveillance systems, highlighting the potential of graph-based models for improving safety and efficiency in dynamic environments. Key keywords: graph neural networks, spatiotemporal interaction modelling, pedestrian action prediction, autonomous vehicles, smart cities.

The objective of this research is to address the challenges in 3D data processing by developing an innovative point embedding framework. Traditional methods often struggle with efficiently capturing the intricate geometric details inherent in 3D data. Our approach leverages a novel point embedding strategy, designed to enhance the representation of 3D data points and improve processing accuracy. The method involves a deep learning model that adapts transformer architectures for embedding point cloud data, allowing for more robust and discriminative feature representation. Key findings from our experiments demonstrate that our point embedding approach significantly outperforms existing techniques in various 3D data processing tasks, such as object recognition and segmentation, across multiple benchmark datasets. Results indicate a marked increase in both precision and recall metrics. The implications of this research are substantial, offering advancements in domains like autonomous driving, augmented reality, and robotics where precise 3D data interpretation is critical. Our study contributes a novel methodology that facilitates better generalization and scalability for 3D data processing, with potential applications in enhancing 3D reconstruction and analysis workflows. Keywords include point embedding, 3D data processing, transformer architectures, object recognition, and deep learning.

This paper proposes a novel approach to sequence labeling using Gaussian Process pseudo-likelihood models. The objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of sequence labeling tasks, such as part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition, by leveraging the flexibility and expressiveness of Gaussian Processes. Our method employs a pseudo-likelihood framework to model the dependencies between labels in a sequence, allowing for the capture of complex relationships and patterns. We utilize a sparse approximation to scale the model to long sequences and large datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. The key findings include improved handling of long-range dependencies and better robustness to noise and outliers. Our research contributes to the development of more accurate and reliable sequence labeling models, with potential applications in natural language processing, bioinformatics, and other fields. Key keywords: Gaussian Process, pseudo-likelihood, sequence labeling, natural language processing, sparse approximation.

The automation of deep brain stimulation (DBS) procedures necessitates precise localization of stimulation electrodes, which is critical for the safety and efficacy of treatment. This paper addresses the challenge of electrode localization by introducing a novel trajectory-based segmentation approach. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative model that employs trajectory-based segmentation to automatically detect and localize stimulation electrodes in DBS procedures. The approach integrates advanced image processing techniques with neural network algorithms to accurately delineate the electrode trajectories from surrounding brain structures. Using a robust dataset, the system was trained to recognize patterns associated with electrode positions, enhancing the model's precision and reliability. Results/Findings: The implemented approach demonstrated a high degree of accuracy in electrode localization, with performance metrics showing significant improvements over traditional manual methods and existing automated techniques. The system not only reduced the error rates in electrode positioning but also increased the speed of localization, providing real-time capabilities suitable for clinical settings. Comparisons with current manual techniques revealed a marked enhancement in both efficiency and accuracy. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel trajectory-based segmentation methodology for the automatic localization of deep brain stimulation electrodes, enhancing the precision and reliability of such medical procedures. The findings highlight the potential of integrating advanced segmentation algorithms in clinical workflows, which can lead to improved treatment outcomes and reduced operative time. This approach can be further extended to other neural interventions requiring precise electrode placement, offering promising applications in the field of neurotechnology. Keywords: deep brain stimulation, electrode localization, trajectory-based segmentation, image processing, neural networks, medical imaging, neurotechnology.

This paper addresses the challenge of achieving high-quality image inpainting, which involves completing missing or corrupted parts of an image with plausible content. Traditional inpainting methods often struggle with producing realistic and coherent results, especially in complex and high-resolution scenarios. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel Pyramid-Context Encoder Network designed to enhance image completion tasks. The model leverages a hierarchical pyramid structure to capture multi-scale contextual information, enabling more accurate and contextually aware predictions. The network incorporates an advanced encoder architecture, which efficiently processes and integrates spatial and semantic information across different scales, promoting a cohesive image reconstruction process. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate the superior performance of the Pyramid-Context Encoder Network across various benchmark datasets. The proposed model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of visual quality and quantitative metrics, particularly in handling challenging inpainting scenarios involving complex structures and textures. Comparative analyses highlight the network's capability to maintain high fidelity and preserve fine details in the reconstructed images. Conclusion/Implications: The Pyramid-Context Encoder Network presents significant advancements in the field of image inpainting, offering a robust solution for high-quality visual content restoration. This approach not only improves the aesthetic appeal of inpainted images but also has potential applications in fields such as digital media restoration, virtual reality, and content creation. The insights from this study pave the way for further research into context-aware deep learning models for image processing tasks. Key Keywords: image inpainting, Pyramid-Context Encoder Network, deep learning, multi-scale context, high-quality reconstruction, digital image restoration.

The increasing adoption of surround-view camera systems in autonomous driving and intelligent transportation necessitates robust vehicle re-identification (Re-ID) techniques to enhance tracking and monitoring capabilities. This paper addresses the challenge of accurately identifying and re-identifying vehicles across multiple camera views in complex urban environments. We propose a novel deep learning-based framework that leverages multi-view feature fusion and spatial-temporal consistency to improve vehicle Re-ID performance. Our approach integrates a transformer-based architecture to capture long-range dependencies and a lightweight attention mechanism to focus on discriminative vehicle features, such as color, shape, and license plates. The proposed model is trained and evaluated on a large-scale dataset comprising diverse urban scenarios, demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods. Experimental results show a significant improvement in mean average precision (mAP) and rank-1 accuracy, achieving state-of-the-art performance. The framework’s efficiency and scalability make it suitable for real-time deployment in surround-view camera systems. This research contributes to advancing vehicle Re-ID by addressing key challenges in multi-view data integration and feature representation, with potential applications in traffic management, surveillance, and autonomous driving systems. **Keywords**: Vehicle Re-Identification, Surround-View Cameras, Deep Learning, Transformer, Multi-View Fusion, Autonomous Driving.

This paper introduces a novel approach for generating high-quality bokeh effects in images through depth-aware blending of smoothed images. The objective is to create visually appealing out-of-focus blur, mimicking the aesthetic qualities of professional photography. Our method utilizes a depth map, either captured or estimated, to guide the blending process. Specifically, we generate multiple smoothed versions of the input image with varying blur radii and then employ a depth-aware weighting scheme to combine these blurred images. This blending strategy allows for precise control over the blur amount at different depths, resulting in a realistic and customizable bokeh effect. We compare our method against existing bokeh simulation techniques and demonstrate improved performance in terms of visual quality and realism. Experimental results show that our approach effectively reduces artifacts, such as halos, often present in other methods, leading to a more natural and pleasing bokeh effect. This technique is applicable to both still images and video, offering a versatile solution for enhancing visual content. Keywords: Bokeh effect, Depth-aware blending, Image smoothing, Image processing, Blur simulation.

Dưới đây là kết quả sớm về hiệu quả của phương pháp này: - Phương pháp can thiệp dẫn lưu qua da đã giúp cứu sống nhiều người bị viêm tụy hoại tử nặng. - Kết quả sớm cho thấy tỷ lệ sống sót của bệnh nhân sau khi điều trị bằng can thiệp dẫn lưu qua da cao hơn so với những người không được điều trị. - Phương pháp này cũng giúp giảm thiểu các biến chứng và giảm tỷ lệ tử vong do viêm tụy hoại tử. Tuy nhiên, cần lưu ý rằng phương pháp can thiệp dẫn lưu qua da chỉ được áp dụng trong những trường hợp nghiêm trọng và cần được thực hiện bởi các chuyên gia y tế có kinh nghiệm.

Phân cấp các khái niệm (taxonomy) trong một miền lĩnh vực cụ thể là một nhiệm vụ quan trọng trong việc tổ chức và hiểu sâu hơn về các khái niệm liên quan. Học máy đã trở thành công cụ mạnh mẽ để tự động hóa quá trình này, giúp xây dựng các hệ thống phân cấp phức tạp một cách hiệu quả và chính xác. Các phương pháp học máy, đặc biệt là học sâu và học có giám sát, được áp dụng để phân loại và sắp xếp các khái niệm dựa trên mối quan hệ ngữ nghĩa và cấu trúc dữ liệu. Quá trình này thường bắt đầu bằng việc thu thập và tiền xử lý dữ liệu, sau đó sử dụng các mô hình như mạng nơ-ron, cây quyết định hoặc phương pháp nhúng từ (word embedding) để trích xuất đặc trưng và xác định mối quan hệ giữa các khái niệm. Các kỹ thuật như phân cụm (clustering) và phân lớp (classification) được sử dụng để nhóm các khái niệm tương đồng và xác định cấu trúc phân cấp. Đánh giá hiệu suất của các mô hình thường dựa trên các chỉ số như độ chính xác, độ phủ và F1-score. Ứng dụng của việc phân cấp khái niệm bằng học máy rất đa dạng, từ xây dựng từ điển chuyên ngành, hỗ trợ tìm kiếm thông tin, đến phát triển hệ thống trí tuệ nhân tạo trong các lĩnh vực như y tế, giáo dục và công nghệ thông tin. Tuy nhiên, thách thức lớn nhất vẫn là xử lý các khái niệm đa nghĩa, thiếu dữ liệu huấn luyện và đảm bảo tính nhất quán trong hệ thống phân cấp. Nghiên cứu trong lĩnh vực này tiếp tục phát triển với sự kết hợp của các phương pháp học máy tiên tiến và kỹ thuật xử lý ngôn ngữ tự nhiên, hứa hẹn mang lại những hệ thống phân cấp khái niệm ngày càng thông minh và chính xác hơn.

With the abundance of data in recent years, interesting challenges are posed in the area of recommender systems. Producing high quality recommendations with scalability and performance is the need of the hour. Singular Value Decomposition(SVD) based recommendation algorithms have been leveraged to produce better results. In this paper, we extend the SVD technique further for scalability and performance in the context of 1) multi-threading 2) multiple computational units (with the use of Graphical Processing Units) and 3) distributed computation. We propose block based matrix factorization (BMF) paired with SVD. This enabled us to take advantage of SVD over basic matrix factorization(MF) while taking advantage of parallelism and scalability through BMF. We used Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) platform and related hardware for leveraging Graphical Processing Unit (GPU) along with block based SVD to demonstrate the advantages in terms of performance and memory.

Accurate forecasting of human trajectory and pose dynamics is crucial for applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and surveillance. This paper introduces TRiPOD, a novel framework for predicting future human movement and pose in complex, unconstrained environments. TRiPOD leverages a recurrent neural network architecture to model the temporal dependencies between trajectory and pose, incorporating contextual information from the surrounding scene through a graph attention mechanism. Our approach predicts both future 2D locations and full 3D human poses, accounting for complex interactions and occlusions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that TRiPOD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both trajectory and pose forecasting accuracy, particularly in crowded and dynamic scenes. These improvements highlight TRiPOD's ability to learn intricate human motion patterns and provide robust predictions in real-world scenarios. Keywords: Human Trajectory Forecasting, Pose Estimation, Motion Prediction, Recurrent Neural Networks, Graph Attention Networks.

Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a pivotal approach for automating the design of deep learning models, yet its computational cost and inefficiency remain significant challenges. This paper investigates the role of Supernet in enhancing NAS by providing a unified framework for evaluating multiple architectures simultaneously. The objective is to explore how Supernet-based approaches reduce search time and computational resources while maintaining competitive model performance. We propose a novel Supernet optimization strategy that leverages weight sharing and gradient-based architecture updates to efficiently traverse the search space. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 40% reduction in search time compared to traditional NAS methods, while delivering architectures with comparable or superior accuracy on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. Furthermore, we analyze the trade-offs between search efficiency and model performance, providing insights into the scalability of Supernet-based NAS for large-scale applications. The findings highlight the potential of Supernet as a foundational tool for advancing NAS, offering a balance between computational efficiency and architectural innovation. This research contributes to the growing body of work on efficient NAS techniques, with implications for accelerating the development of high-performance neural networks in resource-constrained environments. **Keywords**: Neural Architecture Search (NAS), Supernet, weight sharing, gradient-based optimization, deep learning, model efficiency.

Learning from multiple-relational data which contains noise, ambiguities, or duplicate entities is essential to a wide range of applications such as statistical inference based on Web Linked Data, recommender systems, computational biology, and natural language processing. These tasks usually require working with very large and complex datasets - e.g., the Web graph - however, current approaches to multi-relational learning are not practical for such scenarios due to their high computational complexity and poor scalability on large data. In this paper, we propose a novel and scalable approach for multi-relational factorization based on consensus optimization. Our model, called ConsMRF, is based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) framework, which enables us to optimize each target relation using a smaller set of parameters than the state-of-the-art competitors in this task. Due to ADMM's nature, ConsMRF can be easily parallelized which makes it suitable for large multi-relational data. Experiments on large Web datasets - derived from DBpedia, Wikipedia and YAGO - show the efficiency and performance improvement of ConsMRF over strong competitors. In addition, ConsMRF near-linear scalability indicates great potential to tackle Web-scale problem sizes.

This paper investigates the application of transfer learning with deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for the tasks of gender recognition and age estimation from facial images. The primary objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of these tasks, particularly when training data is limited. We leverage pre-trained CNN models, specifically ResNet and VGG architectures, on large-scale image datasets like ImageNet, and then fine-tune them using facial image datasets. Our approach involves experimenting with different fine-tuning strategies and data augmentation techniques to optimize performance. Experimental results demonstrate that transfer learning significantly enhances the accuracy of both gender recognition and age estimation compared to training CNNs from scratch. Specifically, we achieve state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, with improvements of up to 5% in gender recognition accuracy and a reduction of 10% in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for age estimation. The findings highlight the effectiveness of transfer learning for facial attribute prediction, offering a practical solution for applications with limited data. Keywords: Transfer Learning, CNN, Gender Recognition, Age Estimation, Deep Learning, Facial Analysis.

Mục tiêu: Mô tả đặc điểm hình ảnh cắt lớp vi tính (CLVT) của viêm túi thừa đại tràng (VTTĐT) có biến chứng theo WSES 2020. Đối tượng và phương pháp NC: Tất cả các bệnh nhân có kết quả phẫu thuật và hoặc giải phẫu bệnh VTTĐT được nghiên cứu hồi cứu so sánh với hình ảnh cắt lớp vi tính trong thời gian từ tháng 01/2022 đến hết tháng 08/2024. Kết quả: Nghiên cứu có 104 bệnh nhân, trong đó VTTĐT bên phải là 45 và VTTĐT bên trái là 75. Tuổi trung bình của BN VTTĐT có biến chứng là 55,59 ± 15,7. Tỉ lệ nam/nữ là 1,85. Túi thừa viêm biến chứng thủng dễ quan sát hình ảnh trực tiếp ở bên phải hơn. Dày thành đại tràng, thâm nhiễm mỡ nhiều, sự diện của túi thừa, dịch và khí cạnh đại tràng áp xe, viêm phúc mạc lan tỏa là các dấu hiệu thường gặp, rò và tắc ruột chiếm tỷ lệ thấp nhưng cần được quan tâm. Dịch lan tỏa và khí xa đại tràng chỉ gặp ở VTTĐT bên trái. Các giai đoạn của VTTĐT có BC bên phải theo WSES 2020 bao gồm 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3, 4 chiếm tỉ lệ lần lợt là 64,4%, 11,1%, 17,8%, 4,4%, 0%, 0% ; bên trái chiếm tỉ lệ lần lượt là 25,3%, 16%, 17,3%, 8%, 6,7%, 22,7%. VTTĐT bên trái có biến chứng nặng hơn so với bên phải, sự khác biệt này có ý nghĩa thống kê (p = 0,000 < 0,05). Kết luận: Các dấu hiệu hình ảnh thường gặp của VTTĐT có biến chứng theo WSES 2020 là dày thành đại tràng > 10mm; thâm nhiễm mỡ nhiều với đa túi thừa, sung huyết mạch máu mạc treo, khí và dịch cạnh đại tràng, áp xe. This paper introduces LT-GAN, a novel self-supervised Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework designed to enhance image generation through latent transformation detection. The primary objective of LT-GAN is to address the challenge of learning meaningful latent representations in unsupervised settings, which is critical for generating high-quality and diverse images. Unlike traditional GANs, LT-GAN incorporates a self-supervised mechanism that detects and leverages latent transformations to improve the discriminator’s ability to distinguish between real and generated data. The proposed approach involves training the generator and discriminator to jointly learn latent space transformations, enabling the model to capture intricate data distributions more effectively. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and CelebA, demonstrate that LT-GAN outperforms existing GAN variants in terms of image quality and diversity, as measured by metrics such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS). Additionally, LT-GAN exhibits improved stability during training, reducing common issues like mode collapse. The results highlight the effectiveness of self-supervised latent transformation detection in advancing GAN-based image synthesis. The key contribution of this work lies in its innovative integration of self-supervised learning with GANs, offering a new direction for improving unsupervised generative models. LT-GAN has potential applications in areas such as image editing, data augmentation, and synthetic data generation for training machine learning models. This research underscores the importance of leveraging latent space dynamics to enhance generative modeling, paving the way for future advancements in the field. **Keywords**: GAN, self-supervised learning, latent transformation, image generation, unsupervised learning, generative models.

Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) have achieved remarkable success in various domains, but their inherent complexity often leads to a lack of interpretability, hindering trust and adoption in critical applications. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of existing techniques for interpreting ANNs, categorizing them based on their approach and scope. We examine methods that focus on understanding individual neurons, connections, and layers, as well as techniques that provide global explanations of network behavior. The survey also evaluates the strengths and limitations of each approach, considering factors such as computational cost, applicability to different network architectures, and the type of insights they provide. Furthermore, we discuss the evaluation metrics used to assess the quality of interpretations and identify key challenges and open research questions in the field. This work aims to serve as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners seeking to enhance the transparency and trustworthiness of ANNs. Keywords: Artificial Neural Networks, Interpretability, Explainable AI, Deep Learning, Survey.

This paper addresses the challenge of estimating light direction and color from a single image, a critical task in computer vision with applications in augmented reality, 3D reconstruction, and image editing. Traditional methods often rely on complex setups or multiple images, limiting their practicality. To overcome these limitations, we propose a deep regression-based approach that leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to directly predict light direction and color from a single input image. Our method employs a carefully designed network architecture trained on a diverse dataset of synthetic and real-world images, ensuring robustness across varying lighting conditions and scene complexities. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed model also generalizes well to unseen data, making it suitable for real-world applications. This work contributes a novel, end-to-end solution that simplifies light estimation while maintaining high precision, paving the way for more efficient and accessible tools in computer vision and graphics. **Keywords**: light estimation, deep regression, single-image analysis, convolutional neural networks, computer vision, augmented reality.

Salient object detection aims to identify and segment the most visually distinctive objects within an image. This paper introduces a novel Multi-scale Interactive Network (MINet) designed to improve the accuracy and robustness of salient object detection, particularly in complex scenes. Our approach leverages a multi-scale feature extraction module coupled with an interactive fusion mechanism. Specifically, we employ a hierarchical convolutional neural network to capture features at varying scales, enabling the model to understand both local details and global context. The interactive fusion module then selectively aggregates these multi-scale features, allowing for efficient information exchange and suppression of irrelevant background noise. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that MINet achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of precision, recall, and F-measure. The proposed network exhibits superior generalization capability and is more robust to challenging scenarios with cluttered backgrounds and complex object shapes. The code and trained models will be made publicly available. Keywords: Salient Object Detection, Deep Learning, Multi-scale Feature Fusion, Interactive Network, Computer Vision.

The paper presents a novel quantum computational method tailored to address correspondence problems among point sets, a fundamental challenge in various fields such as computer vision and pattern recognition. These problems typically involve identifying relationships or mappings between different sets of points, crucial for tasks like image matching and data alignment. Methods: Leveraging the principles of quantum computing, this study introduces a quantum algorithm that utilizes quantum entanglement and superposition to efficiently process and solve point correspondence issues. The proposed approach is designed to exploit the inherent parallelism of quantum systems, potentially offering a significant improvement in processing time over classical methods. Results: Experimental results demonstrate the quantum algorithm's capability to solve point set correspondence problems with improved speed and scalability compared to traditional computational techniques. The study showcases comparative analyses with leading classical algorithms, revealing the proposed method's superior performance in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy. Conclusion: This research contributes a pioneering technique in the intersection of quantum computing and point set analysis, opening pathways for advancements in complex data processing tasks. The implementation of quantum-based solutions in correspondence problems highlights the potential of quantum technology to transform computational paradigms in high-dimensional data analysis. Future applications could extend to areas such as biological data assessment and large-scale image analysis, emphasizing the algorithm's versatility and impact on the broader field of quantum computation in data science. Keywords: Quantum computing, point set correspondence, quantum algorithms, image matching, data alignment, computational efficiency, entanglement, superposition.

This paper addresses the challenge of clustering attributed networks by proposing a novel approach that leverages variational co-embedding learning. The study aims to improve the effectiveness of clustering by jointly embedding nodes and attributes in a unified latent space, thereby capturing both network structure and attribute information. Methods/Approach: We introduce a variational co-embedding framework that integrates network topology and node attributes through a joint learning process. This method employs a probabilistic generative model to derive embeddings that reflect the inherent community structure of the network. The proposed approach optimizes a variational objective that facilitates the simultaneous inferencing of both structural and attributed patterns within the network. Results/Findings: Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art clustering algorithms. The findings reveal that variational co-embedding yields higher accuracy and robustness, particularly in complex attributed networks where traditional methods struggle with noise and sparsity. Additionally, comparative evaluations indicate superior partition quality and enhanced discriminative capability of node representations. Conclusion/Implications: The research contributes a powerful tool for attributed network analysis by introducing a versatile co-embedding mechanism. This has implications for various applications, including social network analysis, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems, where understanding complex interactions is critical. Our approach not only advances the state of network clustering techniques but also paves the way for further exploration into variational methods for complex data structures. Keywords: attributed networks, clustering, variational co-embedding, network topology, generative models, node attributes.

Predicting driver intention at intersections is critical for developing effective Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) and autonomous vehicles. This paper introduces a novel deep learning model incorporating an attention mechanism to enhance the accuracy and reliability of driver intention prediction. Our approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract spatial features from the driving scene, which are then fed into a recurrent neural network (RNN) with a temporal attention mechanism to capture the dynamic evolution of driving behavior. The attention mechanism focuses on the most relevant historical features for predicting future actions. We evaluate our model on a real-world driving dataset and demonstrate significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly in complex intersection scenarios. The results show that the attention mechanism effectively identifies crucial cues for intention recognition, leading to more reliable predictions. This research contributes to safer and more efficient autonomous driving by enabling proactive decision-making based on accurate driver intention prediction. Keywords: Driver Intention Prediction, Deep Learning, Attention Mechanism, Autonomous Driving, Intersection Management, ADAS.

Accurate localization in aerial imagery is a critical challenge in applications such as autonomous navigation, urban planning, and disaster response. This paper introduces LocGAN, a novel generative adversarial network (GAN)-based framework designed to enhance localization accuracy using grid maps derived from aerial imagery. The primary objective of this research is to address the limitations of existing methods, which often struggle with scalability and precision in complex environments. LocGAN leverages a dual-network architecture, combining a generator to synthesize high-resolution grid maps and a discriminator to refine localization predictions. The proposed approach integrates spatial and contextual features from aerial images, enabling robust localization even in densely populated or occluded areas. Experimental results demonstrate that LocGAN outperforms traditional methods, achieving a 15% improvement in localization accuracy across diverse datasets. Furthermore, the framework exhibits superior generalization capabilities, maintaining high performance in varying environmental conditions. The findings highlight the potential of LocGAN for real-world applications, offering a scalable and efficient solution for aerial imagery localization. This research contributes to the advancement of GAN-based techniques in geospatial analysis and provides a foundation for future developments in autonomous systems and remote sensing technologies. **Keywords**: Localization, Aerial Imagery, Grid Maps, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), LocGAN, Autonomous Systems, Remote Sensing.

Our contributions include the introduction of a novel logical framework for generative modeling, the development of a new class of discriminative models, and the demonstration of improved performance in real-world applications, making this study a valuable addition to the existing literature on machine learning, logic-based modeling, and artificial intelligence.

This paper aims to provide a comprehensive tutorial and survey on Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (SNE), a powerful dimensionality reduction technique widely used for data visualization. We focus on its underlying principles and explore the use of Gaussian and Student-t distributions for optimizing the embeddings, highlighting the distinctions and applications of each. Methods/Approach: We examine the theoretical foundation of SNE, discussing its ability to preserve local data structures in low-dimensional spaces. By delving into the mathematical formulations, we compare the implementations and benefits of employing Gaussian and Student-t distributions within the SNE framework. The analysis includes a detailed breakdown of algorithmic steps, regularization techniques, and computational considerations. Results/Findings: Through a series of experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, we evaluate the performance of Gaussian-SNE and t-SNE. Our findings reveal significant differences in how each distribution handles outliers and density variations. The Student-t distribution's robustness in managing crowding effects and maintaining data spread enables a more faithful representation of high-dimensional data. Conclusion/Implications: This paper elucidates the strengths and limitations of Gaussian and Student-t based SNE approaches, providing insights into their suitability for various data types and visualization tasks. Our survey and tutorial serve as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners looking to apply these methods in data-driven domains such as bioinformatics, social network analysis, and machine learning. By highlighting the nuances of SNE, we contribute to the broader understanding and advancement of dimensionality reduction techniques. Keywords: Stochastic Neighbor Embedding, SNE, t-SNE, Gaussian distribution, Student-t distribution, dimensionality reduction, data visualization, machine learning.

The burgeoning field of causal discovery aims to unravel the underlying mechanisms in complex systems by identifying causal relationships. Traditional approaches often rely on observational data, which limits their effectiveness in real-world applications where interventions are possible. This paper introduces a novel framework for collaborative causal discovery using atomic interventions to enhance the accuracy and robustness of causal inference. Methods/Approach: We propose a collaborative approach that integrates atomic interventions—minimal and highly controlled perturbations to the system—with existing causal discovery algorithms. Our method leverages both observational and interventional data to improve the precision of causal structures. The framework is designed to facilitate scalable and efficient collaboration across distributed systems and datasets, using a blend of statistical modeling and machine learning techniques. Results/Findings: Through extensive experiments, our approach demonstrates significant improvements in identifying true causal relationships compared to traditional methods. Our collaborative causal discovery framework outperforms conventional algorithms particularly in complex, high-dimensional datasets where purely observational methods struggle. Furthermore, the use of atomic interventions allows for a more granular analysis of causal mechanisms, yielding insights that would otherwise remain obscured. Conclusion/Implications: The proposed framework advances the field of causal discovery by providing a robust tool for researchers and practitioners to accurately infer causality in diverse domains. Our findings suggest that incorporating atomic interventions can greatly enhance causal inference, offering potential applications in fields such as biology, economics, and social sciences. This research paves the way for more sophisticated causal models that better reflect the dynamics of real-world systems. Keywords: Causal discovery, atomic interventions, collaborative framework, observational data, interventional data, machine learning, causal inference.

Transfer learning relaxes the hypothesis that the training data must be independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) with the test data, which motivates us to use transfer learning to solve the problem of insufficient training data. This paper investigates the application of posterior sampling methods in reinforcement learning (RL) contexts, particularly evaluating worst-case regret bounds to assess performance efficiency. The study aims to enhance our understanding of how stochastic decision-making techniques perform under adversarial scenarios, addressing gaps in current RL frameworks related to computational efficiency and robustness. Methods: We propose a novel approach leveraging posterior sampling to derive and analyze regret bounds in reinforcement learning environments. Our method incorporates Bayesian updates and explores the asymptotic behavior of regret, offering a direct comparison with other established RL strategies, such as Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) and Epsilon-Greedy algorithms. Theoretical analysis is conducted to evaluate its efficacy against worst-case adversities. Results: Our findings demonstrate that the proposed posterior sampling approach achieves competitive regret bounds, closely approximating the optimal rates under varying conditions. Notably, our method exhibits significant improvements in computational complexity over traditional strategies, while maintaining a high degree of robustness in adversarial setups. Detailed simulations corroborate these theoretical predictions, showcasing superior performance across a range of simulated environments. Conclusion: The research contributes a new perspective on implementing posterior sampling for RL, emphasizing its potential for achieving near-optimal performance with manageable computational resources. This framework broadens the applicability of RL solutions in complex, adversarial domains, offering promising insights for future developments in autonomous systems and decision-making algorithms. Keywords such as reinforcement learning, posterior sampling, regret bounds, Bayesian methods, and adversarial environments highlight the core themes of this study.

This paper introduces a novel self-supervised exploration method for deep reinforcement learning, addressing the challenge of sparse rewards and inefficient exploration in complex environments. We propose a Variational Dynamic Model (VDM) that learns a latent-space representation of the environment dynamics, enabling the agent to predict future states and rewards based on its actions. By maximizing the information gain between predicted and actual outcomes, the agent is incentivized to explore uncertain regions of the environment. The VDM is trained self-supervised, eliminating the need for manually engineered exploration bonuses or intrinsic rewards. We evaluate our approach on a range of challenging benchmark tasks, including those with sparse rewards and deceptive local optima. Results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing exploration strategies, achieving higher returns and faster learning speeds. The VDM demonstrates improved sample efficiency and robustness, facilitating effective exploration in complex, high-dimensional environments. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Self-Supervised Learning, Exploration, Variational Inference, Dynamic Model.

A simple path in a de Bruijn graph forms an Eulerian cycle, and by concatenating the edge symbols along the longest simple path, one obtains a cyclic de Bruijn sequence of order k, which contains every possible string of length k exactly once. To form the acyclic version of this sequence, the sequence corresponding to the first vertex is appended to the end of the cyclic sequence, ensuring that all unique substrings are represented non-cyclically.

In this paper, we revisit the classical representation of 3D point clouds as linear shape models. Our key insight is to leverage deep learning to represent a collection of shapes as affine transformations of low-dimensional linear shape models. Each linear model is characterized by a shape prototype, a low-dimensional shape basis and two neural networks. The networks take as input a point cloud and predict the coordinates of a shape in the linear basis and the affine transformation which best approximate the input. Both linear models and neural networks are learned end-to-end using a single reconstruction loss. The main advantage of our approach is that, in contrast to many recent deep approaches which learn feature-based complex shape representations, our model is explicit and every operation occurs in 3D space. As a result, our linear shape models can be easily visualized and annotated, and failure cases can be visually understood. While our main goal is to introduce a compact and interpretable representation of shape collections, we show it leads to state of the art results for few-shot segmentation.

Mortality prediction is critical in healthcare, yet often relies on structured data, which can be incomplete or delayed. This paper explores the potential of unstructured clinical notes for enhanced mortality prediction. We propose a novel approach leveraging transformer-based language models, specifically fine-tuning BERT on a large corpus of clinical notes to capture nuanced contextual information. Our method incorporates techniques for handling the inherent noise and variability within free-text data, including specialized tokenization and attention mechanisms. We evaluate our model on a large, real-world dataset of patient records, demonstrating significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to traditional models using structured data alone and other state-of-the-art NLP methods. The results indicate that free-text clinical notes offer valuable insights for mortality prediction, potentially enabling earlier intervention and improved patient outcomes. This work highlights the feasibility and effectiveness of using unstructured data for critical healthcare tasks, paving the way for more comprehensive and timely risk assessment. Keywords: Mortality Prediction, Clinical Notes, Natural Language Processing, BERT, Transformer, Unstructured Data, Healthcare, Machine Learning

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) coupled with self-supervised tasks have shown promising results in unconditional and semi-supervised image generation. We propose a self-supervised approach (LT-GAN) to improve the generation quality and diversity of images by estimating the GAN-induced transformation (i.e. transformation induced in the generated images by perturbing the latent space of generator). Specifically, given two pairs of images where each pair comprises of a generated image and its transformed version, the self-supervision task aims to identify whether the latent transformation applied in the given pair is same to that of the other pair. Hence, this auxiliary loss encourages the generator to produce images that are distinguishable by the auxiliary network, which in turn promotes the synthesis of semantically consistent images with respect to latent transformations. We show the efficacy of this pretext task by improving the image generation quality in terms of FID on state-of-the-art models for both conditional and unconditional settings on CIFAR-10, CelebA-HQ and ImageNet datasets. Moreover, we empirically show that LT-GAN helps in improving controlled image editing for CelebA-HQ and ImageNet over baseline models. We experimentally demonstrate that our proposed LT self-supervision task can be effectively combined with other state-of-the-art training techniques for added benefits. Consequently, we show that our approach achieves the new state-of-the-art FID score of 9.8 on conditional CIFAR-10 image generation.

In volumetric medical imaging, accurate segmentation is critical for diagnosis and treatment planning. However, fully supervised approaches demand extensive labeled data, which are often limited and difficult to obtain. This study introduces momentum contrastive voxel-wise representation learning as a method to improve semi-supervised volumetric medical image segmentation, aiming to reduce dependence on labeled datasets while maintaining high segmentation accuracy. Methods/Approach: The proposed method employs a momentum contrastive learning framework to enhance voxel-wise representation learning by constructing a dynamic model that adapts to unlabeled data. It leverages a dual-branch architecture consisting of an encoder trained using momentum contrast and a robust segmentation head to perform volumetric segmentation. The model captures fine-grained spatial and contextual information, thereby improving the segmentation performance even with minimal labeled data. Key features of the approach include a contrastive loss function that enhances voxel representation and a momentum update mechanism to stabilize learning. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations on benchmark volumetric medical imaging datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing semi-supervised methods, achieving superior segmentation accuracy with significantly reduced labeled training data. Comparative analyses highlight improved voxel-wise consistency and boundary delineation, with metrics showing enhanced precision and recall. The effectiveness of the momentum contrastive learning framework in maintaining performance stability across various medical imaging modalities is also validated. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides a novel contribution to the domain of medical image segmentation by introducing a momentum contrastive representation learning approach that excels in semi-supervised settings. The method’s ability to minimize labeled data requirements without compromising accuracy offers promising implications for clinical practice, potentially fostering more accessible and efficient medical diagnosis processes. The findings underscore the potential applications of this methodology in diverse medical scenarios, advocating for further exploration in different imaging contexts. Key Keywords: Momentum Contrastive Learning, Voxel-wise Representation, Semi-supervised Learning, Volumetric Medical Image Segmentation, Medical Imaging, Contrastive Loss.

Electronic health record (EHR) data is sparse and irregular as it is recorded at irregular time intervals, and different clinical variables are measured at each observation point. In this work, we propose a multi-view features integration learning from irregular multivariate time series data by self-attention mechanism in an imputation-free manner. Specifically, we devise a novel multi-integration attention module (MIAM) to extract complex information inherent in irregular time series data. In particular, we explicitly learn the relationships among the observed values, missing indicators, and time interval between the consecutive observations, simultaneously. The rationale behind our approach is the use of human knowledge such as what to measure and when to measure in different situations, which are indirectly represented in the data. In addition, we build an attention-based decoder as a missing value imputer that helps empower the representation learning of the inter-relations among multi-view observations for the prediction task, which operates at the training phase only. We validated the effectiveness of our method over the public MIMIC-III and PhysioNet challenge 2012 datasets by comparing with and outperforming the state-of-the-art methods for in-hospital mortality prediction.

Multiple views of data, both naturally acquired (e.g., image and audio) and artificially produced (e.g., via adding different noise to data samples), have proven useful in enhancing representation learning. Natural views are often handled by multiview analysis tools, e.g., (deep) canonical correlation analysis [(D)CCA], while the artificial ones are frequently used in self-supervised learning (SSL) paradigms, e.g., SimCLR and Barlow Twins. Both types of approaches often involve learning neural feature extractors such that the embeddings of data exhibit high cross-view correlations. Although intuitive, the effectiveness of correlation-based neural embedding is only empirically validated. This work puts forth a theory-backed framework for unsupervised multiview learning. Our development starts with proposing a multiview model, where each view is a nonlinear mixture of shared and private components. Consequently, the learning problem boils down to shared/private component identification and disentanglement. Under this model, latent correlation maximization is shown to guarantee the extraction of the shared components across views (up to certain ambiguities). In addition, the private information in each view can be provably disentangled from the shared using proper regularization design. The method is tested on a series of tasks, e.g., downstream clustering, which all show promising performance. Our development also provides a unifying perspective for understanding various DCCA and SSL schemes.

This paper introduces Evolving-Graph Gaussian Processes, a novel framework for modeling dynamic graph-structured data. The objective is to develop a probabilistic approach that captures the evolving relationships between nodes in a graph over time. Our method leverages Gaussian processes to model the temporal dynamics of graph signals, incorporating a graph kernel that adapts to the changing graph topology. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on several real-world datasets, showcasing improved performance in graph signal forecasting and imputation tasks compared to existing methods. The key findings highlight the importance of accounting for temporal and structural changes in graph data. Our research contributes to the development of more accurate and robust models for dynamic graph analysis, with potential applications in social network analysis, traffic forecasting, and recommendation systems. The proposed framework provides a flexible and scalable approach to modeling evolving graphs, making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of graph learning and artificial intelligence, particularly in areas such as graph neural networks, time-series analysis, and spatial-temporal modeling.

3D point clouds are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, which can significantly degrade the performance of downstream tasks. This paper introduces DUP-Net, a novel network designed to simultaneously denoise and upsample adversarially perturbed point clouds, thereby enhancing their robustness against such attacks. Our approach utilizes a two-branch architecture: a denoising branch that removes adversarial noise and an upsampling branch that increases point density, recovering lost geometric details. We employ a multi-scale feature extraction module in both branches to capture contextual information at varying resolutions. Furthermore, a novel loss function is introduced to encourage both accurate denoising and faithful upsampling. Experimental results on ModelNet40 and ShapeNet datasets demonstrate that DUP-Net significantly improves the classification accuracy of point cloud models under various adversarial attacks, outperforming existing defense methods. Specifically, DUP-Net achieves state-of-the-art defense performance while maintaining high fidelity to the original geometry. The proposed network offers a robust and effective solution for defending against adversarial attacks on 3D point clouds, contributing to more reliable point cloud processing pipelines. Keywords: 3D Point Clouds, Adversarial Attack, Defense, Denoising, Upsampling, Deep Learning.
