Kem dưỡng da có nguồn gốc tự nhiên đang trở thành một trong những xu hướng chăm sóc da phổ biến hiện nay. Để tạo ra sản phẩm này, cần phải hiểu rõ về quá trình bào chế và xây dựng tiêu chuẩn cơ sở. Bào chế kem dưỡng da tự nhiên bao gồm các bước như thu thập nguyên liệu, sơ chế, và phối hợp các thành phần để tạo ra sản phẩm cuối cùng. Một trong những yếu tố quan trọng nhất trong quá trình bào chế là lựa chọn nguyên liệu tự nhiên phù hợp. Các nguyên liệu như dầu dừa, dầu ô liu, và tinh dầu lavender được sử dụng rộng rãi trong sản xuất kem dưỡng da. Sau khi thu thập nguyên liệu, cần phải sơ chế và xử lý để loại bỏ các tạp chất và đảm bảo chất lượng. Tiếp theo, cần phải phối hợp các thành phần để tạo ra sản phẩm cuối cùng. Điều này bao gồm việc trộn các nguyên liệu tự nhiên với nhau để tạo ra hỗn hợp đồng nhất. Quá trình này đòi hỏi sự chính xác và kỹ thuật để đảm bảo sản phẩm có chất lượng tốt. Xây dựng tiêu chuẩn cơ sở là một phần quan trọng trong quá trình bào chế kem dưỡng da tự nhiên. Tiêu chuẩn này bao gồm các yếu tố như chất lượng nguyên liệu, quy trình sản xuất, và kiểm tra chất lượng sản phẩm. This paper proposes a novel approach to LiDAR segmentation using cylindrical and asymmetrical 3D convolution networks. The objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of point cloud segmentation in various applications, such as autonomous driving and robotics. Our method utilizes a unique combination of cylindrical and asymmetrical convolutional layers to capture the complex geometric structures of 3D point clouds. The network architecture is designed to adapt to the sparse and irregular nature of LiDAR data, allowing for more accurate and robust segmentation results. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of cylindrical convolutions for capturing long-range dependencies and the use of asymmetrical convolutions for handling complex geometric relationships. Our work has significant implications for the development of more accurate and efficient LiDAR segmentation systems, with potential applications in fields such as computer vision, robotics, and geospatial analysis. Key keywords: LiDAR segmentation, 3D convolution networks, cylindrical convolutions, asymmetrical convolutions, point cloud processing, autonomous driving, robotics.

Autonomous driving systems require robust and accurate 3D object detection to ensure safe navigation in complex environments. This paper presents a novel Multi-View 3D Object Detection Network (MV3D-Net) designed to enhance the precision and efficiency of detecting objects in three-dimensional space. The proposed approach integrates data from multiple sensor modalities, including LiDAR and camera inputs, to generate a comprehensive representation of the surrounding environment. By leveraging a multi-view fusion strategy, the network effectively combines bird's-eye view and perspective view features, enabling improved object localization and classification. The architecture employs a deep learning framework with attention mechanisms to prioritize relevant spatial and contextual information, reducing computational overhead while maintaining high detection accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that MV3D-Net outperforms existing methods in terms of both detection performance and inference speed. The system achieves state-of-the-art results in 3D bounding box estimation, particularly in challenging scenarios with occlusions and varying lighting conditions. This research contributes to the advancement of autonomous driving technologies by providing a scalable and efficient solution for real-time 3D object detection, with potential applications in robotics, surveillance, and augmented reality. **Keywords**: 3D object detection, autonomous driving, multi-view fusion, LiDAR, deep learning, sensor fusion.

Objective: Low-resource sentiment analysis suffers from insufficient labeled data, limiting the performance of supervised classifiers. This paper proposes a novel data augmentation framework based on generative adversarial networks (GANs) to enrich training sets and improve sentiment prediction in domains with scarce annotations. Methods: We design a conditional text-GAN that learns to generate realistic sentiment-bearing sentences by pitting a generator against a discriminator. The generator produces synthetic reviews conditioned on positive or negative labels, while the discriminator distinguishes between real and generated samples. We introduce a reinforcement-learning–based reward signal to guide the generator toward sentiment coherence and lexical diversity. Augmented data are combined with original training examples to retrain standard sentiment classifiers (e.g., LSTM and transformer-based models). Results: Experiments on two low-resource datasets—a customer reviews corpus with fewer than 1,000 labeled instances and a social media sentiment set—show that our GAN-based augmentation boosts classifier accuracy by 5–8% compared to baseline oversampling and synonym-replacement methods. Ablation studies confirm the importance of the sentiment-conditioned reward and diversity-promoting regularizer. We also demonstrate that performance gains hold across different model architectures and generalize to an unseen domain. Conclusion: The proposed GAN-driven augmentation pipeline effectively alleviates data scarcity in sentiment analysis, offering a scalable approach to generate high-quality labeled text. This work contributes a practical tool for low-resource natural language processing and highlights the potential of adversarial text generation to enhance downstream classifiers. Keywords: data augmentation, sentiment analysis, generative adversarial networks, low-resource NLP, text generation.

This paper introduces ICON, a novel framework for learning regular maps in the context of geometric deep learning by leveraging the principle of inverse consistency. The objective is to address the challenge of constructing smooth and invertible correspondences between complex geometric domains, a fundamental problem in computer vision, 3D reconstruction, and medical imaging. ICON formulates the map learning process as a bi-directional optimization problem that explicitly enforces inverse consistency, ensuring that the forward and backward mappings are mutually consistent and regularized. The approach combines neural network-based mapping functions with a consistency loss, enabling the resulting maps to be smooth, continuous, and robust to noise or perturbations. Extensive experiments on various benchmarks—including synthetic and real-world datasets—demonstrate that ICON significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, regularity, and invertibility of the learned maps. The proposed framework also exhibits enhanced generalization to unseen data and complex shapes. In conclusion, ICON provides a reliable and scalable solution for learning regularity-preserving maps, with broad applicability in areas such as shape matching, non-rigid registration, and morphable model construction. Key contributions include the development of the inverse consistency-driven optimization scheme and empirical evidence of improved map quality. Keywords: geometric deep learning, inverse consistency, map regularity, shape correspondence, 3D reconstruction, neural networks.

This paper introduces a novel approach to synthesizing realistic face photographs from simple line drawings, enabling attribute-level control over the generated images. Our method leverages a generative adversarial network (GAN) architecture, incorporating a novel attribute conditioning mechanism that allows users to manipulate specific facial features, such as age, gender, and expression, directly from the line drawing input. The network consists of a generator that translates the line drawing into a photorealistic image and a discriminator that distinguishes between real and synthesized images. Crucially, attribute control is achieved by integrating attribute vectors into both the generator and discriminator, guiding the synthesis process. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach produces high-quality face photographs that faithfully reflect the input line drawing while accurately reflecting the desired attribute modifications. Quantitative evaluations and user studies confirm the superior performance of our method compared to existing line drawing to face synthesis techniques, particularly in terms of attribute controllability and image realism. This work contributes a practical tool for image editing, face generation, and potentially artistic expression. Keywords: Face synthesis, Line drawing, Generative adversarial networks, Attribute control, Image generation.

Social media is a popular platform for timely information sharing. One of the important challenges for social media platforms like Twitter is whether to trust news shared on them when there is no systematic news verification process. On the other hand, timely detection of rumors is a non-trivial task, given the fast-paced social media environment. In this work, we proposed an ensemble model, which performs majority-voting on a collection of predictions by deep neural networks using time-series vector representation of Twitter data for timely detection of rumors. By combining the proposed data pre-processing method with the ensemble model, better performance of rumor detection has been demonstrated in the experiments using PHEME dataset. Experimental results show that the classification performance has been improved by 7.9% in terms of micro F1 score compared to the baselines.

This paper addresses the challenge of relative camera pose estimation, a critical task in computer vision with applications in augmented reality, robotics, and 3D reconstruction. Traditional methods often rely on handcrafted features and geometric constraints, which can struggle with robustness in complex or dynamic environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel approach leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to directly estimate the relative pose between two camera views. Our method processes pairs of images through a deep learning architecture designed to learn spatial and geometric relationships, eliminating the need for explicit feature extraction and matching. The network is trained on a large-scale dataset of synthetic and real-world image pairs, enabling it to generalize across diverse scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that our CNN-based approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and robustness, outperforming traditional methods in challenging conditions such as low texture and occlusions. The proposed framework also exhibits significant computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications. This work contributes to the advancement of camera pose estimation by introducing a data-driven, end-to-end solution that reduces reliance on manual feature engineering and enhances adaptability to real-world complexities. Keywords: relative camera pose estimation, convolutional neural networks, computer vision, deep learning, 3D reconstruction.

This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing deep neural networks for embedded automation systems, where computational resources are limited. The objective is to improve the efficiency and performance of these networks without sacrificing accuracy. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach called Mean Spectral Normalization, which normalizes the spectral properties of the network's weights to reduce overfitting and improve generalization. Our method is based on a simple yet effective technique that adjusts the weight matrix to have a target spectral distribution, resulting in more stable and efficient training. Experimental results demonstrate that Mean Spectral Normalization outperforms existing normalization techniques, achieving significant reductions in computational cost and memory usage while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy. The implications of this research are substantial, enabling the deployment of deep neural networks in resource-constrained embedded automation systems, such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and industrial control systems. Key contributions include improved network efficiency, reduced overfitting, and enhanced performance in low-resource environments, making this technique an attractive solution for a wide range of applications in embedded automation and beyond.

This study aims to investigate the performance of retinal image quality assessment networks in various color-spaces, addressing the need for accurate image quality evaluation in medical imaging applications. We propose a comprehensive approach, utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to assess image quality in different color-spaces, including RGB, YCbCr, and HSV. Our methodology involves training and testing the networks on a large dataset of retinal images, evaluating their performance using metrics such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM). The results show that the networks achieve high accuracy in assessing image quality, with the YCbCr color-space yielding the best performance. Our findings suggest that the choice of color-space significantly impacts the performance of retinal image quality assessment networks, highlighting the importance of color-space selection in medical image analysis. This research contributes to the development of more accurate and reliable image quality assessment methods, with potential applications in retinal disease diagnosis and treatment. Key keywords: retinal image quality assessment, color-spaces, convolutional neural networks, medical imaging, image analysis.

The "Recognizing Families In the Wild Data Challenge" addresses the complex problem of identifying familial relationships within unstructured, real-world data. The primary objective of this challenge is to advance the development of algorithms capable of recognizing kinship patterns from a diverse set of images that simulate real-life conditions. Methods employed in this challenge include the use of innovative deep learning architectures and advanced computer vision techniques to enhance the accuracy of family recognition systems. Participants were encouraged to implement novel approaches, such as customized convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and feature extraction strategies, to improve kinship detection reliability across various demographics and familial configurations. The challenge resulted in significant findings, indicating a marked improvement in the ability to accurately predict familial ties compared to traditional methods. The top-performing models demonstrated impressive scalability and adaptability, significantly advancing the state-of-the-art in kinship recognition. Concluding the challenge, it is evident that these advancements have broad implications for fields such as social media analysis, security, and genealogy research. This research underscores the potential for refined AI models to transform how we interpret familial relationships through computer vision. Key keywords include kinship recognition, deep learning, CNN, computer vision, and data challenge.

Object separation is a critical process in image analysis, computer vision, and data segmentation, often challenged by overlapping features and complex backgrounds. This paper presents a semi-automated statistical algorithm designed to enhance object separation efficiency and accuracy in diverse datasets. The proposed method utilizes statistical analysis of pixel distributions and feature clustering, enabling preliminary object segmentation with minimal user intervention. Users provide initial input to guide the algorithm, which then employs adaptive thresholding and unsupervised clustering to distinguish and isolate objects from their surroundings. Comparative evaluations on benchmark image datasets demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms conventional fully-automated approaches in terms of precision, robustness to noise, and adaptability to heterogeneous data. The results indicate substantial reductions in manual post-processing while maintaining high separation accuracy. This semi-automated approach bridges the gap between manual and fully-automated systems, offering flexibility and improved performance in scenarios where complete automation is impractical. The proposed framework holds significant potential for applications in medical imaging, remote sensing, and industrial inspection, where reliable and efficient object separation is essential. Key keywords: object separation, statistical algorithm, semi-automated processing, image segmentation, clustering, adaptive thresholding.

Affective computing, which aims to understand and respond to human emotions, benefits significantly from multi-modal data. This paper introduces an unsupervised multi-modal representation learning approach tailored for affective computing using wearable sensor data collected across multiple corpora. The proposed method leverages contrastive learning to fuse representations from physiological signals (e.g., heart rate, skin conductance) and contextual information, without relying on labeled emotion data. We demonstrate that our approach learns robust and generalized affective representations across diverse datasets. Evaluation on benchmark emotion recognition tasks reveals that the learned representations achieve comparable or superior performance compared to supervised methods, particularly in cross-corpus settings. The findings suggest that unsupervised multi-modal learning is a promising avenue for developing affective computing systems that can generalize across different populations and environments. This research contributes to the field by providing a novel and effective technique for learning affective representations from unlabeled wearable data, enabling the development of more robust and adaptable emotion recognition systems. Keywords: Affective Computing, Multi-Modal Learning, Unsupervised Learning, Wearable Sensors, Emotion Recognition, Representation Learning, Contrastive Learning.

Objective: Unsupervised anomaly detection and precise localization in medical images remain challenging due to the scarcity of abnormal samples and the variability of healthy anatomy. We introduce Constrained Contrastive Distribution Learning (CCDL), a novel framework that learns a compact representation of normal tissue and effectively discriminates anomalous regions without requiring labeled pathologies. Methods: CCDL employs a two-branch encoder with a momentum-updated teacher network to generate stable features on healthy images. A constrained contrastive loss enforces that embeddings of normal samples form a tight distribution, while synthetically perturbed or out-of-distribution patches are pushed toward the periphery. We model the healthy feature manifold with a Gaussian distribution and compute anomaly scores based on feature likelihood. Localization maps are produced by mapping pixel-wise deviations from the learned distribution. Results: Extensive experiments on public medical imaging benchmarks—including brain MRI and chest X-ray datasets—demonstrate that CCDL outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised methods in both detection and localization. Our approach achieves substantial gains in area under the ROC curve and mean intersection-over-union for anomaly maps, while maintaining computational efficiency. Conclusion: By integrating contrastive representation learning with explicit distribution constraints, CCDL captures healthy anatomy variations and reliably highlights anomalous regions. This generalizable, label-free framework holds promise for screening and computer-aided diagnosis in diverse medical imaging applications. Keywords: unsupervised anomaly detection, medical image analysis, contrastive learning, distribution modeling, anomaly localization

Kiểm định đồng liên kết cho các mối quan hệ kinh tế dài hạn của cộng đồng Đông Phi bằng chứng từ phương pháp hồi quy vectơ tự động (VAR) đã được thực hiện để đánh giá sự tương tác giữa các quốc gia trong khu vực. Kết quả cho thấy có sự liên kết mạnh mẽ giữa các nền kinh tế Đông Phi, đặc biệt là giữa Kenya, Tanzania và Uganda. Phương pháp VAR đã được sử dụng để phân tích dữ liệu kinh tế của các quốc gia này trong thời gian dài hạn, từ năm 1990 đến năm 2020. Kết quả cho thấy có sự tương tác mạnh mẽ giữa các nền kinh tế, với các biến kinh tế như GDP, lạm phát và lãi suất có mối quan hệ chặt chẽ với nhau. Kết quả kiểm định đồng liên kết cũng cho thấy rằng các quốc gia Đông Phi có sự phụ thuộc lẫn nhau trong kinh tế, với các nền kinh tế lớn như Kenya và Tanzania có ảnh hưởng lớn đến các nền kinh tế nhỏ hơn như Uganda. Điều này cho thấy rằng các quốc gia Đông Phi cần phải hợp tác và xây dựng mối quan hệ kinh tế chặt chẽ hơn để phát triển kinh tế bền vững.

Significant progress has been made in recent years in image captioning, an active topic in the fields of vision and language. However, existing methods tend to yield overly general captions and consist of some of the most frequent words/phrases, resulting in inaccurate and indistinguishable descriptions (see Figure 1). This is primarily due to (i) the conservative characteristic of traditional training objectives that drives the model to generate correct but hardly discriminative captions for similar images and (ii) the uneven word distribution of the ground-truth captions, which encourages generating highly frequent words/phrases while suppressing the less frequent but more concrete ones. In this work, we propose a novel global-local discriminative objective that is formulated on top of a reference model to facilitate generating fine-grained descriptive captions. Specifically, from a global perspective, we design a novel global discriminative constraint that pulls the generated sentence to better discern the corresponding image from all others in the entire dataset. From the local perspective, a local discriminative constraint is proposed to increase attention such that it emphasizes the less frequent but more concrete words/phrases, thus facilitating the generation of captions that better describe the visual details of the given images. We evaluate the proposed method on the widely used MS-COCO dataset, where it outperforms the baseline methods by a sizable margin and achieves competitive performance over existing leading approaches. We also conduct self-retrieval experiments to demonstrate the discriminability of the proposed method.

Hyperspectral image (HSI) denoising is crucial for accurate scene analysis, yet remains challenging due to the presence of complex mixed noise. This paper introduces an unsupervised HSI denoising approach, termed Spatial-Spectral Constrained Deep Image Prior (SSC-DIP), which leverages the implicit regularization of deep neural networks without requiring clean training data. SSC-DIP exploits a convolutional neural network as a generative model, optimized to fit the noisy HSI. A novel spatial-spectral constraint is imposed during the optimization process to enforce local smoothness and spectral consistency, thereby promoting structured noise removal. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that SSC-DIP achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art unsupervised denoising methods, particularly in preserving fine spatial details and spectral signatures. The proposed method offers a practical and effective solution for HSI denoising in scenarios where clean reference data is unavailable. Keywords: Hyperspectral Image, Denoising, Deep Image Prior, Unsupervised Learning, Spatial-Spectral Constraint, Mixed Noise.

Nghiên cứu cho thấy, những bệnh nhân có điểm số cao hơn có nguy cơ tử vong cao hơn, điều này nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc sử dụng bảng điểm này trong lâm sàng. Sự kết hợp giữa AIMS65 và các yếu tố lâm sàng khác có thể cải thiện đáng kể kết quả điều trị cho bệnh nhân xuất huyết tiêu hóa trên.

This paper explores self-supervised learning of amodal 3D feature representations from RGB and RGB-D posed images and videos, agnostic to object and scene semantic content, and evaluates the resulting scene representations in the downstream tasks of visual correspondence, object tracking, and object detection. The model infers a latent3D representation of the scene in the form of 3D feature points, where each continuous world 3D point is mapped to its corresponding feature vector. The model is trained for contrastive view prediction by rendering 3D feature clouds in queried viewpoints and matching against the 3D feature point cloud predicted from the query view. Notably, the representation can be queried for any 3D location, even if it is not visible from the input view. Our model brings together three powerful ideas of recent exciting research work: 3D feature grids as a neural bottleneck for view prediction, implicit functions for handling resolution limitations of 3D grids, and contrastive learning for unsupervised training of feature representations. We show the resulting 3D visual feature representations effectively scale across objects and scenes, imagine information occluded or missing from the input viewpoints, track objects over time, align semantically related objects in 3D, and improve 3D object detection. We outperform many existing state-of-the-art methods for 3D feature learning and view prediction, which are either limited by 3D grid spatial resolution, do not attempt to build amodal 3D representations, or do not handle combinatorial scene variability due to their non-convolutional bottlenecks.

Multi-label classification remains a challenging task, particularly in few-shot and zero-shot scenarios where labeled data is scarce or nonexistent for certain classes. This paper introduces a novel approach to multi-label few-zero-shot learning that leverages knowledge aggregated from multiple label graphs. Our method constructs several label graphs, each capturing distinct semantic relationships between labels extracted from diverse knowledge sources. We then propose a knowledge aggregation module that dynamically weights and integrates information from these graphs to enhance feature representation and improve label prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both few-shot and zero-shot multi-label classification settings. The results highlight the effectiveness of aggregating knowledge from multiple label graphs for improved generalization and adaptation to novel labels. This work provides a new direction for addressing the challenges of limited supervision in multi-label learning. Keywords: Multi-label learning, Few-shot learning, Zero-shot learning, Graph Neural Networks, Knowledge Aggregation, Semantic Relationships.

This paper addresses the challenge of anomaly detection in particulate matter (PM) sensors, which are critical for monitoring air quality. Traditional methods often struggle with high-dimensional data and complex patterns, leading to reduced accuracy and efficiency. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel approach using a Hypothesis Pruning Generative Adversarial Network (HP-GAN). The HP-GAN framework integrates a hypothesis pruning mechanism into the GAN architecture, enabling the model to focus on relevant features while discarding redundant or noisy data. This enhances the model's ability to detect anomalies in PM sensor data with higher precision. Our experiments demonstrate that the HP-GAN outperforms existing anomaly detection methods in terms of accuracy, recall, and computational efficiency. The model achieves a 15% improvement in anomaly detection accuracy compared to state-of-the-art techniques, while reducing false positives by 20%. Additionally, the hypothesis pruning mechanism significantly reduces training time, making the approach scalable for real-time applications. The proposed method has significant implications for environmental monitoring systems, enabling more reliable and efficient detection of sensor malfunctions or data anomalies. This research contributes to the advancement of anomaly detection in IoT-based sensor networks, offering a robust solution for improving air quality monitoring systems. **Keywords**: Anomaly detection, particulate matter sensors, generative adversarial networks, hypothesis pruning, air quality monitoring, IoT.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently transferring knowledge between agents in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) environments by introducing a framework for real-time policy distillation. The objective is to enable the continuous and adaptive distillation of a high-performing teacher policy into a smaller, more efficient student network during ongoing training and deployment, without significant interruptions or retraining phases. Our approach leverages online distillation techniques that dynamically align the student policy with the evolving teacher, facilitating rapid adaptation to changing environments and tasks. Through extensive experiments in benchmark DRL environments, we demonstrate that our real-time distillation method achieves comparable or superior performance to standard offline distillation, with notable gains in scalability and sample efficiency. Results indicate reduced training overhead and faster convergence, making the approach suitable for real-world scenarios where immediate deployment and adaptability are critical. The proposed framework also supports multi-teacher settings and varying student capacities, further enhancing its flexibility. These findings highlight the potential of real-time policy distillation to accelerate knowledge transfer, optimize resource usage, and broaden the applicability of deep reinforcement learning in dynamic contexts. Key keywords: deep reinforcement learning, policy distillation, real-time adaptation, knowledge transfer, sample efficiency.

The rapid advancement of neural style transfer has enabled the synthesis of visually appealing images by combining the content of one image with the artistic style of another. However, existing methods often struggle with arbitrary style transfer, particularly when handling diverse and complex styles. This paper introduces a novel Multi-Adaptation Network (MAN) designed to address these challenges by dynamically adapting to arbitrary styles while preserving content fidelity. The proposed approach leverages a multi-level adaptation mechanism that integrates style features at varying granularities, enabling more flexible and accurate style transfer. Our method employs a lightweight encoder-decoder architecture combined with adaptive instance normalization to ensure efficient and high-quality results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of visual quality, style diversity, and computational efficiency. The results highlight the network's ability to generalize across a wide range of artistic styles, making it a promising tool for applications in digital art, media production, and creative design. This work contributes to the field by offering a robust and scalable solution for arbitrary style transfer, paving the way for future advancements in image synthesis and neural rendering. **Keywords**: Neural style transfer, multi-adaptation network, arbitrary style transfer, adaptive instance normalization, image synthesis.

Khảo sát mới nhất về biến đổi tế bào nội mô và bề dày trung tâm giác mạc sau phẫu thuật Phaco trên bệnh nhân cho thấy những thay đổi đáng kể trong cấu trúc giác mạc sau khi thực hiện phẫu thuật này. Phẫu thuật Phaco là một phương pháp phổ biến để điều trị đục thủy tinh thể, giúp cải thiện thị lực của bệnh nhân. Tuy nhiên, vẫn còn nhiều câu hỏi về tác động của phẫu thuật này lên cấu trúc giác mạc. Automated segmentation in medical image analysis is a challenging task that requires a large amount of manually labeled data. However, manually annotating medical data is often laborious, and most existing learning-based approaches fail to accurately delineate object boundaries without effective geometric constraints. Contrastive learning, a sub-area of self-supervised learning, has recently been noted as a promising direction in multiple application fields. In this work, we present a novel Contrastive Voxel-wise Representation Learning (CVRL) method with geometric constraints to learn global-local visual representations for volumetric medical image segmentation with limited annotations. Our framework can effectively learn global and local features by capturing 3D spatial context and rich anatomical information. Specifically, we introduce a voxel-to-volume contrastive algorithm to learn global information from 3D images, and propose to perform local voxel-to-voxel contrast to explicitly make use of local cues in the embedding space. Moreover, we integrate an elastic interaction-based active contour model as a geometric regularization term to enable fast and reliable object delineations in an end-to-end learning manner. Results on the Atrial Segmentation Challenge dataset demonstrate superiority of our proposed scheme, especially in a setting with a very limited number of annotated data.

This paper addresses the challenge of integrating spectral and spatial information in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to enhance their capacity to learn from complex graph-structured data. While traditional approaches tend to focus on either the spectral domain, leveraging global graph properties, or the spatial domain, capturing local neighborhood information, a unified method that effectively combines both remains underexplored. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel framework that bridges the gap between spectral and spatial domains in GNNs by incorporating a dual-domain architecture. This architecture employs spectral decomposition techniques to leverage global graph structures and combines them with spatial convolution operations tailored to exploit local graph patterns. This hybrid approach is systematically embedded within the neural network training pipeline, allowing for end-to-end learning. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate significant improvements in model accuracy and robustness on benchmark graph datasets compared to state-of-the-art GNN models that operate exclusively in one domain. The proposed method not only enhances graph classification and node prediction tasks but also shows superior performance in handling graphs with diverse topological characteristics. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides a significant contribution to the field of graph neural networks by offering an innovative solution for comprehensive graph representation through dual-domain integration. The framework's flexibility and effectiveness highlight its potential for various applications, including social network analysis, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems. Furthermore, this study opens new avenues for research on multi-domain fusion techniques in machine learning. Keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Spectral Domain, Spatial Domain, Dual-Domain Architecture, Graph Representation, Machine Learning.

This study investigates the trade-off between sensor resolution and classification accuracy in automotive radar systems, comparing off-the-shelf sensors with experimental radar setups. Our objective is to determine the minimum required resolution for reliable object classification, a crucial aspect of autonomous vehicle safety. We employ a machine learning approach, utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify objects detected by radar sensors with varying resolutions. Our results show that while high-resolution radar systems achieve superior classification performance, off-the-shelf sensors with lower resolutions can still provide satisfactory accuracy, depending on the specific classification task. We find that a resolution of 1-2 degrees is sufficient for basic object detection, but higher resolutions (0.5-1 degree) are necessary for more complex classification tasks, such as distinguishing between pedestrians and vehicles. Our research contributes to the development of cost-effective and efficient automotive radar systems, highlighting the importance of balancing sensor resolution with computational complexity and system cost. Key keywords: automotive radar, sensor resolution, object classification, machine learning, CNNs, autonomous vehicles.

In various domains such as signal processing, computer vision, and statistics, matrix decomposition plays a critical role in data analysis and interpretation. However, the presence of outliers can severely impair the performance of standard decomposition techniques. This paper addresses the challenge of performing robust matrix decomposition in the presence of outliers, providing a refined approach that maintains accuracy and reliability under these adverse conditions. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel algorithmic framework that leverages an improved optimization model to achieve robust matrix decomposition. Our approach incorporates an adaptive weighting mechanism to dynamically identify and mitigate the impact of outliers. By integrating techniques from robust statistics and optimization theory, we enhance the traditional low-rank decomposition method to handle anomalous data points effectively. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method in various scenarios with differing types and levels of outlier contamination. Compared to existing methods, our model consistently achieves higher accuracy in matrix reconstruction and demonstrates greater resilience to outliers. Performance evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets illustrate the method's applicability across diverse applications, showcasing its efficiency and robustness. Conclusion/Implications: The research provides a significant contribution to the field of matrix decomposition by offering a robust methodology capable of handling outliers without compromising on computational efficiency. The proposed method holds potential for various practical applications, including image processing, collaborative filtering, and financial data analysis. By delivering improved performance in challenging conditions, this work sets the stage for further exploration and development in robust data analysis techniques. Key Keywords: Robust Matrix Decomposition, Outliers, Optimization Model, Robust Statistics, Low-Rank Decomposition.

High-dimensional data pose challenges in statistical learning and modeling. Sometimes the predictors can be naturally grouped where pursuing the between-group sparsity is desired. Collinearity may occur in real-world high-dimensional applications where the popular l_1 technique suffers from both selection inconsistency and prediction inaccuracy. Moreover, the problems of interest often go beyond Gaussian models. To meet these challenges, nonconvex penalized generalized linear models with grouped predictors are investigated and a simple-to-implement algorithm is proposed for computation. A rigorous theoretical result guarantees its convergence and provides tight preliminary scaling. This framework allows for grouped predictors and nonconvex penalties, including the discrete l_0 and the `l_0+l_2' type penalties. Penalty design and parameter tuning for nonconvex penalties are examined. Applications of super-resolution spectrum estimation in signal processing and cancer classification with joint gene selection in bioinformatics show the performance improvement by nonconvex penalized estimation.

Graph-based data representations are increasingly critical in various domains, including social networks, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems. However, extracting meaningful insights from complex graph structures remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces *Graph Filtration Learning* (GFL), a novel framework designed to enhance the interpretability and efficiency of graph-based machine learning models. The objective of this research is to address the limitations of existing graph analysis methods by leveraging a filtration-based approach that systematically simplifies graph structures while preserving essential topological features. The proposed GFL framework employs a hierarchical filtration process, which iteratively prunes edges based on edge weights or other topological metrics, enabling the extraction of multi-scale graph representations. We integrate this approach with graph neural networks (GNNs) to improve model performance and interpretability. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that GFL outperforms traditional graph analysis methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Specifically, GFL achieves a 12% improvement in classification accuracy on social network datasets and reduces training time by 30% compared to state-of-the-art GNNs. The key contribution of this work lies in its ability to bridge the gap between graph simplification and deep learning, offering a scalable and interpretable solution for graph-based tasks. The implications of GFL extend to applications such as anomaly detection, community identification, and drug discovery, where understanding graph structures is crucial. This research advances the field of graph machine learning by providing a robust framework for handling complex graph data with improved efficiency and interpretability. **Keywords**: Graph filtration, graph neural networks, interpretability, hierarchical graph representation, machine learning, graph simplification.

Objective: Neural networks achieve high predictive performance but often lack transparency, hindering their adoption in critical domains. We introduce LioNets, a novel framework for generating faithful, local interpretations of any feed-forward neural model by decoding activations from its penultimate layer. Methods: LioNets builds a lightweight decoder that learns to invert penultimate representations back into input space. At explanation time, for a target instance, we sample perturbed latent vectors in its neighborhood, reconstruct corresponding synthetic inputs via the decoder, and query the original network to obtain predictions. A locally weighted linear surrogate is then fitted to these synthetic pairs, yielding human-readable feature attributions that reflect the model’s true decision boundary in the vicinity of the instance. Results: We evaluate LioNets on image (MNIST, CIFAR-10) and tabular (UCI) classification benchmarks, comparing it against state-of-the-art local explainers (LIME, SHAP). Across datasets, LioNets achieves higher local fidelity (up to 15% reduction in surrogate error) and greater stability under perturbations, while producing more coherent attributions validated by domain experts. Qualitative analyses illustrate that decoded samples faithfully capture relevant feature variations, improving interpretability without impacting the base model. Conclusion: By leveraging penultimate layer decoding, LioNets delivers transparent, accurate local explanations applicable to diverse neural architectures. Its plug-and-play design makes it a practical tool for practitioners seeking trustworthy model insight in sensitive applications. Keywords: explainable AI; neural network interpretability; local explanations; penultimate layer decoding; feature attribution.

Tăng trưởng kinh tế tại các nước đang phát triển đã trở thành một vấn đề quan trọng trong thời gian gần đây. Một trong những yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến quá trình này là vốn đầu tư gián tiếp nước ngoài (FDI). FDI đã trở thành một nguồn vốn quan trọng cho các nước đang phát triển, giúp họ tăng cường khả năng cạnh tranh và phát triển kinh tế. Tuy nhiên, ảnh hưởng của FDI đến tăng trưởng kinh tế tại các nước đang phát triển còn phụ thuộc vào nhiều yếu tố khác nhau. Một số nước đã đạt được thành công đáng kể trong việc thu hút FDI và sử dụng nó để thúc đẩy tăng trưởng kinh tế. Ví dụ, Việt Nam đã trở thành một trong những quốc gia thu hút FDI hàng đầu tại khu vực Đông Nam Á, với nhiều dự án đầu tư lớn trong các lĩnh vực như công nghệ thông tin, sản xuất và xuất khẩu. Tuy nhiên, cũng có một số nước đang phát triển đã gặp khó khăn trong việc thu hút và sử dụng FDI một cách hiệu quả. Điều này có thể do nhiều nguyên nhân khác nhau, bao gồm cả chính sách đầu tư không phù hợp, khả năng quản lý và giám sát FDI yếu kém, và sự phụ thuộc quá mức vào FDI. Tổng quan, ảnh hưởng của FDI đến tăng trưởng kinh tế tại các nước đang phát triển vẫn còn là một vấn đề phức tạp và đa chiều. Để tận dụng được lợi ích của FDI, các nước đang phát triển cần phải có chính sách đầu tư phù hợp, quản lý và giám sát FDI một cách hiệu quả, và xây dựng được một nền kinh tế đa dạng và bền vững.

This paper addresses the challenge of transferring learned policies across multiple tasks in continuous control environments, where an effective state abstraction is crucial for improving transferability and reducing computational burden. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach for learning state abstractions that facilitates policy transfer in continuous control domains. The approach employs deep reinforcement learning techniques to identify salient features and compress state representations while preserving critical information necessary for effective decision-making. By leveraging a combination of variational autoencoders and policy gradient methods, our model autonomously learns abstractions that are minimally sufficient for task success, enabling efficient transfer across varied tasks. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in transfer learning performance using the proposed state abstractions compared to baseline methods. Our model not only achieves faster convergence on new tasks but also reduces sample complexity, making it suitable for real-world applications where data efficiency is crucial. Additionally, we show that our approach can successfully transfer knowledge in environments characterized by high-dimensional and continuous state spaces. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of this state abstraction framework represents a step forward in the field of continuous control, highlighting its capability to enhance policy transfer between tasks. This work opens up new avenues for research in reinforcement learning, particularly in developing robust and adaptable agents capable of generalizing across diverse environments. Potential applications span robotics, autonomous systems, and complex simulations where continuous control is essential. Keywords: state abstraction, transfer learning, continuous control, reinforcement learning, policy transfer, variational autoencoders, deep learning.

Zero-shot learning (ZSL) aims to classify instances from classes that have not been observed during the training phase, relying on auxiliary information, such as class descriptions, to bridge the gap between seen and unseen categories. This paper addresses the limitations of existing ZSL approaches that often fail to effectively incorporate class descriptions, leading to suboptimal performance. Methods: We introduce a novel framework for zero-shot learning, termed Class Description Regularization (CDR). This approach integrates class semantic vectors and leverages a strategic regularization technique to enhance the alignment between visual and semantic spaces. By embedding class descriptions directly into the learning process, our method effectively mitigates the semantic gap and improves generalization to unseen classes. Results: Our empirical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed CDR method achieves superior performance on multiple benchmark datasets, including Caltech-UCSD Birds, Animals with Attributes, and SUN Attribute. We observe significant improvements over state-of-the-art techniques, with notable gains in accuracy and robustness across varied zero-shot learning scenarios. Moreover, our analysis shows that CDR not only improves model precision but also enhances interpretability by aligning visual attributes more closely with semantic labels. Conclusion: The introduction of Class Description Regularization represents a significant advancement in zero-shot learning, offering a robust mechanism to harness the potential of class descriptions. This research provides novel insights into bridging seen and unseen domains, contributing to the broader field of machine learning and pattern recognition. Future work may extend this framework to other related tasks, such as few-shot learning and domain adaptation. Keywords: Zero-shot learning, Class Description Regularization, semantic gap, unseen classes, attribute alignment, machine learning, pattern recognition.

The objective of this research is to address the challenges posed by uncertain feedback in online learning environments represented as graphs. Traditional models in online learning assume precise and reliable feedback, which is often not the case in real-world applications where feedback may vary in accuracy or relevance. This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework for handling online learning with feedback graphs that are uncertain or subject to noise. Our approach leverages the power of probabilistic graph models, incorporating mechanisms to assess and adaptively respond to the uncertainty inherent in feedback. Through both theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations, we demonstrate that our model outperforms existing baseline methods under various levels of feedback uncertainty, achieving more robust learning outcomes and improved decision-making. The findings underscore significant advancements in online learning strategies, particularly in applications where feedback reliability cannot be guaranteed. This research contributes to the fields of machine learning and graph theory by providing a robust methodology for uncertain feedback environments, with implications for enhancing automated decision systems in complex, noisy settings. Key keywords include online learning, uncertainty, feedback graphs, probabilistic models, and adaptive algorithms.

This paper introduces FD-GAN, a novel Face-Demorphing Generative Adversarial Network designed to restore the facial image of an accomplice from morphed images. Morphing attacks, which combine facial features of multiple individuals, pose significant security risks in identity verification systems. The objective of this research is to develop a robust solution capable of reversing the morphing process and reconstructing the original accomplice's face with high fidelity. FD-GAN employs a dual-path generator architecture combined with a discriminative network to disentangle and reconstruct facial features from morphed inputs. The model is trained on a diverse dataset of morphed and non-morphed facial images, leveraging adversarial learning to enhance reconstruction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that FD-GAN outperforms existing methods in terms of visual quality and structural similarity, achieving a 15% improvement in reconstruction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art techniques. The proposed approach also shows robustness against various morphing techniques and noise levels. This work contributes to the field of biometric security by providing a reliable tool for detecting and reversing morphing attacks, with potential applications in passport verification, border control, and forensic investigations. Keywords: face demorphing, generative adversarial networks, biometric security, image reconstruction, morphing attacks.

Cataract, a leading cause of blindness worldwide, necessitates accurate and efficient diagnostic methods. This paper introduces CaDIS, a novel dataset designed to advance research in automated cataract segmentation in slit-lamp images. CaDIS comprises a diverse collection of meticulously annotated slit-lamp images, capturing varying degrees of cataract severity and morphological characteristics. We employ a semi-automatic annotation pipeline, leveraging expert ophthalmologist knowledge to ensure high-quality ground truth labels. We benchmark several state-of-the-art deep learning models, including U-Net and Mask R-CNN, on CaDIS, providing a comparative analysis of their segmentation performance. Experimental results demonstrate the challenges posed by cataract variability and highlight the potential for deep learning techniques in this domain. Specifically, we achieve a Dice score of 0.85 using a modified U-Net architecture. CaDIS serves as a valuable resource for developing and evaluating automated cataract diagnosis systems, paving the way for improved accessibility and efficiency in ophthalmological care. The dataset and benchmarking code are publicly available to foster further research. Keywords: Cataract Segmentation, Slit-Lamp Imaging, Deep Learning, U-Net, Medical Image Analysis, Dataset.

The proliferation of e-books has led to an information overload problem, making it increasingly difficult for users to discover relevant and appealing titles. This necessitates effective e-book recommendation systems to personalize user experiences and improve engagement. Current recommendation techniques often struggle with scalability and the cold-start problem, particularly in scenarios with sparse user-item interaction data. This thesis addresses these challenges by exploring the application of matrix decomposition techniques to build a robust and efficient e-book recommendation system. The primary objective of this research is to develop an e-book recommendation system that leverages matrix decomposition to predict user preferences and provide personalized recommendations. Specifically, this research aims to mitigate the sparsity problem inherent in e-book usage data and improve the accuracy and relevance of recommendations. To achieve this, we employ Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and other matrix factorization methods implemented using Python and libraries such as NumPy and Scikit-learn. The system architecture involves a data preprocessing stage, a model training phase using matrix decomposition, and a recommendation generation module. The system demonstrates improved recommendation accuracy compared to baseline methods, particularly in scenarios with limited user interaction data. The matrix decomposition approach effectively captures underlying patterns in user-item interactions, leading to more personalized and relevant recommendations. This research contributes to the field of recommender systems by demonstrating the effectiveness of matrix decomposition techniques in the context of e-book recommendation, particularly in addressing the data sparsity challenge. The system offers a practical solution for e-book platforms to enhance user experience and increase e-book consumption. In conclusion, this thesis demonstrates the successful application of matrix decomposition techniques in building an effective e-book recommendation system. The developed system addresses the critical issue of information overload and offers a personalized experience for e-book users. Future research could explore incorporating contextual information, such as user reviews and book descriptions, to further enhance the accuracy and relevance of recommendations. Furthermore, investigating hybrid approaches combining matrix decomposition with other recommendation techniques, such as content-based filtering, could provide further improvements in performance.

Mô hình đảm nhận việc truy cập cơ sở dữ lệu, xử lý dữ lệu và áp dụng quy tắc nghiệp vụ.

In recent years, the growing concerns over data privacy and the demand for scalable machine learning models have highlighted the need for innovative solutions in deep neural network (DNN) architecture. This paper presents a novel algorithmic-cryptographic co-design framework aimed at enhancing the scalability and privacy preservation of DNNs. Our approach integrates advanced cryptographic techniques with machine learning algorithms to ensure secure data processing without compromising model performance. We implement this framework in a series of experiments using benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in scalability with minimal computational overhead. Our results reveal that the co-designed model maintains robust privacy guarantees while achieving competitive accuracy compared to traditional DNNs. This research contributes to the evolving landscape of privacy-preserving AI, offering insights into the intersection of cryptography and artificial intelligence. The proposed framework could see applications across various domains, such as healthcare and finance, where data confidentiality is paramount. Keywords: deep neural networks, privacy-preserving, cryptography, machine learning, scalable systems.

This paper introduces ALBA, a novel reinforcement learning (RL) approach for video object segmentation. The objective is to address the limitations of existing supervised methods that require extensive manual annotation. ALBA employs an agent trained via RL to iteratively refine object segmentation masks across video frames. The method utilizes a deep neural network architecture to process visual features and predict actions that improve segmentation accuracy. The reward function is carefully designed to encourage accurate and consistent segmentation while penalizing errors. Bài toán xây dựng nền tảng dữ liệu khách hàng (Customer Data Platform - CDP) đang ngày càng trở nên cấp thiết trong bối cảnh cạnh tranh số khốc liệt, nơi trải nghiệm khách hàng đóng vai trò then chốt. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc xây dựng phân hệ phân tích dữ liệu và ứng dụng trong một CDP hoàn chỉnh, nhằm khai thác tối đa giá trị từ dữ liệu khách hàng, hỗ trợ các quyết định kinh doanh dựa trên dữ liệu (data-driven decision making). CDP được định nghĩa là một hệ thống hợp nhất dữ liệu khách hàng từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau, tạo ra một cái nhìn toàn diện (single customer view) và cho phép các bộ phận marketing, sales và dịch vụ khách hàng cá nhân hóa trải nghiệm, tương tác hiệu quả hơn. Phân hệ phân tích dữ liệu đóng vai trò trung tâm trong việc chuyển đổi dữ liệu thô thành thông tin chi tiết có giá trị. Nó bao gồm các công cụ và kỹ thuật để khám phá, phân tích và trực quan hóa dữ liệu khách hàng, từ đó xác định các xu hướng, phân khúc khách hàng, và dự đoán hành vi. Các kỹ thuật khai phá dữ liệu (data mining), học máy (machine learning) và thống kê được áp dụng để phân tích dữ liệu nhân khẩu học, hành vi trực tuyến, lịch sử mua hàng, tương tác trên mạng xã hội và các dữ liệu khác liên quan đến khách hàng. Kết quả phân tích được sử dụng để xây dựng các mô hình dự đoán, chẳng hạn như dự đoán khả năng khách hàng rời bỏ (churn prediction), dự đoán nhu cầu sản phẩm (product recommendation), hoặc dự đoán giá trị vòng đời khách hàng (customer lifetime value). Phân hệ ứng dụng sử dụng các thông tin chi tiết từ phân hệ phân tích để tạo ra các ứng dụng marketing và bán hàng được cá nhân hóa. Ví dụ, hệ thống có thể tự động gửi email marketing được cá nhân hóa cho từng phân khúc khách hàng, hiển thị quảng cáo phù hợp trên website, hoặc gợi ý sản phẩm phù hợp với sở thích của từng khách hàng. Ứng dụng cũng có thể được sử dụng để cải thiện trải nghiệm khách hàng trên các kênh khác nhau, chẳng hạn như cung cấp dịch vụ hỗ trợ khách hàng được cá nhân hóa, hoặc đề xuất các ưu đãi đặc biệt cho khách hàng thân thiết. Việc xây dựng CDP và đặc biệt là phân hệ phân tích dữ liệu và ứng dụng đòi hỏi sự kết hợp của nhiều công nghệ và kỹ năng khác nhau, bao gồm quản lý dữ liệu, phân tích dữ liệu, phát triển phần mềm và marketing. Nghiên cứu này trình bày một kiến trúc tổng thể cho CDP, tập trung vào các thành phần chính của phân hệ phân tích dữ liệu và ứng dụng, đồng thời thảo luận về các thách thức và cơ hội trong quá trình triển khai. Các kết quả nghiên cứu được kỳ vọng sẽ cung cấp một khung tham chiếu hữu ích cho các doanh nghiệp đang tìm cách xây dựng CDP để nâng cao hiệu quả marketing, tăng doanh số và cải thiện trải nghiệm khách hàng.

This research paper introduces "Ask & Explore," a novel approach to grounded question answering designed to facilitate curiosity-driven exploration. The objective is to enhance user interactions by enabling a system that effectively combines question answering with an exploration component, allowing users to deeply engage with their topics of interest. Methods/Approach: Our approach integrates state-of-the-art natural language processing techniques with a dynamic knowledge base, allowing the system to not only answer queries but also provide relevant and contextual exploratory paths. We developed a multi-layered algorithm that utilizes semantic embeddings and knowledge graphs to generate answers and suggest related exploration avenues. The system is fine-tuned on a diverse dataset to ensure adaptability across various domains. Results/Findings: The "Ask & Explore" system demonstrates significant improvement in user engagement compared to traditional question answering systems, offering a richer, more interactive exploration experience. In our evaluations, users found the suggested exploration paths to be relevant and enlightening, leading to a deeper understanding of the subject matter. The system also exhibited robust performance in accuracy and the contextual relevance of its answers. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of "Ask & Explore" provides a meaningful contribution to the fields of question answering and user-driven exploration. By bridging the gap between providing answers and facilitating exploration, this approach opens new possibilities for educational tools, informational search engines, and virtual assistants. The system's ability to guide users through a structured yet open-ended exploration has potential applications in education, research, and beyond, offering a new paradigm in human-computer interaction. Keywords: grounded question answering, curiosity-driven exploration, natural language processing, knowledge base, semantic embeddings, user engagement, interactive exploration.

This paper introduces a novel deep learning approach for feature embedding that leverages local similarity information to improve representation learning. The objective is to learn feature embeddings that effectively capture the underlying structure of data by explicitly considering the relationships between neighboring data points. We propose a local similarity-aware embedding network (LSAEN) that incorporates a similarity regularization term into the loss function. This term encourages the network to produce embeddings where similar data points in the original feature space are also close together in the embedded space. The LSAEN architecture consists of a deep neural network followed by a similarity preservation layer that enforces the local similarity constraints. We evaluate the performance of LSAEN on several benchmark datasets for tasks such as clustering and classification. Experimental results demonstrate that LSAEN consistently outperforms existing feature embedding methods, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and F1-score. The proposed approach offers a promising direction for learning more discriminative and robust feature representations, with potential applications in various computer vision and machine learning tasks. Keywords: Feature Embedding, Deep Learning, Similarity Learning, Representation Learning, Clustering, Classification.

Transformers, the default model of choices in natural language processing, have drawn scant attention from the medical imaging community. Given the ability to exploit long-term dependencies, transformers are promising to help atypical convolutional neural networks (convnets) to overcome its inherent shortcomings of spatial inductive bias. However, most of recently proposed transformer-based segmentation approaches simply treated transformers as assisted modules to help encode global context into convolutional representations without investigating how to optimally combine self-attention (i.e., the core of transformers) with convolution. To address this issue, in this paper, we introduce nnFormer (i.e., Not-aNother transFormer), a powerful segmentation model with an interleaved architecture based on empirical combination of self-attention and convolution. In practice, nnFormer learns volumetric representations from 3D local volumes. Compared to the naive voxel-level self-attention implementation, such volume-based operations help to reduce the computational complexity by approximate 98% and 99.5% on Synapse and ACDC datasets, respectively. In comparison to prior-art network configurations, nnFormer achieves tremendous improvements over previous transformer-based methods on two commonly used datasets Synapse and ACDC. For instance, nnFormer outperforms Swin-UNet by over 7 percents on Synapse. Even when compared to nnUNet, currently the best performing fully-convolutional medical segmentation network, nnFormer still provides slightly better performance on Synapse and ACDC.

Open Set Recognition (OSR) addresses the challenge of classifying known classes while identifying unknown or unseen data during inference, a critical requirement for real-world applications. This paper proposes a novel collective decision framework for OSR, leveraging ensemble learning to enhance robustness and accuracy in identifying both known and unknown classes. The proposed approach integrates multiple classifiers, each trained on diverse feature representations, to collectively determine the class of an input sample. By combining confidence scores and uncertainty measures, the framework effectively distinguishes between known and unknown instances. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in OSR performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher accuracy and lower false-positive rates. The framework’s adaptability to various domains and its ability to handle dynamic environments make it a promising solution for applications such as cybersecurity, autonomous systems, and medical diagnostics. This research contributes to advancing OSR by introducing a scalable and interpretable decision-making mechanism that bridges the gap between closed-set and open-set classification. **Keywords**: Open Set Recognition, ensemble learning, uncertainty estimation, collective decision-making, unknown class identification.

The paper addresses the challenge of accurate spatio-temporal forecasting, a critical component for various applications, such as traffic prediction, climate modeling, and resource management. Existing models often struggle with capturing the complex dependencies across space and time. Methods/Approach: We introduce HyperST-Net, a novel framework leveraging hypernetworks designed to enhance spatio-temporal predictive capabilities. HyperST-Net generates dynamic weights for a main network, enabling it to adaptively learn temporal and spatial features. This approach combines the strengths of hypernetworks with state-of-the-art neural network architectures to process multivariate time-series data effectively. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate that HyperST-Net outperforms current leading models in several benchmarking datasets across different domains. The model shows significant improvements in prediction accuracy and computation efficiency, effectively capturing both short-term and long-term dependencies. In addition, HyperST-Net exhibits superior generalization capabilities when applied to datasets not seen during training. Conclusion/Implications: The innovations in HyperST-Net offer valuable insights into the role of hypernetworks in spatio-temporal forecasting, establishing a new direction for future research. Its adaptability and performance gains suggest that HyperST-Net can serve as a foundational tool for industries reliant on predictive analytics. This research highlights the potential of hypernetworks in transforming complex data into actionable forecasts, paving the way for their implementation in real-world applications. Keywords: spatio-temporal forecasting, hypernetworks, predictive analytics, dynamic weights, neural networks, time-series data.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing the efficiency and stability of reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms by developing optimal learning rate policies. Traditional RL methods often rely on fixed or manually tuned learning rates, which can hinder convergence speed and lead to suboptimal performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts the learning rate based on real-time feedback from the training process, leveraging reward trajectories and loss landscape analysis. Our approach incorporates adaptive policy selection, using heuristic and data-driven strategies to fine-tune the learning rate at each episode or step, thereby improving the overall learning dynamics. Experimental evaluations are conducted on benchmark RL environments, demonstrating significant improvements in convergence speed, cumulative rewards, and robustness compared to conventional fixed and scheduled learning rate schemes. The proposed method demonstrates generalizability across multiple RL architectures, including value-based and policy-based algorithms. The results highlight the potential of adaptive learning rate policies to accelerate training and achieve superior performance in complex decision-making tasks. This work contributes to the advancement of RL by providing a practical solution for automated learning rate optimization, with implications for real-world applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and intelligent control. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, learning rate optimization, adaptive policy, convergence, algorithm performance.

Reinforcement learning (RL) agents often struggle to generalize effectively to unseen environments. This paper investigates a novel approach to enhance RL performance by strategically breaking generalization within the agent's neural network. We hypothesize that targeted disruption of generalization can force the agent to learn more robust and environment-agnostic features. Our method involves introducing a controlled level of noise and architectural modifications to specific layers of the neural network during training. Experiments conducted on benchmark RL environments, including Atari games and continuous control tasks, demonstrate significant improvements in both sample efficiency and asymptotic performance compared to traditional RL algorithms and regularization techniques. Specifically, our approach allows the agent to adapt to novel scenarios more rapidly and achieve higher rewards in complex environments. The findings suggest that an appropriate balance between generalization and specialization is crucial for effective RL, and that explicitly breaking generalization can be a valuable tool for improving agent performance. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Generalization, Neural Networks, Deep Learning, Noise Injection, Robustness.

This paper addresses the challenge of non-stationary Markov decision processes (NS-MDPs) by introducing a worst-case approach utilizing model-based reinforcement learning. The objective is to develop a framework that can adapt to changing environments and provide robust decision-making policies. Our approach employs a model-based reinforcement learning algorithm that learns a probabilistic model of the environment and uses it to compute a worst-case optimal policy. The method involves learning a set of probabilistic models that capture the potential changes in the environment and using them to compute a policy that maximizes the expected return in the worst-case scenario. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in various NS-MDPs, outperforming existing methods in terms of cumulative reward and adaptability. The key contributions of this work include a novel model-based reinforcement learning algorithm for NS-MDPs, a worst-case approach to decision-making, and an extensive evaluation of the method in various scenarios. This research has significant implications for real-world applications, such as robotics, finance, and healthcare, where non-stationarity is a common challenge. Key keywords: non-stationary Markov decision processes, model-based reinforcement learning, worst-case approach, robust decision-making, adaptive policies.

In this paper we propose a novel image representation called face X-ray for detecting forgery in face images. The face X-ray of an input face image is a greyscale image that reveals whether the input image can be decomposed into the blending of two images from different sources. It does so by showing the blending boundary for a forged image and the absence of blending for a real image. We observe that most existing face manipulation methods share a common step: blending the altered face into an existing background image. For this reason, face X-ray provides an effective way for detecting forgery generated by most existing face manipulation algorithms. Face X-ray is general in the sense that it only assumes the existence of a blending step and does not rely on any knowledge of the artifacts associated with a specific face manipulation technique. Indeed, the algorithm for computing face X-ray can be trained without fake images generated by any of the state-of-the-art face manipulation methods. Extensive experiments show that face X-ray remains effective when applied to forgery generated by unseen face manipulation techniques, while most existing face forgery detection or deepfake detection algorithms experience a significant performance drop.

Interactive Video Object Segmentation (IVOS) is a critical task in computer vision, enabling precise object segmentation in videos through user interaction. However, selecting the optimal frame for user annotation remains a significant challenge, especially in real-world scenarios with diverse video content. This paper introduces a novel framework for learning to recommend the most informative frame for user interaction, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of IVOS systems. Our approach leverages a deep learning-based model that analyzes video sequences to predict frames with high segmentation potential, considering factors such as object visibility, motion patterns, and scene complexity. We evaluate the proposed method on benchmark datasets and real-world videos, demonstrating its ability to reduce annotation effort while maintaining high segmentation quality. Experimental results show that our frame recommendation strategy outperforms existing methods in terms of both user interaction efficiency and segmentation accuracy. The proposed framework has broad applications in video editing, autonomous driving, and surveillance systems, where precise object segmentation is essential. This work contributes to advancing IVOS by introducing a data-driven approach to frame selection, paving the way for more user-friendly and effective video analysis tools. **Keywords**: Interactive Video Object Segmentation, Frame Recommendation, Deep Learning, Video Analysis, User Interaction, Computer Vision.

The rapid growth of graph-structured data in various domains, such as social networks, molecular structures, and recommendation systems, has necessitated the development of advanced generative models capable of capturing complex dependencies and hierarchical patterns. This paper introduces the Multiresolution Graph Variational Autoencoder (MGVAE), a novel framework designed to learn and generate graph data at multiple levels of granularity. The proposed approach leverages a hierarchical architecture to encode and decode graphs, enabling the model to capture both local and global structural properties effectively. By integrating multiresolution analysis with variational inference, MGVAE achieves superior performance in graph reconstruction and generation tasks compared to existing methods. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in terms of reconstruction accuracy, scalability, and the ability to generate realistic graphs. The model also exhibits robustness in handling sparse and noisy graph data. The findings highlight the potential of MGVAE for applications in drug discovery, network analysis, and other domains requiring high-fidelity graph generation. This work contributes to the advancement of graph-based generative models by introducing a scalable and interpretable framework for multiresolution graph representation learning. **Keywords**: Graph Variational Autoencoder, Multiresolution Analysis, Graph Generation, Hierarchical Models, Graph Representation Learning.

Modern large-scale machine learning applications require stochastic optimization algorithms to be implemented on distributed compute systems. A key bottleneck of such systems is the communication overhead for exchanging information across the workers, such as stochastic gradients. Among the many techniques proposed to remedy this issue, one of the most successful is the framework of compressed communication with error feedback (EF). EF remains the only known technique that can deal with the error induced by contractive compressors which are not unbiased, such as Top-K. In this paper, we propose a new and theoretically and practically better alternative to EF for dealing with contractive compressors. In particular, we propose a construction which can transform any contractive compressor into an induced unbiased compressor. Following this transformation, existing methods able to work with unbiased compressors can be applied. We show that our approach leads to vast improvements over EF, including reduced memory requirements, better communication complexity guarantees and fewer assumptions. We further extend our results to federated learning with partial participation following an arbitrary distribution over the nodes, and demonstrate the benefits thereof. We perform several numerical experiments which validate our theoretical findings.

We propose a novel architecture which is able to automatically anonymize faces in images while retaining the original data distribution. We ensure total anonymization of all faces in an image by generating images exclusively on privacy-safe information. Our model is based on a conditional generative adversarial network, generating images considering the original pose and image background. The conditional information enables us to generate highly realistic faces with a seamless transition between the generated face and the existing background. Furthermore, we introduce a diverse dataset of human faces, including unconventional poses, occluded faces, and a vast variability in backgrounds. Finally, we present experimental results reflecting the capability of our model to anonymize images while preserving the data distribution, making the data suitable for further training of deep learning models. As far as we know, no other solution has been proposed that guarantees the anonymization of faces while generating realistic images.

Hệ thống đo lường tự động dựa trên LabVIEW và Internet of Things (IoT) được thiết kế để giám sát và phân tích các dữ liệu trong thời gian thực.
