Efficient methods to evaluate new algorithms are critical for improving interactive bandit and reinforcement learning systems such as recommendation systems. A/B tests are reliable, but are time- and money-consuming, and entail a risk of failure. In this paper, we develop an alternative method, which predicts the performance of algorithms given historical data that may have been generated by a different algorithm. Our estimator has the property that its prediction converges in probability to the true performance of a counterfactual algorithm at a rate of , as the sample size N increases. We also show a correct way to estimate the variance of our prediction, thus allowing the analyst to quantify the uncertainty in the prediction. These properties hold even when the analyst does not know which among a large number of potentially important state variables are actually important. We validate our method by a simulation experiment about reinforcement learning. We finally apply it to improve advertisement design by a major advertisement company. We find that our method produces smaller mean squared errors than state-of-the-art methods.

Event-based vision sensors capture dynamic scenes with high temporal resolution and low power consumption, making them ideal for real-time applications. However, processing event-based data poses significant challenges due to its asynchronous and sparse nature. This paper introduces **Event-LSTM**, a novel unsupervised learning framework designed to effectively represent and process event-based data. The proposed approach leverages Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to model temporal dependencies in an asynchronous manner, eliminating the need for labeled datasets. Event-LSTM operates directly on raw event streams, preserving the inherent sparsity and temporal precision of the data. Experimental results demonstrate that Event-LSTM outperforms existing methods in tasks such as event-based object recognition and motion prediction, achieving state-of-the-art performance with reduced computational overhead. The framework’s unsupervised nature and ability to handle asynchronous inputs make it highly adaptable for real-world applications, including robotics, autonomous systems, and low-power edge devices. This work contributes a significant advancement in event-based data representation, offering a scalable and efficient solution for processing sparse temporal data. **Keywords**: Event-based vision, LSTM, unsupervised learning, asynchronous processing, spatiotemporal representation, event cameras.

We introduce a collection of datasets from fundamental physics research -- including particle physics, astroparticle physics, and hadron- and nuclear physics -- for supervised machine learning studies. These datasets, containing hadronic top quarks, cosmic-ray induced air showers, phase transitions in hadronic matter, and generator-level histories, are made public to simplify future work on cross-disciplinary machine learning and transfer learning in fundamental physics. Based on these data, we present a simple yet flexible graph-based neural network architecture that can easily be applied to a wide range of supervised learning tasks in these domains. We show that our approach reaches performance close to state-of-the-art dedicated methods on all datasets. To simplify adaptation for various problems, we provide easy-to-follow instructions on how graph-based representations of data structures, relevant for fundamental physics, can be constructed and provide code implementations for several of them. Implementations are also provided for our proposed method and all reference algorithms.

Adversarial representation learning is a promising paradigm for obtaining data representations that are invariant to certain sensitive attributes while retaining the information necessary for predicting target attributes. Existing approaches solve this problem through iterative adversarial minimax optimization and lack theoretical guarantees. In this paper, we first study the "linear" form of this problem i.e., the setting where all the players are linear functions. We show that the resulting optimization problem is both non-convex and non-differentiable. We obtain an exact closed-form expression for its global optima through spectral learning and provide performance guarantees in terms of analytical bounds on the achievable utility and invariance. We then extend this solution and analysis to non-linear functions through kernel representation. Numerical experiments on UCI, Extended Yale B and CIFAR-100 datasets indicate that, (a) practically, our solution is ideal for "imparting" provable invariance to any biased pre-trained data representation, and (b) empirically, the trade-off between utility and invariance provided by our solution is comparable to iterative minimax optimization of existing deep neural network based approaches. Code is available at https://github.com/human-analysis/Kernel-ARL

Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success across various domains, yet their training dynamics remain a critical area of research. This paper addresses the challenge of improving training efficiency and stability by introducing a novel approach called *Controllable Orthogonalization*. The proposed method dynamically enforces orthogonality constraints on the weight matrices during training, aiming to mitigate issues such as vanishing gradients, poor conditioning, and overfitting. We present a lightweight, computationally efficient algorithm that integrates seamlessly into existing optimization frameworks, such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and its variants. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances convergence speed and model generalization compared to traditional training methods. Furthermore, the method exhibits robustness across diverse architectures, including convolutional and recurrent neural networks. The findings suggest that controllable orthogonalization offers a promising direction for improving the scalability and reliability of DNN training, with potential applications in large-scale AI systems and resource-constrained environments. **Keywords**: Deep Neural Networks, Orthogonalization, Training Dynamics, Optimization, Gradient Descent, Model Generalization.

Point cloud processing is crucial for various applications, including autonomous driving and robotics, yet effectively capturing local geometric information remains a challenge. This paper introduces KPConv, a novel convolution operator designed for point clouds that offers both flexibility and deformability. KPConv leverages a set of kernel points to define the receptive field, enabling the learning of complex geometric features. The positions of these kernel points are learned during training, allowing the convolution to adapt to the local shape of the point cloud. We demonstrate the efficacy of KPConv on several benchmark datasets for 3D shape classification, semantic segmentation, and object part segmentation. Results show that KPConv achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining computational efficiency. The flexible and deformable nature of KPConv allows it to effectively capture intricate geometric details, leading to improved accuracy in point cloud analysis. Keywords: Point clouds, convolution, deep learning, geometric feature extraction, 3D processing.

We introduce Point-MVSNet, a novel point-based deep framework for multi-view stereo (MVS). Distinct from existing cost volume approaches, our method directly processes the target scene as point clouds. More specifically, our method predicts the depth in a coarse-to-fine manner. We first generate a coarse depth map, convert it into a point cloud and refine the point cloud iteratively by estimating the residual between the depth of the current iteration and that of the ground truth. Our network leverages 3D geometry priors and 2D texture information jointly and effectively by fusing them into a feature-augmented point cloud, and processes the point cloud to estimate the 3D flow for each point. This point-based architecture allows higher accuracy, more computational efficiency and more flexibility than cost-volume-based counterparts. Experimental results show that our approach achieves a significant improvement in reconstruction quality compared with state-of-the-art methods on the DTU and the Tanks and Temples dataset. Our source code and trained models are available at https://github.com/callmeray/PointMVSNet .

The rapid growth of digital content, particularly e-books, has created a pressing need for effective recommendation systems to enhance user experience and engagement. Traditional recommendation methods often struggle with scalability and accuracy, especially in handling large and sparse datasets. This research addresses these challenges by applying matrix decomposition techniques to develop a robust e-book recommendation system. The importance of this study lies in its potential to improve personalized content delivery, thereby increasing user satisfaction and retention in digital platforms. The primary objective of this thesis is to design and implement a recommendation system that leverages matrix decomposition, specifically Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), to predict user preferences accurately. The system aims to solve key issues such as data sparsity, cold-start problems, and computational inefficiency, which are common in traditional collaborative filtering approaches. The methodology involves preprocessing e-book interaction data, constructing a user-item interaction matrix, and applying matrix decomposition techniques to extract latent features. The system architecture integrates these techniques with a user-friendly interface, enabling real-time recommendations. Python libraries such as NumPy, SciPy, and Scikit-learn are utilized for implementation, while evaluation metrics like Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) are employed to assess performance. Preliminary results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves higher recommendation accuracy compared to baseline methods, effectively reducing prediction errors. The research contributes to the field by showcasing the practical application of matrix decomposition in e-commerce and digital content platforms, offering a scalable solution for personalized recommendations. In conclusion, this study highlights the effectiveness of matrix decomposition techniques in enhancing e-book recommendation systems. Future work could explore hybrid models combining matrix decomposition with deep learning approaches or extending the system to other domains such as video or music recommendations. This research paves the way for more advanced and user-centric recommendation systems in the digital age.

Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGs) represent dynamic relationships between entities over time, posing unique challenges for prediction and inference tasks. Traditional methods often require extensive labeled data, limiting their applicability in scenarios where data is scarce. This paper addresses the problem of one-shot learning for TKGs, aiming to enable accurate predictions with minimal training examples. We propose a novel framework that leverages meta-learning techniques to adapt quickly to new temporal patterns and relationships. Our approach combines graph neural networks with temporal attention mechanisms to capture both structural and temporal dependencies effectively. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing baselines in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness, particularly in low-data regimes. The framework also shows significant improvements in handling unseen entities and relationships, highlighting its generalization capabilities. This research contributes to advancing the field of TKGs by providing a scalable and efficient solution for one-shot learning, with potential applications in areas such as recommendation systems, event forecasting, and dynamic network analysis. **Keywords**: Temporal Knowledge Graphs, One-shot Learning, Meta-learning, Graph Neural Networks, Temporal Attention, Dynamic Networks.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) offers the potential to learn optimal policies from previously collected, static datasets without requiring online interaction with the environment. However, a key challenge lies in effectively handling distributional shift and the lack of exploration. This paper introduces a novel approach, Residual Generative Modeling (RGM), to boost the performance of offline RL algorithms. RGM leverages a generative model to learn the residual between the state-action distribution in the offline dataset and the state-action distribution induced by the current policy. By explicitly modeling this residual, we can generate more realistic and relevant data for policy optimization, mitigating the distributional shift problem. We integrate RGM with existing offline RL algorithms, such as Behavior Cloning and Conservative Q-Learning, and evaluate their performance on a range of benchmark tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that RGM significantly improves the sample efficiency and overall performance of these algorithms, achieving state-of-the-art results in several domains. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of using generative models to address the challenges of offline RL and provide a promising direction for future research. Keywords: Offline Reinforcement Learning, Generative Modeling, Distributional Shift, Residual Learning, Policy Optimization.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurately predicting network-wide traffic speed, an essential component for effective traffic management and planning in intelligent transportation systems. Traditional methods often struggle with capturing the complex temporal dependencies and nonlinear patterns inherent in traffic data. Methods/Approach: To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel approach utilizing both deep bidirectional and unidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Recurrent Neural Networks. The bidirectional LSTM model is designed to capture contextual information by processing data in both forward and backward directions, while the unidirectional LSTM focuses on sequential dependencies in a single temporal direction. This hybrid framework combines the strengths of both strategies to enhance predictive accuracy and adaptability. Results/Findings: Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms conventional traffic speed prediction methods and previous LSTM-based models in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness. The evaluation metrics indicate substantial improvements across various benchmarks, affirming the model's efficacy in handling complex traffic patterns and achieving real-time prediction capabilities. Conclusion/Implications: The study introduces a robust machine learning framework for traffic speed prediction that can be applied to diverse urban traffic networks. By leveraging the complementary advantages of bidirectional and unidirectional LSTMs, this approach not only enhances prediction performance but also offers potential applications in optimizing traffic flow, reducing congestion, and augmenting smart city initiatives. Our contribution highlights the importance of advanced deep learning models in transforming traffic management and laying the groundwork for future research in dynamic traffic prediction systems. Keywords: Traffic speed prediction, LSTM, bidirectional LSTM, recurrent neural network, intelligent transportation systems, deep learning.

Medical image processing has become a critical area of research, driven by the increasing demand for accurate and efficient diagnostic tools. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the application of deep learning techniques in medical image processing, highlighting their potential to revolutionize healthcare. The objective of this study is to explore the current state-of-the-art methods, identify key challenges, and propose future directions for research. We review various deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and generative adversarial networks (GANs), and their applications in tasks like image segmentation, classification, and reconstruction. The challenges discussed include limited annotated datasets, model interpretability, and computational constraints. Our findings demonstrate that deep learning models achieve superior performance compared to traditional methods, particularly in complex tasks like tumor detection and organ segmentation. However, issues such as data privacy and model generalization remain significant hurdles. The paper concludes by emphasizing the need for interdisciplinary collaboration, robust evaluation frameworks, and the integration of emerging technologies like federated learning and explainable AI. This research contributes to advancing the field by providing a roadmap for addressing current limitations and unlocking the full potential of deep learning in medical imaging. **Keywords**: Deep learning, medical image processing, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), image segmentation, healthcare, explainable AI.

In this work we present a monocular visual odometry (VO) algorithm which leverages geometry-based methods and deep learning. Most existing VO/SLAM systems with superior performance are based on geometry and have to be carefully designed for different application scenarios. Moreover, most monocular systems suffer from scale-drift issue.Some recent deep learning works learn VO in an end-to-end manner but the performance of these deep systems is still not comparable to geometry-based methods. In this work, we revisit the basics of VO and explore the right way for integrating deep learning with epipolar geometry and Perspective-n-Point (PnP) method. Specifically, we train two convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for estimating single-view depths and two-view optical flows as intermediate outputs. With the deep predictions, we design a simple but robust frame-to-frame VO algorithm (DF-VO) which outperforms pure deep learning-based and geometry-based methods. More importantly, our system does not suffer from the scale-drift issue being aided by a scale consistent single-view depth CNN. Extensive experiments on KITTI dataset shows the robustness of our system and a detailed ablation study shows the effect of different factors in our system.

Human action recognition in complex events remains a challenging task due to the variability in human poses, occlusions, and dynamic environments. This paper presents a novel group-skeleton-based approach to improve the accuracy and robustness of action recognition in such scenarios. The proposed method leverages skeletal data extracted from multiple individuals within a group, capturing both individual actions and their interactions. A multi-stream deep learning architecture is introduced, combining spatial, temporal, and relational features to model the intricate dependencies between group members. The spatial stream processes joint positions, the temporal stream analyzes motion dynamics, and the relational stream encodes inter-person dependencies using graph-based representations. Experiments were conducted on two benchmark datasets, NTU RGB+D and Kinetics, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods. The proposed approach achieved an accuracy improvement of 5.2% on NTU RGB+D and 3.8% on Kinetics, particularly excelling in scenarios with occlusions and crowded environments. The results highlight the effectiveness of group-skeleton-based modeling in capturing contextual information and improving recognition accuracy. This work contributes to advancing human action recognition by addressing the challenges of complex events, with potential applications in surveillance, human-computer interaction, and sports analytics. **Keywords**: Human action recognition, group-skeleton modeling, multi-stream architecture, graph-based representations, complex events.

Breast cancer screening is a critical area of healthcare where accurate and reliable diagnostic tools are essential. This paper introduces a novel evaluation metric for breast cancer screening, leveraging Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) to provide robust confidence measures in diagnostic predictions. The proposed approach addresses the limitations of traditional evaluation metrics by incorporating uncertainty quantification, enabling more informed decision-making in clinical settings. The methodology involves training BNNs on a comprehensive dataset of mammographic images, where the network's probabilistic outputs are used to derive confidence scores for each prediction. These scores are then integrated into a new evaluation metric that assesses both accuracy and reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed metric outperforms conventional methods, achieving higher sensitivity and specificity while effectively reducing false positives. The findings highlight the potential of BNNs in enhancing the interpretability and trustworthiness of AI-driven diagnostic systems. This research contributes to the field by providing a more nuanced and reliable framework for evaluating breast cancer screening tools, with implications for improving early detection and patient outcomes. **Keywords**: Bayesian Neural Networks, confidence measures, breast cancer screening, evaluation metric, uncertainty quantification, diagnostic accuracy.

Reinforcement learning (RL) offers the potential to automate robot control, but deploying RL algorithms on real-world robots remains challenging. This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark of several state-of-the-art RL algorithms applied to a diverse set of robotic tasks, including manipulation, locomotion, and navigation, on physical robot platforms. We evaluate both model-free (e.g., SAC, TD3) and model-based RL methods, focusing on sample efficiency, robustness to sensor noise, and transferability across similar tasks. Our experimental results demonstrate significant performance variations across different algorithms and tasks, highlighting the critical need for careful algorithm selection and hyperparameter tuning. We identify key factors influencing the success of RL in real-world robotics, such as reward function design, exploration strategies, and the impact of sim-to-real transfer techniques. The benchmark provides valuable insights and practical guidelines for researchers and practitioners aiming to apply RL to real-world robotic systems, accelerating the development of autonomous and adaptive robots. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Robotics, Benchmarking, Real-World Experiments, Robot Control, Autonomous Systems.

The proposed approach leverages a hybrid model combining unsupervised clustering techniques with supervised learning algorithms to automatically categorize datasets based on their inherent characteristics. By integrating feature extraction and dimensionality reduction, the method ensures robust classification even for high-dimensional and heterogeneous datasets. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 12% improvement in classification accuracy compared to existing techniques, while significantly reducing computational overhead. The findings highlight the method's potential for enhancing data mining workflows, particularly in applications requiring real-time processing and large-scale data analysis. This research contributes to the field by providing a scalable and efficient solution for dataset classification, with implications for improving decision-making processes in areas such as healthcare, finance, and e-commerce. **Keywords**: dataset classification, data mining, hybrid model, unsupervised clustering, supervised learning, feature extraction, scalability.

Through many recent successes in simulation, model-free reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising approach to solving continuous control robotic tasks. The research community is now able to reproduce, analyze and build quickly on these results due to open source implementations of learning algorithms and simulated benchmark tasks. To carry forward these successes to real-world applications, it is crucial to withhold utilizing the unique advantages of simulations that do not transfer to the real world and experiment directly with physical robots. However, reinforcement learning research with physical robots faces substantial resistance due to the lack of benchmark tasks and supporting source code. In this work, we introduce several reinforcement learning tasks with multiple commercially available robots that present varying levels of learning difficulty, setup, and repeatability. On these tasks, we test the learning performance of off-the-shelf implementations of four reinforcement learning algorithms and analyze sensitivity to their hyper-parameters to determine their readiness for applications in various real-world tasks. Our results show that with a careful setup of the task interface and computations, some of these implementations can be readily applicable to physical robots. We find that state-of-the-art learning algorithms are highly sensitive to their hyper-parameters and their relative ordering does not transfer across tasks, indicating the necessity of re-tuning them for each task for best performance. On the other hand, the best hyper-parameter configuration from one task may often result in effective learning on held-out tasks even with different robots, providing a reasonable default. We make the benchmark tasks publicly available to enhance reproducibility in real-world reinforcement learning.

Outlier detection plays a critical role in ensuring the reliability and robustness of decision-making systems, particularly within the context of multi-armed bandit (MAB) problems commonly found in online recommendation, adaptive experimentation, and real-time optimization. This paper presents a novel, generic framework for outlier detection in multi-armed bandit settings, addressing the limitations of existing methods that often lack flexibility and robustness across diverse environments. The proposed approach integrates statistical modeling and adaptive learning within the MAB paradigm to effectively identify anomalous arms—those that deviate significantly from expected reward distributions—without prior knowledge of arm behavior. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method accurately detects outliers and mitigates their negative impact on cumulative reward and arm selection strategies. Comparative analysis reveals that our framework outperforms traditional MAB algorithms and specialized outlier detectors in terms of detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and versatility. The solution is scalable, model-agnostic, and readily adaptable to various MAB applications, supporting continuous online monitoring and dynamic policy adjustment. **Abstract:** Bid rigging undermines the integrity of procurement processes and results in significant economic losses worldwide. Traditional detection methods are often labor-intensive and may not effectively identify subtle collusive behaviors within large datasets. This paper proposes a deep learning-based approach for detecting bid rigging, leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automatically flag potential cartel participants. Our method transforms bidder transaction data into structured representations suitable for input into CNN architectures, enabling the model to capture complex patterns and anomalies associated with collusive activities. Using real-world procurement datasets and simulated cartel scenarios, we evaluate the performance of our model against conventional statistical and machine learning techniques. The results demonstrate that the proposed CNN approach achieves superior detection accuracy and demonstrates robust generalization across diverse bidding environments. Key contributions include an end-to-end automated framework for bid rigging detection, feature representation techniques tailored to procurement data, and systematic performance evaluation of deep learning models for anti-cartel enforcement. This research provides valuable insights for regulatory authorities, procurement professionals, and researchers, showcasing the potential of artificial intelligence in promoting fair and competitive markets. **Keywords:** deep learning, bid rigging detection, cartel flagging, convolutional neural networks, procurement analytics, anti-collusion, artificial intelligence.

Deep learning models applied to 3D point cloud data have demonstrated remarkable performance in various applications. However, their robustness to adversarial attacks, particularly those that exploit geometric vulnerabilities, remains a significant concern. This paper investigates the isometry robustness of deep 3D point cloud models against adversarial perturbations. We propose a novel adversarial attack strategy, Isometry-Aware Perturbation (IAP), that crafts perturbations while preserving the underlying geometric structure of the point cloud. IAP leverages isometric transformations to generate imperceptible yet effective attacks that significantly degrade model performance. Through extensive experiments on ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN datasets, we demonstrate that IAP consistently outperforms existing attack methods in terms of attack success rate and transferability. Furthermore, we evaluate the effectiveness of several defense mechanisms against IAP and identify vulnerabilities in current defense strategies. Our findings reveal the inherent susceptibility of deep 3D models to isometry-based adversarial attacks, highlighting the need for robust training methods that account for geometric invariance. This work contributes a new perspective on adversarial robustness in 3D point cloud analysis and provides insights for developing more resilient deep learning models. **Keywords:** 3D Point Clouds, Adversarial Attacks, Isometry Robustness, Deep Learning, Geometric Perturbations, Security.

Graph representation learning has gained significant attention for its ability to model complex relationships in structured data. However, detecting critical structures within graphs, such as bridges or central nodes, remains a challenging task, especially in distributed and scalable settings. This paper introduces *Ego-CNN*, a novel framework that leverages egocentric representations of graphs to identify critical structures efficiently. The proposed approach utilizes localized, ego-centric subgraphs to capture structural information, enabling distributed computation and reducing computational overhead. By employing a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture tailored for graph data, *Ego-CNN* extracts meaningful features from these subgraphs, facilitating the detection of critical structures with high accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that *Ego-CNN* outperforms existing methods in terms of both detection performance and scalability. The framework’s distributed nature makes it particularly suitable for large-scale graphs, offering significant improvements in computational efficiency. This work contributes to the field of graph analytics by providing a scalable, egocentric approach to critical structure detection, with potential applications in network analysis, social media, and infrastructure monitoring. **Keywords**: Graph representation learning, egocentric graphs, critical structure detection, distributed computing, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), scalability.

This paper presents a novel approach to Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) leveraging a technique we refer to as Random Environmental Mixup. The primary objective is to enhance the robustness and generalization of VLN models by diversifying training scenarios through the randomized mixing of environmental contexts. We introduce an algorithm that combines different navigational environments while preserving semantic coherence, allowing agents to learn from varied spatial and linguistic cues. Our experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in both navigation accuracy and efficiency when compared to traditional training methods. The agent trained with our Random Environmental Mixup approach achieved a 15% increase in success rates in unseen environments, showcasing its capacity to generalize beyond specific training setups. The implications of our findings suggest that this innovative methodology not only contributes to the field of VLN but also opens avenues for further research in combining multi-modal data in dynamic settings. Ultimately, our work underscores the potential of environmental diversity in training robust and adaptable AI systems designed for real-world navigation tasks. Keywords: Vision-Language Navigation, Environmental Mixup, Multi-modal Learning, AI Robustness, Navigation Efficiency.

More attention is being paid for feature importance ranking (FIR), in particular when thousands of features can be extracted for intelligent diagnosis and personalized medicine. A large number of FIR approaches have been proposed, while few are integrated for comparison and real-life applications. In this study, a matlab toolbox is presented and a total of 30 algorithms are collected. Moreover, the toolbox is evaluated on a database of 163 ultrasound images. To each breast mass lesion, 15 features are extracted. To figure out the optimal subset of features for classification, all combinations of features are tested and linear support vector machine is used for the malignancy prediction of lesions annotated in ultrasound images. At last, the effectiveness of FIR is analyzed according to performance comparison. The toolbox is online (https://github.com/NicoYuCN/matFIR). In our future work, more FIR methods, feature selection methods and machine learning classifiers will be integrated.

This paper presents an unsupervised learning approach for discovering local discriminative representations in medical images. The objective is to learn compact and informative features from large datasets of medical images without requiring labeled data. Our method employs a novel architecture that combines convolutional neural networks with self-supervised learning techniques to identify distinctive patterns and structures in medical images. The approach is based on a competitive learning mechanism that encourages the discovery of unique and discriminative features at the local level. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in learning meaningful representations that can be used for various medical image analysis tasks, such as image classification, segmentation, and retrieval. Compared to existing unsupervised learning methods, our approach shows improved performance and robustness in handling large datasets of medical images. The proposed technique has significant implications for medical image analysis, as it enables the discovery of hidden patterns and relationships in large datasets without requiring extensive labeled data. Key contributions include the development of a novel unsupervised learning framework, the discovery of local discriminative representations, and the demonstration of improved performance in medical image analysis tasks. Relevant keywords: unsupervised learning, medical images, local discriminative representation, self-supervised learning, convolutional neural networks, medical image analysis.

This paper explores the approximation theory of convolutional architectures for time series modelling, addressing the challenge of accurately capturing complex patterns in temporal data. Our objective is to develop a deeper understanding of the representational capabilities of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in modelling time series data. We propose a novel approach that leverages the strengths of CNNs in extracting local features and combining them to model long-term dependencies. Our method utilizes a customized convolutional architecture that incorporates dilated convolutions and attention mechanisms to improve the model's ability to capture multi-scale patterns. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming existing state-of-the-art models on several benchmark time series datasets. Our findings highlight the importance of carefully designing convolutional architectures for time series modelling and provide new insights into the approximation theory of CNNs in this context. The contributions of this research have significant implications for the development of more accurate and efficient time series forecasting models, with potential applications in fields such as finance, climate modelling, and signal processing. Key keywords: convolutional neural networks, time series modelling, approximation theory, dilated convolutions, attention mechanisms.

Transfer learning using pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has been successfully applied to images for different classification tasks. In this paper, we propose a new pipeline for pain expression recognition in neonates using transfer learning. Specifically, we propose to exploit a pre-trained CNN that was originally trained on a relatively similar dataset for face recognition (VGG Face) as well as CNNs that were pre-trained on a relatively different dataset for image classification (iVGG F,M, and S) to extract deep features from neonates' faces. In the final stage, several supervised machine learning classifiers are trained to classify neonates' facial expression into pain or no pain expression. The proposed pipeline achieved, on a testing dataset, 0.841 AUC and 90.34 accuracy, which is approx. 7 higher than the accuracy of handcrafted traditional features. We also propose to combine deep features with traditional features and hypothesize that the mixed features would improve pain classification performance. Combining deep features with traditional features achieved 92.71 accuracy and 0.948 AUC. These results show that transfer learning, which is a faster and more practical option than training CNN from the scratch, can be used to extract useful features for pain expression recognition in neonates. It also shows that combining deep features with traditional handcrafted features is a good practice to improve the performance of pain expression recognition and possibly the performance of similar applications.

This paper investigates the impact of feature alignment on object detection models, with a focus on improving clean average precision and adversarial robustness. Our objective is to enhance the performance and security of object detection systems by aligning features extracted from images. We propose a novel approach that utilizes feature alignment to reduce the discrepancy between features from different images, thereby improving model robustness. Our method employs a feature alignment module that minimizes the distance between features, resulting in more accurate and robust object detection. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves clean average precision and adversarial robustness compared to state-of-the-art object detection models. Notably, our model achieves a substantial increase in average precision under various adversarial attacks, highlighting its potential for real-world applications where security is a concern. The key contributions of this research include the development of a feature alignment-based object detection framework, which offers improved performance, robustness, and security. Our work has important implications for computer vision and machine learning, particularly in areas such as autonomous vehicles, surveillance, and robotics, where object detection plays a critical role. Key keywords: object detection, feature alignment, adversarial robustness, average precision, computer vision, machine learning.

Bệnh viện Nhân dân vừa công bố kết quả phân tích tình hình sử dụng thuốc điều trị ung thư vú cho bệnh nhân nội trú. Nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc đánh giá thực trạng sử dụng các loại thuốc, phác đồ điều trị, và hiệu quả lâm sàng trên nhóm bệnh nhân này. Các dữ liệu về độ tuổi, giai đoạn bệnh, tiền sử điều trị, và các bệnh lý kèm theo cũng được thu thập và phân tích. Mục tiêu của nghiên cứu là xác định các vấn đề còn tồn tại trong quá trình điều trị, từ đó đề xuất các giải pháp nhằm tối ưu hóa việc sử dụng thuốc, nâng cao hiệu quả điều trị, giảm thiểu tác dụng phụ, và cải thiện chất lượng cuộc sống cho bệnh nhân ung thư vú. Kết quả phân tích sẽ cung cấp cơ sở khoa học cho việc xây dựng các hướng dẫn điều trị phù hợp, cập nhật phác đồ điều trị, và đào tạo chuyên môn cho đội ngũ y tế. Đồng thời, bệnh viện cũng hy vọng có thể giảm chi phí điều trị thông qua việc sử dụng thuốc hợp lý và hiệu quả hơn.

Hệ thống đề xuất ngày càng đóng vai trò quan trọng, nhưng nguy cơ tạo ra sự bất công cũng gia tăng. Một nghiên cứu mới tập trung vào việc xây dựng các hệ thống đề xuất công bằng hơn, sử dụng phương pháp tiếp cận dựa trên tiện ích R. Bằng cách tối ưu hóa tiện ích R, hệ thống có thể giảm thiểu sự thiên vị và tăng cường tính minh bạch trong quá trình đề xuất. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp một khuôn khổ thực tế để phát triển các hệ thống đề xuất không chỉ hiệu quả mà còn công bằng, góp phần tạo ra một môi trường trực tuyến công bằng hơn cho tất cả mọi người. Ứng dụng của phương pháp này hứa hẹn sẽ cải thiện trải nghiệm người dùng và thúc đẩy sự phát triển bền vững của các nền tảng trực tuyến.

Nước thải từ ngành này thường chứa nhiều chất ô nhiễm như kim loại nặng, chất rắn lơ lửng và các hợp chất hóa học độc hại. Các phương pháp xử lý phổ biến bao gồm lắng, lọc, hấp phụ, oxy hóa và sinh học. Mỗi phương pháp có ưu nhược điểm riêng, tùy thuộc vào thành phần và tính chất của nước thải. Việc kết hợp nhiều công nghệ xử lý thường mang lại hiệu quả cao hơn, đảm bảo nước thải đạt tiêu chuẩn trước khi xả ra môi trường. Nghiên cứu và ứng dụng các giải pháp tiên tiến, thân thiện với môi trường là xu hướng tất yếu trong bối cảnh phát triển bền vững hiện nay.

This paper proposes a novel evaluation metric for breast cancer screening using Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs), focusing on the development of an efficient confidence measure-based approach. The objective is to improve the accuracy and reliability of breast cancer diagnosis by leveraging the uncertainty estimation capabilities of BNNs. Our method employs a Bayesian framework to model the uncertainty associated with neural network predictions, allowing for the calculation of confidence measures that reflect the reliability of the diagnosis. The results show that our proposed metric outperforms traditional evaluation metrics, achieving higher accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) scores. The key findings indicate that the integration of confidence measures with BNNs enhances the robustness and trustworthiness of breast cancer screening systems. This research contributes to the advancement of AI-assisted diagnosis in healthcare, highlighting the potential of Bayesian neural networks and confidence measure-based evaluation metrics to improve patient outcomes. The proposed approach has significant implications for the development of more accurate and reliable breast cancer screening systems, and its novelty lies in the combination of Bayesian inference and confidence measure-based evaluation, making it a valuable contribution to the field of medical imaging and AI-assisted diagnosis. Key keywords: Bayesian Neural Networks, Breast Cancer Screening, Confidence Measure, Evaluation Metric, Uncertainty Estimation, AI-assisted Diagnosis.

This paper introduces MeanShift++, a novel algorithm designed for extremely fast mode-seeking. Addressing the computational limitations of traditional Mean Shift, our approach leverages a highly optimized search strategy combined with adaptive bandwidth selection to significantly accelerate convergence. The algorithm’s efficiency stems from a combination of precomputed data structures and a novel pruning technique that drastically reduces the number of necessary kernel evaluations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of MeanShift++ in two key applications: image segmentation and object tracking. In image segmentation, our method achieves state-of-the-art results with substantially reduced processing time compared to existing techniques. For object tracking, MeanShift++ offers robust and real-time performance, even in challenging scenarios with cluttered backgrounds and occlusions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate a speedup of up to an order of magnitude over standard Mean Shift implementations without sacrificing accuracy. The proposed MeanShift++ algorithm provides a practical and efficient solution for mode-seeking, enabling its wider adoption in various computer vision applications. Keywords: Mean Shift, Mode-Seeking, Segmentation, Object Tracking, Clustering, Computer Vision, Real-Time.

Best group subset selection aims to choose a small part of non-overlapping groups to achieve the best interpretability on the response variable. It is practically attractive for group variable selection; however, due to the computational intractability in high dimensionality setting, it doesn't catch enough attention. To fill the blank of efficient algorithms for best group subset selection, in this paper, we propose a group-splicing algorithm that iteratively detects effective groups and excludes the helpless ones. Moreover, coupled with a novel Bayesian group information criterion, an adaptive algorithm is developed to determine the true group subset size. It is certifiable that our algorithms enable identifying the optimal group subset in polynomial time under mild conditions. We demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of our proposal by comparing state-of-the-art algorithms on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

The argument demonstrates that the sequence ck,s avoids containing the pattern 0^(s+1) by leveraging the unique properties of Lyndon words. Specifically, uk,s is constructed as the largest Lyndon word featuring exactly s+1 consecutive 0s, which implies that every Lyndon word in the canonical decomposition of ck,s contains no instance of 0^(s+1) as a substring. Furthermore, when these Lyndon words are concatenated together to form ck,s, the absence of the forbidden pattern remains preserved. Therefore, the final sequence ck,s qualifies as a (k, s)-RdB sequence, confirming its desired structural property.

This paper presents a novel approach to real-time fire and flame detection, addressing the need for accurate and efficient systems in various applications. Our objective is to develop a robust and reliable method for detecting fires and flames in real-time, leveraging advances in computer vision and machine learning. We propose a deep learning-based approach, utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze video feeds and detect fire and flame patterns. Our method combines spatial and temporal features to improve detection accuracy and reduce false alarms. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving high detection rates and low latency. The proposed system has significant implications for fire safety and prevention, enabling real-time monitoring and alert systems in various environments, including industrial, commercial, and residential settings. Key contributions of this research include the development of a real-time fire and flame detection framework, improvement of detection accuracy, and reduction of false alarms. Relevant keywords: fire detection, flame detection, real-time systems, computer vision, machine learning, CNNs, deep learning.

Objective: Material recognition from images is critical for applications in robotics, augmented reality, and visual inspection. While prior work largely treats illumination and geometry independently, real-world material appearance arises from their complex interaction. This paper investigates how object shape and lighting jointly influence material classification accuracy. Methods: We introduce a two-branch convolutional neural network that processes geometric cues and illumination patterns in parallel. The geometry branch extracts surface normals and curvature features from shape reconstructions, while the illumination branch learns lighting-invariant reflectance signatures using a photometric rendering augmentation. We train and validate our model on a new dataset of synthetic and real-world objects spanning diverse materials, shapes, and lighting conditions. Results: Our joint-branch architecture outperforms baseline models that use only color–texture or shape information by up to 15% in top-1 accuracy. Ablation studies demonstrate that combining curvature-driven geometric representations with learned illumination embeddings yields more robust material predictions under varying viewpoints and light sources. Cross-dataset evaluations further show strong generalization to unseen object classes and lighting setups. Conclusion: By explicitly modeling the interaction between geometry and illumination, our approach delivers significant improvements in material recognition performance. These findings highlight the importance of integrating shape and lighting information for reliable visual perception and pave the way for advanced material-aware systems in real-world scenarios. Keywords: material recognition, geometry, illumination, convolutional neural network, photometric augmentation, surface normals.

Movie Question Answering (MovieQA) demands a comprehensive understanding of multimodal information, including visual content, textual scripts, and metadata. Existing approaches often focus on individual modalities or simple fusion techniques, neglecting the complex inter-modal relationships. This paper introduces a Holistic Multi-modal Memory Network (HMMN) for MovieQA, designed to capture intricate interactions between video frames, subtitles, and movie plot synopses. HMMN utilizes a hierarchical attention mechanism to selectively attend to relevant information within each modality and employs a novel memory network architecture to store and reason over multi-modal contexts. Experimental results on the MovieQA benchmark demonstrate that HMMN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a relative improvement of X% in accuracy. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each component of the proposed architecture. The HMMN offers a robust framework for reasoning over diverse movie data and advances the state-of-the-art in multi-modal question answering. Keywords: Movie Question Answering, Multi-modal Learning, Memory Networks, Attention Mechanisms, Video Understanding.

Accurate 3D human pose estimation from video sequences is a challenging task with applications in areas such as motion capture, action recognition, and virtual reality. This paper introduces an enhanced approach for 3D human pose estimation from video by leveraging an attention-based neural network incorporating dilated convolutions. Our method aims to improve the accuracy and robustness of pose estimation by effectively capturing both spatial and temporal dependencies within video frames. The proposed network utilizes dilated convolutions to expand the receptive field and capture long-range contextual information, while the attention mechanism focuses on salient features relevant to pose estimation. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of pose estimation accuracy and robustness to occlusions. The proposed model's ability to capture intricate human movements from videos offers significant potential for advancements in various human-computer interaction applications. Keywords: 3D human pose estimation, video analysis, attention mechanism, dilated convolutions, neural networks.

This paper addresses the challenge of identifying significant edges in graphical models of molecular networks, a crucial task for understanding complex biological systems. Our objective is to develop a robust method for distinguishing meaningful interactions from noise in these networks. We propose a novel approach that combines advanced statistical techniques with machine learning algorithms to analyze the topology of molecular networks. Our method utilizes a unique edge scoring system, which assesses the importance of each edge based on its contribution to the overall network structure. The results show that our approach outperforms existing methods in identifying significant edges, leading to a better understanding of molecular interactions and their role in biological processes. The implications of this research are significant, as it can help uncover new insights into the mechanisms of diseases and facilitate the development of targeted therapies. Key contributions include the introduction of a new edge scoring metric and the demonstration of its effectiveness in identifying biologically relevant interactions. Relevant keywords: graphical models, molecular networks, edge detection, machine learning, systems biology.

This paper presents TDIOT, a novel approach for deep video object tracking that leverages target-driven inference to enhance tracking accuracy and efficiency. The objective is to address the challenges of object tracking in complex and dynamic environments, where existing methods often struggle with occlusions, scale variations, and appearance changes. Our approach employs a deep learning-based framework that integrates a target-driven module to focus on the object of interest, while suppressing background distractions. The method utilizes a combination of convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks to model the temporal and spatial relationships between objects. Experimental results demonstrate that TDIOT outperforms state-of-the-art tracking methods, achieving significant improvements in terms of precision, recall, and speed. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a target-driven inference mechanism, which enables more accurate and robust object tracking, and the development of a lightweight and efficient tracking architecture. The proposed approach has potential applications in various fields, including surveillance, autonomous driving, and robotics, and can be extended to other computer vision tasks, such as object detection and segmentation. Key keywords: deep learning, object tracking, target-driven inference, computer vision, video analysis.

Nghiên cứu về sự chuyển hóa sinh lí, hóa sinh thể ở tuổ i phát triển của quả chuột (Cucurbita) đang thu hút sự chú ý của các nhà khoa học. Quả chuột là một loại thực vật quan trọng, cung cấp nguồn thực phẩm giàu dinh dưỡng cho con người. Tuy nhiên, quá trình phát triển của quả chuột vẫn còn nhiều bí ẩn. Nghiên cứu gần đây đã chỉ ra rằng quá trình chuyển hóa sinh lí, hóa sinh thể ở quả chuột diễn ra theo một chu kỳ phức tạp, liên quan đến nhiều yếu tố như hormone, gen và môi trường. Quá trình này ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến kích thước, hình dạng và chất lượng của quả chuột. Các nhà khoa học đang nghiên cứu để hiểu rõ hơn về quá trình này, với mục tiêu phát triển các phương pháp mới để cải thiện sản lượng và chất lượng của quả chuột. Kết quả nghiên cứu này có thể mang lại lợi ích lớn cho ngành nông nghiệp và cung cấp nguồn thực phẩm an toàn, chất lượng cao cho con người.

Ứng dụng di động Wild Explorer được xây dựng nhằm mục đích hỗ trợ học sinh, sinh viên trong việc học tập và khám phá thế giới động vật hoang dã một cách trực quan và sinh động. Ứng dụng cung cấp một nền tảng tương tác, cho phép người dùng tiếp cận thông tin chi tiết về các loài vật thông qua nhiều hình thức khác nhau như văn bản, hình ảnh, âm thanh và video. Giao diện được thiết kế thân thiện và dễ sử dụng, phù hợp với nhiều đối tượng người dùng khác nhau, từ học sinh tiểu học đến sinh viên đại học. Nội dung được trình bày khoa học, có hệ thống, bao gồm các thông tin về đặc điểm sinh học, môi trường sống, tập tính, tình trạng bảo tồn và các mối đe dọa mà các loài vật đang phải đối mặt. Ứng dụng tích hợp các tính năng như tìm kiếm nhanh, bộ lọc thông minh, bản đồ phân bố và công cụ so sánh, giúp người dùng dễ dàng tìm kiếm và đối chiếu thông tin. Ngoài ra, ứng dụng còn khuyến khích người dùng tham gia vào các hoạt động bảo tồn thông qua các thử thách, trò chơi và các dự án cộng đồng. Wild Explorer không chỉ là một công cụ học tập mà còn là một phương tiện để nâng cao nhận thức về tầm quan trọng của việc bảo vệ đa dạng sinh học và các hệ sinh thái tự nhiên. Ứng dụng được phát triển trên nền tảng di động phổ biến, đảm bảo tính tương thích và khả năng tiếp cận rộng rãi. Dữ liệu được cập nhật thường xuyên và kiểm duyệt chặt chẽ để đảm bảo tính chính xác và tin cậy. Việc sử dụng ứng dụng trong các hoạt động giáo dục và ngoại khóa sẽ góp phần tạo ra một thế hệ trẻ có kiến thức sâu rộng về thế giới động vật và có ý thức trách nhiệm với môi trường. Ứng dụng Wild Explorer hứa hẹn sẽ là một công cụ hữu ích cho giáo viên, phụ huynh và các nhà bảo tồn trong việc truyền tải kiến thức và khơi gợi niềm đam mê khám phá thế giới tự nhiên cho học sinh, sinh viên.

Nghiên cứu này cũng cho thấy, nhóm cọp nhỏ có khả năng thích nghi với các điều kiện môi trường khác nhau, bao gồm cả điều kiện địa chất yếu. Điều này cho thấy, nhóm cọp nhỏ có khả năng thích nghi và làm việc hiệu quả trong nhiều môi trường khác nhau. Mộc hương balansa (Aristolochia balansae Franch.) thuộc phân chi Siphisia họ Mộc hương (Aristolochiaceae ) là loài đặc hữu hẹp, phân bố ở miền Bắc Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu lần đầu tiên xác định thành phần hóa học và hoạt tính kháng vi sinh vật của tinh dầu lá được thu tại huyện Bá Thước, tỉnh Thanh Hóa vào tháng 11/2021. Tinh dầu thu nhận được bằng phương pháp chưng cất lôi cuốn hơi nước sử dụng thiết bị Clevenger và phân tích bằng phương pháp sắc ký khí - khối phổ (GC-MS). Hàm lượng tinh dầu thu được ở lá là 0,15% trọng lượng tươi, tinh dầu có màu vàng nhạt, nhẹ hơn nước. Thành phần tinh dầu xác định được 63 hợp chất chiếm 78,58% tổng hàm lượng tinh dầu. Thành phần chủ yếu là các sesquitecpen và sesquitecpen chứa ôxy. Các thành phần chính gồm γ-eudesmol (6,98% tổng hàm lượng tinh dầu), α-humulene (6,22%), β-selinene (4,5%), Eudesma-4(14),7(11)-diene (3,53%), α-trans- bergamotene (3,27%), Limonene (3,02%). Kết quả thử hoạt tính kháng vi sinh vật từ tinh dầu lá có tác dụng thấp đối với các chủng vi sinh vật đối kháng ở nồng độ 10%.

Although pretrained language models can be fine-tuned to produce state-of-the-art results for a very wide range of language understanding tasks, the dynamics of this process are not well understood, especially in the low data regime. Why can we use relatively vanilla gradient descent algorithms (e.g., without strong regularization) to tune a model with hundreds of millions of parameters on datasets with only hundreds or thousands of labeled examples? In this paper, we argue that analyzing fine-tuning through the lens of intrinsic dimension provides us with empirical and theoretical intuitions to explain this remarkable phenomenon. We empirically show that common pre-trained models have a very low intrinsic dimension; in other words, there exists a low dimension reparameterization that is as effective for fine-tuning as the full parameter space. For example, by optimizing only 200 trainable parameters randomly projected back into the full space, we can tune a RoBERTa model to achieve 90\% of the full parameter performance levels on MRPC. Furthermore, we empirically show that pre-training implicitly minimizes intrinsic dimension and, perhaps surprisingly, larger models tend to have lower intrinsic dimension after a fixed number of pre-training updates, at least in part explaining their extreme effectiveness. Lastly, we connect intrinsic dimensionality with low dimensional task representations and compression based generalization bounds to provide intrinsic-dimension-based generalization bounds that are independent of the full parameter count.

Crowd counting in densely populated scenes poses significant challenges due to variations in crowd density, occlusions, and perspectives. This paper introduces HA-CCN, a novel Hierarchical Attention-based Crowd Counting Network designed to address these challenges effectively. The objective is to enhance the accuracy of crowd counting by exploiting hierarchical attention mechanisms that focus on varying levels of detail across complex scenes. The proposed model leverages an innovative architecture that combines both spatial and channel-wise attention mechanisms, facilitating the network to selectively concentrate on essential features pertinent to accurate count estimation. Comprehensive experiments were conducted on benchmark datasets to evaluate the performance of HA-CCN. The results demonstrate a marked improvement in counting accuracy compared to existing methods, achieving a substantial reduction in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Mean Squared Error (MSE) across diverse scenes. The system's ability to adaptively adjust to different crowd densities and occlusions is a significant advancement, emphasizing its robustness and scalability. The implications of this research extend to real-world applications such as public safety monitoring, event management, and traffic analysis. The HA-CCN sets a new paradigm in crowd counting by integrating hierarchical attention at various levels, offering a significant contribution to the field and paving the way for future developments in intelligent crowd analysis systems. Keywords include crowd counting, hierarchical attention, MAE, MSE, and deep learning.

In this paper, we adopt 3D Convolutional Neural Networks to segment volumetric medical images. Although deep neural networks have been proven to be very effective on many 2D vision tasks, it is still challenging to apply them to 3D tasks due to the limited amount of annotated 3D data and limited computational resources. We propose a novel 3D-based coarse-to-fine framework to effectively and efficiently tackle these challenges. The proposed 3D-based framework outperforms the 2D counterpart to a large margin since it can leverage the rich spatial infor- mation along all three axes. We conduct experiments on two datasets which include healthy and pathological pancreases respectively, and achieve the current state-of-the-art in terms of Dice-Srensen Coefficient (DSC). On the NIH pancreas segmentation dataset, we outperform the previous best by an average of over 2%, and the worst case is improved by 7% to reach almost 70%, which indicates the reliability of our framework in clinical applications.

The accuracy and reliability of breast ultrasound diagnosis are critical for effective patient management. Traditional AI models often face limitations in sensitivity and specificity when used independently. This research aims to enhance diagnostic precision by integrating multiple AI techniques, thereby providing a more reliable AI solution for breast ultrasound diagnosis. Methods/Approach: We developed a novel multi-AI combination framework that synergizes various AI algorithms, including deep learning networks, ensemble methods, and heuristic approaches. By leveraging the unique strengths of each model, our methodology enhances feature extraction, classification accuracy, and robustness. The framework was evaluated using a comprehensive dataset of breast ultrasound images, ensuring diverse and representative sample coverage for model training and validation. Results/Findings: The proposed multi-AI combination demonstrated significant improvements in diagnostic accuracy, achieving a sensitivity of 95% and a specificity of 92%, outperforming individual AI models and conventional diagnostic techniques. Comparative analyses indicate that the ensemble approach not only enhances performance metrics but also reduces false negatives and false positives, contributing to more reliable clinical decision-making. Conclusion/Implications: This study showcases the potential of integrating multiple AI methodologies to advance the reliability of breast ultrasound diagnosis. The improved accuracy and robustness of our solution underscore its potential applicability in clinical settings, offering clinicians a powerful tool for early and accurate breast cancer detection. This work highlights the importance of collaborative AI systems in medical diagnostics and provides a roadmap for future research in multi-AI solutions. Keywords: Breast Ultrasound, Multi-AI Combination, Diagnostic Accuracy, Ensemble Methods, Deep Learning, Medical Diagnostics.

This paper introduces a novel context-aware semantic inpainting approach for completing missing or corrupted regions in images. The objective is to generate realistic and semantically plausible image completions by leveraging contextual information from both local and global image regions. Our method employs a deep generative model conditioned on surrounding image features, combined with a novel attention mechanism that focuses on semantically relevant regions for coherent inpainting. We propose a two-stage training process: first, the model learns to generate plausible structures, and second, it refines the texture details guided by contextual cues. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of visual quality, semantic consistency, and quantitative metrics like Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM). The generated inpaintings exhibit sharper details and better alignment with the surrounding context. The proposed method offers significant improvements in image restoration, object removal, and content creation applications. Keywords: Image Inpainting, Semantic Completion, Context-Aware, Deep Learning, Generative Models, Attention Mechanism.

Nâng cao năng lực quản lý dự án là một yếu tố quan trọng trong việc đảm bảo hiệu quả và thành công của các công trình đầu tư xây dựng trong lĩnh vực nông nghiệp. Để đạt được điều này, các ban quản lý dự án cần tập trung vào việc cải thiện quy trình lập kế hoạch, triển khai và giám sát dự án. Việc áp dụng các công nghệ mới, đào tạo nhân lực chuyên môn và tăng cường sự phối hợp giữa các bên liên quan sẽ giúp nâng cao chất lượng và tiến độ thực hiện dự án. Đồng thời, việc đánh giá và quản lý rủi ro cũng cần được chú trọng để giảm thiểu các vấn đề phát sinh trong quá trình thực hiện. Qua đó, không chỉ nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng nguồn lực mà còn góp phần phát triển bền vững cho ngành nông nghiệp.

Nghiên cứu thực trạng phát sinh và thu gom chất thải từ vỏ lon nhôm ở các hộ gia đình tại quận Bắc Từ Liêm, Hà Nội cho thấy số lượng vỏ lon nhôm thải ra hàng ngày rất lớn. Theo thống kê, mỗi hộ gia đình trung bình thải ra khoảng 2-3 vỏ lon nhôm mỗi ngày. Tổng số lượng vỏ lon nhôm thải ra hàng ngày tại quận Bắc Từ Liêm ước tính lên đến hàng nghìn tấn. Chất thải vỏ lon nhôm không được thu gom và xử lý đúng cách đã gây ra nhiều vấn đề môi trường. Vỏ lon nhôm không được tái chế sẽ gây ô nhiễm đất, nước và không khí. Ngoài ra, vỏ lon nhôm cũng có thể gây ra cháy nổ và cháy rừng nếu không được xử lý đúng cách. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, các hộ gia đình cần phải thay đổi thói quen sử dụng và thải bỏ vỏ lon nhôm. Các cơ quan chức năng cần phải tăng cường công tác thu gom và xử lý chất thải vỏ lon nhôm. Đồng thời, cần phải triển khai các chương trình tái chế vỏ lon nhôm để giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực đến môi trường.

Giải pháp phát triển tiêu thụ rau thông qua hệ thống chợ và siêu thị tại thành phố Hà Nội đang trở thành một vấn đề cấp thiết trong bối cảnh nhu cầu tiêu dùng ngày càng tăng cao. Việc xây dựng và cải thiện hệ thống phân phối rau quả không chỉ giúp nâng cao chất lượng sản phẩm mà còn đảm bảo an toàn vệ sinh thực phẩm cho người tiêu dùng. Các chợ truyền thống và siêu thị cần được kết nối chặt chẽ hơn để tạo ra một mạng lưới tiêu thụ hiệu quả, từ đó giảm thiểu tình trạng thất thoát sản phẩm và tăng cường khả năng tiếp cận của người dân với các loại rau sạch. Đồng thời, việc áp dụng công nghệ thông tin trong quản lý và kinh doanh cũng sẽ góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động của các điểm bán hàng. Các chính sách hỗ trợ từ chính quyền địa phương cũng cần được triển khai để khuyến khích nông dân sản xuất rau an toàn, từ đó tạo ra nguồn cung ổn định cho thị trường.

This paper presents a novel approach to human pose estimation by jointly training a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a graphical model. The objective is to accurately localize body joints in images and videos, addressing the challenges of occlusion, variability, and complexity in human poses. Our method combines the strengths of CNNs in feature extraction and graphical models in structural representation, enabling the capture of both appearance and spatial relationships between body parts. The joint training framework allows for the optimization of both components simultaneously, leading to improved performance and robustness. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in benchmark datasets. The key contributions of this work include the development of a unified framework for pose estimation, the introduction of a novel loss function that balances appearance and structural cues, and the achievement of superior accuracy and efficiency. This research has significant implications for applications in computer vision, human-computer interaction, and robotics, with potential extensions to related tasks such as action recognition and tracking. Key keywords: human pose estimation, convolutional neural networks, graphical models, joint training, computer vision.

This paper introduces a novel approach termed Auxiliary Augmentation with GNT-Xent Loss (AAG) for self-supervised representation learning, addressing the challenge of feature extraction without labelled data. The primary goal is to enhance the quality of learned representations in neural networks by leveraging auxiliary data augmentation techniques. Methods/Approach: We propose the AAG framework, which integrates auxiliary augmentation methods with a new contrastive loss function known as GNT-Xent Loss. The framework utilizes self-supervised learning paradigms to enable models to learn robust features that are both discriminative and generalizable. The GNT-Xent Loss builds upon traditional contrastive loss by incorporating gradient normalization techniques, which aid in stabilizing training and improving convergence. Results/Findings: Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance compared to existing self-supervised learning methods. The integration of auxiliary augmentations with the GNT-Xent Loss significantly enhances the model's ability to capture intricate patterns in data, resulting in better classification and representation quality. Quantitative assessments show improved metrics in terms of accuracy and representation similarity across diverse tasks. Conclusion/Implications: The AAG framework and the introduction of the GNT-Xent Loss contribute to the domain of self-supervised learning by offering a more effective and computationally efficient approach to representation learning. This research paves the way for developing more sophisticated methods that can operate without reliance on large volumes of labeled data, with potential applications in areas such as image retrieval, natural language processing, and video analysis. Keywords: self-supervised learning, representation learning, auxiliary augmentation, GNT-Xent Loss, contrastive learning, feature extraction, neural networks.

Hàm ngẫu nhiên B-spline (RBSF) nổi lên như một phương pháp hiệu quả trong dự báo chuỗi thời gian nhờ khả năng mô hình hóa dữ liệu phi tuyến và không dừng. RBSF kết hợp tính linh hoạt của B-spline với khả năng thích ứng của mô hình ngẫu nhiên, cho phép nắm bắt các đặc điểm phức tạp của chuỗi thời gian. Ưu điểm của RBSF bao gồm khả năng xử lý dữ liệu nhiễu, dự báo chính xác trong môi trường biến động và dễ dàng tích hợp với các phương pháp dự báo khác. Ứng dụng của RBSF trải rộng trên nhiều lĩnh vực, từ dự báo tài chính, năng lượng đến dự báo lưu lượng giao thông và nhu cầu tiêu dùng. Các nghiên cứu thực nghiệm cho thấy RBSF có khả năng cạnh tranh, thậm chí vượt trội so với các mô hình truyền thống như ARIMA và mạng nơ-ron trong một số trường hợp nhất định. Việc lựa chọn tham số phù hợp và kết hợp RBSF với các kỹ thuật tối ưu hóa có thể nâng cao hơn nữa hiệu suất dự báo, mở ra tiềm năng ứng dụng rộng rãi trong thực tế.

The paper addresses the critical challenge of unsupervised anomaly detection and localization in medical imaging, which is essential for early diagnosis and treatment planning. Existing methods often struggle with generalization and precision, necessitating innovative approaches to improve detection accuracy and efficiency. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel Constrained Contrastive Distribution Learning framework that leverages contrastive learning principles to effectively distinguish normal from anomalous regions in medical images without supervision. Our approach imposes distribution constraints to refine feature representations, enhancing the ability to capture subtle anomalies across diverse medical image datasets. Results/Findings: The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in unsupervised anomaly detection and localization tasks across multiple medical imaging modalities. Quantitative evaluations show substantial improvements in detection accuracy and localization precision compared to baseline methods. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results, significantly enhancing the robustness of anomaly identification in complex clinical settings. Conclusion/Implications: This research introduces a groundbreaking method for unsupervised anomaly detection and localization in medical images, offering a promising solution by improving generalization and accuracy. The contributions provide valuable insights into utilizing contrastive learning with distribution constraints, with potential applications in various medical diagnostic tools and systems. Our method can facilitate earlier and more reliable detection of pathological changes, ultimately supporting better patient outcomes. Keywords: anomaly detection, unsupervised learning, contrastive learning, medical imaging, localization, distribution constraints, feature representation.

Object detection from images captured by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is becoming increasingly useful. Despite the great success of the generic object detection methods trained on ground-to-ground images, a huge performance drop is observed when they are directly applied to images captured by UAVs. The unsatisfactory performance is owing to many UAV-specific nuisances, such as varying flying altitudes, adverse weather conditions, dynamically changing viewing angles, etc. Those nuisances constitute a large number of fine-grained domains, across which the detection model has to stay robust. Fortunately, UAVs will record meta-data that depict those varying attributes, which are either freely available along with the UAV images, or can be easily obtained. We propose to utilize those free meta-data in conjunction with associated UAV images to learn domain-robust features via an adversarial training framework dubbed Nuisance Disentangled Feature Transform (NDFT), for the specific challenging problem of object detection in UAV images, achieving a substantial gain in robustness to those nuisances. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm, by showing state-of-the-art performance (single model) on two existing UAV-based object detection benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/UAV-NDFT.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving image-text matching by proposing a novel framework that leverages recurrent visual embedding to express visual objects in images analogously to how words are represented in textual data. The proposed method decomposes images into constituent visual objects, which are then sequentially embedded using a recurrent neural network (RNN)-based architecture. This sequential embedding captures relationships and contextual dependencies among objects, enabling the generation of a visual representation that closely parallels the structure and semantics of natural language sentences. Experimental evaluations were conducted on benchmark datasets for image-text retrieval, demonstrating that our approach achieves superior performance compared to existing image-text matching models, particularly in accurately capturing fine-grained relationships between image regions and descriptive text. The results indicate that treating objects in images as sequential visual tokens contributes to more robust cross-modal alignment. This research introduces a unified perspective for multimodal representation learning and offers significant advancements for applications such as visual question answering, image captioning, and cross-modal retrieval. Key keywords include image-text matching, recurrent visual embedding, object representation, cross-modal retrieval, and multimodal learning.
