Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy, việc kiểm soát các yếu tố như cường độ sóng, hướng dòng chảy và vật liệu bồi lắp đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc ổn định bãi biển. Những phát hiện này không chỉ có ý nghĩa khoa học mà còn góp phần hỗ trợ công tác quản lý và bảo vệ môi trường ven biển.
Định hướng phát triển trong tương lai của hệ thống sẽ tập trung vào mục tiêu cải thiện và mở rộng chức năng điểm đáp ứng nhu cầu ngày càng cao của người dùng.

Neural network pruning aims to reduce the size and complexity of deep learning models while maintaining performance. Despite advancements in pruning techniques, discovering strategies that effectively preserve model accuracy remains challenging. This paper investigates the role of dynamical isometry in neural network pruning, proposing it as a crucial missing component that enhances model robustness and performance post-pruning. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel pruning framework that integrates dynamical isometry—a property ensuring that signal propagation through layers remains consistent during training. Our approach is compared against traditional pruning algorithms by implementing it in various architectures, including convolutional and feedforward neural networks. The models are analyzed using both direct-signal processing metrics and accuracy benchmarks to assess the effectiveness of our method. Results/Findings: The integration of dynamical isometry into the pruning process demonstrates a significant retention of model accuracy, with improvements up to 10% in some cases compared to standard pruning techniques. Evaluations across multiple datasets, including image classification and NLP tasks, reveal that networks pruned with our method achieve superior performance metrics with reduced degeneracy and better generalization. Conclusion/Implications: This study underscores the importance of dynamical isometry in the pruning landscape, highlighting its potential to revolutionize how neural networks are optimized and deployed effectively in resource-constrained environments. Our findings offer novel insights into designing pruning strategies that could lead to more efficient deployment of AI technologies in real-world applications, where computational resources are limited. Future research could explore the scaling of this method to emerging neural architectures and its implications in fields such as autonomous systems and edge computing. Keywords: Dynamical Isometry, Neural Network Pruning, Deep Learning, Model Optimization, Signal Propagation, AI Efficiency, Computational Resources.

Sinh trưởng và năng suất chất xanh của cây cao lương phụ thuộc vào nhiều yếu tố, trong đó lượng đạm bón đóng vai trò quan trọng. Các nghiên cứu đã chỉ ra rằng lượng đạm bón phù hợp có thể tăng sinh trưởng và năng suất chất xanh của cây cao lương. Tuy nhiên, nếu lượng đạm bón quá cao có thể dẫn đến tình trạng dư thừa đạm, gây ra các vấn đề như giảm chất lượng cây, tăng nguy cơ bị bệnh và ảnh hưởng đến môi trường. Ngược lại, nếu lượng đạm bón quá thấp có thể dẫn đến tình trạng thiếu đạm, ảnh hưởng đến sinh trưởng và năng suất của cây. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng chất lượng của cây cao lương cũng bị ảnh hưởng bởi lượng đạm bón. Các cây cao lương được bón đạm phù hợp thường có chất lượng tốt hơn, với các đặc tính như màu sắc tươi sáng, hương vị ngon và độ ẩm cao. Tóm lại, lượng đạm bón phù hợp là chìa khóa để tăng sinh trưởng và năng suất chất xanh của cây cao lương, đồng thời đảm bảo chất lượng của cây.

Đầu tiên, quy trình lập kế hoạch và quản lý dự án có vai trò quyết định, ảnh hưởng đến khả năng phân bổ nguồn lực và thời gian thực hiện. The proliferation of deep learning has reignited interest in the fundamental question of how data quantity and quality influence the performance of neural models. This paper aims to revisit the concept of the "unreasonable effectiveness of data" within the context of modern deep learning architectures. We systematically investigate the impact of dataset scale, diversity, and noise on model performance across various tasks, including image classification and natural language processing. By conducting extensive experiments with different state-of-the-art neural network architectures and data augmentation techniques, we measure how incremental data increases affect convergence, generalization, and robustness. Our findings reveal that, while model gains scale substantially with larger datasets, the marginal benefits diminish past a critical threshold, and data quality begins to play a more decisive role. Furthermore, we highlight the interplay between model capacity and data volume, illustrating scenarios where larger models can exploit abundant data more effectively. The study also explores strategies for optimal data curation and efficient utilization, providing insights for practitioners who seek to maximize model performance under real-world data constraints. Our analysis reaffirms the pivotal role of data in deep learning, clarifies its limitations, and offers practical guidelines for dataset construction and resource allocation. Key keywords: deep learning, dataset scaling, neural networks, model generalization, data quality, data augmentation.

Partial discharge (PD) detection in insulated overhead conductors is critical for maintaining grid reliability and preventing failures. This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework utilizing frequency and phase attention mechanisms to enhance the accuracy of PD detection from noisy field data. Our approach employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features from time-frequency representations of PD signals, followed by frequency and phase attention modules that selectively emphasize informative components. This allows the model to effectively filter out noise and focus on subtle PD signatures. We evaluate our framework on a real-world dataset of PD signals collected from overhead conductors, demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional CNN-based methods and other state-of-the-art techniques. Specifically, our method achieves a significant improvement in F1-score, indicating a better balance between precision and recall. The proposed framework offers a robust and accurate solution for automated PD detection, enabling proactive maintenance and reducing the risk of conductor failures. Keywords: Partial Discharge Detection, Deep Learning, Attention Mechanism, Convolutional Neural Network, Overhead Conductors, Time-Frequency Analysis.

This paper introduces NukeBERT, a pre-trained language model tailored for the low-resource nuclear domain. The objective is to address the scarcity of domain-specific language models in the nuclear field, which hinders efficient information retrieval, text analysis, and knowledge discovery. To achieve this, we employ a transformer-based architecture and fine-tune it on a curated dataset of nuclear-related texts. Our approach leverages a combination of masked language modeling and next sentence prediction to learn domain-specific representations. The results show that NukeBERT outperforms general-purpose language models on nuclear domain-specific tasks, such as text classification and named entity recognition. The model demonstrates improved performance on low-resource scenarios, making it a valuable resource for the nuclear community. The introduction of NukeBERT contributes to the advancement of natural language processing in the nuclear domain, enabling more accurate and efficient analysis of nuclear-related texts. This work contributes to the growing field of explainable AI by offering a robust framework for understanding feature importance in 3D point cloud data. **Keywords**: 3D point clouds, explainable AI, gradient-based methods, feature interpretation, deep learning, saliency maps.

This paper investigates the vulnerability of skeleton-based human action recognition systems to adversarial attacks. With the increasing use of these systems across various applications such as security surveillance and human-computer interaction, understanding their robustness against potential adversarial threats is crucial. Methods/Approach: We design a novel adversarial attack framework specifically targeting skeletal representation data used in action recognition algorithms. The proposed framework generates adversarial perturbations to manipulate the skeletal data, thereby deceiving the recognition model into making incorrect classifications. Our method leverages a gradient-based approach to optimize the perturbations while maintaining the natural appearance of the human movement. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed adversarial attack significantly degrades the performance of several state-of-the-art skeleton-based action recognition models. Our attacks achieve high success rates with minimal perturbations, revealing a substantial vulnerability in current recognition systems. Comparisons with existing attack methods show our approach to be more effective in both attack success rate and robustness. Conclusion/Implications: The findings highlight a critical security concern within the domain of human action recognition, emphasizing the need for more resilient recognition models. This research contributes to the field by identifying weaknesses and prompting the development of more robust defenses against adversarial attacks. Future work should focus on designing countermeasures and enhancing the inherent robustness of skeleton-based recognition systems. Key keywords include adversarial attack, skeleton-based recognition, human action, vulnerability, and security.

The objective of this paper is to investigate the vulnerability of deep networks to membership model inversion attacks, a significant privacy concern in machine learning. We propose a novel approach for conducting these attacks by leveraging adversarial techniques to infer sensitive information about the training data of deep learning models. Our method involves crafting inversion queries that exploit the latent space of a given model, enabling the extraction of approximations of original data points from the model's output. Through a rigorous evaluation using multiple benchmark datasets and various deep network architectures, our experiments demonstrate that the proposed attack outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and granularity of the data recovery. Results reveal that even models with robust privacy defenses are susceptible to such inversion attacks, highlighting an overlooked weakness in model security paradigms. The implications of this research extend to the development of more resilient deep learning frameworks and the adaptation of regulatory measures for data privacy. Our findings underscore the critical need for the AI community to reassess current privacy protection strategies and pave the way for more robust security solutions in artificial intelligence. Key keywords include: deep networks, model inversion, privacy attack, adversarial techniques, and latent space exploration.

GATR (Globally-scalable Automated Target Recognition) is a Lockheed Martin software system for real-time object detection and classification in satellite imagery on a worldwide basis. GATR uses GPU-accelerated deep learning software to quickly search large geographic regions. On a single GPU it processes imagery at a rate of over 16 square km/sec (or more than 10 Mpixels/sec), and it requires only two hours to search the entire state of Pennsylvania for gas fracking wells. The search time scales linearly with the geographic area, and the processing rate scales linearly with the number of GPUs. GATR has a modular, cloud-based architecture that uses the Maxar GBDX platform and provides an ATR analytic as a service. Applications include broad area search, watch boxes for monitoring ports and airfields, and site characterization. ATR is performed by deep learning models including RetinaNet and Faster R-CNN. Results are presented for the detection of aircraft and fracking wells and show that the recalls exceed 90% even in geographic regions never seen before. GATR is extensible to new targets, such as cars and ships, and it also handles radar and infrared imagery.

Trong vô tinh không bế tắc (NOA: nonobstructive azoospermia), thường khó lấy được tinh trùng do có rất ít hoặc không có tinh trùng trưởng thành và sinh tinh thường khu trú, rải rác trong tinh hoàn. Phân tích Cochrane y văn không tìm thấy các thử nghiệm ngẫu nhiên đối chứng, làm cơ sở khoa học cho khuyến cáo kỹ thuật này so với kỹ thuật khác vì mỗi kỹ thuật có ưu và khuyết điểm riêng. This paper presents a novel few-shot learning approach for recognizing historical ciphered manuscripts, addressing the challenge of limited labeled data in this domain. Our objective is to develop a system that can accurately identify and decipher encrypted texts from historical manuscripts with minimal training examples. We propose a hybrid model that combines the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures to learn robust features from limited data. Our approach leverages self-supervised learning and meta-learning techniques to adapt to new, unseen ciphered manuscripts. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, achieving significant improvements in recognition accuracy compared to traditional machine learning approaches. The key findings of this study highlight the potential of few-shot learning for historical manuscript recognition, enabling the efficient deciphering of previously unknown or untranscribed texts. This research contributes to the development of AI-powered tools for historical document analysis, with potential applications in paleography, cryptography, and cultural heritage preservation. Key keywords: few-shot learning, historical ciphered manuscripts, convolutional neural networks, transformer architectures, self-supervised learning, meta-learning.

Continual Relation Extraction (CRE) aims to continuously train a model to learn new relations while preserving its ability on old learned relations. To handle classificationtasks, CRE models often include a softmax classifier that is trained using Cross Entropy (CE) loss. The Nearest Class Mean (NCM) classifier, however, has recently been favored over the traditional Softmax classifier with Cross-Entropy loss in Continual Learning (CL) studies because of its higher performance. One flaw in their research is that they failed to provide an explanation for why the NCM classifier performs better than the Softmax classifier when CE Loss is present. In contrast to those works, I investigate how CE loss degrades performance by impairing the transferability of the learned features. In detail, I revisit CE loss by plugging CE loss into the state-of-the-art framework CRL and note that CRL does not use CE loss. I then give a concrete investigation of the impact of CE loss on the CRE problem through experiments using spectral analysis. In light of this analysis, I propose a simple yet effective class-wise regularization that improves the transferability of the representations. With my regularization, we can take advantage of both mechanisms Supervised Contrastive Learning (SCL) from CRL and Softmax classifier. I observe that my proposed regularization boosts the transferability of the representations and outperforms state-of-the-art CRE methods by a significant margin on the FewRel and TACRED datasets.

This paper introduces a novel method for generating saliency maps in Atari agents by leveraging attention mechanisms, effectively providing "free-lunch" saliency without requiring additional computational overhead or modifications to the agent's architecture. We extract attention weights from existing attention modules within deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents, repurposing them as visual explanations of the agent's decision-making process. Our approach demonstrates that these attention-based saliency maps can effectively highlight relevant game elements contributing to the agent's actions. We evaluate our method on a diverse set of Atari games, demonstrating its ability to identify key objects and regions crucial for successful gameplay. Furthermore, we compare the quality of our attention-based saliency maps with gradient-based saliency methods, revealing comparable or superior performance in terms of localization and relevance. The proposed technique offers a computationally efficient and easily implementable approach for interpreting and understanding the behavior of DRL agents in complex environments, facilitating improved debugging, and potential insights for curriculum learning strategies. Keywords: Saliency, Attention, Atari, Reinforcement Learning, Explainable AI, Deep Learning.

This paper introduces *MeanShift++*, a highly efficient and scalable algorithm for mode-seeking, designed to address the computational bottlenecks of traditional MeanShift methods. The objective of this work is to enable real-time applications in segmentation and object tracking, where speed and accuracy are critical. *MeanShift++* leverages a novel optimization framework that combines spatial hashing and adaptive bandwidth selection to significantly reduce computational complexity while maintaining high precision. The proposed approach is evaluated on benchmark datasets for image segmentation and object tracking tasks, demonstrating a 5x speedup over state-of-the-art methods without compromising accuracy. Experimental results show that *MeanShift++* achieves superior performance in both dense and sparse data environments, making it suitable for real-world applications such as autonomous driving and video surveillance. The key contribution of this research lies in its ability to deliver extremely fast mode-seeking with minimal memory overhead, paving the way for its integration into resource-constrained systems. This work has broad implications for advancing real-time computer vision applications, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid and reliable object localization and segmentation. **Keywords**: MeanShift, mode-seeking, image segmentation, object tracking, spatial hashing, adaptive bandwidth, real-time processing.

Data augmentation is a crucial technique for improving the generalization ability of deep learning models in image classification. This paper introduces Attentive CutMix, an enhanced data augmentation method that builds upon CutMix by incorporating an attention mechanism. The objective is to create more semantically meaningful composite images, guiding the model to focus on informative regions during training. Our approach utilizes a spatial attention module to identify salient areas within images before applying the CutMix operation. This ensures that important features are retained in the mixed samples, preventing the introduction of irrelevant or noisy patches. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, demonstrate that Attentive CutMix consistently outperforms standard CutMix and other state-of-the-art data augmentation techniques. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the attention module in generating more effective training samples. The findings suggest that Attentive CutMix improves model robustness and accuracy by promoting attention to relevant image regions. Keywords: Data augmentation, CutMix, attention mechanism, image classification, deep learning, convolutional neural networks.

The increasing complexity of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) presents challenges in selecting optimal architectures for specific tasks, hindering broader adoption and efficient deployment. This research addresses the need for a simplified and efficient architecture search for GNNs to enhance their usability and performance across varied applications. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel, streamlined architecture search framework that reduces the computational burden associated with traditional search methods. By integrating a heuristic-based algorithm alongside a knowledge-driven selection process, our approach eliminates redundant configurations and prioritizes the most promising architecture candidates. Results/Findings: The proposed method significantly accelerates the architecture search process without compromising the performance of the resulting GNNs. Benchmark comparisons demonstrate that our framework achieves superior accuracy and efficiency over existing search techniques, presenting up to a 30% reduction in computational time and a 15% improvement in model performance across standard graph datasets. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of a simplified architecture search mechanism for GNNs marks a substantial advancement in the field, offering a practical tool for deploying high-performing neural networks in various graph-based applications. This research contributes to democratizing access to GNNs by facilitating easier optimization and deployment, paving the way for new applications and widespread use of graph-based models in real-world scenarios. Keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Architecture Search, Heuristic Algorithm, Model Optimization, Computational Efficiency.

This paper investigates the capabilities and limitations of reinforcement learning (RL) benchmarks by employing random weight guessing as a baseline comparative technique. The objective is to assess how well current RL environments distinguish between learned agent behavior and the outcomes generated by agents with untrained, randomly initialized neural network policies. Our methodology involves systematically applying random policy networks across a variety of standard RL benchmarks, such as those in the Atari and OpenAI Gym suites, and rigorously evaluating their performance metrics. The results reveal intriguing insights: in several environments, randomly weighted agents achieve non-trivial scores, occasionally outperforming poorly tuned or naive RL agents. This finding highlights potential gaps in benchmark design and underscores the need for more discriminative evaluation protocols. Our analysis provides a comprehensive characterization of benchmark sensitivity to agent optimization, raising important questions about what constitutes meaningful RL progress. We conclude by proposing recommendations for future benchmark development and evaluation methodologies. Keywords: reinforcement learning, benchmarks, random weight guessing, policy evaluation, neural networks, agent performance.

Objective: Modern deep neural networks often exhibit miscalibration, producing overconfident or underconfident probability estimates that can undermine reliability in safety‐critical and decision-support applications. This paper revisits the calibration properties of state-of-the-art architectures across vision and language tasks, aiming to (1) quantify miscalibration trends as models scale in depth and data size, and (2) evaluate the effectiveness of existing and novel calibration techniques. Methods: We conduct a systematic empirical study on convolutional (ResNet, DenseNet) and transformer-based (Vision Transformer, BERT) models using benchmark datasets (CIFAR-100, ImageNet, GLUE). Calibration is measured via Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and reliability diagrams. We compare standard post-hoc methods (temperature scaling, isotonic regression) against two new approaches: adaptive temperature scaling that conditions on feature-space activations, and mixup-based calibration regularization during training. Results: Our experiments reveal that calibration often degrades as model capacity increases, despite improved accuracy. Standard temperature scaling reduces ECE by up to 50%, but struggles on highly overparameterized transformers. The proposed adaptive scaling further cuts ECE by 20%–30% relative to vanilla temperature methods. Mixup regularization yields consistent calibration gains (up to 35% ECE reduction) without sacrificing accuracy. Combining both techniques achieves the lowest miscalibration across all tested models. Conclusion: Revisiting calibration in modern networks uncovers systematic overconfidence trends and demonstrates that tailored post-hoc and training-time interventions can substantially improve predictive reliability. These findings inform best practices for deploying deep models in applications demanding trustworthy uncertainty estimates. Keywords: neural network calibration, model uncertainty, temperature scaling, mixup regularization, deep learning reliability.

The problem of minimization of the number of measurements needed for digital image acquisition and reconstruction with a given accuracy is addressed. Basics of the sampling theory are outlined to show that the lower bound of signal sampling rate sufficient for signal reconstruction with a given accuracy is equal to the spectrum sparsity of the signal sparse approximation that has this accuracy. It is revealed that the compressed sensing approach, which was advanced as a solution to the sampling rate minimization problem, is far from reaching the sampling rate theoretical minimum. Potentials and limitations of compressed sensing are demystified using a simple and intutive model, A method of image Arbitrary Sampling and Bounded Spectrum Reconstruction (ASBSR-method) is described that allows to draw near the image sampling rate theoretical minimum. Presented and discussed are also results of experimental verification of the ASBSR-method and its possible applicability extensions to solving various underdetermined inverse problems such as color image demosaicing, image in-painting, image reconstruction from their sparsely sampled or decimated projections, image reconstruction from the modulus of its Fourier spectrum, and image reconstruction from its sparse samples in Fourier domain

This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently adapting machine learning models to new tasks with limited data, a critical requirement in many real-world applications. We propose a novel Bayesian Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (BMAML) framework that integrates Bayesian inference with meta-learning to enhance generalization and uncertainty quantification. Unlike traditional meta-learning approaches, BMAML leverages probabilistic modeling to provide robust predictions and reliable uncertainty estimates, even in low-data regimes. Our method employs a gradient-based meta-learning algorithm combined with a variational inference technique to approximate the posterior distribution over model parameters. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that BMAML outperforms existing meta-learning methods in terms of task adaptation speed, prediction accuracy, and uncertainty calibration. The framework also exhibits improved robustness to noisy and sparse data, making it suitable for applications such as few-shot learning, robotics, and personalized recommendation systems. This work contributes a scalable and interpretable meta-learning approach that bridges the gap between Bayesian methods and meta-learning, offering significant potential for advancing adaptive AI systems. **Keywords**: Bayesian inference, meta-learning, few-shot learning, uncertainty quantification, variational inference, adaptive AI.

**Abstract** Optimizing compiler performance is a critical aspect of software development, yet traditional heuristic-based approaches often struggle to adapt to diverse programs and hardware architectures. This paper presents a novel framework for static neural compiler optimization leveraging deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Our approach models the optimization selection process as a sequential decision-making problem, where a neural agent learns to map program features to optimal transformation sequences without requiring runtime feedback. We employ a deep neural network as the policy function, trained using simulated execution rewards derived from static code analysis and profiling data. Experimental evaluations on standard compiler benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms classical static optimization heuristics and several recent learning-based baselines in terms of execution speed and code size reduction. Notably, the DRL-based optimizer exhibits strong generalization to previously unseen program types and architectures. These findings indicate that deep reinforcement learning offers a powerful, adaptable tool for static compiler optimization, with significant implications for automating software performance tuning and enhancing cross-platform development. Keywords: compiler optimization, deep reinforcement learning, neural networks, static analysis, program optimization, automated code tuning.

Our results demonstrate that this method effectively identifies patients at high risk of acquiring AMR, achieving a significant improvement in classification accuracy compared to traditional methods. The proposed approach offers a promising tool for proactive AMR surveillance, enabling timely interventions and improved antimicrobial stewardship in ICUs. Gesture recognition is a crucial component in human-computer interaction, enabling intuitive control and communication. This paper introduces a novel path searching method within a weighted graph framework to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of gesture recognition, particularly focusing on identifying important, high-impact actions. Our approach represents gesture sequences as paths in a graph, where nodes correspond to gesture components and edge weights reflect the likelihood of transitions between them. We then employ a modified shortest path algorithm to identify the most probable gesture sequence, emphasizing paths associated with predefined “important actions” by assigning higher weights to their constituent nodes and edges. The system was evaluated on a custom dataset of dynamic hand gestures, demonstrating a significant improvement in recognition accuracy compared to traditional Hidden Markov Model (HMM) and Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) based approaches, especially for complex, multi-step gestures. The results highlight the potential of weighted graph-based path searching for robust and efficient gesture recognition, paving the way for more natural and responsive human-computer interfaces. Keywords: Gesture Recognition, Weighted Graph, Path Searching, Human-Computer Interaction, Dynamic Hand Gestures, Action Recognition.

This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling Bahdanau Attention by leveraging election methods enhanced with Q-Learning. The primary objective is to improve the interpretability and efficiency of attention mechanisms in sequence-to-sequence tasks, such as machine translation and text summarization. Traditional attention mechanisms often face challenges in dynamically allocating focus across input sequences, leading to suboptimal performance in complex tasks. To address this, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates election-based voting systems with Q-Learning, enabling the model to learn optimal attention distributions through reinforcement learning. The election methods provide a structured mechanism for aggregating contextual information, while Q-Learning ensures adaptability and fine-tuning of attention weights. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms conventional Bahdanau Attention in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed model achieves a 12% improvement in BLEU scores for machine translation tasks and reduces training time by 18% compared to baseline methods. This research contributes to the advancement of attention mechanisms by introducing a scalable and interpretable framework, with potential applications in natural language processing, recommendation systems, and other domains requiring dynamic sequence modeling. **Keywords**: Bahdanau Attention, Election Methods, Q-Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Sequence-to-Sequence Models, Natural Language Processing.

Dynamic graphs, representing entities and their relationships over time, are prevalent in various domains. While existing graph representation learning methods capture structural or attribute dynamics separately, they often overlook the intricate co-evolution between the graph structure and node attributes. This paper introduces a novel framework, Attribute-Structure Co-Evolutions Learning (ASCL), designed to simultaneously model the temporal dependencies of both graph structure and node attributes. ASCL leverages a coupled recurrent architecture to capture the mutual influence between evolving graph topology and attribute changes. Specifically, we employ separate recurrent units to model structural evolution and attribute dynamics, with cross-feeding mechanisms to facilitate information exchange. We further introduce an attention mechanism to selectively aggregate neighborhood information, adapting to varying node importance over time. Extensive experiments on several real-world dynamic graph datasets demonstrate that ASCL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in node classification and link prediction tasks. The results highlight the importance of modeling attribute-structure co-evolutions for effective dynamic graph representation learning. Keywords: Dynamic Graphs, Graph Neural Networks, Representation Learning, Temporal Networks, Attribute Learning, Co-evolution.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurately detecting text within complex scenes, a crucial task in various applications such as autonomous driving and digital content processing. The research focuses on enhancing scene text detection by employing predictive ensemble learning, a strategy that integrates multiple machine learning models to improve performance and reliability. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel ensemble learning framework that combines the strengths of diverse predictive models. The approach leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and integrates multiple classifiers to predict text presence with higher precision. Advanced techniques for model selection and parameter tuning are utilized to optimize the ensemble configuration. Additionally, the framework incorporates a dynamic weighting mechanism, allowing it to adaptively prioritize models based on the scene context. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed ensemble learning approach significantly outperforms individual models and traditional ensemble methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. Benchmark evaluations on standard datasets highlight substantial improvements in detecting text across varied and cluttered scenes. The adaptive weighting strategy effectively improves detection performance in challenging conditions, showcasing the adaptability of the ensemble. Conclusion/Implications: The findings underline the efficacy of predictive ensemble learning in enhancing scene text detection capabilities. This research contributes a scalable, adaptable, and high-performing methodology for real-world applications where text detection is pivotal. The proposed framework's adaptability to different scene contexts suggests potential extensions to other computer vision tasks, indicating its broad applicability and significance in enhancing machine learning-based detection systems. Keywords: Predictive Ensemble Learning, Scene Text Detection, Convolutional Neural Networks, Machine Learning, Adaptive Weighting, Computer Vision.

While many image colorization algorithms have recently shown the capability of producing plausible color versions from gray-scale photographs, they still suffer from limited semantic understanding. To address this shortcoming, we propose to exploit pixelated object semantics to guide image colorization. The rationale is that human beings perceive and distinguish colors based on the semantic categories of objects. Starting from an autoregressive model, we generate image color distributions, from which diverse colored results are sampled. We propose two ways to incorporate object semantics into the colorization model: through a pixelated semantic embedding and a pixelated semantic generator. Specifically, the proposed convolutional neural network includes two branches. One branch learns what the object is, while the other branch learns the object colors. The network jointly optimizes a color embedding loss, a semantic segmentation loss and a color generation loss, in an end-to-end fashion. Experiments on PASCAL VOC2012 and COCO-stuff reveal that our network, when trained with semantic segmentation labels, produces more realistic and finer results compared to the colorization state-of-the-art.

In this paper, a new interval type-2 fuzzy neural network able to construct non-separable fuzzy rules with adaptive shapes is introduced. To reflect the uncertainty, the shape of fuzzy sets considered to be uncertain. Therefore, a new form of interval type-2 fuzzy sets based on a general Gaussian model able to construct different shapes (including triangular, bell-shaped, trapezoidal) is proposed. To consider the interactions among input variables, input vectors are transformed to new feature spaces with uncorrelated variables proper for defining each fuzzy rule. Next, the new features are fed to a fuzzification layer using proposed interval type-2 fuzzy sets with adaptive shape. Consequently, interval type-2 non-separable fuzzy rules with proper shapes, considering the local interactions of variables and the uncertainty are formed. For type reduction the contribution of the upper and lower firing strengths of each fuzzy rule are adaptively selected separately. To train different parameters of the network, the Levenberg-Marquadt optimization method is utilized. The performance of the proposed method is investigated on clean and noisy datasets to show the ability to consider the uncertainty. Moreover, the proposed paradigm, is successfully applied to real-world time-series predictions, regression problems, and nonlinear system identification. According to the experimental results, the performance of our proposed model outperforms other methods with a more parsimonious structure.

**Abstract** Transfer learning has significantly advanced natural language processing (NLP) by enabling models to leverage knowledge from diverse tasks and domains. However, state-of-the-art approaches often require extensive model parameters and large-scale labeled datasets, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained scenarios. This paper introduces a conditionally adaptive multi-task learning (CA-MTL) framework designed to improve transfer learning efficiency in NLP while minimizing parameter usage and data requirements. The proposed method integrates a conditional adaptation mechanism that dynamically modulates shared representations based on task-specific signals, allowing for more effective information sharing across multiple tasks. We evaluate CA-MTL on a suite of benchmark NLP tasks, including text classification, sequence labeling, and question answering. Experimental results demonstrate that CA-MTL achieves competitive or superior performance compared to conventional multi-task and single-task transfer learning baselines, while utilizing significantly fewer parameters and less labeled data. Our analysis reveals improved generalization, faster convergence, and robust performance in low-resource settings. The proposed approach offers a scalable and resource-efficient solution for NLP transfer learning, with potential applications in domains where computational resources or annotated data are limited. Key keywords: multi-task learning, transfer learning, NLP, parameter efficiency, data efficiency, conditional adaptation, deep learning.

Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are widely used for representing structured information, but their utility is often hindered by noise and errors in the data. This paper addresses the challenge of error detection in noisy KGs by proposing a novel approach that leverages graph embeddings guided by path-ranking methods. The objective is to enhance the accuracy of error detection by incorporating relational paths that capture contextual dependencies within the graph. Our method integrates path-ranking algorithms with graph embedding techniques to identify inconsistencies and anomalies in the KG structure. We evaluate the proposed approach on benchmark datasets, comparing its performance against state-of-the-art methods. Results demonstrate significant improvements in error detection accuracy, with our method outperforming existing techniques in identifying both structural and semantic errors. The findings highlight the effectiveness of combining path-based reasoning with graph embeddings for robust error detection. This research contributes to the advancement of KG quality assurance, offering a scalable and interpretable solution for real-world applications in domains such as recommendation systems, semantic search, and data integration. Key innovations include the integration of path-ranking mechanisms into embedding frameworks and the development of a unified model for error detection. Keywords: Knowledge Graphs, Graph Embeddings, Path-Ranking, Error Detection, Noise Reduction, Semantic Analysis.

Image-text matching is a critical task in multimodal learning, aiming to bridge the semantic gap between visual and textual data. This paper introduces a novel approach, Recurrent Visual Embedding (RVE), which treats visual objects in images similarly to words in sentences, enabling a more cohesive alignment between the two modalities. The proposed method leverages recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to encode visual objects sequentially, mimicking the sequential nature of textual data. By doing so, RVE captures fine-grained relationships between objects and words, enhancing the accuracy of image-text matching. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, such as MS-COCO and Flickr30K, demonstrate that RVE outperforms existing methods in terms of retrieval accuracy and cross-modal alignment. The results highlight the effectiveness of treating visual objects as sequential entities, offering a new perspective for multimodal representation learning. This work contributes to advancing image-text matching by providing a robust framework that aligns visual and textual semantics more effectively, with potential applications in image captioning, visual question answering, and multimedia retrieval. **Keywords**: Image-text matching, recurrent neural networks, visual embedding, multimodal learning, semantic alignment.

In this paper a hierarchical model for pixel clustering and image segmentation is developed. In the model an image is hierarchically structured. The original image is treated as a set of nested images, which are capable to reversibly merge with each other. An object is defined as a structural element of an image, so that, an image is regarded as a maximal object. The simulating of none-hierarchical optimal pixel clustering by hierarchical clustering is studied. By providing a common framework for messages, JSON-RPC supports seamless integration between software components, thereby ensuring compatibility and interoperability. As a result, developers can build robust distributed applications with reliable data exchange and reduced complexity.

Bài toán đảm bảo an ninh và phòng chống thất thoát hàng hóa tại các cửa hàng tiện lợi ngày càng trở nên cấp thiết, đặc biệt trong bối cảnh số lượng cửa hàng không ngừng gia tăng. Một hệ thống có khả năng tự động phát hiện người và hành động đáng ngờ như lấy đồ mà không thanh toán sẽ giúp giảm thiểu rủi ro và nâng cao hiệu quả quản lý. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc xây dựng một ứng dụng thông minh sử dụng công nghệ thị giác máy tính để giải quyết vấn đề trên. Ứng dụng được thiết kế để phân tích video từ camera giám sát, xác định sự hiện diện của con người và theo dõi các hành động của họ trong khu vực cửa hàng. Các thuật toán học sâu, đặc biệt là các mô hình phát hiện đối tượng và nhận dạng hành động, được sử dụng để trích xuất các đặc trưng quan trọng từ video. Mô hình phát hiện đối tượng có khả năng xác định và định vị chính xác vị trí của người trong khung hình, đồng thời loại bỏ các yếu tố gây nhiễu như vật thể tĩnh hoặc chuyển động của nhân viên. Sau khi phát hiện người, hệ thống sẽ theo dõi chuyển động của họ và phân tích các hành động liên quan đến việc lấy đồ từ kệ hàng. Các hành động này được so sánh với các mẫu hành vi đã được định nghĩa trước, chẳng hạn như cầm sản phẩm lên, di chuyển đến khu vực thanh toán hoặc rời khỏi cửa hàng mà không thanh toán. Nếu một hành động đáng ngờ được phát hiện, hệ thống sẽ gửi cảnh báo đến nhân viên hoặc người quản lý cửa hàng. Ứng dụng được xây dựng với giao diện thân thiện, dễ sử dụng, cho phép người dùng dễ dàng cấu hình các thông số như khu vực quan sát, ngưỡng phát hiện hành động và phương thức cảnh báo. Kết quả thử nghiệm trên dữ liệu video thực tế từ các cửa hàng tiện lợi cho thấy ứng dụng có khả năng phát hiện người và hành động lấy đồ với độ chính xác cao, giảm thiểu đáng kể số lượng cảnh báo sai. Hệ thống cũng được thiết kế để dễ dàng tích hợp với các hệ thống an ninh hiện có, tạo thành một giải pháp toàn diện cho việc bảo vệ tài sản và đảm bảo an ninh tại các cửa hàng tiện lợi. Hướng phát triển tiếp theo của nghiên cứu bao gồm việc cải thiện khả năng nhận dạng hành động trong điều kiện ánh sáng yếu hoặc khi có nhiều người trong khung hình, cũng như tích hợp thêm các tính năng như nhận dạng khuôn mặt để xác định khách hàng quen và theo dõi lịch sử mua hàng.

Nghiên cứu về sàng lọc người mang đột biến gen SRD5A2 gây thiếu hụt 5-alpha reductase 2 trên thai phụ Việt Nam đang thu hút sự quan tâm của giới y khoa. Đột biến gen SRD5A2 là nguyên nhân dẫn đến tình trạng thiếu hụt enzyme 5-alpha reductase 2, gây ảnh hưởng đến sự phát triển giới tính ở nam giới. Việc sàng lọc sớm trên thai phụ giúp phát hiện nguy cơ di truyền, từ đó có biện pháp can thiệp kịp thời. Tại Việt Nam, nghiên cứu này được thực hiện nhằm đánh giá tỷ lệ mang đột biến gen trong cộng đồng, đồng thời cung cấp dữ liệu quan trọng để xây dựng chiến lược tư vấn di truyền và chăm sóc sức khỏe sinh sản. Kết quả nghiên cứu không chỉ hỗ trợ các gia đình có nguy cơ cao mà còn góp phần nâng cao nhận thức về tầm quan trọng của sàng lọc di truyền trong thai kỳ.

Nghiên cứu thiết lập mô hình số tính toán phát thải khí nhà kính từ hệ thống xử lý nước thải sinh hoạt đang thu hút sự quan tâm lớn trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu ngày càng nghiêm trọng. Mô hình này nhằm đánh giá lượng khí thải, đặc biệt là khí metan và nitơ oxit, phát sinh từ quá trình xử lý nước thải. Bằng cách sử dụng các công cụ tính toán hiện đại, nghiên cứu giúp dự đoán chính xác hơn tác động môi trường của các hệ thống xử lý nước thải, từ đó đề xuất các giải pháp giảm thiểu phát thải hiệu quả. Kết quả nghiên cứu không chỉ góp phần bảo vệ môi trường mà còn hỗ trợ các nhà quản lý trong việc hoạch định chính sách phát triển bền vững.

This paper addresses the challenge of extracting meaningful representations from complex time series data by introducing a novel approach to learn low-dimensional state embeddings and identify metastable clusters. Our objective is to develop a method that can effectively capture the underlying dynamics of high-dimensional systems and reveal their intrinsic patterns. We employ a combination of dimensionality reduction techniques and clustering algorithms to analyze time series data, leveraging advances in machine learning and data analysis. Our approach yields key findings, including the ability to identify metastable states and transitions between them, which are crucial for understanding complex systems. The results demonstrate improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly in terms of clustering quality and robustness to noise. The implications of this research are significant, enabling the application of our method to a wide range of fields, from physics and biology to finance and social sciences, where time series data analysis is critical. By providing a powerful tool for uncovering hidden patterns and structures in complex data, our work contributes to the advancement of data-driven research and discovery, with key keywords including time series analysis, dimensionality reduction, clustering, metastable states, and machine learning.

Hiện nay có rất nhiều dịch vụ đám mây từ nhiều nhà cung cấp nổi tiếng. Chúng ta có thể dễ dàng tìm kiếm các dịch vụ từ những trang web do chính nhà cung cấp điốt phát triển. Cùng với sự đa dạng, nhiều sự lựa chọn đó, người dùng cũng sẽ gặp khó khăn khi không biết nhà cung cấp dịch vụ đám mây nào sẽ phù hợp với mô hình kinh doanh của mình. Vấn đề này đã được trình bày trong chương 1. Hình 2.1 minh họa các phương pháp người dùng sử dụng để ra quyết định lựa chọn (Tìm kiếm trên nhà cung cấp cụ thể, tìm hiểu hướng dẫn lựa chọn).

: Nghiên cứu sự hài lòng về nhà ở tái định cư của người dân đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc hoạch định, điều chỉ nh chính sách v ề nhà ở nói chung và chính sách v ề nhà ở tái định cư nói riêng. Bài vi ết này nhằm mụ c tiêu xác định các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến sự hài lòng về nhà ở tái định cư của người dân tại các dự án xây dựng lại nhà chung cư cũ trên đị a bàn TP Hà N ội. Dữ liệu khảo sát th u thậ p từ 663 người dân đang sinh sống tại các căn hộ tái định cư đã được bàn giao sau khi xây dựng lại một số nhà chung c ư cũ trên địa bàn mộ t số quận trung tâm của TP Hà Nội. Kết quả hồi sức phòng sanh của trẻ sơ sinh cực non tại Bệnh viện Hùng Vương cho thấy những tiến bộ đáng kể trong việc cải thiện tình trạng sức khỏe của trẻ. Nghiên cứu đã phân tích các phương pháp hồi sức được áp dụng, bao gồm thở oxy, hỗ trợ hô hấp và các biện pháp can thiệp kịp thời. Dữ liệu thu thập từ 200 trẻ sơ sinh cực non cho thấy tỷ lệ sống sót sau hồi sức tăng lên rõ rệt, đồng thời giảm thiểu các biến chứng nghiêm trọng. Các yếu tố như thời gian hồi sức, sự phối hợp giữa các chuyên gia y tế và trang thiết bị hiện đại đã đóng vai trò quan trọng trong thành công này. Kết quả nghiên cứu không chỉ khẳng định hiệu quả của các phương pháp hồi sức mà còn mở ra hướng đi mới cho việc chăm sóc trẻ sơ sinh cực non tại các cơ sở y tế, góp phần nâng cao chất lượng dịch vụ y tế cho nhóm đối tượng nhạy cảm này.

This paper introduces Luna, a novel Linear Unified Nested Attention mechanism designed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of attention-based neural networks. The objective of this research is to address the limitations of existing attention models, which often suffer from high computational complexity and limited scalability. To achieve this, we propose a unified framework that integrates linear attention and nested attention, enabling the model to capture both local and global dependencies in input data. Our approach leverages a combination of linear transformations and nested attention layers to reduce computational costs while preserving the expressive power of traditional attention mechanisms. Experimental results demonstrate that Luna outperforms state-of-the-art attention models on several benchmark tasks, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency. The proposed mechanism has important implications for a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Key contributions of this work include the introduction of a linear unified nested attention framework, which enables efficient and effective attention-based processing, and the demonstration of its potential to advance the field of artificial intelligence. Relevant keywords: attention mechanisms, linear attention, nested attention, neural networks, artificial intelligence, deep learning.

Nghiên cứu về chỉ tiêu sinh lý và sinh hóa máu của trâu nuôi tại huyện Cẩm Thủy, tỉnh Thanh Hóa đã được thực hiện nhằm đánh giá tình trạng sức khỏe và chất lượng chăn nuôi. Kết quả cho thấy các chỉ số như hồng cầu, bạch cầu, hemoglobin và các enzyme trong máu đều nằm trong ngưỡng bình thường, phản ánh sức khỏe ổn định của đàn trâu. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng chế độ dinh dưỡng và điều kiện chăn nuôi tại địa phương đáp ứng tốt nhu cầu sinh lý của trâu. Những phát hiện này không chỉ giúp nâng cao hiệu quả chăn nuôi mà còn góp phần cải thiện chất lượng sản phẩm từ trâu, đảm bảo an toàn thực phẩm và phát triển bền vững ngành chăn nuôi tại địa phương.

Explainable artificial intelligence has been gaining attention in the past few years. However, most existing methods are based on gradients or intermediate features, which are not directly involved in the decision-making process of the classifier. In this paper, we propose a slot attention-based classifier called SCOUTER for transparent yet accurate classification. Two major differences from other attention-based methods include: (a) SCOUTER's explanation is involved in the final confidence for each category, offering more intuitive interpretation, and (b) all the categories have their corresponding positive or negative explanation, which tells "why the image is of a certain category" or "why the image is not of a certain category." We design a new loss tailored for SCOUTER that controls the model's behavior to switch between positive and negative explanations, as well as the size of explanatory regions. Experimental results show that SCOUTER can give better visual explanations in terms of various metrics while keeping good accuracy on small and medium-sized datasets.

Trường Đại học Phú Yên đã thực hiện một phân tích chuyên sâu về "nguyên sơ không rút gọn được" và "bao đóng nguyên" của Idean, một khái niệm trừu tượng trong lĩnh vực toán học hoặc khoa học máy tính. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc khám phá các đặc tính cơ bản và cấu trúc nền tảng của Idean mà không áp dụng bất kỳ phép đơn giản hóa hay lược bỏ nào. Tiếp cận này cho phép làm sáng tỏ bản chất cốt lõi và các mối quan hệ nội tại của Idean. Đồng thời, việc phân tích "bao đóng nguyên" giúp xác định phạm vi ảnh hưởng và các yếu tố liên quan chặt chẽ đến Idean, từ đó cung cấp cái nhìn toàn diện và sâu sắc hơn về đối tượng nghiên cứu. Kết quả của phân tích này có thể ứng dụng trong nhiều lĩnh vực khác nhau, đặc biệt là trong việc xây dựng các mô hình toán học phức tạp hoặc phát triển các thuật toán mới.

This paper introduces a novel approach to learning plannable representations in complex environments by integrating causal reasoning with generative adversarial networks (GANs). The proposed framework, Causal InfoGAN, leverages the strengths of GAN-based representation learning while incorporating causal inference to enhance the interpretability and controllability of learned representations. The primary objective is to enable efficient planning and decision-making in environments where traditional methods struggle due to high dimensionality or sparse rewards. The Causal InfoGAN architecture combines an information-theoretic objective with a causal structure learning mechanism, allowing the model to disentangle latent factors and identify causal relationships within the data. This approach not only improves the quality of generated representations but also ensures that they are actionable for downstream planning tasks. Experiments conducted on benchmark environments demonstrate that Causal InfoGAN outperforms existing methods in terms of representation quality, planning efficiency, and robustness to environmental changes. Key findings reveal that the learned representations are highly interpretable and enable more accurate predictions of future states, facilitating better decision-making in dynamic settings. The implications of this work extend to applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and reinforcement learning, where plannable and causally grounded representations are critical for success. This research contributes a significant advancement in the integration of causal reasoning with deep generative models, offering a promising direction for future work in AI and machine learning. **Keywords**: Causal inference, GANs, representation learning, planning, decision-making, generative models.

This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing sequential decision-making processes under uncertainty, leveraging the principles of free energy minimization. The objective is to derive a generalized framework for decision-making that integrates probabilistic reasoning and optimization to enhance computational efficiency and decision accuracy. We propose a novel approach based on the free energy principle, which extends traditional optimality equations to account for complex, dynamic environments. Our method employs variational inference techniques to approximate posterior distributions, enabling scalable and adaptive decision-making strategies. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing methods in terms of both computational efficiency and decision quality, particularly in high-dimensional and uncertain scenarios. The results highlight the potential of free energy-based approaches to bridge the gap between theoretical optimality and practical applicability in sequential decision-making tasks. This work contributes to the advancement of decision-making algorithms in artificial intelligence, robotics, and autonomous systems, offering a robust and generalizable solution for real-world applications. **Keywords**: free energy, sequential decision-making, optimality equations, variational inference, probabilistic reasoning, adaptive systems.

Nghiên cứu thiết kế và chế tạo máy phay CNC mini 4 trục sử dụng chương trình Mach3 là một dự án nhằm phát triển một thiết bị gia công chính xác, nhỏ gọn và hiệu quả cho các ứng dụng chế tạo. Máy phay CNC mini này được thiết kế với bốn trục, cho phép thực hiện các thao tác phay phức tạp và linh hoạt hơn so với các máy phay truyền thống. Việc sử dụng phần mềm Mach3 giúp điều khiển máy một cách dễ dàng và chính xác, đồng thời mở rộng khả năng lập trình cho người sử dụng. Dự án không chỉ tập trung vào việc cải thiện hiệu suất gia công mà còn hướng đến việc giảm chi phí sản xuất và tăng tính khả thi cho các xưởng chế tạo nhỏ. Qua đó, nghiên cứu này góp phần thúc đẩy sự phát triển của công nghệ chế tạo tại Việt Nam, đáp ứng nhu cầu ngày càng cao trong ngành công nghiệp chế biến và sản xuất.

Kiên Giang là tỉnh có tiềm năng rất lớn về phát triển nghề nuôi biển bền vững ở nước ta và động lực hải văn là một trong những yếu tố quan trọng trong việc lựa chọn khu vực nuôi biển phù hợp. Bài báo trình bày kết quả nghiên cứu, phân tích đánh giá động lực hải văn vùng biển tỉnh Kiên Giang thông qua công cụ mô hình tính toán MIKE21/3FM. Từ k ết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy ở khu vực nghiên cứu vùng biển Kiên Giang, sóng nhật triều đóng vai trò chính và chế độ thủy triều mang tính nhật triều không đều với dao động triều trung bình xấp xỉ 1m. Nhìn chung tốc độ dòng chảy ở vùng nghiên cứu là tương đối nhỏ, trung bình dao động 20 -35cm/s, trừ một số vùng biển của An Thới và Gành Dầu. Khác với một số vùng biển khác ở Việt Nam, chế độ trường sóng yếu với độ cao sóng vào khoảng 0,3m -0,7m ở vùng biển Kiên Giang vào gió mùa Đông Bắc nhỏ hơn so với vào gió mùa Tây nam với độ cao sóng trung bình vào khoảng 0,5m -1,0m. Từ kết quả tính toán động lực hải văn, bài báo cũng đã đề xuất một số khu vực nuôi biển phù hợp có tiềm năng tại vùng biển Kiên Giang, trong đó hai khu vực có tiềm năng lớn là đảo Phú Quốc và quần đảo Nam Du.

This paper introduces ALET, a comprehensive framework for automated labeling of equipment and tools in real-world environments. The objective is to develop a robust tool detection system capable of identifying and categorizing tools in uncontrolled settings. To achieve this, we created a large-scale dataset comprising diverse tools and equipment, which serves as the foundation for our research. Our approach employs a deep learning-based baseline model, leveraging computer vision techniques to detect and classify tools. The results show significant improvements in detection accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. A key use case demonstrates the practical application of ALET in a construction site scenario, highlighting its potential to enhance workplace safety and productivity. The contributions of this research include the introduction of a novel dataset, a robust baseline model, and a real-world use case, paving the way for future advancements in tool detection and automated labeling. Key keywords: tool detection, automated labeling, computer vision, deep learning, equipment recognition.

Hà Nội đang đẩy mạnh phát triển Khu công nghiệp và chế xuất, tạo động lực cho sự phát triển kinh tế - xã hội của thành phố. Tuy nhiên, việc quản lý và vận hành các khu nhà ở phục vụ khu công nghiệp và chế xuất còn nhiều hạn chế. This paper introduces a novel approach for anomaly detection in particulate matter (PM) sensor data, addressing the challenges of data drift and sensor malfunction. We propose a Hypothesis Pruning Generative Adversarial Network (HP-GAN) that combines the strengths of GANs in learning data distributions with a hypothesis pruning mechanism to identify anomalous data points. The HP-GAN is trained on historical PM sensor data to model normal operating conditions. The hypothesis pruning component dynamically adjusts the discriminator's decision boundary, enhancing sensitivity to subtle anomalies and reducing false positives. Experiments conducted on a real-world PM sensor dataset demonstrate that HP-GAN outperforms traditional anomaly detection methods and standard GAN-based approaches, achieving a significant improvement in F1-score and area under the ROC curve. The proposed method offers a robust and efficient solution for ensuring data quality and reliability in environmental monitoring applications. Keywords: Anomaly Detection, Generative Adversarial Network, Particulate Matter Sensor, Hypothesis Pruning, Environmental Monitoring, Data Quality.

Blockchain technology represents a revolutionary advance in the realm of digital record-keeping, offering an innovative framework that ensures security, transparency, and decentralization within electronic transactions while eliminating the reliance on traditional intermediaries. Its evolution is anchored in the necessity to address long-standing issues of trust and centralized control in digital ecosystems, setting the stage for a more democratic method of handling data and value exchange. Central to this development is Satoshi Nakamoto’s profound contribution with the 2008 publication of the whitepaper "Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System." This seminal document outlined the foundational principles of blockchain, presenting a blueprint for a decentralized digital currency capable of operating on a peer-to-peer basis and establishing a new paradigm for monetary transactions and data integrity. The introduction of blockchain, as defined by Nakamoto, catalyzed the rise of cryptocurrencies and spurred transformative change across industries reliant on secure, trustworthy transactions.

Multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) addresses the challenge of optimizing multiple, often conflicting objectives simultaneously, a critical requirement in real-world applications such as personalized recommendation systems and resource allocation. This paper investigates the problem of accommodating "picky" customers—users with highly specific and diverse preferences—in MORL frameworks. We propose a novel algorithm that balances exploration and exploitation to efficiently learn policies tailored to such users. Our approach leverages a regret-bound analysis to quantify the trade-offs between competing objectives, ensuring robust performance across diverse user preferences. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that our method achieves significantly lower regret compared to existing MORL techniques, particularly in scenarios with high-dimensional preference spaces. Additionally, we analyze the exploration complexity of our algorithm, providing theoretical guarantees on its efficiency in discovering optimal policies. The results highlight the algorithm's ability to adapt to varying user demands while maintaining computational tractability. This work contributes to the advancement of MORL by offering a scalable and user-centric solution for applications requiring fine-grained preference alignment. Key implications include improved customer satisfaction in recommendation systems and enhanced adaptability in dynamic decision-making environments. **Keywords**: multi-objective reinforcement learning, regret bound, exploration complexity, personalized recommendation, user preferences, optimization.

In the field of computer vision, accurately detecting and recognizing multiple simultaneous activities remains a significant challenge. This research introduces a novel approach leveraging hierarchical Graph Recurrent Neural Networks (Graph-RNNs) to enhance the precision and scalability of action detection tasks in complex environments. Methods/Approach: Our approach utilizes a hierarchical architecture of Graph-RNNs that captures temporal dependencies and spatial relationships among detected entities in a scene. The model integrates graph-based structures to represent interactions and dynamically propagates temporal information through recurrent units. This methodology enables the system to decode complex activity sequences more effectively compared to traditional models. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the Hierarchical Graph-RNN model outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The system achieved superior performance metrics, showcasing its ability to generalize across diverse scenarios with multiple concurrent activities. Conclusion/Implications: The proposed Hierarchical Graph-RNN approach significantly advances the state-of-the-art in action detection for multi-activity settings by providing a more nuanced understanding of interactions and temporal evolutions. The insights gained from this research have the potential to be applied in various domains, including surveillance, human-computer interaction, and autonomous systems. This work lays the groundwork for future studies aiming to further improve action detection systems in complex, real-world environments. Keywords: Action Detection, Hierarchical Graph-RNN, Computer Vision, Multiple Activities, Temporal Dependencies, Spatial Relationships, Deep Learning.

This paper introduces a novel approach to automated code generation, specifically focusing on the creation of markup languages such as HTML and CSS. Our method, Neural Markup Generation with Visual Attention (NMG-VA), aims to bridge the gap between visual design and code by enabling machines to directly generate markup code from visual inputs. NMG-VA employs a deep neural network architecture incorporating a visual attention mechanism that selectively focuses on relevant features within the visual input, mimicking the way a human developer interprets a design. The model is trained end-to-end on a dataset of paired visual designs and corresponding markup code. Experimental results demonstrate that NMG-VA significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of code accuracy, structural correctness, and visual fidelity, particularly in generating complex layouts. The visual attention mechanism contributes to improved interpretability and allows the model to generalize to unseen designs more effectively. This research offers a promising avenue for automating web development tasks and facilitating design-to-code workflows. Keywords: code generation, markup languages, visual attention, neural networks, automated web development.

This paper addresses the vulnerability of face recognition systems in the physical world to adversarial attacks. Our objective is to design and develop meaningful adversarial stickers that can effectively evade face detection and recognition models in real-world scenarios. We propose a novel approach that utilizes a combination of computer vision and machine learning techniques to generate stickers that are not only adversarial but also visually appealing and meaningful. Our method involves training a generative model to produce stickers that can be worn on the face, allowing individuals to maintain their privacy and security in public spaces. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, with a significant reduction in face recognition accuracy when our stickers are worn. Instance segmentation, a critical task in computer vision, aims to precisely delineate and classify individual objects within an image. Traditional mask representations often rely on pixel-level or polygon-based approaches, which can be computationally expensive and memory-intensive. This paper introduces **DCT-Mask**, a novel framework that leverages the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) to represent instance masks efficiently. By encoding masks in the frequency domain, DCT-Mask significantly reduces memory usage while maintaining high segmentation accuracy. The proposed method integrates DCT-based mask compression with a state-of-the-art instance segmentation model, enabling real-time performance on resource-constrained devices. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DCT-Mask achieves competitive segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods, with a 40% reduction in memory footprint. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robustness across diverse object shapes and scales, making it suitable for applications in autonomous driving, medical imaging, and robotics. The key contribution of this work lies in its innovative use of frequency-domain representations for instance segmentation, offering a balance between computational efficiency and performance. DCT-Mask paves the way for deploying advanced segmentation models in edge computing environments, where resource efficiency is paramount. **Keywords**: Instance segmentation, Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), mask representation, frequency domain, memory efficiency, real-time processing.

In this paper we consider the problem of learning undirected graphical models from data generated according to the Glauber dynamics. The Glauber dynamics is a Markov chain that sequentially updates individual nodes (variables) in a graphical model and it is frequently used to sample from the stationary distribution (to which it converges given sufficient time). Additionally, the Glauber dynamics is a natural dynamical model in a variety of settings. This work deviates from the standard formulation of graphical model learning in the literature, where one assumes access to i.i.d. samples from the distribution. Much of the research on graphical model learning has been directed towards finding algorithms with low computational cost. As the main result of this work, we establish that the problem of reconstructing binary pairwise graphical models is computationally tractable when we observe the Glauber dynamics. Specifically, we show that a binary pairwise graphical model on p nodes with maximum degree d can be learned in time f(d)p^2\log p, for a function f(d), using nearly the information-theoretic minimum number of samples.

Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable progress in various real-world applications, especially when abundant training data are provided. However, data isolation has become a serious problem currently. Existing works build privacy preserving DNN models from either algorithmic perspective or cryptographic perspective. The former mainly splits the DNN computation graph between data holders or between data holders and server, which demonstrates good scalability but suffers from accuracy loss and potential privacy risks. In contrast, the latter leverages time-consuming cryptographic techniques, which has strong privacy guarantee but poor scalability. In this paper, we propose SPNN - a Scalable and Privacy-preserving deep Neural Network learning framework, from algorithmic-cryptographic co-perspective. From algorithmic perspective, we split the computation graph of DNN models into two parts, i.e., the private data related computations that are performed by data holders and the rest heavy computations that are delegated to a server with high computation ability. From cryptographic perspective, we propose using two types of cryptographic techniques, i.e., secret sharing and homomorphic encryption, for the isolated data holders to conduct private data related computations privately and cooperatively. Furthermore, we implement SPNN in a decentralized setting and introduce user-friendly APIs. Experimental results conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of SPNN.

Mô hình được sử dụng để trích xuất đặc trưng khuôn mặt trong đồ án này được xây dựng dựa trên kiến trúc ResNet50, một kiến trúc mạng nổi tiếng trong lĩnh vực học sâu. ResNet50, vớ 50 tầng học, đã chứng tỏ được khả năng học tập xuất sắc của mình trên nhiều bài toán trong lĩnh vực thị giác máy tính, bao gồm nhận diện khuôn mặt. Trong đồ án, mô hình ResNet50 được sử dụng như là một bộ trích xuất đặc trưng nghĩa là, nó được sử dụng để học cách chuyển đổi mỗ ảnh khuôn mặt thành một vector đặc trưng, biểu diễn số học của thông tin trong ảnh. Đầu vào cho mô hình là các ảnh khuôn mặt điã điược tền xử lý, vớ kích thước chuẩn hóa là 112x112 pixel. Mô hình được huấn luyện và hàm mất mát Arcade, một hàm mất mát được thiết kế đặc biệt cho bài toán nhận diện khuôn mặt. Hàm mất mát Arc Face gúp mô hình học cách tố ưu hóa khoảng cách giữa các vector đặc trưng của các ảnh cùng một người (nghĩa là giúp chúng trở nên gần nhau hơn trong không gian đặc trưng) và đồng thờ tăng khoảng cách giữa các vector đặc trưng của các ảnh của các người khác nhau (nghĩa là đẩy chúng ra xa nhau hơn trong không gian đặc trưng). Mô hình được huấn luyện trên một tập dữ lệu điã điược tăng cường, bằng cách sử dụng phương pháp dựng khuôn mặt 3D để tạo ra nhiều hình ảnh từ nhiều góc độ khác nhau cho mỗi người. Tập dữ liệu tăng cường này giúp mô hình học được sự đa dạng hơn về cách biểu hiện của khuôn mặt từ các góc nhìn khác nhau, đồng thờ cúng gúp giảm thiểu sự mất cân đối giữa các lớp dữ liệu.

Các kết quả cho thấy, hiệu suất HMF cao nhất tại nhiệt độ phản ứng 140ºC trong 1 giờ với hàm lượng cellulose 162 mg, 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride ([EMIM]Cl) 6 mmol, xúc tác SAC 10 mg và DES ChCl:CrCl3 0,5 mmol. Đặc biệt, chất xúc tác có khả năng thu hồi và tái sử dụng 3 lần với hiệu suất giảm không đáng kể trong quá trình chuyển hóa cellulose thành HMF.

With the growing prevalence of smart grid technology, short-term load forecasting (STLF) becomes particularly important in power system operations. There is a large collection of methods developed for STLF, but selecting a suitable method under varying conditions is still challenging. This paper develops a novel reinforcement learning based dynamic model selection (DMS) method for STLF. A forecasting model pool is first built, including ten state-of-the-art machine learning based forecasting models. Then a Q-learning agent learns the optimal policy of selecting the best forecasting model for the next time step, based on the model performance. The optimal DMS policy is applied to select the best model at each time step with a moving window. Numerical simulations on two-year load and weather data show that the Q-learning algorithm converges fast, resulting in effective and efficient DMS. The developed STLF model with Q-learning based DMS improves the forecasting accuracy by approximately 50%, compared to the state-of-the-art machine learning based STLF models.

Benefiting from the spatial cues embedded in depth images, recent progress on RGB-D saliency detection shows impressive ability on some challenge scenarios. However, there are still two limitations. One hand is that the pooling and upsampling operations in FCNs might cause blur object boundaries. On the other hand, using an additional depth-network to extract depth features might lead to high computation and storage cost. The reliance on depth inputs during testing also limits the practical applications of current RGB-D models. In this paper, we propose a novel collaborative learning framework where edge, depth and saliency are leveraged in a more efficient way, which solves those problems tactfully. The explicitly extracted edge information goes together with saliency to give more emphasis to the salient regions and object boundaries. Depth and saliency learning is innovatively integrated into the high-level feature learning process in a mutual-benefit manner. This strategy enables the network to be free of using extra depth networks and depth inputs to make inference. To this end, it makes our model more lightweight, faster and more versatile. Experiment results on seven benchmark datasets show its superior performance.
