This paper introduces ICON, a novel approach to learning regular maps by enforcing inverse consistency. The objective is to improve the accuracy and robustness of geometric correspondence learning, a critical task in computer vision. ICON leverages the principle that transformations between two shapes should be invertible; thus, the composition of a forward and backward mapping should ideally result in the identity transformation. We formulate a loss function that explicitly penalizes deviations from this inverse consistency, guiding the network to learn more geometrically plausible and accurate maps. Experiments on shape matching and deformation transfer tasks demonstrate that ICON significantly outperforms existing methods, producing more regular and accurate mappings, particularly in the presence of noise or significant geometric variations. Key findings reveal that enforcing inverse consistency regularizes the learned map space, leading to improved generalization and robustness. ICON represents a significant advance in geometric correspondence learning, offering a powerful framework for various applications, including shape analysis, animation, and medical image registration. Keywords: geometric correspondence, inverse consistency, shape matching, deformation transfer, regularization, neural networks.

The design of novel molecules with desired properties is a critical challenge in drug discovery and materials science. This paper presents a deep generative model for fragment-based molecule generation, leveraging advancements in machine learning to address the limitations of traditional approaches. The proposed model integrates a graph-based neural network with a variational autoencoder (VAE) framework, enabling the generation of chemically valid and diverse molecular structures by assembling predefined molecular fragments. The method emphasizes the preservation of chemical feasibility and the exploration of a vast chemical space. Experimental results demonstrate that the model outperforms existing methods in terms of molecular validity, diversity, and property optimization. Additionally, the generated molecules exhibit improved drug-like properties, as validated by standard cheminformatics metrics. This work contributes a novel, scalable approach to molecule generation, with potential applications in accelerating drug discovery and materials design. Key innovations include the integration of fragment-based assembly with deep generative techniques, offering a robust and interpretable framework for molecular design. Keywords: deep learning, generative models, molecule generation, drug discovery, variational autoencoder, graph neural networks.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of accurately segmenting overlapping chromosomes in cytogenetic images, a fundamental task for various genetic analyses and diagnosis processes. The proposed study introduces an innovative method termed Adversarial Multiscale Feature Learning (AMFL), designed to enhance the segmentation performance of overlapping chromosomes. The approach leverages an adversarial framework combined with multiscale feature extraction to capture and learn both global and local contextual information effectively. Utilizing a generative adversarial network (GAN)-based architecture, the model generates more precise and robust segmentation outcomes by dynamically adjusting to the varying shapes and overlaps of chromosome clusters. The performance of the AMFL method was evaluated on a publicly available dataset and demonstrated superior segmentation accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art models, evidenced by higher Intersection over Union (IoU) and F1 metrics. The results indicate significant improvements in distinguishing tightly clustered and partially overlapping chromosome instances. This research thereby contributes a novel technique that holds potential utility in enhancing automated karyotyping and advancing cytogenetic analyses. Future applications may extend to broader medical imaging domains that require precise segmentation of intricate and overlapping structures. Key keywords include chromosome segmentation, adversarial learning, multiscale feature extraction, GAN, and medical image analysis.

Our approach utilizes a combination of recurrent neural networks and conditional GANs to model complex temporal dependencies and capture nuanced patterns in medical time series. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in generating realistic and diverse synthetic data, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. The key findings of this research highlight the potential of RCGANs in medical time series generation, enabling the creation of anonymized datasets for research and development purposes. This contribution has significant implications for the field of medical informatics, particularly in areas such as disease diagnosis, patient monitoring, and personalized medicine. Abstract: Evaluating text generation models requires a nuanced assessment of both the diversity and quality of their outputs, yet most existing metrics focus on these aspects independently, often overlooking their trade-offs. This paper introduces a novel framework for jointly measuring diversity and quality in text generation models, addressing critical limitations of current evaluation methodologies. Our approach leverages a combination of semantic similarity metrics and distributional statistics to capture the breadth of generated content alongside its linguistic coherence and relevance. We propose new composite scoring techniques that seamlessly integrate measures such as lexical variety, semantic distance, and fluency, enabling comprehensive evaluation across varied text generation tasks. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets using state-of-the-art neural language models—including transformers and large generative models—demonstrate that our metrics better correspond with human judgments compared to traditional isolated measures. The results reveal deeper insights into model performance, highlighting informative trade-offs and guiding the selection of generation strategies. This joint evaluation framework advances the field by offering a robust, interpretable tool for assessing and improving text generation systems. Keywords: text generation, diversity, quality assessment, evaluation metrics, natural language processing, neural language models.

This paper introduces a novel graph-driven communication framework to enhance multi-agent coordination in complex environments. The objective is to enable agents to learn effective communication strategies that facilitate efficient task completion. Our approach involves constructing dynamic communication graphs, where nodes represent agents and edges indicate communication channels, optimized using a reinforcement learning algorithm. This graph structure allows agents to selectively share information with relevant peers, reducing communication overhead and improving decision-making. We evaluate our framework on several benchmark cooperative tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in team performance compared to state-of-the-art methods with fixed or no communication structures. Specifically, agents learn to adapt the communication graph based on the task requirements and agent roles, leading to more robust and scalable coordination. Our findings highlight the importance of adaptive communication topologies for effective multi-agent learning. Keywords: multi-agent systems, reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, communication, coordination, distributed AI.

The interpretation of seafloor imagery is critical for marine exploration, environmental monitoring, and resource management. However, the complexity and variability of underwater environments pose significant challenges for automated image analysis. This paper introduces **GeoCLR**, a novel georeference-based contrastive learning framework designed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of seafloor image interpretation. The proposed approach leverages geospatial metadata to guide the learning process, enabling the model to capture spatial relationships and contextual features inherent in seafloor imagery. By employing a contrastive learning strategy, GeoCLR learns robust representations of seafloor features without requiring extensive labeled datasets, addressing the scarcity of annotated underwater imagery. Experiments conducted on real-world seafloor datasets demonstrate that GeoCLR outperforms traditional methods in terms of feature discrimination and generalization capabilities. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in tasks such as habitat classification and object detection, while significantly reducing computational overhead. The results highlight the potential of GeoCLR to advance underwater image analysis, offering a scalable and resource-efficient solution for marine research and applications. This work contributes to the growing field of geospatial machine learning, providing a foundation for future innovations in automated seafloor exploration and monitoring. **Keywords**: geospatial machine learning, contrastive learning, seafloor image analysis, underwater imagery, georeference, marine exploration.

This paper introduces a novel approach to human pose estimation, demonstrating that 15 keypoints are sufficient to achieve state-of-the-art performance in various applications. Traditional methods often rely on complex models with a large number of keypoints, which can be computationally expensive and prone to overfitting. In contrast, our method leverages a streamlined architecture that focuses on 15 strategically selected keypoints, balancing accuracy and efficiency. We propose a lightweight deep learning model optimized for real-time processing, incorporating advanced techniques such as attention mechanisms and spatial-temporal modeling to enhance robustness. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that our approach achieves comparable or superior accuracy to existing methods while significantly reducing computational overhead. Furthermore, the model demonstrates strong generalization capabilities across diverse environments and datasets. The findings suggest that reducing the number of keypoints does not compromise performance when combined with intelligent feature extraction and optimization strategies. This work has significant implications for applications requiring real-time pose estimation, such as augmented reality, robotics, and human-computer interaction, offering a practical and scalable solution. Keywords: human pose estimation, keypoints, deep learning, real-time processing, attention mechanisms.

Video frame synthesis aims to generate intermediate frames between existing ones, enhancing frame rates and enabling slow-motion effects. This paper introduces a novel Multi-Scale Video Frame-Synthesis Network (MSVFS-Net) designed to improve the quality and consistency of synthesized frames. Our approach utilizes a multi-scale architecture to capture both fine-grained details and global motion patterns within the video sequence. Specifically, we employ a series of convolutional and deconvolutional layers at multiple scales, allowing the network to effectively learn temporal dependencies and spatial relationships. Furthermore, we propose a Transitive Consistency Loss (TCL) that enforces consistency between synthesized frames and their neighboring real frames. TCL ensures that the transformation between two real frames is consistent with the composition of transformations through the synthesized intermediate frame. We evaluate MSVFS-Net on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in PSNR, SSIM, and perceptual quality compared to state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the multi-scale architecture and the TCL. Our approach contributes a robust and accurate video frame synthesis method suitable for a wide range of applications, including video editing and high-frame-rate video generation. Keywords: Video Frame Synthesis, Frame Interpolation, Multi-Scale Network, Transitive Consistency Loss, Deep Learning.

Objective: This paper investigates the theoretical performance of nonparametric reinforcement learning (RL) methods by deriving regret bounds for kernel-based algorithms in continuous Markov decision processes (MDPs). Our goal is to bridge the gap between practical kernel-based value estimation and provable guarantees on cumulative suboptimality. Methods: We introduce KernelUCRL, an RL framework that combines kernel ridge regression in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with an optimism-under-uncertainty exploration strategy. At each episode, the agent fits transition and reward functions via kernel methods, constructs high-probability confidence sets around these estimates, and computes an optimistic policy by planning over the induced confidence MDP. Results: We prove that KernelUCRL achieves a regret bound of Õ(√T · ‖f*‖_ℋ), where T is the total time horizon and ‖f*‖_ℋ denotes the RKHS norm of the true value function. This bound scales sublinearly in T, matching the minimax rate for tabular settings up to kernel-dependent factors. Empirical simulations on benchmark continuous control tasks confirm that KernelUCRL outperforms baseline algorithms in sample efficiency while maintaining computational tractability. Conclusion: Our analysis provides the first regret guarantees for nonparametric, kernel-based RL in continuous spaces, offering dimension-free performance bounds under smoothness assumptions. These results pave the way for principled deployment of kernel methods in high-dimensional, real-world decision-making problems. Keywords: reinforcement learning, regret analysis, kernel methods, RKHS, nonparametric RL, continuous MDP.

This paper introduces a novel unsupervised learning framework for multi-object tracking (MOT) by leveraging animation-inspired techniques to enhance object tracking accuracy and robustness. The proposed approach, termed *Tracking by Animation*, employs a self-supervised learning paradigm to train attentive trackers without requiring labeled data. By simulating object motion and interactions through synthetic animations, the model learns to predict object trajectories and maintain consistent identities across frames. The framework integrates a multi-object attention mechanism to handle occlusions and complex scenes, enabling precise tracking in dynamic environments. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art supervised approaches, with significant improvements in handling occlusions and long-term tracking scenarios. The study highlights the potential of unsupervised learning in MOT and provides a scalable solution for real-world applications such as surveillance, autonomous driving, and video analysis. Key contributions include the innovative use of animation-based training, the integration of attention mechanisms for multi-object tracking, and the demonstration of unsupervised learning’s effectiveness in reducing dependency on labeled datasets. Keywords: multi-object tracking, unsupervised learning, attention mechanisms, animation-based training, self-supervised learning.

In this paper, we demonstrated a practical application of realistic river image generation using deep learning. Specifically, we explored a generative adversarial network (GAN) model capable of generating high-resolution and realistic river images that can be used to support modeling and analysis in surface water estimation, river meandering, wetland loss, and other hydrological research studies. First, we have created an extensive repository of overhead river images to be used in training. Second, we incorporated the Progressive Growing GAN (PGGAN), a network architecture that iteratively trains smaller-resolution GANs to gradually build up to a very high resolution to generate high quality (i.e., 1024x1024) synthetic river imagery. With simpler GAN architectures, difficulties arose in terms of exponential increase of training time and vanishing/exploding gradient issues, which the PGGAN implementation seemed to significantly reduce. The results presented in this study show great promise in generating high-quality images and capturing the details of river structure and flow to support hydrological research, which often requires extensive imagery for model performance.

This paper introduces a novel high-order differentiable autoencoder (HDA) for nonlinear model reduction. The HDA leverages higher-order derivatives in the encoding and decoding processes to capture complex nonlinear relationships within high-dimensional data, surpassing the limitations of traditional linear or first-order methods. Our approach involves a tailored neural network architecture integrated with differentiable programming techniques to ensure end-to-end differentiability, enabling efficient training via gradient-based optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the HDA through experiments on several benchmark problems, including fluid dynamics simulations and structural mechanics. Results indicate that the HDA achieves significantly improved accuracy and compression rates compared to standard autoencoders and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) based reduction methods, especially in scenarios with strong nonlinearities. The proposed method offers a powerful tool for reducing the computational cost of complex simulations and facilitating real-time analysis and control. Keywords: Autoencoder, Model Reduction, Nonlinear Dynamics, Differentiable Programming, Neural Networks, Dimensionality Reduction.

Addressing the challenge of factor analysis where preserving the inherent order of data is crucial, this paper proposes a novel method called Order-Preserving Factor Analysis (OPFA). Traditional factor analysis methods often overlook the ordinal nature of data, leading to suboptimal interpretation and analysis. This research seeks to develop a technique that integrates ordinality into the factor extraction process, enhancing the analytical capability for datasets with ordered categories. Methods/Approach: OPFA extends conventional factor analysis by incorporating a rank-preserving mechanism that retains the original order of data throughout the analysis. This is achieved by leveraging a modified optimization framework that respects ordinal constraints, ensuring the extracted factors reflect the sequence of data categories. The approach is tested on synthetic and real-world datasets compared against standard factor analysis techniques to demonstrate its robustness and applicability. Results/Findings: The application of OPFA shows superior performance in scenarios where ordinality is a significant factor, resulting in more accurate and meaningful factor extraction. The results indicate that OPFA maintains the ordinal integrity of the data while achieving comparable, if not improved, levels of explained variance and interpretability over traditional methods. Notably, OPFA demonstrates a distinct advantage in fields such as psychometrics and sociometrics, where the order of data points conveys critical information. Conclusion/Implications: OPFA offers a valuable advancement in factor analysis by preserving data order, thus providing more reliable insights for analyses involving ordered categories. By integrating ordinal constraints into the factor extraction process, OPFA widens the application scope of factor analysis models and contributes to more nuanced data interpretation in various domains. This innovative approach presents opportunities for enhanced data analysis within fields requiring order preservation, including social sciences and market research. Keywords: Order-preserving factor analysis, ordinal data, data interpretation, factor extraction, ordered categories.

Geometric representation learning has recently shown great promise in several machine learning settings, ranging from relational learning to language processing and generative models. In this work, we consider the problem of performing manifold-valued regression onto an hyperbolic space as an intermediate component for a number of relevant machine learning applications. In particular, by formulating the problem of predicting nodes of a tree as a manifold regression task in the hyperbolic space, we propose a novel perspective on two challenging tasks: 1) hierarchical classification via label embeddings and 2) taxonomy extension of hyperbolic representations. To address the regression problem we consider previous methods as well as proposing two novel approaches that are computationally more advantageous: a parametric deep learning model that is informed by the geodesics of the target space and a non-parametric kernel-method for which we also prove excess risk bounds. Our experiments show that the strategy of leveraging the hyperbolic geometry is promising. In particular, in the taxonomy expansion setting, we find that the hyperbolic-based estimators significantly outperform methods performing regression in the ambient Euclidean space.

Single-view depth estimation is a challenging problem in computer vision. Existing convolutional neural networks often struggle to effectively integrate multi-scale information while accounting for camera-specific parameters, limiting their accuracy and generalization capability. This paper introduces Camera-Aware Multi-Scale Convolutions (CAM-Convs), a novel convolutional layer that explicitly incorporates camera intrinsic parameters into the multi-scale feature extraction process. CAM-Convs utilize a set of parallel convolutional branches with varying kernel sizes, each modulated by camera parameters to adapt to different scales and perspectives. We demonstrate that CAM-Convs enhance the network's ability to capture fine-grained details and global context relevant to depth estimation. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including NYU Depth V2 and KITTI, show that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing single-view depth estimation techniques. Specifically, CAM-Convs improve depth accuracy by effectively integrating camera-aware features, demonstrating the importance of considering camera specifics in single-view depth prediction. This approach offers a promising direction for advancing depth estimation and other vision tasks that benefit from camera parameter awareness. Keywords: Depth Estimation, Convolutional Neural Networks, Multi-Scale Convolutions, Camera Parameters, Computer Vision.

This paper addresses the need for standardized documentation of machine learning models, focusing on the development and implementation of 'Model Cards' as a novel approach for model reporting. Model Cards aim to provide a transparent, concise summary of a model’s purpose, limitations, intended use, and performance metrics. Methods/Approach: We introduce the concept of Model Cards and outline a structured framework for their creation. The framework includes essential information about the model such as datasets used for training, evaluation metrics, ethical considerations, and potential biases. The research evaluates the framework through case studies involving various AI models, including image classifiers and natural language processing systems. Results/Findings: Our findings demonstrate that Model Cards significantly enhance the clarity and accessibility of model information for diverse stakeholders, facilitating better understanding and trust in AI systems. The comparative study reveals that models documented with Model Cards exhibit improved stakeholder satisfaction and informed decision-making compared to those without. Conclusion/Implications: Model Cards represent a critical advancement in model transparency, offering a standardized approach to model reporting that can be adopted across various AI domains. This research contributes to the broader discussion on responsible AI development, suggesting that adopting Model Cards can address the challenges of bias, ethical use, and misinterpretation of AI model outputs. Future applications may extend to privacy-sensitive domains, ensuring responsible deployment and governance of AI technologies. Keywords: Model Cards, model transparency, documentation framework, AI ethics, machine learning models, responsible AI, model reporting.

Mục tiêu: Khảo sát phổ vi khuẩn gây nhiễm trùng bàn chân ở người đái tháo đường, phân theo mức độ nhiễm trùng hoặc bệnh động mạch ngoại biên hay viêm xương và xác định mức độ đề kháng kháng sinh thông dụng. Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang trên 50 mẫu bệnh phẩm được lấy chuẩn từ sang thương bàn chân nhiễm trùng ở người bệnh đái tháo đường có kết quả cấy. Định danh vi khuẩn bằng bằng phương pháp thường quy hoặc hệ thống Vitek 2 tự động. Xác định tính nhạy cảm kháng sinh bằng phương pháp khuếch tán đĩa thạch và MIC/E-test. Kết quả: Có 63 loại vi khuẩn được phân lập. Nhiễm khuẩn Gr- (66,7%) gặp nhiều gấp hai lần khuẩn Gr+ (31,7%) và phần lớn nhiễm đơn khuẩn (74%). Các vi khuẩn thường gặp là E. coli (20,6%), Proteus spp. (19%), S. aureus (19%), K. pneumoniae (14,3%) và hiếm gặp trực khuẩn Gr- không lên men. Mức độ nhiễm trùng càng nặng thì tác nhân Gr- gặp càng nhiều, nhưng phổ vi khuẩn không khác nhau giữa nhóm viêm xương và không viêm xương, giữa nhóm có bệnh động mạch ngoại biên và không bệnh động mạch ngoại biên. S.aureus kháng rất cao với clindamycin (83%), ciprofloxacin (75%), vẫn còn nhạy với tobramycine (92%), TMP/SMZ (80%) và vancomycine (67%). Tỉ lệ nhiễm MRSA lên đến 75% trong số các trường hợp nhiễm S.aureus Trực khuẩn Gr- thường gặp còn nhạy với ampicillin nhưng với amoxcillin/clavulanic chỉ còn 67%, với aminoglycoside hay TMP/SMZ chỉ nhạy khoảng 70%, nhạy imipenem 100%. Vi khuẩn Gr- đề kháng cephalosporin thế hệ 3 rất thay đổi (30 - 50%). E. coli kháng ciprofloxacin (75%) nhưng Proteus spp. hay K.pneumonia vẫn nhạy (75%). Các khuẩn Gr- tiết ESBL chiếm 21%. Kết luận: Lựa chọn kết hợp kháng sinh nên dựa vào mức độ nhiễm trùng hơn là có viêm xương hay bệnh động mạch ngoại biên. Không dùng clindamycin để điều trị S.aureus , khuyến cáo dùng vancomycin/linezolide do tỉ lệ nhiễm MRSA quá cao. Cân nhắc các kháng sinh khác ngoài imipenem đối với Gr âm vì tỉ lệ kháng thuốc rất thay đổi.

Cá đốm (Mugil cephalus Linnaeus, 1758) là một loài cá biển phổ biến ở vùng biển Đông Nam Á, bao gồm Đầm Ô Loan, tỉnh Phú Yên. Cá đốm có đặc tính dinh dưỡng quan trọng, cung cấp nguồn thực phẩm giàu protein và omega-3 cho con người. Cá đốm là một loài cá đa dạng, có thể sống ở các môi trường nước khác nhau, từ nước mặn đến nước lợ. Chúng có thể phát triển đến kích thước lớn, với trọng lượng tối đa lên đến 20 kg. Cá đốm là nguồn thực phẩm quan trọng cho nhiều cộng đồng dân cư ở vùng biển Phú Yên. Chúng được đánh bắt bằng các phương pháp truyền thống, như lưới và câu cá. Cá đốm cũng được nuôi trồng trên quy mô nhỏ, nhằm cung cấp nguồn thực phẩm ổn định và giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực đến môi trường. Cá đốm chứa nhiều chất dinh dưỡng có lợi cho sức khỏe con người, bao gồm protein, omega-3, và các khoáng chất như canxi, sắt, và vitamin D. Chúng cũng chứa các chất chống oxy hóa giúp bảo vệ cơ thể khỏi các tác động tiêu cực của các gốc tự do. Tuy nhiên, cá đốm cũng có thể chứa các chất độc hại như thủy ngân và cadmium, đặc biệt là ở các khu vực bị ô nhiễm môi trường. Do đó, việc đánh bắt và tiêu thụ cá đốm cần được thực hiện một cách cẩn thận và an toàn. Tổng kết, cá đốm là một loài cá biển đa dạng và quan trọng, cung cấp nguồn thực phẩm giàu dinh dưỡng cho con người. Tuy nhiên, cần phải thực hiện các biện pháp bảo vệ môi trường và đảm bảo an toàn khi đánh bắt và tiêu thụ cá đốm.

This paper introduces Bayesian Attention Belief Networks (BABNs), a novel probabilistic framework designed to enhance interpretability and robustness in attention-based neural networks. The objective of this research is to address the limitations of traditional attention mechanisms, which often lack uncertainty quantification and are prone to overfitting in complex tasks. To achieve this, we propose a Bayesian approach that integrates attention mechanisms with probabilistic graphical models, enabling the network to model uncertainty in attention weights and improve generalization. Our method leverages variational inference for efficient training and employs a hierarchical structure to capture dependencies between attention layers. Experimental results on benchmark datasets in natural language processing and computer vision demonstrate that BABNs outperform conventional attention models in terms of predictive accuracy and uncertainty estimation. Furthermore, the proposed framework provides interpretable attention distributions, offering insights into model decision-making processes. The findings highlight the potential of BABNs for applications requiring reliable and explainable AI, such as medical diagnosis and autonomous systems. This work contributes to the growing field of probabilistic deep learning by bridging the gap between attention mechanisms and Bayesian inference, paving the way for more trustworthy and adaptive AI systems. **Keywords**: Bayesian networks, attention mechanisms, uncertainty quantification, probabilistic deep learning, interpretable AI.

The paper addresses the growing need for efficient and real-time object detection in applications such as autonomous vehicles and robotics. Traditional object detection relies heavily on processing full LiDAR scans, which can lead to latency and inefficiencies. This research presents a novel approach to detect objects from streaming LiDAR packets, enhancing both speed and accuracy. Methods/Approach: We introduce StrObe, a state-of-the-art system designed to perform object detection directly on streaming data from LiDAR sensors. StrObe leverages advanced algorithms and a sophisticated data-processing pipeline to incrementally analyze LiDAR packets, detecting objects without waiting for a full scan completion. Our approach includes a robust detection framework capable of handling high-speed data streams while maintaining low computational overhead. Results/Findings: The findings demonstrate that StrObe significantly reduces detection latency compared to traditional methods by processing data as it arrives. In comparative tests, StrObe outperformed existing systems in both detection speed and accuracy, particularly in dynamic and high-speed scenarios. The system's ability to operate in real-time makes it highly suitable for applications demanding rapid response times. Conclusion/Implications: StrObe represents a significant advancement in the field of object detection using LiDAR technology. Its capability to process streaming data in real-time provides critical improvements in applications such as autonomous navigation and robotic control. The flexibility and efficiency of StrObe's architecture promise potential applications beyond autonomous vehicles, including surveillance, mapping, and disaster response scenarios. By enabling faster and more precise object detection, StrObe contributes to the ongoing development of smarter, more responsive technologies in various sectors. Bằng cách kết hợp IoT với thương mại điện tử, các doanh nghiệp nông nghiệp có thể theo dõi và quản lý chuỗi cung ứng một cách hiệu quả hơn. Điều này bao gồm việc theo dõi tình trạng hàng hóa, quản lý nhiệt độ và độ ẩm, cũng như giám sát chất lượng sản phẩm. Ứng dụng IoT trong thương mại điện tử nông sản cũng giúp tăng cường khả năng dự đoán và ngăn chặn các vấn đề có thể xảy ra trong quá trình sản xuất và phân phối. Điều này có thể giúp giảm thiểu tổn thất và tăng cường hiệu suất sản xuất. Hơn nữa, việc sử dụng IoT trong thương mại điện tử nông sản cũng giúp tăng cường khả năng tương tác với khách hàng. Các doanh nghiệp nông nghiệp có thể cung cấp thông tin chi tiết về sản phẩm và quy trình sản xuất, giúp khách hàng hiểu rõ hơn về sản phẩm và tăng cường lòng tin. Tóm lại, ứng dụng IoT trong thương mại điện tử nông sản là một bước tiến quan trọng trong việc hướng đến số hóa và tăng cường hiệu suất trong toàn bộ quy trình sản xuất và phân phối nông sản.

Label Propagation (LPA) and Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCN) are both message passing algorithms on graphs. Both solve the task of node classification but LPA propagates node label information across the edges of the graph, while GCN propagates and transforms node feature information. However, while conceptually similar, theoretical relation between LPA and GCN has not yet been investigated. Here we study the relationship between LPA and GCN in terms of two aspects: (1) feature/label smoothing where we analyze how the feature/label of one node is spread over its neighbors; And, (2) feature/label influence of how much the initial feature/label of one node influences the final feature/label of another node. Based on our theoretical analysis, we propose an end-to-end model that unifies GCN and LPA for node classification. In our unified model, edge weights are learnable, and the LPA serves as regularization to assist the GCN in learning proper edge weights that lead to improved classification performance. Our model can also be seen as learning attention weights based on node labels, which is more task-oriented than existing feature-based attention models. In a number of experiments on real-world graphs, our model shows superiority over state-of-the-art GCN-based methods in terms of node classification accuracy.

Bài báo trình bày các kết quả tính toán sơ bộ về thủy nhiệt cho lò phản ứng mô đun nhỏ (SMR - Small modular reactor) với công suất nhiệt 200 MW dựa trên công nghệ lò phản ứng ACPR50S (Advanced customer-friendly practicable reliable 50 MWe compact SMR). Các thông số cơ bản và an toàn thủy nhiệt được đánh giá bao gồm lưu lượng chất tải nhiệt qua vùng hoạt, nhiệt độ nhiên liệu và vỏ bọc nhằm đảm bảo khả năng vận hành của lò phản ứng trong điều kiện giới hạn an toàn. Cấu hình SMR được mô phỏng bằng chương trình RELAP5 và thực hiện tính toán trong khoảng 500 giây ở trạng thái dừng. Nhiệt độ của chất tải nhiệt dọc theo chiều cao của vùng hoạt tại lối vào và lối ra có độ lệch nhỏ (1,7%) so với giá trị tham khảo. Về khía cạnh an toàn, tỷ số thông lượng nhiệt tại điểm khởi phát sôi nhân (DNBR - Departure from nucleate boiling ratio) cũng được ước lượng dọc theo kênh nhiên liệu trung bình và kênh nóng nhất trong vùng hoạt ở trạng thái hoạt động ổn định. Kết quả từ nghiên cứu này sẽ được tiếp tục sử dụng cho tính toán chuyển tiếp và phân tích sự cố cho SMR.

The rapid advancement of Natural Language Processing (NLP) has been driven by large-scale models trained on extensive computational resources. However, the need for efficient, resource-constrained models remains critical for practical applications. This paper introduces *Small-Bench NLP*, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of NLP models trained on a single GPU with limited computational resources. The objective is to address the gap in benchmarking tools tailored for small-scale models, enabling researchers and practitioners to assess their effectiveness in real-world scenarios. We propose a comprehensive evaluation framework that includes diverse NLP tasks such as text classification, sentiment analysis, and named entity recognition. The benchmark leverages lightweight architectures, including distilled transformers and compact neural networks, optimized for single-GPU training. Our approach emphasizes balancing model efficiency with task performance, ensuring practicality for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Experimental results demonstrate that small-scale models trained using *Small-Bench NLP* achieve competitive performance compared to larger counterparts, with significant reductions in computational overhead. The benchmark also highlights the trade-offs between model size, training time, and accuracy, providing valuable insights for optimizing NLP systems. This research contributes a standardized tool for evaluating small-scale NLP models, fostering innovation in efficient AI development. The implications extend to applications in edge computing, mobile devices, and low-resource settings, where computational efficiency is paramount. Keywords: NLP, single-GPU training, lightweight models, benchmarking, resource efficiency.

This paper introduces Portrait Image Embedding (PIE), a novel approach for semantic control in portrait image manipulation. PIE leverages a pre-trained facial recognition model to extract a compact embedding vector that captures crucial semantic attributes from a portrait image, such as pose, expression, and lighting. These embeddings are then utilized within a generative adversarial network (GAN) framework to enable fine-grained control over image synthesis and editing. We demonstrate that PIE allows for intuitive manipulation of portrait attributes, achieving state-of-the-art performance in tasks like pose editing, expression transfer, and relighting. Experimental results, including quantitative metrics and qualitative evaluations, showcase the superiority of PIE compared to existing methods in terms of both realism and control accuracy. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement in portrait image manipulation, with potential applications in virtual avatars, personalized content creation, and image editing tools. Keywords: Portrait Image Embedding, GAN, Semantic Control, Image Manipulation, Facial Attributes.

Most of the existing deep reinforcement learning (RL) approaches for session-based recommendations either rely on costly online interactions with real users, or rely on potentially biased rule-based or data-driven user-behavior models for learning. In this work, we instead focus on learning recommendation policies in the pure batch or offline setting, i.e. learning policies solely from offline historical interaction logs or batch data generated from an unknown and sub-optimal behavior policy, without further access to data from the real-world or user-behavior models. We propose BCD4Rec: Batch-Constrained Distributional RL for Session-based Recommendations. BCD4Rec builds upon the recent advances in batch (offline) RL and distributional RL to learn from offline logs while dealing with the intrinsically stochastic nature of rewards from the users due to varied latent interest preferences (environments). We demonstrate that BCD4Rec significantly improves upon the behavior policy as well as strong RL and non-RL baselines in the batch setting in terms of standard performance metrics like Click Through Rates or Buy Rates. Other useful properties of BCD4Rec include: i. recommending items from the correct latent categories indicating better value estimates despite large action space (of the order of number of items), and ii. overcoming popularity bias in clicked or bought items typically present in the offline logs.

This paper addresses the challenge of generating compact and efficient representations of 3D point clouds, a critical task in applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. We propose a novel framework leveraging Adversarial Autoencoders (AAEs) to learn low-dimensional, semantically rich embeddings of 3D point cloud data. The proposed approach combines the reconstruction capabilities of autoencoders with the adversarial training mechanism of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to ensure that the learned representations are both compact and robust. Our method is evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of reconstruction accuracy and representation quality compared to traditional autoencoders and other state-of-the-art techniques. The results highlight the effectiveness of adversarial training in capturing fine-grained geometric details while maintaining computational efficiency. This work contributes to advancing 3D data processing by providing a scalable and lightweight solution for point cloud representation, with potential applications in real-time systems and resource-constrained environments. **Keywords**: Adversarial Autoencoders, 3D Point Clouds, Compact Representations, Generative Adversarial Networks, 3D Reconstruction.

This paper introduces GLEAN, a novel generative latent bank approach for large-factor image super-resolution. The objective is to develop an efficient and effective method for enhancing low-resolution images by a significant factor, while maintaining image quality and realism. Our approach utilizes a generative model to learn a latent space of high-resolution images, which is then used to guide the super-resolution process. The proposed method leverages a combination of generative adversarial networks and latent variable models to produce high-quality, high-resolution images. Experimental results demonstrate that GLEAN outperforms state-of-the-art super-resolution methods, particularly for large upscaling factors. The key findings include significant improvements in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM), as well as visually pleasing results. The contributions of this research lie in its ability to generate high-quality images at large scaling factors, making it a valuable tool for applications such as image and video enhancement, surveillance, and medical imaging. Key keywords: image super-resolution, generative models, latent variable models, GANs, computer vision.

This paper introduces Ensemble Squared, a novel meta-AutoML system designed to optimize and enhance the performance of automated machine learning pipelines. The primary objective is to address the limitations of individual AutoML systems by leveraging the strengths of multiple AutoML solutions through a sophisticated ensemble strategy. Ensemble Squared employs a two-layered approach: first, it independently executes several state-of-the-art AutoML systems on a given dataset; second, it intelligently combines the resulting pipelines using a learned weighting scheme based on performance metrics and diversity measures. Experiments on a diverse set of benchmark datasets demonstrate that Ensemble Squared consistently outperforms individual AutoML systems, achieving significant improvements in predictive accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, the system's adaptive weighting mechanism allows it to dynamically adjust to the characteristics of different datasets, ensuring optimal performance across a range of problem domains. This research contributes a practical and effective meta-learning framework for AutoML, significantly reducing the need for manual intervention in model selection and hyperparameter tuning, and facilitating broader adoption of machine learning in real-world applications. Keywords: AutoML, Meta-Learning, Ensemble Learning, Machine Learning, Model Selection, Hyperparameter Optimization.

This paper explores the relationship between entropy and policy optimization in reinforcement learning, with the objective of improving the efficiency and stability of policy optimization algorithms. We employ a novel approach that incorporates entropy regularization into the policy optimization process, utilizing a modified trust region method to balance exploration and exploitation. Our results show that entropy regularization can significantly enhance the performance of policy optimization, leading to more robust and adaptive policies. Key findings include improved convergence rates and increased resilience to environmental changes. The conclusions drawn from this research highlight the importance of entropy in policy optimization and demonstrate the potential for entropy-based methods to improve the overall performance of reinforcement learning systems. This study contributes to the field of reinforcement learning by providing new insights into the role of entropy in policy optimization, with potential applications in areas such as robotics, game playing, and autonomous systems, and is relevant to keywords including reinforcement learning, policy optimization, entropy regularization, and trust region methods.

Analog computing hardwares, such as Processing-in-memory (PIM) accelerators, have gradually received more attention for accelerating the neural network computations. However, PIM accelerators often suffer from intrinsic noise in the physical components, making it challenging for neural network models to achieve the same performance as on the digital hardware. Previous works in mitigating intrinsic noise assumed the knowledge of the noise model, and retraining the neural networks accordingly was required. In this paper, we propose a noise-agnostic method to achieve robust neural network performance against any noise setting. Our key observation is that the degradation of performance is due to the distribution shifts in network activations, which are caused by the noise. To properly track the shifts and calibrate the biased distributions, we propose a "noise-aware" batch normalization layer, which is able to align the distributions of the activations under variational noise inherent in the analog environments. Our method is simple, easy to implement, general to various noise settings, and does not need to retrain the models. We conduct experiments on several tasks in computer vision, including classification, object detection and semantic segmentation. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, achieving robust performance under a wide range of noise settings, more reliable than existing methods. We believe that our simple yet general method can facilitate the adoption of analog computing devices for neural networks.

Kết quả cho thấy tảo phát triển tốt nhất ở thí nghiệm NO 3- = 1,2mg/L; PO 43- = 0,5mg/L đạt số lượng cực đại ( 8,93  2,5)x106 tb/mL và có chu kỳ phát triển ổn định ở thí nghiệm NO 3- = 1,2mg/L; PO 43- = 0,25mg/L kéo dài 2 1 ngày nuôi cấy. Tuy nhiên, thống kê (Two -way ANOVA) cho thấy không có sự khác biệt về tăng trưởng và chu kỳ sống giữa các lô thí nghiệm (P ≥ 0.05) có hàm lượng NO 3-, PO 43-khác nhau.

Nghiên cứu mới đây tập trung vào ảnh hưởng của bốc hơi nước ngầm đến quá trình bổ cập tự nhiên cho các thấu kính nước nhạt, đặc biệt tại các dải cồn ven biển. Bốc hơi nước ngầm, một yếu tố thường bị bỏ qua, có thể đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc giảm lượng nước ngọt thấm vào các tầng chứa nước. Quá trình này đặc biệt đáng chú ý ở các khu vực có mực nước ngầm nông và nhiệt độ cao, làm tăng tốc độ bốc hơi. Các nhà khoa học đã sử dụng mô hình toán học và dữ liệu thực địa để định lượng tác động của bốc hơi nước ngầm, từ đó đưa ra các ước tính chính xác hơn về lượng nước thực tế bổ cập cho các thấu kính nước nhạt. Kết quả cho thấy, ở một số khu vực, bốc hơi nước ngầm có thể làm giảm đáng kể lượng nước ngọt sẵn có, gây ảnh hưởng tiêu cực đến nguồn cung cấp nước cho sinh hoạt và sản xuất nông nghiệp. Việc hiểu rõ và tính toán chính xác ảnh hưởng này là rất quan trọng để quản lý bền vững tài nguyên nước, đặc biệt trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu và mực nước biển dâng.

Uncertainty quantification (UQ) in classification tasks is critical for improving the reliability and interpretability of machine learning models, particularly in high-stakes applications such as healthcare and autonomous systems. This study addresses the challenge of accurately estimating predictive uncertainty in classification models, which is often overlooked or inadequately implemented. We propose a novel framework that integrates ensemble-based methods with advanced calibration techniques to enhance UQ in deep learning classifiers. Our approach leverages Monte Carlo Dropout and temperature scaling to improve uncertainty estimates while maintaining model performance. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrate that our method significantly reduces uncertainty estimation errors compared to existing approaches. Additionally, we introduce a new metric, *Uncertainty Calibration Error (UCE)*, to evaluate the reliability of uncertainty estimates. Results show that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in both classification accuracy and uncertainty calibration. The proposed method not only advances the field of UQ but also provides practical insights for deploying trustworthy AI systems in real-world scenarios. Key contributions include a robust framework for uncertainty-aware classification, a novel evaluation metric, and empirical validation across diverse datasets. This work has broad implications for improving the safety and reliability of AI-driven decision-making systems. **Keywords**: Uncertainty Quantification, Classification, Deep Learning, Ensemble Methods, Model Calibration, Trustworthy AI.

Vịnh Nghi Sơn, huy ện Tĩnh Gia l à nơi duy nh ất của tỉnh Thanh Hóa phát tri ển ngh ề nuôi cá b ằng lồng trên bi ển. Nghề này tuy có xu hư ớng ngày càng tăng nhưng đang b ộc lộ những nguy cơ phát tri ển thiếu bền vững. Nguyên nhân là do m ật độ ô lồng đã vượt ngư ỡng cho phép, năng su ất cá nuôi l ồng có xu hư ớng gi ảm trong nh ững năm g ần đây. Ngoài ra, ngư ời nuôi cá l ồng đang ph ải đối mặt với nhiều khó khăn như thi ếu vốn cho s ản xuất, mua gi ống xa, nguồn thức ăn chưa ổn định, môi trư ờng nuôi ngày càng ô nhi ễm và th ị trường tiêu th ụ còn b ấp bênh. B ởi vậy, nghiên c ứu đã sử dụng phương pháp phân t ổ thống kê, phương pháp so sánh, phân tích nh ằm làm rõ th ực trạng và các nh ân tố ảnh hư ởng, từ đó đề xuất các gi ải pháp nh ằm phát tri ển ngh ề nuôi cá l ồng ở vịnh Nghi Sơn đ ể khai thác được tiềm năng v ốn có c ủa vùng.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have exhibited significant potential in diverse applications, particularly in generating high-quality synthetic data. However, traditional GAN architectures often suffer from issues like mode collapse and instability during training. This paper introduces a novel approach using reparameterized sampling to enhance the performance and stability of GANs. Methods/Approach: Our proposed method leverages a reparameterization technique within the sampling process of GANs, aiming to improve convergence and diversity of generated outputs. By introducing a reparameterized sampling layer, we adaptively adjust the latent space exploration, thereby facilitating a more robust learning process. We test the proposed method on various datasets, evaluating its impact on GAN performance metrics. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that the reparameterized sampling approach significantly enhances the stability and quality of GAN-generated samples as compared to conventional GAN setups. We observe notable improvements in reducing mode collapse and achieving higher fidelity in outputs. Comparative analysis with existing state-of-the-art GAN variants highlights our method's superiority in generating more diverse and realistic datasets. Conclusion/Implications: The integration of reparameterized sampling in GANs presents a compelling advancement in addressing common challenges associated with generative models. This enhancement not only contributes to more stable training processes but also opens avenues for broader applications in fields requiring high-quality synthetic data generation, such as image synthesis, data augmentation, and beyond. The adoption of this technique could significantly influence future developments in generative models and their applications. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, GANs, Reparameterized Sampling, Stability, Mode Collapse, Synthetic Data Generation, Machine Learning.

Nghiên cứu về chỉ tiêu sinh lý và sinh hóa máu của trâu nuôi tại huyện Cẩm Thủy, tỉnh Thanh Hóa đã chỉ ra những đặc điểm quan trọng liên quan đến sức khỏe và khả năng sinh sản của loài vật này. Các chỉ tiêu sinh lý như nhịp tim, nhịp thở và nhiệt độ cơ thể được đo lường và phân tích, cho thấy sự ổn định trong điều kiện nuôi dưỡng hiện tại. Bên cạnh đó, các chỉ tiêu sinh hóa máu như hàm lượng protein, glucose, cholesterol và các enzyme gan cũng được đánh giá, giúp xác định tình trạng dinh dưỡng và sức khỏe tổng thể của trâu. Kết quả nghiên cứu không chỉ cung cấp thông tin quý giá cho việc chăm sóc và quản lý trâu nuôi mà còn góp phần vào việc phát triển chăn nuôi bền vững tại địa phương. Những phát hiện này có thể làm cơ sở cho các chương trình cải thiện giống và nâng cao năng suất chăn nuôi trong tương lai.

Tích hợp thuật toán Jellyfish Search với phương pháp phân tử hữu hạn nhằm tối ưu hóa quy trình tìm kiếm và xử lý dữ liệu là một bước tiến quan trọng trong lĩnh vực công nghệ thông tin. Thuật toán Jellyfish Search nổi bật với khả năng tìm kiếm hiệu quả trong không gian lớn, trong khi phương pháp phân tử hữu hạn cung cấp một cách tiếp cận chính xác để mô phỏng và phân tích các hệ thống phức tạp. Sự kết hợp này không chỉ nâng cao hiệu suất tìm kiếm mà còn cải thiện độ chính xác của các kết quả thu được. Việc áp dụng hai phương pháp này trong các bài toán thực tiễn có thể mang lại những giải pháp tối ưu hơn, giúp tiết kiệm thời gian và tài nguyên trong quá trình xử lý thông tin. Nghiên cứu này mở ra hướng đi mới cho các ứng dụng trong lĩnh vực trí tuệ nhân tạo và khai thác dữ liệu, đồng thời khẳng định vai trò quan trọng của việc kết hợp các phương pháp khác nhau để giải quyết các thách thức hiện tại.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc đánh giá mức độ ảnh hưởng của các kỹ năng nghề nghiệp đến khả năng được tuyển dụng của sinh viên, dựa trên cảm nhận chủ quan của chính họ. Khảo sát được thực hiện nhằm thu thập thông tin về những kỹ năng mà sinh viên tự đánh giá là quan trọng và có tác động lớn nhất đến cơ hội việc làm sau khi tốt nghiệp. Kết quả cho thấy, sinh viên có xu hướng đánh giá cao các kỹ năng mềm như giao tiếp, làm việc nhóm, giải quyết vấn đề, tư duy phản biện, bên cạnh các kỹ năng chuyên môn được đào tạo tại trường. Mức độ tự tin vào các kỹ năng này có tương quan chặt chẽ với kỳ vọng về khả năng tìm được việc làm phù hợp. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra sự khác biệt trong nhận thức về tầm quan trọng của kỹ năng giữa các nhóm sinh viên thuộc các ngành học khác nhau. Điều này gợi ý về sự cần thiết của việc điều chỉnh chương trình đào tạo để đáp ứng tốt hơn nhu cầu thực tế của thị trường lao động và nâng cao khả năng cạnh tranh của sinh viên.

Nghiên cứu về hiệu quả sử dụng đạm của cây lúa cạn vùng Tây Bắc đã chỉ ra tầm quan trọng của việc tối ưu hóa lượng đạm trong quá trình canh tác. Các tác giả đã tiến hành thí nghiệm để đánh giá ảnh hưởng của các mức đạm khác nhau đến năng suất và chất lượng lúa cạn. Kết quả cho thấy, việc áp dụng đạm hợp lý không chỉ giúp tăng năng suất mà còn cải thiện chất lượng hạt lúa, đồng thời giảm thiểu ô nhiễm môi trường do dư thừa phân bón. Nghiên cứu cũng nhấn mạnh sự cần thiết phải điều chỉnh lượng đạm theo từng giai đoạn sinh trưởng của cây lúa để đạt hiệu quả cao nhất. Những phát hiện này có thể giúp nông dân vùng Tây Bắc nâng cao năng suất cây trồng, góp phần phát triển bền vững nông nghiệp tại địa phương.

This paper introduces a novel game-theoretic optimization algorithm based on the Nikaido-Isoda function, leveraging gradient information to enhance convergence and stability. Traditional game-theoretic solvers often struggle with high-dimensional strategy spaces and complex payoff structures. Our approach addresses these limitations by incorporating gradient-based updates derived from the Nikaido-Isoda function, effectively guiding players towards Nash equilibria. We demonstrate the efficacy of our algorithm through a series of experiments on benchmark game problems, including congestion games and network resource allocation, achieving significant improvements in convergence speed and equilibrium quality compared to existing methods like fictitious play and gradient descent ascent. Specifically, our method exhibits superior performance in finding stable Nash equilibria in non-convex games. This work contributes a robust and efficient optimization technique applicable to various domains requiring game-theoretic solutions, such as multi-agent systems and economic modeling. **Keywords:** Game Theory, Optimization, Nikaido-Isoda Function, Nash Equilibrium, Gradient Descent, Multi-Agent Systems.

Học sinh lớp 10 cần nắm vững kiến thức về hình học, đặc biệt là các hệ thức lượng trong tam giác. Đây là một phần quan trọng trong chương trình toán học, giúp học sinh hiểu rõ về mối quan hệ giữa các cạnh và góc trong tam giác. Hệ thức lượng trong tam giác bao gồm ba công thức cơ bản: - Công thức Pythagorean (a² + b² = c²) để tính độ dài cạnh huyền của tam giác vuông. - Công thức lượng giác (sin, cos, tan) để tính góc và độ dài cạnh trong tam giác bất kỳ. - Công thức Heron để tính diện tích của tam giác. Học sinh cần nắm vững các công thức này để giải quyết các bài toán liên quan đến tam giác, từ đó mở rộng kiến thức về hình học và toán học.

The field of multiple object tracking (MOT) has witnessed advancements in detection capabilities, yet remains vulnerable to adversarial attacks aimed at disrupting tracking accuracy. This study presents the first comprehensive adversarial attack framework targeting multiple object tracking systems, challenging the assumption that robust detection alone suffices for reliable tracking. Methods/Approach: The research introduces a novel adversarial attack strategy designed to exploit vulnerabilities in MOT systems by generating perturbations that affect both detection and tracking components synchronously. The proposed method leverages gradient-based optimization to create adversarial examples, focusing on imperceptible changes to frames that lead to significant tracking errors across consecutive video clips. Results/Findings: Extensive experiments were conducted on popular benchmark datasets for multiple object tracking. The findings demonstrate that the proposed adversarial strategy significantly degrades the performance of state-of-the-art MOT algorithms, leading to decreased tracking accuracy and stability even when object detection rates remain high. Comparisons with other adversarial methods targeting detection alone underscore the increased efficacy of this comprehensive attack approach. Conclusion/Implications: This research highlights critical vulnerabilities in contemporary MOT systems, illustrating that robustness in detection is insufficient without fortified tracking processes against adversarial manipulations. The insights pave the way for future enhancements in MOT systems, advocating for integrated defense mechanisms that bolster both detection and tracking components against potential adversarial threats. Key Keywords: multiple object tracking, adversarial attack, object detection, tracking vulnerability, gradient-based optimization, defense mechanisms.

Giải pháp vận hành mạng lưới phân phối điện trung thế với sự tích hợp nguồn năng lượng phân tán đang trở thành xu hướng quan trọng trong ngành điện lực hiện đại. Với sự gia tăng của các nguồn năng lượng tái tạo như điện mặt trời và điện gió, việc quản lý hiệu quả hệ thống phân phối trung thế đòi hỏi các giải pháp công nghệ tiên tiến. Các hệ thống điều khiển thông minh, công nghệ đo lường tiên tiến và các thuật toán tối ưu hóa được áp dụng để đảm bảo sự ổn định, an toàn và hiệu quả của mạng lưới. Đồng thời, việc tích hợp các nguồn năng lượng phân tán cũng đặt ra thách thức về cân bằng tải, quản lý công suất và giảm thiểu tổn thất điện năng. Những tiến bộ trong lĩnh vực này không chỉ góp phần nâng cao chất lượng dịch vụ điện mà còn thúc đẩy quá trình chuyển đổi sang năng lượng sạch và bền vững.

This paper addresses the challenge of transferring learned policies across continuous control tasks with varying dynamics and state spaces. The objective is to develop a framework for learning state abstractions that enable efficient transfer learning in reinforcement learning (RL) settings. We propose a novel approach that leverages unsupervised learning techniques to identify low-dimensional, task-invariant representations of high-dimensional state spaces. Our method combines variational autoencoders (VAEs) with a reward-prediction auxiliary task to ensure that the learned abstractions preserve task-relevant information while discarding domain-specific details. Experiments are conducted on a suite of continuous control benchmarks, including robotic manipulation and locomotion tasks, to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Results demonstrate that our method significantly improves transfer performance compared to baseline methods, achieving higher sample efficiency and faster adaptation to new tasks. The key contribution of this work is a scalable and generalizable framework for state abstraction that bridges the gap between source and target domains in continuous control. This research has implications for real-world applications, such as robotics and autonomous systems, where transfer learning is critical for deploying RL agents in diverse environments. **Keywords**: reinforcement learning, transfer learning, state abstraction, continuous control, variational autoencoders, robotics.

This paper re-examines the relationship between the softmax function and cross-entropy loss in neural network classifiers, proposing a novel perspective that frames the classifier as a mutual information estimator. The objective is to explore how the softmax-cross-entropy combination inherently captures the mutual information between input data and class labels, offering a deeper understanding of its effectiveness in classification tasks. We present a theoretical framework that connects the optimization of cross-entropy loss to the maximization of mutual information, providing insights into the underlying principles of neural network training. To validate this perspective, we conduct experiments on benchmark datasets, comparing the performance of our mutual information-based interpretation with traditional approaches. Results demonstrate that this reinterpretation not only aligns with empirical observations but also offers a principled foundation for improving classifier design. The findings suggest that mutual information maximization can serve as a guiding principle for developing more robust and interpretable neural network models. This work contributes to the broader understanding of deep learning by bridging information theory and neural network optimization, with potential applications in enhancing model generalization and interpretability. **Keywords**: Softmax, Cross-Entropy, Mutual Information, Neural Networks, Classification, Information Theory, Deep Learning.

The objective of this paper is to address the challenge of regression with unlabeled data, exploiting semi-supervised learning techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of predictive models. Specifically, the research focuses on integrating deep kernel learning within a semi-supervised framework to enhance predictive performance through variability reduction. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel algorithm that combines semi-supervised learning with deep kernel methods, leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data. The approach prioritizes minimizing predictive variance as a metric for model optimization, allowing the system to capture uncertainties associated with unlabeled data. Our model employs Gaussian processes within the deep learning architecture to dynamically learn the kernel functions in a data-driven manner, enhancing the adaptation to the underlying data manifold. Results/Findings: Extensive experiments demonstrate that our semi-supervised deep kernel learning approach significantly improves regression accuracy over traditional supervised methods. The incorporation of unlabeled data through variance minimization leads to reduced prediction errors and better generalization on unseen datasets. Comparative analyses indicate that our method outperforms existing semi-supervised and supervised regression models in terms of both prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Conclusion/Implications: This research introduces a promising direction for regression in scenarios where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. By minimizing predictive variance, the proposed semi-supervised deep kernel learning framework not only enhances model performance but also provides a robust mechanism for uncertainty quantification. The methodology presents significant potential applications in fields where data labeling is expensive or infeasible, offering contributions to the advancement of machine learning techniques in real-world environments. Keywords: Semi-supervised learning, Deep kernel learning, Regression, Unlabeled data, Predictive variance, Gaussian processes, Model optimization.

Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has shown great potentials in automatically designing scalable network architectures for dense image predictions. However, existing NAS algorithms usually compromise on restricted search space and search on proxy task to meet the achievable computational demands. To allow as wide as possible network architectures and avoid the gap between target and proxy dataset, we propose a Densely Connected NAS (DCNAS) framework, which directly searches the optimal network structures for the multi-scale representations of visual information, over a large-scale target dataset. Specifically, by connecting cells with each other using learnable weights, we introduce a densely connected search space to cover an abundance of mainstream network designs. Moreover, by combining both path-level and channel-level sampling strategies, we design a fusion module to reduce the memory consumption of ample search space. We demonstrate that the architecture obtained from our DCNAS algorithm achieves state-of-the-art performances on public semantic image segmentation benchmarks, including 84.3% on Cityscapes, and 86.9% on PASCAL VOC 2012. Given an incomplete image without additional constraint, image inpainting natively allows for multiple solutions as long as they appear plausible. Recently, multiplesolution inpainting methods have been proposed and shown the potential of generating diverse results. However, these methods have difficulty in ensuring the quality of each solution, e.g. they produce distorted structure and/or blurry texture. We propose a two-stage model for diverse inpainting, where the first stage generates multiple coarse results each of which has a different structure, and the second stage refines each coarse result separately by augmenting texture. The proposed model is inspired by the hierarchical vector quantized variational auto-encoder (VQ-VAE), whose hierarchical architecture isentangles structural and textural information. In addition, the vector quantization in VQVAE enables autoregressive modeling of the discrete distribution over the structural information. Sampling from the distribution can easily generate diverse and high-quality structures, making up the first stage of our model. In the second stage, we propose a structural attention module inside the texture generation network, where the module utilizes the structural information to capture distant correlations. We further reuse the VQ-VAE to calculate two feature losses, which help improve structure coherence and texture realism, respectively. Experimental results on CelebA-HQ, Places2, and ImageNet datasets show that our method not only enhances the diversity of the inpainting solutions but also improves the visual quality of the generated multiple images. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/USTC-JialunPeng/Diverse-Structure-Inpainting.

Learning data representations that are useful for various downstream tasks is a cornerstone of artificial intelligence. While existing methods are typically evaluated on downstream tasks such as classification or generative image quality, we propose to assess representations through their usefulness in downstream control tasks, such as reaching or pushing objects. By training over 10,000 reinforcement learning policies, we extensively evaluate to what extent different representation properties affect out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization. Finally, we demonstrate zero-shot transfer of these policies from simulation to the real world, without any domain randomization or fine-tuning. This paper aims to establish the first systematic characterization of the usefulness of learned representations for real-world OOD downstream tasks.

Bằng cách điều chỉnh tần số cộng hưởng phù hợp với khoảng cách và tốc độ di chuyển của xe, hệ thống có thể tối ưu hóa năng lượng truyền tải, giảm thiểu tổn thất và đảm bảo an toàn. This paper explores the application of multimodal image captioning for enhanced marketing analysis. The objective is to automatically generate descriptive captions from product images, incorporating both visual and textual data to gain deeper insights into consumer perception and market trends. We propose a novel deep learning architecture that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image feature extraction with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and attention mechanisms for caption generation. The model is trained on a large dataset of product images and associated marketing text, enabling it to produce captions that accurately reflect the visual content and relevant marketing context. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms existing image captioning techniques in terms of caption quality, relevance, and informativeness, as measured by BLEU, ROUGE, and CIDEr scores. Furthermore, we show how the generated captions can be used to extract key marketing attributes, perform sentiment analysis, and identify emerging trends. This research contributes a valuable tool for marketers to efficiently analyze visual content, understand consumer preferences, and optimize marketing strategies. Keywords: Multimodal Image Captioning, Marketing Analysis, Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, Attention Mechanisms, Sentiment Analysis.

Low-light imaging poses significant challenges for computer vision systems and everyday photography, often resulting in noisy, low-contrast images that obscure critical details. This paper presents "Kindling the Darkness," a practical and efficient low-light image enhancement system designed to improve image quality while maintaining real-time performance. Our approach leverages a hybrid deep learning model that combines attention mechanisms with adaptive image processing techniques to selectively enhance brightness, suppress noise, and restore color fidelity. The system requires minimal computational resources and is suitable for deployment on consumer devices and embedded platforms. Experimental evaluations on multiple public low-light image datasets demonstrate substantial improvements in visual clarity, peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and structural similarity index (SSIM) over existing state-of-the-art methods. User studies further confirm the system’s effectiveness in visual enhancement and usability. The proposed method offers a robust solution for applications in mobile photography, surveillance, and autonomous navigation under challenging lighting conditions. Key innovations include dynamic parameter adjustment based on scene characteristics and an end-to-end trainable framework. Our findings highlight the practical value of integrating advanced deep learning techniques into real-world low-light image enhancement systems. Keywords: low-light image enhancement, deep learning, attention mechanism, image restoration, real-time processing, image quality, computer vision.

The paper addresses the challenge of enhancing session-based recommendation systems by leveraging reinforcement learning techniques, specifically focusing on improving the quality and efficiency of recommendations in online platforms where user interactions occur in sessions. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach using Batch-Constrained Distributional Reinforcement Learning (BC-DRL) to model the inherent uncertainties in session-based recommendations. Our approach integrates distributional reinforcement learning with a batch-constrained framework to effectively manage exploration and exploitation, ensuring that the recommendations are both diverse and relevant to the user's immediate context. Results/Findings: The proposed BC-DRL approach demonstrates significant improvements in recommendation accuracy and user satisfaction metrics compared to traditional reinforcement learning methods and standard recommendation algorithms. Our experimental results, conducted on benchmark session-based recommendation datasets, reveal that BC-DRL enhances prediction quality and system efficiency, outperforming baseline methods in both precision and recall. Conclusion/Implications: Our research introduces a robust framework for session-based recommendation systems, contributing to the field by optimizing the recommendation process through advanced reinforcement learning techniques. The findings imply potential applications in personalized e-commerce, content streaming platforms, and other online services, where session-based interactions are prevalent. This work paves the way for further exploration of distributional approaches in recommendation systems, offering a scalable solution for real-world deployment. Keywords: Session-based recommendation, Reinforcement learning, Distributional reinforcement learning, Batch-constrained, User interaction, Personalized recommendations.

This paper presents an in-depth examination of k-Nearest Neighbour (k-NN) classifiers, a fundamental algorithm in machine learning and data classification. The objective of this research is to provide a comprehensive overview of the k-NN approach, including its theoretical foundations, implementation, and applications. The methods employed in this study involve a detailed analysis of the k-NN algorithm, including distance metrics, choice of k, and handling of ties. Python examples are used to illustrate the implementation and application of k-NN classifiers. The results show that k-NN classifiers can achieve high accuracy in various classification tasks, and the choice of k and distance metric significantly impacts performance. This research contributes to the existing body of knowledge by providing a clear and concise explanation of k-NN classifiers, making it accessible to both beginners and experienced practitioners. The implications of this study are significant, as k-NN classifiers can be applied to a wide range of fields, including image classification, natural language processing, and recommender systems. Key keywords: k-Nearest Neighbour, machine learning, data classification, Python, distance metrics.

This paper introduces ST3D++, a novel approach for unsupervised domain adaptation in 3D object detection, leveraging denoised self-training to bridge the gap between synthetic and real-world data. The objective is to improve the accuracy and robustness of 3D object detectors when faced with domain shifts. Our method employs a self-training framework, where a teacher model generates pseudo-labels for unlabeled target domain data, and a student model is trained to minimize the difference between its predictions and these pseudo-labels. To address the noise in pseudo-labels, we propose a denoising mechanism that selectively filters out low-confidence predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that ST3D++ outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, achieving significant improvements in detection accuracy and domain adaptation. The key contributions of this work include the introduction of a denoising mechanism for self-training and the application of this approach to 3D object detection, highlighting the potential for unsupervised domain adaptation in this field. Our approach has important implications for real-world applications, such as autonomous driving and robotics, where domain shifts are common. Key keywords: 3D object detection, unsupervised domain adaptation, self-training, denoising, autonomous driving, robotics.

This paper presents an empirical study on graph-based approaches for semi-supervised time series classification, addressing the challenge of limited labeled data in real-world applications. Our objective is to investigate the effectiveness of graph convolutional networks (GCNs) and graph attention networks (GATs) in leveraging unlabeled data to improve classification accuracy. We propose a novel framework that integrates graph-based models with time series features, and evaluate its performance on several benchmark datasets. Our results show that the proposed approach outperforms traditional semi-supervised methods, achieving significant improvements in classification accuracy and F1-score. The study highlights the importance of graph structure in time series data and demonstrates the potential of graph-based approaches in semi-supervised learning. Our contributions include the development of a graph-based framework for time series classification, and the empirical evaluation of its effectiveness in real-world datasets. The findings of this study have implications for applications such as anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and time series forecasting, and can be extended to other domains with limited labeled data. Key keywords: semi-supervised learning, time series classification, graph convolutional networks, graph attention networks, anomaly detection.

We propose methods to train convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with both binarized weights and activations, leading to quantized models that are specifically friendly to mobile devices with limited power capacity and computation resources. Previous works on quantizing CNNs often seek to approximate the floating-point information using a set of discrete values, which we call value approximation, typically assuming the same architecture as the full-precision networks. Here we take a novel "structure approximation" view of quantization -- it is very likely that different architectures designed for low-bit networks may be better for achieving good performance. In particular, we propose a "network decomposition" strategy, termed Group-Net, in which we divide the network into groups. Thus, each full-precision group can be effectively reconstructed by aggregating a set of homogeneous binary branches. In addition, we learn effective connections among groups to improve the representation capability. Moreover, the proposed Group-Net shows strong generalization to other tasks. For instance, we extend Group-Net for accurate semantic segmentation by embedding rich context into the binary structure. Furthermore, for the first time, we apply binary neural networks to object detection. Experiments on both classification, semantic segmentation and object detection tasks demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed methods over various quantized networks in the literature. Our methods outperform the previous best binary neural networks in terms of accuracy and computation efficiency.
