Point cloud completion, a critical task in 3D vision, aims to reconstruct complete and accurate 3D shapes from partial or incomplete point cloud data. This paper introduces a novel Skip-attention Network with Hierarchical Folding (SAN-HF) to address the challenges of missing data and geometric detail preservation. The proposed method leverages a skip-attention mechanism to effectively aggregate multi-level features from the encoder to the decoder, enabling the network to capture both global structures and fine-grained details. Additionally, a hierarchical folding strategy is employed to progressively refine the point cloud, ensuring high-quality reconstruction. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SAN-HF outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of completion accuracy and visual quality. The model achieves significant improvements in Chamfer Distance and F1 score, showcasing its ability to handle complex shapes and large missing regions. This research contributes to advancing 3D reconstruction technologies, with potential applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. Key innovations include the integration of skip-attention and hierarchical folding, offering a robust and efficient solution for point cloud completion tasks. **Keywords**: Point cloud completion, 3D reconstruction, skip-attention mechanism, hierarchical folding, deep learning, 3D vision.

Quả đào Lào Cai bảo quản lạnh là một trong những loại quả phổ biến được sử dụng rộng rãi trong lĩnh vực thực phẩm. Tuy nhiên, quá trình xử lý chất chống nâu hóa có thể ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng và tuổi thọ của quả đào này. Tuy nhiên, quá trình này có thể gây ra một số tác động tiêu cực đến chất lượng và tuổi thọ của quả đào. Một số nghiên cứu đã chỉ ra rằng, quá trình xử lý chất chống nâu hóa có thể làm giảm chất lượng của quả đào Lào Cai bảo quản lạnh. Quả đào có thể trở nên mềm, nhũn và mất đi hương vị tự nhiên. Bên cạnh đó, quá trình xử lý chất chống nâu hóa cũng có thể ảnh hưởng đến tuổi thọ của quả đào. Quả đào có thể trở nên dễ bị hư hỏng và mất đi giá trị dinh dưỡng. Tổng kết lại, quá trình xử lý chất chống nâu hóa có thể ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng và tuổi thọ của quả đào Lào Cai bảo quản lạnh. We address a question answering task on real-world images that is set up as a Visual Turing Test. By combining latest advances in image representation and natural language processing, we propose Neural-Image-QA, an end-to-end formulation to this problem for which all parts are trained jointly. In contrast to previous efforts, we are facing a multi-modal problem where the language output (answer) is conditioned on visual and natural language input (image and question). Our approach Neural-Image-QA doubles the performance of the previous best approach on this problem. We provide additional insights into the problem by analyzing how much information is contained only in the language part for which we provide a new human baseline. To study human consensus, which is related to the ambiguities inherent in this challenging task, we propose two novel metrics and collect additional answers which extends the original DAQUAR dataset to DAQUAR-Consensus.

This paper introduces a novel approach for latent space manipulation in generative models, leveraging a surrogate gradient field to enable precise and interpretable control over generated outputs. The objective of this work is to address the challenge of disentangling and manipulating latent representations in high-dimensional spaces, which is critical for applications such as image synthesis, style transfer, and data augmentation. We propose a method that constructs a surrogate gradient field within the latent space, allowing for efficient traversal and modification of latent vectors while preserving semantic coherence. Our approach combines principles from differentiable optimization and geometric deep learning to ensure robustness and scalability across diverse datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of manipulation accuracy, computational efficiency, and visual quality of generated outputs. Furthermore, the surrogate gradient field enables fine-grained control over specific attributes, such as object orientation, texture, and color, without compromising the overall structure of the generated content. This research contributes a powerful tool for latent space exploration, with potential applications in creative design, data generation, and interpretable AI systems. Keywords: latent space manipulation, generative models, surrogate gradient field, interpretable AI, image synthesis.

Đặt vấn đề: Bệnh phổi tắc nghẽn mạn tính (BPTNMT) là một trong những gánh nặng bệnh tật toàn cầu, với diễn tiến thường gặp nhất là đợt cấp của bệnh thường đi kèm tình trạng nhiễm trùng. Cấy đàm giúp xác định vi khuẩn nhằm điều trị kháng sinh tối ưu cho bệnh nhân. Mục tiêu: Nghiên cứu giá trị của phương pháp cấy đàm và các yếu tố liên quan ở bệnh nhân cao tuổi vào đợt cấp BPTNMT điều trị nội trú tại khoa Nội Hô hấp của Bệnh viện Thống Nhất từ tháng 10/2019 đến hết tháng 06/2020. Phương pháp và đối tượng: Nghiên cứu tiến cứu cắt ngang mô tả trên 167 bệnh nhân ≥ 60 tuổi nhập viện vì đợt cấp BPTNMT, được khai thác tiền căn, bệnh sử, triệu chứng lâm sàng và được cấy đàm định lượng, sau đó tiến hành phân tích kết quả cấy đàm. Kết quả: Tỷ lệ cấy đàm phân lập được tác nhân vi sinh là 25,1%. Bệnh nhân đàm đổi màu có khả năng cấy đàm dương tính cao hơn nhóm còn lại (OR 2,24, KTC 95% 1,08 - 4,65, p = 0,033). Bệnh nhân có mức độ tắc nghẽn nặng và rất nặng (GOLD3 - 4) có tỷ lệ cấy dương tính cao hơn (OR 3,88, KTC 95% 1,42 - 10,59, p = 0,005). Không ghi nhận mối liên quan giữa phân nhóm nguy cơ thấp hoặc cao và tiền căn sử dụng kháng sinh với tỷ lệ cấy đàm dương tính. Kết luận: Chỉ 1/4 bệnh nhân nhập viện vì đợt cấp BPTNMT có kết quả cấy đàm dương tính. Tỷ lệ nuôi cấy đàm dương tính cao hơn ở bệnh nhân có đàm đổi màu, bệnh nhân tắc nghẽn nặng và rất nặng, trong khi phân nhóm nguy cơ và tiền căn sử dụng kháng không có mối liên quan.

This is a machine learning application paper involving big data. We present high-accuracy prediction methods of rare events in semi-structured machine log files, which are produced at high velocity and high volume by NORC's computer-assisted telephone interviewing (CATI) network for conducting surveys. We judiciously apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques and data-mining strategies to train effective learning and prediction models for classifying uncommon error messages in the log---without access to source code, updated documentation or dictionaries. In particular, our simple but effective approach of features preallocation for learning from imbalanced data coupled with naive Bayes classifiers can be conceivably generalized to supervised or semi-supervised learning and prediction methods for other critical events such as cyberattack detection.

The study addresses the challenges associated with sequence labeling tasks, which are critical in numerous natural language processing (NLP) applications such as part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition. Current models often struggle with the effective representation and prediction of long-range dependencies within sequences. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach using Embedded-State Latent Conditional Random Fields (ES-LCRFs), a sophisticated framework that combines the strengths of latent variable models and conditional random fields. Our model introduces latent states that capture implicit structure within the data, enabling a more nuanced understanding of complex dependencies. We employ a robust learning algorithm that efficiently estimates the parameters of this extended CRF model. Results/Findings: The ES-LCRF model demonstrates superior performance over traditional sequence labeling techniques, particularly in datasets with intricate and long sequence dependencies. Experimental results show significant improvements in accuracy and F1 scores compared to baseline CRFs and other contemporary models. Our method excels in scenarios where extracting latent structure is crucial, thereby outperforming in both synthetic and real-world benchmarks. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Embedded-State Latent CRFs offers a promising direction for advancing sequence labeling technologies. This research not only enhances the capability of handling complex sequential data but also paves the way for further exploration into latent variable integration within CRF frameworks. Our findings indicate potential applications in various NLP domains and open up opportunities for optimizing sequence labeling tasks in more diverse and complex environments. Keywords: sequence labeling, conditional random fields, latent variables, natural language processing, ES-LCRF, NLP, machine learning.

Entity Resolution (ER) aims to identify and link records referring to the same real-world entity across different data sources. Active learning can reduce the labeling effort required for ER, but existing approaches often incur high computational costs due to the complexity of variational inference. This paper introduces a cost-effective variational active entity resolution framework that balances accuracy and computational efficiency. We propose a novel variational inference method that leverages a combination of amortized inference and targeted sampling to approximate the posterior distribution over entity matchings. This approach significantly reduces the computational burden associated with variational inference while maintaining competitive ER performance. We evaluate our framework on several real-world datasets, demonstrating its superiority in terms of F1-score and labeling cost compared to state-of-the-art active ER methods. The results highlight the potential of our approach for scaling ER to large and complex datasets with limited labeling resources. Keywords: Entity Resolution, Active Learning, Variational Inference, Cost-Effectiveness, Data Integration.

The research addresses the challenge of efficiently training large-scale neural networks using the mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, which is notorious for its high computational and memory demands. FastMoE introduces a novel system designed to enhance the speed and resource efficiency of training in MoE architectures. Methods/Approach: FastMoE innovatively integrates lightweight adaptive routing mechanisms and optimized parallel processing techniques to distribute computation across multiple expert networks dynamically. The system leverages state-of-the-art communication protocols to minimize the overhead associated with model parallelism, thereby facilitating large-scale model training. Results/Findings: Our empirical evaluations demonstrate that FastMoE significantly reduces training time while preserving model accuracy. Compared to traditional MoE training setups, FastMoE achieves up to a 50% reduction in computational cost and memory usage on benchmark datasets. The speed improvements are consistent across different model sizes and configurations, showcasing the system's scalability and robustness. Conclusion/Implications: FastMoE offers a breakthrough in efficiently training mixture-of-experts models, making them more accessible for large-scale AI applications. This research significantly contributes to the field by enabling the deployment of sophisticated AI models in environments previously deemed resource-constrained. The system shows potential to be applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, where rapid model iteration and deployment are crucial. Key innovations in this work can pave the way for further advancements in distributed machine learning systems. Keywords: FastMoE, mixture-of-experts, neural networks, adaptive routing, model parallelism, distributed machine learning, AI efficiency.

The increasing prevalence of surveillance cameras in public and private spaces has created a pressing need for automated systems capable of detecting violent activities in real time. Violence detection is a critical challenge in computer vision, with applications in security, law enforcement, and public safety. Traditional surveillance systems rely heavily on human monitoring, which is prone to errors, fatigue, and inefficiency. This research addresses the growing demand for intelligent systems that can autonomously identify violent incidents, thereby enhancing situational awareness and response times. The primary objective of this thesis is to develop a robust and efficient violence detection system using advanced computer vision and deep learning techniques. The system aims to accurately classify violent and non-violent activities in surveillance footage, addressing challenges such as varying lighting conditions, occlusions, and diverse types of violence. By leveraging state-of-the-art models, the research seeks to improve detection accuracy while minimizing computational overhead, making it suitable for real-time applications. The proposed methodology employs a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture both spatial and temporal features from video sequences. Preprocessing techniques, including frame extraction and optical flow analysis, are utilized to enhance input data quality. The system is trained and evaluated on publicly available violence detection datasets, with performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score used to assess its effectiveness. Preliminary results demonstrate the system's ability to achieve high detection accuracy, outperforming baseline models in terms of both speed and reliability. The expected contributions of this research include a scalable violence detection framework that can be integrated into existing surveillance infrastructures, providing a proactive approach to crime prevention and public safety. In conclusion, this thesis advances the field of automated violence detection by proposing a novel, efficient, and accurate system. Future work will focus on optimizing the model for edge devices, expanding the dataset to include more diverse scenarios, and exploring multimodal approaches that incorporate audio and contextual data for enhanced performance.

Nghiên cứu áp dụng phương pháp viễn thám, xác định số liệu về tăng trưởng sinh khối, mô hình ALU, AFOLU để kiểm kê, tính toán lượng phát thải khí nhà kính và ước tính lợi ích tích lũy trong chuyển đổi đất ngập nước tỉnh Quảng Bình. Thấp nhất là huyện Tuyên Hóa có lợi ích tích lũy chỉ 2.569 tấn CO2tđ. Giải pháp chuyển đổi mục đích sử dụng đất từ đất ngập nước sang các loại hình khác theo bảng mã WF, WC, WG, WS, WO và bảo tồn, phát triển diện tích rừng được ưu tiên trong biện pháp giảm thiểu khí nhà kính, tăng hấp thụ khí CO2tđ và nâng cao trữ lượng các bon của tỉnh Quảng Bình.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving image processing techniques by developing a novel approach that integrates weighted nonlocal total variation (WNTV). Traditional image processing methods often struggle with noise reduction and edge preservation, motivating the need for more sophisticated strategies. Methods/Approach: We introduce a weighted nonlocal total variation model that leverages a novel weighting scheme to enhance its adaptability and effectiveness in capturing complex image structures. The approach employs a nonlocal means technique, which considers the similarity between distant pixels, allowing for more nuanced adjustments over traditional local methods. We also propose an efficient algorithm for optimizing the WNTV model, which integrates seamlessly into existing image processing workflows. Results/Findings: Our findings demonstrate that the WNTV model significantly outperforms conventional total variation models and other nonlocal methods in terms of both noise suppression and edge preservation. Comparative analysis with existing approaches shows that our method achieves superior performance across a variety of standard image datasets and scenarios. Quantitative metrics indicate marked improvements in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM). Conclusion/Implications: The proposed WNTV model offers a robust tool for advanced image processing tasks, with potential applications in areas such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and photography. Its ability to effectively balance noise reduction and detail retention presents a significant advancement over existing methodologies. Furthermore, the model's compatibility with modern computing environments ensures it can be widely adopted for enhancing image quality in practical applications. Keywords: Image Processing, Weighted Nonlocal Total Variation, Noise Reduction, Edge Preservation, Nonlocal Means, PSNR, SSIM.

This paper introduces SQuantizer, a novel approach that simultaneously learns both sparse and low-precision neural networks. The objective is to reduce the computational cost and memory requirements of deep neural networks while maintaining their accuracy. Our method employs a dual-optimization framework that jointly optimizes the sparsity and precision of neural network weights. The SQuantizer algorithm leverages a combination of regularization techniques and knowledge distillation to achieve state-of-the-art performance. Experimental results demonstrate that SQuantizer outperforms existing sparse and low-precision quantization methods, achieving significant reductions in model size and computational cost. The key findings include up to 90% sparsity and 4-bit precision with minimal accuracy loss. The SQuantizer approach has important implications for edge AI, real-time inference, and resource-constrained devices, enabling the deployment of accurate and efficient neural networks in a wide range of applications. Key contributions include simultaneous sparse and low-precision learning, dual-optimization framework, and state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. Relevant keywords: neural networks, sparsity, low-precision quantization, knowledge distillation, edge AI, real-time inference.

**Abstract** The generation of realistic medical time series data is essential for advancing research in healthcare analytics, disease prediction, and clinical decision support. This paper presents a novel approach for synthesizing real-valued medical time series using Recurrent Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (RCGANs). Our method leverages the temporal modeling capabilities of recurrent neural networks within the GAN framework, conditioning the generation process on patient attributes and clinical covariates to produce contextually relevant sequences. We evaluate the performance of our model on multiple benchmark medical datasets, including electrocardiogram (ECG) and intensive care unit (ICU) patient monitoring data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RCGAN architecture outperforms traditional GANs and baseline generative models in capturing complex temporal dynamics and preserving the statistical characteristics of the original time series. Furthermore, clinical experts verified the plausibility of the generated sequences. This work contributes a practical tool for data augmentation, privacy-preserving data sharing, and simulation in medical AI applications, addressing key challenges in real-world healthcare data scarcity and heterogeneity. Keywords: time series generation, generative adversarial networks, RNN, medical data, data augmentation, synthetic data.

This paper introduces PointContrast, a novel unsupervised pre-training approach for 3D point cloud understanding. The objective is to learn effective representations of 3D point clouds without relying on annotated data, addressing the challenge of scarce labeled datasets in this domain. Our method leverages a contrastive learning framework, which maximizes the agreement between different views of the same point cloud while minimizing the agreement between views of different point clouds. The approach utilizes a combination of spatial and channel-wise transformations to generate multiple views, and a neural network architecture to learn compact and informative representations. Experimental results demonstrate that PointContrast achieves state-of-the-art performance on various 3D point cloud understanding tasks, including object classification, part segmentation, and scene segmentation, outperforming existing unsupervised and supervised methods. The key findings highlight the importance of contrastive learning in capturing geometric and structural information from 3D point clouds. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and effective 3D point cloud analysis pipelines, with potential applications in fields such as robotics, autonomous driving, and computer-aided design. Key keywords: 3D point clouds, unsupervised learning, contrastive learning, representation learning, computer vision.

Deep learning models for image processing tasks often require extensive and diverse datasets to achieve robust performance. However, acquiring such datasets can be costly and time-consuming. This paper introduces *Adversarial Policy Gradient (APG)*, a novel approach for automated image augmentation that enhances the quality and diversity of training data for deep learning models. The proposed method leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically generate augmentation policies tailored to the specific characteristics of the dataset and task. By employing an adversarial framework, APG optimizes augmentation strategies to maximize model performance while minimizing overfitting. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrate that APG outperforms traditional augmentation techniques and state-of-the-art automated methods in terms of classification accuracy and generalization. The results highlight the effectiveness of APG in improving model robustness and reducing the need for extensive manual data curation. This work contributes a scalable and adaptive solution for image augmentation, with potential applications in computer vision, medical imaging, and other domains reliant on deep learning. **Keywords**: Deep learning, image augmentation, adversarial learning, reinforcement learning, policy gradient, computer vision.

Accurately predicting corn yields at the county level is crucial for informed decision-making in agriculture, impacting resource allocation, supply chain management, and economic forecasting. This paper investigates the application of deep Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models for forecasting corn yields at the county level, leveraging historical weather data, soil characteristics, and planting information. We propose a novel architecture incorporating multiple LSTM layers to capture complex temporal dependencies within agricultural datasets. Our experiments across various counties demonstrate that the deep LSTM model outperforms traditional statistical methods and simpler machine learning algorithms, achieving a significant reduction in prediction error, up to 15% improvement in Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) compared to benchmark models. These findings highlight the potential of deep learning techniques to enhance agricultural forecasting accuracy, providing valuable insights for farmers, policymakers, and agribusinesses. This approach offers a scalable and adaptable solution for yield prediction across diverse geographical regions. **Keywords:** Corn Yield Prediction, LSTM, Deep Learning, Time Series Forecasting, Agriculture, County Level.

Abstract: Medical image analysis plays a vital role in modern healthcare, facilitating accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the inherent complexity and high dimensionality of medical imaging data present significant challenges for conventional processing methods. This paper investigates the application of modern convex optimization techniques to various tasks in medical image analysis, including image segmentation, reconstruction, and denoising. We propose a unified framework that leverages advanced convex optimization algorithms, such as primal-dual and accelerated gradient methods, to efficiently solve key medical imaging problems. Our approach incorporates domain-specific constraints and regularization strategies to enhance robustness and accuracy, especially in noisy or incomplete data scenarios. Extensive experiments on benchmark medical image datasets demonstrate significant improvements in segmentation accuracy and reconstruction quality compared to traditional non-convex and heuristic-based methods. The results highlight the effectiveness of convex optimization in achieving faster convergence, improved reproducibility, and scalability to large-scale imaging studies. This research showcases the potential of modern convex optimization as a foundational tool for medical image analysis, offering practical insights for future integration into clinical decision support systems and automated diagnostic workflows. Keywords: convex optimization, medical image analysis, image segmentation, image reconstruction, denoising, biomedical imaging, algorithm efficiency.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising approach for training policies using pre-collected datasets, eliminating the need for costly online interactions. However, existing offline RL methods often exhibit excessive conservativeness, leading to suboptimal performance and limited generalization. This paper addresses the challenge of reducing conservativeness in offline RL while maintaining stability and safety. We propose a novel framework that leverages uncertainty quantification and adaptive policy constraints to balance exploration and exploitation in offline settings. Our approach integrates a probabilistic model to estimate the uncertainty of state-action pairs and dynamically adjusts the policy constraints based on dataset coverage and risk tolerance. Experimental results on benchmark tasks demonstrate that our method significantly reduces conservativeness, achieving higher performance compared to state-of-the-art offline RL algorithms. The proposed framework also exhibits improved generalization to unseen environments, highlighting its potential for real-world applications where data efficiency and safety are critical. This work contributes to advancing offline RL by providing a principled and practical solution to mitigate conservativeness, paving the way for more robust and scalable deployment of RL in data-driven domains. **Keywords**: Offline reinforcement learning, conservativeness reduction, uncertainty quantification, adaptive policy constraints, generalization, data efficiency.

Estimating the structure of discrete graphical models is a fundamental challenge in statistical machine learning and data mining. This paper introduces a novel approach for structure estimation based on the properties of generalized covariance matrices and their inverses. We leverage the unique characteristics of these matrices to develop a new algorithm that identifies conditional independence relationships within the data, thereby revealing the underlying graph structure. Our method avoids strong assumptions about the data distribution, offering robustness compared to existing techniques. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our algorithm achieves superior accuracy in structure recovery, particularly in high-dimensional settings, while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed approach provides a valuable tool for understanding complex dependencies in various applications, including bioinformatics, social network analysis, and causal inference. Keywords: graphical models, structure learning, covariance matrix, conditional independence, high-dimensional data.

Chi Lan hài (Paphiopedilum Pfitzer) gồm nhiều loài thực vật bị đe dọa tuyệt chủng. Những nhóm tuyến trùng thực vật trên các loài Lan đã được công bố cho thấy, nhóm tuyến trùng thân lá và nhóm hại rễ đều có mặt gây hại trực tiếp đối với các loài chi Lan hài. Bên cạnh đó, tuyến trùng thực vật cũng là một trong những môi giới cho nhóm bệnh hại khác xâm nhập gây thiệt hại về phẩm chất đối với các cây Lan thương mại. Do vậy, nghiên cứu này được thực hiện với mục tiêu bước đầu xác định loài tuyến trùng chính ký sinh Lan hài đài cuốn [Paphiopedilum appletonianum (Gower) Rolfe 1896] thu được tại rừng tự nhiên Bà Nà (Đà Nẵng) để phục vụ phòng chống bệnh hại thực vật trong công tác bảo tồn loài Lan hài này. Kết quả nghiên cứu lần đầu tiên ghi nhận 12 loài tuyến trùng ký sinh thực vật xung quanh vùng rễ Lan hài đài cuốn ở Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu đã mô tả 2 loài chính gây hại (Paratrichodorus minor và Helicotylenchus dihystera) có mật độ cao trong đất và xuất hiện trong cả thân, rễ để có thể đưa ra các biện pháp phòng trừ thích hợp trong quá trình bảo tồn loài Lan hài quý hiếm này.

Distributional reinforcement learning (DRL) has shown promise in addressing the limitations of traditional value-based methods by learning a distribution of returns rather than a single expected value. However, the impact of sample size and statistical methods on the performance and stability of DRL algorithms remains underexplored. This paper investigates the interplay between different statistical techniques, specifically focusing on various estimators and sampling strategies within the DRL framework. We analyze the effect of using different estimators such as the empirical mean, quantile regression, and Wasserstein barycenter, on the learned return distributions. We further investigate the influence of different sampling methods, including uniform sampling and prioritized experience replay, on the stability and convergence of DRL agents. Our experiments, conducted on a range of benchmark environments, demonstrate that the choice of estimator and sampling strategy significantly affects the performance and robustness of DRL algorithms. We identify specific combinations of estimators and sampling methods that lead to improved performance and propose guidelines for selecting appropriate statistical tools for DRL. Our findings provide valuable insights into the statistical properties of DRL and offer practical recommendations for designing more effective and reliable DRL agents. Keywords: Distributional Reinforcement Learning, Statistics, Sampling, Reinforcement Learning, Quantile Regression, Experience Replay.

This paper addresses the challenge of analyzing correlated multivariate time series data, a common problem in various domains such as finance, meteorology, and healthcare, where complex interdependencies among time series require advanced analytical models. Methods: We propose a novel deep structural model leveraging hierarchical recurrent neural networks to capture both temporal patterns and structural dependencies within multivariate time series. Our approach integrates a multi-headed attention mechanism to enhance the model's ability to focus on relevant features and relationships among different series. Results: Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, our model demonstrates superior performance in prediction accuracy and correlation estimation compared to existing methods such as Vector Autoregression (VAR) and traditional recurrent neural networks. The model effectively identifies latent structures and scales well with increasing data complexity and dimensionality. Conclusion: This research introduces a significant advancement in time series analysis by providing a robust framework capable of addressing the intricacies of multivariate data. The deep structural model not only improves predictive performance but also offers meaningful insights into the underlying correlations, paving the way for applications in risk management, anomaly detection, and system optimization across industries. Keywords: multivariate time series, deep learning, recurrent neural networks, hierarchical models, attention mechanism, predictive analytics, correlation analysis.

Tại Đồng bằng sông Hồng, tình trạng khai thác nước ngầm quá mức dẫn đến sụt lún đất, trong khi ở Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long, việc xây dựng đập thượng nguồn làm thay đổi dòng chảy tự nhiên, gây hạn hán và thiếu nước ngọt. This paper introduces a novel automatic face recognition system leveraging Local Fourier-Bessel Features (LFB) for enhanced performance and robustness. The objective is to improve face recognition accuracy, particularly under challenging conditions such as varying illumination and facial expression. Our method utilizes a novel approach for extracting discriminative features from facial images by applying a Fourier-Bessel expansion within localized regions. This captures both frequency and spatial information, leading to a more comprehensive representation of facial characteristics. Experimental results on benchmark face databases, including LFW and FERET, demonstrate that the proposed LFB-based system achieves superior recognition rates compared to traditional methods like PCA and LBP, and comparable performance to state-of-the-art deep learning approaches, while requiring significantly less computational resources. The system exhibits strong robustness against variations in lighting and expression. The findings highlight the potential of Fourier-Bessel features for efficient and accurate face recognition, offering a computationally effective alternative to deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Key words: Face Recognition, Fourier-Bessel Transform, Feature Extraction, Pattern Recognition, Biometrics.

Các cơ sở dữ liệu chất lượng đất được thu thập và phân tích để cung cấp thông tin về tính chất đất và yêu cầu về chất lượng đất cho từng loại sử dụng đất sản xuất nông nghiệp.

This paper explores the development of Lifelong Reinforcement Learning (LRL) systems, which aim to continuously learn and adapt through diverse tasks over an extended period. We address the pivotal challenge of enhancing LRL systems in retaining valuable knowledge without succumbing to catastrophic forgetting. Methods/Approach: Our approach integrates novel mechanisms for knowledge retention and transfer within an LRL framework. We introduce an adaptive memory architecture that selectively consolidates experiences while utilizing a task-aware transfer strategy to leverage past learning in novel environments. The framework employs deep reinforcement learning algorithms optimized for cross-task adaptation and incremental learning. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our LRL system achieves superior performance in retaining critical knowledge and transferring skills across multiple domains compared to traditional reinforcement learning models. The evaluation involves standard benchmarks and real-world scenarios, showcasing improved efficiency and adaptability. Moreover, the system exhibits resilience against task interference and forgetting, maintaining a high level of competence over time. Conclusion/Implications: The research advances the field of lifelong learning in reinforcement learning by presenting a robust methodology for continuous adaptation and knowledge retention. The implications of this work suggest vast potential for applications requiring robust, adaptable AI systems in dynamic environments, such as robotics, autonomous decision-making, and personalized learning platforms. Our findings contribute to the foundational understanding of LRL systems and pave the way for future exploration into more sophisticated adaptive learning systems. Keywords: Lifelong Reinforcement Learning, Catastrophic Forgetting, Knowledge Transfer, Adaptive Memory, Continuous Learning, AI Systems.

Việc quản lý và vận hành tòa nhà cũng tác động đáng kể, bao gồm việc duy trì hệ thống PCCC, tổ chức diễn tập thường xuyên và nâng cao nhận thức cho nhân viên, người thuê văn phòng. Bên cạnh đó, các yếu tố khách quan như biến đổi khí hậu, mật độ xây dựng cao và khả năng tiếp cận của lực lượng cứu hỏa cũng gây ảnh hưởng không nhỏ đến hiệu quả PCCC tại các cao ốc văn phòng.

The study addresses the challenge of accurately modeling interatomic forces in materials science using machine learning potentials. Traditional descriptors often struggle to capture local environmental dependencies, which are crucial for reliable predictions. This research introduces Localized Coulomb Descriptors (LCDs) to enhance the Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) framework, facilitating improved representation of atomic interactions. Methods/Approach: We propose the use of Localized Coulomb Descriptors, which are designed to represent the local electronic environment of atoms more effectively. These descriptors are integrated into the Gaussian Approximation Potential, an advanced machine-learning model for predicting potential energy surfaces. The proposed method's performance is benchmarked against existing descriptor frameworks through rigorous assessments involving diverse datasets representing varied atomic configurations and geometries. Results/Findings: The incorporation of Localized Coulomb Descriptors demonstrates a significant enhancement in the accuracy of energy predictions and force computations when embedded into the GAP model. Our approach achieves superior performance across multiple benchmark datasets, evidencing a reduction in mean absolute errors compared to traditional descriptors. This improvement is especially pronounced in systems with complex chemical environments, highlighting the efficacy of LCDs in capturing intricate atomic-level interactions. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Localized Coulomb Descriptors for the Gaussian Approximation Potential advances the precision of machine-learning-based methods in materials modeling. This research contributes novel insights into descriptor optimization and provides a robust foundation for future developments in atomic interaction modeling. The enhanced model holds substantial potential applications in computational materials science, enabling the accurate prediction of properties for novel materials and facilitating new material discovery pipelines. Keywords: Localized Coulomb Descriptors, Gaussian Approximation Potential, machine learning, materials science, interatomic forces, atomic interactions.

This paper introduces Points2Vec, a novel unsupervised learning approach for object-level feature learning from point clouds. The objective is to enable effective representation of 3D objects without relying on labeled data. Our method leverages a vector-based embedding technique to learn compact and informative features from point cloud data. By utilizing a self-supervised framework, Points2Vec learns to identify and represent object-level structures, facilitating downstream tasks such as object recognition, segmentation, and reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of feature quality and robustness. The key contributions of this work include the introduction of a scalable and efficient unsupervised learning pipeline for point cloud data, and the demonstration of its potential applications in various 3D vision tasks. Our approach has significant implications for fields such as robotics, autonomous driving, and computer-aided design, where high-quality 3D representations are crucial. Key keywords: point clouds, unsupervised learning, object-level features, 3D vision, self-supervised learning, vector-based embedding.

The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and edge computing has created a demand for efficient machine learning (ML) solutions on resource-constrained embedded systems. This paper explores TensorFlow Lite Micro (TFLM), a lightweight ML framework designed for TinyML applications, enabling on-device inference for microcontrollers and low-power devices. The objective of this research is to evaluate TFLM's capabilities in optimizing ML models for deployment on hardware with limited memory, processing power, and energy resources. We present a systematic approach to model optimization, including quantization, pruning, and efficient kernel implementations, tailored for embedded systems. Experimental results demonstrate TFLM's ability to achieve real-time inference with minimal latency and memory footprint, outperforming traditional ML frameworks in constrained environments. Furthermore, we compare TFLM's performance across various microcontroller architectures, highlighting its versatility and scalability. The findings underscore TFLM's potential to revolutionize embedded ML applications, enabling intelligent decision-making at the edge. This research contributes to the growing field of TinyML by providing insights into model optimization techniques and practical deployment strategies, paving the way for innovative applications in healthcare, agriculture, and industrial automation. **Keywords**: TensorFlow Lite Micro, TinyML, embedded systems, machine learning, model optimization, edge computing, IoT.

This paper addresses the challenge of preferences prediction in mobile device usage by leveraging advanced scene recognition and object detection techniques. The objective is to develop a robust model that accurately predicts user preferences based on visual information captured through mobile cameras. Our approach incorporates state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for scene recognition, combined with object detection frameworks to identify and classify objects in real-time. Through extensive experiments on a diverse dataset, our system demonstrates a significant improvement in prediction accuracy compared to traditional preference prediction methods. Results indicate that the proposed model achieves an accuracy rate of over 85% when evaluating user preference patterns in various environments, showcasing its effectiveness in dynamic contexts. The innovative integration of scene and object analysis not only enhances the prediction capabilities but also opens new avenues for personalized user experiences in mobile applications. This contributes to the field by providing a practical solution for context-aware systems, with potential applications in targeted advertising, content curation, and user interface design. Key contributions include the introduction of a comprehensive mobile gallery framework that adapts to real-time inputs, offering insights into user behavior that were previously unattainable. This research lays the groundwork for future advancements in personalized mobile technology. Keywords: preferences prediction, scene recognition, object detection, mobile devices, convolutional neural networks, context-aware systems.

In this paper, we present a self-training method, named ST3D++, with a holistic pseudo label denoising pipeline for unsupervised domain adaptation on 3D object detection. ST3D++ aims at reducing noise in pseudo label generation as well as alleviating the negative impacts of noisy pseudo labels on model training. First, ST3D++ pre-trains the 3D object detector on the labeled source domain with random object scaling (ROS) which is designed to reduce target domain pseudo label noise arising from object scale bias of the source domain. Then, the detector is progressively improved through alternating between generating pseudo labels and training the object detector with pseudo-labeled target domain data. Here, we equip the pseudo label generation process with a hybrid quality-aware triplet memory to improve the quality and stability of generated pseudo labels. Meanwhile, in the model training stage, we propose a source data assisted training strategy and a curriculum data augmentation policy to effectively rectify noisy gradient directions and avoid model over-fitting to noisy pseudo labeled data. These specific designs enable the detector to be trained on meticulously refined pseudo labeled target data with denoised training signals, and thus effectively facilitate adapting an object detector to a target domain without requiring annotations. Finally, our method is assessed on four 3D benchmark datasets (i.e., Waymo, KITTI, Lyft, and nuScenes) for three common categories (i.e., car, pedestrian and bicycle). ST3D++ achieves state-of-the-art performance on all evaluated settings, outperforming the corresponding baseline by a large margin (e.g., 9.6% \sim 38.16% on Waymo \rightarrow KITTI in terms of AP_}), and even surpasses the fully supervised oracle results on the KITTI 3D object detection benchmark with target prior. This paper addresses the challenge of learning robust and expressive latent representations in adversarial autoencoders. Traditional latent space approaches in this domain often neglect the geometric properties essential for effective data representation. We introduce adversarial autoencoders integrated with constant-curvature latent manifolds to enhance the quality and versatility of learned representations. Methods/Approach: We extend the framework of adversarial autoencoders to incorporate a curvature-aware latent space, leveraging Riemannian geometry to manage constant curvature manifolds within the latent variable model. By utilizing a principled approach to enforce curvature constraints, the autoencoder better aligns with the natural data distribution. The manifold structure is dynamically optimized during the adversarial training to maintain a consistent curvature throughout the latent space, thus enabling more meaningful data embeddings. Results/Findings: Experimental validations demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms standard adversarial autoencoders in capturing the intrinsic geometry of data distributions, resulting in improved generation quality and more accurate reconstructions. Our approach shows competitive performance benchmarks across various datasets, illustrating enhanced capacity for dimensionality reduction and representation learning. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of constant-curvature latent manifolds in adversarial autoencoders represents a novel contribution to the domain of representational learning, providing a more geometrically coherent framework. This innovation paves the way for broader applications in fields requiring intricate data representation and synthesis, such as image processing, natural language processing, and anomaly detection. Future work will explore extending this approach to accommodate varying curvature scenarios, further enhancing adaptability and performance. Keywords: adversarial autoencoders, latent manifolds, constant curvature, Riemannian geometry, representation learning, data embeddings.

Đặc biệt, khu vực này có địa hình phức tạp với nhiều sông suối nhỏ, dễ dẫn đến tình trạng ngập úng khi có mưa lớn kéo dài. Ngoài ra, việc khai thác rừng bừa bãi cũng làm giảm khả năng giữ nước của đất, gia tăng nguy cơ lũ quét. Các biện pháp phòng ngừa và ứng phó cần được triển khai kịp thời nhằm giảm thiểu thiệt hại cho người dân và bảo vệ môi trường sống. Việc nâng cao nhận thức cộng đồng về nguy cơ lũ quét cũng là một yếu tố quan trọng trong công tác phòng chống thiên tai tại địa phương.

Kết quả cho thấy rằng dữ liệu mưa lũ hiện tại còn hạn chế, không đầy đủ và không chính xác, dẫn đến khó khăn trong việc dự báo và cảnh báo mưa lũ. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng hệ thống thu thập và phân tích dữ liệu mưa lũ trên khu vực thành phố Hà Tĩnh còn nhiều hạn chế, bao gồm thiếu số liệu, không có hệ thống thu thập dữ liệu mưa lũ đồng bộ và không có công cụ phân tích dữ liệu mưa lũ hiện đại. Để cải thiện chất lượng dữ liệu mưa lũ và đảm bảo an toàn cho người dân, các nhà nghiên cứu đề xuất cần đầu tư vào hệ thống thu thập và phân tích dữ liệu mưa lũ hiện đại, bao gồm việc lắp đặt các trạm đo mưa lũ đồng bộ và sử dụng công cụ phân tích dữ liệu mưa lũ hiện đại. We address the problem of automatically learning the main steps to complete a certain task, such as changing a car tire, from a set of narrated instruction videos. The contributions of this paper are three-fold. First, we develop a new unsupervised learning approach that takes advantage of the complementary nature of the input video and the associated narration. The method solves two clustering problems, one in text and one in video, applied one after each other and linked by joint constraints to obtain a single coherent sequence of steps in both modalities. Second, we collect and annotate a new challenging dataset of real-world instruction videos from the Internet. The dataset contains about 800,000 frames for five different tasks that include complex interactions between people and objects, and are captured in a variety of indoor and outdoor settings. Third, we experimentally demonstrate that the proposed method can automatically discover, in an unsupervised manner, the main steps to achieve the task and locate the steps in the input videos.

This paper addresses the challenge of deploying deep neural networks (DNNs) for image recognition tasks on resource-constrained devices by proposing a novel framework for Structured Binary Neural Networks (SBNNs). The objective is to reduce computational complexity and memory usage while maintaining competitive accuracy. To achieve this, we introduce a structured binarization approach that leverages weight grouping and hierarchical quantization, enabling efficient binary operations without significant loss of information. Our method integrates a gradient-aware training strategy to optimize the binarization process, ensuring robust feature extraction. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrate that SBNNs achieve up to a 95% reduction in model size and a 3x speedup in inference time compared to full-precision counterparts, with only a marginal drop in accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed approach outperforms existing binary neural network techniques in terms of both efficiency and recognition performance. The findings highlight the potential of SBNNs for real-time image recognition applications on edge devices, offering a practical solution for deploying lightweight yet accurate models. This work contributes to the growing field of efficient deep learning by providing a structured and scalable framework for binary neural network design. **Keywords**: Binary Neural Networks, Image Recognition, Model Compression, Edge Computing, Efficient Deep Learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) path planning for efficient wireless data harvesting. The objective is to develop an optimal flight path that maximizes data collection while minimizing energy consumption. A deep reinforcement learning approach is employed, utilizing a novel algorithm that integrates UAV mobility and wireless communication models. The method involves training a neural network to learn the optimal policy for UAV trajectory planning, taking into account factors such as data density, transmission power, and UAV speed. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in data harvesting efficiency and reduced energy consumption compared to traditional path planning methods. The proposed approach offers a novel solution for UAV-based wireless data harvesting, with potential applications in various fields, including environmental monitoring, smart cities, and IoT networks. Key contributions include the development of a deep reinforcement learning framework for UAV path planning and the demonstration of its effectiveness in optimizing wireless data harvesting. Relevant keywords: UAV, path planning, deep reinforcement learning, wireless data harvesting, IoT, smart cities.

This paper explores the theoretical foundations of neural networks through the lens of reproducing kernel Banach spaces (RKBS), offering a novel perspective on their mathematical properties and behavior. The objective is to bridge the gap between practical neural network applications and their underlying theoretical frameworks, providing deeper insights into their approximation capabilities and generalization performance. We propose a methodological approach that leverages RKBS to analyze the structure and dynamics of neural networks, focusing on their ability to model complex, high-dimensional data. Our findings demonstrate that RKBS provides a robust framework for understanding the expressiveness and stability of neural networks, particularly in scenarios involving non-Euclidean data spaces. The results highlight significant improvements in interpretability and theoretical guarantees compared to traditional reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) approaches. This research contributes to the broader understanding of neural networks by offering a mathematically rigorous framework that enhances their design and optimization. The implications extend to applications in machine learning, computer vision, and data science, where improved theoretical insights can lead to more efficient and reliable models. Keywords: neural networks, reproducing kernel Banach spaces, approximation theory, machine learning, non-Euclidean data.

This paper addresses the challenge of unsupervised action recognition by proposing a novel Augmented Skeleton Based Contrastive Action Learning framework utilizing a Momentum Long Short-Term Memory (M-LSTM) architecture. The primary objective is to enhance the discriminative power of skeleton-based representations for human action recognition in scenarios lacking labeled training data. Our approach leverages data augmentation techniques specifically tailored for skeleton sequences, generating diverse views that enrich the contrastive learning process. We introduce a momentum mechanism within the LSTM network to stabilize feature representations over temporal sequences, improving the model’s capacity to capture long-term action dependencies and variations. Extensive experiments on benchmark skeleton action datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing unsupervised methods, and approaches the accuracy of some supervised counterparts. The proposed system exhibits improved robustness to noise and irregularities in input skeletal data, attributing to its effective feature extraction and temporal modeling capabilities. This research contributes a scalable and annotation-efficient solution for action recognition in fields such as video surveillance, human-computer interaction, and physical therapy, highlighting the potential of momentum-based recurrent networks in unsupervised learning settings. Key keywords include action recognition, skeleton-based learning, unsupervised learning, contrastive learning, Momentum LSTM, and data augmentation.

This paper presents a comprehensive review of statistical shape spaces specifically tailored for 3D data, with a focused comparative analysis on their application in modeling human faces. The research seeks to evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of various statistical approaches in capturing the complexities and nuances of human facial structures. Methods/Approach: We investigate a range of statistical shape models, including active shape models (ASMs), principal component analysis (PCA), Gaussian process models, and deep learning-based methods like generative adversarial networks (GANs). The analysis emphasizes the ability of these models to process and reconstruct 3D facial geometries accurately. Comparative studies are conducted to assess computational efficiency, robustness to noise, and flexibility in handling diverse datasets. Results/Findings: Our findings reveal that each statistical method offers distinct advantages depending on the application context. Traditional approaches like ASMs and PCA demonstrate superior computational efficiency and simplicity, while deep learning-based techniques, particularly GANs, excel in generating highly realistic facial variations. The study highlights the trade-offs between accuracy and computational demand, showcasing scenarios where hybrid models provide optimal performance. Conclusion/Implications: The review not only elucidates the current landscape of statistical shape spaces for 3D facial data but also identifies key areas for future research. The comparative insights derived could guide the selection and development of specific applications in fields such as computer vision, biometric security, and facial recognition technologies. The study underscores the potential of hybridized models to balance performance and efficiency, paving the way for more innovative solutions in 3D modeling. Keywords: 3D shape modeling, statistical shape spaces, human faces, active shape models, principal component analysis, Gaussian process models, generative adversarial networks, facial reconstruction.

This paper introduces SimPool, a novel graph pooling approach that leverages topology-based methods and incorporates structural similarity features to effectively downsample graphs while preserving crucial information. The objective is to address the limitations of existing graph pooling techniques, which often fail to capture complex structural relationships between nodes. SimPool utilizes a unique combination of graph topology and node similarity measures to identify and select the most representative nodes, resulting in a more accurate and efficient graph pooling process. Experimental results demonstrate that SimPool outperforms state-of-the-art graph pooling methods, achieving significant improvements in graph classification and clustering tasks. The key contributions of this research include the development of a topology-based graph pooling framework, the integration of structural similarity features, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in various graph-based applications. This work has important implications for graph neural networks, network analysis, and related fields, highlighting the potential of SimPool to enhance the performance and interpretability of graph-based models. Key keywords: graph pooling, topology-based methods, structural similarity, graph neural networks, network analysis.

Single-view depth estimation suffers from the problem that a network trained on images from one camera does not generalize to images taken with a different camera model. Thus, changing the camera model requires collecting an entirely new training dataset. In this work, we propose a new type of convolution that can take the camera parameters into account, thus allowing neural networks to learn calibration-aware patterns. Experiments confirm that this improves the generalization capabilities of depth prediction networks considerably, and clearly outperforms the state of the art when the train and test images are acquired with different cameras.

Nowadays, the use of machine learning models is becoming a utility in many applications. Companies deliver pre-trained models encapsulated as application programming interfaces (APIs) that developers combine with third party components and their own models and data to create complex data products to solve specific problems. The complexity of such products and the lack of control and knowledge of the internals of each component used cause unavoidable effects, such as lack of transparency, difficulty in auditability, and emergence of potential uncontrolled risks. They are effectively black-boxes. Accountability of such solutions is a challenge for the auditors and the machine learning community. In this work, we propose a wrapper that given a black-box model enriches its output prediction with a measure of uncertainty. By using this wrapper, we make the black-box auditable for the accuracy risk (risk derived from low quality or uncertain decisions) and at the same time we provide an actionable mechanism to mitigate that risk in the form of decision rejection; we can choose not to issue a prediction when the risk or uncertainty in that decision is significant. Based on the resulting uncertainty measure, we advocate for a rejection system that selects the more confident predictions, discarding those more uncertain, leading to an improvement in the trustability of the resulting system. We showcase the proposed technique and methodology in a practical scenario where a simulated sentiment analysis API based on natural language processing is applied to different domains. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the uncertainty computed by the wrapper and its high correlation to bad quality predictions and misclassifications.

This paper addresses the challenge of capturing long-range dependencies in deep neural networks, a limitation present in traditional convolutional and recurrent architectures primarily focused on local information. We propose a novel non-local neural network framework that introduces non-local operations, allowing each output position to aggregate features from all positions in the input, regardless of their spatial or temporal distance. Our approach is formulated as a generic, end-to-end trainable module that can be seamlessly integrated into existing architectures. To evaluate its effectiveness, we implement our non-local blocks in several computer vision tasks, including video classification and object detection. Experimental results demonstrate that models augmented with non-local operations consistently outperform their baselines, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with minimal increase in computational cost. The findings indicate that explicitly modeling global context leads to richer feature representations and improved performance in complex tasks involving scenes with intricate and long-range relationships. This work highlights the potential of non-local neural networks as a key advancement in deep learning, with applications in video analysis, image recognition, and sequence modeling. Keywords: non-local neural networks, deep learning, global context, feature aggregation, video classification, object detection.

This paper addresses the challenge of extracting meaningful patterns from complex, multi-dimensional data by introducing a novel approach to regularized tensor factorizations and higher-order principal components analysis. Our objective is to develop a robust and efficient method for decomposing high-order tensors into interpretable components, enabling insights into underlying structures and relationships. We propose a new algorithm that integrates regularization techniques with tensor factorization, allowing for improved generalization and reduced overfitting. Our approach is evaluated on various real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing higher-order correlations and outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The results show that our regularized tensor factorization method can identify meaningful patterns and principal components in high-dimensional data, with significant implications for applications in data mining, machine learning, and signal processing. Key contributions of this research include the development of a scalable and flexible tensor factorization framework, the introduction of novel regularization techniques, and the demonstration of improved performance in higher-order principal components analysis. Relevant keywords: tensor factorization, higher-order principal components analysis, regularization techniques, multi-dimensional data analysis, machine learning, data mining.

Smartphone photo scanning has become a ubiquitous tool for digitizing physical documents, yet real-world challenges such as lighting variations, shadows, and perspective distortions often degrade scan quality. This paper introduces *Deep Photo Scan*, a novel semi-supervised learning framework designed to address these degradation issues effectively. The proposed approach leverages a hybrid model combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to enhance image quality while preserving critical details. By utilizing a small labeled dataset alongside a large pool of unlabeled real-world images, the model achieves robust performance across diverse degradation scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in image clarity, edge sharpness, and color accuracy compared to existing methods, with a 15% increase in perceptual quality metrics. The framework also introduces a lightweight post-processing module optimized for mobile deployment, ensuring real-time performance on resource-constrained devices. This research contributes to advancing smartphone-based document digitization by offering a scalable, efficient solution that bridges the gap between supervised and unsupervised learning paradigms. The proposed method has broad applications in mobile computing, digital archiving, and augmented reality, paving the way for more reliable and accessible photo scanning technologies. **Keywords**: smartphone photo scanning, semi-supervised learning, image enhancement, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), mobile computing.

This paper introduces a novel approach to trajectory prediction by leveraging social behavior patterns in crowded environments. The objective is to develop a predictive model that captures the complex interactions between individuals and their surroundings, enabling accurate forecasting of future trajectories. Our method utilizes a Recursive Social Behavior Graph (RSBG) framework, which integrates graph-based modeling with recursive neural networks to learn spatio-temporal relationships between agents. The RSBG approach allows for the incorporation of social norms, environmental constraints, and agent-specific characteristics, resulting in improved prediction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our model in predicting trajectories in various scenarios, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a recursive graph-based architecture and the incorporation of social behavior patterns, enabling more accurate and human-like trajectory predictions. This work has significant implications for applications such as autonomous systems, crowd simulation, and surveillance, and highlights the importance of social awareness in predictive modeling. Key keywords: trajectory prediction, social behavior, graph-based modeling, recursive neural networks, autonomous systems.

Task-oriented dialogue systems (TODS) trained with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) often suffer from inefficient exploration, leading to slow convergence and suboptimal policies. To address this, we introduce BBQ-Networks, a novel DRL framework designed to enhance exploration efficiency in TODS. BBQ-Networks employs a bootstrapped Q-network ensemble with a behavior cloning regularizer to promote diverse exploration strategies. Specifically, the bootstrapped ensemble encourages disagreement among Q-value estimates, while behavior cloning leverages expert demonstrations to guide exploration towards promising dialogue states. Empirical results on benchmark TODS datasets demonstrate that BBQ-Networks significantly outperforms existing DRL methods in terms of sample efficiency and dialogue success rate. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each component in BBQ-Networks. The proposed approach offers a practical solution for accelerating DRL training and improving the performance of task-oriented dialogue systems. Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems, Exploration, Bootstrapped Q-Networks, Behavior Cloning.

Learning invariant representations is a critical challenge in machine learning, particularly for tasks requiring robustness to domain shifts or sensitive attribute variations. Traditional approaches often rely on adversarial training, which introduces computational complexity and instability during optimization. This paper proposes a novel framework for learning invariant representations without adversarial training, offering a more efficient and stable alternative. Our method leverages a combination of contrastive learning and regularization techniques to enforce invariance while preserving task-relevant information. We evaluate the proposed approach on benchmark datasets across multiple domains, including image classification and natural language processing. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive or superior performance compared to adversarial-based approaches, with significantly reduced training time and improved stability. Furthermore, the framework exhibits strong generalization capabilities under domain shifts and adversarial attacks. The findings highlight the potential of non-adversarial methods for invariant representation learning, paving the way for more scalable and reliable solutions in real-world applications. **Keywords**: invariant representations, contrastive learning, regularization, domain adaptation, machine learning, robustness.

This paper introduces XCI-Sketch, a novel approach for generating colored outlines and sketches from images by effectively extracting and utilizing color information. Current sketch generation techniques often produce grayscale outputs, limiting their expressive potential. XCI-Sketch addresses this limitation by incorporating a color extraction module that analyzes image gradients and color distributions to identify salient color regions. A modified edge detection algorithm is then applied, weighted by the extracted color information, to produce colored outlines. Furthermore, a multi-layered abstraction process refines these outlines into stylized colored sketches. Experimental results demonstrate that XCI-Sketch generates visually appealing and informative colored sketches that better represent the original image's aesthetic compared to grayscale alternatives. Quantitative evaluations using image similarity metrics confirm the superior performance of XCI-Sketch in preserving color information. The proposed method has potential applications in artistic style transfer, image editing, and non-photorealistic rendering. Keywords: Sketch Generation, Colored Outlines, Edge Detection, Color Extraction, Image Processing, Non-Photorealistic Rendering.

This paper addresses the challenge of multimodal remote sensing image registration, where images acquired from different sensors or at varying times need to be accurately aligned. The objective is to develop a fast and robust matching approach that can handle significant differences in intensity, texture, and feature appearance between images. A novel framework is proposed, combining the strengths of feature extraction and machine learning techniques to establish reliable correspondences between images. The approach leverages a deep learning-based feature descriptor to extract robust and discriminative features, which are then matched using an efficient and scalable algorithm. The contributions of this research include the development of a highly efficient and accurate image registration method, with potential applications in change detection, image fusion, and environmental monitoring. Key keywords: multimodal image registration, remote sensing, deep learning, feature matching, computer vision.

The rapid proliferation of streaming data poses significant challenges for time series classification, demanding robust and efficient models capable of real-time performance. This study investigates the performance of deep learning models for time series classification in streaming environments, aiming to enhance accuracy and responsiveness. Methods/Approach: Our approach involves a comprehensive evaluation of various deep learning architectures, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and hybrid models, specifically optimized for time series streaming data. We implemented and tested these models using a tailored framework designed to accommodate high velocity data input while maintaining model integrity and reliability. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that deep learning models, particularly those with hybrid layers integrating RNN and CNN components, significantly outperform traditional methods in streaming scenarios. Key metrics such as classification accuracy, latency, and computation efficiency underscore the capability of these models to adapt swiftly to dynamic data inputs, making them suitable for high-throughput applications. Conclusion/Implications: This research highlights the potential of advanced deep learning architectures to transform time series classification in streaming contexts, offering improved performance and operational scalability. The findings indicate promising implications for various applications, including financial market analysis, real-time monitoring systems, and IoT analytics, where timely and accurate data processing is paramount. Our study paves the way for further exploration into optimizing deep learning frameworks tailored to the unique demands of streaming environments. Keywords: Deep learning, time series classification, streaming data, RNN, CNN, real-time processing, hybrid models.

Nâng cao năng lực cạnh tranh của các doanh nghiệp sản xuất nông sản chủ lực trên địa bàn là một vấn đề cấp thiết trong bối cảnh thị trường ngày càng khốc liệt.
