Synthetic data offers a scalable solution for training depth estimation models, but performance often lags when applied to real-world images due to domain shift. This paper introduces Domain Decluttering, a novel image simplification technique designed to reduce the discrepancy between synthetic and real image distributions. Our method selectively removes complex background elements and irrelevant objects from synthetic images, focusing the model's attention on essential depth cues and scene structure. We evaluate our approach by training a depth estimation network on decluttered synthetic data and testing it on real-world datasets. Results demonstrate significant improvements in depth estimation accuracy compared to models trained on standard synthetic data and other domain adaptation techniques. Furthermore, our approach reduces overfitting to synthetic artifacts, leading to better generalization. Domain Decluttering offers a practical strategy for bridging the synthetic-to-real gap in depth estimation, enhancing the effectiveness of synthetic training data. Keywords: Depth Estimation, Domain Adaptation, Synthetic Data, Domain Shift, Image Simplification, Computer Vision.

Conventional few-shot object segmentation methods learn object segmentation from a few labelled support images with strongly labelled segmentation masks. Recent work has shown to perform on par with weaker levels of supervision in terms of scribbles and bounding boxes. However, there has been limited attention given to the problem of few-shot object segmentation with image-level supervision. We propose a novel multi-modal interaction module for few-shot object segmentation that utilizes a co-attention mechanism using both visual and word embeddings. It enables our model to achieve 5.1% improvement over previously proposed image-level few-shot object segmentation. Our method compares relatively close to the state of the art methods that use strong supervision, while ours use the least possible supervision. We further propose a novel setup for few-shot weakly supervised video object segmentation(VOS) that relies on image-level labels for the first frame. The proposed setup uses weak annotation unlike semi-supervised VOS setting that utilizes strongly labelled segmentation masks. The setup evaluates the effectiveness of generalizing to novel classes in the VOS setting. The setup splits the VOS data into multiple folds with different categories per fold. It provides a potential setup to evaluate how few-shot object segmentation methods can benefit from additional object poses, or object interactions that is not available in static frames as in PASCAL-5i benchmark.

For safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving, CNNs have to be robust with respect to unavoidable image corruptions, such as image noise. While previous works addressed the task of robust prediction in the context of full-image classification, we consider it for dense semantic segmentation. We build upon an insight from image classification that output robustness can be improved by increasing the network-bias towards object shapes. We present a new training schema that increases this shape bias. Our basic idea is to alpha-blend a portion of the RGB training images with faked images, where each class-label is given a fixed, randomly chosen color that is not likely to appear in real imagery. This forces the network to rely more strongly on shape cues. We call this data augmentation technique ``Painting-by-Numbers''. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our training schema for DeepLabv3+ with various network backbones, MobileNet-V2, ResNets, and Xception, and evaluate it on the Cityscapes dataset. With respect to our 16 different types of image corruptions and 5 different network backbones, we are in 74% better than training with clean data. For cases where we are worse than a model trained without our training schema, it is mostly only marginally worse. However, for some image corruptions such as images with noise, we see a considerable performance gain of up to 25%.

Scene flow estimation, which involves predicting the 3D motion of every point in a scene, is a critical component in various computer vision and robotics applications, such as autonomous driving and augmented reality. Traditional approaches often rely on 2D projections or volumetric representations, limiting their scalability and accuracy when dealing with raw 3D point cloud data. In this paper, we introduce FlowNet3D, a deep neural network specifically designed to learn and predict scene flow directly from unordered 3D point clouds. Our method leverages novel point-by-point feature learning modules and embedding mechanisms to efficiently capture geometric relationships and motion patterns between consecutive 3D scans. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that FlowNet3D achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming conventional and recent deep learning-based methods in terms of scene flow accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, the end-to-end architecture enables robust performance under challenging scenarios, including sparse and noisy point clouds. The proposed approach opens new avenues for precise 3D motion understanding in dynamic environments. Key contributions include the introduction of point-based scene flow estimation, architectural innovations for direct processing of point clouds, and comprehensive evaluation demonstrating superior generalization capabilities. Keywords: scene flow, 3D point cloud, deep learning, FlowNet3D, motion estimation, feature learning, neural networks.

This paper addresses the challenge of conversational fashion image retrieval, where users refine search results through multiturn natural language feedback. Traditional image retrieval systems often fail to adapt dynamically to user preferences expressed in natural language, limiting their effectiveness in real-world applications. To overcome this, we propose a novel framework that integrates multimodal learning and conversational AI to enable iterative refinement of search results based on user feedback. Our approach leverages a combination of pre-trained vision-language models and a reinforcement learning-based feedback mechanism to interpret user inputs and update retrieval results in real time. Experiments conducted on a large-scale fashion dataset demonstrate that our system achieves significant improvements in retrieval accuracy and user satisfaction compared to existing methods. Key findings reveal that the multiturn feedback loop enhances the system’s ability to capture nuanced user preferences, leading to more precise and personalized results. This research contributes to the advancement of conversational AI in fashion e-commerce and highlights the potential of integrating natural language feedback into image retrieval systems for improved user interaction and experience. **Keywords**: conversational AI, fashion image retrieval, natural language feedback, multimodal learning, reinforcement learning, personalized search.

Nghiên cứu đã phân lập và xác định đặc điểm sinh học của các chủng vi khuẩn nội sinh từ rễ cây nha đam (Aloe vera L.) nhằm tìm kiếm các chủng có khả năng hỗ trợ sinh trưởng thực vật. Kết quả cho thấy một số chủng vi khuẩn có khả năng sinh trưởng tốt trong môi trường thiếu đạm, đồng thời có khả năng chuyển hóa lân khó tan thành dạng dễ hấp thụ cho cây trồng. Việc sử dụng các chủng vi khuẩn nội sinh này có thể là một giải pháp sinh học tiềm năng, giúp tăng cường sức khỏe và năng suất của cây nha đam một cách bền vững, giảm thiểu sự phụ thuộc vào phân bón hóa học.

The paper addresses the challenge of efficient feature selection in Factored Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), which is crucial for enhancing decision-making efficiency in complex environments. Traditional methods often require large sample sizes to identify relevant features, posing computational challenges. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel algorithmic approach that leverages model-based reinforcement learning to achieve sample-efficient feature selection for Factored MDPs. This approach utilizes a structured representation of the environment to identify and exploit relevant features with significantly reduced data requirements. Our method incorporates techniques from graph theory and probabilistic modeling to enhance the selection process. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly outperforms existing techniques in terms of sample efficiency and computational cost. We provide a comprehensive evaluation using benchmark problems, which shows a reduction in required samples by up to 50% compared to conventional approaches. Our findings indicate robust performance improvements, particularly in high-dimensional state spaces, illustrating the adaptability and efficiency of the model. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides crucial insights into efficient feature selection in Factored MDPs. By reducing the sample size requirements, our method opens new possibilities for deploying reinforcement learning solutions in real-time decision-making systems where data collection is expensive or time-consuming. The contributions of this study can significantly impact applications in robotics, automated planning, and intelligent system design, where efficient learning from limited data is paramount. Keywords: Factored MDPs, Feature Selection, Sample Efficiency, Reinforcement Learning, Graph Theory, Probabilistic Modeling, Decision-Making Systems.

Vở kịch "Julius Caesar" của William Shakespeare, được Nguyễn Thanh Minh, Trịnh Thị Thu Hà và Hoàng Thị Thu Hà chuyển ngữ, tái hiện một giai đoạn lịch sử đầy biến động của La Mã cổ đại. Brutus, một người bạn thân thiết của Caesar, bị thuyết phục tham gia vào âm mưu này vì lòng yêu nước và nỗi lo sợ về sự suy tàn của nền cộng hòa. Sau vụ ám sát, Mark Antony, một đồng minh trung thành của Caesar, đã sử dụng tài hùng biện của mình để kích động đám đông chống lại những kẻ chủ mưu, dẫn đến một cuộc nội chiến đẫm máu. Vở kịch khám phá các chủ đề phức tạp như lòng trung thành, sự phản bội, tham vọng quyền lực và hậu quả của bạo lực chính trị, đồng thời đặt ra câu hỏi về sự khác biệt giữa công lý và trả thù. Cái chết của Caesar đã mở ra một kỷ nguyên mới, nhưng cũng gieo rắc mầm mống của sự hỗn loạn và bất ổn trong xã hội La Mã.

Bokeh effect is used in photography to capture images where the closer objects look sharp and every-thing else stays out-of-focus. Bokeh photos are generally captured using Single Lens Reflex cameras using shallow depth-of-field. Most of the modern smartphones can take bokeh images by leveraging dual rear cameras or a good auto-focus hardware. However, for smartphones with single-rear camera without a good auto-focus hardware, we have to rely on software to generate bokeh images. This kind of system is also useful to generate bokeh effect in already captured images. In this paper, an end-to-end deep learning framework is proposed to generate high-quality bokeh effect from images. The original image and different versions of smoothed images are blended to generate Bokeh effect with the help of a monocular depth estimation network. The proposed approach is compared against a saliency detection based baseline and a number of approaches proposed in AIM 2019 Challenge on Bokeh Effect Synthesis. Extensive experiments are shown in order to understand different parts of the proposed algorithm. The network is lightweight and can process an HD image in 0.03 seconds. This approach ranked second in AIM 2019 Bokeh effect challenge-Perceptual Track.

Objective: Multi-relational learning—such as knowledge‐graph embedding and tensor factorization—enables applications ranging from link prediction to recommendation. However, existing algorithms often struggle to scale to web-size graphs due to tightly coupled optimization and high memory demands. This paper introduces a general, scalable framework based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) that decouples the global learning problem into smaller, parallelizable subproblems. Methods: We formulate a broad class of multi‐relational models (including bilinear and tensor‐factorization approaches) under an ADMM‐based consensus framework. Each worker optimizes local model parameters on a data shard, while a central coordinator enforces consistency via multiplier updates. Our method supports asynchronous updates, sparse regularization, and non‐convex embeddings. Results: On three large benchmarks (FB15k‐237, YAGO3-10, and OGBN‐PGDD), our ADMM solver achieves up to 4× faster convergence than centralized stochastic gradient methods, with comparable or improved link‐prediction accuracy (Hits@10 gains of 1–3%). We demonstrate near‐linear speedup across up to 64 compute nodes and show that memory per node remains bounded despite growing data size. Conclusion: By leveraging ADMM’s decomposability, our approach offers a flexible, high‐throughput solution for multi‐relational learning at scale. This framework can be extended to new relation types, regularizers, and streaming settings, making it well suited for real‐world knowledge‐graph applications. Keywords: multi‐relational learning, ADMM, distributed optimization, knowledge‐graph embedding, scalability.

This paper introduces Deep Adaptive Multi-Intention Inverse Reinforcement Learning (DAMIRL), a novel framework designed to address the challenge of inferring multiple, potentially conflicting intentions from observed behaviors in complex environments. Traditional Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) methods often struggle to model diverse intentions simultaneously, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios such as autonomous driving, robotics, and human-computer interaction. The proposed approach leverages deep neural networks to adaptively learn a set of reward functions, each corresponding to a distinct intention, while dynamically adjusting to the underlying structure of the observed data. By incorporating a multi-intention mechanism and an adaptive weighting scheme, DAMIRL effectively disentangles and models overlapping intentions, even in high-dimensional and noisy environments. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that DAMIRL outperforms existing IRL methods in terms of intention recovery accuracy and reward function generalization. The framework’s ability to handle diverse and conflicting intentions opens new possibilities for applications in multi-agent systems, personalized AI, and decision-making under uncertainty. This work contributes to advancing the state-of-the-art in IRL by providing a robust and scalable solution for multi-intention learning. **Keywords**: Inverse Reinforcement Learning, Multi-Intention Learning, Deep Learning, Adaptive Modeling, Reward Inference, Decision-Making.

Thiết kế bơm hướng trục n cao đối mặt với nhiều thách thức thực tế. Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown remarkable success in various domains, but ensuring safety and efficiency during policy improvement remains a critical challenge. This paper addresses the problem of constrained policy optimization in RL, where the goal is to maximize performance while adhering to safety constraints. We propose a novel constrained policy improvement framework that integrates safety constraints directly into the policy update process, ensuring that the learned policies are both effective and safe. Our approach leverages a constrained optimization formulation, combined with a trust-region method to balance exploration and exploitation. We evaluate the proposed framework on a range of benchmark environments, including robotic control and autonomous navigation tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing constrained RL algorithms, with significant improvements in constraint satisfaction and sample efficiency. The findings highlight the potential of our approach for real-world applications where safety and efficiency are paramount. This work contributes to the growing body of research on safe RL by providing a robust and scalable solution for constrained policy optimization. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Constrained Optimization, Safe RL, Policy Improvement, Trust-Region Methods, Autonomous Systems.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning disentangled representations in the realm of deep learning, with a focus on improving the interpretability and efficiency of latent variable models. The research specifically investigates the use of product manifold projection as a means to achieve effective disentanglement. Methods/Approach: Our approach involves developing a novel framework that integrates manifold learning techniques with advanced neural architectures. By leveraging the mathematical properties of product manifolds, our method facilitates the separation of complex data into independent underlying factors, enhancing the capacity for diverse data generation and manipulation. Results/Findings: Experimental results indicate that our model significantly outperforms existing disentanglement methods in various benchmark datasets. Notably, it achieves superior accuracy in encoding disentangled factors, exhibiting robustness across tasks such as data reconstruction, classification, and generative tasks. Comparative analyses with traditional methods highlight improvements in both model efficiency and interpretability without compromising performance. Conclusion/Implications: The research contributes a novel perspective on disentangled representation learning by proposing an innovative method that combines product manifold projection with neural architectures. This contribution is particularly valuable for applications in AI where interpretability and generative capacity are critical. Our findings suggest potential applications in fields such as computer graphics, robotics, and natural language processing, marking a substantial advancement in the development of sophisticated, interpretable AI systems. Keywords: Disentangled representations, product manifold projection, manifold learning, latent variable models, interpretability, deep learning.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for learning representations of graph-structured data, with message passing being a core mechanism driving their effectiveness. This paper investigates the underlying principles of message passing in GNNs by drawing parallels to Power Iteration Clustering (PIC), a well-established method for graph-based clustering. We propose a novel framework that interprets message passing as an iterative process akin to PIC, enabling a deeper understanding of how information propagates and aggregates across graph nodes. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, we demonstrate that this perspective not only provides theoretical insights into GNN behavior but also leads to practical improvements in model performance. Our approach achieves competitive results in node classification and graph classification tasks, outperforming several state-of-the-art GNN architectures. The findings highlight the potential of leveraging clustering-inspired techniques to enhance GNN design and optimization. This work contributes to the growing body of research on interpretable and efficient graph-based learning, offering new directions for advancing GNN methodologies. **Keywords**: Graph Neural Networks, Message Passing, Power Iteration Clustering, Graph Representation Learning, Node Classification, Graph Classification.

Humans are able to describe image contents with coarse to fine details as they wish. However, most image captioning models are intention-agnostic which can not generate diverse descriptions according to different user intentions initiatively. In this work, we propose the Abstract Scene Graph (ASG) structure to represent user intention in fine-grained level and control what and how detailed the generated description should be. The ASG is a directed graph consisting of three types of \textbf (object, attribute, relationship) grounded in the image without any concrete semantic labels. Thus it is easy to obtain either manually or automatically. From the ASG, we propose a novel ASG2Caption model, which is able to recognise user intentions and semantics in the graph, and therefore generate desired captions according to the graph structure. Our model achieves better controllability conditioning on ASGs than carefully designed baselines on both VisualGenome and MSCOCO datasets. It also significantly improves the caption diversity via automatically sampling diverse ASGs as control signals.

Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) is critical for various applications, yet its vulnerability to adversarial attacks remains underexplored. This paper introduces a novel adversarial attack targeting MOT systems, demonstrating that fooling the detection component alone is insufficient for a successful attack. Our approach crafts adversarial perturbations that not only mislead the detector but also disrupt the tracking association process by manipulating object features and trajectories. We employ a gradient-based optimization method to generate adversarial examples that maximize the tracking errors while maintaining stealthiness. Experiments on benchmark MOT datasets, including MOT17 and MOT20, show a significant drop in tracking performance compared to baseline methods. Specifically, our attack reduces MOTA by over 40% in several scenarios, even when the detection accuracy remains relatively high. These findings highlight the importance of considering the entire MOT pipeline when evaluating adversarial robustness. Our research underscores the need for robust MOT systems that are resilient to sophisticated adversarial manipulations beyond just detection. Keywords: Adversarial Attack, Multiple Object Tracking, Object Detection, Robustness, Computer Vision.

This paper proposes a novel approach for the classification of datasets in data mining, addressing the challenge of accurate and efficient data categorization. Our objective is to develop a method that improves upon existing classification techniques, enabling better decision-making and insight extraction from complex datasets. We employ a hybrid approach, combining machine learning algorithms with statistical analysis to create a robust and adaptable classification model. The results show significant improvements in classification accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional methods. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in handling diverse datasets, including those with high-dimensional features and noisy data. The contributions of this research include the introduction of a new classification algorithm and the evaluation of its performance on various benchmark datasets. This study has important implications for data mining applications, such as customer segmentation, fraud detection, and recommender systems, highlighting the potential for improved data-driven decision-making. Key keywords: data mining, classification, machine learning, dataset analysis, pattern recognition.

Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) is a powerful metric for comparing distributions, widely used in computer vision, machine learning, and data analysis. However, its high computational cost limits its applicability to large datasets. This paper introduces a novel, low-complexity approximation algorithm for EMD calculation designed for data-parallel architectures. Our approach leverages a hierarchical clustering strategy combined with efficient parallel processing techniques to significantly reduce computational complexity without sacrificing accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves a substantial speedup compared to existing EMD approximation algorithms, while maintaining competitive accuracy. Furthermore, the data-parallel nature of our algorithm makes it highly suitable for implementation on modern GPUs and multi-core CPUs, enabling efficient processing of large-scale datasets. This work provides a practical and scalable solution for EMD computation, facilitating its broader adoption in various applications. Keywords: Earth Mover's Distance, approximation algorithms, data-parallelism, hierarchical clustering, computational complexity, large-scale data.

Nghiên cứu về ảnh hưởng của các loại phân bón lá đến sinh trưởng, phát triển và năng suất cây trồng đã được tiến hành nhằm đánh giá hiệu quả của chúng trong nông nghiệp. Kết quả cho thấy, việc sử dụng phân bón lá có tác động tích cực đến quá trình sinh trưởng của cây, giúp tăng chiều cao, số lá và khả năng quang hợp. Đặc biệt, một số loại phân bón lá chứa vi lượng và chất kích thích sinh trưởng đã cải thiện đáng kể năng suất cây trồng, đồng thời nâng cao chất lượng nông sản. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng, việc áp dụng đúng liều lượng và thời điểm bón phân sẽ tối ưu hóa hiệu quả, giảm thiểu chi phí và tác động tiêu cực đến môi trường. Đây là cơ sở quan trọng giúp nông dân lựa chọn loại phân bón phù hợp, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả sản xuất nông nghiệp bền vững.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc tối ưu hóa giàn thép phi tuyến với sự xem xét đến độ tin cậy, áp dụng kết hợp thuật toán LPSS-EIS và phương pháp tiến hóa vi phân. Mục tiêu chính là cải thiện hiệu suất và độ bền của giàn thép trong các điều kiện tải trọng khác nhau, đồng thời đảm bảo tính an toàn và ổn định trong quá trình sử dụng. Thuật toán LPSS-EIS được sử dụng để phân tích và tối ưu hóa cấu trúc, trong khi phương pháp tiến hóa vi phân giúp tìm kiếm các giải pháp tối ưu một cách hiệu quả hơn. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy sự kết hợp này không chỉ nâng cao độ tin cậy của giàn thép mà còn giảm thiểu chi phí và thời gian thiết kế, mở ra hướng đi mới cho các ứng dụng trong ngành xây dựng và kỹ thuật kết cấu.

Hồ Gươm có diện tích khoảng 12 ha, nằm trong khu vực trung tâm thành phố, với nhiều công trình kiến trúc lịch sử và hiện đại xung quanh. Đặc điểm của hồ bao gồm hệ thống kênh rạch, hệ sinh thái đa dạng, và cảnh quan thiên nhiên đẹp. Tiềm năng của hồ bao gồm khả năng phát triển du lịch, tạo nguồn thu cho ngân sách, và trở thành điểm đến hấp dẫn cho du khách. Để định hướng bảo tồn không gian Hồ Gươm, cần phải có chiến lược và kế hoạch cụ thể. Điều này bao gồm việc bảo vệ và tôn tạo các công trình kiến trúc lịch sử, phát triển hệ sinh thái và cảnh quan thiên nhiên, và tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho du lịch và phát triển kinh tế. Đồng thời, cần phải cân nhắc và giải quyết các vấn đề liên quan đến ô nhiễm môi trường, giao thông và an ninh. Bằng cách bảo tồn và phát huy giá trị của Hồ Gươm, chúng ta có thể tạo ra một không gian văn hóa và lịch sử độc đáo, hấp dẫn và đáng nhớ. Điều này sẽ không chỉ mang lại lợi ích cho Hà Nội và Việt Nam, mà còn góp phần vào việc bảo vệ và phát triển di sản văn hóa thế giới.

This paper proposes an extension of the Isolation Forest algorithm, a widely used anomaly detection technique in machine learning. The objective is to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of anomaly detection in complex datasets by incorporating additional features and improving the decision-making process. Our approach introduces a novel method for selecting the optimal number of decision trees and utilizes a new scoring function that takes into account the density of the data points. The results show that the Extended Isolation Forest outperforms the traditional Isolation Forest in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score, particularly in datasets with high-dimensional features and noisy data. The conclusion highlights the significance of this research in advancing anomaly detection capabilities, with potential applications in fraud detection, network security, and healthcare monitoring. Key contributions include improved handling of high-dimensional data, enhanced robustness to noise and outliers, and increased interpretability of the results. Relevant keywords: anomaly detection, Isolation Forest, machine learning, outlier detection, data mining.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving generalization in reinforcement learning (RL) by introducing an instance-based approach. The research explores how leveraging specific instances within an environment can enhance the adaptability and performance of RL algorithms across diverse tasks. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel instance-based generalization model that utilizes a combination of instance memory and similarity assessment techniques. The approach involves storing key instances encountered during the learning phase and employing a similarity function to guide decision-making in new, unseen situations. This method is integrated into existing RL frameworks, allowing for seamless adoption and evaluation. Results/Findings: Experiments conducted on standard benchmark environments demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, with significant improvements in terms of generalization and policy performance compared to traditional RL methods. Our results highlight superior adaptability to novel scenarios, reducing the sample complexity and increasing the learning speed. The instance-based method consistently outperformed baseline models, affirming its capability to generalize from past experiences. Conclusion/Implications: The research contributes to the field of reinforcement learning by providing a scalable and effective solution to the generalization problem. The instance-based generalization framework not only enhances RL performance but also broadens the applicability of these algorithms to more complex real-world tasks. The insights gained open new avenues for developing RL systems capable of learning with less data and adapting to dynamic environments. Keywords associated with this research include reinforcement learning, instance memory, generalization, adaptability, and policy performance.

This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark on optimization techniques for large-scale image retrieval systems. The objective is to investigate the effectiveness of various tricks, including indexing methods, query optimization, and feature extraction techniques, in improving the efficiency and accuracy of image retrieval. We employ a range of state-of-the-art models and algorithms, such as convolutional neural networks and approximate nearest neighbor search, to evaluate the performance of different tricks on multiple large-scale image datasets. Our results show that the proposed benchmark provides a significant improvement in retrieval accuracy and efficiency, outperforming existing methods by a substantial margin. The key findings highlight the importance of carefully selecting and combining tricks to achieve optimal performance. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and accurate large-scale image retrieval systems, with potential applications in computer vision, robotics, and multimedia analysis. The benchmark provides a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners, enabling the evaluation and comparison of different techniques for large-scale image retrieval. Key keywords: image retrieval, large-scale datasets, convolutional neural networks, approximate nearest neighbor search, benchmarking.

This paper addresses the challenge of imbalanced data in corporate credit rating prediction, a critical task in financial risk assessment. Traditional machine learning methods often struggle with class imbalance, leading to biased predictions and undermined reliability in identifying companies with poor creditworthiness. To overcome this, we propose a novel contrastive pre-training framework tailored to enhance the representation learning of underrepresented rating categories. Our approach leverages contrastive learning to distinguish subtle differences between similar credit profiles, ensuring improved feature discrimination even under severe imbalance. We conduct extensive experiments using real-world corporate credit rating datasets, benchmarking our method against classic and state-of-the-art techniques, including oversampling and cost-sensitive learning. The results demonstrate significant improvements in both minority class recall and overall classification metrics, highlighting the robustness and adaptability of our approach. Notably, our method requires no domain-specific data augmentation, preserving the integrity of financial information. In conclusion, the proposed contrastive pre-training method presents a scalable and effective solution for imbalanced corporate credit rating prediction, offering valuable insights for financial institutions and credit risk analysts. Keywords: contrastive learning, pre-training, class imbalance, corporate credit rating, financial risk assessment, machine learning.

Image segmentation is a critical task in computer vision with applications in medical imaging, autonomous driving, and object recognition. Watershed algorithms are widely used for image segmentation, but often suffer from over-segmentation. This paper introduces a novel approach to image segmentation that addresses the over-segmentation issue by employing a size-dependent single linkage clustering method on a watershed basin graph. The objective is to merge oversegmented regions based on their size and adjacency relationships. Specifically, watershed transformation is first applied to generate an initial segmentation. A graph is then constructed where nodes represent watershed basins and edges represent adjacency. A size-dependent single linkage clustering algorithm is applied to merge adjacent basins, prioritizing smaller regions for merging to reduce over-segmentation. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on standard benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to traditional watershed and graph-based segmentation methods. The results show the algorithm effectively reduces over-segmentation while preserving meaningful boundaries, leading to more accurate and visually appealing image segmentations. This approach offers a robust and efficient solution for image segmentation with potential applications across various domains. Keywords: Image Segmentation, Watershed Algorithm, Graph-Based Segmentation, Single Linkage Clustering, Over-segmentation, Computer Vision.

Objective: Thin structures such as blood vessels, wires, or cracks often occupy only a few pixels in high-resolution images, making their restoration under large missing regions particularly challenging. This paper addresses the problem of blind inpainting for large-scale masks occluding thin structures, where neither the occlusion shape nor the underlying content is known. Methods: We propose a two-stage deep learning framework that combines adversarial training with reinforcement learning. First, a generative adversarial network (GAN) learns to produce initial inpainting results guided by a structure-preserving loss that emphasizes continuity and thin-line coherence. Second, a reinforcement learning (RL) agent refines these results through sequential patch selection, using a reward function that balances local detail recovery and global consistency. The RL agent adaptively focuses on hard-to-recover regions, dynamically adjusting its inpainting strategy based on feedback from a discriminator network. Results: Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets (including medical angiograms and urban aerial imagery) demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art blind inpainting and general image restoration models by 12–18% in structural similarity (SSIM) and reduces thin-line discontinuities by up to 25%. Qualitative evaluations show sharper, more coherent reconstructions of occluded filaments and curves. Conclusion: By integrating adversarial learning with reinforcement-driven refinement, our approach offers a robust solution for the blind inpainting of thin structures under extensive occlusion. This framework can be readily adapted to applications in medical image analysis, infrastructure inspection, and historical document restoration. Keywords: blind inpainting, thin structures, generative adversarial network, reinforcement learning, image restoration.

This paper addresses the challenge of sparse coral classification, a crucial task for marine conservation efforts. Our objective is to develop an accurate and efficient method for classifying coral species from sparse and varied image data. We propose a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) approach, leveraging transfer learning and fine-tuning techniques to adapt to the unique characteristics of coral images. Our method utilizes a compact and efficient architecture, enabling real-time classification on resource-constrained devices. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving high accuracy and outperforming traditional machine learning methods. The key findings of this research highlight the potential of deep learning for coral classification, with significant implications for automated monitoring and conservation efforts. Our contributions include the development of a novel CNN architecture and the creation of a large, annotated dataset for sparse coral classification. This research has important applications in marine biology, ecology, and conservation, with key keywords including coral classification, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, marine conservation, and image classification.

This research addresses the robustness challenges faced by Sequential Neural Processes (SNPs), a class of models highly effective in modeling complex sequential data. SNPs often encounter difficulties related to noise and data variability, which can impede their predictive accuracy and reliability. Methods/Approach: To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel framework that integrates adversarial training techniques with a carefully crafted noise-augmentation strategy. The framework enhances the robustness of SNPs by augmenting their ability to generalize across diverse input conditions. We employ a hybrid model architecture that unifies deterministic and stochastic pathways, improving the resilience of predictions against noisy and incomplete data. Results/Findings: Our approach demonstrates substantial improvements in robustness across various benchmark datasets, including time-series forecasting and trajectory prediction tasks. Quantitative evaluations show that the proposed method outperforms baseline SNP models and traditional neural process architectures by reducing error rates and increasing model reliability under noise-induced conditions. Additionally, comparative studies with existing robust learning techniques highlight the enhanced capacity of our model to maintain performance consistency. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of robustifying methods in SNP architectures underscores a significant advancement in their applicability for real-world scenarios where data quality cannot always be ensured. The contributions of this study pave the way for deploying SNPs in critical applications like financial forecasting and autonomous systems, where robustness is paramount. Key Keywords: Sequential Neural Processes, robustness, adversarial training, noise augmentation, time-series forecasting.

This paper introduces a novel approach for one-shot semantic part segmentation by repurposing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Addressing the challenge of limited labeled data, our method leverages the generative capabilities of GANs, pre-trained on relevant image datasets, to synthesize diverse and realistic training examples with corresponding part segmentations. Specifically, we fine-tune the generator network to produce images conditioned on part segmentation maps, enabling the creation of a large, synthetic dataset from a single labeled example. A segmentation network is then trained on this synthetic data and evaluated on real-world images. Our experiments demonstrate that this GAN-repurposing strategy significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of part segmentation compared to traditional methods trained directly on limited real data. The proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in one-shot scenarios, offering a promising solution for semantic part segmentation in domains where labeled data is scarce. Keywords: GAN, semantic part segmentation, one-shot learning, data augmentation, image synthesis.

Abstract: This paper presents a novel deep learning framework for semantics-aware photo adjustment, aiming to enhance image quality by intelligently adapting adjustments to the semantic content within photographs. Traditional photo editing techniques often apply global or rudimentary local enhancements without considering the underlying scene semantics, leading to suboptimal or unnatural results. To address this limitation, we propose a semantics-guided adjustment network that leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract contextual features and segment images into meaningful regions, such as sky, vegetation, or human subjects. Each region undergoes adaptive adjustment based on its semantic category, allowing for targeted enhancement and preserving visual consistency throughout the image. Our approach is trained on a large-scale dataset annotated with both semantic maps and artist-curated adjustments, enabling the model to learn context-sensitive photo enhancement strategies. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art automatic and learning-based photo adjustment techniques in terms of both objective quality metrics and subjective user studies. The proposed deep semantics-aware adjustment not only provides visually appealing results but also offers a flexible tool for intelligent photo editing in applications such as photography, social media, and content creation. Keywords: deep learning, photo adjustment, semantic segmentation, image enhancement, convolutional neural networks, context-aware processing.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurate road detection in autonomous driving systems by leveraging the complementary advantages of LIDAR and camera data. The integration of these modalities aims to enhance environmental perception, crucial for improving navigation safety and efficiency. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach utilizing fully convolutional neural networks (FCNNs) to achieve robust road detection through LIDAR-camera fusion. The system incorporates a multi-layer architecture that processes and fuses the dense, spatial LIDAR data with high-resolution camera images. The FCNN is designed to jointly learn and predict road boundaries, optimizing data fusion strategies at various levels of the network architecture. Results/Findings: Experiments demonstrate that our fusion model significantly outperforms baseline methods relying on single-sensor input. The network achieves higher precision and recall rates in detecting road areas, demonstrating robustness across varying light and weather conditions prevalent in urban driving scenarios. Comparative analysis with other state-of-the-art fusion techniques reveals an enhancement in classification performance and computational efficiency. Conclusion/Implications: The research introduces a novel FCNN-based approach for multisensor data fusion, marking a significant step forward in road detection for autonomous vehicles. This work not only offers a deeper integration of LIDAR and vision data but also sets the groundwork for future developments in the field. Its application potential spans the broader domains of intelligent transportation systems and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), promising to enhance the reliability and safety of next-generation autonomous vehicles. Keywords: LIDAR, camera fusion, fully convolutional neural networks, road detection, autonomous driving, multisensor integration, environmental perception.

In this paper, we explore a formalized set of axioms defining rational behavior in the context of Reinforcement Learning (RL), aiming to bridge the gap between theoretical foundations and practical applications. The purpose of our research is to establish clear criteria and principles that govern rational decision-making processes in RL agents. We propose a novel framework of axioms inspired by classical decision theory and adapted to the dynamics of RL environments. Our approach involves constructing a mathematical model that encapsulates these axioms, facilitating the analysis and development of RL algorithms that align with rationality standards. Through rigorous experimentation, we apply our framework to a suite of benchmark tasks, demonstrating notable improvements in agent performance and decision consistency compared to existing methodologies. The findings reveal that adherence to these axioms not only enhances the logical coherence of decisions but also optimizes long-term reward acquisition. This research contributes to the field by providing a robust theoretical basis for evaluating and constructing RL systems, offering insights into the design of more effective algorithms. Potential applications of our axiomatized approach include autonomous systems, game theory, and strategic planning, where rational agent behavior is paramount. Keywords: reinforcement learning, rationality, decision-making, axioms, RL algorithms, theoretical model.

This paper presents an empirical evaluation of a Q-Learning algorithm applied to the challenging problem of model-free autonomous soaring. The objective is to develop an agent capable of autonomously exploiting thermal updrafts to maximize flight time and distance without prior knowledge of the environment. We implemented a discrete-state, discrete-action Q-Learning algorithm and evaluated its performance in a realistic simulated soaring environment. The agent learns to select optimal actions based on sensed atmospheric conditions, including altitude, airspeed, and estimated thermal strength. Results demonstrate the algorithm's ability to discover effective soaring strategies, achieving significant improvements in flight duration and distance compared to a baseline policy. Performance is further analyzed by examining the learned Q-values and agent trajectories. The findings suggest that Q-Learning provides a viable approach for autonomous soaring, even in the absence of a precise environmental model. The research contributes to the field of reinforcement learning for autonomous flight and highlights the potential for real-world applications in areas such as environmental monitoring and aerial exploration. **Keywords:** Q-Learning, Autonomous Soaring, Reinforcement Learning, Autonomous Flight, Model-Free Control, Thermal Updrafts.

This paper introduces the Signal Transformer, a novel framework designed to enhance signal recognition tasks through the integration of complex-valued attention mechanisms and meta-learning. The objective of this research is to address the limitations of traditional signal processing methods, which often struggle with non-stationary and high-dimensional signals. The proposed approach leverages a complex-valued attention mechanism to capture intricate phase and amplitude relationships within signals, enabling more robust feature extraction. Additionally, meta-learning is employed to adapt the model to diverse signal environments, improving generalization across varying conditions. Experiments conducted on benchmark signal datasets demonstrate that the Signal Transformer outperforms existing methods in terms of recognition accuracy and computational efficiency. Key findings reveal significant improvements in handling noisy and low-resolution signals, with a 15% increase in accuracy compared to state-of-the-art models. The framework’s ability to generalize across different signal types highlights its potential for real-world applications, such as wireless communication, medical imaging, and radar systems. This research contributes a scalable and adaptive solution to signal recognition, paving the way for advancements in domains requiring precise and efficient signal analysis. **Keywords**: Signal Transformer, complex-valued attention, meta-learning, signal recognition, feature extraction, adaptive learning.

**Abstract:** Deep video completion aims to restore missing or corrupted regions of video sequences in a temporally consistent and visually plausible manner. In this paper, we introduce Onion-Peel Networks, a novel deep learning framework designed specifically for video completion tasks. The proposed approach leverages a hierarchical, layered architecture that incrementally reconstructs missing content from the outer boundaries inward, mimicking the natural "peeling" process of an onion. This design allows the model to effectively exploit spatial and temporal dependencies across video frames, leading to more stable and coherent inpainting results. We implement our method using an encoder-decoder backbone with multiple iterative refinement stages, each responsible for filling progressively deeper masked regions while maintaining context consistency. Extensive experiments on benchmark video datasets demonstrate that Onion-Peel Networks outperform existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both quantitative metrics, such as PSNR and SSIM, and qualitative assessments of visual realism. Furthermore, our model exhibits superior generalization to diverse video content and mask patterns. The results highlight the effectiveness of hierarchical region reconstruction and provide valuable insights for future developments in video restoration, editing, and augmented reality applications. Key keywords: deep video completion, Onion-Peel Networks, hierarchical reconstruction, video inpainting, temporal consistency.

We report the application of machine learning to smartphone based colorimetric detection of pH values. The strip images were used as the training set for Least Squares-Support Vector Machine (LS-SVM) classifier algorithms that were able to successfully classify the distinct pH values. The difference in the obtained image formats was found not to significantly affect the performance of the proposed machine learning approach. Moreover, the influence of the illumination conditions on the perceived color of pH strips was investigated and further experiments were carried out to study effect of color change on the learning model. Test results on JPEG, RAW and RAW-corrected image formats captured in different lighting conditions lead to perfect classification accuracy, sensitivity and specificity, which proves that the colorimetric detection using machine learning based systems is able to adapt to various experimental conditions and is a great candidate for smartphone based sensing in paper-based colorimetric assays.

Conditional image generation has emerged as a critical area in computer vision, enabling the synthesis of realistic images based on specific input conditions. However, evaluating the quality and relevance of generated images remains a significant challenge due to the lack of standardized metrics. This paper addresses this gap by proposing a comprehensive framework for evaluating conditional image generation models. We introduce a set of novel metrics that assess both the fidelity of generated images to the input conditions and their perceptual quality. Our approach combines quantitative measures, such as conditional consistency and diversity, with human perceptual studies to ensure a robust evaluation. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed metrics in distinguishing between state-of-the-art models and providing actionable insights for model improvement. The results highlight the importance of aligning evaluation metrics with the specific goals of conditional image generation tasks. This work contributes to the field by offering a standardized evaluation toolkit, facilitating fair comparisons, and guiding future advancements in conditional image synthesis. **Keywords**: conditional image generation, evaluation metrics, perceptual quality, image fidelity, computer vision, generative models.

This paper introduces U-GAT-IT, a novel unsupervised generative attentional network designed for image-to-image translation tasks. The objective is to develop a framework that can effectively translate images from one domain to another without requiring paired training data. U-GAT-IT employs a combination of generative adversarial networks (GANs) and attention mechanisms, along with adaptive layer-instance normalization, to achieve high-quality image translations. Our approach integrates advanced optimization techniques with probabilistic inference, ensuring faster convergence without compromising the quality of the approximation. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithms achieve up to 40% faster convergence compared to traditional EP methods, while maintaining comparable or superior accuracy. Furthermore, we provide theoretical insights into the conditions under which our algorithms guarantee convergence. The proposed methods are particularly beneficial for applications requiring real-time inference, such as online learning and large-scale Bayesian networks. This work contributes to the broader field of probabilistic machine learning by offering a scalable and efficient solution for approximate Bayesian inference, with potential applications in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and decision-making systems. **Keywords**: Expectation Propagation, Bayesian Inference, Fast Convergence, Adaptive Optimization, Probabilistic Machine Learning, Real-Time Inference.

The rapid expansion of neural network models in various applications has led to increased computational and storage demands. This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing these models by introducing SQuantizer, a novel approach for simultaneously learning both sparse and low-precision neural networks, aiming to reduce their resource consumption without compromising performance. Methods: SQuantizer employs a unified training framework that integrates sparsity and quantization techniques within the learning process, allowing models to efficiently leverage both techniques concurrently. This approach utilizes adaptive gradient methods to dynamically adjust weights, achieving an optimal trade-off between sparsity and precision. The method was tested across various model architectures and tasks to verify its effectiveness and generalizability. Results: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that SQuantizer effectively reduces model size and computational requirements, achieving significant improvements in both storage efficiency and inference speed. When compared with existing state-of-the-art methods, SQuantizer consistently outperforms in terms of model compression rates and accuracy retention across multiple benchmark datasets and neural network structures. Conclusion: SQuantizer presents a significant advancement in the field of model optimization by enabling the parallel learning of sparse and low-precision characteristics within a single framework. This innovation not only enhances the deployability of neural networks on resource-constrained devices but also contributes to the broader goal of sustainable AI deployment. The proposed method holds potential applications in areas where efficient resource usage is critical, such as on-device AI, edge computing, and IoT systems. Keywords: SQuantizer, neural networks, sparsity, low-precision, model optimization, adaptive gradient methods, AI efficiency, edge computing.

In the emerging high mobility Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications using millimeter Wave (mmWave) and sub-THz, Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) channel estimation is an extremely challenging task. At mmWaves/sub-THz frequencies, MIMO channels exhibit few leading paths in the space-time domain (i.e., directions or arrival/departure and delays). Algebraic Low-rank (LR) channel estimation exploits space-time channel sparsity through the computation of position-dependent MIMO channel eigenmodes leveraging recurrent training vehicle passages in the coverage cell. LR requires vehicles' geographical positions and tens to hundreds of training vehicles' passages for each position, leading to significant complexity and control signalling overhead. Here we design a DL-based LR channel estimation method to infer MIMO channel eigenmodes in V2X urban settings, starting from a single LS channel estimate and without needing vehicle's position information. Numerical results show that the proposed method attains comparable Mean Squared Error (MSE) performance as the position-based LR. Moreover, we show that the proposed model can be trained on a reference scenario and be effectively transferred to urban contexts with different space-time channel features, providing comparable MSE performance without an explicit transfer learning procedure. This result eases the deployment in arbitrary dense urban scenarios.

This paper investigates the robustness of Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures when subjected to adversarial examples, a critical concern in deploying deep learning models for computer vision tasks. The primary objective is to evaluate the vulnerability of ViTs compared to conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) under various adversarial attack scenarios. We employ a suite of adversarial attack methods—including Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM), Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), and AutoAttack—to systematically assess the resilience of several ViT variants across standard image classification benchmarks. A comprehensive experimental framework is implemented, incorporating both white-box and black-box attack settings, to measure classification accuracy, perturbation sensitivity, and transferability of adversarial examples. Our findings reveal that while ViTs demonstrate improved robustness against certain low-intensity perturbations, they also exhibit unique failure modes distinct from CNNs, particularly under high-intensity or transfer-based attacks. Furthermore, we explore the impact of adversarial training and input preprocessing as mitigation strategies, highlighting their effectiveness in enhancing ViT robustness. These results provide key insights into the security profile of transformer-based vision models and underscore the necessity for specialized defense mechanisms tailored to their unique architecture. Our work contributes to advancing the understanding of adversarial robustness in vision models and informs the design of more secure AI systems. Keywords: Vision Transformers, adversarial examples, robustness, deep learning, computer vision, adversarial attacks, security.

Semantic segmentation aims to classify each pixel in an image, a task crucial for various applications including autonomous driving and medical imaging. However, achieving accurate segmentation, especially along object boundaries, remains a challenge. This paper introduces Boundary Neural Fields (BNF), a novel approach that integrates neural implicit representations into the semantic segmentation pipeline to explicitly model and refine object boundaries. BNF learns a continuous, signed distance function representing object boundaries, allowing for precise localization. We train BNF jointly with a standard semantic segmentation network, enabling the segmentation network to leverage boundary information. Experiments on Cityscapes and Pascal VOC datasets demonstrate that BNF improves segmentation accuracy, particularly at object boundaries, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The proposed method effectively combines the strengths of neural implicit representations and semantic segmentation, leading to enhanced boundary delineation and overall segmentation quality. This research contributes a new perspective on semantic segmentation by incorporating continuous boundary information, opening avenues for further exploration in high-precision segmentation tasks. Keywords: Semantic Segmentation, Neural Implicit Representation, Boundary Detection, Deep Learning, Computer Vision.

Quantitative evaluation has increased dramatically among recent video inpainting work, but the video and mask content used to gauge performance has received relatively little attention. Although attributes such as camera and background scene motion inherently change the difficulty of the task and affect methods differently, existing evaluation schemes fail to control for them, thereby providing minimal insight into inpainting failure modes. To address this gap, we propose the Diagnostic Evaluation of Video Inpainting on Landscapes (DEVIL) benchmark, which consists of two contributions: (i) a novel dataset of videos and masks labeled according to several key inpainting failure modes, and (ii) an evaluation scheme that samples slices of the dataset characterized by a fixed content attribute, and scores performance on each slice according to reconstruction, realism, and temporal consistency quality. By revealing systematic changes in performance induced by particular characteristics of the input content, our challenging benchmark enables more insightful analysis into video inpainting methods and serves as an invaluable diagnostic tool for the field. Our code is available at https://github.com/MichiganCOG/devil .

Công nghệ 5G đang mở ra kỷ nguyên mới với tốc độ truyền dữ liệu cực cao, đặc biệt là ở dải tần milimet. Thiết kế này tận dụng hình dạng độc đáo của hai nửa vòng tròn để tối ưu hóa hiệu suất bức xạ và độ lợi, đồng thời giảm thiểu nhiễu giữa các kênh. Vật liệu β-Ga2O3 pha tạp ion Cr được chế tạo bằng phương pháp khuếch tán nhiệt, mở ra tiềm năng ứng dụng rộng rãi trong các thiết bị quang điện tử. Quá trình này cho phép kiểm soát nồng độ và sự phân bố của Cr trong cấu trúc tinh thể, từ đó điều chỉnh các tính chất quang học của vật liệu. Nghiên cứu sâu về tính chất phát quang của vật liệu cho thấy sự tồn tại của các vạch phát xạ đặc trưng của ion Cr3+, đồng thời làm rõ ảnh hưởng của nhiệt độ ủ đến cường độ và thời gian sống của phát quang. Kết quả phân tích quang phổ kích thích phát quang cung cấp thông tin quan trọng về cơ chế hấp thụ và truyền năng lượng trong vật liệu. Việc khảo sát chi tiết này không chỉ giúp hiểu rõ hơn về các đặc tính cơ bản của β-Ga2O3 pha tạp Cr mà còn tạo tiền đề cho việc tối ưu hóa vật liệu, hướng đến các ứng dụng cụ thể như cảm biến quang, laser và các thiết bị phát sáng hiệu quả.

Thiết kế giàn thép chịu tải trọng động đất là một lĩnh vực quan trọng trong xây dựng công trình, đặc biệt ở những khu vực có nguy cơ xảy ra động đất cao. Phân tích trực tiếp được áp dụng để đánh giá khả năng chịu lực và độ bền của giàn thép dưới tác động của các lực động đất. Phương pháp này cho phép các kỹ sư mô phỏng chính xác các tình huống khác nhau, từ đó tối ưu hóa thiết kế nhằm đảm bảo an toàn và hiệu quả kinh tế. Việc sử dụng các phần mềm phân tích hiện đại giúp rút ngắn thời gian thiết kế và nâng cao độ chính xác trong việc dự đoán hành vi của kết cấu khi chịu tải trọng động đất. Kết quả từ các nghiên cứu này không chỉ góp phần nâng cao chất lượng công trình mà còn bảo vệ tính mạng con người và tài sản trong các tình huống khẩn cấp.

Lợn đực Piétrain là một trong những giống lợn được ưa chuộng trên toàn thế giới nhờ vào khả năng sinh sản và tăng trưởng nhanh chóng. Tuy nhiên, việc chọn lọc đối với giống lợn này đã dẫn đến tình trạng tăng khối lượng trung bình của chúng, ảnh hưởng đến sức khỏe và chất lượng thịt. Giá trị giống ức tính của lợn đực Piétrain đã được đánh giá cao nhờ vào khả năng sinh sản và tăng trưởng nhanh chóng. Chúng có thể sinh sản từ 2-3 lứa mỗi năm, với số lượng con non trung bình khoảng 12-15 con. Tuy nhiên, việc chọn lọc đối với giống lợn này đã dẫn đến tình trạng tăng khối lượng trung bình của chúng, từ 100-150 kg trở lên. Tình trạng tăng khối lượng trung bình của lợn đực Piétrain đã gây ra nhiều vấn đề về sức khỏe và chất lượng thịt. Chúng dễ bị mắc các bệnh về xương và cơ, cũng như tăng nguy cơ mắc các bệnh về tim mạch. Ngoài ra, thịt của chúng cũng có thể chứa nhiều chất béo và ít chất dinh dưỡng. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, các nhà sản xuất lợn cần phải thay đổi chiến lược chọn lọc và chăm sóc để giảm thiểu tình trạng tăng khối lượng trung bình của lợn đực Piétrain. Điều này có thể được thực hiện bằng cách chọn lọc các cá thể lợn có khả năng tăng trưởng chậm hơn, cũng như cung cấp cho chúng một chế độ ăn uống và chăm sóc tốt hơn.

The research addresses the challenge of accurately forecasting motion trajectories for autonomous driving vehicles, a critical component for ensuring safety and efficiency in autonomous systems. The study leverages the Waymo Open Motion Dataset to enhance predictive accuracy and interaction reasoning in large-scale driving scenarios. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel motion forecasting framework that integrates deep learning models with complex traffic interaction analysis. Utilizing a combination of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and attention mechanisms, the model captures both temporal dependencies and contextual interactions among multiple agents. The use of the extensive Waymo Open Motion Dataset allows for robust training and validation across diverse real-world driving environments. Results/Findings: Our framework demonstrates significant improvements in motion prediction accuracy compared to existing methods. Key findings include enhancements in trajectory smoothness and interaction reasoning, resulting in a 15% reduction in prediction error. Comparative evaluations against state-of-the-art models reveal competitive performance, particularly in scenarios with dense traffic and complex interactions. Conclusion/Implications: This study contributes to the field of autonomous driving by providing a scalable and effective solution for interactive motion forecasting. The proposed method's efficacy in utilizing comprehensive datasets like the Waymo Open Motion Dataset underscores its potential for real-world applications. The insights gained from this research facilitate advancements in autonomous driving systems, improving both safety and operational performance. Key terms include motion forecasting, autonomous driving, Waymo Open Motion Dataset, deep learning, and traffic interaction modeling.

This paper presents a novel approach to inverse reinforcement learning, introducing Deep Adaptive Multi-Intention Inverse Reinforcement Learning (DAMIRL). The objective is to develop an algorithm that can effectively learn multiple intentions behind an expert's behavior in complex environments. To achieve this, we propose a deep learning-based framework that adaptively identifies and learns from demonstrations of multiple intentions. Our approach utilizes a combination of reinforcement learning and intention-aware modeling to improve the efficiency and accuracy of learning. The results show that DAMIRL outperforms existing methods in learning complex behaviors and generalizing to new situations. Key findings include improved performance in multi-intention scenarios and enhanced robustness to variations in expert demonstrations. The proposed method has significant implications for areas such as robotics, autonomous driving, and human-computer interaction, where understanding and replicating complex human behaviors is crucial. By introducing a novel deep adaptive framework, this research contributes to the advancement of inverse reinforcement learning and intention-aware modeling, with potential applications in AI, machine learning, and robotics. Keywords: inverse reinforcement learning, multi-intention learning, deep learning, adaptive modeling, intention-aware systems.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of modeling and predicting nonstationary processes that are prevalent in real-world applications. Gaussian Processes (GPs) are powerful tools for modeling uncertainties but have traditionally struggled with nonstationarity, thus limiting their impact in dynamic environments where such conditions are common. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative approach to efficiently learn nonstationary Gaussian Processes by incorporating adaptive kernel functions that dynamically adjust to changing patterns in data. Our method leverages a novel algorithmic framework that optimizes the learning process, ensuring the scalability and adaptability required for large-scale, real-world applications. The model is designed to seamlessly integrate with existing GP frameworks, enhancing its usability and accessibility for practitioners. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances the predictive performance of GPs in nonstationary settings, outperforming traditional stationary GPs and other state-of-the-art methods. The proposed algorithm exhibits superior adaptability and accuracy in capturing the underlying data dynamics, enabling more precise forecasts. Benchmarked against real-world datasets, our method shows a marked improvement in prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Conclusion/Implications: The advancements presented in this study open new avenues for the application of Gaussian Processes in nonstationary environments, such as financial markets, climate modeling, and real-time sensor data analysis. Our contributions provide a step forward in making Gaussian Processes a more versatile and robust tool, facilitating their application in a wider range of scenarios that demand responsiveness to changing conditions. The proposed method significantly broadens the potential for real-world impact, making nonstationary GPs more practical and effective in complex and dynamic domains. Keywords: Gaussian Processes, nonstationarity, adaptive kernel, predictive modeling, real-world applications, algorithmic framework, scalability.

Scene text recognition often involves linking individual character predictions to form complete words, a task where traditional methods struggle with irregular layouts and complex backgrounds. This paper introduces NENET, a novel Edge Learnable Network designed specifically for robust link prediction in scene text. NENET employs a graph-based approach, representing characters as nodes and potential links between them as edges. The network utilizes a custom graph neural network architecture, enabling edges to learn and adapt based on contextual information extracted from both character features and their spatial relationships. This allows NENET to dynamically model the complex dependencies crucial for accurate link prediction. Experimental results on challenging scene text datasets demonstrate that NENET significantly outperforms existing link prediction methods, particularly in scenarios with irregular text and noisy backgrounds, achieving a 15% improvement in F1-score on average. The proposed approach offers a more flexible and accurate solution for scene text recognition by enabling edges to learn, contributing to more robust and reliable text extraction in real-world images. Keywords: Scene Text Recognition, Link Prediction, Graph Neural Network, Edge Learning, Computer Vision.

Addressing the challenges of annotation scarcity and domain shifts in machine learning, this paper introduces a novel framework termed "Extreme Consistency" for robust model training. Our approach leverages consistency regularization techniques, specifically designed to enforce consistent predictions across diverse data augmentations and simulated domain variations. We propose a multi-faceted augmentation strategy incorporating both traditional image transformations and adversarial perturbations to enhance model invariance. Empirical evaluations on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing semi-supervised and domain adaptation techniques, particularly when labeled data is limited and the target domain differs substantially from the source domain. Specifically, we observe a 15% improvement in accuracy on a challenging cross-domain image classification task. The findings highlight the efficacy of Extreme Consistency in promoting generalization and reducing reliance on extensive labeled data. Keywords: Consistency Regularization, Semi-Supervised Learning, Domain Adaptation, Data Augmentation, Machine Learning, Generalization, Adversarial Perturbations.

This paper explores the problem of reconstructing high-resolution light field (LF) images from hybrid lenses, including a high-resolution camera surrounded by multiple low-resolution cameras. To tackle this challenge, we propose a novel end-to-end learning-based approach, which can comprehensively utilize the specific characteristics of the input from two complementary and parallel perspectives. Specifically, one module regresses a spatially consistent intermediate estimation by learning a deep multidimensional and cross-domain feature representation; the other one constructs another intermediate estimation, which maintains the high-frequency textures, by propagating the information of the high-resolution view. We finally leverage the advantages of the two intermediate estimations via the learned attention maps, leading to the final high-resolution LF image. Extensive experiments demonstrate the significant superiority of our approach over state-of-the-art ones. That is, our method not only improves the PSNR by more than 2 dB, but also preserves the LF structure much better. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end deep learning method for reconstructing a high-resolution LF image with a hybrid input. We believe our framework could potentially decrease the cost of high-resolution LF data acquisition and also be beneficial to LF data storage and transmission. The code is available at https://github.com/jingjin25/LFhybridSR-Fusion.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing video quality in real-time applications, focusing on improving both visual clarity and computational efficiency. Traditional video enhancement methods often struggle to balance accuracy and speed, particularly when dealing with sparse depth information. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel framework that leverages sparse depth data to guide the enhancement process, enabling faster and more accurate results. Our approach integrates a lightweight neural network architecture optimized for sparse depth inputs, combined with a multi-scale feature extraction mechanism to preserve fine details. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant improvements in video quality, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both processing speed and enhancement accuracy. Specifically, our framework reduces computational overhead by 30% while maintaining superior visual fidelity, as validated on benchmark datasets. The findings highlight the potential of sparse depth-guided video enhancement for real-world applications, such as augmented reality, autonomous driving, and video surveillance. This research contributes a scalable and efficient solution that bridges the gap between real-time performance and high-quality video enhancement, paving the way for future advancements in the field. **Keywords**: video enhancement, sparse depth, real-time processing, neural networks, computational efficiency.

The mainstream image captioning models rely on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) image features to generate captions via recurrent models. Recently, image scene graphs have been used to augment captioning models so as to leverage their structural semantics, such as object entities, relationships and attributes. Several studies have noted that the naive use of scene graphs from a black-box scene graph generator harms image captioning performance and that scene graph-based captioning models have to incur the overhead of explicit use of image features to generate decent captions. Addressing these challenges, we propose \textbf, a framework that utilizes only the scene graph labels for competitive image captioning performance. The basic idea is to close the semantic gap between the two scene graphs - one derived from the input image and the other from its caption. In order to achieve this, we leverage the spatial location of objects and the Human-Object-Interaction (HOI) labels as an additional HOI graph. SG2Caps outperforms existing scene graph-only captioning models by a large margin, indicating scene graphs as a promising representation for image captioning. Direct utilization of scene graph labels avoids expensive graph convolutions over high-dimensional CNN features resulting in 49% fewer trainable parameters. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Kien085/SG2Caps

Các nghiên cứu cũng cho thấy rằng fucoidan chiết xuất từ rong nâu Tubinaria decurrens có thể có các đặc tính chống oxy hóa và chống viêm mạnh mẽ, giúp bảo vệ cơ thể khỏi các tác động tiêu cực của các gốc tự do và viêm nhiễm. Điều này cho thấy rằng fucoidan có thể là một thành phần quan trọng trong các sản phẩm chăm sóc sức khỏe và mỹ phẩm. Tổng kết, phương pháp chiết fucoidan từ rong nâu Tubinaria decurrens bằng phương pháp chiết đã được tối ưu hóa, giúp tăng cường hiệu suất chiết và giảm thiểu chi phí. Fucoidan chiết xuất từ rong nâu Tubinaria decurrens cũng có thể có các đặc tính chống oxy hóa và chống viêm mạnh mẽ, giúp bảo vệ cơ thể khỏi các tác động tiêu cực.

This paper introduces DeepV2D, a novel approach to estimate depth from monocular videos by leveraging differentiable structure from motion. The objective is to accurately recover 3D scene geometry from 2D video sequences, addressing the long-standing challenge of depth estimation in computer vision. Our method employs a deep learning framework that integrates structure from motion principles, enabling end-to-end training and optimization. By combining convolutional neural networks with differentiable pose estimation, DeepV2D achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in depth accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenes with complex motion and occlusions. The proposed approach has far-reaching implications for applications such as 3D reconstruction, autonomous driving, and augmented reality. Key contributions include a differentiable structure from motion module, a novel depth estimation architecture, and a large-scale dataset for video-based depth estimation. Relevant keywords: depth estimation, structure from motion, differentiable rendering, monocular video, 3D reconstruction, computer vision, deep learning.
