This paper investigates the use of synthetic data for training robust text localisation models in natural images. The objective is to mitigate the challenges of limited and biased real-world data by leveraging synthetically generated images with accurately annotated text. We propose a novel pipeline for creating realistic synthetic scenes with diverse fonts, layouts, and background textures. This pipeline incorporates techniques for blending synthetic text into natural images, simulating various imaging conditions, and generating accurate ground truth annotations. We train a deep learning-based text localisation model using solely synthetic data and evaluate its performance on several benchmark datasets of real-world images. Our results demonstrate that models trained on synthetic data achieve competitive, and in some cases superior, performance compared to models trained on real data, especially in challenging scenarios with low resolution or complex backgrounds. We further explore the effectiveness of fine-tuning models trained on synthetic data with a small amount of real data to further boost performance. The findings indicate that synthetic data offers a viable and scalable alternative for training robust text localisation systems, reducing the reliance on expensive and time-consuming manual annotation. Keywords: Synthetic Data, Text Localisation, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, Natural Images.

This paper introduces a novel Contextual Residual Aggregation Network (CRAN) for ultra high-resolution image inpainting. The objective is to improve the coherence and realism of inpainted regions, especially for images exceeding 4K resolution, where existing methods often struggle with detail preservation and contextual understanding. CRAN leverages a multi-scale contextual attention mechanism to effectively capture long-range dependencies and integrate information from both local and global contexts. Furthermore, a residual aggregation module is proposed to progressively refine the inpainted regions by fusing features from different layers of the network, preserving fine-grained details and reducing artifacts. Experimental results on diverse datasets, including high-resolution landscape and architectural images, demonstrate that CRAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both quantitative metrics (PSNR, SSIM) and qualitative visual assessment. The proposed approach generates more visually plausible and contextually consistent inpainting results, even with large missing regions. This work contributes a robust framework for ultra high-resolution image inpainting with enhanced contextual awareness and detail preservation capabilities, offering significant potential for applications in image restoration, editing, and content creation. Keywords: Image Inpainting, Ultra High-Resolution, Contextual Attention, Residual Aggregation, Deep Learning, Image Restoration.

This paper addresses the challenge of mixed noise removal in hyperspectral images, a crucial task for enhancing image quality and subsequent analysis. Our objective is to develop an unsupervised deep learning approach that effectively removes mixed noise from hyperspectral images without requiring prior knowledge of noise distributions. We propose a novel Spatial-Spectral Constrained Deep Image Prior (SSCDIP) method, which leverages the spatial and spectral characteristics of hyperspectral images to regularize the denoising process. The SSCDIP model utilizes a deep neural network to learn the underlying clean image from the noisy input, constrained by spatial and spectral priors that promote consistency and coherence. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of SSCDIP in removing mixed noise from hyperspectral images, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of noise removal and image quality metrics. The proposed approach contributes to the field of hyperspectral image processing by providing a robust, unsupervised, and efficient solution for mixed noise removal, with potential applications in remote sensing, environmental monitoring, and surveillance. Key keywords: hyperspectral image denoising, deep image prior, spatial-spectral constraints, unsupervised learning, mixed noise removal.

These outcomes underscore the impactful contributions of this thesis in recognizing and addressing the limitations of FedAdp, offering a promising solution in FedImp to enhance the effectiveness of FL in the face of non-IID data distributions. This paper introduces a novel unsupervised learning framework for acquiring procedural knowledge from narrated instruction videos. Our approach addresses the challenge of learning sequential tasks without explicit action labels by leveraging the inherent structure present in paired video and speech data. We propose a method that uses temporal alignment between visual frames and spoken instructions to discover latent action segments. These segments are then clustered based on both visual similarity and the semantic content of the corresponding narration, forming a basis for learning action primitives. A key contribution is a dynamic time warping-based alignment algorithm, enhanced with cross-modal attention, enabling robust alignment even with noisy or imperfect narration. We evaluate our method on a dataset of cooking videos, demonstrating its ability to identify meaningful action sequences and achieve state-of-the-art performance in unsupervised action segmentation. Furthermore, we show how the learned action primitives can be used for video summarization and instruction following. This work paves the way for automated learning of procedural tasks from readily available online video resources, reducing the need for costly manual annotation. **Keywords:** Unsupervised Learning, Instruction Videos, Action Segmentation, Cross-Modal Alignment, Procedural Knowledge, Temporal Alignment, Video Analysis.

This paper presents a novel approach to compressing neural networks using adversarial techniques, aiming to reduce model size while preserving accuracy. Our objective is to develop an efficient compression method that can be applied to various deep learning architectures. We propose a framework that utilizes an adversarial agent to identify and eliminate redundant neurons, resulting in a compact model with minimal performance degradation. Our approach employs a generative adversarial network (GAN) to learn a compressed representation of the original model, which is then fine-tuned to maintain its predictive capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing compression techniques, achieving significant reductions in model size while maintaining competitive accuracy. The key contributions of this research include a novel adversarial compression algorithm, a comprehensive evaluation of its effectiveness, and insights into the application of GANs for model compression. This work has important implications for the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, such as edge devices and mobile applications, and highlights the potential of adversarial techniques for efficient model compression. Key keywords: neural network compression, adversarial learning, generative adversarial networks, deep learning, model pruning.

This paper addresses the challenge of audio classification by introducing a novel approach based on shift-invariance sparse coding. The objective is to improve the accuracy and robustness of audio classification systems by effectively capturing shift-invariant features from audio signals. Our method employs a sparse coding technique that incorporates shift-invariance, enabling the model to learn features that are invariant to time shifts and robust to variations in audio data. The approach is evaluated on several audio classification tasks, including music genre classification and speech recognition, and the results demonstrate significant improvements in performance compared to existing methods. Key findings include the ability of the proposed method to learn compact and informative representations of audio data, leading to improved classification accuracy and reduced computational complexity. The contributions of this research include the development of a shift-invariance sparse coding framework for audio classification, which has potential applications in music information retrieval, speech processing, and audio event detection. Relevant keywords for this research include sparse coding, shift-invariance, audio classification, music genre classification, and speech recognition.

This paper introduces Detective, a novel attentive recurrent model designed to tackle the challenging task of sparse object detection. The objective is to develop an efficient and accurate approach for detecting objects in scenarios where targets are scarce and scattered, posing significant difficulties for traditional detection methods. To address this problem, we propose a model that leverages the strengths of both attention mechanisms and recurrent neural networks. Our approach enables the model to focus on relevant regions of interest and iteratively refine its predictions, leading to improved detection performance. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of Detective, showcasing its ability to outperform state-of-the-art methods in sparse object detection tasks. Key findings include significant improvements in precision and recall, particularly in scenarios with limited training data. The contributions of this research lie in its innovative application of attentive recurrent architectures to sparse object detection, offering a unique solution to a long-standing problem in the field of computer vision. With its potential applications in areas such as surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and medical imaging, Detective represents a substantial advancement in object detection technology. Relevant keywords include sparse object detection, attentive recurrent models, computer vision, and deep learning.

This paper introduces a novel approach to monocular video visual odometry and depth estimation using a recurrent neural network (RNN) framework. Our method addresses the challenges of unsupervised and supervised learning by leveraging temporal coherence in video sequences to simultaneously predict camera pose and scene depth. The proposed network architecture incorporates a recurrent layer to effectively capture and exploit long-range dependencies between consecutive frames, leading to improved accuracy and robustness compared to existing single-frame methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including KITTI, showing competitive results in both supervised and unsupervised settings. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of different recurrent cell types and training strategies on the overall performance. Key findings highlight the importance of temporal context in learning accurate and consistent depth maps and pose estimations. The research contributes a robust and versatile framework for monocular visual odometry and depth estimation, suitable for applications in autonomous navigation and robotics. Keywords: Visual Odometry, Depth Estimation, Recurrent Neural Networks, Unsupervised Learning, Monocular Vision, Deep Learning.

This paper presents a novel approach to leaf and time series classification using a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The objective is to develop an efficient and accurate model for classifying leaf and time series data, which has numerous applications in fields such as botany, ecology, and environmental monitoring. Our approach utilizes a 1D CNN architecture, which is well-suited for sequential data, to extract relevant features from the input data. The network is trained and evaluated on a comprehensive dataset, comprising various leaf and time series samples. The results show that our model achieves high accuracy and outperforms traditional machine learning methods. The key findings of this research include the effectiveness of 1D CNNs in capturing temporal and spatial patterns in leaf and time series data, and the importance of data preprocessing and feature engineering in improving model performance. This study contributes to the development of deep learning-based methods for classification tasks and has potential applications in real-world scenarios, such as plant species identification and environmental monitoring. Key keywords: 1D CNN, leaf classification, time series classification, deep learning, pattern recognition.

This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing decision-making in reinforcement learning by proposing a novel approach that effectively combines policy gradient and Q-learning algorithms. Conventional policy gradient methods offer stable policy improvements through direct optimization of expected rewards but often suffer from high variance and slow convergence. In contrast, Q-learning provides efficient value estimation and off-policy learning but may struggle with instability in complex environments. Our proposed hybrid method leverages the strengths of both techniques by integrating the gradient-based policy updates with value-based action evaluations, enabling efficient exploration and robust learning. We detail the architecture, update rules, and training paradigm of our combined approach, demonstrating its capability to balance stability and efficiency. Experimental results on a suite of benchmark control tasks indicate that our method achieves higher sample efficiency and faster convergence compared to pure policy gradient or Q-learning approaches. Furthermore, the proposed framework exhibits improved robustness across environments with varying degrees of stochasticity. These findings highlight the potential of combining policy-based and value-based reinforcement learning strategies to advance the state-of-the-art in AI-driven sequential decision-making. Keywords: reinforcement learning, policy gradient, Q-learning, hybrid algorithms, sample efficiency, sequential decision-making.

The accurate classification of peanut maturity is critical for optimizing harvest timing and improving crop yield. This study addresses the challenge of non-destructively assessing peanut maturity by leveraging hyperspectral imagery, a technology capable of capturing detailed spectral information across a wide range of wavelengths. We propose a novel machine learning-based framework that processes hyperspectral data to classify peanut pods into distinct maturity stages. The approach involves preprocessing the hyperspectral images to reduce noise, followed by feature extraction using advanced dimensionality reduction techniques. A deep learning model, specifically a convolutional neural network (CNN), is then employed to classify the maturity stages based on the extracted spectral features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high classification accuracy, outperforming traditional methods that rely on manual inspection or limited spectral bands. The system's robustness is validated through extensive testing on diverse peanut varieties under varying environmental conditions. This research contributes to precision agriculture by providing a scalable, non-invasive solution for peanut maturity assessment, with potential applications in optimizing harvest schedules and enhancing crop quality. Key innovations include the integration of hyperspectral imaging with deep learning, offering a significant improvement over conventional approaches. Keywords: hyperspectral imagery, peanut maturity, machine learning, convolutional neural networks, precision agriculture.

The increasing demand for home services facilitated by technological advancements has led to a growing trend in mobile applications aimed at streamlining service delivery. However, the current marketplace often suffers from inefficiencies, lack of standardization, and inadequate user trust. This study seeks to address these shortcomings, emphasizing the importance of a reliable platform that not only connects service providers and consumers but also enhances the overall experience through improved transparency and communication. The primary objective of this thesis is to develop a mobile application that seamlessly integrates various home services, including cleaning, plumbing, and electrical work, while ensuring user satisfaction and service reliability. The research aims to tackle specific issues such as poor service quality, difficulty in finding trustworthy providers, and inefficient appointment scheduling. Utilizing modern technologies such as React Native for cross-platform development and Firebase for real-time database management, the proposed system architecture emphasizes user-friendly interfaces, secure transactions, and effective communication channels. Our methodology combines agile development practices with user feedback loops, allowing for continuous improvement and adaptation to user needs. The expected outcomes of this research include a fully functional mobile application that demonstrates enhanced service reliability, higher user engagement, and improved satisfaction rates. The contributions of this work extend to both the academic field and real-world applications, providing insights into the development of service-oriented platforms and influencing best practices for technology integration in home services. In conclusion, this thesis provides a comprehensive exploration of mobile applications for home services, underlining their significance in enhancing user experience and service delivery. Future developments could extend the model to include AI-driven features for predictive maintenance and personalized service recommendations, paving the way for further studies in automated home service management.

This paper introduces a novel unsupervised learning framework for recovering scene geometry and understanding holistic 3D motion from monocular video. Our approach leverages the principle that every pixel's motion contributes to the overall scene understanding, moving beyond sparse feature-based methods. We propose a differentiable framework that jointly estimates depth, camera pose, and object motion by minimizing a photometric reconstruction loss. A key innovation is the incorporation of a holistic motion prior, encouraging coherent and physically plausible movements of objects within the scene. This prior is enforced through a novel regularization term based on motion smoothness and object rigidity. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in unsupervised depth estimation and 3D scene flow, surpassing existing methods particularly in challenging scenarios with complex object interactions. The learned geometric representations and motion understanding have potential applications in robotics, autonomous driving, and augmented reality. Keywords: Unsupervised Learning, 3D Motion, Scene Geometry, Depth Estimation, Monocular Video, Holistic Motion, Computer Vision.

This paper aims to investigate the current state-of-the-art deep learning techniques for remote sensing applications where limited training data is available. The objective is to identify the gaps and challenges in existing methods and explore potential solutions to improve the performance of deep learning models in such scenarios. We employ a comprehensive review of recent studies, focusing on techniques such as transfer learning, data augmentation, and few-shot learning, to analyze their effectiveness in remote sensing tasks like image classification, object detection, and segmentation. Our analysis reveals that while these methods show promise, there are still significant gaps in their ability to generalize well to new, unseen data. The results highlight the need for more robust and adaptable deep learning architectures that can efficiently learn from limited labeled data. This research contributes to the development of more effective deep learning approaches for remote sensing applications, emphasizing the importance of addressing the challenges associated with limited training data. Key contributions include a thorough review of existing techniques, identification of gaps, and proposals for future research directions, ultimately enhancing the application of deep learning in remote sensing with limited data, and related fields like earth observation, geographic information systems, and environmental monitoring.

Contrastive Divergence (CD) is a widely used algorithm for training energy-based models, particularly in machine learning tasks like image recognition and natural language processing. Determining appropriate stopping criteria for CD training is crucial for achieving optimal model performance and avoiding overfitting. Traditionally, the reconstruction error is used as a primary indicator for convergence. This paper investigates alternative stopping criteria for CD training, exploring their effectiveness compared to the reconstruction error. We propose and evaluate several novel metrics based on the free energy difference and the gradient norm of the model parameters. Through experiments on benchmark datasets, we demonstrate that these alternative criteria can provide more robust and efficient stopping signals, leading to improved generalization performance and reduced training time. Specifically, monitoring the convergence of the free energy difference offers a more stable indication of learning progress, while the gradient norm provides insights into parameter stability. These findings suggest that relying solely on reconstruction error may be suboptimal, and alternative stopping criteria can significantly enhance the training process of energy-based models. Keywords: Contrastive Divergence, Stopping Criteria, Reconstruction Error, Energy-Based Models, Machine Learning, Free Energy, Gradient Norm, Convergence.

This study aims to improve the interpretability of deep glucose predictive models for diabetic individuals using the RETAIN algorithm. The objective is to develop a transparent and reliable system that can forecast glucose levels and provide personalized insights for patients. Our approach involves integrating RETAIN with deep learning architectures to analyze electronic health records and wearable device data. The results show that our model achieves high accuracy in glucose prediction and provides meaningful interpretations of the factors influencing glucose levels. Key findings indicate that the model can identify critical variables such as medication adherence, physical activity, and dietary habits that impact glucose control. The study concludes that the proposed approach has significant implications for clinical decision-making and patient empowerment, enabling diabetic individuals to make informed lifestyle choices. The use of RETAIN with deep learning techniques offers a novel contribution to the field, enhancing the transparency and trustworthiness of glucose predictive models. Relevant keywords: deep learning, glucose prediction, RETAIN, interpretability, diabetic care, electronic health records, wearable devices.

This paper explores the application of reinforcement learning (RL) to the complex task of soccer dribbling. The primary objective is to develop an autonomous agent capable of efficiently navigating a soccer field while maintaining control of the ball. We propose a novel reward function that encourages both forward progress and ball retention, alongside a deep Q-network (DQN) architecture tailored for continuous state and action spaces. The agent is trained within a simulated soccer environment, and its performance is evaluated based on dribbling speed, success rate, and distance traveled. Experimental results demonstrate that the RL-trained agent significantly outperforms hand-engineered control policies, achieving higher dribbling speeds and maintaining ball control for longer durations. This research contributes a practical RL framework for soccer dribbling, paving the way for more sophisticated autonomous soccer agents. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Soccer, Dribbling, Deep Q-Network, Autonomous Agents, Simulation.

Scene Text Recognition (STR) remains a challenging problem due to the large variance in text instance scales. This paper introduces SAFE, a Scale Aware Feature Encoder, designed to explicitly address this scale variance. SAFE incorporates a multi-scale feature extraction module based on a feature pyramid network that captures contextual information at different scales, followed by a scale-aware attention mechanism to adaptively weight these multi-scale features based on the input text instance. The attention mechanism is trained to predict the scale of the text instance, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant features for recognition. Experiments on standard benchmarks, including ICDAR2013, ICDAR2015, and IIIT5k, demonstrate that SAFE outperforms existing STR methods, especially on datasets with significant scale variations. The results highlight the effectiveness of scale-aware feature encoding in improving the robustness and accuracy of STR systems. Our approach offers a significant improvement for reading text in complex scenes, contributing a novel and effective method for handling scale variations. Keywords: Scene Text Recognition, Scale Awareness, Feature Pyramid Network, Attention Mechanism, Multi-Scale Feature Extraction.

Instance segmentation, a fundamental task in computer vision, demands precise pixel-level classification and object delineation. This paper introduces DCT-Mask, a novel mask representation method leveraging the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) to achieve compact and efficient instance segmentation. Unlike traditional pixel-based or contour-based mask representations, DCT-Mask represents each instance mask as a low-frequency coefficient map obtained through DCT. This compressed representation reduces memory footprint and computational overhead. We propose a lightweight network architecture that directly predicts these DCT coefficient maps. Experiments on standard datasets such as COCO demonstrate that DCT-Mask achieves competitive instance segmentation accuracy with significantly reduced mask storage requirements compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the DCT representation facilitates efficient mask reconstruction and manipulation. Our approach provides a promising alternative for resource-constrained environments and real-time applications. Keywords: Instance Segmentation, Discrete Cosine Transform, Mask Representation, Image Compression, Computer Vision, Deep Learning.

Sequential Neural Processes (SNPs) have emerged as a promising framework for modeling sequential data by combining the strengths of neural networks and stochastic processes. However, their robustness to noisy or incomplete data remains a critical challenge, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios. This paper addresses this gap by proposing a novel approach to robustify SNPs, enhancing their resilience to data imperfections while maintaining predictive accuracy. We introduce a robust training mechanism that integrates uncertainty estimation and adaptive regularization, enabling the model to dynamically adjust its learning process in the presence of outliers or missing data. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the robustness of SNPs across diverse datasets, including time-series forecasting and sequential decision-making tasks. Comparative analysis with existing methods highlights the superior performance of our approach in handling noisy inputs and recovering accurate predictions. The results underscore the potential of robustified SNPs for applications in domains such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems, where data quality is often compromised. This work contributes to advancing the reliability and practicality of sequential modeling frameworks, paving the way for more robust and trustworthy AI systems. **Keywords**: Sequential Neural Processes, robustness, uncertainty estimation, adaptive regularization, time-series forecasting, noisy data.

This paper presents ICADx, an innovative system designed for the interpretable computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) of breast masses. The objective of this research is to enhance early breast cancer detection by providing a reliable and understandable diagnostic tool for medical professionals. To achieve this, we developed a hybrid model that integrates advanced machine learning techniques with expert-defined features, enabling the system to generate interpretable predictions alongside diagnostic results. Evaluation of ICADx was conducted through a comprehensive analysis using diverse datasets, showing that our system can achieve an accuracy rate of 92%, significantly outperforming existing CAD systems. Furthermore, the interpretability aspect of ICADx allows practitioners to visualize decision pathways, thereby facilitating better clinical decision-making and enhancing trust in AI-assisted diagnostics. The findings suggest that ICADx not only improves diagnostic performance but also addresses the critical need for transparency in AI applications within healthcare. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts in developing intelligent systems that assist in medical diagnoses while promoting user confidence and understanding. Potential applications of ICADx include integration in clinical workflows and use as a training tool for radiologists. Keywords: computer-aided diagnosis, breast cancer, machine learning, interpretability, medical imaging.

We propose a new perspective on video understanding by casting the video recognition problem as an image recognition task. We show that an image classifier alone can suffice for video understanding without temporal modeling. Our approach is simple and universal. It composes input frames into a super image to train an image classifier to fulfill the task of action recognition, in exactly the same way as classifying an image. We prove the viability of such an idea by demonstrating strong and promising performance on four public datasets including Kinetics400, Something-to-something (V2), MiT and Jester, using a recently developed vision transformer. We also experiment with the prevalent ResNet image classifiers in computer vision to further validate our idea. This paper presents a novel non-alternating graph hashing algorithm designed to efficiently facilitate large-scale image search. The objective is to address the challenges of existing hashing methods that often suffer from information loss and poor retrieval performance. Our approach leverages a graph-based framework to preserve the semantic relationships between images, allowing for more accurate and robust hashing. The algorithm utilizes a non-alternating optimization strategy to learn compact and informative hash codes, enabling fast and effective image retrieval. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our method over state-of-the-art hashing algorithms, achieving significant improvements in search accuracy and efficiency. The proposed algorithm has important implications for various applications, including image recognition, object detection, and visual search. Key contributions include the introduction of a non-alternating graph hashing framework, which enables better preservation of image semantics and improved search performance. Relevant keywords: graph hashing, image search, non-alternating optimization, large-scale retrieval, computer vision.

This paper explores novel Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) architectures for high-quality image synthesis by integrating capsule networks. Addressing limitations in GANs related to capturing hierarchical relationships and viewpoint invariance in images, we propose a Capsule-GAN framework. This framework replaces traditional convolutional layers in both the generator and discriminator with capsule layers, enabling the network to explicitly model part-whole relationships and spatial arrangements. Several Capsule-GAN architectures, varying in capsule routing mechanisms and network depth, are evaluated. Experimental results on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10 and CelebA demonstrate that Capsule-GANs achieve improved image quality and stability compared to traditional CNN-based GANs, as evidenced by higher Inception Score and lower Frechet Inception Distance (FID). The study highlights the potential of capsule networks to enhance GAN performance by improving feature representation and offers new directions for generative modeling. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, Capsule Networks, Image Synthesis, GAN Architectures, Deep Learning.

Human action recognition from skeleton data, fueled by the Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), has attracted lots of attention, due to its powerful capability of modeling non-Euclidean structure data. However, many existing GCN methods provide a pre-defined graph and fix it through the entire network, which can loss implicit joint correlations. Besides, the mainstream spectral GCN is approximated by one-order hop, thus higher-order connections are not well involved. Therefore, huge efforts are required to explore a better GCN architecture. To address these problems, we turn to Neural Architecture Search (NAS) and propose the first automatically designed GCN for skeleton-based action recognition. Specifically, we enrich the search space by providing multiple dynamic graph modules after fully exploring the spatial-temporal correlations between nodes. Besides, we introduce multiple-hop modules and expect to break the limitation of representational capacity caused by one-order approximation. Moreover, a sampling- and memory-efficient evolution strategy is proposed to search an optimal architecture for this task. The resulted architecture proves the effectiveness of the higher-order approximation and the dynamic graph modeling mechanism with temporal interactions, which is barely discussed before. To evaluate the performance of the searched model, we conduct extensive experiments on two very large scaled datasets and the results show that our model gets the state-of-the-art results.

Recent reference-based face restoration methods have received considerable attention due to their great capability in recovering high-frequency details on real low-quality images. However, most of these methods require a high-quality reference image of the same identity, making them only applicable in limited scenes. To address this issue, this paper suggests a deep face dictionary network (termed as DFDNet) to guide the restoration process of degraded observations. To begin with, we use K-means to generate deep dictionaries for perceptually significant face components (\ie, left/right eyes, nose and mouth) from high-quality images. Next, with the degraded input, we match and select the most similar component features from their corresponding dictionaries and transfer the high-quality details to the input via the proposed dictionary feature transfer (DFT) block. In particular, component AdaIN is leveraged to eliminate the style diversity between the input and dictionary features (\eg, illumination), and a confidence score is proposed to adaptively fuse the dictionary feature to the input. Finally, multi-scale dictionaries are adopted in a progressive manner to enable the coarse-to-fine restoration. Experiments show that our proposed method can achieve plausible performance in both quantitative and qualitative evaluation, and more importantly, can generate realistic and promising results on real degraded images without requiring an identity-belonging reference. Các yếu tố liên quan đến cường độ tiếng ồn tại các tuyến đường này bao gồm lưu lượng giao thông, tốc độ xe, loại xe, và thời gian hoạt động. Các tuyến đường có lưu lượng giao thông cao, tốc độ xe nhanh, và hoạt động trong thời gian dài sẽ có cường độ tiếng ồn cao hơn. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, chính quyền địa phương cần có các biện pháp cụ thể để giảm cường độ tiếng ồn, như xây dựng các tuyến đường mới, cải thiện hệ thống giao thông, và tăng cường quản lý lưu lượng giao thông. Đồng thời, người dân cũng cần có ý thức hơn trong việc bảo vệ môi trường và giảm thiểu tiếng ồn.

This research introduces an innovative approach to address the challenge of predicting multiple brain graphs from a single brain graph, a task critical for understanding complex connectivity patterns and their variations across different mental states or conditions. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel Topology-Aware Generative Adversarial Network (TAGAN) designed to leverage the structural information inherent in brain graphs. The TAGAN framework incorporates a topology-aware generator and a discriminator that jointly learn the intricate dependencies between brain regions, ensuring that the generated graphs preserve the topological properties of the input graph. Our method uniquely adapts to structural variations and maintains consistency across different graph modalities. Results/Findings: Experiments demonstrate that TAGAN excels in generating accurate and topologically consistent brain graphs, outperforming existing methods both in qualitative and quantitative evaluations. The generated graphs closely replicate the real-world connectivity patterns, highlighting the model's capability in capturing essential topological features. The performance was assessed using various graph similarity metrics, showcasing significant improvements over baseline models. Conclusion/Implications: This study contributes to the field by introducing a topology-aware framework that advances the state-of-the-art in brain graph prediction. The TAGAN model paves the way for more nuanced neurological studies and potential clinical applications, such as predicting disease progression or treatment effects. By enhancing the fidelity of brain graph predictions, this work injects robustness and reliability into neuroimaging analyses and tools. Keywords: Topology-Aware, Generative Adversarial Network, Brain Graph Prediction, Neural Connectivity, Graph-Based Learning.

Đố với những người đi du lịch tự túc : Việc tìm kiếm các thông tin liên quan đến nơi ở và các điểm du lịch nên đi tạ nơ đi có mất nhiều thờ gần và công sức do các thông tin thường rời rạc, không tập trung tại một chỗ nhất định. Nghiên cứu mô tả thực trạng quản lý người bệnh đái tháo đường tại các trạm y tế thuộc tỉnh Trà Vinh, từ việc phát hiện sớm, điều trị, đến dự phòng. Điều tra 106 trạm y tế cho thấy hầu hết đã thực hiện các chương trình quản lý bệnh đái tháo đường với tỷ lệ 98,1%, tuy nhiên sử dụng công nghệ thông tin và phần mềm quản lý còn thấp. Công tác đào tạo và tư vấn phòng ngừa bệnh được triển khai rộng rãi, tuy nhiên vẫn cần chú trọng hơn nữa đến các vùng khó khăn. Sàng lọc và tư vấn dự phòng tại trạm y tế đạt tỷ lệ cao, song công tác truyền thông cần được tăng cường, đặc biệt là tài liệu bằng tiếng Khmer cho cộng đồng dân tộc thiểu số. Kết luận rằng hoạt động quản lý, đào tạo và cung cấp dịch vụ cho người bệnh đái tháo đường cần được tiếp tục và tăng cường, nhất là ở các khu vực có dân tộc Khmer.

This paper presents a novel approach to multi-object tracking, introducing an unsupervised learning framework termed Tracking by Animation. The objective is to develop attentive trackers that can effectively follow multiple objects within a scene without requiring manual annotations. Our method leverages animation principles to generate synthetic data, which is then used to train a deep neural network. The network learns to focus attention on specific objects, enabling the tracking of multiple targets across frames. Results demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, outperforming existing unsupervised tracking methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. Key findings include improved handling of occlusions and enhanced ability to track objects with complex motions. The proposed framework contributes to the field of computer vision by providing a unique, annotation-free solution for multi-object tracking, with potential applications in areas such as surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and human-computer interaction. Our approach highlights the importance of attentive mechanisms in tracking tasks, paving the way for future research in unsupervised learning and multi-object tracking. Relevant keywords: multi-object tracking, unsupervised learning, attentive trackers, deep learning, computer vision.

Zero-shot image recognition has gained significant traction due to its ability to classify images that lack labeled training data. This research introduces a novel approach to zero-shot image recognition through a Graph-based Visual-Semantic Entanglement Network (GVEN), which leverages the intricate relationships between visual and semantic domains. Methods/Approach: The proposed GVEN model constructs an entanglement framework that utilizes graph-based structures to bridge visual features and semantic attributes. By embedding both visual data and semantic information into a unified graph, the model effectively captures the interdependencies and hierarchical relationships inherent in complex data sets. This graph-based structure enables the network to learn robust representations that generalize well to unseen classes. Results/Findings: Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of GVEN compared to state-of-the-art zero-shot learning models. The proposed network exhibits significant improvements in recognition accuracy and generalization to novel classes. Additionally, the graph-based entanglement framework showcases enhanced capacity in handling diverse datasets with complex feature interactions. Conclusion/Implications: The GVEN's innovative approach to integrating visual and semantic domains through a graph-based model presents a valuable contribution to zero-shot image recognition research. This work not only enhances the theoretical understanding of feature entanglement but also provides practical implications for applications in areas such as automated image classification, semantic search, and intelligent content retrieval. Future work will explore the extension of this model to other domains requiring sophisticated feature understanding and categorization. Keywords: Zero-shot learning, graph networks, visual-semantic entanglement, image recognition, feature embedding, machine learning.

Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) agents often struggle to learn efficient policies in complex environments due to the high dimensionality of raw observations and the diverse dynamics of multiple objects. This paper introduces a relevance-guided modeling framework that selectively focuses on object dynamics most predictive of task success. Our approach consists of two key components: a relevance estimator that assigns importance scores to detected objects based on their influence on future rewards, and a dynamic object model that learns transition functions only for high-relevance entities. By combining these modules within a model-based RL pipeline, the agent builds a compact predictive representation that emphasizes critical interactions while ignoring distractors. We evaluate our method on benchmark control tasks featuring interacting objects, including simulated manipulation and navigation scenarios. Compared to baseline model-based and model-free algorithms, relevance-guided modeling yields faster convergence, requiring up to 50% fewer environment steps to reach comparable performance. Ablation studies confirm that both relevance estimation and targeted dynamics learning contribute significantly to sample efficiency and policy robustness. Our findings demonstrate that guiding the modeling process with task-specific relevance not only reduces computational overhead but also enhances generalization to novel configurations. This relevance-guided paradigm offers a principled way to integrate object-centric representations into RL, paving the way for more scalable and interpretable decision-making agents. Keywords: reinforcement learning, object dynamics, relevance-guided modeling, model-based RL, sample efficiency.

Để giải quyết vấn đề này, cần có các giải pháp đồng bộ như nâng cao nhận thức về bảo vệ môi trường, phát triển sản phẩm du lịch thân thiện với thiên nhiên, và khuyến khích sự tham gia của cộng đồng trong quá trình phát triển. This paper addresses the challenge of preserving depth perception in arbitrary style transfer, a critical limitation in existing methods that often overlook spatial structure during artistic rendering. We propose a novel depth-aware style transfer framework that integrates instance normalization with depth-aware feature modulation to maintain the spatial coherence of the stylized output. Our approach leverages a pre-trained depth estimation network to extract depth information, which is then used to guide the style transfer process. By incorporating depth-aware constraints into the instance normalization layers, our method ensures that the stylized images retain both the artistic style and the original depth structure. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms state-of-the-art style transfer methods in preserving depth perception while achieving high-quality artistic rendering. The proposed method is evaluated on diverse datasets, showcasing its robustness and versatility across various styles and content. This work contributes to the field of neural style transfer by introducing a depth-aware mechanism, enabling applications in augmented reality, 3D rendering, and digital art creation. **Keywords**: style transfer, instance normalization, depth perception, neural networks, image processing, artistic rendering.

This paper addresses the challenge of class imbalance in data classification, a common problem in many real-world applications. Our objective is to develop an effective approach to handle imbalance data using deep learning techniques. We propose a Class Expert Generative Adversarial Network (CE-GAN) model, which leverages the strengths of generative adversarial networks to generate synthetic samples for the minority class, thereby improving classification performance. Our approach utilizes a novel architecture that combines an expert generator for each class, allowing for more precise control over the generated samples. Experimental results demonstrate that our CE-GAN model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in handling class imbalance, achieving significant improvements in accuracy, precision, and recall. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a class-expert based GAN architecture and the demonstration of its effectiveness in addressing class imbalance. Our work has important implications for applications where class imbalance is a significant challenge, such as medical diagnosis, fraud detection, and text classification. Key keywords: class imbalance, generative adversarial networks, deep learning, classification, CE-GAN.

This paper explores the potential of unsupervised learning through a novel approach based on competing hidden units. The objective is to develop a framework that enables neural networks to learn meaningful representations from unlabeled data without relying on explicit supervision. We propose a model where hidden units compete to represent input patterns, fostering the emergence of sparse and interpretable features. The approach leverages a biologically inspired mechanism of competition, implemented through a combination of inhibitory connections and adaptive learning rules. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance in feature extraction and clustering tasks compared to traditional unsupervised learning techniques. The results highlight the model's ability to capture hierarchical structures and disentangle latent factors in complex data. This work contributes to the advancement of unsupervised learning by introducing a biologically plausible and computationally efficient alternative to existing methods, with potential applications in data compression, anomaly detection, and representation learning. **Keywords**: unsupervised learning, neural networks, competitive learning, feature extraction, sparse representations.

Mục đích – Mục đích của nghiên cứu này là để hiểu và phân tích các chủ đề liên quan đến huy động vốn từ cộng đồng và vai trò của nó vai trò của nó trong các quốc gia thuộc Hội đồng Hợp tác vùng Vịnh (GCC) từ góc độ Hồi giáo. Multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) offers a powerful framework for addressing complex decision-making problems with multiple, potentially conflicting, objectives. This paper tackles the challenge of optimizing policies for “picky” customers, where preferences are not explicitly known but revealed through feedback. We introduce a novel MORL algorithm designed to efficiently learn policies that satisfy diverse customer needs while minimizing regret. Our approach leverages a modified upper confidence bound (UCB) exploration strategy tailored for multi-objective settings, balancing exploration of less-known policy spaces with exploitation of promising regions. We derive theoretical regret bounds demonstrating the algorithm's performance and provide exploration complexity guarantees, indicating the number of interactions required to achieve near-optimal policies. Experimental results on benchmark MORL environments validate the effectiveness of our algorithm, showcasing its ability to adapt to varying customer preferences and outperform existing MORL methods in terms of cumulative reward and preference satisfaction. This work contributes to the development of practical MORL solutions for personalized recommendation systems, adaptive robotics, and other applications requiring preference-aware decision-making. Keywords: Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning, Regret Bound, Exploration Complexity, Preference Learning, Upper Confidence Bound, Reinforcement Learning.

This paper introduces CoachNet, a novel reinforcement learning (RL) approach designed to improve sample efficiency and robustness through adversarial sampling. CoachNet addresses the challenge of sparse rewards and inefficient exploration in complex environments by employing an adversarial network to identify and prioritize informative experiences for training. Specifically, the adversarial network, acting as a "coach," learns to distinguish between experiences that contribute significantly to policy improvement and those that do not. This allows the RL agent to focus on a curated subset of experiences, thereby accelerating learning. We evaluate CoachNet on a range of benchmark tasks, including those with sparse and deceptive rewards, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art RL algorithms. Our results show that CoachNet not only achieves higher rewards but also exhibits improved sample efficiency and stability during training. The key contribution of this work is the adversarial sampling framework, which can be integrated with various RL algorithms to enhance their learning capabilities, particularly in challenging environments. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Adversarial Sampling, Sample Efficiency, Sparse Rewards, Deep Learning.

Objective: Accurate near-field distance estimation around vehicles is critical for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) but remains challenging due to severe distortion in surround-view fisheye imagery and scarcity of annotated depth maps. This paper presents SVDistNet, a novel self-supervised learning framework designed to estimate per-pixel distances in the 0–10 m range using only four surround‐view fisheye cameras. Methods: SVDistNet employs a multi-branch convolutional backbone that processes each fisheye view independently before fusing features in a shared representation space. Self-supervision arises from geometric consistency across overlapping fields of view: reprojection loss enforces agreement between predicted distances and relative camera poses, while a photometric reconstruction loss refines fine details. A soft-distortion module explicitly models fisheye lens effects, enabling the network to learn spatially varying pixel mappings without requiring explicit calibration labels. Results: Experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that SVDistNet achieves a mean absolute error of 0.12 m within 5 m and 0.25 m within 10 m—improving over state-of-the-art supervised and unsupervised baselines by up to 30%. Qualitative tests confirm robust performance under varying illumination and occlusion conditions. Conclusion: By eliminating the need for dense ground-truth distances and leveraging multi-view geometry, SVDistNet offers a practical, scalable solution for near-field perception in automotive applications. Its self-supervised design paves the way for continual learning on diverse deployment vehicles. Potential extensions include integration with semantic segmentation and dynamic object tracking for full-scene understanding. Keywords: Self-Supervised Learning, Distance Estimation, Fisheye Cameras, Surround View, Automotive Perception.

Năng lực nghiên cứu khoa học của giảng viên đại học tại Lào chịu ảnh hưởng bởi nhiều yếu tố phức tạp. Trong đó, trình độ học vấn đóng vai trò then chốt, giảng viên có trình độ cao hơn thường có năng lực nghiên cứu tốt hơn. Kinh nghiệm nghiên cứu trước đây, bao gồm số lượng công bố và dự án đã tham gia, cũng tác động đáng kể đến khả năng thực hiện các nghiên cứu mới. This paper presents a novel approach for self-supervised visual representation learning by leveraging hierarchical grouping mechanisms. The primary objective is to address the challenge of learning robust visual features from unlabeled image data, which is crucial for reducing reliance on large quantities of annotated samples. Our method introduces a hierarchical grouping framework that dynamically organizes image regions at multiple scales, enabling the model to capture both local and global visual structures without human supervision. The proposed system employs a combination of contrastive learning objectives and region-based clustering to guide the representation learning process. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing self-supervised learning baselines, particularly in tasks such as image classification and object detection. Notably, the learned representations exhibit improved transferability and generalization across diverse visual domains. This research contributes an effective and scalable solution to unsupervised feature learning and highlights the impact of hierarchical organization in self-supervised visual understanding. Potential applications include computer vision tasks where annotated data is scarce, such as medical imaging and autonomous navigation. Keywords: self-supervised learning, visual representation, hierarchical grouping, unsupervised learning, contrastive learning, computer vision.

Accurate and timely traffic speed prediction is crucial for intelligent transportation systems. This paper presents a novel deep learning model leveraging both bidirectional and unidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural networks for network-wide traffic speed prediction. The model captures both historical and future dependencies in traffic flow by employing a bidirectional LSTM to process historical data and a unidirectional LSTM to forecast future speeds. The approach utilizes network-wide traffic data as input, allowing the model to learn complex spatial-temporal correlations between different road segments. Experimental results using real-world traffic data demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms traditional time-series methods and other deep learning architectures, achieving significant improvements in prediction accuracy, particularly during peak hours and under congested conditions. The findings highlight the effectiveness of combining bidirectional and unidirectional LSTMs for capturing intricate traffic patterns, offering a promising solution for real-time traffic management and control. Keywords: Traffic Speed Prediction, Deep Learning, LSTM, Recurrent Neural Networks, Bidirectional LSTM, Intelligent Transportation Systems.

The research paper addresses the problem of optimizing autonomous soaring strategies in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) using reinforcement learning. The primary objective is to explore the effectiveness of a Q-Learning algorithm in developing model-free strategies for efficient energy management and altitude maintenance during flight. Methods/Approach: This study employs a Q-Learning algorithm, a well-known reinforcement learning technique, to enable UAVs to learn soaring strategies without relying on pre-existing environmental models. The research involves simulating thermal updraft environments to test the UAV's ability to autonomously optimize flight paths. A series of empirical evaluations were conducted to assess the algorithm's learning efficiency and adaptability in varying atmospheric conditions. Results/Findings: The Q-Learning algorithm demonstrated significant improvement in the autonomous soaring capability of UAVs by increasing flight duration and energy efficiency. The empirical results showed that UAVs equipped with this algorithm could dynamically adapt to environmental changes, outperforming traditional model-based approaches in tests. The learning-based strategies resulted in an increase in altitude gain and enhanced utilization of thermal currents. Conclusion/Implications: The study contributes to the advancement of autonomous flight technology by providing a novel, model-free approach to UAV soaring. These findings highlight the potential of Q-Learning as a powerful tool for enhancing UAV autonomy and energy management. The implications of this research extend to applications in environmental monitoring, search and rescue operations, and other domains where efficient flight performance is critical. Keywords included in this research are Q-Learning, reinforcement learning, autonomous soaring, UAV, and model-free strategies.

Object detection plays an important role in various visual applications. However, the precision and speed of detector are usually contradictory. One main reason for fast detectors' precision reduction is that small objects are hard to be detected. To address this problem, we propose a multiple receptive field and small-object-focusing weakly-supervised segmentation network (MRFSWSnet) to achieve fast object detection. In MRFSWSnet, multiple receptive fields block (MRF) is used to pay attention to the object and its adjacent background's different spatial location with different weights to enhance the feature's discriminability. In addition, in order to improve the accuracy of small object detection, a small-object-focusing weakly-supervised segmentation module which only focuses on small object instead of all objects is integrated into the detection network for auxiliary training to improve the precision of small object detection. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method on both PASCAL VOC and MS COCO detection datasets. In particular, with a lower resolution version of 300x300, MRFSWSnet achieves 80.9% mAP on VOC2007 test with an inference speed of 15 milliseconds per frame, which is the state-of-the-art detector among real-time detectors.

Deep transfer learning (DTL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm in machine learning, enabling knowledge transfer from data-rich source domains to data-scarce target domains. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of DTL, categorizing existing approaches based on transfer strategies, network architectures, and application areas. We examine various DTL techniques, including fine-tuning, feature-based transfer, and adversarial transfer learning, highlighting their strengths and limitations. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of different deep neural network architectures, such as convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks, on transfer performance. We also discuss challenges in DTL, such as negative transfer and domain shift, and potential solutions to mitigate these issues. Finally, we explore the wide range of applications where DTL has achieved significant success, including computer vision, natural language processing, and healthcare. This survey aims to provide researchers and practitioners with a structured understanding of DTL, guiding future research directions and practical applications. Keywords: Deep Transfer Learning, Transfer Learning, Deep Learning, Domain Adaptation, Machine Learning, Survey.

This paper introduces an efficient and robust algorithm for image matching based on Least Squares Normalized Cross Correlation (LSNCC). Addressing the limitations of traditional Normalized Cross Correlation (NCC) in handling varying illumination and contrast, LSNCC incorporates a least squares fitting step to normalize image patches before correlation. The method minimizes the intensity differences between the template and search image patch, making it more resilient to photometric distortions. Experiments on diverse image datasets demonstrate that LSNCC achieves superior matching accuracy compared to NCC and other correlation-based techniques, particularly in challenging scenarios with significant illumination changes and noise. Furthermore, we present an optimized implementation of LSNCC that significantly reduces computational cost, making it suitable for real-time applications. The proposed LSNCC algorithm offers a valuable tool for various computer vision tasks including object tracking, image registration, and 3D reconstruction. Keywords: Image Matching, Normalized Cross Correlation, Least Squares, Illumination Invariance, Computer Vision.

This paper explores a novel deep learning framework for extracting transferable multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel modes to enhance sixth-generation (6G) vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications. The primary objective is to address the growing demands for high-reliability and ultra-low latency in highly dynamic vehicular environments under 6G requirements. We propose an end-to-end neural architecture that leverages domain adaptation and transfer learning to build robust representations of MIMO channel characteristics across diverse V2X scenarios. The approach incorporates convolutional and attention-based modules to capture spatial and temporal dependencies, enabling efficient learning of latent channel modes that generalize well between simulation environments and real-world datasets. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed model achieves superior channel estimation accuracy and improved link reliability when compared to traditional signal processing methods and baseline deep learning approaches. The findings also indicate significant gains in adaptability and performance robustness—even when transferred across geographically and spectrally distinct environments. This research provides a foundational step towards intelligent, adaptive wireless systems for connected vehicles in 6G, with broad implications for real-time resource allocation, interference mitigation, and scalable deployment in next-generation V2X communications. Key keywords: deep learning, 6G, MIMO, V2X communications, channel modeling, transfer learning, domain adaptation, intelligent wireless systems.

Most neural networks utilize the same amount of compute for every example independent of the inherent complexity of the input. Further, methods that adapt the amount of computation to the example focus on finding a fixed inference-time computational graph per example, ignoring any external computational budgets or varying inference time limitations. In this work, we utilize conditional computation to make neural sequence models (Transformer) more efficient and computation-aware during inference. We first modify the Transformer architecture, making each set of operations conditionally executable depending on the output of a learned control network. We then train this model in a multi-task setting, where each task corresponds to a particular computation budget. This allows us to train a single model that can be controlled to operate on different points of the computation-quality trade-off curve, depending on the available computation budget at inference time. We evaluate our approach on two tasks: (i) WMT English-French Translation and (ii) Unsupervised representation learning (BERT). Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed Conditional Computation Transformer (CCT) is competitive with vanilla Transformers when allowed to utilize its full computational budget, while improving significantly over computationally equivalent baselines when operating on smaller computational budgets.

This paper addresses the challenge of image segmentation by proposing a novel approach based on size-dependent single linkage clustering of a watershed basin graph. The objective is to improve segmentation accuracy by effectively grouping regions while preserving fine-grained details in complex images. The proposed method leverages a watershed transform to partition the image into distinct basins, which are then represented as nodes in a graph. A size-dependent single linkage clustering algorithm is applied to merge these nodes, ensuring that regions are grouped based on both spatial proximity and size constraints. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional methods, such as over-segmentation and sensitivity to noise. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques, particularly in handling images with varying textures and object sizes. The findings highlight the method's robustness and adaptability, making it suitable for applications in medical imaging, remote sensing, and computer vision. This research contributes a scalable and efficient solution to image segmentation, offering significant potential for advancing automated image analysis systems. **Keywords**: image segmentation, watershed transform, single linkage clustering, graph-based methods, size-dependent clustering, computer vision.

This paper proposes a novel approach to multi-label classification by integrating cross-modality attention with semantic graph embedding. The objective is to improve the accuracy of classification models by effectively capturing complex relationships between labels and leveraging features from multiple modalities. Our method employs a graph embedding technique to represent semantic relationships between labels, which are then incorporated into a cross-modality attention mechanism to selectively focus on relevant features from different modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant improvements in classification accuracy and F1-score. The key contributions of this research lie in its ability to model intricate label relationships and adaptively weigh features from different modalities, making it particularly suitable for applications involving multi-label classification, such as image and text analysis. By combining cross-modality attention with semantic graph embedding, this study provides a new perspective on multi-label classification, highlighting the potential of graph-based methods and attention mechanisms in enhancing model performance. Key keywords: multi-label classification, cross-modality attention, semantic graph embedding, graph-based methods, attention mechanisms.

Unsupervised learning can leverage large-scale data sources without the need for annotations. In this context, deep learning-based auto encoders have shown great potential in detecting anomalies in medical images. However, state-of-the-art anomaly scores are still based on the reconstruction error, which lacks in two essential parts: it ignores the model-internal representation employed for reconstruction, and it lacks formal assertions and comparability between samples. We address these shortcomings by proposing the Context-encoding Variational Autoencoder (ceVAE) which combines reconstruction- with density-based anomaly scoring. This improves the sample- as well as pixel-wise results. In our experiments on the BraTS-2017 and ISLES-2015 segmentation benchmarks, the ceVAE achieves unsupervised ROC-AUCs of 0.95 and 0.89, respectively, thus outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a considerable margin.

Spatial mapping is a critical task in fields such as robotics, geospatial analysis, and environmental monitoring, where accurate modeling of spatial phenomena is essential. This paper presents a novel approach to spatial mapping by leveraging Gaussian Processes (GPs) enhanced with nonstationary Fourier features. Traditional GPs with stationary kernels often struggle to capture complex, varying patterns in real-world spatial data. To address this limitation, we introduce a nonstationary kernel representation using Fourier feature expansions that adapt their spectral properties across the spatial domain. Our method enables efficient learning and inference by providing a scalable approximation to nonstationary GPs, making it suitable for large and heterogeneous datasets. Through extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world spatial mapping benchmarks, we demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms conventional GP models and state-of-the-art stationary feature techniques in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness to nonuniform data distributions. The proposed framework offers a flexible and efficient solution for high-fidelity spatial mapping, with potential applications in autonomous navigation, environmental monitoring, and urban planning. Key contributions include the integration of adaptive Fourier features into GP modeling and a thorough evaluation of their impact on spatial prediction tasks. Keywords: spatial mapping, Gaussian processes, nonstationary kernels, Fourier features, spatial modeling, machine learning, robot mapping.

Variational inference is a widely-used technique for approximating complex probability distributions in fields such as machine learning and statistics. Traditional methods often rely on minimizing divergences like the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, which may lead to biased approximations, especially for multi-modal or heavy-tailed distributions. This paper investigates the use of Fisher divergence as an alternative objective for variational approximations. We propose a novel framework that leverages the properties of Fisher divergence to construct tighter and more representative variational distributions. The approach utilizes the score function and gradient-based optimization to efficiently approximate intractable posterior distributions. Experimental results demonstrate that variational approximations using Fisher divergence outperform conventional KL-based methods on benchmark tasks, leading to improved coverage of target distributions and enhanced estimation accuracy. Our findings suggest that integrating Fisher divergence into the variational inference pipeline offers significant benefits for probabilistic modeling, with applications in Bayesian neural networks, unsupervised learning, and complex generative models. Keywords: variational inference, Fisher divergence, probabilistic modeling, Bayesian learning, approximate inference.

Adam, a widely adopted optimization algorithm in deep learning, combines the benefits of adaptive learning rates with momentum. This paper revisits Adam through a novel lens, framing its update rules as a weighted average of past gradients. By explicitly analyzing these weights, we uncover previously unobserved properties that contribute to Adam's empirical success and potential limitations. Our analysis reveals that Adam's weighting scheme can, under certain circumstances, lead to an over-reliance on early gradients, potentially hindering convergence in later stages of training. To mitigate this issue, we propose a modification to Adam's weight decay mechanism, dynamically adjusting the influence of past gradients based on the current training epoch. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets, including image classification and natural language processing tasks, demonstrate that our modified Adam variant consistently outperforms the original algorithm, particularly in scenarios requiring fine-grained optimization. This work provides a deeper understanding of Adam's internal dynamics and offers a practical improvement for enhanced performance and robustness. Keywords: Adam, Optimization, Deep Learning, Gradient Descent, Momentum, Weight Decay.

A large number of image super resolution algorithms based on the sparse coding are proposed, and some algorithms realize the multi-frame super resolution. In multi-frame super resolution based on the sparse coding, both accurate image registration and sparse coding are required. Previous study on multi-frame super resolution based on sparse coding firstly apply block matching for image registration, followed by sparse coding to enhance the image resolution. In this paper, these two problems are solved by optimizing a single objective function. The results of numerical experiments support the effectiveness of the proposed approch.

This paper addresses the challenges in image captioning by exploring the potential of scene graphs, a structured representation capturing objects and their relationships within an image, as a valuable asset for enhancing caption generation. Despite advancements in deep learning models, the complexity of integrating semantic relationships to produce contextually rich descriptions remains a significant hurdle. Methods/Approach: We present an image captioning framework leveraging scene graphs to systematically interpret visual scenes. The approach involves generating scene graphs from images using a neural network-based model, followed by employing a graph-to-text transformer that translates structured information into descriptive captions. This method is compared against conventional deep learning models to assess the augmentation capabilities provided by scene graphs. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate that incorporating scene graphs significantly improves the quality of image captions, resulting in higher scores on standardized metrics such as BLEU, METEOR, and CIDEr. The framework enables better semantic comprehension, thereby generating more coherent and context-aware captions. Additionally, comparison with existing models highlights the framework's superior ability to capture intricate relationships within images. Conclusion/Implications: The findings reaffirm the relevance and utility of scene graphs in advancing image captioning technologies. By integrating structured representations, the proposed method contributes a meaningful approach to address the limitations of current models, fostering improvements in automated image description tasks. This research provides a foundation for further exploration of scene graphs in other visual understanding applications, promoting richer media interpretation and enhanced human-computer interaction. Keywords: Image Captioning, Scene Graphs, Visual Understanding, Semantic Relationships, Neural Networks, Graph-to-Text Transformer.

3D perception using sensors under vehicle industrial standard is the rigid demand in autonomous driving. MEMS LiDAR emerges with irresistible trend due to its lower cost, more robust, and meeting the mass-production standards. However, it suffers small field of view (FoV), slowing down the step of its population. In this paper, we propose LEAD, i.e., LiDAR Extender for Autonomous Driving, to extend the MEMS LiDAR by coupled image w.r.t both FoV and range. We propose a multi-stage propagation strategy based on depth distributions and uncertainty map, which shows effective propagation ability. Moreover, our depth outpainting/propagation network follows a teacher-student training fashion, which transfers depth estimation ability to depth completion network without any scale error passed. To validate the LiDAR extension quality, we utilize a high-precise laser scanner to generate a ground-truth dataset. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations show that our scheme outperforms SOTAs with a large margin. We believe the proposed LEAD along with the dataset would benefit the community w.r.t depth researches.
