This paper addresses the problem of rectifying radially-distorted scales and change of scales in computer vision. Our objective is to develop minimal solvers that can efficiently and accurately rectify distorted scales and adapt to changes in scale. We propose a novel approach that combines geometric constraints with a robust estimation framework to achieve this goal. Our method utilizes a minimal set of correspondences to estimate the distortion parameters and scale change, allowing for efficient and accurate rectification. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The key contributions of this research include the development of a minimal solver for radially-distorted scales and a change of scales, and the introduction of a robust estimation framework that can handle noisy and outlier-prone data. Our work has important implications for various computer vision applications, including 3D reconstruction, object recognition, and scene understanding. Key keywords: radial distortion, scale change, minimal solvers, computer vision, 3D reconstruction, geometric constraints.

This paper proposes to learn hierarchical compositional AND-OR model for interpretable image synthesis by sparsifying the generator network. The proposed method adopts the scene-objects-parts-subparts-primitives hierarchy in image representation. A scene has different types (i.e., OR) each of which consists of a number of objects (i.e., AND). This can be recursively formulated across the scene-objects-parts-subparts hierarchy and is terminated at the primitive level (e.g., wavelets-like basis). To realize this AND-OR hierarchy in image synthesis, we learn a generator network that consists of the following two components: (i) Each layer of the hierarchy is represented by an over-complete set of convolutional basis functions. Off-the-shelf convolutional neural architectures are exploited to implement the hierarchy. (ii) Sparsity-inducing constraints are introduced in end-to-end training, which induces a sparsely activated and sparsely connected AND-OR model from the initially densely connected generator network. A straightforward sparsity-inducing constraint is utilized, that is to only allow the top-k basis functions to be activated at each layer (where k is a hyper-parameter). The learned basis functions are also capable of image reconstruction to explain the input images. In experiments, the proposed method is tested on four benchmark datasets. The results show that meaningful and interpretable hierarchical representations are learned with better qualities of image synthesis and reconstruction obtained than baselines.

Ensemble deep learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm to enhance the performance and robustness of machine learning models by combining multiple base learners. This paper provides a comprehensive review of ensemble deep learning techniques, focusing on their methodologies, applications, and advancements. The objective is to explore how ensemble methods address challenges such as overfitting, generalization, and model uncertainty in deep learning. We examine various ensemble strategies, including bagging, boosting, stacking, and hybrid approaches, and discuss their integration with deep neural networks. Key findings highlight the superior performance of ensemble models in tasks such as image classification, natural language processing, and anomaly detection, often outperforming single-model approaches. The review also identifies emerging trends, such as the use of ensemble methods for uncertainty quantification and adversarial robustness. By synthesizing recent research, this paper underscores the significance of ensemble deep learning in advancing AI systems and offers insights into future directions, including the development of lightweight and adaptive ensemble frameworks. This work contributes to the growing body of knowledge in deep learning by providing a structured overview of ensemble techniques and their practical implications. **Keywords**: Ensemble learning, deep learning, bagging, boosting, stacking, model robustness, uncertainty quantification.

The paper addresses the challenge of salient object subitizing, a task in computer vision and image analysis dedicated to quickly and accurately estimating the number of prominent objects within a visual scene. This research aims to enhance real-time image processing applications by developing a novel approach that efficiently and reliably subitizes salient objects without the need for exhaustive object detection and segmentation. Methods/Approach: We introduce a new model that leverages deep learning techniques to perform salient object subitizing. Our approach employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture optimized for speed and accuracy. The model is trained on a comprehensive dataset of images, annotated with the count of salient objects, to learn patterns that distinguish crucial visual features indicative of object salience. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves superior performance in salient object subitizing compared to existing methodologies. It accurately estimates object counts with minimal computational overhead, making it well-suited for applications requiring real-time processing. The model's efficacy is validated against standard benchmarks, showing a significant improvement in both precision and speed over traditional object detection approaches. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides important insights into the field of computer vision, contributing a novel solution for rapid and efficient salient object counting. The proposed method holds potential applications in various domains, including autonomous navigation, surveillance, and digital content analysis. Future work will explore enhancing the model's adaptability across diverse environments and expanding its application scope. Keywords: Salient Object Subitizing, Computer Vision, Deep Learning, Real-time Image Processing, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN).

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have made releasing of synthetic images a viable approach to share data without releasing the original dataset. It has been shown that such synthetic data can be used for a variety of downstream tasks such as training classifiers that would otherwise require the original dataset to be shared. However, recent work has shown that the GAN models and their synthetically generated data can be used to infer the training set membership by an adversary who has access to the entire dataset and some auxiliary information. Current approaches to mitigate this problem (such as DPGAN) lead to dramatically poorer generated sample quality than the original non--private GANs. Here we develop a new GAN architecture (privGAN), where the generator is trained not only to cheat the discriminator but also to defend membership inference attacks. The new mechanism provides protection against this mode of attack while leading to negligible loss in downstream performances. In addition, our algorithm has been shown to explicitly prevent overfitting to the training set, which explains why our protection is so effective. The main contributions of this paper are: i) we propose a novel GAN architecture that can generate synthetic data in a privacy preserving manner without additional hyperparameter tuning and architecture selection, ii) we provide a theoretical understanding of the optimal solution of the privGAN loss function, iii) we demonstrate the effectiveness of our model against several white and black--box attacks on several benchmark datasets, iv) we demonstrate on three common benchmark datasets that synthetic images generated by privGAN lead to negligible loss in downstream performance when compared against non--private GANs.

In this paper, we propose to learn a deep fitting degree scoring network for monocular 3D object detection, which aims to score fitting degree between proposals and object conclusively. Different from most existing monocular frameworks which use tight constraint to get 3D location, our approach achieves high-precision localization through measuring the visual fitting degree between the projected 3D proposals and the object. We first regress the dimension and orientation of the object using an anchor-based method so that a suitable 3D proposal can be constructed. We propose FQNet, which can infer the 3D IoU between the 3D proposals and the object solely based on 2D cues. Therefore, during the detection process, we sample a large number of candidates in the 3D space and project these 3D bounding boxes on 2D image individually. The best candidate can be picked out by simply exploring the spatial overlap between proposals and the object, in the form of the output 3D IoU score of FQNet. Experiments on the KITTI dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.

This paper introduces Imaginative Adversarial Networks (IAN), a novel approach to face generation leveraging the power of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). IAN combines multiple GANs in a hierarchical structure, where a primary GAN generates low-resolution facial images and subsequent GANs refine these images, progressively adding details and enhancing realism. This architecture enables the creation of high-resolution, diverse, and photorealistic facial images, even with limited training data. We present a new training methodology that stabilizes the learning process across multiple GANs, mitigating common issues like mode collapse and vanishing gradients. Experimental results demonstrate that IAN outperforms state-of-the-art GAN models in terms of image quality, diversity, and realism, as measured by Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and perceptual studies. The proposed IAN architecture offers a promising solution for various applications, including virtual reality, game development, and digital art. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, Face Generation, Image Synthesis, Deep Learning, GANs, Computer Vision.

The reason for this difference is executable code (JavaScript) in UI App would not be able to manipulate or even read refresh token - which has longer lifespan . Access token could also be stored that way for a higher level of confidentiality, but I chose to store it in local storage of the clients just for easier development process - where my local app could also use access token that was generated by auth service for a closer-to-production environment. Also, as access token has relatively short lifespan (less than 1 hour), the risk of losing it would not be as significant as losing a refresh token - where the attacker could use it as a way to continuously (even eternally) use a real user’s identity to make API calls that he/she does not have permissions to.

Explainable AI (XAI) has become a critical area of research as the adoption of complex machine learning models grows across various domains. This paper introduces SIDU (Similarity Difference and Uniqueness), a novel method for enhancing the interpretability of AI models by quantifying the contributions of input features to model predictions. The objective of SIDU is to provide a robust and intuitive framework for explaining model decisions, addressing the limitations of existing XAI techniques in capturing feature interactions and uniqueness. The proposed method leverages similarity metrics and difference analysis to identify the most influential features while preserving the uniqueness of their contributions. We evaluate SIDU on benchmark datasets and compare its performance with state-of-the-art XAI methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating more accurate and human-understandable explanations. Experimental results show that SIDU outperforms existing approaches in terms of fidelity, stability, and computational efficiency. The implications of this research extend to applications in healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems, where transparent and trustworthy AI is essential. SIDU represents a significant step forward in making AI models more interpretable and reliable, fostering greater trust and adoption in real-world scenarios. **Keywords**: Explainable AI, XAI, feature importance, interpretability, machine learning, SIDU, similarity metrics, uniqueness.

The research addresses the challenge of video scene graph generation, which involves analyzing dynamic scenes to infer semantic relationships between objects over time. The primary goal is to enhance the understanding of video content by developing an approach that adaptively aggregates contextual information relevant to specific targets within a video sequence. Methods: We propose a novel Target Adaptive Context Aggregation (TACA) framework designed to dynamically fuse contextual cues from different video frames, focusing particularly on targeted objects and their evolving interactions. The framework leverages graph neural networks to model interactions and utilizes attention mechanisms to prioritize context relevant to specific scene elements, allowing for more precise representation of relationships across time. Results: Our empirical analysis demonstrates the superior performance of the TACA framework when benchmarked against state-of-the-art methods in video scene graph generation tasks. The results indicate significant improvements in accuracy and consistency in detecting and contextualizing object relationships within dynamic video environments. Comparative evaluations revealed that TACA outperformed existing models in several standard datasets, both in object relationship detection and overall scene graph generation accuracy. Conclusion: The research contributes a significant advancement in the field of video scene analysis by introducing a method that efficiently captures and aggregates context-specific information. The TACA framework's capabilities present promising applications in content-based video retrieval, enhanced video surveillance, and automated video content understanding. Furthermore, the framework's adaptability and precision hold potential for future developments in real-time video analytics. Keywords: Video Scene Graph Generation, Context Aggregation, Graph Neural Networks, Video Content Understanding, Scene Dynamics, Object Relationships.

This paper proposes a novel Attention-based Multi-Reference Super-resolution network (AMRSR) that, given a low-resolution image, learns to adaptively transfer the most similar texture from multiple reference images to the super-resolution output whilst maintaining spatial coherence. The use of multiple reference images together with attention-based sampling is demonstrated to achieve significantly improved performance over state-of-the-art reference super-resolution approaches on multiple benchmark datasets. Reference super-resolution approaches have recently been proposed to overcome the ill-posed problem of image super-resolution by providing additional information from a high-resolution reference image. Multi-reference super-resolution extends this approach by providing a more diverse pool of image features to overcome the inherent information deficit whilst maintaining memory efficiency. A novel hierarchical attention-based sampling approach is introduced to learn the similarity between low-resolution image features and multiple reference images based on a perceptual loss. Ablation demonstrates the contribution of both multi-reference and hierarchical attention-based sampling to overall performance. Perceptual and quantitative ground-truth evaluation demonstrates significant improvement in performance even when the reference images deviate significantly from the target image. The project website can be found at https://marcopesavento.github.io/AMRSR/

We report improvements in recognition accuracy by up to 15% compared to single-modality datasets. Comparative analyses with existing datasets demonstrate the superior richness and variance our dataset offers, thereby facilitating more generalized and adaptable models. Conclusion/Implications: The MEx dataset provides a substantial contribution to the field of human activity recognition by offering a comprehensive and multi-faceted source of data. This work lays the groundwork for future research and applications, promoting advancements in domains such as personalized medicine, sports science, and interactive systems. Ultimately, the MEx dataset is a pivotal resource for researchers and practitioners seeking to develop accurate and reliable human activity recognition systems. Continuous blood pressure (CBP) monitoring offers significant advantages in healthcare management, but traditional methods are invasive. Photoplethysmography (PPG) provides a non-invasive alternative, yet developing robust, personalized models remains a challenge due to data heterogeneity and privacy concerns. This paper proposes a federated learning (FL) approach to estimate CBP from PPG signals. Our method enables collaborative model training across multiple decentralized datasets without sharing raw patient data, addressing privacy issues. We developed a novel FL framework incorporating personalized layers to capture individual-specific physiological characteristics. The proposed approach was evaluated on a benchmark dataset and compared to traditional centralized learning and conventional FL methods. Results demonstrate that our personalized federated learning method achieves superior accuracy in CBP estimation, as measured by mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean squared error (RMSE), while preserving data privacy. This study highlights the potential of FL in developing robust and personalized CBP estimation models, paving the way for improved non-invasive blood pressure monitoring and personalized healthcare. **Keywords:** Continuous Blood Pressure, Photoplethysmography (PPG), Federated Learning, Personalized Modeling, Privacy-Preserving, Non-Invasive Monitoring.

**Abstract** Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a powerful framework for enabling collaborative machine learning across distributed entities without the need for centralized data aggregation. However, traditional FL approaches often assume homogeneous data distributions and lack mechanisms to address data scarcity or domain divergence across clients. This paper introduces a novel Secure Federated Transfer Learning (SFTL) framework that integrates federated learning with advanced transfer learning techniques to facilitate effective knowledge sharing between diverse clients while preserving data privacy and security. The proposed approach utilizes secure multi-party computation and homomorphic encryption to ensure that sensitive data remains confidential throughout training, while adaptive transfer learning modules dynamically align and transfer knowledge between source and target domains. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SFTL achieves significant improvements in model accuracy and convergence speed compared to standard federated and transfer learning models, especially in non-IID (non-independent and identically distributed) and data-sparse scenarios. The framework's robust security guarantees are validated through comprehensive threat modeling and empirical analysis. Our findings highlight the potential of SFTL to enable privacy-preserving, cross-domain collaboration in sensitive fields such as healthcare, finance, and smart city applications. Key contributions include the design of the secure transfer mechanism and empirical evaluation of its effectiveness and scalability. Keywords: federated learning, transfer learning, privacy-preserving, homomorphic encryption, secure computation, domain adaptation, collaborative AI.

This paper introduces VSpSR, a novel approach to image super-resolution that leverages variational sparse representation to enable explorability. The objective is to enhance low-resolution images while allowing users to explore and control the super-resolution process. Our method employs a sparse coding technique to represent images, combined with a variational autoencoder to model the underlying distribution of image features. The VSpSR framework achieves high-quality super-resolution results while enabling users to manipulate and refine the output through an interactive interface. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of VSpSR in comparison to state-of-the-art super-resolution methods, with significant improvements in terms of visual quality and user control. The proposed approach has important implications for applications such as image editing, computer vision, and multimedia processing, and contributes to the development of more flexible and user-centric image super-resolution techniques. Key contributions include the integration of variational sparse representation and super-resolution, as well as the introduction of an exploratory interface for user-controlled image enhancement. Relevant keywords: super-resolution, variational autoencoder, sparse representation, image processing, computer vision.

Real-time fire and flame detection is critical for preventing catastrophic damage and ensuring public safety. This paper introduces a novel approach to address the challenges of accurate and rapid fire detection in complex environments. Our method combines a computationally efficient convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture with a custom-designed color and motion analysis module. The CNN is trained to identify fire-like patterns from visual input, while the color and motion module filters out false positives caused by factors such as sunlight or flickering lights. We evaluate our system on a diverse dataset of videos containing various fire scenarios, including different scales, types of environments, and obstructions. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed solution achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of detection accuracy and processing speed, surpassing existing methods by 15% in F1-score while maintaining a frame rate of over 60 FPS. This enables real-time deployment on resource-constrained devices, making it suitable for early warning systems and surveillance applications. Our findings offer a significant advancement in fire detection technology, providing a robust and efficient solution for enhancing safety and minimizing fire-related risks. Keywords: Fire detection, flame recognition, real-time processing, convolutional neural networks, computer vision, video surveillance.

The field of quantum communication promises secure and efficient information transfer, but faces challenges related to signal degradation and efficient encoding. A critical aspect involves mapping classical data onto quantum states, necessitating robust and efficient encoding schemes. This thesis addresses the need for optimized encoding strategies in quantum communication by exploring the application of Run Length Limited (RLL) de Bruijn sequences. RLL codes are essential for limiting the number of consecutive identical symbols, which is crucial for mitigating errors and ensuring reliable signal transmission in quantum channels. This research aims to develop and analyze novel RLL de Bruijn sequences tailored for quantum communication protocols. The objective is to construct RLL de Bruijn sequences with specific constraints on the run lengths of '0's and '1's, optimizing them for implementation in quantum key distribution (QKD) and other quantum communication systems. The methodology involves algorithmic design and implementation using Python, followed by simulation and analysis of the generated sequences. The system architecture utilizes established de Bruijn sequence generation techniques, modified to incorporate RLL constraints through constraint satisfaction algorithms and sequence filtering. The developed algorithms successfully generate RLL de Bruijn sequences meeting predefined run length limitations. These sequences exhibit improved characteristics compared to standard de Bruijn sequences in terms of error resilience and signal integrity, as demonstrated through simulations emulating noisy quantum channels. This research contributes to the field by providing a practical encoding strategy for quantum communication, potentially enhancing the performance and security of QKD systems. In conclusion, this thesis presents a novel approach to encoding data for quantum communication using RLL de Bruijn sequences. The results demonstrate the potential for improved performance and reliability in quantum communication systems. Future work could focus on implementing these RLL de Bruijn sequences in real-world quantum communication hardware and exploring adaptive RLL encoding strategies to further optimize performance under varying channel conditions. Furthermore, investigating the security implications of using RLL de Bruijn sequences within specific QKD protocols is a promising avenue for future research.

Berberin được biết đến như một loại kháng sinh thực vật với tác dụng kháng khuẩn, kháng nấm mạnh. Berberin ở kích thước nano cho thấy tiềm năng khắc phục các nhược điểm về độ tan trong nước và tính sinh khả dụng, từ đó mở ra nhiều tiềm năng ứng dụng. Trong nghiên cứu này, nano berberin (BerNPs) được hấp phụ trên màng cellulose vi khuẩn tạo vật liệu composite với tiềm năng ứng dụng làm vật liệu kháng khuẩn. Tính chất hạt BerNPs, cấu trúc và sự thay đổi cấu trúc bề mặt màng cellulose sinh học (Bacterial cellulose - BC) trước và sau khi hấp phụ BerNPs được khảo sát bằng phương pháp chụp FE-SEM, XRD và FT-IR. Khả năng kháng khuẩn của BerNPs và vật liệu composite được khảo sát trên vi khuẩn Escherichia coli và Streptococcus pyogenes trong điều kiện in vitro bằng phương pháp đồng nuôi cấy. Kết quả cho thấy, BerNPs có hoạt tính kháng E. coli và S. pyogenes mạnh, hạt BerNPs kích thước 50-60 nm có khả năng hấp phụ lên màng BC tốt nhất sau 2 giờ ngâm. Nghiên cứu bước đầu tạo được vật liệu composite có khả năng kháng lại E. coli và S. pyogenes với hiệu quả trên 80%.

Objective: Unsupervised many-to-many image translation models aim to map images across multiple domains without paired data, yet evaluating the correctness of these translations remains an open challenge. This paper introduces a comprehensive framework to assess how accurately such models preserve semantic content, style attributes, and inter-domain consistency. Methods: We propose three complementary evaluation metrics: (1) Semantic Consistency Score, based on feature-level similarity between input and translated images; (2) Domain Classification Accuracy, measuring how well a trained classifier recognizes the target domain; and (3) Perceptual Distance Index, which quantifies visual fidelity using a pretrained perceptual network. We further create a diverse benchmark dataset spanning facial attributes, artistic styles, and seasonal scenes, each with pseudo–ground-truth annotations for objective validation. Results: We apply our framework to several state-of-the-art many-to-many translators, including StarGAN variants and emerging attention-based architectures. Our metrics demonstrate strong correlation (Pearson’s r > 0.85) with human judgments of correctness, outperforming existing unsupervised evaluation methods such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS). Ablation studies show that combining semantic and perceptual measures yields the most robust assessment across all translation tasks. Conclusion: The proposed evaluation framework offers a principled, automated approach for quantifying correctness in unsupervised many-to-many image translation. By providing reliable, domain-agnostic metrics and a standard benchmark, our work facilitates fairer comparisons among models and guides future improvements in architecture design and training strategies. Keywords: Unsupervised Image Translation; Many-to-Many Mapping; Correctness Evaluation; Benchmark Metrics; Semantic Consistency; Perceptual Fidelity.

This paper investigates the application of deep learning techniques to enhance the classification of time series data, addressing the challenges posed by temporal dependencies and dynamic patterns inherent in such datasets. The study aims to provide a robust framework capable of accurately classifying time series instances across diverse domains. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel deep learning architecture, incorporating recurrent neural networks (RNN) and convolutional neural networks (CNN), designed specifically to capture both short-term and long-term dependencies in time series data. Our approach leverages advanced data preprocessing methods and feature extraction techniques to optimize model performance. A comprehensive evaluation is conducted using various benchmark datasets to demonstrate the adaptability and accuracy of the proposed model. Results/Findings: The experimental results show that our deep learning-based approach significantly outperforms traditional machine learning methods and existing deep learning models, achieving higher classification accuracy and reduced computational time. The model demonstrated strong performance across different types of time series data, highlighting its robustness and generalizability. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field of time series analysis by introducing an innovative deep learning framework that offers improved classification accuracy and efficiency. The findings have significant implications for real-world applications, including finance, healthcare, and environmental monitoring, where accurate time series analysis is crucial. Our approach sets the stage for future research in applying deep learning to complex temporal datasets, paving the way for further advancements in the field. Keywords: time series classification, deep learning, recurrent neural networks, convolutional neural networks, temporal dependencies, feature extraction.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown remarkable success in various domains, but its efficiency is often hindered by the need for extensive interaction with the environment. This paper addresses the challenge of experience reuse in RL by introducing a novel approach based on Policy Residual Representation (PRR). The objective is to enhance learning efficiency by leveraging past experiences to accelerate policy optimization in new tasks. We propose a framework that encodes the residual differences between policies, enabling the reuse of experiences across tasks with varying dynamics. Our method employs a deep neural network architecture to model these residuals, coupled with a dynamic experience replay mechanism that prioritizes relevant past experiences. Experimental results on benchmark environments demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces the sample complexity and improves convergence rates compared to traditional RL methods. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robust performance in transfer learning scenarios, showcasing its ability to generalize across tasks with minimal additional training. The findings highlight the potential of PRR for advancing RL applications in real-world settings, where data efficiency and adaptability are critical. This work contributes a scalable and practical solution for experience reuse, paving the way for more efficient and versatile RL systems. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Experience Reuse, Policy Residual Representation, Transfer Learning, Sample Efficiency, Deep Neural Networks.

This paper investigates the application of reinforcement learning (RL) within the R programming environment, providing a comprehensive exploration of how this powerful framework can be utilized for various problem-solving tasks. The objective of the study is to bridge the gap between theoretical RL concepts and practical implementation using R, making RL techniques more accessible to data scientists and researchers familiar with this programming language. The paper presents a detailed methodology for implementing Q-learning and policy gradient algorithms, two of the foundational RL techniques, within R. The approach involves integrating existing R packages with custom-built functions to create a robust RL toolkit. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of these implementations through several benchmark tasks commonly used in the RL domain, highlighting the performance of our R-based solutions in comparison to traditional Python-based RL libraries. The findings reveal that R can efficiently handle the computational demands of RL tasks, providing comparable results to more conventional environments. By successfully implementing RL algorithms in R, this research contributes a novel resource for data analysts and researchers, expanding the capability of R in machine learning and AI applications. The implications of this study suggest potential for future expansions into more advanced RL methods and applications in various industrial and academic fields. Key keywords include reinforcement learning, R programming, Q-learning, policy gradient, and machine learning.

With the rapid increase in model sizes and complexities, efficient model compression techniques become crucial for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This paper introduces LIT, a novel Block-wise Intermediate Representation Training approach aimed at enhancing model compression without compromising performance. Methods/Approach: The proposed method leverages intermediate representations within neural networks to strategically adjust the learning process on a block-by-block basis. LIT integrates an innovative mechanism for segmenting and reducing redundancy in model parameters, enabling smaller and more efficient model architectures. The approach is designed to maintain the fidelity of original model representations while smoothing the adaptation to compressed forms. Results/Findings: Extensive experimentation shows that LIT achieves significant compression ratios compared to conventional methods, with a minimal loss in accuracy across a range of benchmark datasets. The technique demonstrates superior performance on convolutional and transformer-based models, highlighting its versatility and effectiveness. Comparative analysis indicates that LIT outperforms existing model compression techniques both in speed and memory efficiency. Conclusion/Implications: By focusing on intermediate representations, LIT presents a transformative step forward in model compression for deep learning applications. The contributions of this research have substantial implications for deploying AI models in scenarios where computational and storage resources are limited. This makes LIT a valuable tool for diverse applications requiring efficient neural network deployments, including mobile and edge computing. Key Keywords: model compression, deep learning, intermediate representation, neural networks, resource-constrained environments, convolutional models, transformer models.

Data augmentation is a crucial technique for improving the generalization ability of deep learning models, especially when training data is limited. While existing methods have shown promise, many lack the ability to selectively focus on the most relevant parts of an image during augmentation, potentially introducing noise or irrelevant features. This paper introduces SaliencyMix, a novel data augmentation strategy that leverages saliency maps to guide the mixing of image regions. SaliencyMix identifies the salient regions of input images and mixes them proportionally, encouraging the model to focus on the most informative features. We evaluate SaliencyMix on several benchmark datasets for image classification, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. The experimental results demonstrate that SaliencyMix consistently outperforms state-of-the-art data augmentation techniques, leading to improved accuracy and robustness. Specifically, SaliencyMix achieves significant gains in top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, while requiring minimal computational overhead. These findings highlight the effectiveness of saliency guidance in data augmentation, offering a more targeted and efficient approach to regularization. Keywords: Data Augmentation, Saliency Map, Deep Learning, Regularization, Image Classification.

The results of this research demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in uncovering actionable insights from cryptocurrency data. The developed system successfully identifies patterns in price fluctuations, detects outliers, and generates user-friendly visualizations that aid in decision-making. The expected contributions of this work include advancing the field of cryptocurrency analytics, providing practical tools for stakeholders, and fostering a deeper understanding of market dynamics. In conclusion, this thesis highlights the importance of data-driven approaches in navigating the complexities of cryptocurrency markets. The findings underscore the potential of combining analytical techniques with visualization tools to unlock valuable insights. Future research directions include expanding the framework to incorporate real-time data, integrating additional data sources, and exploring advanced machine learning models for enhanced predictive accuracy. This study lays the groundwork for further exploration and innovation in the rapidly evolving domain of cryptocurrency analysis.

Various fonts give us various impressions, which are often represented by words. This paper proposes Impressions2Font (Imp2Font) that generates font images with specific impressions. Imp2Font is an extended version of conditional generative adversarial networks (GANs). More precisely, Imp2Font accepts an arbitrary number of impression words as the condition to generate the font images. These impression words are converted into a soft-constraint vector by an impression embedding module built on a word embedding technique. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations prove that Imp2Font generates font images with higher quality than comparative methods by providing multiple impression words or even unlearned words.

Super-resolution (SR) techniques have gained significant attention for their ability to enhance image quality by reconstructing high-resolution (HR) images from low-resolution (LR) inputs. However, existing methods often lack interpretability and fail to provide users with control over the reconstruction process. This paper introduces *Explorable Super Resolution* (ESR), a novel framework that integrates user-guided exploration into the SR pipeline. ESR leverages a hybrid approach combining deep learning-based generative models with interactive optimization techniques, enabling users to influence the reconstruction process and explore multiple plausible HR outputs. The proposed method employs a multi-scale feature extraction network and a differentiable exploration module, allowing real-time adjustments to texture, sharpness, and structural details. Experimental results demonstrate that ESR outperforms state-of-the-art SR methods in terms of both perceptual quality and user satisfaction, achieving a 15% improvement in structural similarity (SSIM) and a 20% reduction in computational overhead. Furthermore, ESR's interactive capabilities open new avenues for applications in medical imaging, satellite imagery, and digital restoration. This work contributes a significant step toward making SR systems more transparent, adaptable, and user-centric. **Keywords**: Super Resolution, Image Enhancement, Interactive Systems, Deep Learning, Generative Models, User-Guided Exploration.

This paper introduces a novel approach to self-supervised contrastive video representation learning, leveraging cycle encoding prediction to enhance the quality of learned representations. The objective is to improve the ability of models to capture complex temporal dynamics in videos without relying on labeled data. Our method employs a cycle consistency loss to predict future frames based on past frames, and vice versa, effectively encoding temporal information into the representation. We utilize a contrastive learning framework to maximize the similarity between positive pairs of frames while minimizing the similarity between negative pairs. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art self-supervised video representation learning methods, achieving significant improvements in video classification, object detection, and action recognition tasks. The key contributions of this work include the introduction of cycle encoding prediction as a means to capture temporal relationships and the demonstration of its effectiveness in learning robust video representations. Our approach has potential applications in various areas, including autonomous driving, surveillance, and human-computer interaction, and is particularly relevant to researchers interested in self-supervised learning, contrastive learning, and video analysis, with key keywords including self-supervised learning, contrastive learning, video representation, and temporal encoding.

Neural network pruning is a widely adopted technique to reduce model complexity and computational overhead, but it often introduces unintended biases that degrade model fairness and performance. This paper investigates the impact of pruning on bias amplification in neural networks and proposes a novel approach to mitigate these effects using knowledge distillation. We evaluate the bias introduced by various pruning techniques across multiple datasets and architectures, focusing on fairness metrics such as demographic parity and equalized odds. Our method leverages knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge from a robust, unpruned teacher model to a pruned student model, ensuring that the pruned network retains fairness while maintaining accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces bias in pruned models compared to traditional pruning methods, achieving a balance between model efficiency and fairness. The findings highlight the importance of addressing bias in resource-constrained environments and provide a practical framework for deploying fair and efficient neural networks. Key contributions include a comprehensive evaluation of pruning-induced bias and a distillation-based mitigation strategy that advances the state-of-the-art in fair model compression. **Keywords**: Neural network pruning, knowledge distillation, bias mitigation, fairness, model compression, AI ethics.

Face anti-spoofing is a critical challenge in biometric security, aimed at distinguishing genuine human faces from spoofing attacks such as printed photos, videos, or 3D masks. Traditional methods often struggle with generalization across diverse attack types and environmental conditions. This paper introduces a novel Physics-Guided Spoof Trace Disentanglement (PGSTD) framework for generic face anti-spoofing. The proposed approach leverages physical properties of spoofing traces, such as reflection, texture, and depth anomalies, to disentangle spoof-specific features from genuine facial characteristics. A multi-branch neural network architecture is employed, integrating physics-based constraints to guide the learning process and enhance interpretability. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including CASIA-SURF, Replay-Attack, and OULU-NPU, demonstrate that PGSTD achieves state-of-the-art performance, with significant improvements in cross-dataset generalization. The framework also exhibits robustness under varying lighting conditions and attack scenarios. By combining physical insights with deep learning, this work advances the field of face anti-spoofing, offering a more reliable and adaptable solution for real-world applications. **Keywords**: Face anti-spoofing, spoof trace disentanglement, physics-guided learning, biometric security, deep learning, generalization.

This study aims to develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based approach for cervical cancer classification in whole-slide histopathology images. The proposed method utilizes a deep learning architecture to automatically detect and classify cervical cancer from histopathological images. Our approach involves a transfer learning-based strategy, where a pre-trained CNN model is fine-tuned on a dataset of annotated whole-slide images. The results show that our method achieves high accuracy and sensitivity in distinguishing between normal and abnormal tissue samples, outperforming traditional machine learning-based approaches. The key findings of this study highlight the potential of CNN-based methods for automated cervical cancer diagnosis, enabling faster and more accurate detection. This research contributes to the development of computer-aided diagnosis systems for cervical cancer, with potential applications in clinical practice and medical research. The novelty of this approach lies in its ability to handle large whole-slide images and provide accurate classification results, making it a valuable tool for pathologists and medical professionals. Key keywords: CNN, deep learning, histopathology images, cervical cancer classification, computer-aided diagnosis.

This paper addresses the challenge of localization in aerial imagery by proposing a novel approach that leverages Grid Maps and LocGAN, a location-aware generative adversarial network. The objective is to accurately determine the location of an aerial image within a given map, which is crucial for various applications such as geographic information systems, autonomous vehicles, and surveillance. Our method utilizes a grid-based representation of the map, which is then used to train LocGAN to generate location-specific features from aerial images. The results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of localization accuracy, with a significant reduction in error rates. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of Grid Maps for aerial image localization and the development of LocGAN, which enables the generation of location-specific features. This work has important implications for the development of more accurate and efficient localization systems, with potential applications in fields such as computer vision, robotics, and geospatial analysis. Key keywords: aerial imagery, localization, Grid Maps, LocGAN, generative adversarial networks, computer vision, geographic information systems.

The paper addresses the challenge of environmental sound classification, a critical aspect of audio analysis with applications in surveillance, acoustic scene analysis, and smart environments. Traditional audio-based models often struggle to capture complex sound patterns effectively. This research aims to improve environmental sound classification by leveraging visual domain models, which have demonstrated superior performance in image recognition tasks. Methods/Approach: We propose ESResNet, a novel approach that adapts ResNet, a well-established visual recognition model, for environmental sound classification. The method involves converting audio signals into spectrograms, treating them as images, and subsequently using the ResNet architecture to classify these images. This approach allows us to harness the powerful feature extraction capabilities of ResNet, optimized for visual data, to enhance audio classification tasks. Results/Findings: Experiments conducted on benchmark environmental sound datasets demonstrate that ESResNet achieves significantly higher accuracy compared to traditional audio-based models. The model shows robust performance across diverse sound categories, achieving a notable improvement in classification precision and recall. The results underscore the effectiveness of integrating techniques across the visual and audio domains. Conclusion/Implications: The findings reveal that employing visual domain models like ResNet for environmental sound classification can lead to substantial improvements in accuracy and robustness. ESResNet sets a new benchmark for sound classification performance, offering valuable insights for the development of cross-domain models. The approach highlights the potential for broader applications, including real-time surveillance systems, urban monitoring, and intelligent acoustic environments, benefiting from enhanced sound recognition capabilities. Keywords: Environmental Sound Classification, ESResNet, ResNet, Spectrograms, Visual Domain Models, Audio Analysis, Cross-Domain Models.

This paper investigates the existence of universal adversarial examples in speech command classification, a crucial aspect of voice-controlled systems. The objective is to understand how these examples can compromise the integrity of speech recognition models. We employ a novel approach, leveraging a combination of adversarial attack methods and speech processing techniques to generate universal perturbations that can fool state-of-the-art speech classification models. Our results show that these perturbations can achieve high success rates in misclassifying speech commands across various models and datasets. The findings have significant implications for the security and reliability of voice-activated devices, highlighting the need for robust defenses against such attacks. This research contributes to the growing field of adversarial machine learning, with key applications in speech recognition, voice assistants, and audio classification. Keywords: universal adversarial examples, speech command classification, adversarial attacks, speech recognition, voice-controlled systems.

This paper presents an empirical evaluation of a Q-Learning algorithm for model-free autonomous soaring, addressing the challenge of enabling unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to efficiently exploit atmospheric thermals without prior environmental knowledge. The objective of this study is to develop and validate a reinforcement learning-based approach that allows UAVs to autonomously learn and adapt to dynamic thermal conditions. We propose a Q-Learning framework that leverages real-time sensor data to make decisions on flight path adjustments, optimizing energy gain from thermals. The algorithm is implemented in a simulated environment that replicates realistic atmospheric conditions, and its performance is evaluated against traditional rule-based soaring strategies. Results demonstrate that the Q-Learning algorithm achieves significant improvements in energy efficiency and flight duration, outperforming conventional methods by up to 25% in thermal exploitation. Furthermore, the model-free nature of the approach eliminates the need for pre-programmed environmental models, enhancing adaptability in unpredictable conditions. The findings highlight the potential of reinforcement learning in advancing autonomous soaring capabilities, with implications for applications in long-endurance UAV missions, environmental monitoring, and search-and-rescue operations. Key contributions include a novel Q-Learning-based framework for autonomous soaring and empirical evidence of its superiority over existing methods. Keywords: Q-Learning, autonomous soaring, reinforcement learning, UAVs, thermal exploitation, model-free control.

Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has gained significant attention for its potential in solving complex, collaborative tasks. However, the high variance in policy gradient methods remains a critical challenge, hindering convergence and scalability in multi-agent systems. This paper addresses the problem of variance reduction in multi-agent policy gradients, aiming to improve the stability and efficiency of learning in decentralized environments. We propose a novel framework that integrates variance-reduction techniques with decentralized policy optimization, leveraging both local and global information to minimize variance while maintaining policy independence. Our approach combines importance sampling, baseline subtraction, and adaptive learning rates to achieve robust performance across diverse multi-agent scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in convergence speed and final performance compared to existing methods, particularly in environments with high-dimensional state and action spaces. The proposed framework not only reduces variance but also enhances scalability, making it suitable for large-scale multi-agent applications. This work contributes to the advancement of MARL by providing a theoretically grounded and empirically validated solution to the variance problem, paving the way for more reliable and efficient multi-agent systems in real-world applications. **Keywords**: multi-agent reinforcement learning, policy gradients, variance reduction, decentralized optimization, scalability.

Graph-based data representation is a powerful tool for modeling complex relationships in various domains, including social networks, bioinformatics, and computer vision. However, traditional graph analysis methods often struggle with scalability and computational efficiency. This paper introduces *Stochastic Graphlet Embedding* (SGE), a novel approach for graph representation that leverages stochastic sampling to efficiently capture local and global structural patterns. The proposed method employs a randomized algorithm to extract and encode graphlets—small subgraphs that serve as building blocks for larger graphs—into a low-dimensional embedding space. By combining stochastic sampling with graphlet-based feature extraction, SGE significantly reduces computational complexity while preserving the discriminative power of graph representations. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SGE outperforms existing graph embedding techniques in terms of both accuracy and scalability, achieving state-of-the-art performance in graph classification and clustering tasks. Furthermore, the method exhibits robustness to noise and variations in graph structure, making it suitable for real-world applications. The key contribution of this work lies in its ability to balance efficiency and effectiveness, offering a scalable solution for large-scale graph analysis. Potential applications include network anomaly detection, molecular property prediction, and social network analysis. Keywords: graph embedding, graphlets, stochastic sampling, graph representation, graph classification, scalability.

Tây Nguyên, vùng trọng điểm cà phê của Việt Nam, đang chứng kiến sự hợp tác ngày càng chặt chẽ giữa hộ nông dân và doanh nghiệp trong chuỗi sản xuất và tiêu thụ. Doanh nghiệp, ngược lại, có được nguồn cung cà phê chất lượng cao, ổn định, đáp ứng yêu cầu khắt khe của thị trường trong nước và quốc tế. Để phát triển bền vững, cần có chính sách hỗ trợ từ nhà nước, tăng cường đào tạo kỹ năng cho nông dân, khuyến khích doanh nghiệp đầu tư vào công nghệ, xây dựng thương hiệu, và tạo dựng lòng tin giữa các đối tác. Sự liên kết hiệu quả sẽ là chìa khóa để nâng tầm ngành cà phê Tây Nguyên, tăng cường khả năng cạnh tranh trên thị trường toàn cầu.

Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) has gained significant attention for its ability to leverage learned dynamics models to improve sample efficiency. However, a critical challenge in MBRL is the propagation of uncertainty from the learned model to the policy optimization process, which can lead to suboptimal or unstable performance. This paper introduces an uncertainty-aware model-based policy optimization framework that explicitly addresses this challenge. Our approach integrates probabilistic dynamics models with a novel uncertainty quantification mechanism, enabling the policy to account for model inaccuracies during training. We propose a robust optimization algorithm that balances exploration and exploitation by dynamically adjusting the policy's reliance on the learned model based on its confidence estimates. Experimental results on benchmark control tasks demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing MBRL approaches, particularly in environments with high stochasticity or partial observability. The proposed framework not only enhances sample efficiency but also improves the robustness and reliability of learned policies, making it a promising solution for real-world applications where uncertainty is inherent. Key contributions include the integration of uncertainty quantification into policy optimization and a scalable algorithm that generalizes across diverse environments. Keywords: model-based reinforcement learning, uncertainty quantification, policy optimization, probabilistic models, sample efficiency.

The identification of lane-change maneuvers, particularly during on-ramp merges, is critical for understanding driver behavior and improving traffic safety. This study addresses the challenge of unsupervised lane-change identification in naturalistic driving data, where labeled datasets are often unavailable or costly to obtain. We propose a novel unsupervised approach leveraging clustering techniques and vehicle trajectory analysis to detect lane-change events without prior annotations. Our method integrates spatiotemporal features, such as relative velocity, acceleration, and lateral displacement, to distinguish lane changes from other driving behaviors. The algorithm is evaluated on a large-scale naturalistic driving dataset, demonstrating high accuracy in identifying lane-change maneuvers during on-ramp merges. Comparative analysis with existing supervised methods reveals that our approach achieves competitive performance while eliminating the need for labeled training data. The results highlight the potential of unsupervised techniques for scalable and cost-effective analysis of driving behaviors. This research contributes to the development of advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving technologies by providing a robust framework for lane-change detection in real-world scenarios. **Keywords**: lane-change identification, unsupervised learning, naturalistic driving data, on-ramp merge, trajectory analysis, driver behavior, ADAS.

The development of robust object detection systems crucially relies on high-quality, diverse datasets. This paper introduces the EuroCity Persons (ECP) dataset, a novel benchmark specifically designed for training and evaluating pedestrian detection algorithms in complex urban environments. The ECP dataset comprises high-resolution images and videos captured across multiple European cities, exhibiting significant variations in lighting conditions, weather, and pedestrian density. We meticulously annotated the dataset with detailed bounding boxes for all visible pedestrians, including occluded and partially visible instances, using a consistent annotation protocol. We evaluated several state-of-the-art object detection models on the ECP dataset and present a comprehensive performance analysis, highlighting the challenges posed by the dataset's complexity. Results demonstrate that existing models struggle to maintain high accuracy across all environmental conditions, indicating significant room for improvement. The ECP dataset provides a valuable resource for advancing pedestrian detection research and fostering the development of more reliable and robust autonomous systems in real-world scenarios. The dataset and evaluation code will be publicly available. Keywords: Object Detection, Pedestrian Detection, Dataset, Benchmark, Autonomous Systems, Computer Vision.

Objective: Traditional resizing operations in convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—such as fixed pooling or interpolation—lack flexibility to adapt feature-map dimensions to task-specific needs. We propose Shape Adaptor, a novel learnable resizing module that dynamically adjusts spatial and channel dimensions within deep architectures to improve representational efficiency and task performance. Methods: Shape Adaptor embeds differentiable scaling parameters into standard resizing layers. During training, the module jointly optimizes scale factors for height, width, and channel depth via backpropagation, guided by a regularization term that encourages stability and prevents degenerate shapes. It can be seamlessly inserted between convolutional blocks or used in multi-branch network designs without altering existing optimization pipelines. Results: We evaluate Shape Adaptor on image classification (CIFAR-100, ImageNet), object detection (COCO), and semantic segmentation (Cityscapes). Compared to fixed pooling and interpolation baselines, networks equipped with Shape Adaptor achieve up to 2.5% higher top-1 accuracy on ImageNet and 1.8% mAP improvement on COCO, while maintaining comparable inference cost. Ablation studies demonstrate that learned resizing yields more discriminative feature maps and accelerates convergence by 15% on average. Conclusion: By transforming resizing from a hand-crafted to a learnable operation, Shape Adaptor enhances model adaptability and performance across diverse vision tasks. Its plug-and-play design and minimal overhead make it a practical tool for network architecture optimization, efficient feature aggregation, and dynamic resource allocation. Keywords: Shape Adaptor, learnable resizing, deep learning, convolutional neural network, dynamic scaling.

The aim of this study is to explore an innovative approach for vertebral body segmentation using the GrowCut algorithm, a method known for its applicability in image segmentation tasks. This research addresses the challenges associated with accurate, efficient segmentation of vertebral bodies, which is critical for various medical analyses and interventions. Methods/Approach: We implemented the GrowCut algorithm to perform vertebral body segmentation. GrowCut is a cellular automaton-based method that utilizes user-defined seeds to propagate labels across images, effectively capturing complex structures. The workflow developed includes preprocessing steps for enhancing image quality and interactive user input for seed placement, ensuring optimal segmentation results. Results/Findings: Our findings indicate that the GrowCut-based segmentation method delivers high accuracy and consistency in delineating vertebral bodies when tested on medical imaging datasets. Comparative analysis with conventional methods demonstrated that this approach significantly reduces manual intervention time while maintaining precision. The system's performance was evaluated in terms of computational efficiency and segmentation accuracy, showing promising results for clinical application. Conclusion/Implications: This study demonstrates the practical utility of the GrowCut algorithm in vertebral body segmentation, presenting an effective workflow that enhances both speed and accuracy. The contributions include a robust segmentation technique that can be integrated into clinical environments, aiding in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures related to spinal conditions. Further research could expand its application to other anatomical regions and explore integration with automated medical imaging systems. Key Keywords: Vertebral body segmentation, GrowCut algorithm, medical imaging, image segmentation, cellular automaton, clinical application.

This paper introduces *Subject2Vec*, a novel generative-discriminative framework designed to transform a set of image patches into a compact, informative vector representation. The primary objective is to address the challenge of efficiently encoding high-dimensional image data into a low-dimensional space while preserving critical discriminative features. The proposed approach combines generative modeling to capture the underlying distribution of image patches with a discriminative mechanism to ensure the resulting vector is optimized for downstream tasks such as classification, clustering, or retrieval. The framework leverages advanced deep learning techniques, including variational autoencoders (VAEs) and contrastive learning, to achieve robust and generalizable representations. Experimental results demonstrate that *Subject2Vec* outperforms existing methods in terms of both reconstruction accuracy and task-specific performance across multiple benchmark datasets. The model's ability to generate interpretable and task-agnostic vectors highlights its potential for applications in medical imaging, remote sensing, and computer vision. This work contributes a scalable and versatile solution for feature extraction from image sets, offering significant improvements in efficiency and performance over traditional approaches. **Keywords**: Image representation, generative-discriminative models, deep learning, variational autoencoders, contrastive learning, feature extraction.

Tình trạng xơ hóa gan và nhiễm mỡ gan ở bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ liên quan đang trở thành một vấn đề sức khỏe nghiêm trọng. Bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ liên quan (NAFLD) là một tình trạng phổ biến ở những người thừa cân, béo phì, nơi gan bị nhiễm mỡ do tích tụ mỡ trong tế bào gan. Theo nghiên cứu, khoảng 25% dân số thế giới bị NAFLD, và tỷ lệ này đang tăng lên do sự gia tăng của béo phì và thừa cân. NAFLD có thể dẫn đến xơ hóa gan, một tình trạng nghiêm trọng nơi tế bào gan bị thay thế bằng mô xơ, làm giảm khả năng gan của cơ thể. Xơ hóa gan có thể dẫn đến các vấn đề sức khỏe nghiêm trọng, bao gồm suy gan, ung thư gan và thậm chí là tử vong. Vì vậy, việc chẩn đoán và điều trị NAFLD một cách sớm và hiệu quả là rất quan trọng. Các nghiên cứu gần đây đã chỉ ra rằng việc giảm cân và thay đổi lối sống có thể giúp ngăn chặn sự tiến triển của NAFLD và xơ hóa gan. Ngoài ra, các phương pháp điều trị như thuốc và phẫu thuật cũng đang được nghiên cứu để giúp điều trị NAFLD. Tóm lại, tình trạng xơ hóa gan và nhiễm mỡ gan ở bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ liên quan là một vấn đề sức khỏe nghiêm trọng cần được chú ý và điều trị sớm.

This paper addresses the challenge of predicting the co-evolution of event and knowledge graphs, which is crucial for understanding the dynamics of complex systems and making informed decisions. Our objective is to develop a novel framework that can forecast the future states of both event and knowledge graphs, capturing their interdependent relationships. We propose a hybrid approach that combines graph neural networks with temporal convolutional networks to model the co-evolutionary process. Our method learns to represent events and entities as embedded vectors, allowing us to predict future graph structures and identify key factors driving the co-evolution. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming baseline methods in predicting graph evolution and event occurrence. Our research contributes to the development of predictive models for complex systems, with potential applications in areas such as recommendation systems, social network analysis, and decision support systems. Key keywords: co-evolution, event graphs, knowledge graphs, graph neural networks, temporal convolutional networks, predictive modeling.

Segmenting transparent objects in complex environments is a challenging task due to their unique visual properties and diverse contexts. This research aims to develop a robust method for accurately identifying and segmenting transparent objects 'in the wild,' where unpredictable conditions and backgrounds are common. Methods/Approach: We introduce an advanced segmentation model leveraging a combination of deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures. Our model is trained on a diverse dataset specifically curated for transparent object segmentation, enhanced by data augmentation strategies to simulate real-world scenarios. We also incorporate a novel attention mechanism to improve the model's ability to distinguish transparent objects from their surrounding environment. Results/Findings: The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing existing methods in segmenting transparent objects across various real-world settings. Experimental results indicate a significant improvement in segmentation accuracy and robustness, particularly in challenging lighting conditions and complex scenes. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a marked increase in precision and recall compared to previous approaches. Conclusion/Implications: This study presents a novel approach to transparent object segmentation, providing a significant contribution to the fields of computer vision and image processing. Our model's ability to handle diverse and unpredictable environments has potential applications in augmented reality, robotics, and autonomous systems where interaction with transparent materials is prevalent. The standardization of the transparent object dataset further supports future research and development in this domain. Keywords: Transparent object segmentation, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, transformers, attention mechanism, computer vision.

Tkey provides a user-friendly API and comprehensive documentation, greatly simplifying the integration of cryptographic key management into various applications. Its open-source library is fully extendable, with custom modules designed to enhance compatibility with different system architectures, enabling seamless adaptation to specific project requirements. Furthermore, Tkey leverages Docker to package and deploy applications within isolated, portable containers. This approach not only ensures a consistent operating environment across diverse infrastructures but also reduces deployment complexity and mitigates potential differences between development, testing, and production stages. By combining robust key management capabilities with flexible modularity and containerization, Tkey empowers developers to securely and efficiently manage keys while maintaining high levels of system compatibility and operational reliability across multiple platforms and environments.

Image super-resolution (SR) techniques have been developing rapidly, benefiting from the invention of deep networks and its successive breakthroughs. However, it is acknowledged that deep learning and deep neural networks are difficult to interpret. SR networks inherit this mysterious nature and little works make attempt to understand them. In this paper, we perform attribution analysis of SR networks, which aims at finding the input pixels that strongly influence the SR results. We propose a novel attribution approach called local attribution map (LAM), which inherits the integral gradient method yet with two unique features. One is to use the blurred image as the baseline input, and the other is to adopt the progressive blurring function as the path function. Based on LAM, we show that: (1) SR networks with a wider range of involved input pixels could achieve better performance. (2) Attention networks and non-local networks extract features from a wider range of input pixels. (3) Comparing with the range that actually contributes, the receptive field is large enough for most deep networks. (4) For SR networks, textures with regular stripes or grids are more likely to be noticed, while complex semantics are difficult to utilize. Our work opens new directions for designing SR networks and interpreting low-level vision deep models.

This paper presents a novel approach to virtual character animation control through data-driven reinforcement learning. The objective is to enhance the realism and adaptability of animated characters in interactive environments by using a learning-based framework that can efficiently generate responsive and lifelike animations. Methods/Approach: We propose a reinforcement learning model that leverages large datasets of motion capture data to train virtual characters. By integrating advanced neural network architectures, specifically designed to handle high-dimensional input spaces, our approach optimizes policy learning for character control. This model is further refined through a reward function tailored to maintain natural and physically plausible movements. Results/Findings: The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in animation quality and control flexibility as compared to traditional keyframe-based and procedural approaches. Our system can generate seamless transitions between diverse actions and adapt to different scenarios with minimal preprogramming. Experimental results show that characters trained using our data-driven reinforcement learning method exhibit more fluid and realistic motion patterns. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field of virtual animation by introducing a robust and scalable solution for character control using reinforcement learning. The implications of this work extend to various applications, including gaming, virtual reality, and simulation environments, where dynamic and believable character interaction is crucial. Our findings open avenues for further exploration in real-time character animation driven by AI technologies, promising advancements in how virtual worlds are populated and experienced. Keywords: reinforcement learning, virtual character animation, data-driven methods, motion capture, neural networks, AI, animation control, realistic animation.

We motivate and present feature selective anchor-free (FSAF) module, a simple and effective building block for single-shot object detectors. It can be plugged into single-shot detectors with feature pyramid structure. The FSAF module addresses two limitations brought up by the conventional anchor-based detection: 1) heuristic-guided feature selection; 2) overlap-based anchor sampling. The general concept of the FSAF module is online feature selection applied to the training of multi-level anchor-free branches. Specifically, an anchor-free branch is attached to each level of the feature pyramid, allowing box encoding and decoding in the anchor-free manner at an arbitrary level. During training, we dynamically assign each instance to the most suitable feature level. At the time of inference, the FSAF module can work jointly with anchor-based branches by outputting predictions in parallel. We instantiate this concept with simple implementations of anchor-free branches and online feature selection strategy. Experimental results on the COCO detection track show that our FSAF module performs better than anchor-based counterparts while being faster. When working jointly with anchor-based branches, the FSAF module robustly improves the baseline RetinaNet by a large margin under various settings, while introducing nearly free inference overhead. And the resulting best model can achieve a state-of-the-art 44.6% mAP, outperforming all existing single-shot detectors on COCO.

This paper presents an innovative approach to belief propagation, a fundamental algorithm in probabilistic graphical models, by introducing anytime belief propagation using sparse domains. The objective is to improve the efficiency and scalability of belief propagation in large-scale networks. Our method leverages sparse domain representations to reduce computational complexity, enabling anytime inference that can provide approximate solutions at any point during the computation. We employ a novel sparse domain construction technique, which adaptively prunes irrelevant variables and factors, resulting in significant speedups without sacrificing accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming traditional belief propagation methods in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy. The key contributions of this research include the development of a sparse domain-based anytime belief propagation algorithm, which has significant implications for real-time applications, such as computer vision, robotics, and artificial intelligence. Our approach combines probabilistic graphical models, sparse representations, and anytime algorithms, making it a valuable contribution to the field of machine learning and AI. Key keywords: belief propagation, sparse domains, anytime algorithms, probabilistic graphical models, machine learning, artificial intelligence.

The vehicle re-identification (ReID) plays a critical role in the perception system of autonomous driving, which attracts more and more attention in recent years. However, to our best knowledge, there is no existing complete solution for the surround-view system mounted on the vehicle. In this paper, we argue two main challenges in above scenario: i) In single camera view, it is difficult to recognize the same vehicle from the past image frames due to the fisheye distortion, occlusion, truncation, etc. ii) In multi-camera view, the appearance of the same vehicle varies greatly from different camera's viewpoints. Thus, we present an integral vehicle Re-ID solution to address these problems. Specifically, we propose a novel quality evaluation mechanism to balance the effect of tracking box's drift and target's consistency. Besides, we take advantage of the Re-ID network based on attention mechanism, then combined with a spatial constraint strategy to further boost the performance between different cameras. The experiments demonstrate that our solution achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while being real-time in practice. Besides, we will release the code and annotated fisheye dataset for the benefit of community.
