Object detection has been a focus of research in human-computer interaction. Skin area detection has been a key to different recognitions like face recognition, human motion detection, pornographic and nude image prediction, etc. Most of the research done in the fields of skin detection has been trained and tested on human images of African, Mongolian and Anglo-Saxon ethnic origins. Although there are several intensity invariant approaches to skin detection, the skin color of Indian sub-continentals have not been focused separately. The approach of this research is to make a comparative study between three image segmentation approaches using Indian sub-continental human images, to optimize the detection criteria, and to find some efficient parameters to detect the skin area from these images. The experiments observed that HSV color model based approach to Indian sub-continental skin detection is more suitable with considerable success rate of 91.1% true positives and 88.1% true negatives.

The channel redundancy in feature maps of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) results in the large consumption of memories and computational resources. In this work, we design a novel Slim Convolution (SlimConv) module to boost the performance of CNNs by reducing channel redundancies. Our SlimConv consists of three main steps: Reconstruct, Transform and Fuse, through which the features are splitted and reorganized in a more efficient way, such that the learned weights can be compressed effectively. In particular, the core of our model is a weight flipping operation which can largely improve the feature diversities, contributing to the performance crucially. Our SlimConv is a plug-and-play architectural unit which can be used to replace convolutional layers in CNNs directly. We validate the effectiveness of SlimConv by conducting comprehensive experiments on ImageNet, MS COCO2014, Pascal VOC2012 segmentation, and Pascal VOC2007 detection datasets. The experiments show that SlimConv-equipped models can achieve better performances consistently, less consumption of memory and computation resources than non-equipped conterparts. For example, the ResNet-101 fitted with SlimConv achieves 77.84% top-1 classification accuracy with 4.87 GFLOPs and 27.96M parameters on ImageNet, which shows almost 0.5% better performance with about 3 GFLOPs and 38% parameters reduced.

Markhacanasin, một hợp chất tự nhiên, đang được nghiên cứu về khả năng gây chết tế bào theo chương trình (apoptosis) trong tế bào ung thư. Các nghiên cứu in silico (mô phỏng trên máy tính) cho thấy Markhacanasin có thể tương tác với các protein quan trọng liên quan đến quá trình apoptosis, mở ra tiềm năng ức chế sự phát triển của tế bào ung thư. Nghiên cứu sâu hơn về Markhacanasin có thể mở ra hướng đi mới trong việc phát triển các liệu pháp điều trị ung thư dựa trên các hợp chất tự nhiên.

This paper introduces TSI, a novel framework for video action recognition that leverages temporal saliency integration to enhance the accuracy of action detection. The objective is to address the challenge of capturing complex and dynamic actions in videos by developing a more effective and efficient approach. Our method utilizes a multi-scale temporal saliency map to highlight important regions and frames, which are then integrated into a deep neural network to learn robust action representations. Experimental results demonstrate that TSI outperforms state-of-the-art methods on several benchmark datasets, achieving significant improvements in action recognition accuracy. The key findings indicate that the proposed temporal saliency integration strategy can effectively capture long-range dependencies and subtle action cues, leading to better performance in recognizing complex actions. This research contributes to the field of computer vision and has potential applications in areas such as surveillance, human-computer interaction, and autonomous systems. Key keywords: video action recognition, temporal saliency, deep learning, computer vision, action detection.

This paper introduces Pix2seq, a novel language modeling framework designed for object detection tasks. The objective is to bridge the gap between computer vision and natural language processing by leveraging the strengths of both domains. Our approach utilizes a sequence-to-sequence model, where images are encoded into a sequence of tokens that can be processed by a language model. This enables the application of powerful language modeling techniques, such as transformer architectures, to object detection problems. Our results show that Pix2seq achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, outperforming traditional computer vision-based approaches. The key findings indicate that the framework's ability to capture complex relationships between objects and scenes is a major contributor to its success. The implications of this research are significant, as it opens up new avenues for applying language modeling techniques to a wide range of computer vision tasks. The contributions of Pix2seq include its unique architecture, which enables efficient and effective object detection, and its potential to be extended to other applications such as image captioning and visual question answering. Key keywords: object detection, language modeling, transformer, sequence-to-sequence, computer vision, natural language processing.

This paper aims at revisiting Graph Convolutional Neural Networks by bridging the gap between spectral and spatial design of graph convolutions. We theoretically demonstrate some equivalence of the graph convolution process regardless it is designed in the spatial or the spectral domain. The obtained general framework allows to lead a spectral analysis of the most popular ConvGNNs, explaining their performance and showing their limits. Moreover, the proposed framework is used to design new convolutions in spectral domain with a custom frequency profile while applying them in the spatial domain. We also propose a generalization of the depthwise separable convolution framework for graph convolutional networks, what allows to decrease the total number of trainable parameters by keeping the capacity of the model. To the best of our knowledge, such a framework has never been used in the GNNs literature. Our proposals are evaluated on both transductive and inductive graph learning problems. Obtained results show the relevance of the proposed method and provide one of the first experimental evidence of transferability of spectral filter coefficients from one graph to another. Our source codes are publicly available at: https://github.com/balcilar/Spectral-Designed-Graph-Convolutions

This research addresses the challenge of object detection and delineation in computer vision, proposing a novel method that utilizes extreme points to represent objects effectively. The extreme points approach aims to simplify the process of identifying and outlining objects within images, enhancing accuracy and efficiency. Methods/Approach: The study introduces a new methodology wherein objects are represented by their extreme points—specifically the topmost, bottommost, leftmost, and rightmost points—which serve as key markers for object detection. This approach reduces the complexity associated with traditional bounding box methods. To evaluate the proposed method, we implemented a deep learning-based model that harnesses these extreme points to improve object localization and segmentation tasks. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that the extreme points method significantly improves the precision of object delineation across various standard benchmarking datasets. The method showcases superior performance in terms of speed and accuracy compared to conventional techniques, such as bounding boxes and contour-based methods. Additionally, the approach proved to be versatile across different types of objects and image environments, making it a robust solution in the field of object detection. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of extreme points as a fundamental element in object detection represents a notable advancement in simplifying and enhancing object localization tasks. This research contributes to the broader field of computer vision by providing an efficient, accurate, and scalable technique that can be applied in numerous applications, including autonomous vehicles, robotics, and image-based search engines. Future work will explore extending this approach to handle highly dynamic scenes and improving integration with other advanced computer vision algorithms. Keywords: Object detection, extreme points, computer vision, object localization, deep learning, image segmentation.

Deep semi-supervised learning (SSL) has gained significant attention for leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data to improve classification performance. However, existing clustering-based regularization methods often struggle with scalability, robustness, and adaptability to complex datasets. This paper introduces **CycleCluster**, a novel framework designed to modernize clustering regularization for deep SSL. The proposed approach integrates cyclic consistency and adaptive clustering mechanisms to enhance feature representation and ensure robust decision boundaries. CycleCluster employs a dual-phase training process, where clustering constraints are dynamically adjusted based on the evolving feature space, enabling better alignment between labeled and unlabeled data distributions. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CycleCluster outperforms state-of-the-art SSL methods, achieving significant improvements in classification accuracy and robustness to label scarcity. The framework also exhibits superior scalability and adaptability across diverse data domains. By addressing key limitations in traditional clustering regularization, CycleCluster offers a promising direction for advancing deep SSL in real-world applications, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data. **Keywords**: Semi-supervised learning, clustering regularization, deep learning, cyclic consistency, adaptive clustering, classification.

Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is widely used for temporal data processing. However, existing methods can neither learn the discriminative prototypes of different classes nor exploit such prototypes for further analysis. We propose Discriminative Prototype DTW (DP-DTW), a novel method to learn class-specific discriminative prototypes for temporal recognition tasks. DP-DTW shows superior performance compared to conventional DTWs on time series classification benchmarks. Combined with end-to-end deep learning, DP-DTW can handle challenging weakly supervised action segmentation problems and achieves state of the art results on standard benchmarks. Moreover, detailed reasoning on the input video is enabled by the learned action prototypes. Specifically, an action-based video summarization can be obtained by aligning the input sequence with action prototypes.

Many important real-world problems have action spaces that are high-dimensional, continuous or both, making full enumeration of all possible actions infeasible. Instead, only small subsets of actions can be sampled for the purpose of policy evaluation and improvement. In this paper, we propose a general framework to reason in a principled way about policy evaluation and improvement over such sampled action subsets. This sample-based policy iteration framework can in principle be applied to any reinforcement learning algorithm based upon policy iteration. Concretely, we propose Sampled MuZero, an extension of the MuZero algorithm that is able to learn in domains with arbitrarily complex action spaces by planning over sampled actions. We demonstrate this approach on the classical board game of Go and on two continuous control benchmark domains: DeepMind Control Suite and Real-World RL Suite.

Objective: Recovering complete 3D shapes from partial point clouds is crucial for applications in robotics, autonomous driving, and augmented reality. Existing methods often struggle to preserve fine-grained geometry and global context simultaneously. Methods: We propose a novel Skip-Attention Network with Hierarchical Folding (SAN-HF) for point cloud completion. Our encoder extracts multi-scale features from the incomplete input, while a skip-attention module dynamically fuses high-resolution details with deep semantic representations. In the decoder, a hierarchical folding scheme generates point clouds in a coarse-to-fine manner: a base surface is first reconstructed at low resolution, then progressively refined through local folding operations that capture detailed geometry. We optimize the network end-to-end using a combination of Chamfer Distance and Earth Mover’s Distance losses. In many practical applications, such as fraud detection, credit risk modeling or medical decision making, classification models for assigning instances to a predefined set of classes are required to be both precise as well as interpretable. Linear modeling methods such as logistic regression are often adopted, since they offer an acceptable balance between precision and interpretability. Linear methods, however, are not well equipped to handle categorical predictors with high-cardinality or to exploit non-linear relations in the data. As a solution, data preprocessing methods such as weight-of-evidence are typically used for transforming the predictors. The binning procedure that underlies the weight-of-evidence approach, however, has been little researched and typically relies on ad-hoc or expert driven procedures. The objective in this paper, therefore, is to propose a formalized, data-driven and powerful method. To this end, we explore the discretization of continuous variables through the binning of spline functions, which allows for capturing non-linear effects in the predictor variables and yields highly interpretable predictors taking only a small number of discrete values. Moreover, we extend upon the weight-of-evidence approach and propose to estimate the proportions using shrinkage estimators. Together, this offers an improved ability to exploit both non-linear and categorical predictors for achieving increased classification precision, while maintaining interpretability of the resulting model and decreasing the risk of overfitting. We present the results of a series of experiments in a fraud detection setting, which illustrate the effectiveness of the presented approach. We facilitate reproduction of the presented results and adoption of the proposed approaches by providing both the dataset and the code for implementing the experiments and the presented approach.

We propose a systematic framework to evaluate the embeddability of various types of relations, focusing on their geometric and topological characteristics. Using a combination of graph theory and optimization techniques, we develop a novel algorithm that determines the minimal dimensionality required for accurate embeddings. Our experiments demonstrate that certain classes of relations, such as hierarchical and symmetric structures, exhibit high embeddability, while others, like cyclic or highly irregular relations, pose significant challenges. The results reveal a clear trade-off between embedding dimensionality and preservation of relational properties. This work provides a theoretical foundation for designing efficient embedding methods and offers practical insights for applications in natural language processing, recommendation systems, and network analysis. The proposed approach advances the state-of-the-art by enabling more reliable and interpretable embeddings, with potential implications for improving the performance of downstream machine learning tasks. **Keywords**: relational embedding, Euclidean space, graph theory, dimensionality reduction, knowledge representation, machine learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of identifying profitable options strategies under budget constraints using a novel approach based on Budgeted Reinforcement Learning (BRL). The proposed framework integrates reinforcement learning with budget-aware decision-making to optimize trading actions while adhering to predefined financial limits. We introduce a tailored algorithm that dynamically allocates resources across multiple options contracts, balancing exploration and exploitation to maximize returns. Experimental results on real-world market data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming traditional heuristic-based strategies in terms of profitability and risk management. The findings highlight the potential of BRL in financial decision-making, offering a scalable and adaptive solution for options discovery. This research contributes to the growing field of AI-driven finance by providing a robust framework for budget-constrained trading, with implications for both individual investors and institutional traders. **Keywords**: Options trading, Budgeted Reinforcement Learning, Financial decision-making, AI-driven finance, Risk management.

Accurate and fine-grained urban traffic flow inference is crucial for intelligent transportation systems. However, existing methods often struggle with data sparsity and the complex spatial dependencies inherent in urban traffic. This paper introduces a novel road network guided approach for fine-grained traffic flow inference. Our method leverages the underlying road network structure to regularize and enhance the inference process. We propose a graph-based deep learning model that explicitly incorporates road network connectivity and hierarchy as inductive biases. This model aggregates traffic information from neighboring road segments, effectively mitigating the impact of data sparsity. Furthermore, we design a specialized loss function that promotes consistency between inferred traffic flows and the road network topology. Experimental results on real-world traffic datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios with limited data availability. The proposed approach provides more accurate and reliable traffic flow estimates, enabling better traffic management and urban planning. Keywords: Traffic Flow Inference, Road Network, Graph Neural Networks, Deep Learning, Intelligent Transportation Systems.

The rapid evolution of DeepFake technology has raised significant concerns regarding its misuse and the challenges it poses to digital media authenticity. This study investigates the evolution of DeepFakes by analyzing the manipulation of specific facial regions and evaluating the performance of state-of-the-art fake detection methods. We employ a systematic approach, leveraging advanced deep learning models to generate and detect synthetic facial manipulations across diverse datasets. Our analysis focuses on identifying the most vulnerable facial regions to DeepFake alterations and assessing the robustness of detection algorithms under varying conditions, including resolution, lighting, and compression artifacts. Experimental results reveal that certain facial regions, such as the eyes and mouth, are more susceptible to manipulation, while detection performance varies significantly depending on the dataset and the quality of the DeepFake. Furthermore, we propose a novel detection framework that integrates multi-region analysis and temporal consistency checks, achieving improved accuracy compared to existing methods. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to combat DeepFake threats by providing insights into the vulnerabilities of facial regions and advancing detection techniques. The findings have implications for developing more reliable authentication systems and enhancing digital media integrity in the era of AI-driven content generation. **Keywords**: DeepFakes, facial manipulation, fake detection, deep learning, digital media integrity, AI-driven content.

This paper addresses the problem of relative camera pose estimation, a crucial task in various computer vision applications such as 3D reconstruction, augmented reality, and robotics. Our objective is to develop a robust and accurate method for estimating the relative pose between two cameras using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). We propose a novel CNN-based approach that takes a pair of images as input and predicts the relative rotation and translation between the cameras. Our method leverages the capabilities of deep learning to learn features from images and estimate the relative pose. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. The proposed method outperforms traditional feature-based approaches and other deep learning-based methods, with significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. Our research contributes to the development of more accurate and efficient computer vision systems, with potential applications in fields such as autonomous vehicles, virtual reality, and surveillance. Key keywords: relative camera pose estimation, convolutional neural networks, deep learning, computer vision, 3D reconstruction.

This paper presents a novel approach to neural architecture search (NAS) using graph-based methods and operation embeddings. The objective is to efficiently explore the vast space of possible neural network architectures to find optimal designs for specific tasks. Our method represents neural networks as graphs, where nodes denote operations and edges signify connections between them. We leverage operation embeddings to capture the semantic meaning of different operations, enabling the search process to focus on the most promising architectures. The search algorithm utilizes a reinforcement learning framework to navigate the graph space, guided by a reward function that balances performance and computational cost. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing NAS methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, particularly on large-scale image classification tasks. The key contributions of this work include the introduction of operation embeddings to NAS and the development of a graph-based search algorithm that effectively exploits these embeddings. Our research has significant implications for the automated design of neural networks, enabling faster and more accurate model development for a wide range of applications, including computer vision and natural language processing. Key keywords: neural architecture search, graph-based methods, operation embeddings, reinforcement learning, automated machine learning.

Human visual recognition of activities or external agents involves an interplay between high-level plan recognition and low-level perception. Given that, a natural question to ask is: can low-level perception be improved by high-level plan recognition? We formulate the problem of leveraging recognized plans to generate better top-down attention maps \cite to improve the perception performance. We call these top-down attention maps specifically as plan-recognition-driven attention maps. To address this problem, we introduce the Pixel Dynamics Network. Pixel Dynamics Network serves as an observation model, which predicts next states of object points at each pixel location given observation of pixels and pixel-level action feature. This is like internally learning a pixel-level dynamics model. Pixel Dynamics Network is a kind of Convolutional Neural Network (ConvNet), with specially-designed architecture. Therefore, Pixel Dynamics Network could take the advantage of parallel computation of ConvNets, while learning the pixel-level dynamics model. We further prove the equivalence between Pixel Dynamics Network as an observation model, and the belief update in partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) framework. We evaluate our Pixel Dynamics Network in event recognition tasks. We build an event recognition system, ER-PRN, which takes Pixel Dynamics Network as a subroutine, to recognize events based on observations augmented by plan-recognition-driven attention.

In self-supervised learning, one trains a model to solve a so-called pretext task on a dataset without the need for human annotation. The main objective, however, is to transfer this model to a target domain and task. Currently, the most effective transfer strategy is fine-tuning, which restricts one to use the same model or parts thereof for both pretext and target tasks. In this paper, we present a novel framework for self-supervised learning that overcomes limitations in designing and comparing different tasks, models, and data domains. In particular, our framework decouples the structure of the self-supervised model from the final task-specific fine-tuned model. This allows us to: 1) quantitatively assess previously incompatible models including handcrafted features; 2) show that deeper neural network models can learn better representations from the same pretext task; 3) transfer knowledge learned with a deep model to a shallower one and thus boost its learning. We use this framework to design a novel self-supervised task, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on the common benchmarks in PASCAL VOC 2007, ILSVRC12 and Places by a significant margin. Our learned features shrink the mAP gap between models trained via self-supervised learning and supervised learning from 5.9% to 2.6% in object detection on PASCAL VOC 2007.

**Abstract** Gesture recognition plays a critical role in enabling intuitive human-computer interaction, but reliably identifying important or context-relevant actions remains a challenge, especially in complex environments with similar or overlapping gestures. This paper presents a novel gesture recognition framework that emphasizes the detection of important actions by employing a path searching method within a weighted graph. The proposed approach models gesture sequences as nodes and transitions on a graph, where edge weights are dynamically assigned based on the significance and correlation of adjacent actions. By leveraging an efficient path searching algorithm, the system prioritizes gesture sequences that represent important or target actions, leading to improved recognition accuracy for critical gestures. Experimental results on publicly available gesture datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms conventional sequence matching and deep learning-based classifiers, particularly in scenarios where distinguishing similar gestures is crucial. The findings highlight significant improvements in recognition precision and robustness, with minimal computational overhead. This research contributes a scalable and adaptable solution for gesture-based systems in applications such as sign language interpretation, surveillance, and smart device control. Key contributions include the integration of weighted graph modeling with path search optimization for gesture recognition and the focused detection of important actions. Keywords: gesture recognition, important action detection, weighted graph, path searching, human-computer interaction, action recognition.

In this contribution, we used the GrowCut segmentation algorithm publicly available in three-dimensional Slicer for three-dimensional segmentation of vertebral bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time that the GrowCut method has been studied for the usage of vertebral body segmentation. In brief, we found that the GrowCut segmentation times were consistently less than the manual segmentation times. Hence, GrowCut provides an alternative to a manual slice-by-slice segmentation process.

We present a framework, which we call Molecule Deep Q-Networks (MolDQN), for molecule optimization by combining domain knowledge of chemistry and state-of-the-art reinforcement learning techniques (double Q-learning and randomized value functions). We directly define modifications on molecules, thereby ensuring 100\% chemical validity. Further, we operate without pre-training on any dataset to avoid possible bias from the choice of that set. Inspired by problems faced during medicinal chemistry lead optimization, we extend our model with multi-objective reinforcement learning, which maximizes drug-likeness while maintaining similarity to the original molecule. We further show the path through chemical space to achieve optimization for a molecule to understand how the model works.

An informative measurement is the most efficient way to gain information about an unknown state. We give a first-principles derivation of a general-purpose dynamic programming algorithm that returns a sequence of informative measurements by sequentially maximizing the entropy of possible measurement outcomes. This algorithm can be used by an autonomous agent or robot to decide where best to measure next, planning a path corresponding to an optimal sequence of informative measurements. This algorithm is applicable to states and controls that are continuous or discrete, and agent dynamics that is either stochastic or deterministic; including Markov decision processes. Recent results from approximate dynamic programming and reinforcement learning, including on-line approximations such as rollout and Monte Carlo tree search, allow an agent or robot to solve the measurement task in real-time. The resulting near-optimal solutions include non-myopic paths and measurement sequences that can generally outperform, sometimes substantially, commonly-used greedy heuristics such as maximizing the entropy of each measurement outcome. This is demonstrated for a global search problem, where on-line planning with an extended local search is found to reduce the number of measurements in the search by half.

The proliferation of 3D data in applications such as augmented reality and automated driving necessitates efficient methods for processing point clouds, which are collections of discrete data points in 3D space. This study presents a novel convolutional decoder employing adaptive instance normalization specifically designed for point cloud data, addressing limitations in existing point cloud decoding techniques. Methods: We introduce an innovative approach leveraging convolutional neural networks enhanced with adaptive instance normalization (AdaIN) to decode point clouds. The proposed model adaptively adjusts feature maps by normalizing the instances and incrporating learned affine parameters, enabling more accurate and scalable reconstructions of original 3D shapes. This method is tested against standard datasets to benchmark its performance and versatility. Results: Our experiments demonstrate that the convolutional decoder with AdaIN significantly improves the fidelity of point cloud reconstructions compared to traditional normalization methods. The adaptive aspect of the normalization facilitates superior generalization to diverse 3D objects. Quantitative evaluations show improvements in metrics such as reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency, validating the superiority of our model. Conclusion: The introduction of adaptive instance normalization in the realm of point cloud decoding reveals significant advancements, offering a novel contribution that enhances performance beyond existing decoders. The proposed framework has potential applications in various fields requiring 3D data processing, including virtual reality environments, robotic navigation, and object recognition systems. These findings encourage further exploration into adaptive normalization techniques for other point cloud processing tasks. Keywords: Convolutional neural networks, point clouds, adaptive instance normalization, 3D data processing, reconstruction accuracy, AI models.

Several works based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) have been recently proposed to predict a set of medical images from a single modality (e.g, FLAIR MRI from T1 MRI). However, such frameworks are primarily designed to operate on images, limiting their generalizability to non-Euclidean geometric data such as brain graphs. While a growing number of connectomic studies has demonstrated the promise of including brain graphs for diagnosing neurological disorders, no geometric deep learning work was designed for multiple target brain graphs prediction from a source brain graph. Despite the momentum the field of graph generation has gained in the last two years, existing works have two critical drawbacks. First, the bulk of such works aims to learn one model for each target domain to generate from a source domain. Thus, they have a limited scalability in jointly predicting multiple target domains. Second, they merely consider the global topological scale of a graph (i.e., graph connectivity structure) and overlook the local topology at the node scale of a graph (e.g., how central a node is in the graph). To meet these challenges, we introduce MultiGraphGAN architecture, which not only predicts multiple brain graphs from a single brain graph but also preserves the topological structure of each target graph to predict. Its three core contributions lie in: (i) designing a graph adversarial auto-encoder for jointly predicting brain graphs from a single one, (ii) handling the mode collapse problem of GAN by clustering the encoded source graphs and proposing a cluster-specific decoder, (iii) introducing a topological loss to force the reconstruction of topologically sound target brain graphs. Our MultiGraphGAN significantly outperformed its variants thereby showing its great potential in multi-view brain graph generation from a single graph.

This paper introduces MeshGAN, a novel approach to creating non-linear 3D morphable models of human faces using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The objective of this research is to address the limitations of traditional linear 3D morphable models in capturing the complex and nuanced variations in human facial geometry. Our approach employs a GAN-based architecture, which consists of a generator capable of producing realistic and diverse facial meshes, and a discriminator that ensures the generated meshes are indistinguishable from real data. The MeshGAN model is trained on a comprehensive dataset of 3D facial scans, enabling it to learn high-dimensional, non-linear facial morphologies. The results demonstrate that MeshGAN can generate a wide spectrum of facial shapes with high fidelity and realism, surpassing the capabilities of existing linear models. MeshGAN's efficacy is evaluated through quantitative metrics and visual comparisons, showcasing its superior performance in representing intricate facial features and expressions. Our findings suggest potential applications in fields such as virtual reality, animation, and identity verification, where accurate 3D facial representation is crucial. This research contributes to the advancement of 3D facial modeling by providing a robust tool for crafting more lifelike and varied facial models, paving the way for future innovations in computational graphics and computer vision. Key keywords include MeshGAN, 3D morphable models, GANs, neural networks, facial reconstruction, and non-linear modeling.

Cấp nước an toàn cho đô thị là một thách thức toàn cầu, đặc biệt khi đối mặt với biến đổi khí hậu và sự gia tăng dân số. Kinh nghiệm quốc tế cho thấy quản lý rủi ro là yếu tố then chốt để đảm bảo nguồn cung nước bền vững. Các quốc gia tiên tiến áp dụng phương pháp tiếp cận toàn diện, bao gồm đánh giá và giảm thiểu rủi ro từ nguồn nước, hệ thống xử lý, mạng lưới phân phối đến người tiêu dùng. This paper addresses the challenge of unsupervised video depth estimation, a critical task in computer vision with applications in autonomous navigation, augmented reality, and 3D reconstruction. Traditional methods often rely on supervised learning with labeled datasets, which are costly and time-consuming to acquire. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel framework that leverages ego-motion and disparity consensus for unsupervised depth estimation from monocular video sequences. Our approach integrates a self-supervised learning pipeline that utilizes geometric constraints derived from camera motion and stereo correspondence, eliminating the need for ground-truth depth labels. The proposed model employs a dual-branch architecture to jointly optimize depth prediction and ego-motion estimation, ensuring consistency between predicted depth maps and observed scene geometry. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art supervised and unsupervised approaches, with significant improvements in depth accuracy and robustness under varying lighting and motion conditions. The key contribution of this work lies in its ability to generate reliable depth maps without labeled data, making it highly scalable and practical for real-world applications. This research advances the field of unsupervised learning in computer vision and provides a foundation for future work in self-supervised depth estimation. **Keywords**: unsupervised learning, depth estimation, ego-motion, disparity consensus, monocular video, self-supervised learning, computer vision.

This paper proposes AD-Cluster, a novel approach to domain adaptive person re-identification that leverages augmented discriminative clustering to enhance the robustness and accuracy of person re-identification models in unseen target domains. The objective is to address the challenge of domain shift in person re-identification, where models trained on a source domain often struggle to generalize to a target domain with different environmental conditions. AD-Cluster employs a unique clustering-based approach that augments the discriminative power of the model by generating pseudo-labels for the target domain, which are then used to fine-tune the model. Experimental results demonstrate that AD-Cluster outperforms state-of-the-art methods in domain adaptive person re-identification, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a novel clustering-based domain adaptation method and the demonstration of its effectiveness in person re-identification. This work has important implications for real-world applications, such as surveillance and security, where person re-identification models are often required to operate in diverse and unseen environments. Key keywords: domain adaptive person re-identification, augmented discriminative clustering, pseudo-label generation, fine-tuning, deep learning.

This paper introduces PyKEEN 1.0, a comprehensive Python library designed to facilitate the training and evaluation of knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models. Knowledge graph embeddings are crucial for representing large, complex relational data in a continuous vector space, enabling applications such as link prediction, entity classification, and data integration. PyKEEN 1.0 addresses the growing need for a unified, extensible, and user-friendly framework that supports a wide range of KGE algorithms and evaluation protocols. The library implements a modular design, allowing researchers and practitioners to easily train, test, and benchmark various embedding models across multiple datasets. PyKEEN 1.0 offers robust support for hyperparameter optimization, reproducible experiments, and extensible pipeline components, which streamline the development and comparison of new approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that PyKEEN 1.0 achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art models, while significantly reducing the effort required for experimentation and deployment. The library’s flexibility, well-documented APIs, and active community contributions make it a valuable resource for both academic research and practical applications in knowledge graph analytics. Keywords: knowledge graph embeddings, Python library, link prediction, entity classification, KGE models, machine learning, open-source software.

This paper investigates the performance capabilities of Vision Transformers (ViTs) compared to Residual Networks (ResNets) in image classification tasks, particularly in scenarios without pretraining or the use of strong data augmentations. The aim is to explore the efficiency and effectiveness of ViTs under minimal preprocessing conditions. Methods/Approach: We conducted a series of experiments using both Vision Transformers and ResNets on multiple standard image datasets. Unlike traditional approaches that rely heavily on pretraining and elaborate data augmentation techniques to enhance model performance, our approach evaluates these architectures in their raw form. The study involves training from scratch and applying only basic image transformations during the training phase. Results/Findings: The results reveal that Vision Transformers can outperform Residual Networks without the need for extensive pretraining or strong data augmentation strategies. ViTs demonstrated superior generalization capabilities across diverse datasets, achieving higher accuracy rates compared to ResNets in the majority of cases. Our analysis indicates that the flexibility in the attention mechanism of ViTs contributes significantly to their robustness when faced with varied data distributions and limited preprocessing. Conclusion/Implications: This research highlights a significant shift in the landscape of image classification architectures, showcasing the potential of Vision Transformers in scenarios where computationally intensive preprocessing techniques are not feasible. This has profound implications for deploying efficient and high-performing models in environments with limited resources. Our findings suggest a path forward for harnessing the power of Transformers in computer vision tasks, opening opportunities for further exploration into optimization and deployment strategies for ViTs. Keywords: Vision Transformers, Residual Networks, Image Classification, Pretraining, Data Augmentation, Attention Mechanism, Deep Learning.

Expectation Propagation (EP) is a powerful approximate Bayesian inference technique, but its computational cost and convergence speed can be limiting factors, particularly for complex models. This paper introduces two novel algorithms designed to accelerate the convergence of EP while maintaining accuracy. First, we propose a damped EP algorithm that incorporates a damping factor to stabilize the iterative updates of the approximate posterior, preventing oscillations and divergence. Second, we develop an accelerated EP algorithm based on Anderson acceleration, which extrapolates from previous iterations to predict a more optimal solution. We demonstrate the efficacy of our algorithms on several benchmark problems, including Bayesian logistic regression and Gaussian mixture models. Empirical results show that our proposed algorithms significantly reduce the number of iterations required for convergence compared to standard EP, leading to substantial computational savings. Furthermore, our algorithms exhibit improved stability and are less prone to divergence. These fast convergent EP algorithms offer a practical alternative for approximate Bayesian inference in computationally demanding scenarios. Keywords: Expectation Propagation, Bayesian Inference, Approximate Inference, Convergence Acceleration, Damping, Anderson Acceleration.

Key keywords: sheep identification, age estimation, weight estimation, deep learning, CNNs, livestock monitoring, precision agriculture.

We study the video super-resolution (SR) problem for facilitating video analytics tasks, e.g. action recognition, instead of for visual quality. The popular action recognition methods based on convolutional networks, exemplified by two-stream networks, are not directly applicable on video of low spatial resolution. This can be remedied by performing video SR prior to recognition, which motivates us to improve the SR procedure for recognition accuracy. Tailored for two-stream action recognition networks, we propose two video SR methods for the spatial and temporal streams respectively. On the one hand, we observe that regions with action are more important to recognition, and we propose an optical-flow guided weighted mean-squared-error loss for our spatial-oriented SR (SoSR) network to emphasize the reconstruction of moving objects. On the other hand, we observe that existing video SR methods incur temporal discontinuity between frames, which also worsens the recognition accuracy, and we propose a siamese network for our temporal-oriented SR (ToSR) training that emphasizes the temporal continuity between consecutive frames. We perform experiments using two state-of-the-art action recognition networks and two well-known datasets--UCF101 and HMDB51. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed SoSR and ToSR in improving recognition accuracy.

Imitation learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for training agents to perform complex tasks by mimicking expert demonstrations. However, most existing approaches rely on first-person demonstrations, which are often costly or impractical to obtain. This paper introduces a novel framework for *third-person imitation learning*, where an agent learns to perform tasks by observing expert demonstrations from a third-person perspective. Our approach leverages a combination of deep reinforcement learning and domain adaptation techniques to bridge the gap between third-person observations and first-person actions. We propose a two-stage training process: first, a feature extraction module aligns third-person observations with the agent's first-person state space, and second, a policy network learns to map these aligned states to actions. Experiments conducted in simulated and real-world environments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to traditional first-person imitation learning approaches, while significantly reducing the need for costly first-person data collection. The results highlight the potential of third-person imitation learning as a scalable and practical alternative for training intelligent agents in diverse applications, including robotics and autonomous systems. **Keywords**: imitation learning, third-person perspective, reinforcement learning, domain adaptation, robotics, autonomous systems.

This paper introduces GTNet, a novel Generative Transfer Network designed to tackle the challenging task of zero-shot object detection. The objective is to enable detectors to recognize objects from unseen classes without requiring any prior training data. To achieve this, GTNet employs a generative approach, leveraging a transfer learning framework to learn a shared feature space between seen and unseen classes. The method utilizes a combination of generative adversarial networks and transfer learning to synthesize features for unseen classes, allowing the detector to generalize to new objects. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of GTNet, outperforming state-of-the-art zero-shot object detection methods on benchmark datasets. The key findings highlight the importance of generative modeling in zero-shot learning, enabling the detection of objects from unseen classes with significant improvements in accuracy. GTNet contributes to the advancement of zero-shot object detection, paving the way for applications in autonomous systems, surveillance, and robotics, where detecting unseen objects is crucial. Key keywords: zero-shot object detection, generative transfer network, transfer learning, generative adversarial networks, computer vision, object recognition.

Mở đầu: Trong những năm gần đây, tiêm vi điểm botulinum toxin (BoNT) và acid hyaluronic (HA) được ứng dụng rộng rãi trong trẻ hóa da. Tuy nhiên chưa tìm thấy nghiên cứu nào so sánh hiệu quả trẻ hóa da của tiêm vi điểm botulinum toxin so với acid hyaluronic. Mục tiêu: Nghiên cứu nhằm đánh giá hiệu quả và an toàn của tiêm vi điểm botulinum toxin so với acid hyaluronic trẻ hóa da tại Bệnh Viện Da Liễu Thành Phố Hồ Chí Minh. Phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu quan sát mô tả trên 31 trường hợp được tiêm vi điểm nửa mặt bằng botulinum toxin và nửa mặt còn lại bằng acid hyaluronic không liên kết chéo. Dữ liệu ghi nhận dựa trên phân tích hình ảnh, chụp phân tích nếp nhăn bằng máy Visia, bảng câu hỏi khảo sát. Ghi nhận dữ liệu ở thời điểm trước khi tiêm và sau khi tiêm ở tuần 1, 2, 4, 8 và 12. Kết quả: Tiêm vi điểm BoNT, HA không liên kết chéo an toàn. Các tác dụng không mong muốn xảy ra thoáng qua, không có sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thống kê về tỷ lệ phản ảnh mức độ đau, vết đỏ do kim tiêm, sẩn phù, sưng bầm giữa 2 nhóm (p > 0.05). Các đối tượng tham gia nghiên cứu đều hài lòng với cả BoNT và HA. Mức độ hài lòng BoNT cao nhất ở tuần thứ 8, trong khi HA cao nhất ở tuần thứ 4. Mức độ hài lòng với BoNT luôn cao hơn HA, có ý nghĩa thống kê ở tuần thứ 8 (p < 0.001). Hiệu quả cải thiện nếp nhăn của HA cao nhất ở tuần thứ 1 (theo thang Glogau và GAIS) và ở tuần thứ 4 (theo máy phân tích da). Hiệu quả giảm nhăn BoNT kéo dài 12 tuần, đạt hiệu quả tối đa ở tuần thứ 2 (theo thang Glogau và GAIS) và ở tuần thứ 4 (theo máy phân tích da). Tiêm vi điểm BoNT cho hiệu quả cao hơn so với HA, kết quả có ý nghĩa thống kê ở tuần thứ 1, 2, 4 và 8 theo thang GAIS (p < 0.05), kết quả không có ý nghĩa thống kê theo thang Glogau và máy phân tích da (p > 0.05). Kết luận: Tiêm vi điểm BoNT và HA không liên kết chéo có tính an toàn, tạo sự hài lòng cho bệnh nhân. Tiêm vi điểm HA phù hợp cho mong muốn hiệu quả nhanh trong khi tiêm vi điểm BoNT là lựa chọn ưu thế cho những người cần cải thiện nếp nhăn.

Nghiên cứu về hành vi tiêu dùng của sinh viên tại Hà Nội đối với chuỗi cung ứng ứng dụng (app) cho thấy nhiều yếu tố tác động đáng kể. Các yếu tố văn hóa, xã hội như gia đình, bạn bè và nhóm tham khảo có ảnh hưởng lớn đến quyết định sử dụng ứng dụng. Thu nhập cá nhân và khả năng tài chính cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng, đặc biệt với các ứng dụng trả phí hoặc yêu cầu mua hàng trong ứng dụng. Sự tiện lợi, dễ sử dụng và tính năng hữu ích của ứng dụng là những yếu tố then chốt thu hút sinh viên. Bên cạnh đó, các chương trình khuyến mãi, giảm giá và đánh giá từ người dùng khác cũng tác động đến quyết định lựa chọn ứng dụng. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng, nhận thức về rủi ro bảo mật thông tin cá nhân có thể ảnh hưởng tiêu cực đến hành vi sử dụng ứng dụng của sinh viên. Các yếu tố này cần được các nhà phát triển ứng dụng và nhà cung cấp dịch vụ chú trọng để đáp ứng nhu cầu và thu hút đối tượng người dùng tiềm năng là sinh viên tại Hà Nội.

Most compilers for machine learning (ML) frameworks need to solve many correlated optimization problems to generate efficient machine code. Current ML compilers rely on heuristics based algorithms to solve these optimization problems one at a time. However, this approach is not only hard to maintain but often leads to sub-optimal solutions especially for newer model architectures. Existing learning based approaches in the literature are sample inefficient, tackle a single optimization problem, and do not generalize to unseen graphs making them infeasible to be deployed in practice. To address these limitations, we propose an end-to-end, transferable deep reinforcement learning method for computational graph optimization (GO), based on a scalable sequential attention mechanism over an inductive graph neural network. GO generates decisions on the entire graph rather than on each individual node autoregressively, drastically speeding up the search compared to prior methods. Moreover, we propose recurrent attention layers to jointly optimize dependent graph optimization tasks and demonstrate 33%-60% speedup on three graph optimization tasks compared to TensorFlow default optimization. On a diverse set of representative graphs consisting of up to 80,000 nodes, including Inception-v3, Transformer-XL, and WaveNet, GO achieves on average 21% improvement over human experts and 18% improvement over the prior state of the art with 15x faster convergence, on a device placement task evaluated in real systems.

Kỹ thuật ủ hiếu khí vi sinh vật đang được ứng dụng rộng rãi trong xử lý chất thải hữu cơ, đặc biệt là xác cá và phân vịt. Phương pháp này tận dụng hoạt động của các vi sinh vật hiếu khí để phân hủy chất thải một cách hiệu quả, giảm thiểu mùi hôi và nguy cơ ô nhiễm môi trường. Quá trình ủ hiếu khí không chỉ giúp xử lý nhanh chóng lượng lớn chất thải mà còn tạo ra sản phẩm phụ có giá trị như phân bón hữu cơ, góp phần vào việc phát triển nông nghiệp bền vững. Nghiên cứu của Phạm Hồng Ngân và Trương Thế Quyết đã chứng minh hiệu quả của kỹ thuật này trong việc xử lý xác cá và phân vịt, mở ra hướng đi mới trong quản lý chất thải chăn nuôi và thủy sản.

This paper introduces *Learning Subspace Minimization (LSM)*, a novel framework for addressing low-level vision tasks such as image denoising, super-resolution, and inpainting. The objective of this research is to overcome the limitations of traditional optimization-based methods, which often struggle with computational inefficiency and suboptimal performance on complex visual data. LSM leverages a data-driven approach to learn a low-dimensional subspace that captures the essential features of natural images, enabling efficient and accurate minimization of energy functions. The proposed method combines the strengths of deep learning and classical optimization techniques, employing a neural network to predict subspace parameters and a lightweight iterative solver to refine the results. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that LSM achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple low-level vision tasks, outperforming existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The framework’s ability to generalize across diverse datasets and its robustness to noise further highlight its practical applicability. This work contributes a scalable and versatile solution for low-level vision problems, with potential applications in medical imaging, autonomous systems, and real-time video processing. Key innovations include the integration of subspace learning with energy minimization and the development of a hybrid architecture that bridges the gap between data-driven and model-based approaches. Keywords: low-level vision, subspace learning, energy minimization, image restoration, deep learning, optimization.

The rapid advancement of automotive radar systems has raised critical questions about the trade-offs between sensor resolution and classification performance in real-world applications. This study investigates the necessity of high-resolution experimental radar systems compared to off-the-shelf, lower-resolution sensors for automotive radar classification tasks. We evaluate the performance of both sensor types in detecting and classifying common road objects, such as vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, under varying environmental conditions. A machine learning-based classification framework is employed to process radar data, leveraging feature extraction and supervised learning techniques to assess accuracy, precision, and recall metrics. Our findings reveal that while high-resolution experimental radar systems offer marginal improvements in classification accuracy, off-the-shelf sensors achieve comparable performance in most practical scenarios, particularly when combined with robust signal processing algorithms. These results suggest that cost-effective, lower-resolution sensors may suffice for many automotive applications, reducing the need for expensive, high-resolution systems. This research provides valuable insights for automotive manufacturers and researchers aiming to balance performance and cost in radar-based classification systems. **Keywords**: automotive radar, sensor resolution, object classification, machine learning, signal processing, cost-performance trade-off.

Weakly supervised object localization (WSOL) aims to identify object bounding boxes using only image-level labels, posing a significant challenge. This paper introduces an attention-based dropout layer designed to enhance feature discrimination and localization accuracy in WSOL. Our approach leverages the attention maps generated by a convolutional neural network to selectively drop less relevant feature activations, encouraging the network to focus on discriminative regions corresponding to the target objects. By adaptively pruning feature maps based on attention scores during training, the proposed layer promotes the learning of more robust and localized feature representations. Experimental results on the benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing WSOL techniques, with significant improvements in both localization accuracy and classification performance. The attention-based dropout layer effectively mitigates the common issue of focusing on background clutter and improves the network's ability to identify the complete extent of objects. This research offers a novel and effective strategy for improving weakly supervised object localization. Keywords: Weakly Supervised Object Localization, Attention Mechanism, Dropout, Convolutional Neural Networks, Feature Discrimination.

This paper investigates the efficacy of leveraging just 15 keypoints for accurate human pose estimation in computer vision applications. The motivation stems from the need to optimize computational resources and simplify model complexity without significantly sacrificing performance. We present a streamlined deep learning-based approach that utilizes a reduced set of anatomically informative keypoints, carefully selected to capture essential aspects of human posture. The proposed method is evaluated on standard human pose datasets, demonstrating competitive accuracy compared to models using denser keypoint annotations while achieving notable improvements in inference speed and resource consumption. Extensive experiments reveal that the 15-keypoint configuration not only reduces the dimensionality of pose representation but also maintains robustness across varied poses and occlusion scenarios. The findings suggest that precise localization and action recognition tasks can be accomplished effectively with significantly fewer keypoints, challenging the prevailing notion that high-resolution keypoint sets are necessary for performance. This work provides practical insights for real-time applications such as motion analysis, augmented reality, and human-computer interaction, where efficiency and accuracy are paramount. Keywords: human pose estimation, keypoints, deep learning, efficiency, computer vision, dimensionality reduction, real-time applications.

Nghiên cứu sử dụng kỹ thuật cộng hưởng từ tương phản pha để định lượng dòng chảy dịch não tủy (CSF) tại cống não ở người khỏe mạnh. Mục tiêu là thiết lập các giá trị tham chiếu cho dòng chảy CSF bình thường, yếu tố quan trọng để đánh giá các rối loạn liên quan đến sự lưu thông của dịch này. Kết quả cho thấy có sự khác biệt đáng kể về lưu lượng CSF theo chu kỳ tim, với lưu lượng lớn nhất xảy ra trong thì tâm thu. Các thông số như lưu lượng đỉnh, lưu lượng trung bình và thể tích nhát bóp đã được đo lường và phân tích, cung cấp dữ liệu định lượng chi tiết về động lực học CSF tại cống não. Nghiên cứu này đóng góp vào việc hiểu rõ hơn về sinh lý học CSF và có thể được sử dụng để so sánh với các trường hợp bệnh lý, hỗ trợ chẩn đoán và theo dõi điều trị các bệnh lý liên quan đến rối loạn lưu thông dịch não tủy như não úng thủy. Việc định lượng chính xác dòng chảy CSF là rất quan trọng để đánh giá chức năng hệ thần kinh trung ương và phát hiện sớm các bất thường.

Trầm cảm là vấn đề sức khỏe tâm thần đáng quan tâm, đặc biệt trong môi trường học tập căng thẳng như sinh viên Y khoa. Nghiên cứu về dấu hiệu trầm cảm và các yếu tố liên quan ở sinh viên Y đa khoa Trường Đại học Y khoa Phạm Ngọc Thạc cho thấy, tỷ lệ sinh viên có biểu hiện trầm cảm khá cao, chủ yếu do áp lực học tập, thi cử và thiếu thời gian nghỉ ngơi. Các triệu chứng phổ biến bao gồm mệt mỏi, mất ngủ, giảm hứng thú với các hoạt động thường ngày và cảm giác tự ti. Yếu tố gia đình, môi trường sống và khả năng thích ứng với căng thẳng cũng ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến tình trạng này. Nghiên cứu nhấn mạnh sự cần thiết của các biện pháp hỗ trợ tâm lý và nâng cao nhận thức về sức khỏe tâm thần trong cộng đồng sinh viên Y khoa.

Quy trình giải trình tự Sanger là một phương pháp quan trọng trong việc chẩn đoán các biến thể đa hình đơn nucleotide (SNP) trên gen CLDN-1, một gen có vai trò quan trọng trong việc duy trì tính toàn vẹn của hàng rào biểu mô. Phương pháp này cho phép xác định chính xác các biến thể di truyền có thể ảnh hưởng đến chức năng của gen, từ đó góp phần vào việc hiểu rõ hơn về các bệnh lý liên quan. Quy trình bao gồm các bước như chuẩn bị mẫu DNA, thực hiện phản ứng PCR để khuếch đại đoạn gen cần nghiên cứu, sau đó tiến hành giải trình tự để phân tích các nucleotide. Kết quả thu được không chỉ giúp xác định các SNP mà còn có thể hỗ trợ trong việc phát triển các phương pháp điều trị cá nhân hóa cho bệnh nhân. Việc áp dụng quy trình này trong nghiên cứu gen CLDN-1 mở ra hướng đi mới trong việc chẩn đoán và điều trị các bệnh lý liên quan đến gen này.

WebSocket là một giao thức mạng hai chiều cho phép truyền tải dữ liệu theo thời gian thực giữa máy khách và máy chủ. WebSocket cho phép truyền dữ liệu trong thờ gan thực và có thể được sử dụng để tạo các ứng dụng như trò chuyện trực tuyến, cập nhật dữ liệu theo thời gian thực. Trong hệ thống này, chúng tôi sử dụng thư viện Socket.o điểm triển khai việc truyền dữ liệu thời gian thực giữa các người dùng. Thư viện này cung cấp một cách dễ dàng để thiết lập kết nối hai chiều giữa máy chủ và máy khách thông qua các kênh truyền thông dựa trên giao thức WebSocket .

Nghiên cứu về ảnh hưởng của hệ số dẫn nhiệt tầng móng và nền đường tới nhiệt độ lớp bê tông nhựa trên đường ô tô đã được thực hiện, nhằm làm rõ tác động của các yếu tố này đến tuổi thọ và độ bền của mặt đường. Kết quả cho thấy, hệ số dẫn nhiệt của tầng móng và nền đường có ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến sự thay đổi nhiệt độ trong lớp bê tông nhựa. Hệ số dẫn nhiệt thấp có thể dẫn đến nhiệt độ cao hơn trong lớp bê tông nhựa vào mùa hè, làm tăng nguy cơ biến dạng vĩnh viễn và hư hỏng do lún vệt bánh xe. Ngược lại, vào mùa đông, hệ số dẫn nhiệt thấp có thể làm giảm nguy cơ nứt nẻ do nhiệt độ thấp. Việc lựa chọn vật liệu và thiết kế kết cấu đường cần xem xét đến hệ số dẫn nhiệt để đảm bảo ổn định nhiệt cho mặt đường, từ đó kéo dài tuổi thọ công trình và giảm chi phí bảo trì. Loài nấm ký sinh côn trùng *Isaria javanica* (Frider. & Bally) Samsom là một trong những loại nấm có khả năng kiểm soát sinh học hiệu quả, thường được sử dụng để quản lý các loài côn trùng gây hại. Nấm này có đặc điểm sinh học nổi bật như khả năng phát triển mạnh trong điều kiện ẩm ướt và nhiệt độ ôn hòa, thích hợp cho việc ký sinh trên cơ thể côn trùng. Quá trình xâm nhập của nấm bắt đầu từ việc bào tử bám dính trên bề mặt côn trùng, sau đó phát triển sợi nấm và tiết ra enzyme phân hủy lớp vỏ ngoài. Khi côn trùng bị nhiễm nấm, chúng sẽ chết dần do sự phát triển của nấm bên trong cơ thể. *Isaria javanica* còn có khả năng sinh sản nhanh, tạo ra lượng lớn bào tử để lây lan sang các cá thể khác, giúp kiểm soát quần thể côn trùng gây hại một cách tự nhiên và bền vững.

With increasing reliance on the outcomes of black-box models in critical applications, post-hoc explainability tools that do not require access to the model internals are often used to enable humans understand and trust these models. In particular, we focus on the class of methods that can reveal the influence of input features on the predicted outputs. Despite their wide-spread adoption, existing methods are known to suffer from one or more of the following challenges: computational complexities, large uncertainties and most importantly, inability to handle real-world domain shifts. In this paper, we propose PRoFILE, a novel feature importance estimation method that addresses all these challenges. Through the use of a loss estimator jointly trained with the predictive model and a causal objective, PRoFILE can accurately estimate the feature importance scores even under complex distribution shifts, without any additional re-training. To this end, we also develop learning strategies for training the loss estimator, namely contrastive and dropout calibration, and find that it can effectively detect distribution shifts. Using empirical studies on several benchmark image and non-image data, we show significant improvements over state-of-the-art approaches, both in terms of fidelity and robustness.

Object detection is a critical task in computer vision, with applications ranging from autonomous driving to surveillance systems. This paper introduces YOLOv4, a state-of-the-art object detection framework designed to achieve optimal balance between speed and accuracy. Building upon the success of its predecessors, YOLOv4 incorporates advanced techniques such as Cross-Stage Partial connections (CSP), Mish activation, and a modified spatial pyramid pooling (SPP) module to enhance feature extraction and model efficiency. Additionally, the framework leverages Bag of Freebies (BoF) and Bag of Specials (BoS) strategies to improve training stability and detection performance without significantly increasing computational cost. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv4 outperforms existing object detection models in terms of both inference speed and accuracy on benchmark datasets such as COCO and PASCAL VOC. Specifically, YOLOv4 achieves a 10% improvement in average precision (AP) while maintaining real-time processing capabilities. The model's efficiency makes it suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, further broadening its applicability. The contributions of this work include a comprehensive analysis of modern object detection techniques, the integration of novel architectural improvements, and the establishment of a new benchmark for real-time object detection. YOLOv4 represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a robust solution for applications requiring high-speed and high-accuracy detection. **Keywords**: YOLOv4, object detection, real-time processing, computer vision, deep learning, CSP, Mish activation, SPP.

This paper addresses the challenge of deep model compression by exploring the correlations between filters in convolutional neural networks. Our objective is to develop an efficient method for reducing the computational complexity and memory requirements of deep models while preserving their accuracy. We propose a novel approach that leverages filter correlations to identify and merge redundant filters, resulting in a significant reduction in model size. Our method utilizes a correlation analysis technique to identify highly correlated filters and a merging strategy to combine them into a single, more efficient filter. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves a substantial reduction in model size and computational cost, with minimal loss in accuracy. Our findings have important implications for the deployment of deep models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and embedded systems. The key contributions of this research include a novel filter correlation analysis technique, an efficient filter merging strategy, and a significant reduction in model size and computational cost. Our approach has the potential to enable the widespread adoption of deep models in a variety of applications, including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. Keywords: deep model compression, filter correlations, convolutional neural networks, efficient neural networks, model pruning.

This paper introduces BRP-NAS, a novel prediction-based Neural Architecture Search (NAS) framework that leverages Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to efficiently explore the vast architecture space. The objective is to develop a method that can accurately predict the performance of neural architectures without requiring extensive training, thereby reducing the computational cost associated with traditional NAS methods. BRP-NAS employs a GCN-based encoder to learn compact representations of neural architectures, which are then used to predict their performance on a given task. The results show that BRP-NAS achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, outperforming existing NAS methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The key findings highlight the effectiveness of GCNs in capturing the structural properties of neural architectures and the importance of prediction-based approaches in NAS. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and effective NAS methods, with potential applications in automated machine learning, computer vision, and natural language processing. Key keywords: Neural Architecture Search, Graph Convolutional Networks, Prediction-based NAS, Automated Machine Learning.

This paper introduces a novel representation learning framework, Adversarially-Contrastive Optimal Transport (ACOT), designed to learn robust and discriminative feature representations. ACOT leverages optimal transport (OT) to align feature distributions across different views of the same data while simultaneously employing an adversarial objective to enforce feature invariance and robustness. Specifically, the framework minimizes the OT cost between representations of original data and adversarially perturbed versions, encouraging the model to learn features insensitive to noise. Contrastive learning is integrated to further enhance the discriminative power of the learned representations by attracting similar instances and repelling dissimilar ones. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ACOT on several benchmark datasets, including image classification and domain adaptation tasks. Experimental results show that ACOT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art representation learning methods, achieving significant improvements in classification accuracy and robustness. The learned representations exhibit superior generalization capabilities, making ACOT a promising approach for various downstream tasks. Key words: Representation Learning, Optimal Transport, Adversarial Learning, Contrastive Learning, Feature Invariance.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently learning on graph-structured data, which is pivotal in various domains such as social networks, biological networks, and recommendation systems. We aim to evaluate and enhance the performance of graph convolutional networks (GCNs) by proposing a novel architecture that balances simplicity and depth. Methods/Approach: We introduce a new framework for graph convolutional networks that optimizes layer configuration to capture both local and global structural features. Our approach involves the integration of lightweight convolutional operations with deeper network architectures, enabling more comprehensive information propagation through the graph. We implement a modified training procedure to ensure stability and efficiency in deeper networks. Results/Findings: Our proposed Simple and Deep Graph Convolutional Networks (SD-GCNs) demonstrate superior performance in node classification, link prediction, and clustering tasks on several benchmark datasets. We compare our model against state-of-the-art models, including traditional GCNs, showcasing improved accuracy and scalability. The experiments show that SD-GCNs can learn effectively from graph data with fewer parameters while maintaining robustness against overfitting. Conclusion/Implications: The research presents a significant advancement in graph neural network architectures by combining simplicity with depth to achieve enhanced learning capabilities. This work contributes to the broader field of graph-based machine learning, offering a practical solution for efficiently processing complex graph data. The proposed model has potential applications in fields requiring graph analysis, such as fraud detection, drug discovery, and effective network design. Keywords: Graph Convolutional Networks, Deep Learning, Network Architecture, Node Classification, Link Prediction, Graph Data, Efficiency, Scalability.

The analysis of satellite imagery will prove a crucial tool in the pursuit of sustainable development. While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have made large gains in natural image analysis, their application to multi-spectral satellite images (wherein input images have a large number of channels) remains relatively unexplored. In this paper, we compare different methods of leveraging multi-band information with CNNs, demonstrating the performance of all compared methods on the task of semantic segmentation of agricultural vegetation (vineyards). We show that standard industry practice of using bands selected by a domain expert leads to a significantly worse test accuracy than the other methods compared. Specifically, we compare: using bands specified by an expert; using all available bands; learning attention maps over the input bands; and leveraging Bayesian optimisation to dictate band choice. We show that simply using all available band information already increases test time performance, and show that the Bayesian optimisation, first applied to band selection in this work, can be used to further boost accuracy.

This paper investigates the challenges in semi-supervised learning, specifically focusing on improving model performance with minimal labeled data through a novel technique called Pseudo-Representation Labeling (PRL). Current semi-supervised models often struggle with the effective utilization of unlabeled data, impacting their generalization capabilities. Methods/Approach: We propose the PRL framework, which enhances conventional semi-supervised learning paradigms by leveraging pseudo-labeling techniques combined with a unique representation learning strategy. The approach involves generating pseudo-labels for the vast amount of unlabeled data while simultaneously refining feature representations to ensure accurate classification. Our methodology incorporates a dual-network architecture and employs a consistency-based loss function to optimize both labeling accuracy and feature extraction. Results/Findings: Empirical evaluations on benchmark datasets reveal that our PRL approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning models in terms of accuracy and robustness. Particularly, PRL demonstrates superior performance on challenging tasks with limited labeled data, providing a consistent improvement in classification accuracy, while efficiently managing computational resources. Comparative analysis shows marked advancements over traditional pseudo-labeling methods, confirming the enhanced efficacy of our proposed strategy. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Pseudo-Representation Labeling marks a substantial contribution to the field of semi-supervised learning, enabling efficient learning from unlabeled data with improved accuracy. This work not only augments existing semi-supervised methodologies but also lays the groundwork for future research in adaptive learning models. The implications of our findings suggest broad applicability across various domains, such as natural language processing and computer vision, where labeled data is often scarce. Key Keywords: semi-supervised learning, pseudo-labeling, representation learning, machine learning, accuracy, unlabeled data.

Source coding plays the role of changing the message source to a code that is suitable for transmitting through the channel. For example, ASCII code is a source coding standard converting each character to a byte of 8 bits is an example of source coding. Another way to think about source coding is to treat it as a compress-decompress process. At the transmitter, the source encoder compresses the message for the purpose of economizing on the length of the transmission. At the other end, the source decoder decompresses the received signal or sequence.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing probabilistic modeling capabilities through the development of a novel framework named Variational Mixture of Normalizing Flows (VMoNF). The objective is to improve the flexibility and expressiveness of density approximations in complex data distributions. Methods/Approach: We propose a hybrid model that integrates variational inference with normalizing flows, leveraging the strengths of both techniques. The mixture model dynamically combines multiple flow transformations, enabling a richer representation of data complexity. This approach utilizes a successful coupling of normalizing flows to variational distributions, ensuring both tractability and expressiveness. The model is trained using stochastic variational inference to optimize the evidence lower bound (ELBO), facilitating efficient learning and performance evaluation. Results/Findings: Our experimental results demonstrate that VMoNF significantly outperforms traditional variational methods and other flow-based models in terms of log-likelihood on benchmark datasets. The proposed framework effectively captures multimodality and complex dependencies in data distributions, exhibiting superior adaptability to intricate data patterns compared to existing methods. Conclusion/Implications: The Variational Mixture of Normalizing Flows presents a compelling advancement in probabilistic modeling, offering enhanced flexibility and precision in density estimation tasks. Its application potential spans various domains such as anomaly detection, image generation, and financial modeling, paving the way for more robust and adaptable machine learning systems. Future research may explore scalability to larger datasets and integration with other AI technologies to further extend its applicability. Keywords: normalizing flows, variational inference, density estimation, probabilistic modeling, multimodality.
