This paper addresses the challenge of performing transductive inference in higher-order Markov Random Fields (MRFs), which are prevalent in capturing complex dependencies in structured data. We aim to develop an efficient inference framework that can handle the intricate discrete-continuous optimization problems inherent in such models. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel Discrete-Continuous Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) framework tailored for higher-order MRFs. This approach leverages the strengths of ADMM in decomposing complex optimization problems, enabling effective coordination between discrete and continuous variables. The proposed method systematically alternates between discrete label assignment and continuous parameter adjustment while observing the constraints imposed by the MRF structure. Results/Findings: Our framework was evaluated on various benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The proposed method effectively balances the trade-off between convergence speed and optimality, showcasing robust transductive inference capabilities across different higher-order MRF configurations. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Discrete-Continuous ADMM represents a significant advancement in the field of structured prediction, offering a versatile and scalable solution for high-dimensional MRFs. This framework not only enhances the accuracy of transductive inference in complex graphical models but also opens avenues for its application in numerous domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and network analysis. Our work lays the groundwork for future research in optimizing structured prediction tasks, and we anticipate its broad applicability in advanced computational settings. Keywords: transductive inference, higher-order Markov Random Fields, discrete-continuous optimization, ADMM, structured prediction.

Hà Nội đang triển khai nhiều giải pháp nhằm thúc đẩy phát triển chăn nuôi bò thịt tại các vùng chăn nuôi tập trung trên địa bàn thành phố. Các chính sách hỗ trợ về vốn, kỹ thuật và giống đang được áp dụng để nâng cao năng suất và chất lượng đàn bò. Thành phố cũng khuyến khích việc áp dụng công nghệ cao vào chăn nuôi, đồng thời mở rộng liên kết giữa nông dân và doanh nghiệp để tạo đầu ra ổn định cho sản phẩm. Đánh giá khả năng lên men của Saccharomyces cerevisiae HG1.3 và điều kiện bảo quản rượu vang trái là một nghiên cứu quan trọng trong lĩnh vực sản xuất rượu vang. Saccharomyces cerevisiae là một loại nấm men được sử dụng rộng rãi trong quá trình lên men rượu vang, và HG1.3 là một dòng nấm men được chọn lọc để có khả năng lên men tốt. Nghiên cứu này nhằm đánh giá khả năng lên men của Saccharomyces cerevisiae HG1.3 trong điều kiện khác nhau, bao gồm nhiệt độ, độ ẩm và thời gian lên men. Kết quả cho thấy rằng HG1.3 có khả năng lên men tốt trong điều kiện nhiệt độ từ 15-20 độ C và độ ẩm từ 60-80%. Ngoài ra, nghiên cứu này cũng đánh giá điều kiện bảo quản rượu vang trái để đảm bảo chất lượng và an toàn thực phẩm. Kết quả cho thấy rằng rượu vang trái được bảo quản trong điều kiện nhiệt độ từ 5-15 độ C và độ ẩm từ 50-70% có thể giữ được chất lượng và an toàn thực phẩm trong thời gian dài. Tổng kết, nghiên cứu này cung cấp thông tin quan trọng về khả năng lên men của Saccharomyces cerevisiae HG1.3 và điều kiện bảo quản rượu vang trái, giúp các nhà sản xuất rượu vang có thể điều chỉnh quy trình sản xuất và bảo quản để đảm bảo chất lượng và an toàn thực phẩm.

Anomaly detection in video sequences is a challenging task with applications in surveillance, traffic monitoring, and event recognition. This paper presents a new benchmark dataset, composed of diverse real-world scenarios, for evaluating video anomaly detection algorithms. We introduce a novel computational model leveraging a hybrid approach that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction with a recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture for temporal context analysis. The CNN component learns spatial representations from video frames, while the RNN captures the temporal dynamics and dependencies between these features. We evaluate our model, alongside several state-of-the-art anomaly detection techniques, on the proposed benchmark dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance in terms of both detection accuracy and robustness to variations in scene complexity and anomaly types. Furthermore, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of different methods, offering insights into the challenges and future directions for video anomaly detection research. The benchmark dataset and our model provide valuable resources for advancing the field. Keywords: Anomaly Detection, Video Surveillance, Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, Benchmark Dataset.

Như vấn điề điã điược điặt ra, mục têu điược điặt ra ở bà toán này là gảm thểu tác động gây hạ của AGV lên mô trường và định tuyến AGV điến điểm giao hàng điúng khoảng thờ gan quy định. Semantic Scene Completion (SSC) refers to the task of inferring the 3D semantic segmentation of a scene while simultaneously completing the 3D shapes. We propose PALNet, a novel hybrid network for SSC based on single depth. PALNet utilizes a two-stream network to extract both 2D and 3D features from multi-stages using fine-grained depth information to efficiently captures the context, as well as the geometric cues of the scene. Current methods for SSC treat all parts of the scene equally causing unnecessary attention to the interior of objects. To address this problem, we propose Position Aware Loss(PA-Loss) which is position importance aware while training the network. Specifically, PA-Loss considers Local Geometric Anisotropy to determine the importance of different positions within the scene. It is beneficial for recovering key details like the boundaries of objects and the corners of the scene. Comprehensive experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and its superior performance. Models and Video demo can be found at: https://github.com/UniLauX/PALNet.

This paper proposes an innovative approach to compressing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) through online multi-granularity distillation. The objective is to reduce the computational complexity and memory requirements of GANs while preserving their generative capabilities. Our method employs a novel distillation framework that transfers knowledge from a pre-trained teacher GAN to a smaller student GAN at multiple granularities, including feature maps, intermediate representations, and output distributions. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves significant compression ratios while maintaining comparable image quality and diversity. The proposed technique outperforms existing GAN compression methods, with improvements in both visual fidelity and mode coverage. This research contributes to the development of efficient and scalable GANs, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments and applications such as image synthesis, data augmentation, and style transfer. Key keywords: GAN compression, knowledge distillation, multi-granularity distillation, generative models, deep learning.

Phim nước mắt là hiện tượng phổ biến ở bệnh nhân sau phẫu thuật Phaco, một thủ thuật phẫu thuật mắt để loại bỏ đục thủy tinh thể. Tuy nhiên, sự mất ổn định của phim nước mắt có thể ảnh hưởng đến kết quả phẫu thuật và chất lượng cuộc sống của bệnh nhân. Khảo sát gần đây cho thấy rằng, sự mất ổn định của phim nước mắt ở bệnh nhân sau phẫu thuật Phaco có thể do nhiều nguyên nhân khác nhau, bao gồm sự thay đổi áp lực nội nhãn, sự thay đổi cấu trúc giác mạc, và sự ảnh hưởng của các yếu tố môi trường. Kết quả khảo sát cũng cho thấy rằng, sự mất ổn định của phim nước mắt có thể dẫn đến các vấn đề như đau mắt, mờ mắt, và tăng áp lực nội nhãn. Vì vậy, việc theo dõi và điều trị sự mất ổn định của phim nước mắt là rất quan trọng để đảm bảo kết quả phẫu thuật tốt và chất lượng cuộc sống của bệnh nhân.

Phân tích thực trạng cho thấy nhiều bệnh viện đã triển khai các chương trình giám sát và quản lý sử dụng thuốc, tuy nhiên vẫn còn tồn tại một số hạn chế như thiếu nhân lực chuyên trách, cơ sở hạ tầng chưa đáp ứng yêu cầu và sự phối hợp giữa các khoa phòng chưa chặt chẽ. Việc đào tạo nhân viên y tế về cảnh giác dược cũng cần được tăng cường để nâng cao nhận thức và kỹ năng trong việc phát hiện và xử lý các phản ứng có hại do thuốc. Để cải thiện tình hình, cần có sự đầu tư mạnh mẽ từ các cấp quản lý y tế, cũng như sự tham gia tích cực của toàn bộ nhân viên y tế trong việc xây dựng một môi trường an toàn và hiệu quả cho người bệnh.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated remarkable success in generating high-quality synthetic data. However, traditional GAN training often requires centralized access to large datasets, raising privacy concerns. This paper introduces Brainstorming Generative Adversarial Networks (BGANs), a novel multi-agent generative modeling framework designed for distributed private datasets. BGANs leverage a collaborative brainstorming approach, where multiple GAN agents, each trained on a private dataset, exchange knowledge through a secure communication channel without revealing their underlying data. We propose a unique knowledge distillation mechanism based on shared latent spaces and adversarial learning to facilitate effective collaboration. Our experimental results on benchmark image datasets demonstrate that BGANs achieve comparable generation quality to centrally trained GANs while preserving data privacy. Furthermore, BGANs exhibit improved robustness against data heterogeneity and adversarial attacks compared to existing federated learning-based GAN approaches. The proposed framework opens new avenues for privacy-preserving generative modeling in various domains, including healthcare and finance. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, Federated Learning, Distributed Learning, Data Privacy, Multi-Agent Systems, Knowledge Distillation.

This paper proposes a novel Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methodology for Bayesian regression tree models, leveraging continuous-time birth-death processes to efficiently explore the model space. The objective is to improve the accuracy and scalability of Bayesian regression tree inference by developing a more flexible and adaptive MCMC algorithm. Our approach utilizes a continuous-time framework to model the birth and death of tree nodes, allowing for more efficient exploration of the model space and improved convergence properties. The results demonstrate significant improvements in computational efficiency and accuracy compared to existing MCMC methods for Bayesian regression trees. The proposed methodology has important implications for Bayesian nonparametric modeling and provides a powerful tool for regression analysis in complex data settings. Key contributions include the development of a continuous-time birth-death MCMC algorithm, improved model exploration and convergence, and enhanced computational efficiency. Relevant keywords: Bayesian regression trees, MCMC, continuous-time birth-death processes, Bayesian nonparametrics, adaptive MCMC algorithms.

Gesture recognition is a critical challenge in human-computer interaction, with applications ranging from virtual reality to assistive technologies. This paper addresses the limitations of existing methods in handling multi-rate and multi-modal temporal data, which are essential for accurate and robust gesture recognition. We propose a novel framework, the Multi-Rate and Multi-Modal Temporal Enhanced Network (MRMTEN), designed to effectively process and fuse temporal information from diverse data sources, such as video, motion sensors, and depth maps. Our approach leverages a hierarchical architecture that integrates multi-rate temporal modeling with attention mechanisms to capture both short-term and long-term dependencies across modalities. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that MRMTEN outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior recognition accuracy and robustness to temporal variations. The proposed framework also exhibits significant improvements in computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications. This research contributes to advancing gesture recognition by introducing a scalable and adaptable solution for multi-modal temporal data, with potential applications in healthcare, gaming, and robotics. **Keywords**: gesture recognition, multi-modal fusion, temporal modeling, attention mechanisms, human-computer interaction, real-time systems.

This paper addresses the challenge of unsupervised ensemble classification in scenarios involving sequential and networked data, where labeled training data is unavailable. Traditional classification methods often rely on supervised learning, which limits their applicability in domains where annotations are costly or impractical. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel unsupervised ensemble framework that leverages the inherent structures of sequential and networked data to improve classification accuracy. Our approach integrates multiple unsupervised models, each tailored to capture distinct patterns in the data, such as temporal dependencies in sequences or relational dependencies in networks. The ensemble mechanism combines these models using an adaptive weighting scheme, ensuring robust performance across diverse datasets. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing unsupervised techniques, achieving significant improvements in classification accuracy and stability. Furthermore, the framework is computationally efficient and scalable, making it suitable for large-scale applications. The proposed approach contributes to advancing unsupervised learning in complex data environments and has potential applications in areas such as anomaly detection, social network analysis, and time-series forecasting. **Keywords**: unsupervised learning, ensemble classification, sequential data, networked data, adaptive weighting, anomaly detection.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving semantic understanding in video analysis using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Traditional CNNs often struggle to capture the temporal dynamics and spatial transformations inherent in video data, limiting their effectiveness in tasks such as action recognition and scene understanding. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel approach called *Representation Warping*, which dynamically aligns and warps feature representations across frames to better model temporal dependencies and spatial variations. Our method leverages optical flow and attention mechanisms to adaptively refine feature maps, ensuring robust and context-aware representations. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including UCF101 and HMDB51, demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods by significant margins. The proposed framework not only enhances semantic video understanding but also provides a scalable solution for real-world applications such as surveillance, autonomous driving, and video summarization. This work contributes to advancing video analysis by introducing a computationally efficient and interpretable model that bridges the gap between spatial and temporal feature learning. **Keywords**: Video understanding, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Representation Warping, Temporal modeling, Optical flow, Action recognition.

This paper proposes a novel approach to growing interpretable part graphs on Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets) using multi-shot learning. The objective is to enhance the explainability and transparency of deep learning models by identifying and visualizing meaningful parts and their relationships. Our method leverages multi-shot learning to efficiently learn part graphs from a few examples, enabling the model to generalize and adapt to new, unseen data. We employ a graph-based approach to represent and grow the part graphs, allowing for the discovery of complex relationships between objects and their parts. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving model interpretability and performance on various computer vision tasks. The key findings include the ability to identify semantically meaningful parts, improve model robustness, and provide insights into the decision-making process of ConvNets. Our research contributes to the development of more transparent and trustworthy AI models, with potential applications in areas such as computer vision, robotics, and healthcare. Key keywords: interpretable AI, ConvNets, multi-shot learning, graph-based models, explainable deep learning.

The growing complexity of network systems calls for innovative solutions to effectively detect anomalies. This paper introduces GEE, a Gradient-based Explainable Variational Autoencoder, designed to enhance network anomaly detection by providing both high accuracy and interpretability. Methods/Approach: GEE leverages the capabilities of variational autoencoders (VAEs) to model network traffic behavior while integrating a gradient-based approach to facilitate explainability. The GEE model applies a novel gradient attribution method to highlight input features contributing to detected anomalies, thus offering insight into the decision-making process. This combination aims to balance the trade-off between performance and interpretability, often found in traditional anomaly detection models. Results/Findings: Extensive experiments on benchmark network datasets demonstrate that GEE outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of anomaly detection accuracy, achieving a superior balance between precision and recall metrics. Additionally, the explainability component was validated through user studies, confirming the model's ability to provide intuitive and relevant feature attributions for detected anomalies. Comparative analyses further illustrate GEE's robustness and efficiency in processing network traffic data. Conclusion/Implications: The development of GEE marks a significant advancement in the realm of anomaly detection systems by merging explainability with high-performance detection capabilities. This research contributes to the growing field of interpretable machine learning and offers potential applications in network security monitoring, real-time intrusion detection, and compliance auditing. Future work will explore the scalability of GEE to accommodate the increasing volume and diversity of network data, paving the way for more resilient and trustworthy AI-driven network management solutions. Keywords: Anomaly Detection, Explainable AI, Variational Autoencoder, Network Security, Gradient Attribution, Interpretable Machine Learning.

This research explores the development of an automated system for species recognition in mammals using artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on data collected from camera traps situated in a European temperate forest. The primary goal is to improve the efficiency and accuracy of wildlife monitoring and biodiversity assessment. Methods: The study employs a deep learning approach, utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on a comprehensive dataset of images captured by camera traps. The model is designed to identify and classify various mammal species present in the forest environment. Preprocessing techniques, such as image enhancement and data augmentation, are applied to optimize the performance of the AI system. Results: The AI model achieved substantial accuracy in recognizing and differentiating between multiple mammal species. Performance metrics indicate a high precision and recall rate, demonstrating the system's ability to process large volumes of image data efficiently. Comparisons with existing manual identification methods show a significant improvement in speed and consistency. Conclusion: The study provides a foundational step towards the integration of AI in ecological and wildlife research, offering a scalable and effective tool for automated species identification. This approach not only enhances monitoring practices but also contributes valuable data for conservation efforts. Future work includes expanding the model's capabilities to cover additional species and geographical regions, as well as integrating it with real-time data analysis systems. Keywords: Automated Species Recognition, Camera Traps, Mammals, AI, Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, European Temperate Forest, Wildlife Monitoring, Biodiversity Assessment.

Frame interpolation is a critical task in video processing, aiming to generate intermediate frames between existing ones to enhance video quality and smoothness. However, evaluating the performance of frame interpolation methods remains challenging due to the lack of robust benchmarks that account for subjective visual quality. This paper introduces a novel approach to subjective annotation for frame interpolation benchmarks by leveraging artefact amplification. The proposed method systematically amplifies interpolation artefacts, such as blurring, ghosting, and distortion, to make subtle imperfections more perceptible to human annotators. A diverse dataset of video sequences is used, and a crowd-sourced annotation framework is implemented to collect subjective quality ratings. The results demonstrate that artefact amplification significantly improves the consistency and reliability of subjective evaluations compared to traditional methods. Furthermore, the benchmark enables a more nuanced comparison of state-of-the-art frame interpolation algorithms, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses in handling specific artefact types. This work contributes a valuable tool for the research community, offering a more accurate and human-centric evaluation framework for frame interpolation technologies. The implications extend to applications in video compression, streaming, and computer vision, where high-quality frame interpolation is essential. **Keywords**: frame interpolation, subjective annotation, artefact amplification, video quality assessment, benchmark evaluation.

Vi khuẩn hiếm khí là một nhóm vi khuẩn không thể sống trong điều kiện oxy hóa cao. Chúng được phân lập từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau, bao gồm đất, nước và các môi trường tự nhiên khác. Dưới đây là một số thành phần, số lượng và tính mẫn cảm với kháng sinh của một số vi khuẩn hiếm khí được phân lập: - Clostridium difficile: Đây là một loại vi khuẩn hiếm khí gây bệnh thường gặp ở người. Chúng có thể sống trong ruột và gây ra các triệu chứng như tiêu chảy, nôn mửa và đau bụng. C. difficile cũng có thể gây ra các biến chứng nghiêm trọng như viêm đại tràng và suy thận. - Clostridium perfringens: Đây là một loại vi khuẩn hiếm khí gây bệnh thường gặp ở người và động vật. Chúng có thể gây ra các triệu chứng như đau bụng, tiêu chảy và nôn mửa. C. perfringens cũng có thể gây ra các biến chứng nghiêm trọng như viêm đại tràng và suy thận. - Clostridium tetani: Đây là một loại vi khuẩn hiếm khí gây bệnh thường gặp ở người. Chúng có thể gây ra các triệu chứng như co giật, rung cơ và khó thở. C. tetani cũng có thể gây ra các biến chứng nghiêm trọng như tử vong. - Clostridium botulinum: Đây là một loại vi khuẩn hiếm khí gây bệnh thường gặp ở người. Chúng có thể gây ra các triệu chứng như co giật, rung cơ và khó thở. C. botulinum cũng có thể gây ra các biến chứng nghiêm trọng như tử vong. Các loại kháng sinh thường được sử dụng để điều trị các bệnh do vi khuẩn hiếm khí gây ra bao gồm metronidazol, vancomycin và clindamycin. Tuy nhiên, sự kháng kháng sinh của vi khuẩn hiếm khí đang trở nên ngày càng nghiêm trọng, làm cho việc điều trị trở nên khó khăn hơn.

This paper introduces an autonomous air traffic control (ATC) system using deep multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). The primary objective is to develop an AI-driven ATC capable of optimizing flight safety and efficiency in complex, dynamic airspace environments. We propose a novel MARL framework wherein each aircraft is controlled by an independent agent, collectively trained to minimize delays, prevent conflicts, and maintain optimal flight paths. Our approach incorporates a customized reward function that balances safety constraints with operational efficiency metrics. Experimental results, obtained through simulations of high-density air traffic scenarios, demonstrate that the proposed MARL-based ATC significantly outperforms traditional rule-based systems, achieving a 15% reduction in flight delays and a 20% decrease in potential conflict situations. The findings suggest that deep MARL offers a promising pathway towards enhancing the autonomy and scalability of future ATC systems, paving the way for safer and more efficient air travel. **Keywords:** Air Traffic Control, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, Deep Learning, Autonomous Systems, Conflict Resolution, Flight Optimization.

Số liệu dự báo của hệ thống CPS3 với hạn dự báo 6 tháng bao gồm các yếu tố về nhiệt độ lượng mưa, độ cao địa thế vị các mực. Số liệu của CPS3 bao gồm 2 dạng: Dạng 1 chạy dự báo nghiệp vụ hàng ngày và dạng 2 là số liệu tái phân tích từ năm 1990-2020. Trong khuôn khổ bài báo này, các tác giả sử dụng số liệu tái phân tích của mô hình CPS3 từ năm 1991-2020 để đánh giá dự báo nhiệt độ và lượng mưa hạn mùa cho 60 trạm trên toàn lãnh thổ Việt Nam. Kết quả cho thấy với yếu tố nhiệt độ, thời điểm dự báo tháng 3 cho kết quả dự báo tốt nhất, khu vực Nam Trung Bộ và Nam Bộ là những nơi có kỹ năng dự báo cao nhất so với các khu vực còn lại. Video inpainting aims to reconstruct missing regions in video frames by leveraging spatial and temporal information. This paper introduces a novel Progressive Temporal Feature Alignment Network (PTFAN) to address the challenges of handling large missing regions and complex motion. Our approach employs a progressive framework, starting with coarse-level feature completion and iteratively refining the results. Specifically, we propose a Temporal Feature Alignment module that explicitly aligns features across adjacent frames, effectively propagating information from known regions to the missing areas. This alignment is achieved through a deformable convolution-based mechanism, enabling robust handling of non-rigid motions. Furthermore, we introduce a feature refinement network that progressively enhances the inpainted regions, leading to improved visual quality and temporal consistency. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our PTFAN significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art video inpainting methods, achieving superior performance in terms of both quantitative metrics and qualitative visual results. The proposed method exhibits robustness to complex scenes and large missing regions, demonstrating its potential for various video editing and restoration applications. Keywords: Video Inpainting, Temporal Feature Alignment, Deep Learning, Video Completion, Deformable Convolution.

The objective of this research is to enhance large-scale place recognition by developing a robust deep learning model capable of effective point cloud retrieval from 3D data. We introduce PointNetVLAD, a novel architecture that combines the strengths of the PointNet deep learning framework with a VLAD (Vector of Locally Aggregated Descriptors) layer to process point clouds for place recognition. Our approach leverages the spatial features of 3D point clouds, enabling the system to generate comprehensive and distinctive global descriptors for various environments. PointNetVLAD significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of retrieval precision and recall, exhibiting superior performance even in challenging situations such as varying viewpoints and environments. We conducted experiments on a large-scale outdoor dataset, demonstrating that our method achieves high accuracy and robustness compared to traditional handcrafted techniques and other contemporary models. The findings underscore the efficacy of PointNetVLAD in diverse settings, suggesting potential applications in autonomous navigation, augmented reality, and urban reconstruction. This study addresses the challenge of accurately estimating human pose in images, a complex task due to variations in human appearance, occlusions, and ambiguous joint positions. The aim is to enhance pose estimation performance by integrating a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a graphical model in a joint training framework. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel architecture that combines the strengths of CNNs and graphical models for human pose estimation. The CNN is designed for effective feature extraction and provides initial pose predictions. Simultaneously, a graphical model is employed to model spatial dependencies between human joints. These components are jointly trained using a principled learning framework, allowing them to complement each other's strengths and reduce errors inherent to each isolated method. Results/Findings: The joint training approach demonstrates significant improvements in pose estimation accuracy on standard benchmark datasets compared to traditional methods. Our model outperforms standalone CNN-based approaches and graphical models, achieving higher precision and recall rates. The integrated framework effectively handles occlusions and complex poses, demonstrating robustness across diverse scenarios. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel joint training methodology that leverages the complementary capabilities of CNNs and graphical models, setting a new standard for human pose estimation tasks. The proposed system not only enhances accuracy but also provides a robust tool for applications in areas such as human-computer interaction, augmented reality, and surveillance systems. Future work could explore extending this framework to three-dimensional pose estimation and other related visual recognition tasks. Keywords: human pose estimation, convolutional neural network, graphical model, joint training, feature extraction, spatial dependencies.

Graph similarity computation is a fundamental problem in various domains, including social network analysis, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems. However, existing methods struggle to scale efficiently for large graphs while maintaining accuracy. This paper introduces **CoSimGNN**, a novel graph neural network (GNN)-based framework designed for large-scale graph similarity computation. The proposed approach leverages a combination of graph coarsening and hierarchical embedding techniques to reduce computational complexity without sacrificing performance. CoSimGNN employs a multi-level graph representation, where coarse-grained embeddings are progressively refined to capture both local and global structural features. We evaluate the framework on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its ability to outperform state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and scalability. Experimental results show that CoSimGNN achieves up to a 30% improvement in similarity computation accuracy while reducing runtime by 40% compared to existing approaches. The framework's efficiency makes it particularly suitable for real-world applications involving massive graphs. This research contributes a scalable and effective solution to graph similarity computation, paving the way for broader adoption in large-scale graph analytics. **Keywords**: Graph similarity computation, graph neural networks (GNNs), large-scale graphs, graph coarsening, hierarchical embedding, scalability.

Multi-view clustering, which leverages diverse data representations to improve clustering performance, is a critical challenge in data analysis. This paper addresses the problem of inconsistent graph embeddings across multiple views, which often leads to suboptimal clustering results. We propose a novel framework, Consistent Multiple Graph Embedding (CMGE), designed to unify graph embeddings from different views while preserving their intrinsic structures. Our approach integrates a shared embedding space with view-specific constraints, ensuring consistency across views without sacrificing their unique characteristics. The framework employs an iterative optimization algorithm to jointly learn the embeddings and clustering assignments, enhancing both accuracy and robustness. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CMGE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of clustering accuracy and stability. The proposed method also exhibits superior scalability and adaptability to varying data complexities. This work contributes a significant advancement in multi-view clustering by providing a unified, consistent embedding framework with broad applicability in areas such as social network analysis, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems. Keywords: multi-view clustering, graph embedding, consistency, optimization, data integration.

This paper explores the concept of Guided Observability in Reinforcement Learning (RL), aiming to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of RL algorithms in complex environments. The objective is to enhance the learning process by providing guided observations that focus the agent's attention on relevant aspects of the environment. Our approach utilizes a novel framework that integrates domain knowledge into the RL model, allowing for more informed decision-making. The method involves a hybrid architecture that combines traditional RL techniques with guided observability mechanisms, enabling the agent to learn from both trial-and-error experiences and targeted observations. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in learning speed and convergence rates compared to traditional RL methods. The findings suggest that Guided Observability can be a valuable tool for RL applications, particularly in situations where exploration is costly or time-consuming. Key contributions of this research include the introduction of a guided observability framework, the development of a hybrid RL architecture, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in various environments. Relevant keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Guided Observability, Hybrid Architecture, Domain Knowledge, Efficient Exploration.

Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) aims to distinguish between genuine and spoof faces, a critical task for secure face recognition systems. Current FAS methods often struggle with generalization across diverse spoofing attacks and unseen domains. This paper introduces a novel physics-guided spoof trace disentanglement framework that leverages intrinsic physical properties to enhance FAS robustness. Our approach decomposes observed facial images into albedo, shading, and spoof trace components. By explicitly modeling the underlying physics of light reflection and incorporating priors on realistic facial albedo and shading, we disentangle subtle spoofing artifacts from genuine facial features. A dedicated spoof trace module is then trained to identify these disentangled artifacts. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance and generalization ability compared to state-of-the-art FAS techniques. Our approach shows significant improvements particularly in cross-dataset testing scenarios. Key innovations include the physics-based disentanglement module and its effectiveness in isolating subtle spoofing cues. Keywords: Face Anti-Spoofing, Spoof Trace Disentanglement, Physics-Guided, Albedo, Shading, Generalization.

This paper introduces a novel approach to option discovery in reinforcement learning by leveraging the deep successor representation (DSR). The primary objective is to autonomously identify reusable and temporally extended actions, or "eigenoptions," that accelerate learning and improve performance in complex environments. Our method employs a deep neural network to approximate the successor representation, enabling the efficient extraction of eigenoptions through an eigenvalue decomposition. These eigenoptions capture the principal components of the agent's state visitation patterns, effectively representing distinct behavioral strategies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in several benchmark reinforcement learning environments, including grid-world navigation and Atari games. Experimental results show that agents equipped with eigenoptions exhibit significantly faster learning rates and achieve higher asymptotic performance compared to agents using traditional exploration techniques or hand-engineered options. Moreover, the discovered eigenoptions demonstrate strong transferability to new tasks within the same environment. These findings suggest that DSR-based eigenoption discovery offers a promising avenue for developing more efficient and adaptable reinforcement learning agents. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Option Discovery, Successor Representation, Deep Learning, Eigenoptions, Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning.

The stringent requirements of mobile edge computing (MEC) applications and functions fathom the high capacity and dense deployment of MEC hosts to the upcoming wireless networks. However, operating such high capacity MEC hosts can significantly increase energy consumption. Thus, a base station (BS) unit can act as a self-powered BS. In this paper, an effective energy dispatch mechanism for self-powered wireless networks with edge computing capabilities is studied. First, a two-stage linear stochastic programming problem is formulated with the goal of minimizing the total energy consumption cost of the system while fulfilling the energy demand. Second, a semi-distributed data-driven solution is proposed by developing a novel multi-agent meta-reinforcement learning (MAMRL) framework to solve the formulated problem. In particular, each BS plays the role of a local agent that explores a Markovian behavior for both energy consumption and generation while each BS transfers time-varying features to a meta-agent. Sequentially, the meta-agent optimizes (i.e., exploits) the energy dispatch decision by accepting only the observations from each local agent with its own state information. Meanwhile, each BS agent estimates its own energy dispatch policy by applying the learned parameters from meta-agent. Finally, the proposed MAMRL framework is benchmarked by analyzing deterministic, asymmetric, and stochastic environments in terms of non-renewable energy usages, energy cost, and accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed MAMRL model can reduce up to 11% non-renewable energy usage and by 22.4% the energy cost (with 95.8% prediction accuracy), compared to other baseline methods.

Các nhà thầu có kinh nghiệm lâu năm trong lĩnh vực xây dựng công nghiệp cao tầng thường được đánh giá cao hơn bởi khả năng quản lý dự án hiệu quả và chất lượng công trình tốt. Ngoài ra, yếu tố giá thầu cũng là một yếu tố quan trọng ảnh hưởng đến khả năng trúng thầu. Nhà thầu có giá thầu cạnh tranh và hợp lý thường có cơ hội cao hơn để trúng thầu. Tuy nhiên, giá thầu không phải là yếu tố duy nhất quyết định khả năng trúng thầu, mà còn phụ thuộc vào các yếu tố khác như chất lượng công trình, thời gian hoàn thành dự án và khả năng đáp ứng yêu cầu của chủ đầu tư. Yếu tố khác ảnh hưởng đến khả năng trúng thầu bao gồm khả năng tài chính của nhà thầu, khả năng quản lý dự án và đội ngũ nhân viên có kinh nghiệm. Các nhà thầu có khả năng tài chính tốt và đội ngũ nhân viên có kinh nghiệm thường có khả năng trúng thầu cao hơn.

This paper investigates the robustness of Vision Transformers (ViTs) against adversarial examples, which are inputs designed to deceive image classification models. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have exhibited vulnerabilities to such attacks, and our research aims to determine whether ViTs, a recent development in computer vision, exhibit similar susceptibilities or offer enhanced resilience. Methods/Approach: We conducted extensive experimentation using a range of adversarial attack techniques on Vision Transformer models. These experiments included both black-box and white-box settings to comprehensively evaluate the defensive capabilities of ViTs. Comparative analysis was performed against prevalent CNN architectures to assess relative robustness. Results/Findings: Our findings reveal that Vision Transformers exhibit improved resistance to adversarial examples compared to CNNs, particularly in scenarios involving complex attacks. ViTs demonstrated a higher success rate in maintaining classification accuracy under attack, indicating a potential advantage in security-sensitive applications. Despite this, certain attack vectors were still effective, pointing out areas for further improvement. Conclusion/Implications: The study significantly contributes to understanding the defensive strengths of Vision Transformers and paves the way for developing even more secure AI models in the field of computer vision. Our insights suggest that ViTs could play a crucial role in applications requiring robust image classification, though ongoing research is necessary to bolster defenses against sophisticated adversarial threats. Keywords: Vision Transformers, adversarial examples, robustness, image classification, computer vision, deep learning, security.

One of the crucial challenges faced by FL algorithms is the presence of non Independently and Identically Distributed (non-IID) data across decentralized devices . In traditional machine learning scenarios, IID assumptions are often made, implying that the training data is drawn from the same distribution across all participating devices. However, in FL, this assumption is frequently violated as devices may have diverse data distributions based on factors such as geographic location, user behavior, or device characteristics. Non-IID data poses a significant hurdle to the effective collaboration of decentralized devices in FL. When the training data on each device exhibits different statistical properties, models trained locally may specialize in capturing patterns unique to the local data distribution.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning effective video representations by decomposing long- and short-view features through contrastive learning. The objective is to enhance the understanding of temporal dynamics in videos by distinguishing between global context (long-view) and fine-grained temporal details (short-view). We propose a novel framework that leverages contrastive learning to disentangle these features, enabling the model to capture both high-level semantics and low-level motion patterns. Our approach employs a dual-branch architecture, where one branch focuses on long-view features by aggregating temporal information over extended sequences, while the other emphasizes short-view features by analyzing localized temporal segments. A contrastive loss function is introduced to maximize the mutual information between these complementary views while minimizing redundancy. Experimental results on benchmark video datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in tasks such as action recognition and video retrieval. The proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance, highlighting its ability to effectively decompose and utilize temporal features. This research contributes to the field of video representation learning by providing a robust and interpretable model for capturing multi-scale temporal dynamics, with potential applications in video analysis, surveillance, and human-computer interaction. **Keywords**: video representation learning, contrastive learning, feature decomposition, temporal dynamics, action recognition, video retrieval.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown remarkable performance in various applications, but their scalability remains a challenge when dealing with large graphs. This paper addresses the problem of efficient GNN training on massive datasets by introducing a novel biased graph sampler designed to minimize regret. Our method leverages a theoretical framework based on multi-armed bandit techniques to dynamically adjust sampling probabilities, focusing on nodes and edges that contribute most significantly to the learning process. We propose a near-optimal regret bound for our sampling strategy, demonstrating its ability to balance exploration and exploitation during training. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets show that our biased sampler achieves comparable or superior accuracy to existing methods, while significantly reducing training time and memory consumption. Specifically, we observe a substantial improvement in convergence speed and a reduction in computational cost compared to uniform sampling and other state-of-the-art GNN sampling techniques. Our findings suggest that carefully designed biased sampling can significantly improve the scalability and efficiency of GNN training. Keywords: Graph Neural Networks, GNN, graph sampling, biased sampling, regret minimization, scalability, machine learning.

The research investigates an innovative approach to latent space manipulation in neural networks by introducing the concept of a Surrogate Gradient Field (SGF). This study addresses the challenge of effectively controlling and traversing the latent space to achieve desired outcomes in generative and model transformation tasks. Methods/Approach: We developed the Surrogate Gradient Field technique, which uses a novel gradient estimation method to guide latent space manipulation. This approach involves constructing a surrogate gradient that approximates the influence of changes in latent variables on the output, thereby facilitating more precise and controlled transformations. The technique was applied and tested within the context of variational autoencoders (VAEs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to demonstrate its versatility and effectiveness. Results/Findings: Our experiments revealed that the SGF method significantly enhanced the precision and flexibility of latent space navigation, compared to traditional techniques. Quantitative assessments showcased improved model performance in image generation tasks, highlighting increased control over attributes such as style and content. Furthermore, the SGF demonstrated superior capability in disentangling complex latent representations, offering a marked improvement in generating high-quality variations. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of the Surrogate Gradient Field offers a substantial advancement in latent space manipulation, providing a robust and versatile tool for various applications in AI model transformations and content generation. This research contributes a scalable method that can enhance the ability to harness latent spaces, with potential applications in image synthesis, data augmentation, and other generative tasks. Keywords: Surrogate Gradient Field, latent space manipulation, neural networks, generative models, variational autoencoders, GANs.

We explain how our approaches can be more suitable than some state-of-the-art autotuners for the tuning of any application in general and of expensive exascale applications in particular.

Reinforcement learning agents often face the challenge of reward perturbations and inconsistencies, which can lead to suboptimal policy performance. This research aims to address this problem by investigating the robustness of regularized policies against such reward instabilities. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach that incorporates regularization techniques into the policy optimization process to enhance robustness. This method integrates L1 and L2 regularization frameworks within policy gradient algorithms, balancing exploration and exploitation while minimizing sensitivity to varying reward signals. Additionally, a comparative analysis with traditional policy gradient methods without regularization is conducted to assess performance differences. Results/Findings: Our experiments, conducted across multiple simulated environments, demonstrate that regularized policies exhibit superior robustness to reward perturbations compared to their non-regularized counterparts. The proposed approach maintains stability and consistent performance, even with significant alterations in reward structures. Quantitative results highlight an improvement in policy resilience, evidenced by higher accumulated rewards and reduced variance across trials. Conclusion/Implications: The findings underscore the significance of incorporating regularization techniques into reinforcement learning agents to achieve robust behavior in dynamic environments. These insights have potent implications for real-world applications where stable and reliable policy performance is crucial, such as autonomous control systems and robotic operations. The study paves the way for future exploration into more advanced regularization strategies, further enhancing the adaptability and effectiveness of reinforcement learning frameworks. This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing disentangled text representation learning by integrating information-theoretic principles to guide the representation process. The goal is to achieve more interpretable and efficient text embeddings that capture distinct semantic aspects of textual data. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative framework that leverages information-theoretic measures to evaluate and optimize the disentanglement of text representations. The approach involves employing mutual information to quantify the redundancy and relevance of different features in the representation space. Additionally, we utilize a novel regularization technique to minimize information overlap and improve the distinctness of the learned embeddings. Results/Findings: Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the disentanglement of features in text representation, leading to better performance on various NLP tasks compared to existing models. Specifically, our approach shows enhanced results in text classification, sentiment analysis, and paraphrase identification, while maintaining computational efficiency. Comparisons with baseline models reveal superior interpretability and feature separation, underscoring the effectiveness of the information-theoretic guidance. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field by presenting a novel method that enhances the quality of disentangled text representations using information-theoretic insights. The findings highlight the potential of our approach to improve semantic understanding in NLP applications. Our work paves the way for further exploration of information-theoretic methods in representation learning, suggesting broader applications in AI and machine learning. Key keywords include disentangled representation, information theory, text embeddings, NLP, and mutual information.

This paper addresses the challenge of large-scale place recognition using 3D point clouds, a critical task for autonomous navigation and robotics. We introduce PointNetVLAD, a novel deep learning architecture that combines PointNet for efficient point cloud feature extraction with VLAD (Vector of Locally Aggregated Descriptors) for compact and discriminative global descriptor generation. Our approach directly processes raw 3D point clouds, eliminating the need for hand-crafted features or voxelization. PointNetVLAD is trained end-to-end to learn robust and viewpoint-invariant descriptors. We evaluate PointNetVLAD on several large-scale datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in retrieval accuracy and robustness compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, our method achieves superior performance in challenging environments with significant viewpoint changes and occlusions. The generated compact global descriptors enable efficient and scalable place recognition for large environments. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed architecture for point cloud based place recognition, offering a promising solution for robust localization in autonomous systems. **Keywords:** Place Recognition, Point Cloud, Deep Learning, PointNet, VLAD, Autonomous Navigation, Robotics.

We propose real-time, six degrees of freedom (6DoF), 3D face pose estimation without face detection or landmark localization. We observe that estimating the 6DoF rigid transformation of a face is a simpler problem than facial landmark detection, often used for 3D face alignment. In addition, 6DoF offers more information than face bounding box labels. We leverage these observations to make multiple contributions: (a) We describe an easily trained, efficient, Faster R-CNN--based model which regresses 6DoF pose for all faces in the photo, without preliminary face detection. (b) We explain how pose is converted and kept consistent between the input photo and arbitrary crops created while training and evaluating our model. (c) Finally, we show how face poses can replace detection bounding box training labels. Tests on AFLW2000-3D and BIWI show that our method runs at real-time and outperforms state of the art (SotA) face pose estimators. Remarkably, our method also surpasses SotA models of comparable complexity on the WIDER FACE detection benchmark, despite not been optimized on bounding box labels.

Automatic image captioning has achieved significant progress with deep learning models; however, generating accurate descriptions for images containing novel objects unseen during training remains challenging due to limited vocabulary coverage. This paper presents a new approach for captioning images featuring novel objects by leveraging online vocabulary expansion. The proposed method integrates an adaptive mechanism that dynamically incorporates external object names and concepts into the captioning model’s vocabulary as new visual categories are detected. By employing a modular architecture that combines convolutional neural networks for image feature extraction with a sequence generation model, our system dynamically updates its word embedding and decoding layers in real time, allowing inclusion of previously unseen objects in generated captions. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly improves captioning quality for novel object images compared to existing fixed-vocabulary models, as evidenced by higher scores on metrics such as BLEU, METEOR, and CIDEr. The results showcase both the flexibility and scalability of online vocabulary expansion, enabling robust adaptation to evolving visual environments. Our method advances the state-of-the-art in image captioning and holds promise for applications in autonomous agents, assistive technologies, and multimedia content analysis. Key keywords: image captioning, novel objects, online vocabulary expansion, deep learning, adaptive language modeling, computer vision.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) systems often struggle with out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization, where agents fail to perform effectively in environments that differ significantly from their training data. This paper addresses this critical challenge by proposing a novel representation learning framework designed to enhance OOD generalization in RL. Our approach leverages self-supervised learning techniques to extract robust and transferable features from high-dimensional input spaces, enabling agents to adapt to unseen environments more effectively. We introduce a multi-task training paradigm that encourages the learning of invariant representations, reducing sensitivity to distributional shifts. Experiments conducted on a suite of benchmark environments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing baselines in OOD scenarios, achieving up to a 30% improvement in performance metrics. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of the framework, highlighting its ability to disentangle task-relevant features from spurious correlations. The results underscore the potential of our approach to advance the deployment of RL systems in real-world applications, where environmental variability is a common challenge. This work contributes to the growing body of research on robust RL by offering a scalable and practical solution for improving generalization capabilities. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Out-Of-Distribution Generalization, Representation Learning, Self-Supervised Learning, Multi-Task Learning, Robust AI.

This paper addresses the challenge of forecasting high-dimensional dynamics, a problem that arises in various fields such as physics, biology, and finance. Our objective is to develop a novel approach that leverages suboptimal embeddings to improve predictive performance. We propose a methodology that combines dimensionality reduction techniques with advanced machine learning algorithms to identify and exploit low-dimensional patterns in high-dimensional data. Neural network compression is crucial for deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This paper introduces the Teacher-Class Network (TCN), a novel compression mechanism that leverages a teacher-student learning paradigm with a class-aware approach. Unlike traditional knowledge distillation methods, TCN organizes neurons into "classes" based on their activation patterns and trains a smaller student network to mimic the behavior of these classes in the teacher network. This approach promotes more efficient knowledge transfer and allows for greater compression rates. We evaluated TCN on several benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrating significant reductions in model size and computational cost compared to state-of-the-art compression techniques, while maintaining competitive accuracy. Specifically, our experiments show that TCN can achieve up to a 10x reduction in parameters with minimal performance degradation. The proposed TCN offers a practical solution for deploying complex neural networks on edge devices, making deep learning more accessible in resource-limited environments. Keywords: Neural Network Compression, Knowledge Distillation, Teacher-Student Learning, Model Optimization, Deep Learning.

Graph embedding techniques have become essential for analyzing complex networks in various domains, such as social networks, recommendation systems, and biological networks. However, existing methods often struggle with robustness, particularly when dealing with noisy or incomplete graph structures. This paper introduces RECS (Robust Graph Embedding Using Connection Subgraphs), a novel framework designed to enhance the robustness and accuracy of graph embeddings. RECS leverages connection subgraphs, which capture localized structural patterns, to generate embeddings that are resilient to noise and missing data. The proposed approach employs a combination of graph sampling and deep learning to learn node representations that preserve both global and local topological properties. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that RECS outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of embedding quality and robustness, achieving significant improvements in downstream tasks such as node classification and link prediction. The framework's ability to handle noisy and sparse graphs makes it particularly suitable for real-world applications where data quality is often suboptimal. This research contributes to the advancement of graph representation learning by providing a scalable and robust solution that can be applied across diverse domains. **Keywords**: graph embedding, connection subgraphs, robustness, deep learning, node classification, link prediction.

This paper proposes Embedded-State Latent Conditional Random Fields (ES-LCRFs), a novel approach for sequence labeling tasks. The objective is to improve the accuracy of sequence labeling by incorporating latent variables into the model, allowing for more nuanced representations of complex sequences. Our method employs a conditional random field framework, combining it with embedded state representations to capture long-range dependencies and latent structures in the data. The ES-LCRF model is trained using a discriminative algorithm, enabling efficient inference and learning of model parameters. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of ES-LCRFs in achieving state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark sequence labeling datasets, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and F1-score. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of embedded state representations into LCRFs, enabling the model to capture complex sequence patterns, and the development of an efficient training algorithm. This work has significant implications for natural language processing, information extraction, and other sequence labeling applications, highlighting the potential of ES-LCRFs for improving the accuracy and robustness of sequence labeling models. Key keywords: sequence labeling, conditional random fields, latent variables, embedded state representations, natural language processing.

This paper addresses the issue of "fake background" in object tracking, where the tracker loses focus on the target object and instead follows the background. The objective is to develop a novel approach that can effectively re-engage the tracker with the target object. Our method, termed "One More Check," utilizes a dual-module framework, combining a foreground-aware module with a background-suppression module. The foreground-aware module enhances the features of the target object, while the background-suppression module reduces the impact of distracting background information. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves tracking performance, especially in scenarios with complex backgrounds or occlusions. Compared to state-of-the-art tracking methods, "One More Check" achieves superior accuracy and robustness. The key contributions of this research include a innovative dual-module architecture and a novel loss function that facilitates effective tracking. This work has important implications for various applications, including surveillance, autonomous driving, and robotics, where reliable object tracking is crucial. Key keywords: object tracking, fake background, dual-module framework, foreground-aware, background-suppression.

Graphical models of molecular networks are essential tools for understanding complex biological systems, as they capture interactions between molecular components. However, identifying the most significant edges in these networks remains a critical challenge, as it directly impacts the accuracy of downstream analyses and predictions. This study addresses the problem of edge significance identification by proposing a novel computational framework that combines graph-theoretic measures with statistical inference techniques. Our approach leverages edge centrality metrics and probabilistic models to rank edges based on their contribution to network stability and biological relevance. We evaluate the proposed method on synthetic and real-world molecular networks, demonstrating its ability to outperform existing techniques in terms of precision and robustness. The results highlight the framework’s effectiveness in distinguishing biologically meaningful interactions from noise, offering valuable insights for applications such as drug target identification and pathway analysis. This work contributes to advancing the field of network biology by providing a scalable and interpretable solution for edge significance identification, with potential implications for personalized medicine and systems biology research. **Keywords**: graphical models, molecular networks, edge significance, network biology, statistical inference, centrality metrics.

This paper proposes Het-node2vec, a novel embedding method for heterogeneous multigraphs, which leverages second-order random walk sampling to capture complex relationships between nodes. Our method extends traditional node embedding techniques by incorporating second-order proximity, enabling the capture of subtle patterns and community structures in multigraphs. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of Het-node2vec in various downstream tasks, such as node classification, link prediction, and graph clustering, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. The key contributions of this research include the design of a second-order random walk sampler, the development of a heterogeneous multigraph embedding framework, and the demonstration of its applicability in real-world scenarios. This work has significant implications for network analysis, recommender systems, and data mining applications, particularly in domains with complex, heterogeneous relationships. Key keywords: heterogeneous multigraphs, node embedding, second-order random walk, graph representation learning, network analysis.

Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for solving complex continuous control tasks, yet its performance varies significantly across algorithms, environments, and hyperparameters. This paper presents a comprehensive benchmarking study of state-of-the-art DRL algorithms for continuous control, aiming to provide insights into their strengths, limitations, and practical applicability. We evaluate popular algorithms, including Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), and Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), across a diverse set of simulated environments, such as robotic manipulation and locomotion tasks. Our methodology involves systematic hyperparameter tuning, reward analysis, and computational efficiency comparisons to ensure fair and reproducible results. The findings reveal that SAC consistently outperforms other methods in terms of sample efficiency and final performance, while PPO demonstrates robustness in high-dimensional tasks. Additionally, we identify key challenges, such as sensitivity to hyperparameters and scalability issues, that hinder the deployment of DRL in real-world applications. This study contributes a standardized framework for evaluating DRL algorithms, offering actionable recommendations for researchers and practitioners. The results underscore the potential of DRL for continuous control while highlighting areas for future improvement, particularly in terms of stability and generalization. **Keywords**: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Continuous Control, Benchmarking, PPO, SAC, TD3, Robotic Control.

The paper addresses the challenge of balancing exploration and exploitation in reinforcement learning by introducing a novel approach called Almost Boltzmann Exploration. Traditional exploration strategies often struggle to efficiently explore vast state-action spaces in uncertain and dynamic environments. This work aims to enhance learning efficiency and effectiveness through a refined exploration mechanism. Methods/Approach: The Almost Boltzmann Exploration method builds upon the classical Boltzmann exploration strategy by dynamically adjusting the exploration parameter based on the agent's performance and environmental characteristics. This technique integrates a temperature scaling factor that adapts over time, allowing for a more efficient trade-off between exploring new actions and exploiting known rewarding actions. The approach is evaluated using several benchmark reinforcement learning environments to demonstrate its capability. Results/Findings: Experimental results indicate that Almost Boltzmann Exploration significantly improves learning speed and cumulative rewards compared to traditional methods. The adaptive temperature mechanism facilitates more targeted exploration, leading to faster convergence in various test scenarios. The method shows robustness and scalability, outperforming existing state-of-the-art exploration strategies across multiple experimental domains. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Almost Boltzmann Exploration offers a significant advancement in reinforcement learning by optimizing exploration strategies through an adaptive approach. This work contributes a novel perspective on exploration-exploitation trade-offs, with potential applications in complex real-world problems where efficient learning is crucial. Future research may explore its integration with other learning paradigms, such as multi-agent systems and hierarchical reinforcement learning. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Exploration-Exploitation, Boltzmann Exploration, Adaptive Temperature, Machine Learning, Efficient Learning.

This paper introduces a novel adversarial approach to automated image augmentation for deep learning. The primary objective is to improve the generalization performance of image classifiers, particularly when training data is limited. We propose an Adversarial Policy Gradient (APG) framework, where a policy network learns an optimal augmentation policy by interacting with a target classifier in an adversarial manner. The policy network generates augmentation parameters, while the classifier acts as the environment, providing feedback signals based on its validation performance. We employ a policy gradient algorithm to train the policy network, optimizing for augmentation policies that maximize classifier accuracy and robustness. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrate that APG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art augmentation techniques, achieving higher classification accuracy and improved resilience to adversarial attacks. This research offers a new paradigm for automating the design of effective image augmentation strategies, reducing the reliance on manual tuning and enabling more robust deep learning models. Keywords: Image Augmentation, Adversarial Learning, Policy Gradient, Deep Learning, Generalization, Reinforcement Learning.

The selection of optimal data sources is a critical challenge in Bayesian learning, as it directly impacts the accuracy and efficiency of inference processes. This paper addresses the problem of near-optimal data source selection to enhance Bayesian learning outcomes. We propose a novel algorithmic framework that leverages probabilistic modeling and optimization techniques to identify the most informative data sources while minimizing computational overhead. Our approach integrates a hybrid sampling strategy with adaptive weighting mechanisms to dynamically prioritize data sources based on their contribution to the learning objective. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant improvements in prediction accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional selection methods. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robust performance across diverse datasets and learning scenarios, highlighting its versatility. The findings underscore the importance of strategic data source selection in Bayesian learning and provide a scalable solution for real-world applications, such as decision-making systems and predictive analytics. This research contributes to advancing the field by introducing a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded approach to data source optimization. **Keywords**: Bayesian learning, data source selection, probabilistic modeling, optimization, adaptive weighting, computational efficiency.

Autonomous driving systems rely heavily on accurate and efficient object detection to ensure safety and reliability. However, challenges such as suboptimal anchor generation and class imbalance in datasets often hinder the performance of detection models. This paper addresses these issues by proposing a novel framework that enhances object detection through optimized anchor generation and a tailored approach to mitigate class imbalance. Our method introduces an adaptive anchor generation algorithm that dynamically adjusts anchor sizes and aspect ratios based on the distribution of objects in the dataset, improving localization accuracy. This paper introduces a novel approach for salient object detection by leveraging a Multi-scale Interactive Network (MIN). The primary goal of this research is to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of identifying and segmenting salient objects within complex visual scenes, addressing existing challenges such as varying object sizes, cluttered backgrounds, and illumination variations. Methods/Approach: The proposed MIN architecture integrates multi-scale feature extraction with interactive learning strategies to improve the detection performance. The network employs a hierarchical framework that processes input images at multiple scales, enabling the capture of both global context and fine-grained details. An innovative interactive learning module is designed to facilitate information flow between scales, ensuring coherent feature integration and refinement across the network layers. Results/Findings: Our experimental evaluations, conducted on several benchmark datasets, demonstrate that the Multi-scale Interactive Network significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in salient object detection. Quantitative results show improvements in standard metrics such as F-measure, precision, and recall. The extensive comparative analysis highlights the capability of MIN to handle diverse scene complexities and object sizes more effectively than existing approaches. Conclusion/Implications: The research offers critical insights into the design and implementation of advanced networks for visual perception tasks, with implications extending to real-world applications such as automated image editing, object tracking, and autonomous driving. The key contributions of this study include the development of a robust framework for salient object detection that enhances both detection accuracy and computational efficiency, paving the way for future advancements in multimedia processing and computer vision. Keywords: salient object detection, multi-scale feature extraction, interactive learning, neural networks, computer vision, automated segmentation.

This paper introduces DRIFT, a novel framework leveraging Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) techniques to advance the field of functional software testing. Traditional automated software testing approaches often struggle to effectively explore complex input spaces, resulting in suboptimal test coverage and undetected bugs. To address these challenges, DRIFT formulates the testing process as a Markov Decision Process and utilizes modern DRL algorithms to dynamically generate test cases that adapt based on feedback from code execution. The proposed method integrates a neural network-based policy model to learn exploration strategies that maximize code coverage and defect discovery over time. In extensive experiments on open-source software systems, DRIFT demonstrated significantly higher efficiency and bug-detection rates compared to conventional random and model-based testing frameworks. Furthermore, DRIFT’s adaptive mechanism allows for continuous improvement as testing progresses, making it highly suitable for real-world, large-scale software systems. The main contributions of this research include the development of an end-to-end DRL-based test generation pipeline, a detailed evaluation on diverse benchmarks, and analysis of DRL’s effectiveness in functional testing scenarios. These results underscore the potential of deep reinforcement learning to transform automated software testing, enhancing software quality and reliability. Keywords: deep reinforcement learning, functional testing, software testing automation, neural networks, code coverage.

Segmenting transparent objects in real-world images presents a significant challenge due to the inherent ambiguity in identifying object boundaries and separating them from background clutter. This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework, TransWildSeg, designed to address these complexities. TransWildSeg incorporates a specialized attention mechanism that focuses on subtle variations in texture and refraction patterns indicative of transparent surfaces. We employ a two-stage training process, first pre-training the model on synthetic data with diverse lighting conditions and object shapes, followed by fine-tuning on a newly curated dataset of real-world images containing a variety of transparent objects. Experimental results demonstrate that TransWildSeg outperforms existing state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, achieving a 15% improvement in IoU score on our real-world dataset. The proposed approach demonstrates effective segmentation of transparent objects under complex and unconstrained environmental conditions, offering potential applications in robotics, augmented reality, and material recognition. Keywords: Transparent Object Segmentation, Deep Learning, Attention Mechanism, Image Processing, Computer Vision.

With recent developments in smart technologies, there has been a growing focus on the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for affective computing to further enhance the user experience through emotion recognition. Typically, machine learning models used for affective computing are trained using manually extracted features from biological signals. Such features may not generalize well for large datasets and may be sub-optimal in capturing the information from the raw input data. One approach to address this issue is to use fully supervised deep learning methods to learn latent representations of the biosignals. However, this method requires human supervision to label the data, which may be unavailable or difficult to obtain. In this work we propose an unsupervised framework reduce the reliance on human supervision. The proposed framework utilizes two stacked convolutional autoencoders to learn latent representations from wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) and electrodermal activity (EDA) signals. These representations are utilized within a random forest model for binary arousal classification. This approach reduces human supervision and enables the aggregation of datasets allowing for higher generalizability. To validate this framework, an aggregated dataset comprised of the AMIGOS, ASCERTAIN, CLEAS, and MAHNOB-HCI datasets is created. The results of our proposed method are compared with using convolutional neural networks, as well as methods that employ manual extraction of hand-crafted features. The methodology used for fusing the two modalities is also investigated. Lastly, we show that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art results that have performed arousal detection on the same datasets using ECG and EDA biosignals. The results show the wide-spread applicability for stacked convolutional autoencoders to be used with machine learning for affective computing.
