The increasing demand for efficient and accessible deep learning solutions in medical imaging, particularly for 3D segmentation tasks, has highlighted the limitations of GPU-dependent models in resource-constrained environments. This paper introduces **TernaryNet**, a novel deep learning framework designed to accelerate model inference without relying on GPUs by leveraging **sparse and binary convolutions**. TernaryNet addresses the computational inefficiencies of traditional 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by reducing the precision of weights and activations to ternary values (-1, 0, +1), enabling faster computations on CPU-based systems. Our approach integrates a sparse convolution mechanism to minimize redundant operations, further enhancing inference speed. Experiments on benchmark medical 3D segmentation datasets demonstrate that TernaryNet achieves comparable accuracy to state-of-the-art models while reducing inference time by up to **60%** on CPUs. The framework also exhibits significant memory efficiency, making it suitable for deployment in low-resource clinical settings. By eliminating the need for GPUs, TernaryNet provides a cost-effective and scalable solution for real-time medical image analysis, with potential applications in telemedicine and point-of-care diagnostics. This work contributes to the growing field of efficient deep learning by introducing a lightweight yet powerful architecture tailored for medical 3D segmentation tasks. **Keywords**: TernaryNet, 3D segmentation, sparse convolutions, binary convolutions, CPU inference, medical imaging, efficient deep learning.

Đơn vị tính toán cơ bản là "gas"; thông thường, một bước tính toán tốn 1 gas, nhưng một số hoạt động têu tốn lượng gas cao hơn vì chúng điắt hơn về mặt tính toán hoặc tăng lượng dữ liệu phải được lưu trữ như một phần của trạng thá. Ngoà ra còn có một khoản phí 5 gas cho mỗ byte trong dữ liệu giao dịch. Mục điích của hệ thống tính phí là yêu cầu kẻ tấn công trả tền tương ứng cho mọ tài nguyên mà chúng têu thụ, bao gồm tính toán, băng thông và lưu trữ; do đó, bất kỳ giao dịch nào dẫn đến việc mạng têu thụ nhều hơn bất kỳ tài nguyên nào trong số này điều phả có phí gas gần như tỷ lệ thuận với mức tăng.

Nghiên cứu thực trạng về các công trình tiêu giảm sóng hiện đang áp dụng cho thấy sự phát triển mạnh mẽ trong lĩnh vực này nhằm bảo vệ môi trường và giảm thiểu tác động của sóng đến các công trình xây dựng. Các công trình này được thiết kế với nhiều công nghệ tiên tiến, giúp giảm thiểu năng lượng sóng tác động lên bờ biển và các công trình ven biển. Tuy nhiên, nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra một số ưu nhược điểm đáng chú ý. Ưu điểm bao gồm khả năng bảo vệ hiệu quả, giảm thiểu xói mòn và bảo vệ hệ sinh thái ven biển. Ngược lại, nhược điểm chủ yếu nằm ở chi phí đầu tư ban đầu cao và yêu cầu bảo trì thường xuyên. Việc phân tích kỹ lưỡng các yếu tố này sẽ giúp các nhà quản lý và nhà đầu tư đưa ra quyết định hợp lý hơn trong việc lựa chọn và triển khai các giải pháp tiêu giảm sóng phù hợp với từng khu vực cụ thể.

Việt Nam cam kết giảm 8% lượng phát thải khí nhà kính so với kịch bản phát triển thông thường vào năm 2030 và có thể giảm tiếp đến 25% nếu nhận được hỗ trợ quốc tế (NDC) [6]. Để đạt được mục tiêu trên, Việt Nam cần xây dựng được một hệ thống đo đạc, báo cáo và thẩm tra (MRV) công khai và minh bạch các hoạt động giảm nhẹ phát thải khí nhà kính nói chung và áp dụng cho từng ngành nói riêng, trong đó có lĩnh vực luyện kim. Bài báo giới thiệu về bộ chỉ số MRV với 12 chỉ số chính và đề xuất quy trình MRV cho hoạt động giảm nhẹ phát thải khí nhà kính lĩnh vực luyện kim của Việt Nam. Kết quả của bài báo sẽ cung cấp cơ sở khoa học cho các nhà hoạch định chính sách và cơ quan nghiên cứu khoa học liên quan để xây dựng hệ thống MRV cho các hoạt động giảm nhẹ phát thải khí nhà kính quốc gia tại Việt Nam.

Accurate detection of salient objects in RGB-D images is critical for various applications in computer vision and robotics. This paper presents a novel approach to RGB-D Salient Object Detection through Collaborative Learning, aimed at enhancing detection accuracy and robustness. The proposed method integrates a collaborative framework that leverages both RGB and depth information to effectively identify and segment salient objects. By employing advanced deep learning models, the approach utilizes cross-modal feature fusion and attention mechanisms to improve the precision of saliency maps. Our evaluation, conducted on benchmark datasets, demonstrates a significant improvement in detection accuracy compared to existing methods, with a marked reduction in false positives and improved boundary accuracy. The results reveal that our collaborative learning framework outperforms traditional approaches, indicating enhanced adaptability in diverse environments. This study contributes to the field by providing a robust solution for real-time applications, paving the way for more sophisticated autonomous systems. Future applications could include augmented reality, intelligent surveillance, and human-machine interaction with improved environmental awareness. Key terms include RGB-D saliency, deep learning, collaborative learning, and attention mechanisms.

Việt Nam đang đối mặt với thách thức lớn trong việc phát triển bền vững, và vai trò của các doanh nghiệp trong việc thực hiện trách nhiệm xã hội ngày càng trở nên quan trọng. Các doanh nghiệp không chỉ cần tập trung vào lợi nhuận mà còn phải chú trọng đến tác động của hoạt động kinh doanh đối với cộng đồng và môi trường. Việc thúc đẩy trách nhiệm xã hội sẽ giúp các doanh nghiệp xây dựng hình ảnh tích cực, thu hút khách hàng và đối tác, đồng thời góp phần vào sự phát triển bền vững của nền kinh tế. Các chính sách hỗ trợ từ chính phủ, cùng với sự tham gia tích cực của cộng đồng và các tổ chức phi chính phủ, sẽ là yếu tố then chốt để nâng cao nhận thức và khuyến khích các doanh nghiệp thực hiện các hoạt động có trách nhiệm xã hội. Điều này không chỉ mang lại lợi ích cho doanh nghiệp mà còn cho toàn xã hội, hướng tới một tương lai phát triển bền vững hơn cho Việt Nam.

Probabilistic programs offer a powerful and flexible framework for modeling complex systems with uncertainty. However, performing inference in these programs remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel meta-learning approach to automatically learn an efficient inference algorithm tailored to a specific class of probabilistic programs. Our method uses a recurrent neural network to parameterize an inference procedure, and trains this network across a distribution of program structures and datasets. This enables the learned inference algorithm to generalize to unseen programs within the same distribution. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a variety of probabilistic programming tasks, including Bayesian regression, hierarchical modeling, and time series analysis. Empirical results show that the meta-learned inference algorithm achieves significant improvements in inference speed and accuracy compared to traditional methods like Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) and variational inference. This work provides a promising direction for automating and accelerating probabilistic inference, making it more accessible and scalable for real-world applications. **Keywords:** Meta-learning, probabilistic programming, inference algorithm, neural networks, Bayesian methods, MCMC, variational inference.

Image captioning, the task of generating descriptive text for images, has seen significant advancements with the integration of deep learning techniques. However, existing models often struggle to align textual descriptions with specific visual details, leading to generic or inaccurate captions. This paper proposes a novel **Text-guided Attention Model (TAM)** for image captioning, which leverages textual guidance to enhance the alignment between visual and linguistic features. The model employs a dual-attention mechanism, where one stream focuses on visual features while the other dynamically adjusts attention based on the generated text, ensuring more contextually relevant captions. We evaluate TAM on benchmark datasets such as MS COCO and Flickr30k, demonstrating its superior performance over state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and diversity of generated captions. Experimental results show improvements in BLEU, METEOR, and CIDEr scores, highlighting the model's ability to produce more precise and human-like descriptions. The proposed approach not only advances the field of image captioning but also has potential applications in assistive technologies, content generation, and multimedia retrieval. Key innovations include the integration of text-guided attention and the ability to dynamically refine visual focus during caption generation. Keywords: image captioning, text-guided attention, deep learning, visual-language alignment, dual-attention mechanism.

The increasing vulnerability of deep learning models to adversarial attacks necessitates robust defense mechanisms. This paper introduces Deep Latent Defence (DLD), a novel defense strategy that operates within the latent space of a deep neural network. DLD employs an autoencoder architecture to map input data into a lower-dimensional latent space, effectively filtering out adversarial perturbations before classification. By learning a clean latent representation, DLD enhances model resilience without significantly impacting accuracy on benign samples. Our approach incorporates a latent perturbation detector that identifies and mitigates adversarial manipulations in the latent space. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet, demonstrate that DLD achieves state-of-the-art defense performance against various adversarial attacks, such as FGSM, PGD, and C&W, while maintaining competitive clean accuracy. The proposed method offers a practical and effective solution for enhancing the security of deep learning systems in adversarial environments. Keywords: adversarial defense, deep learning, latent space, autoencoder, robustness, adversarial attacks.

Hồ Gươm, biểu tượng văn hóa và lịch sử của Hà Nội, không chỉ là một danh thắng nổi tiếng mà còn là không gian sống quan trọng của người dân thủ đô. Với diện tích khoảng 12 hecta, hồ mang giá trị đặc biệt về cảnh quan, sinh thái và tâm linh. Tuy nhiên, trong bối cảnh đô thị hóa nhanh chóng, Hồ Gươm đang đối mặt với nhiều thách thức như ô nhiễm môi trường, áp lực từ các công trình xây dựng và sự gia tăng dân số. Để bảo tồn và phát huy giá trị của không gian này, cần có những giải pháp đồng bộ, từ việc quản lý chặt chẽ các hoạt động xung quanh hồ, nâng cao ý thức cộng đồng, đến việc phát triển các dự án bền vững, hài hòa giữa bảo tồn và phát triển. Định hướng tương lai cần đảm bảo Hồ Gươm vừa là điểm đến du lịch hấp dẫn, vừa là không gian xanh, trong lành, gắn kết với đời sống người dân.

**Abstract:** This paper presents TensorFlow Lite Micro, an optimized framework designed to enable embedded machine learning on resource-constrained devices, commonly referred to as TinyML systems. The objective of this research is to address the growing demand for deploying neural network models on microcontrollers and edge devices with limited memory and processing capabilities. We detail the architecture of TensorFlow Lite Micro, highlighting its lightweight kernel design, efficient memory footprint, and portability across a wide range of hardware platforms. Through systematic experiments, we evaluate the deployment of various machine learning models, such as keyword spotting and anomaly detection, demonstrating low-latency inference and minimal resource consumption on devices with as little as 16KB RAM. Comparative analysis with existing inference engines shows superior adaptability and ease of integration into embedded workflows. The results underscore how TensorFlow Lite Micro empowers real-time, on-device AI, eliminating the need for constant cloud connectivity and enhancing privacy and responsiveness in IoT applications. Our study concludes by discussing the framework's potential to accelerate the adoption of TinyML in industrial, healthcare, and smart home scenarios, establishing a foundation for further advancements in embedded AI. Key keywords: TinyML, embedded systems, microcontrollers, machine learning, TensorFlow Lite, on-device inference, edge AI.

Dậy thì sớm trung ương (CPP) đang gia tăng, đặc biệt ở trẻ thừa cân và béo phì. Nghiên cứu cho thấy mối liên hệ chặt chẽ giữa tình trạng cân nặng và tuổi dậy thì ở trẻ em gái, với nguy cơ CPP tăng cao ở nhóm thừa cân béo phì so với nhóm cân nặng bình thường. Leptin, một hormone do mô mỡ tiết ra, có thể đóng vai trò quan trọng trong cơ chế bệnh sinh của CPP ở trẻ béo phì. Nồng độ leptin cao có thể kích hoạt trục dưới đồi - tuyến yên - tuyến sinh dục, dẫn đến dậy thì sớm. Các yếu tố khác như insulin, yếu tố tăng trưởng giống insulin 1 (IGF-1) và tình trạng viêm cũng có thể góp phần vào quá trình này. Việc kiểm soát cân nặng hợp lý thông qua chế độ ăn uống lành mạnh và tăng cường hoạt động thể chất là rất quan trọng để giảm nguy cơ CPP ở trẻ em, đặc biệt là nhóm có nguy cơ cao như trẻ thừa cân và béo phì. Cần có thêm nghiên cứu để hiểu rõ hơn về cơ chế phức tạp giữa béo phì và dậy thì sớm, từ đó đưa ra các biện pháp phòng ngừa và điều trị hiệu quả.

Nghiên cứu mới đây đã chỉ ra rằng giá trị dinh dưỡng của các loại thực phẩm có thể bị ảnh hưởng bởi quá trình hình thành và phát triển của chúng. Các nhà khoa học đã thực hiện một nghiên cứu sâu rộng về ảnh hưởng của các yếu tố môi trường, như ánh sáng mặt trời, độ ẩm và nhiệt độ, đến giá trị dinh dưỡng của các loại thực phẩm. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy rằng quá trình hình thành và phát triển của thực phẩm có thể ảnh hưởng đến sự hiện diện của các chất dinh dưỡng quan trọng như vitamin, khoáng chất và chất chống oxy hóa. Ví dụ, các loại rau củ được trồng dưới ánh sáng mặt trời mạnh mẽ có thể chứa nhiều vitamin hơn so với những loại được trồng dưới ánh sáng yếu. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng quá trình bảo quản và xử lý thực phẩm có thể ảnh hưởng đến giá trị dinh dưỡng của chúng. Ví dụ, các loại rau củ được bảo quản ở nhiệt độ thấp có thể giữ được giá trị dinh dưỡng lâu hơn so với những loại được bảo quản ở nhiệt độ cao. Tổng kết, nghiên cứu này cho thấy rằng giá trị dinh dưỡng của thực phẩm có thể bị ảnh hưởng bởi nhiều yếu tố, bao gồm quá trình hình thành và phát triển, bảo quản và xử lý. Điều này có ý nghĩa quan trọng đối với việc sản xuất và tiêu thụ thực phẩm, và có thể giúp chúng ta hiểu rõ hơn về giá trị dinh dưỡng của các loại thực phẩm khác nhau.

Cascading Style Sheets, viết tắt là CSS, là một ngôn ngữ được sử dụng để mô tả các trình bày của một tập tin HTML hoặc XML. CSS sẽ mô tả cách mà các phần tử được hiển thị trên màn hình, trên giấy hoặc trên các phương tiện truyền thông khác. Một cách đơn giản, nếu HTML có nhiệm vụ mô tả cấu trúc của các phần tử trong một trang web, thì CSS sẽ có va trò thêm các kiểu (style) cho các phần tử đó như màu sắc, cỡ chữ, trật tự hiển thị,... Hình 3.4 điã cho thấy vớ cùng một tài liệu HTML không sử dụng tệp CSS khác nhau có thể sẽ cho ra 4 kiểu bố cục và hiển thị khác nhau.Hình 3.4: Ví dụ về một tài liệu HTML được hiển thị với 4 kiểu khác nhau CSS ban đầu được phát triển bởi W3C (World Wide Web Consortium) vớ vai trò hỗ trợ định dạng trang web cho HTML. CSS đưa ra khái niệm vùng chọn. Vùng chọn có thể là tổ hợp của d của phần từ HTML, tên class,... CSS sẽ xác định các các vùng chọn này và áp dụng các thuộc tính tương ứng để thay đổi kiểu của vùng chọn đó. Chính vì thế, HTML và CSS có mối quan hệ mật thiết với nhau.

Kh kết hợp các công nghệ khác nhau, nhà phát triển thường luôn phải tìm cách tích hợp được sự khác nhau của các ngôn ngữ lập trình. Tuy nhện, đi với MEM, lập trình viên chỉ cần thành thạo JavaScript và JSON và không cần thiết phải chuyển đồ mô trường. ĐATN điã lựa chọn MEAN điểm xây dựng App QLDA cũng vì những lí do trên.

Gradient descent (GD) is an iterative first-order optimisation algorithm used to find a local minimum or a local maximum of a given function. This method is commonly used in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) to minimise a cost function (e.g., in a ar regression). However, its use is not limited to Machine Learning or Deep Learning only, it’s being widely used also in areas like, control engineering (robotics, chemical, etc.), computer games and mechanical engineering.

Nấm ăn là lo ại thực phẩm sạch có giá tr ị dinh dư ỡng đư ợc sử dụng trong các b ữa ăn hàng ngày và giá tr ị y học đã được biết đến từ hàng nghìn n ăm. Nhi ều nghiên c ứu đã chỉ ra rằng trong n ấm ăn có ch ứa các polyphenol và L - ergothioneine (ERGO) , đây là các ch ất chống oxi hóa có tác d ụng lớn trong phòng ch ống bệnh tật. Bài báo này trình bày các k ết quả nghiên c ứu thu đư ợc về hàm lương polyphenol và ho ạt tính ch ống oxi hóa trong m ũ nấm, thân n ấm và ph ế phụ phẩm (PPP) c ủa 5 lo ại nấm. Hàm lư ợng poly phenol trong m ũ nấm, thân n ấm và ph ế phụ phẩm của nấm Sò tím ( Pleurotus spp.), nấm Sò tr ắng (Pleurotus spp.), nấm Ng ọc châm ( Hypsizygus marmoreu) , nấm Mỡ (Agaricus bisporus), nấm Đùi gà ( Pleurotus eryngii) là khác nhau ph ụ thuộc vào t ừng lo ại nấm. Retrosynthesis, of which the goal is to find a set of reactants for synthesizing a target product, is an emerging research area of deep learning. While the existing approaches have shown promising results, they currently lack the ability to consider availability (e.g., stability or purchasability) of the reactants or generalize to unseen reaction templates (i.e., chemical reaction rules). In this paper, we propose a new approach that mitigates the issues by reformulating retrosynthesis into a selection problem of reactants from a candidate set of commercially available molecules. To this end, we design an efficient reactant selection framework, named RetCL (retrosynthesis via contrastive learning), for enumerating all of the candidate molecules based on selection scores computed by graph neural networks. For learning the score functions, we also propose a novel contrastive training scheme with hard negative mining. Extensive experiments demonstrate the benefits of the proposed selection-based approach. For example, when all 671k reactants in the USPTO are given as candidates, our RetCL achieves top-1 exact match accuracy of 71.3\% for the USPTO-50k benchmark, while a recent transformer-based approach achieves 59.6\%. We also demonstrate that RetCL generalizes well to unseen templates in various settings in contrast to template-based approaches.

Electronic Health Records (EHRs) contain a wealth of information for improving healthcare delivery and research. However, their high dimensionality and complex structure pose significant challenges for effective analysis. This paper investigates the use of autoencoders, a class of neural networks for unsupervised representation learning, to extract meaningful features from EHR data. We comparatively evaluate several autoencoder architectures, including vanilla, sparse, and variational autoencoders, on real-world EHR datasets. The models are assessed based on their ability to reconstruct input data and their performance on downstream tasks such as patient classification and risk prediction. Results demonstrate that variational autoencoders achieve superior performance in capturing the underlying data distribution, leading to improved feature representations and enhanced predictive accuracy compared to other autoencoder variants and traditional methods. This study highlights the potential of autoencoders for unlocking valuable insights from EHR data, facilitating more informed clinical decision-making and personalized healthcare. Keywords: Electronic Health Records, Autoencoders, Representation Learning, Machine Learning, Healthcare, Deep Learning.

Spatio-temporal information is very important to capture the discriminative cues between genuine and fake faces from video sequences. To explore such a temporal feature, the fine-grained motions (e.g., eye blinking, mouth movements and head swing) across video frames are very critical. In this paper, we propose a joint CNN-LSTM network for face anti-spoofing, focusing on the motion cues across video frames. We first extract the high discriminative features of video frames using the conventional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Then we leverage Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with the extracted features as inputs to capture the temporal dynamics in videos. To ensure the fine-grained motions more easily to be perceived in the training process, the eulerian motion magnification is used as the preprocessing to enhance the facial expressions exhibited by individuals, and the attention mechanism is embedded in LSTM to ensure the model learn to focus selectively on the dynamic frames across the video clips. Experiments on Replay Attack and MSU-MFSD databases show that the proposed method yields state-of-the-art performance with better generalization ability compared with several other popular algorithms.

Điều này mở ra hướng đi mới trong việc sử dụng các vi sinh vật có lợi để tăng cường hiệu quả của các biện pháp xử lý ô nhiễm môi trường bằng thực vật, đặc biệt là ô nhiễm crom, một vấn đề đang ngày càng trở nên cấp thiết. Nghiên cứu này tập trung xem xét tầm quan trọng của các khía cạnh vốn xã hội trong mối quan hệ người mua - nhà cung cấp, đồng thời cũng xem xét tác động của thay đổi công nghệ với mối quan hệ giữa các quy mô vốn xã hội và hiệu quả của các nhà cung cấp. Nghiên cứu thực hiện khảo sát trên 92 nhà cung cấp. Phương pháp hồi quy tuyến tính bội được sử dụng để xác định mức độ ảnh hưởng của các yếu tố. Kết quả phân tích cho thấy nhận thức vốn xã hội có tác động tích cực và đáng kẻ đến chiến lược hoạt động của các doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa Việt Nam. Tuy nhiên, tác động của cấu trúc vốn xã hội không xác định được. Bên cạnh đó, phân tích cũng cho thấy rằng sự thay đổi trong công nghệ có thể giúp các nhà cung cấp phát triển sản phẩm mới và thâm nhập vào những thị trường mới. This paper introduces SLIDE, a novel framework for single-image 3D photography that leverages soft layering and depth-aware inpainting to generate high-quality 3D reconstructions from a single 2D image. The objective of this research is to address the challenges of depth estimation and occlusion handling in monocular 3D reconstruction, which are critical for applications in augmented reality, virtual environments, and digital content creation. SLIDE employs a two-stage approach: first, it utilizes a soft layering mechanism to decompose the input image into depth-ordered layers, enabling precise depth estimation and scene segmentation. Second, a depth-aware inpainting module is applied to reconstruct occluded regions, ensuring seamless and realistic 3D outputs. Experimental results demonstrate that SLIDE outperforms existing methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy, visual fidelity, and computational efficiency. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, with significant improvements in handling complex scenes and occlusions. The proposed method not only advances the field of single-image 3D photography but also provides a robust solution for real-world applications requiring efficient and accurate 3D scene generation. **Keywords**: 3D photography, depth estimation, occlusion handling, soft layering, depth-aware inpainting, monocular reconstruction.

This paper introduces ASM2TV, an Adaptive Semi-Supervised Multi-Task Multi-View learning framework designed to leverage both labeled and unlabeled data across multiple views and tasks. The objective is to improve model generalization and performance in scenarios where data is heterogeneous and labels are scarce. ASM2TV employs an adaptive weighting mechanism to dynamically adjust the contribution of each view and task based on their respective relevance and uncertainty. A novel semi-supervised learning approach is integrated to effectively utilize unlabeled data, enhancing the model's ability to capture underlying data distributions. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that ASM2TV outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, particularly when dealing with incomplete or noisy data. The proposed framework offers a promising solution for complex learning problems involving multi-view and multi-task data, contributing to advancements in areas such as data fusion and transfer learning. Keywords: Multi-view learning, Multi-task learning, Semi-supervised learning, Adaptive weighting, Data fusion.

This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of a two-stage feature transfer approach in deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for the classification of diffuse lung diseases. The proposed method involves transferring features from a pre-trained CNN model to a target model in two stages, allowing for a more efficient and accurate representation of lung disease characteristics. Our approach utilizes a combination of convolutional and fully connected layers to extract and refine features, which are then used for disease classification. Experimental results demonstrate that the two-stage feature transfer method outperforms traditional single-stage transfer learning approaches, achieving a significant improvement in classification accuracy. The findings of this research contribute to the development of more accurate and reliable computer-aided diagnosis systems for diffuse lung diseases, highlighting the potential of deep learning techniques in medical image analysis. Key contributions include the introduction of a novel two-stage feature transfer method, the evaluation of feature representation in deep CNNs, and the application of this approach to a critical medical imaging task, with relevant keywords including deep learning, convolutional neural networks, feature transfer, lung disease classification, and medical image analysis.

Kết quả ban đầu cho thấy phương pháp này mang lại hiệu quả cao trong việc giảm thiểu biến chứng, rút ngắn thời gian điều trị và cải thiện chất lượng cuộc sống cho bệnh nhân. Đa dạng hóa thu nhập đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc giảm thiểu rủi ro phá sản của các ngân hàng thương mại tại Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu chỉ ra rằng việc mở rộng các nguồn thu nhập không chỉ giúp ngân hàng tăng cường khả năng tài chính mà còn tạo ra sự ổn định trong hoạt động kinh doanh. Khi ngân hàng phụ thuộc vào một nguồn thu nhập duy nhất, họ dễ bị tổn thương trước những biến động của thị trường. Ngược lại, việc đa dạng hóa giúp phân tán rủi ro, từ đó nâng cao khả năng chống chịu trước các cú sốc kinh tế. Các ngân hàng có chiến lược đa dạng hóa hiệu quả thường có tỷ lệ phá sản thấp hơn, nhờ vào việc duy trì dòng tiền ổn định và cải thiện khả năng quản lý rủi ro. Do đó, việc thúc đẩy đa dạng hóa thu nhập không chỉ là một chiến lược kinh doanh thông minh mà còn là yếu tố then chốt trong việc bảo vệ sự bền vững của các ngân hàng thương mại trong bối cảnh kinh tế đầy biến động.

Nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc tổng hợp và đánh giá khả năng ức chế enzyme lipase tụy của các dẫn chất aurone mới, trong đó vòng benzylidene được thay thế bằng các nhóm chức khác nhau. Mục tiêu là tìm ra các hợp chất có khả năng ức chế lipase tụy mạnh mẽ, từ đó có tiềm năng ứng dụng trong điều trị béo phì và các bệnh liên quan đến rối loạn lipid máu. Các dẫn chất aurone được tổng hợp thông qua các phản ứng hóa học chọn lọc và sau đó được kiểm tra hoạt tính ức chế lipase tụy trong điều kiện in vitro. Kết quả cho thấy một số dẫn chất aurone thể hiện khả năng ức chế đáng kể, với hoạt tính mạnh hơn so với các hợp chất aurone không thế hoặc các chất ức chế lipase tụy đã biết. Nghiên cứu này mở ra hướng đi mới trong việc phát triển các loại thuốc ức chế lipase tụy hiệu quả hơn, góp phần vào việc kiểm soát cân nặng và cải thiện sức khỏe tim mạch. Các nhà nghiên cứu cũng nhấn mạnh sự cần thiết của các nghiên cứu sâu hơn về cơ chế tác động và đánh giá an toàn của các dẫn chất aurone này trước khi đưa vào thử nghiệm lâm sàng.

Các không gian truyền thống như vỉa hè, công viên, chợ đang dần thay đổi chức năng và diện mạo dưới áp lực của giao thông, thương mại và xây dựng. Việc thiếu quy hoạch đồng bộ và quản lý hiệu quả dẫn đến tình trạng không gian công cộng bị lấn chiếm, sử dụng sai mục đích, gây ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng sống của người dân. Nghiên cứu cho thấy cần có giải pháp quy hoạch và thiết kế phù hợp để bảo tồn các giá trị văn hóa, lịch sử, đồng thời tạo ra các không gian công cộng đa chức năng, đáp ứng nhu cầu của cộng đồng và thúc đẩy sự phát triển bền vững của thành phố. Việc cải thiện hình thái không gian công cộng không chỉ nâng cao tính thẩm mỹ đô thị mà còn góp phần tăng cường sự gắn kết xã hội và tạo dựng môi trường sống tốt đẹp hơn cho người dân thành phố.

In the rapidly evolving field of event prediction, accurately estimating uncertainties remains a pivotal challenge. This paper presents a novel approach to scalable joint models aimed at enhancing reliability in uncertainty-aware event prediction. Our methodology integrates advanced probabilistic techniques with machine learning algorithms to construct adaptable models capable of processing large-scale data efficiently. We leverage a multi-faceted framework that combines feature extraction, data normalization, and model optimization, demonstrating an innovative synergy of existing methodologies. Through extensive experiments on diverse datasets, we reveal that our joint models outperform traditional event prediction methods in terms of accuracy and reliability, particularly when handling uncertain information. Key findings indicate a significant improvement in prediction intervals and reduced mean absolute errors, thereby affirming the robustness of our approach across varying conditions. These contributions not only advance the state-of-the-art in uncertainty quantification for event predictions but also present potential applications in fields such as disaster management, finance, and healthcare, where accurate forecasting is critical. Our work establishes foundational insights into scalable uncertainty-aware models, paving the way for future research in high-dimensional data analysis. Keywords: uncertainty-aware prediction, scalable models, joint modeling, machine learning, event prediction, probabilistic techniques.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving data efficiency in hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) frameworks, which are often hampered by high sample complexity and slow convergence rates. We propose a novel architecture that integrates efficient state abstraction and sub-policy reuse within a hierarchical structure, enabling more effective exploration and faster learning in complex environments. The proposed method employs a meta-controller to dynamically select from a library of learned sub-policies, each specialized for specific subtasks, and leverages transfer learning techniques to share knowledge across related tasks. Through extensive experiments on benchmark continuous control and navigation tasks, our approach demonstrates significant improvements in learning speed and performance compared to standard HRL and flat reinforcement learning baselines. Results indicate a substantial reduction in the number of interactions required with the environment to achieve optimal or near-optimal policy performance. The findings highlight the potential of modular abstractions and policy sharing to make hierarchical reinforcement learning more practical for real-world applications where data collection is costly or limited. Our contributions include a scalable framework for data-efficient HRL, comprehensive empirical validation, and insights into the trade-offs between hierarchy depth and learning efficiency. This work advances the state of the art in reinforcement learning by promoting data efficiency, scalability, and adaptability in complex sequential decision-making problems. Key keywords: hierarchical reinforcement learning, data efficiency, sub-policy reuse, state abstraction, transfer learning, reinforcement learning.

Sim-to-real domain adaptation remains a significant challenge in reinforcement learning (RL), limiting the deployment of agents trained in simulation to real-world environments due to discrepancies between the two domains. This paper introduces a meta-reinforcement learning (meta-RL) approach to address this challenge by enabling faster adaptation to new real-world environments. Our method trains an agent across a distribution of simulated environments with varying dynamics, allowing it to learn a general policy initialization and adaptation strategy. The agent then leverages this learned knowledge to quickly adapt to unseen real-world environments with minimal on-policy fine-tuning. We evaluate our approach on a series of simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks. Results demonstrate that our meta-RL agent significantly outperforms agents trained from scratch or using standard RL techniques, achieving faster convergence and higher asymptotic performance in real-world settings. The findings highlight the potential of meta-RL for enabling robust and efficient sim-to-real transfer in reinforcement learning. Keywords: Meta-Reinforcement Learning, Sim-to-Real, Domain Adaptation, Reinforcement Learning, Robotics, Transfer Learning.

This paper presents a comprehensive benchmarking study of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms for continuous control tasks. The objective is to evaluate and compare the performance of state-of-the-art DRL methods, including policy gradient, actor-critic, and deep deterministic policy gradient algorithms. We employ a range of benchmark environments, such as robotic arm manipulation and locomotion tasks, to assess the algorithms' ability to learn complex control policies. Our results show that while all algorithms demonstrate impressive performance, significant differences exist in their sample efficiency, stability, and ability to handle high-dimensional action spaces. We identify key factors influencing algorithmic performance, including exploration strategies, network architectures, and hyperparameter tuning. The findings of this study have important implications for the development of autonomous systems, robotics, and other applications requiring continuous control. Our benchmarking framework and results provide a foundation for future research in DRL, highlighting the need for more efficient, robust, and generalizable algorithms. Key keywords: deep reinforcement learning, continuous control, benchmarking, policy gradient, actor-critic, robotic arm manipulation, locomotion tasks.

This paper proposes a novel approach to training Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) by integrating self-labeling and self-attention mechanisms. Experimental results demonstrate that our unified framework outperforms existing GAN training methods, achieving superior image quality and diversity. The key findings include improved inception scores, reduced training time, and enhanced robustness to hyperparameter settings. Our approach contributes to the advancement of GAN research, offering a promising direction for applications in image synthesis, data augmentation, and AI-generated content. Key keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, Self-Labeling, Self-Attention, Deep Learning, Image Synthesis.

Facial Expression Recognition (FER) is a crucial task in human-computer interaction, enabling machines to understand and respond to human emotions. This paper explores the effectiveness of using pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) features for FER. We leverage features extracted from CNNs pre-trained on large-scale image datasets like ImageNet, transferring the learned representations to the FER task. Specifically, we investigate the performance of different CNN architectures, including VGG16, ResNet50, and InceptionV3, by employing their intermediate layer outputs as feature vectors for training a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, such as FER-2013 and CK+, demonstrate that the pre-trained CNN features achieve competitive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods that involve training CNNs from scratch. Furthermore, our approach significantly reduces training time and computational resources. The findings suggest that pre-trained CNN features offer a powerful and efficient solution for FER, especially when limited labeled data is available. This transfer learning technique provides a robust and easily adaptable method for facial expression analysis in various applications. Keywords: Facial Expression Recognition, Convolutional Neural Networks, Transfer Learning, Pre-trained Models, Feature Extraction, ImageNet, Emotion Recognition.

Objective: Graph Attention Networks (GATs) have become a cornerstone in graph-based learning, leveraging learned attention coefficients to weight neighbor contributions. However, the extent to which these coefficients genuinely reflect structural relevance and support model interpretability remains underexplored. Methods: We introduce a suite of quantitative metrics—including attention entropy, edge-salience alignment, and centrality correlation—to evaluate attention distributions in GATs across standard node-classification and link-prediction benchmarks. We further compare vanilla GATs with variants employing sparsity regularization and attention sharpening to assess the impact of architectural choices on focus and interpretability. Results: Our experiments reveal that, in many settings, GATs assign near-uniform attention weights, yielding limited discrimination among neighbors. Attention scores exhibit only moderate correlation with classical edge-importance measures (e.g., betweenness or structural similarity) and often fail to highlight task-critical nodes. Introducing targeted regularization reduces entropy by up to 40%, sharpens attention on high-salience edges, and leads to 3–5% gains in predictive accuracy without added complexity. Temporal action localization aims to localize starting and ending time with action category. Limited by GPU memory, mainstream methods pre-extract features for each video. Therefore, feature quality determines the upper bound of detection performance. In this technical report, we explored classic convolution-based backbones and the recent surge of transformer-based backbones. We found that the transformer-based methods can achieve better classification performance than convolution-based, but they cannot generate accuracy action proposals. In addition, extracting features with larger frame resolution to reduce the loss of spatial information can also effectively improve the performance of temporal action localization. Finally, we achieve 42.42% in terms of mAP on validation set with a single SlowFast feature by a simple combination: BMN+TCANet, which is 1.87% higher than the result of 2020's multi-model ensemble. Finally, we achieve Rank 1st on the CVPR2021 HACS supervised Temporal Action Localization Challenge.

Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) is crucial for securing face recognition systems against presentation attacks. While existing methods primarily focus on spatial features, temporal dynamics indicative of genuine liveness are often overlooked. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhance motion cues for FAS by integrating a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. The CNN extracts frame-level spatial features, while the LSTM models temporal dependencies to capture subtle motion patterns indicative of spoofing attacks. We introduce a motion magnification technique to further amplify these subtle cues, improving the LSTM's ability to distinguish between real and fake faces. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including CASIA-SURF CeFA and Replay-Attack, demonstrate that our CNN-LSTM architecture significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The results highlight the importance of incorporating motion cues for robust FAS, with our approach achieving a 5% improvement in Average Classification Error Rate (ACER) compared to existing spatial-based methods. This research contributes a more effective and robust FAS solution, enhancing the security of face recognition systems. Keywords: Face Anti-Spoofing, CNN, LSTM, Motion Cues, Deep Learning, Presentation Attack Detection.

The pel-recursive computation of 2-D optical flow has been extensively studied in computer vision to estimate motion from image sequences, but it still raises a wealth of issues, such as the treatment of outliers, motion discontinuities and occlusion. It relies on spatio-temporal brightness variations due to motion. Our proposed adaptive regularized approach deals with these issues within a common framework. It relies on the use of a data-driven technique called Mixed Norm (MN) to estimate the best motion vector for a given pixel. In our model, various types of noise can be handled, representing different sources of error. The motion vector estimation takes into consideration local image properties and it results from the minimization of a mixed norm functional with a regularization parameter depending on the kurtosis. This parameter determines the relative importance of the fourth norm and makes the functional convex. The main advantage of the developed procedure is that no knowledge of the noise distribution is necessary. Experiments indicate that this approach provides robust estimates of the optical flow.

Abstract: Time series classification is a fundamental task in fields such as finance, healthcare, and sensor analytics, where accurate analysis of sequential data is critical. This paper investigates the application of deep learning techniques for time series classification, aiming to address limitations of traditional methods that often require manual feature engineering and struggle with complex patterns. We present a comprehensive approach utilizing advanced deep neural network architectures, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), to automatically extract and model temporal features from raw data. Experimental evaluations are conducted on several benchmark datasets, comparing the proposed deep learning models against established classification algorithms. Results demonstrate that deep learning approaches significantly outperform traditional methods in terms of classification accuracy, robustness to noise, and scalability across diverse time series domains. The study further explores the effects of network depth, hyperparameter tuning, and training strategies on model performance. Our findings highlight the potential of deep learning to revolutionize time series analysis by enabling end-to-end learning and adaptability to various application scenarios. This research offers valuable insights for practitioners seeking to leverage deep learning for improved time series classification, and lays the groundwork for future advances in intelligent sequential data processing. Keywords: deep learning, time series classification, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, sequential data, pattern recognition, feature extraction.

Deep learning classifiers have achieved remarkable success in various domains, but their reliability in real-world applications remains a significant concern. This paper addresses the challenge of assessing the robustness and reliability of deep learning classifiers by combining robustness evaluation techniques with the construction of operational profiles. We propose a novel methodology that first evaluates the classifier's performance under various types of input perturbations and adversarial attacks. The resulting robustness metrics are then integrated with operational profiles, which capture the expected distribution of inputs in the target deployment environment. This allows for a more realistic assessment of the classifier's reliability compared to traditional benchmark datasets. Our experiments on image classification tasks demonstrate that this approach provides a more accurate and nuanced understanding of classifier performance, revealing potential failure modes that are not apparent from standard accuracy metrics. The findings highlight the importance of considering both robustness and operational context when deploying deep learning classifiers in safety-critical applications. This work contributes a practical framework for evaluating and improving the reliability of deep learning systems. Keywords: Deep Learning, Reliability, Robustness Evaluation, Operational Profiles, Adversarial Attacks, Machine Learning.

Keypoint localization is a fundamental task in computer vision, crucial for applications such as pose estimation, action recognition, and object tracking. This paper introduces TransPose, a novel keypoint localization framework leveraging the transformer architecture. Unlike traditional convolutional neural networks, TransPose models long-range dependencies between image features, enabling a more holistic understanding of the object's structure. The method employs a transformer encoder to extract global context and a lightweight decoder to predict keypoint locations. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including COCO and MPII, demonstrate that TransPose achieves state-of-the-art performance with fewer parameters and lower computational cost compared to existing methods. The improved accuracy and efficiency highlight the potential of transformer-based models for keypoint localization, offering a promising direction for future research in pose estimation and related computer vision tasks. Keywords: Keypoint Localization, Pose Estimation, Transformer, Computer Vision, Deep Learning.

This research addresses the challenge of optimizing information agent operations in partially-observable environments, where agents lack full visibility of the state space and must rely on local information. The goal is to develop a model that enhances decision-making efficiency and performance. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel modeling framework for local information agents, leveraging a combination of probabilistic reasoning and reinforcement learning techniques. Within this framework, agents assess their immediate surroundings and historical data to predict environmental changes and take informed actions. The model employs a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) to represent the environment's uncertainty and guide the agent's decision-making process. Results/Findings: The proposed framework was tested through a series of simulation experiments in various partially-observable scenarios. Our findings indicate a significant improvement in the agents' decision-making capacity, with enhanced adaptability and reduced error rates compared to traditional models. Furthermore, our approach demonstrated superior performance in terms of convergence speed and resource efficiency, thereby validating its effectiveness. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field of intelligent agent systems by providing a robust solution for navigating and operating in partially-observable environments. The model's improved decision accuracy and operational efficiency have practical implications for applications in dynamic and resource-constrained settings, such as autonomous robotics, network security, and real-time data analysis. Future exploration of multi-agent collaborations within this framework could further expand its applicability and impact. Key Keywords: information agent, partially-observable environments, local information, probabilistic reasoning, reinforcement learning, POMDP, decision-making.

This paper addresses the challenge of merging images in the context of low-level machine vision tasks, where lossless and reversible processing is crucial for maintaining data integrity. The research explores a novel approach to reversible image merging that ensures the original images can be perfectly reconstructed while enhancing the capabilities of various machine vision applications. Methods/Approach: We propose a cutting-edge algorithm that leverages reversible data hiding techniques combined with advanced image transformation methods to achieve lossless image merging. The algorithm is designed to process images with minimal computational overhead, maintaining high efficiency critical for real-time machine vision systems. Key technical mechanisms include bit-plane decomposition and reversible prediction error expansion, which facilitate an exact reconstruction of the merged images. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our reversible image merging approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both merge efficiency and recovery accuracy. The method yields superior results with a minimal storage overhead, proving effective across a range of image resolutions and types. Benchmark comparisons indicate improvements in accuracy and processing speed, validating the robustness of the proposed solution in practical machine vision scenarios. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel solution to the field of low-level machine vision by enabling reversible image merging without data loss. The implications of this study extend to various applications, including surveillance, medical imaging, and real-time image analysis, where maintaining original image quality is paramount. The findings pave the way for further research into reversible image processing methods, enhancing the performance and capabilities of automated vision systems. Keywords: reversible image merging, low-level machine vision, lossless processing, data hiding, image transformation, computational efficiency.

Nghiên cứu cũng xem xét các yếu tố về trải nghiệm người dùng (UX) và thiết kế giao diện người dùng (UI) để tạo ra một sản phẩm thân thiện và dễ tiếp cận. This paper proposes a novel Spatially and Temporally Efficient Non-local Attention Network (STEN) for video-based person re-identification, aiming to improve the accuracy and efficiency of existing methods. The objective is to develop a framework that can effectively capture spatial and temporal cues from video sequences to identify individuals across different cameras. Our approach utilizes a non-local attention mechanism to model long-range dependencies between frames, combined with a spatially efficient module to reduce computational costs. Experimental results demonstrate that our STEN network achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and speed. The key findings indicate that our network can efficiently handle large-scale video data and provide robust re-identification results. The contributions of this research lie in its ability to balance spatial and temporal efficiency, making it suitable for real-world applications. The proposed STEN network has significant implications for surveillance, security, and smart city applications, where fast and accurate person re-identification is crucial. Key keywords: person re-identification, non-local attention, video-based, spatially efficient, temporally efficient, deep learning.

The growing demand for energy-efficient solutions in Internet of Things (IoT) applications has driven interest in sustainable power sources, such as energy harvesting sensors. This research addresses the challenge of optimizing the configuration of these sensors to operate efficiently and autonomously in dynamic environments. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative approach that employs reinforcement learning, a machine learning paradigm well-suited for adaptive control processes, to enhance the scaling configuration of energy harvesting sensors. Our method leverages a reinforcement learning algorithm to dynamically adjust sensor settings, ensuring optimal energy efficiency while maintaining necessary operational performance. Results/Findings: Through extensive simulations and real-world tests, our reinforcement learning-based approach demonstrated a significant improvement in energy efficiency compared to traditional fixed configuration strategies. The findings reveal a remarkable ability to adapt to varying energy conditions and operational demands, thereby prolonging sensor lifespan and reducing the need for manual intervention. Conclusion/Implications: This study contributes to the field of IoT by introducing a scalable and autonomous configuration method for energy harvesting sensors, enhancing their viability in sustainable and self-sufficient deployment. The novel application of reinforcement learning in this context not only offers immediate benefits in terms of energy savings but also sets a precedent for future research in adaptive sensor configurations. Key applications of this research can be seen in smart city infrastructures, environmental monitoring, and various remote sensing applications. Keywords: energy harvesting, sensors, reinforcement learning, IoT, adaptive control, sustainable power, sensor configuration.

Deep learning is a broad set of techniques that uses multiple layers of representation to automatically learn relevant features directly from structured data. Recently, such techniques have yielded record-breaking results on a diverse set of difficult machine learning tasks in computer vision, speech recognition, and natural language processing. Despite the enormous success of deep learning, relatively little is understood theoretically about why these techniques are so successful at feature learning and compression. Here, we show that deep learning is intimately related to one of the most important and successful techniques in theoretical physics, the renormalization group (RG). RG is an iterative coarse-graining scheme that allows for the extraction of relevant features (i.e. operators) as a physical system is examined at different length scales. We construct an exact mapping from the variational renormalization group, first introduced by Kadanoff, and deep learning architectures based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs). We illustrate these ideas using the nearest-neighbor Ising Model in one and two-dimensions. Our results suggests that deep learning algorithms may be employing a generalized RG-like scheme to learn relevant features from data.

This paper proposes Onion-Peel Networks, a novel deep learning approach for video completion tasks. The objective is to develop an effective method for filling in missing regions in videos, which is a crucial problem in various applications such as video editing, restoration, and surveillance. Our approach utilizes a multi-scale architecture, inspired by the concept of onion peels, to progressively refine the completion results. The Onion-Peel Network employs a combination of convolutional and recurrent neural networks to capture both spatial and temporal information in videos. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of completion quality and efficiency. The Onion-Peel Network achieves significant improvements in handling complex scenes, large missing regions, and diverse video content. Our research contributes to the development of advanced video completion techniques, with potential applications in computer vision, video processing, and artificial intelligence. Key keywords: video completion, deep learning, Onion-Peel Networks, computer vision, video processing.

Causal discovery from time-series data is a critical challenge in understanding complex systems, with applications ranging from healthcare to finance. Traditional methods often struggle with scalability and computational efficiency, especially when dealing with large datasets. This paper introduces *Amortized Causal Discovery* (ACD), a novel framework that leverages deep learning to infer causal graphs from time-series data efficiently. The proposed approach employs a neural network-based model trained to predict causal relationships across diverse datasets, enabling generalization to unseen data without requiring retraining. By amortizing the inference process, ACD significantly reduces computational overhead compared to traditional causal discovery methods. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that ACD achieves competitive accuracy in identifying causal structures while being orders of magnitude faster than existing techniques. The framework also incorporates robustness to noise and missing data, making it suitable for practical applications. This research contributes a scalable and efficient solution to causal discovery, paving the way for real-time analysis of dynamic systems. The implications of this work extend to domains such as predictive modeling, decision-making, and system diagnostics, where understanding causal relationships is paramount. **Keywords**: causal discovery, time-series data, deep learning, neural networks, amortized inference, causal graphs.

Objective: GraphiT addresses the challenge of integrating explicit graph structure into transformer architectures for graph representation learning. While transformers excel at capturing long-range dependencies, they lack built-in mechanisms to leverage the relational information intrinsic to graph data. Methods/Approach: We introduce GraphiT, a novel transformer variant that encodes graph topology through an adjacency-aware attention bias and learnable path encodings. GraphiT augments standard self-attention with structural masks derived from node neighborhoods and shortest-path distances, enabling the model to attend preferentially to connected nodes. To preserve efficiency, we adopt sparse attention kernels and hierarchical pooling layers that scale linearly with graph size. Results/Findings: We evaluate GraphiT on six benchmark datasets spanning node classification, graph classification, and molecular property prediction. Across all tasks, GraphiT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines—including Graph Convolutional Networks, GraphSAGE, and existing graph transformer models—achieving up to 4.3% relative improvement in accuracy and reducing training time by 20% on large graphs. Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of adjacency bias and path encoding, demonstrating robust performance even on graphs with diverse structural patterns. Conclusion/Implications: By seamlessly combining structural priors with global attention, GraphiT advances the expressiveness and scalability of graph transformers. Its flexible design facilitates adaptation to domains such as social network analysis, cheminformatics, and recommendation systems, paving the way for more powerful and interpretable graph-based learning models. Keywords: GraphiT, graph transformer, structural encoding, attention bias, graph representation learning, sparse attention.

This paper introduces a novel approach to dense multi-view 3D reconstruction that circumvents the necessity for explicit dense correspondences between images. Our method leverages differentiable rendering and a learned implicit surface representation to directly optimize the 3D geometry from multi-view images. Unlike traditional methods that rely on feature matching and triangulation, we employ a neural network to learn a signed distance function (SDF) representing the scene geometry. The network is trained by minimizing a photometric loss between the rendered images and the input images, as well as a regularization term to ensure surface smoothness and accurate SDF values. This allows for robust reconstruction even in the presence of challenging conditions such as texture-less regions, occlusions, and lighting variations. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves comparable or superior reconstruction quality compared to state-of-the-art methods while avoiding the computationally expensive and often unreliable step of dense correspondence estimation. The proposed technique offers a promising alternative for accurate and efficient 3D reconstruction, enabling applications in robotics, augmented reality, and virtual reality. Keywords: 3D reconstruction, multi-view stereo, differentiable rendering, implicit surfaces, signed distance function, neural networks.

Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to image processing by introducing Weighted Nonlocal Total Variation (WNLTV), a method aimed at enhancing image denoising and restoration. Traditional total variation (TV) methods are effective in preserving edges, but often fail to capture nonlocal similarities and can result in loss of fine details. Our proposed WNLTV model integrates adaptive weighting schemes into the nonlocal total variation framework, allowing for more accurate modeling of pixel relationships over larger spatial neighborhoods. The method employs a similarity-based weighting function to selectively enforce regularization based on both spatial distance and intensity similarity, improving the preservation of textures and subtle structures. Extensive experiments were conducted on both synthetic and real images to assess the performance of the proposed technique. Results demonstrate that WNLTV consistently outperforms classic local and nonlocal TV methods in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and visual quality, especially in challenging noise and artifact scenarios. This research highlights the effectiveness of adaptive, weighted regularization in nonlocal frameworks, providing a valuable tool for various image processing applications, including medical imaging, photography enhancement, and remote sensing. Keywords: image processing, total variation, nonlocal methods, image denoising, weighted regularization, image restoration.

Understanding causal relationships in complex systems is a fundamental challenge in information technology, with significant implications for fields such as healthcare, finance, and recommendation systems. This paper introduces Graph Intervention Networks (GIN), a novel framework for causal effect estimation that leverages the structural properties of graph-based models to identify, represent, and quantify causal dependencies among variables. Our approach utilizes a combination of graph neural networks and intervention modeling techniques to learn the underlying causal graph and estimate treatment effects from observational and experimental data. Through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, we demonstrate that GIN outperforms existing baseline methods in accuracy and robustness, particularly in the presence of confounders and non-linear relationships. The results reveal that our method provides improved interpretability and predictive performance for counterfactual inference tasks. This research highlights the potential of integrating graph-based learning with intervention analysis to advance causal inference methodologies, enabling more informed decision-making in complex IT systems. Key keywords: causal inference, graph neural networks, intervention, treatment effect estimation, counterfactual analysis, deep learning.

The objective of this research is to address the challenge of 3D object detection in autonomous systems by developing an innovative fusion method that integrates Camera and LiDAR data, known as CLOCs (Camera-LiDAR Object Candidates Fusion). Traditional 3D object detection approaches often rely on either purely monocular vision or LiDAR point cloud data, each having its limitations in terms of depth accuracy and object detection reliability. The CLOCs method leverages the complementary strengths of both sensing modalities by proposing a novel fusion framework that enhances detection accuracy and robustness. Our approach involves generating object candidates independently from camera images and LiDAR scans, followed by a strategic fusion stage that optimizes candidate selection and validation through a deep neural network model. The experimental results demonstrate that the CLOCs fusion algorithm significantly outperforms single modality methods, achieving notable improvements in detection accuracy and precision, particularly in complex environments and under various lighting conditions. This research contributes to the field by offering a scalable and efficient 3D object detection framework that can be readily integrated into existing autonomous systems, potentially enhancing their environmental perception and decision-making capabilities. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as powerful platforms for real-time object detection in diverse applications such as surveillance, environmental monitoring, and disaster response. However, aerial imagery is often challenged by varying altitudes, dynamic backgrounds, scale changes, and environmental nuisances that negatively impact detection performance. This paper introduces a novel deep nuisance disentanglement approach to enhance robust object detection from UAV-acquired images. Our method integrates a dual-branch deep neural network designed to separately encode critical object semantics and disentangle complex nuisance factors such as illumination variations, background motion, and atmospheric distortions. To train and validate the proposed architecture, we compile a comprehensive UAV dataset that captures a wide range of nuisance scenarios. Comparative experiments demonstrate significant improvements in detection accuracy and robustness over state-of-the-art models, especially under challenging conditions. Our results highlight reduced false positives, better localization, and improved adaptation across diverse flight environments. The proposed nuisance disentanglement framework sets a new benchmark for UAV object detection, offering valuable insights for deploying reliable and versatile vision systems in real-world aerial applications. Key keywords: UAV, object detection, deep learning, nuisance disentanglement, aerial imagery, robust vision systems.

This paper presents a novel dynamic programming algorithm designed to address the dual challenges of informative measurements and near-optimal path-planning in complex environments. The objective is to optimize the acquisition of critical data while minimizing resource expenditure, such as time or energy, during navigation. The proposed approach integrates a dynamic programming framework with probabilistic models to evaluate and prioritize measurement points based on their informational value. By leveraging recursive optimization techniques, the algorithm efficiently computes paths that balance exploration and exploitation, ensuring both high-quality data collection and near-optimal traversal. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm’s superior performance compared to traditional methods, achieving significant improvements in measurement accuracy and path efficiency across various simulated and real-world scenarios. The findings highlight the algorithm’s potential for applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and environmental monitoring, where informed decision-making and resource-efficient navigation are critical. This work contributes a scalable and adaptable solution to the growing demand for intelligent systems capable of operating in dynamic and uncertain environments. **Keywords**: dynamic programming, informative measurements, path-planning, optimization, autonomous systems, probabilistic models.

Recent trends of incorporating attention mechanisms in vision have led researchers to reconsider the supremacy of convolutional layers as a primary building block. Beyond helping CNNs to handle long-range dependencies, Ramachandran et al. (2019) showed that attention can completely replace convolution and achieve state-of-the-art performance on vision tasks. This raises the question: do learned attention layers operate similarly to convolutional layers? This work provides evidence that attention layers can perform convolution and, indeed, they often learn to do so in practice. Specifically, we prove that a multi-head self-attention layer with sufficient number of heads is at least as expressive as any convolutional layer. Our numerical experiments then show that self-attention layers attend to pixel-grid patterns similarly to CNN layers, corroborating our analysis. Our code is publicly available.

The objective of this research is to address the challenge of color-accurate reproduction in High Dynamic Range (HDR) images through the development of an advanced gamut-mapping framework. Recognizing the limitations of existing methods that often lead to color distortion and loss of detail in HDR rendering, this study proposes a novel approach that integrates enhanced tone-mapping techniques with a sophisticated color correction model to ensure fidelity in chromatic reproduction across various display technologies. The framework employs an adaptive algorithm that dynamically adjusts the color gamut of HDR images, aligning it with the target display's capabilities while maintaining visual integrity and perceptual accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms conventional gamut-mapping strategies, exhibiting significant improvements in maintaining color accuracy and contrast in both simulated environments and real-world applications. The findings highlight the potential of the proposed framework to enhance HDR content delivery in diverse fields such as digital photography, cinematic production, and virtual reality. This research contributes a robust solution to the field of image processing, setting a new benchmark for color reproduction in HDR imaging. Key innovations include the integration of dynamic color correction with adaptive tone mapping, offering a scalable and efficient tool for rendering HDR images. Keywords: HDR images, gamut mapping, color reproduction, tone mapping, image processing.

Human action recognition is pivotal in a multitude of applications ranging from surveillance systems to human-computer interaction. However, accurately identifying actions in complex events remains a significant challenge due to the dynamic interactions and occlusions characteristic of such environments. This research addresses the problem by introducing a novel approach to human action recognition based on group-skeleton information. Methods/Approach: This study presents a unique group-skeleton-based framework that leverages the structural relationship of multiple human figures within a scene to enhance action recognition accuracy. The approach involves extracting and modeling group skeleton data using a state-of-the-art pose estimation algorithm, which captures intricate interrelationships between actors. This structural data is then processed using a tailored deep learning model optimized for group dynamics. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed group-skeleton-based approach significantly outperforms traditional single-skeleton methods, especially in scenarios characterized by complex interactions. Our method achieved an improvement in recognition accuracy across multiple benchmark datasets with diverse action categories, highlighting its robustness and generalization capabilities. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field of human action recognition by offering a robust solution that effectively handles the intricacies of complex events through group skeleton analysis. The findings underline the potential of leveraging group dynamics for more accurate recognition and pave the way for applications in enhanced surveillance systems, improved interactive system designs, and advanced video content analysis. Key keywords include human action recognition, group skeleton, pose estimation, deep learning, and complex events.

Monocular 3D object detection is a challenging task in computer vision, crucial for applications like autonomous driving and robotics. This paper introduces FCOS3D, a novel, fully convolutional, one-stage approach for monocular 3D object detection. Departing from previous anchor-based methods, FCOS3D leverages a per-pixel prediction strategy, directly regressing 3D bounding box parameters from each pixel on the feature map. This significantly reduces the number of design hyperparameters and simplifies the training process. Furthermore, we propose a centerness-based weighting strategy to suppress low-quality predictions and improve localization accuracy. Extensive experiments on the KITTI benchmark demonstrate that FCOS3D achieves state-of-the-art performance among monocular 3D object detectors, surpassing existing methods in both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed approach offers a simpler, more effective solution for monocular 3D object detection, paving the way for real-time and resource-constrained applications. Keywords: Monocular 3D Object Detection, One-Stage Detector, Fully Convolutional Network, Autonomous Driving, Computer Vision.

The objective is to generate diverse and high-quality Yuru-Chara characters, which are popular in Japanese culture, by leveraging the strengths of GANs in image generation and clustering methods to enhance data utilization. Our approach employs a custom GAN architecture that incorporates clustering to better capture the underlying patterns in the limited dataset, allowing for more efficient training and improved generation capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that YuruGAN outperforms existing methods in generating Yuru-Chara characters, both in terms of visual quality and diversity. The key findings highlight the potential of combining GANs with clustering techniques for small dataset scenarios, contributing to the advancement of generative modeling in character design and related applications. This research has significant implications for the field of computer-generated imagery and character design, offering a novel solution for generating unique and engaging characters with minimal data requirements. Key keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, GANs, Clustering, Small Dataset, Yuru-Chara, Character Generation, Computer-Generated Imagery.

Accurate traffic forecasting is crucial for intelligent transportation systems, yet its performance heavily relies on the availability and quality of historical data. This paper investigates the effectiveness of transfer learning (TL) and online learning (OL) techniques for traffic forecasting under varying data availability scenarios. We evaluate different TL strategies for adapting models trained on data-rich source domains to data-scarce target domains. Furthermore, we explore OL algorithms to continuously update forecasting models as new traffic data becomes available, addressing non-stationary traffic patterns. Our results demonstrate that TL can significantly improve forecasting accuracy in data-scarce scenarios, but careful selection of source domains and TL methods is crucial to avoid negative transfer. OL techniques, particularly those employing adaptive learning rates, effectively capture evolving traffic dynamics and outperform static models. A comparative analysis reveals the trade-offs between TL and OL under different data conditions, highlighting potential pitfalls and providing guidelines for their effective deployment. This work contributes to a better understanding of how to leverage TL and OL to enhance traffic forecasting accuracy and robustness in real-world transportation networks. Belief Propagation has been widely used for marginal inference, however it is slow on problems with large-domain variables and high-order factors. Previous work provides useful approximations to facilitate inference on such models, but lacks important anytime properties such as: 1) providing accurate and consistent marginals when stopped early, 2) improving the approximation when run longer, and 3) converging to the fixed point of BP. To this end, we propose a message passing algorithm that works on sparse (partially instantiated) domains, and converges to consistent marginals using dynamic message scheduling. The algorithm grows the sparse domains incrementally, selecting the next value to add using prioritization schemes based on the gradients of the marginal inference objective. Our experiments demonstrate local anytime consistency and fast convergence, providing significant speedups over BP to obtain low-error marginals: up to 25 times on grid models, and up to 6 times on a real-world natural language processing task.

We study a fundamental problem in Bayesian learning, where the goal is to select a set of data sources with minimum cost while achieving a certain learning performance based on the data streams provided by the selected data sources. First, we show that the data source selection problem for Bayesian learning is NP-hard. We then show that the data source selection problem can be transformed into an instance of the submodular set covering problem studied in the literature, and provide a standard greedy algorithm to solve the data source selection problem with provable performance guarantees. Next, we propose a fast greedy algorithm that improves the running times of the standard greedy algorithm, while achieving performance guarantees that are comparable to those of the standard greedy algorithm. The fast greedy algorithm can also be applied to solve the general submodular set covering problem with performance guarantees. Finally, we validate the theoretical results using numerical examples, and show that the greedy algorithms work well in practice.

A novel locally statistical active contour model (ACM) for image segmentation in the presence of intensity inhomogeneity is presented in this paper. The inhomogeneous objects are modeled as Gaussian distributions of different means and variances, and a moving window is used to map the original image into another domain, where the intensity distributions of inhomogeneous objects are still Gaussian but are better separated. The means of the Gaussian distributions in the transformed domain can be adaptively estimated by multiplying a bias field with the original signal within the window. A statistical energy functional is then defined for each local region, which combines the bias field, the level set function, and the constant approximating the true signal of the corresponding object. Experiments on both synthetic and real images demonstrate the superiority of our proposed algorithm to state-of-the-art and representative methods.

Vật liệu có cơ tính bi ến thiên (Functionally Graded Materials - FGM) là loại vật liệu không đ ồng nh ất, đẳng hướng có tính ch ất cơ h ọc thay đ ổi trơn, liên t ục theo chi ều dày c ủa tấm.
