Polyphenol là một nhóm hợp chất tự nhiên có trong thực vật với đặc tính kháng khuẩn và chống ôxy hóa, mang lại nhiều tiềm năng ứng dụng trong sản xuất dược phẩm và nông nghiệp. Với mục đích tách chiết và thu nhận hàm lượng hợp chất polyphenol cao từ hạt cau (Areca catechu L.), nghiên cứu đã sử dụng phương pháp đáp ứng bề mặt để đánh giá ảnh hưởng của một số yếu tố kỹ thuật như nồng độ dung môi (X1), tỷ lệ dung môi/nguyên liệu (DM/NL) (v/w) (X2) và thời gian ngâm (giờ) (X3) đến hàm lượng hợp chất polyphenol (Y) được trích ly trong hạt cau. Kết quả nghiên cứu thu được mô hình mô tả tách chiết hợp chất polyphenol từ hạt cau bằng hàm mục tiêu Y = 80,64 + 3,10X1 - 1,27X3 - 6,00X12 - 3,66X22 - 5,07X32. Dựa vào hàm mục tiêu, kết quả hàm lượng polyphenol được thu nhận cao nhất là 80,72 mg GAE/g nguyên liệu, với các điều kiện tối ưu như sau: nồng độ dung môi ethanol 55%, tỷ lệ ngâm DM/NL (v/w) 35/1 và thời gian ngâm 2 giờ. Kết quả hàm lượng polyphenol của thực nghiệm không có sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thống kê so với kết quả dự đoán của mô hình. Kết quả này là tiền đề cho quy trình thu nhận hợp chất polyphenol từ hạt cau ứng dụng kháng khuẩn trong nông nghiệp và y dược.

Non-stationary time series prediction presents a significant challenge due to its evolving spectral characteristics. This paper introduces Spectral Evolution Analysis Feature Extraction (SAFE), a novel approach for enhancing prediction accuracy in such time series. SAFE leverages a sliding window Fourier transform to capture temporal variations in the frequency domain, extracting key features representing the spectral evolution. These features are then used as input to a predictive model. The proposed method is evaluated on several real-world non-stationary datasets, including financial markets and climate data. Results demonstrate that SAFE outperforms traditional time-domain feature extraction methods and established frequency-domain techniques, achieving significant improvements in prediction accuracy and robustness. The findings suggest that incorporating spectral evolution features effectively captures the dynamic nature of non-stationary time series, leading to more accurate and reliable predictions. Keywords: time series, non-stationary, spectral analysis, feature extraction, prediction, Fourier transform.

Để đáp ứng nhu cầu này, các tạp chí khoa học cần phải tuân thủ các tiêu chuẩn nghiêm ngặt để đảm bảo chất lượng và uy tín. Tiêu chuẩn ACI (Association for Computing Machinery) là một trong những tiêu chuẩn được công nhận quốc tế về xây dựng tạp chí khoa học. Theo tiêu chuẩn này, tạp chí khoa học cần phải đáp ứng các yêu cầu về nội dung, hình thức và quy trình xuất bản. Một số yêu cầu chính của tiêu chuẩn ACI bao gồm: - Nội dung: Tạp chí khoa học cần phải có nội dung liên quan đến lĩnh vực khoa học, công nghệ và sáng tạo. - Hình thức: Tạp chí khoa học cần phải có hình thức trình bày rõ ràng, dễ hiểu và dễ đọc. - Quy trình xuất bản: Tạp chí khoa học cần phải có quy trình xuất bản nghiêm ngặt, bao gồm đánh giá chất lượng bài viết, kiểm tra và chỉnh sửa trước khi xuất bản. Để xây dựng tạp chí khoa học theo tiêu chuẩn ACI, các tạp chí cần phải thực hiện các bước sau: - Xác định mục tiêu và đối tượng độc giả. - Xây dựng quy trình xuất bản nghiêm ngặt. - Đánh giá chất lượng bài viết và kiểm tra trước khi xuất bản. - Cung cấp thông tin và hướng dẫn cho các tác giả và độc giả. Bằng cách tuân thủ tiêu chuẩn ACI, các tạp chí khoa học ở Việt Nam có thể nâng cao chất lượng và uy tín, đáp ứng nhu cầu của cộng đồng khoa học và đóng góp vào sự phát triển của khoa học và công nghệ.

The increasing demand for artificial intelligence to learn efficiently from limited data presents a significant challenge in many real-world applications. This paper addresses the problem of few-shot learning in reinforcement learning (RL) frameworks, focusing on developing a method that allows for effective extrapolation beyond the initial data set. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel approach called Structured MaxEnt RL, which integrates principles from maximum entropy reinforcement learning to enhance few-shot extrapolation capabilities. By leveraging structured exploration strategies, our method systematically expands its knowledge base under scarce sample settings. This approach allows the model to generalize with improved precision by effectively utilizing available data. Results/Findings: Extensive experiments demonstrate that Structured MaxEnt RL outperforms traditional RL techniques in few-shot scenarios across a variety of benchmark environments. Our findings reveal a marked improvement in extrapolative accuracy and efficiency, showing significant advances in tasks that require generalization beyond seen data. Comparative analysis illustrates that our approach reduces the reliance on extensive training data while maintaining high-performance levels. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a significant step forward in the field of RL by highlighting that multiple solutions are necessary for effective learning in limited data contexts. The Structured MaxEnt RL model offers promising applications in environments where rapid learning and adaptation are required, such as robotics, autonomous systems, and real-time decision-making processes. By enhancing the ability to extrapolate in few-shot settings, this study paves the way for more robust, adaptive artificial intelligence systems that can navigate complex, dynamic environments efficiently. Keywords: Few-shot learning, Reinforcement Learning, MaxEnt RL, Extrapolation, Structured Exploration, Artificial Intelligence.

Several imaging applications (vessels, retina, plant roots, road networks from satellites) require the accurate segmentation of thin structures for subsequent analysis. Discontinuities (gaps) in the extracted foreground may hinder down-stream image-based analysis of biomarkers, organ structure and topology. In this paper, we propose a general post-processing technique to recover such gaps in large-scale segmentation masks. We cast this problem as a blind inpainting task, where the regions of missing lines in the segmentation masks are not known to the algorithm, which we solve with an adversarially trained neural network. One challenge of using large images is the memory capacity of current GPUs. The typical approach of dividing a large image into smaller patches to train the network does not guarantee global coherence of the reconstructed image that preserves structure and topology. We use adversarial training and reinforcement learning (Policy Gradient) to endow the model with both global context and local details. We evaluate our method in several datasets in medical imaging, plant science, and remote sensing. Our experiments demonstrate that our model produces the most realistic and complete inpainted results, outperforming other approaches. In a dedicated study on plant roots we find that our approach is also comparable to human performance. Implementation available at \url.

Tổng hợp 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) từ cellulose đang trở thành một trong những chủ đề được quan tâm trong lĩnh vực hóa học và công nghệ sinh học. Trong nghiên cứu mới đây, các nhà khoa học đã phát triển một phương pháp tổng hợp HMF từ cellulose sử dụng xúc tác silica-amorphous carbon và choline chloride. Phương pháp này bao gồm ba bước chính: đầu tiên, cellulose được thủy phân thành glucose; sau đó, glucose được chuyển đổi thành HMF bằng xúc tác của silica-amorphous carbon và choline chloride; cuối cùng, HMF được thu thập và tinh chế. Phương pháp này có nhiều ưu điểm, bao gồm độ bền cao, tính chọn lọc tốt và khả năng tái sử dụng xúc tác. HMF là một hợp chất quan trọng trong sản xuất nhiên liệu sinh học, hóa chất và vật liệu mới. Nghiên cứu này mở ra một hướng mới trong việc tổng hợp HMF từ cellulose, giúp giảm thiểu chi phí và tăng hiệu suất sản xuất. Đây là một bước tiến quan trọng trong việc phát triển công nghệ sinh học và hóa học bền vững.

Vật liệu composite Fe-O-C, được chế tạo thông qua quá trình nhiệt phân muối sắt (II) oxalat ngậm nước trong môi trường khí trơ, thể hiện cấu trúc độc đáo với các hạt nano oxit sắt phân tán trong nền carbon vô định hình. Quá trình này tạo ra vật liệu có diện tích bề mặt lớn và độ xốp cao, mở ra tiềm năng ứng dụng trong nhiều lĩnh vực như xúc tác, hấp phụ và lưu trữ năng lượng. Các tính chất từ tính của vật liệu có thể điều chỉnh thông qua việc kiểm soát kích thước hạt oxit sắt và tỷ lệ thành phần. Nghiên cứu sâu hơn về cấu trúc vi mô và các tính chất vật lý khác nhau, bao gồm tính chất điện và hóa học, cho thấy vật liệu composite Fe-O-C hứa hẹn là một vật liệu chức năng đa năng, có thể được tối ưu hóa cho các ứng dụng cụ thể bằng cách điều chỉnh các thông số chế tạo.

This research addresses the challenge of optimizing neural network architectures specifically tailored for mobile platforms, where computational and energy efficiency are critical. Traditional methods often overlook the unique constraints imposed by mobile devices, leading to suboptimal performance and battery consumption. Methods: We propose MnasNet, a novel platform-aware neural architecture search (NAS) framework that integrates reinforcement learning with performance prediction models to generate efficient mobile-specific network architectures. The NAS process evaluates possible configurations by forecasting their hardware performance metrics and selects the architecture that optimally balances accuracy and resource consumption on mobile processors. Results: Our experiments demonstrate that MnasNet significantly outperforms existing mobile architectures by achieving state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing computational cost. In validation tests, MnasNet delivers up to 30% faster inference speeds with equivalent accuracy compared to alternative models like MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNet. Conclusion: MnasNet represents a noteworthy advance in mobile AI development by offering a systematic approach to design efficient and high-performing neural networks specifically for the constraints of mobile devices. This research not only contributes to reduced latency and improved energy efficiency but also facilitates the broader deployment of sophisticated AI applications in mobile environments. Key potential applications include real-time image processing and augmented reality. Keywords: neural architecture search, mobile AI, MnasNet, platform-aware optimization, reinforcement learning, computational efficiency, mobile devices.

Khảo sát người tiêu dùng là một phần quan trọng trong các tranh chấp về nhãn hiệu. Quá trình này giúp xác định ý kiến và thái độ của người tiêu dùng đối với nhãn hiệu, sản phẩm hoặc dịch vụ liên quan. Thông qua khảo sát, các bên liên quan có thể thu thập thông tin cần thiết để xây dựng chiến lược marketing hiệu quả, tăng cường nhận thức và lòng trung thành của khách hàng. Khảo sát người tiêu dùng trong các tranh chấp về nhãn hiệu giúp xác định: - Ý kiến và thái độ của người tiêu dùng đối với nhãn hiệu, sản phẩm hoặc dịch vụ liên quan. - Sự nhận biết và nhận thức của người tiêu dùng về nhãn hiệu. - Sự khác biệt giữa người tiêu dùng và các bên liên quan về nhãn hiệu. - Các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến quyết định mua hàng của người tiêu dùng. This paper introduces Dynamic Filter Networks as a novel approach to enhance the adaptability and efficiency of neural networks in processing varying input types and complexities. Traditional neural network architectures utilize static filters which can limit their responsiveness to diverse input data. Methods/Approach: Our approach involves the design of a dynamic filtering mechanism within convolutional layers that adjusts in real-time to the specific characteristics of the input data. This is achieved through the integration of a parameterized module that outputs filter coefficients based on the input features, allowing the model to dynamically adapt its filtering process. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that Dynamic Filter Networks outperform conventional static-filter models across various benchmarks, particularly in tasks involving heterogeneous data such as variable resolution image classification and dynamic object detection. The proposed architecture shows significant improvements in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, reducing unnecessary operations through adaptive filtering. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Dynamic Filter Networks presents a significant advancement in neural network architecture by exploiting real-time adaptability of network parameters, which can lead to improved performance across a wide array of applications. This research contributes a versatile and efficient model framework that can be readily implemented in domains requiring variable processing capabilities, such as mobile computing, real-time analytics, and autonomous systems. Key Keywords: Dynamic filtering, neural networks, adaptive architectures, convolutional layers, real-time processing.

Chính sách hỗ trợ tưới tiên tiến và tiết kiệm nước trên vùng đất chuyển đổi từ lúa sang các cây trồng nhằm mục đích nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng nước trong nông nghiệp, đồng thời khuyến khích nông dân chuyển đổi cơ cấu cây trồng phù hợp với điều kiện khí hậu và thị trường. Chính sách này bao gồm các biện pháp như cung cấp công nghệ tưới hiện đại, đào tạo kỹ thuật cho nông dân, và hỗ trợ tài chính để giảm bớt gánh nặng đầu tư ban đầu. Việc áp dụng các hệ thống tưới tiết kiệm nước không chỉ giúp tăng năng suất cây trồng mà còn bảo vệ nguồn nước, góp phần vào phát triển bền vững và thích ứng với biến đổi khí hậu. Chính sách này được kỳ vọng sẽ tạo ra những thay đổi tích cực trong sản xuất nông nghiệp, nâng cao đời sống của người dân và bảo vệ môi trường.

Many computer vision tasks address the problem of scene understanding and are naturally interrelated e.g. object classification, detection, scene segmentation, depth estimation, etc. We show that we can leverage the inherent relationships among collections of tasks, as they are trained jointly, supervising each other through their known relationships via consistency losses. Furthermore, explicitly utilizing the relationships between tasks allows improving their performance while dramatically reducing the need for labeled data, and allows training with additional unsupervised or simulated data. We demonstrate a distributed joint training algorithm with task-level parallelism, which affords a high degree of asynchronicity and robustness. This allows learning across multiple tasks, or with large amounts of input data, at scale. We demonstrate our framework on subsets of the following collection of tasks: depth and normal prediction, semantic segmentation, 3D motion and ego-motion estimation, and object tracking and 3D detection in point clouds. We observe improved performance across these tasks, especially in the low-label regime.

When multiple agents learn in a decentralized manner, the environment appears non-stationary from the perspective of an individual agent due to the exploration and learning of the other agents. Recently proposed deep multi-agent reinforcement learning methods have tried to mitigate this non-stationarity by attempting to determine which samples are from other agent exploration or suboptimality and take them less into account during learning. Based on the same philosophy, this paper introduces a decentralized quantile estimator, which aims to improve performance by distinguishing non-stationary samples based on the likelihood of returns. In particular, each agent considers the likelihood that other agent exploration and policy changes are occurring, essentially utilizing the agent's own estimations to weigh the learning rate that should be applied towards the given samples. We introduce a formal method of calculating differences of our return distribution representations and methods for utilizing it to guide updates. We also explore the effect of risk-seeking strategies for adjusting learning over time and propose adaptive risk distortion functions which guides risk sensitivity. Our experiments, on traditional benchmarks and new domains, show our methods are more stable, sample efficient and more likely to converge to a joint optimal policy than previous methods.

Spectral methods have long been fundamental in machine learning, providing powerful tools for dimensionality reduction, clustering, and manifold learning. However, they often struggle with scalability and adaptability to complex data distributions. In contrast, deep learning excels at feature extraction but lacks interpretability and theoretical guarantees. To bridge this gap, we propose Spectral Inference Networks (SIN), a novel framework that unifies spectral learning and deep neural networks to leverage the strengths of both approaches. Our method integrates spectral decomposition techniques within a deep learning architecture, enabling efficient inference of eigenfunctions and low-dimensional representations in an end-to-end manner. By parameterizing spectral components with neural networks, SIN can adaptively learn task-specific embeddings while preserving the mathematical foundations of spectral learning. Additionally, we introduce a regularization mechanism that maintains stability in the learned spectral representations, improving robustness to noisy and high-dimensional data. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SIN achieves state-of-the-art performance in spectral clustering, graph-based learning, and representation learning tasks, surpassing conventional spectral methods and deep learning baselines. These results highlight the effectiveness of combining spectral insights with deep learning for improved generalization and interpretability. Keywords: Spectral Learning, Deep Learning, Eigenfunction Inference, Representation Learning, Spectral Decomposition, Graph-Based Learning.

This paper presents an empirical study of spatial attention mechanisms in deep neural networks, focusing on their effectiveness in enhancing model performance across various computer vision tasks. The objective of this research is to systematically evaluate how different spatial attention designs influence feature extraction, model interpretability, and task-specific accuracy. We conduct extensive experiments using state-of-the-art attention modules, including self-attention and channel-wise attention, integrated into popular architectures such as ResNet and Transformer-based models. Our approach involves benchmarking these mechanisms on standard datasets for image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation. The results demonstrate that spatial attention significantly improves model accuracy, particularly in scenarios requiring fine-grained feature discrimination. Furthermore, we identify key design choices, such as attention granularity and integration strategies, that impact computational efficiency and scalability. The findings highlight the trade-offs between performance gains and resource overhead, providing practical insights for deploying attention mechanisms in resource-constrained environments. This study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on attention mechanisms by offering a comprehensive analysis of their strengths and limitations, paving the way for more efficient and interpretable deep learning models in real-world applications. **Keywords**: spatial attention, deep learning, computer vision, self-attention, feature extraction, model interpretability.

This research addresses the challenge of zero-shot learning in visual speech recognition, aiming to recognize new classes of lip movements without prior exposure during training. This capability is crucial for advancing the adaptability and scalability of automated speech reading systems. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative approach utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate synthetic visual speech data for unseen classes. Our model leverages a generator to create realistic lip movement sequences based on text prompts, while a discriminator ensures these sequences are indistinguishable from authentic visual speech. This GAN-based framework enhances the learning of a zero-shot classifier, enabling it to generalize from visual features of known classes to new, unencountered categories. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our approach significantly improves zero-shot classification accuracy in visual speech recognition tasks compared to traditional methods. Our model demonstrates an ability to bridge the gap between source and target class domains, achieving notable performance on benchmark datasets. Moreover, it outperforms existing zero-shot learning techniques by a margin, showcasing the effectiveness of GAN-generated data in enhancing model robustness and generalization. Conclusion/Implications: The implementation of GANs in zero-shot visual speech recognition presents a promising avenue for developing more flexible and intelligent speech reading systems. Our research contributes to the field by providing an effective platform for extending recognition capabilities to new classes without retraining. This advancement has potential applications in areas such as automated sign language interpretation, human-computer interaction, and assistive technologies for the hearing impaired. Keywords: Zero-shot learning, Visual speech recognition, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Lip movement recognition, Synthetic data generation, Human-computer interaction.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc phân tích các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến mô-men xoắn trung bình và độ nhấp nhô của mô-men xoắn trong động cơ điện. Các biến số chính được xem xét bao gồm góc cực của stato và rôto, cũng như vật liệu chế tạo động cơ. Mục tiêu là xác định mối tương quan giữa các yếu tố này và hiệu suất của động cơ, đặc biệt là khả năng tạo ra mô-men xoắn ổn định và giảm thiểu độ rung. Kết quả nghiên cứu có thể cung cấp thông tin quan trọng cho việc thiết kế và tối ưu hóa động cơ điện, giúp nâng cao hiệu suất và độ bền, đồng thời giảm thiểu tiếng ồn và độ rung trong quá trình vận hành. Việc lựa chọn vật liệu phù hợp và điều chỉnh góc cực có thể mang lại những cải thiện đáng kể về mô-men xoắn và độ ổn định của động cơ.

Bài báo này trình bày một phương pháp điều khiển trượt (Sliding Mode Control - SMC) được thiết kế cho các bộ nghịch lưu (inverter) kết nối lưới điện sử dụng bộ lọc LCL. Mục tiêu là nâng cao chất lượng dòng điện đầu ra và đảm bảo tính ổn định của hệ thống. Thiết kế bộ điều khiển tập trung vào việc giải quyết các vấn đề như ảnh hưởng của bộ lọc LCL, sự biến động của các thông số lưới điện và sự không chắc chắn trong mô hình hệ thống. Phương pháp SMC được chọn vì khả năng mạnh mẽ chống lại các nhiễu loạn và tính bất định. Kết quả mô phỏng cho thấy bộ điều khiển đề xuất có khả năng theo dõi dòng điện tham chiếu một cách chính xác, giảm thiểu sóng hài và duy trì hiệu suất ổn định ngay cả khi có sự thay đổi trong điều kiện hoạt động. Điều này góp phần cải thiện hiệu quả và độ tin cậy của các hệ thống điện phân tán kết nối lưới.

Mục tiêu giáo dục phổ thông hiện nay không chỉ dừng lại ở việc trang bị kiến thức mà còn hướng đến xây dựng môi trường học tập hạnh phúc, nơi học sinh được phát triển toàn diện cả về trí tuệ, thể chất và tinh thần. Thực tiễn giáo dục Việt Nam đang chứng kiến những bước chuyển mình tích cực khi các trường học ngày càng chú trọng đến việc tạo dựng không gian thân thiện, khuyến khích sự sáng tạo và tôn trọng cá tính của từng học sinh. Giáo viên không chỉ là người truyền đạt kiến thức mà còn là người đồng hành, hỗ trợ học sinh trong quá trình tự khám phá và phát triển bản thân. Để đạt được mục tiêu này, cần sự chung tay của cả nhà trường, gia đình và xã hội, cùng nhau xây dựng một hệ thống giáo dục lấy con người làm trung tâm, hướng đến sự hạnh phúc và thành công lâu dài cho thế hệ trẻ.

Nghiên cứu về ảnh hưởng của khoáng cách trồng và lượng bón phân kali đến năng suất và chất lượng cây trồng đã chỉ ra rằng việc điều chỉnh khoảng cách giữa các cây và lượng phân bón kali có tác động đáng kể đến sự phát triển của cây. Kết quả cho thấy, khoảng cách trồng hợp lý không chỉ giúp cây có đủ không gian để phát triển mà còn tối ưu hóa khả năng hấp thụ dinh dưỡng từ đất. Đồng thời, việc bón phân kali với liều lượng phù hợp góp phần nâng cao năng suất và cải thiện chất lượng sản phẩm nông nghiệp. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp những thông tin quý giá cho nông dân trong việc áp dụng các biện pháp canh tác hiệu quả, từ đó nâng cao sản lượng và chất lượng nông sản, đáp ứng nhu cầu thị trường ngày càng cao.

Image editing guided by textual descriptions has gained increasing attention, offering an intuitive way to manipulate images. However, existing methods often struggle with complex edits requiring global scene understanding and struggle to maintain consistency across the entire image. This paper introduces a novel approach, the Global Editing Network (GEN), designed to learn global image manipulations from textual descriptions. GEN employs a transformer-based architecture to fuse textual and visual features, enabling a holistic understanding of the desired edit. A key innovation is the introduction of a spatial attention mechanism that focuses on relevant regions while ensuring consistent changes across the image. We evaluate GEN on a diverse set of image editing tasks, including object replacement, style transfer, and scene modification. Experimental results demonstrate that GEN significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and semantic accuracy, as measured by quantitative metrics and human evaluation. The results showcase GEN's ability to perform complex, globally consistent edits guided solely by textual descriptions, offering a promising direction for future research in text-based image manipulation. Keywords: Image editing, text-guided manipulation, transformers, spatial attention, global consistency, generative models.

The free energy functional has recently been proposed as a variational principle for bounded rational decision-making, since it instantiates a natural trade-off between utility gains and information processing costs that can be axiomatically derived. Here we apply the free energy principle to general decision trees that include both adversarial and stochastic environments. We derive generalized sequential optimality equations that not only include the Bellman optimality equations as a limit case, but also lead to well-known decision-rules such as Expectimax, Minimax and Expectiminimax. We show how these decision-rules can be derived from a single free energy principle that assigns a resource parameter to each node in the decision tree. These resource parameters express a concrete computational cost that can be measured as the amount of samples that are needed from the distribution that belongs to each node. The free energy principle therefore provides the normative basis for generalized optimality equations that account for both adversarial and stochastic environments.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) faces significant challenges in learning efficient and generalizable representations from high-dimensional observations, which are critical for decision-making in complex environments. This paper introduces Masked Contrastive Representation Learning (MCRL), a novel framework designed to enhance representation learning in RL by leveraging masked autoencoding and contrastive learning. MCRL employs a dual-objective approach: it reconstructs masked observations to capture fine-grained details while simultaneously maximizing the similarity between representations of semantically related states through contrastive loss. This combination enables the model to learn robust and task-relevant features while reducing redundancy in the learned representations. Experiments conducted on benchmark RL environments demonstrate that MCRL outperforms existing representation learning methods in terms of sample efficiency, generalization, and final task performance. The framework is particularly effective in sparse-reward and partially observable settings, where high-quality representations are crucial. The results highlight the potential of MCRL to advance RL applications in real-world scenarios, such as robotics and autonomous systems, by improving the quality of learned representations. This work contributes a scalable and versatile approach to representation learning, bridging the gap between unsupervised learning and RL. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Representation Learning, Masked Autoencoding, Contrastive Learning, Sample Efficiency, Generalization.

This paper introduces TempoRL, a novel reinforcement learning framework that focuses on learning the optimal timing for actions in complex environments. Our approach combines traditional reinforcement learning methods with a tempo-based module that predicts the optimal action timing. The results show that TempoRL outperforms existing methods in various environments, demonstrating improved performance and sample efficiency. The key findings highlight the importance of adaptive action timing in reinforcement learning and the potential applications of TempoRL in real-world scenarios, such as robotics and autonomous systems. By learning when to act, TempoRL contributes to the development of more intelligent and adaptive agents, paving the way for future research in reinforcement learning and artificial intelligence. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, action timing, adaptive decision-making, robotics, autonomous systems.

Objective: Accurate county-level forecasting of corn yields is critical for agricultural planning and supply chain management. This study investigates the use of deep Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict annual corn yields at the U.S. county scale by capturing complex temporal dependencies in weather, soil, and historical yield data. Methods: We develop a sequence-to-one LSTM architecture that ingests multiyear time series of climatic variables (temperature, precipitation, solar radiation), soil properties, and past yield records. The model is trained and tested on data spanning 2000–2020 for over 2,000 counties, with hyperparameters tuned via cross-validation. Performance is benchmarked against conventional machine learning baselines, including Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, and feedforward neural networks. Results: The LSTM model achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 3.2 bushels/acre and a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.87, outperforming the best baseline by 15% in MAE reduction and 0.10 in R² improvement. Ablation studies show that integrating seasonal weather forecasts and soil moisture indices contributes to a 7% additional reduction in error. Temporal attention mechanisms further enhance interpretability by highlighting key growth-period influences. Conclusion: Deep LSTM networks provide a robust framework for county-level corn yield prediction, offering policymakers and agribusiness stakeholders high-resolution, data-driven insights. The proposed approach facilitates early-season decision making and resource allocation, and can be extended to other crops and regions. Keywords: corn yield prediction, Long Short-Term Memory, time-series forecasting, precision agriculture, deep learning, county-level modeling

Single-shot object detection has gained significant attention due to its efficiency in real-time applications. However, achieving high accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency remains a challenge, particularly in handling scale variations and complex backgrounds. This paper introduces the Feature Selective Anchor-Free (FSAF) module, a novel approach designed to enhance the performance of single-shot object detectors. The FSAF module operates by dynamically selecting optimal feature levels for each object instance, eliminating the need for predefined anchor boxes and reducing computational overhead. We integrate the FSAF module into a state-of-the-art single-shot detection framework and evaluate its performance on benchmark datasets, including COCO and PASCAL VOC. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior detection accuracy compared to existing anchor-based and anchor-free approaches, with significant improvements in handling small and occluded objects. The FSAF module also exhibits robustness across diverse object scales and complex scenes, making it a promising solution for real-world applications. This work contributes to advancing single-shot object detection by introducing a lightweight, efficient, and scalable module that bridges the gap between accuracy and computational efficiency. **Keywords**: Single-shot object detection, anchor-free, feature selection, real-time detection, scale variation, computational efficiency.

This paper presents a novel approach to learning invariant representations by leveraging local transformations. The objective is to develop a framework that enables deep neural networks to learn features that are robust to various transformations, such as rotations, scaling, and translations. Our method utilizes a transformation-based regularization technique, which encourages the network to learn representations that are invariant to local transformations. We employ a combination of convolutional neural networks and transformation-based modules to achieve this goal. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of robustness and generalization, particularly in scenarios where data augmentation is limited. The key findings of this study highlight the importance of incorporating local transformations into the learning process, leading to improved performance in image classification, object recognition, and other computer vision tasks. Our research contributes to the development of more robust and generalizable neural networks, with potential applications in areas such as robotics, autonomous driving, and medical imaging, and is relevant to keywords such as invariant representations, local transformations, deep learning, and computer vision.

This paper proposes a novel Self-supervised Video Retrieval Transformer Network, designed to efficiently retrieve relevant videos from large datasets. The objective is to develop a model that can learn effective video representations without relying on manual annotations. Our approach utilizes a transformer-based architecture, leveraging self-supervised learning techniques to learn robust and generalizable features from video data. The network is trained using a combination of contrastive learning and masked language modeling, enabling it to capture both spatial and temporal information in videos. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our model, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in video retrieval tasks. The proposed network achieves significant improvements in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score, making it a promising solution for applications such as video search, recommendation systems, and surveillance. Our research contributes to the advancement of self-supervised learning and transformer-based architectures in the field of computer vision, with potential applications in areas like AI-powered video analysis and 3D reconstruction. Key keywords: self-supervised learning, transformer network, video retrieval, computer vision, AI models.

Tensor factorization techniques, particularly higher-order principal component analysis (HOPCA), are increasingly used for dimensionality reduction and feature extraction in diverse domains. However, ill-posed problems and overfitting can hinder their performance, especially with high-dimensional data. This paper investigates the use of regularization techniques to improve the stability and generalization capability of tensor factorizations and HOPCA. We propose and analyze several regularization strategies, including L1, L2, and total variation penalties, tailored for tensor decompositions. These regularizers are incorporated into standard HOPCA algorithms and evaluated on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed regularized tensor factorization methods significantly enhance performance in terms of reconstruction accuracy, noise robustness, and feature interpretability compared to unregularized approaches. Specifically, L1 regularization promotes sparsity in the factor matrices, leading to more interpretable components, while L2 regularization improves stability and prevents overfitting. The findings suggest that regularized tensor factorizations offer a powerful tool for robust dimensionality reduction and feature extraction in high-dimensional data analysis. Keywords: Tensor Factorization, Higher-Order PCA, Regularization, Dimensionality Reduction, Machine Learning.

This paper introduces Permuted AdaIN, a novel approach designed to mitigate the bias towards global statistics in image classification tasks. The objective is to enhance the robustness and fairness of deep learning models by reducing their reliance on global image features. Our method builds upon the Adaptive Instance Normalization (AdaIN) technique, incorporating a permutation mechanism that randomizes the order of feature channels. This permutation process encourages the model to focus on local, rather than global, image statistics. Experimental results demonstrate that Permuted AdaIN outperforms conventional AdaIN and other state-of-the-art methods in terms of classification accuracy and robustness to adversarial attacks. Our approach also exhibits improved fairness metrics, indicating a reduced bias towards dominant global features. The key contributions of this research include the development of a permutation-based AdaIN method, the demonstration of its effectiveness in reducing global statistic bias, and the exploration of its applications in image classification and beyond. Relevant keywords: AdaIN, image classification, deep learning, fairness, robustness, permutation mechanism.

The objective of this paper is to introduce Res2Net, a novel multi-scale backbone architecture that enhances the representation capability of deep neural networks for visual recognition tasks. Traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) backbones struggle to simultaneously capture multi-scale features, resulting in a compromise in feature representation quality. Methods/Approach: Res2Net innovatively extends the hierarchical structure of ResNet by embedding a new multi-scale convolutional mechanism within each building block. This architecture divides feature maps into multiple segments and incorporates a cascade of hierarchical connections within a single block, enabling the network to capture a broader range of receptive fields and multi-scale features more effectively. Results/Findings: Our extensive experiments on widely recognized benchmarks demonstrate that Res2Net outperforms state-of-the-art backbone architectures across multiple visual recognition tasks, including image classification, object detection, and segmentation. The proposed architecture consistently shows superior accuracy and efficiency, with minimal additional computational overhead compared to existing backbones. Conclusion/Implications: Res2Net represents a significant advancement in CNN backbone design, providing a powerful yet efficient tool for enhancing the performance of deep learning models across various applications. Its innovative approach to embedding multi-scale features within fine-grained blocks offers new possibilities for developing more robust and versatile vision systems. Potential applications of Res2Net extend beyond traditional computer vision tasks, providing a scalable solution for diverse AI-driven domains requiring enhanced feature extraction capabilities. Keywords: Res2Net, multi-scale backbone, CNN, image classification, object detection, segmentation, deep learning, feature representation, neural networks.

Breast cancer diagnosis using ultrasound imaging is a critical area of research, with the potential to improve early detection and patient outcomes. This study addresses the challenge of achieving high diagnostic accuracy and reliability in AI-based breast ultrasound analysis by proposing a novel multi-AI combination approach. Unlike traditional single-model systems, our method integrates multiple AI models, each specialized in different aspects of ultrasound image interpretation, to enhance overall diagnostic performance. The proposed framework employs a fusion mechanism that combines outputs from convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and transformer-based architectures, leveraging their complementary strengths. Experimental results on a large-scale dataset demonstrate that the multi-AI combination achieves a 12% improvement in diagnostic accuracy compared to state-of-the-art single-model approaches, with a significant reduction in false positives and false negatives. Additionally, the system exhibits robust performance across diverse patient demographics and imaging conditions. This research contributes a reliable and scalable AI solution for breast ultrasound diagnosis, offering potential applications in clinical settings to support radiologists and improve diagnostic workflows. Key innovations include the integration of diverse AI architectures and a dynamic decision-making framework that adapts to varying diagnostic complexities. Keywords: breast ultrasound, AI diagnosis, multi-AI combination, convolutional neural networks, transformer models, medical imaging.

We study distributed computing of the truncated singular value decomposition problem. We develop an algorithm that we call \texttt for improving communication efficiency. Specifically, we uniformly partition the dataset among m nodes and alternate between multiple (precisely p) local power iterations and one global aggregation. In the aggregation, we propose to weight each local eigenvector matrix with orthogonal Procrustes transformation (OPT). As a practical surrogate of OPT, sign-fixing, which uses a diagonal matrix with \pm 1 entries as weights, has better computation complexity and stability in experiments. We theoretically show that under certain assumptions \texttt lowers the required number of communications by a factor of p to reach a constant accuracy. We also show that the strategy of periodically decaying p helps obtain high-precision solutions. We conduct experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of \texttt.

This paper introduces a novel training methodology for neural networks that leverages $\ell 1$-regularization in conjunction with bi-fidelity data to enhance model performance and reduce overfitting. The objective is to improve the generalization capability of neural networks when trained with limited high-fidelity data. Our approach uses a combination of computationally inexpensive low-fidelity data and a smaller set of accurate high-fidelity data. We employ $\ell 1$-regularization to promote sparsity in the network's weights, effectively pruning less important connections and improving robustness. We demonstrate that training with bi-fidelity data, guided by $\ell 1$-regularization, yields significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to training solely on high-fidelity data or using traditional regularization techniques. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show a substantial reduction in test error and improved model interpretability. This method offers a practical solution for training accurate neural networks in scenarios where acquiring large amounts of high-fidelity data is challenging or costly. Key words: Neural networks, $\ell 1$-regularization, bi-fidelity data, machine learning, training algorithms, sparse models, generalization.

This paper presents a novel approach for gesture recognition in RGB videos utilizing human body keypoints and Dynamic Time Warping (DTW). The objective is to develop an accurate and efficient gesture recognition system applicable to real-time applications. The proposed method extracts 2D human body keypoints from RGB video frames using a pre-trained pose estimation model. These keypoints are then used to represent gestures as temporal sequences. DTW is employed to compare and classify these sequences against a pre-defined gesture library. We introduce a keypoint selection strategy that optimizes the feature set for specific gestures, improving recognition accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing techniques, particularly in handling variations in speed and execution style. The system’s robustness to noise and occlusion is also evaluated. The findings suggest that the combination of keypoint-based representation and DTW provides a powerful framework for gesture recognition in video. This approach has implications for human-computer interaction, sign language recognition, and virtual reality applications. Keywords: Gesture Recognition, Human Body Keypoints, Dynamic Time Warping, RGB Video, Pose Estimation, Action Recognition.

The paper addresses the critical challenge of detecting objects in densely packed scenes, a scenario often encountered in urban environments, crowds, and complex industrial settings. Precise detection under these conditions is crucial for applications in surveillance, autonomous driving, and robotics. Methods/Approach: The study proposes a novel detection framework utilizing an advanced neural network architecture designed to improve spatial resolution and segmentation accuracy. The approach integrates a dual-path convolutional network that processes both global and local context information, combined with an attention mechanism that dynamically focuses on congested regions of the scene. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, significantly outperforming existing models in terms of precision and recall on benchmark datasets such as COCO and Cityscapes. The findings reveal enhancements in detecting small, overlapping, and occluded objects, with the model achieving up to 15% higher accuracy in densely packed environments compared to conventional techniques. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field by introducing a robust detection algorithm tailored for densely populated scenes. The proposed framework not only advances object recognition accuracy but also opens new pathways for real-time applications in complex environments. These improvements have the potential to enhance the capabilities of automated systems and provide valuable insights for further developments in computer vision. Keywords: Dense scene detection, object recognition, neural network architecture, attention mechanism, computer vision, urban environments.

This paper presents an end-to-end trainable framework for multi-instance pose estimation using transformer-based architectures. The objective is to address the challenges of accurately detecting and estimating poses for multiple instances in complex scenes, where occlusions and overlapping instances often degrade performance. We propose a novel approach that leverages the self-attention mechanism of transformers to model global dependencies among keypoints, enabling robust pose estimation even in crowded environments. Our method integrates a multi-instance detection module with a pose estimation network, allowing for joint optimization of both tasks. The framework is trained end-to-end, eliminating the need for complex post-processing steps. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly in scenarios with high instance density. The proposed approach achieves a 5% higher mean average precision (mAP) on the COCO dataset and shows superior generalization across diverse datasets. This work contributes to the field by introducing a scalable and efficient solution for multi-instance pose estimation, with potential applications in robotics, augmented reality, and human-computer interaction. Key innovations include the integration of transformers for global context modeling and the end-to-end trainable architecture, which simplifies the pipeline while enhancing performance. **Keywords**: Pose estimation, transformers, multi-instance detection, end-to-end learning, self-attention, keypoint detection.

The objective of this research is to introduce and evaluate a novel approach termed Non-Transferable Learning (NTL) for model verification and authorization, addressing security and intellectual property challenges in deploying AI models. Traditional models often face risks related to unauthorized replication or misuse, necessitating robust mechanisms to ensure controlled access and use. The proposed NTL approach integrates cryptographic techniques with machine learning frameworks to safeguard model integrity while allowing legitimate verification processes. Our method involves embedding non-transferable tokens within model architectures, ensuring that any unauthorized transfer or copying results in model non-functionality or errors in deployment. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that NTL retains model performance with minimal overhead while significantly enhancing security features compared to conventional transfer learning and model verification methods. Results show that our approach prevents unauthorized usage, ensuring proprietary models retain their operational exclusivity and intellectual value. The implications of NTL extend to secure deployment in sensitive applications, such as financial technology and bioinformatics, where model authenticity and protection against tampering are paramount. Our study contributes to the field by providing a scalable, effective solution for AI model owners to maintain control over their intellectual assets, fostering trust and reliability in AI systems. Key terms include model security, authorization, cryptographic integration, and non-transferable tokens.

This paper addresses the challenge of model misspecification in continuous control tasks using reinforcement learning (RL). The objective is to develop a robust RL framework that can effectively handle uncertainties and inaccuracies in the system dynamics model. We propose a novel approach that combines model-based RL with robust control techniques to mitigate the effects of model misspecification. Our method utilizes a probabilistic ensemble of models to capture the uncertainty in the system dynamics and incorporates this uncertainty into the RL algorithm. The results show that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of robustness and stability, achieving improved control performance in the presence of model errors. The key findings highlight the importance of accounting for model uncertainty in continuous control tasks and demonstrate the potential of our approach for real-world applications. This research contributes to the development of more reliable and efficient RL algorithms for complex control tasks, with implications for fields such as robotics, autonomous systems, and process control. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, continuous control, model misspecification, robust control, uncertainty quantification.

Monocular depth estimation, a crucial task in computer vision, remains vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper investigates the susceptibility of deep neural networks used for monocular depth estimation to such attacks. We analyze the impact of various adversarial perturbation strategies on the accuracy and robustness of state-of-the-art depth estimation models. Our approach involves crafting adversarial examples using gradient-based methods, specifically targeting the predicted depth maps. We demonstrate that even subtle perturbations can significantly degrade the performance of these networks, leading to substantial errors in depth prediction. Furthermore, we propose a novel defense mechanism based on adversarial training and feature denoising to enhance the robustness of monocular depth estimation models against these attacks. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our defense method in mitigating the impact of adversarial perturbations, improving the overall resilience of the depth estimation process. This work highlights the importance of considering adversarial robustness in the design and deployment of deep learning models for monocular depth estimation. Keywords: Monocular Depth Estimation, Adversarial Attacks, Deep Learning, Adversarial Training, Robustness, Computer Vision.

Unsupervised visual representation learning has emerged as a critical area of research in computer vision, aiming to reduce the reliance on labeled datasets. This paper introduces a novel approach for learning visual representations by leveraging the temporal coherence of video data through patch tracking. The proposed method focuses on tracking small image patches across consecutive video frames, enabling the model to learn meaningful representations without manual annotations. We employ a self-supervised framework where patches are extracted, tracked, and reconstructed, encouraging the network to capture spatial and temporal features inherent in the data. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance on benchmark datasets for tasks such as image classification and object detection, outperforming several existing unsupervised methods. The key contribution of this work lies in its simplicity and effectiveness, offering a scalable solution for representation learning in video domains. This research opens new avenues for applications in video analysis, motion understanding, and other vision tasks where labeled data is scarce. **Keywords**: unsupervised learning, visual representation, patch tracking, video analysis, self-supervised learning, computer vision.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated remarkable success in generating high-quality images. However, controlling the generation process to achieve specific desired attributes remains a challenge. This paper investigates the "steerability" of GANs, defined as the ability to manipulate the generated output by directly modifying latent space vectors to control image attributes. We propose a novel approach that combines unsupervised discovery of semantic directions in the GAN's latent space with a regularized optimization technique to enhance the precision and consistency of attribute manipulation. Our method identifies meaningful directions corresponding to interpretable image features without requiring explicit labels. We evaluate our approach on several GAN architectures and datasets, demonstrating its superior performance in controlled attribute editing compared to existing methods. Quantitative results show improved attribute manipulation accuracy and reduced unintended artifacts. This work contributes a practical framework for enhancing the steerability of GANs, enabling finer-grained control over image generation and facilitating applications in image editing and content creation. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, GAN, steerability, latent space, image generation, attribute manipulation.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have shown promise in explaining complex classifier decisions, but often lack control over the explanation's visual attributes. This paper introduces a novel approach: training a GAN to generate explanations in the StyleSpace of a pre-trained StyleGAN2. Our method aims to produce interpretable and visually controllable explanations for arbitrary classifiers. By mapping classifier decisions to the StyleSpace latent code, we achieve fine-grained control over explanation style, enabling users to manipulate features such as color, texture, and shape independently. We employ a novel loss function that encourages both fidelity to the classifier's decision boundary and disentanglement in the StyleSpace representation. Experiments demonstrate that our method generates high-quality, diverse explanations while offering unprecedented control over visual style. Quantitative evaluations, including perceptual metrics and user studies, validate the effectiveness of our approach compared to existing GAN-based explanation techniques. Our work contributes a new paradigm for generating interpretable explanations, facilitating deeper understanding and trust in classifier decisions. Keywords: GAN, Explainable AI, StyleGAN2, StyleSpace, Classifier Explanation, Interpretable Machine Learning.

Anomaly detection is a critical task in various domains, including cybersecurity, healthcare, and industrial systems, where identifying deviations from normal behavior is essential. This paper introduces a novel approach for anomaly detection using prototype-guided discriminative latent embeddings. The proposed method leverages a deep learning framework to learn compact and discriminative representations of normal data, guided by prototype samples that encapsulate the core characteristics of the normal class. By contrasting these prototypes with potential anomalies, the model effectively identifies outliers with high precision. The approach incorporates a joint optimization strategy that simultaneously minimizes intra-class variance and maximizes inter-class separation in the latent space, enhancing the discriminative power of the embeddings. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art anomaly detection techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness. The framework is particularly effective in scenarios with imbalanced data distributions and limited labeled anomalies. This research contributes to the field by providing a scalable and interpretable solution for anomaly detection, with potential applications in real-time monitoring systems and predictive maintenance. **Keywords**: anomaly detection, deep learning, latent embeddings, prototype guidance, discriminative learning, outlier detection.

This research addresses the challenge of effectively analyzing complex time series data to uncover low-dimensional state embeddings and identify metastable clusters, which are crucial for understanding dynamic systems across various contexts. By focusing on capturing the intrinsic structure embedded in temporal sequences, the study aims to facilitate improved interpretability and predictive modeling. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative approach that leverages a combination of dimensionality reduction techniques and clustering algorithms designed specifically for time series data. Our method integrates autoencoders with recurrent neural network architectures to learn compact state embeddings. Subsequently, a novel clustering algorithm is applied to these embeddings to detect metastable states, providing insights into system dynamics. Results/Findings: The proposed framework was evaluated on multiple time series datasets from diverse application domains. Results demonstrate that our method consistently yields superior performance in discovering low-dimensional state representations compared to conventional techniques. Additionally, the identified metastable clusters exhibit high stability and coherence, showcasing their potential in capturing meaningful temporal patterns. Conclusion/Implications: The findings highlight our approach's capability to enhance the analysis of time series data by extracting significant features and dynamic patterns that are often obscured in high-dimensional spaces. This research contributes to the field by offering a robust methodology for time series analysis that can be applied to various domains, including finance, healthcare, and environmental science, facilitating predictive analytics and decision-making processes. Keywords include state embeddings, metastable clusters, time series analysis, dimensionality reduction, and machine learning.

Existing state-of-the-art disparity estimation works mostly leverage the 4D concatenation volume and construct a very deep 3D convolution neural network (CNN) for disparity regression, which is inefficient due to the high memory consumption and slow inference speed. In this paper, we propose a network named EDNet for efficient disparity estimation. Firstly, we construct a combined volume which incorporates contextual information from the squeezed concatenation volume and feature similarity measurement from the correlation volume. The combined volume can be next aggregated by 2D convolutions which are faster and require less memory than 3D convolutions. Secondly, we propose an attention-based spatial residual module to generate attention-aware residual features. The attention mechanism is applied to provide intuitive spatial evidence about inaccurate regions with the help of error maps at multiple scales and thus improve the residual learning efficiency. Extensive experiments on the Scene Flow and KITTI datasets show that EDNet outperforms the previous 3D CNN based works and achieves state-of-the-art performance with significantly faster speed and less memory consumption.

This paper presents TDIOT: Target-driven Inference for Deep Video Object Tracking, a novel framework designed to improve the robustness and efficiency of object tracking in video sequences. The objective of this work is to address the limitations of conventional deep tracking algorithms, particularly in handling long-term occlusions, appearance variations, and background clutter. TDIOT leverages a target-driven approach, where a target-specific feature extractor is combined with an inference module that dynamically adapts to the evolving appearance of the object of interest throughout the video. The proposed architecture integrates deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with attention mechanisms to selectively focus on discriminative target features while suppressing distractors. Extensive experiments were conducted on multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating that TDIOT achieves superior tracking accuracy and real-time performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. Key findings reveal that the target-driven design significantly enhances adaptability to challenging scenarios, such as abrupt motion or partial occlusions. In conclusion, TDIOT provides a significant advancement in deep video object tracking by introducing a flexible and effective target-driven inference strategy. The proposed framework holds promise for various applications, including intelligent surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and human-computer interaction. Keywords: video object tracking, deep learning, target-driven inference, convolutional neural networks, visual attention.

Accurate forecasting of operating room (OR) data, such as surgery duration and resource utilization, is crucial for efficient hospital management and patient care. This paper introduces a novel hybrid model combining Gradient Boosting Trees (GBT) and Neural Networks (NN) to improve the accuracy of OR data forecasting. Our approach leverages GBT to capture non-linear relationships and feature importance, while NN refines predictions through pattern recognition in residual errors. The model was trained and validated on a comprehensive dataset of surgical procedures, encompassing multiple features like patient demographics, surgical team, and procedure type. Results demonstrate that the hybrid GBT-NN model outperforms standalone GBT and NN models, achieving a 15% reduction in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for surgery duration prediction. Furthermore, the hybrid approach provides more reliable estimates of resource consumption, leading to better scheduling and resource allocation. This hybrid model offers a significant advancement in OR data forecasting, contributing to optimized hospital operations and enhanced patient outcomes. Keywords: Operating Room, Forecasting, Gradient Boosting Trees, Neural Networks, Hybrid Model, Healthcare, Resource Allocation.

This research focuses on developing an innovative 3D moving object detection framework inspired by the visual processing of Drosophila, commonly known as fruit flies. The study aims to address the limitations of current object detection systems in handling dynamic and cluttered environments by leveraging point cloud data. Methods/Approach: The proposed framework employs a biologically inspired algorithm that mimics the neural circuits and processing strategies of Drosophila for visual detection. By utilizing point clouds, the system efficiently processes 3D spatial data to discern moving objects. The approach integrates advanced filtering techniques and point cloud segmentation to improve accuracy and response times, allowing for real-time application capabilities. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the Drosophila-inspired model outperforms existing state-of-the-art 3D object detection methods, particularly in detecting dynamic objects within dense and noisy environments. The framework achieves superior detection accuracy and demonstrates significant improvements in processing speed compared to traditional approaches, thus proving its effectiveness in real-time scenarios. Conclusion/Implications: This research introduces a novel paradigm in 3D moving object detection by combining biological inspiration with modern computational techniques. The proposed method offers significant contributions to the field of robotics and autonomous systems, offering potential applications in areas such as autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotic navigation. The findings underline the importance of integrating biological insights into technology development, paving the way for future advancements in perceptual computing. Keywords: 3D moving object detection, Drosophila, point clouds, real-time processing, autonomous systems, perceptual computing.

This paper presents a novel approach to molecular optimization through multimodal graph-to-graph translation. The objective is to develop an efficient method for generating optimized molecular structures with desired properties. Our approach utilizes a deep learning model that learns to translate input molecular graphs into output graphs with improved properties, such as solubility or bioactivity. The model is trained on a large dataset of molecular structures and their corresponding properties, and leverages techniques from graph neural networks and multimodal learning to capture complex relationships between molecular structures and properties. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in generating high-quality optimized molecular structures, outperforming existing methods in terms of efficiency and accuracy. The proposed method has significant implications for drug discovery, materials science, and other fields where molecular optimization is crucial. Key contributions include the introduction of a multimodal graph-to-graph translation framework, which enables the generation of diverse optimized molecular structures, and the development of a novel loss function that balances property optimization and molecular diversity. Relevant keywords: graph neural networks, multimodal learning, molecular optimization, drug discovery, materials science.

This paper addresses the problem of identifying critical points in persistence homology, a crucial task in topological data analysis. The objective is to develop a systematic approach to determine these points, which are essential for understanding the underlying structure of complex data. We propose a novel method based on a combination of computational geometry and machine learning techniques. Our approach utilizes a graph-based algorithm to efficiently identify critical points, which are then refined using a neural network model. The results show that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various datasets, including those from biology, materials science, and image analysis. The key findings of this research include the development of a robust and scalable method for determining critical points, which has significant implications for the analysis of complex systems and networks. Our work contributes to the advancement of persistence homology and topological data analysis, with potential applications in fields such as computer vision, bioinformatics, and materials science. Key keywords: persistence homology, critical points, topological data analysis, computational geometry, machine learning.

This paper introduces Likelihood Quantile Networks (LQN), a novel approach to coordinating multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) in complex, partially observable environments. LQN addresses the challenge of decentralized execution by enabling agents to reason about the likelihood of other agents' policies, thereby improving coordination and decision-making. The method involves learning a distribution over quantiles representing the likelihood of each agent's policy, allowing agents to estimate the joint action distribution and select actions that maximize expected team reward. We evaluate LQN on a set of challenging cooperative MARL tasks, including StarCraft II micromanagement scenarios, and demonstrate significant performance improvements compared to state-of-the-art MARL algorithms. The results indicate that LQN fosters more effective coordination and robustness, particularly in environments with noisy communication and limited information. The learned likelihood quantiles provide a valuable mechanism for agents to understand and anticipate the behavior of their teammates, leading to more efficient and reliable collaboration. Keywords: multi-agent reinforcement learning, coordination, decentralized execution, likelihood estimation, quantile regression, deep learning.

Infographics are documents designed to effectively communicate information using a combination of textual, graphical and visual elements. In this work, we explore the automatic understanding of infographic images by using Visual Question Answering technique.To this end, we present InfographicVQA, a new dataset that comprises a diverse collection of infographics along with natural language questions and answers annotations. The collected questions require methods to jointly reason over the document layout, textual content, graphical elements, and data visualizations. We curate the dataset with emphasis on questions that require elementary reasoning and basic arithmetic skills. Finally, we evaluate two strong baselines based on state of the art multi-modal VQA models, and establish baseline performance for the new task. The dataset, code and leaderboard will be made available at http://docvqa.org

The paper addresses the challenge of fast and accurate object detection, particularly focusing on the segmentation of small objects, which are often overlooked in existing methods. This research seeks to enhance object detection by integrating multiple receptive fields and a novel weakly-supervised segmentation approach. Methods/Approach: We introduce a segmentation network that utilizes multiple receptive fields to capture diverse context information effectively. The network is designed with a specific emphasis on small-object targeting, using a weakly-supervised learning framework that reduces the need for extensive labeled data. Our approach leverages a combination of feature pyramid networks and attention mechanisms to prioritize small object regions, ensuring they are accurately detected alongside larger objects. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of speed and accuracy. The integration of multiple receptive fields allows the model to adapt to various object scales, while the small-object-focusing mechanism ensures enhanced precision for smaller targets. Comparisons across standard datasets reveal a marked improvement in detection rates and computational efficiency. Conclusion/Implications: This research presents a novel contribution to object detection methodologies by combining multiple receptive fields with a weakly-supervised framework, particularly optimizing the detection of small objects. The proposed approach offers substantial implications for real-time applications in areas such as surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and robotics where fast and reliable object detection is crucial. This study paves the way for further advancements in segmentation networks, with potential extensions towards more complex detection tasks and broader applications. Keywords: object detection, multiple receptive fields, weakly-supervised learning, segmentation network, small-object detection, feature pyramid networks, attention mechanisms.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurately predicting noisy chaotic time series, which appears prominently in a wide range of complex dynamical systems. Traditional methods often require detailed models of the underlying processes, making them unsuitable for real-time or large-scale applications where noise and chaos prevail. Methods/Approach: We propose a model-free, deep learning-based framework to predict noisy chaotic time series. Our approach leverages advanced neural network architectures capable of capturing intricate nonlinear patterns without prior knowledge of the dynamics. Specifically, we employ a combination of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to handle temporal sequences and extract relevant features from noisy data effectively. Results/Findings: Our empirical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed deep learning model outperforms traditional predictive models in both accuracy and computational efficiency. We tested the framework across several benchmark chaotic systems known for their noisy data output, and our model exhibited superior capabilities in maintaining prediction quality in the presence of significant noise, surpassing conventional state-space reconstruction techniques. Conclusion/Implications: The study introduces a novel and robust model-free strategy for predicting noisy chaotic time series, highlighting the potential of deep learning methods in circumventing the limitations of traditional models. This research contributes to the fields of time series analysis and dynamical systems, offering a valuable tool for applications in weather forecasting, financial markets, and other areas where chaos and noise are prevalent. The findings emphasize the versatility and scalability of deep learning as a reliable solution in complex environments. Key Keywords: chaotic time series, model-free prediction, deep learning, noise robustness, RNN, CNN, nonlinear patterns.

Time series forecasting is a critical task in various domains, including finance, healthcare, and energy management. This paper presents a novel approach to time series forecasting using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks combined with symbolic representation techniques. The objective is to enhance the accuracy and interpretability of predictions by transforming raw time series data into symbolic sequences, which capture essential patterns and trends. The proposed method leverages the LSTM's ability to model long-term dependencies and the symbolic approach's efficiency in reducing data complexity. Experiments were conducted on multiple benchmark datasets, comparing the performance of the proposed method with traditional LSTM models and other state-of-the-art forecasting techniques. Results demonstrate significant improvements in prediction accuracy, particularly for datasets with high noise and non-linear patterns. Additionally, the symbolic representation provides a more interpretable framework for understanding the underlying dynamics of the time series. The findings highlight the potential of this hybrid approach for real-world applications, offering both robust forecasting capabilities and enhanced transparency. This research contributes to the growing body of work on advanced time series analysis and underscores the value of integrating symbolic methods with deep learning architectures. **Keywords**: Time series forecasting, LSTM networks, symbolic representation, deep learning, interpretability, pattern recognition.

Skeleton-based action recognition has gained significant attention due to its robustness and efficiency in representing human motion. However, the adversarial vulnerability of these systems remains underexplored, posing potential risks in real-world applications such as surveillance and human-computer interaction. This study investigates the susceptibility of skeleton-based action recognition models to adversarial attacks, aiming to identify critical weaknesses and propose mitigation strategies. We employ a systematic approach, leveraging state-of-the-art adversarial attack techniques, including gradient-based and optimization-based methods, to evaluate the robustness of widely used models such as Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). Our experiments reveal that even subtle perturbations to skeleton data can significantly degrade model performance, highlighting the inherent vulnerability of these systems. Furthermore, we introduce a novel defense mechanism that enhances model resilience by incorporating adversarial training and data augmentation techniques. The results demonstrate a notable improvement in robustness without compromising accuracy on clean data. This research provides valuable insights into the adversarial vulnerabilities of skeleton-based action recognition and offers practical solutions to enhance the security of such systems in critical applications. **Keywords**: Skeleton-based action recognition, adversarial attacks, Graph Convolutional Networks, robustness, adversarial training, human motion analysis.

This paper addresses the challenge of developing interpretable and efficient reinforcement learning (RL) models for continuous action spaces. Traditional RL approaches often struggle with balancing performance and interpretability, particularly in complex environments. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel framework that leverages a mixture of interpretable experts (MoIE) to guide decision-making in continuous action domains. Our approach integrates multiple specialized models, each designed to handle specific aspects of the environment, enabling both high performance and transparency in decision-making. The proposed method employs a hierarchical architecture where a gating mechanism dynamically selects and combines the outputs of these experts based on the current state. We evaluate our framework on benchmark continuous control tasks, demonstrating its ability to achieve competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art RL algorithms while maintaining interpretability. Key findings indicate that the MoIE framework not only improves task performance but also provides insights into the decision-making process, making it suitable for applications requiring both accuracy and explainability, such as robotics and autonomous systems. This research contributes a scalable and interpretable solution for continuous action RL, bridging the gap between complex models and practical usability. **Keywords**: reinforcement learning, continuous action spaces, interpretability, mixture of experts, hierarchical models, decision-making.
