Laser quang quang đông toàn võng mạc (PRP) là điều trị tiêu chuẩn trong võng mạc đái tháo đường (VMĐTĐ) nhờ thoái triển tân mạch. Tuy nhiên, dù bệnh nhân đã được điều trị tích cực với PRP, vẫn có tỷ lệ bệnh tiến triển nặng hơn cần cắt dịch kính. Cắt dịch kính kèm laser nội nhãn là điều trị tiêu chuẩn VMĐTĐ tăng sinh kèm xuất huyết dịch kính không tan và bong võng mạc co kéo. Việc tuân thủ tái khám của bệnh nhân VMĐTĐ tăng sinh là một thách thức lớn trên lâm sàng. Giảm thị lực đáng kể khi mới tái khám lại chủ yếu là do xuất huyết dịch kính. Dịch kính của bệnh nhân VMĐTĐ có nồng độ yếu tố tăng trưởng nội mô mạch máu (VEGF) cao, có xu hướng hóa lỏng, tách lớp, dính với võng mạc cực sau nhiều, dễ gây xuất huyết dịch kính, màng trước võng mạc và tân mạch. Vậy cắt dịch kính là phương pháp trực tiếp gây bong dịch kính sau, được xem là có lợi khi loại bỏ dịch kính có hại của bệnh nhân VMĐTĐ tăng sinh. Cắt dịch kính trực tiếp làm bong dịch kính sau giúp loại đi thành phần dịch kính có hại, giảm nồng độ VEGF, cải thiện nuôi dưỡng võng mạc, giảm tân mạch, giảm tiến triển bệnh. Laser nội nhãn kĩ lưỡng toàn võng mạc giúp ngăn ngừa biến chứng xuất huyết dịch kính tái phát, tân mạch mống, tân mạch gai. Laser nội nhãn là cơ hội thuận lợi nhất để tiến hành PRP kĩ lưỡng, đầy đủ trên bệnh nhân VMĐTĐTS. Thời điểm tiến hành là sau khi loại bỏ dịch kính xuất huyết, bong dịch kính sau và loại bỏ màng tăng sinh, laser nội nhãn được thực hiện từ võng mạc chu biên giữa đến ora serrata, khoảng cách giữa các nốt gần bằng 1 đường kính nốt laser. Laser nội nhãn giúp nâng cao hiệu quả điều trị của laser ngoại trú, ngăn ngừa biến chứng xuất huyết dịch kính tái phát, tân mạch mống và glaucoma tân mạch.

The objective of this study is to introduce a comprehensive benchmark for Image Scene Graph Generation (SGG), a critical task in visual understanding that involves detecting objects and predicting their relationships within images. Our approach involves the development of a standardized dataset and evaluation protocol to effectively compare and assess various SGG methodologies. We utilize state-of-the-art deep learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and graph-based networks, to generate refined scene graphs that capture complex semantic relationships. Our findings indicate that our benchmark facilitates the identification of strengths and limitations within current SGG techniques, presenting a clear landscape of performance across different models. We demonstrate that our benchmark not only robustly compares existing methods but also highlights key areas for future research and development. The implications of this work include providing the research community with an essential tool for driving innovation in scene graph generation, thereby enhancing machine vision applications such as image retrieval, automatic image annotation, and human-computer interaction. Key contributions of this research are the establishment of a unified evaluation framework and the advancement of computational techniques in SGG. Keywords include scene graph generation, visual understanding, deep learning, CNNs, graph networks, and image semantic relationships.

Manifold learning techniques are crucial for dimensionality reduction and data representation, particularly in high-dimensional data spaces. This paper explores the potential of deep neural networks (DNNs) to act as Locality Sensitive Hash functions (LSH) within the context of manifold learning. We propose a novel DNN architecture trained to preserve local neighborhood structures inherent in the data manifold. Our approach utilizes a specifically designed loss function that encourages data points close on the manifold to map to similar binary codes in the DNN's output layer, effectively functioning as LSH. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our DNN-based LSH method achieves superior performance compared to traditional LSH techniques and other manifold learning algorithms in terms of retrieval accuracy and computational efficiency. The results suggest that DNNs can effectively capture complex manifold structures and generate locality-sensitive hashes, offering a scalable and accurate solution for similarity search and data indexing in high-dimensional spaces. Key words: Manifold Learning, Deep Neural Networks, Locality Sensitive Hashing, Dimensionality Reduction, Similarity Search.

This paper introduces Deep Geodesic Learning (DGL), a novel framework for simultaneous segmentation and anatomical landmarking in medical images. DGL leverages deep neural networks to estimate geodesic distances from a sparse set of user-defined points, effectively encoding shape and anatomical context. By integrating geodesic information into the learning process, our method overcomes limitations of purely Euclidean approaches, particularly in cases with complex anatomical structures and topological variations. The network is trained to predict signed geodesic distance maps, which are subsequently used for both segmentation and landmark localization through simple post-processing steps. We evaluate DGL on multiple anatomical structures, demonstrating improved segmentation accuracy and landmarking precision compared to state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, DGL exhibits robustness to noise and variations in image quality, achieving superior performance in challenging anatomical regions. The proposed framework offers a flexible and efficient solution for medical image analysis, with potential applications in computer-assisted surgery, diagnostic imaging, and personalized medicine. Keywords: deep learning, geodesic distance, segmentation, anatomical landmarking, medical image analysis.

With the increasing demand for efficient video analysis, our research addresses the challenge of whether image classifiers can be effectively applied to video understanding tasks. Traditional approaches to video understanding often rely on complex and computationally intensive models. This study explores the feasibility of using pre-trained image classifiers to simplify and enhance video content analysis. Methods/Approach: We developed a framework that repurposes conventional image classification models for video understanding tasks. This approach involves extracting frames from video sequences and applying image classifiers to each frame. We introduce novel techniques to aggregate frame-level predictions into coherent video-level insights, leveraging temporal consistency and motion cues for improved accuracy. Results/Findings: Our findings indicate that image classifiers can achieve competitive performance in video understanding when adapted appropriately. The proposed method demonstrated superior or comparable accuracy to state-of-the-art video processing techniques across multiple datasets, while significantly reducing computational overhead. The experiments reveal that leveraging image-based models can streamline video analysis, offering efficient processing without a substantial loss in accuracy. Conclusion/Implications: This research highlights a paradigm shift in video understanding, showcasing that existing image classifiers can be repurposed to handle video content effectively. The proposed approach not only simplifies the process but also has the potential to drastically reduce the computational cost associated with video processing. Visual attribute prediction plays a crucial role in understanding and interpreting complex image content for various computer vision tasks. This paper introduces Progressive Attention Networks (PANs), a novel deep learning architecture designed to enhance the accuracy and interpretability of visual attribute prediction. The proposed approach utilizes a multi-stage attention mechanism that incrementally refines focus on relevant regions within images, enabling the model to capture subtle and context-dependent visual cues. Through the integration of progressive attention layers, PANs dynamically allocate computational resources to salient features, leading to improved discrimination between similar visual attributes. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that PANs achieve state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of precision, recall, and overall prediction accuracy. Additionally, the interpretability of the attention maps provides valuable insights into the decision-making process of the network. The results indicate that PANs are particularly effective in handling challenging scenarios with occlusions, ambiguous attributes, and complex visual contexts. This research highlights the potential of progressive attention models for advancing visual recognition systems and sets a new direction for attribute-based image analysis in applications such as image search, surveillance, and human-computer interaction. Keywords: visual attribute prediction, progressive attention, deep learning, computer vision, image understanding.

We study empirical scaling laws for transfer learning between distributions in an unsupervised, fine-tuning setting. When we train increasingly large neural networks from-scratch on a fixed-size dataset, they eventually become data-limited and stop improving in performance (cross-entropy loss). When we do the same for models pre-trained on a large language dataset, the slope in performance gains is merely reduced rather than going to zero. We calculate the effective data "transferred" from pre-training by determining how much data a transformer of the same size would have required to achieve the same loss when training from scratch. In other words, we focus on units of data while holding everything else fixed. We find that the effective data transferred is described well in the low data regime by a power-law of parameter count and fine-tuning dataset size. We believe the exponents in these power-laws correspond to measures of the generality of a model and proximity of distributions (in a directed rather than symmetric sense). We find that pre-training effectively multiplies the fine-tuning dataset size. Transfer, like overall performance, scales predictably in terms of parameters, data, and compute.

This paper introduces *AI Playground*, an innovative Unreal Engine-based data ablation tool designed to enhance the robustness and generalizability of deep learning models. The primary objective of this research is to address the challenge of limited and biased training datasets, which often hinder the performance of AI systems in real-world scenarios. *AI Playground* leverages the photorealistic rendering capabilities of Unreal Engine to generate synthetic datasets with controlled variations in environmental conditions, object textures, and lighting. This approach enables systematic data ablation studies, allowing researchers to evaluate model performance under diverse and challenging conditions. The tool employs a modular architecture, integrating customizable scene generation, automated data labeling, and seamless export to popular deep learning frameworks. Experiments conducted on object detection and segmentation tasks demonstrate that models trained with *AI Playground*-generated datasets exhibit improved generalization and robustness compared to those trained on traditional datasets. Key findings reveal a 15% increase in accuracy under adverse conditions, such as low lighting and occlusions. The implications of this work are significant for the AI community, offering a scalable and cost-effective solution for dataset augmentation and model evaluation. *AI Playground* not only bridges the gap between synthetic and real-world data but also provides a versatile platform for advancing research in computer vision and deep learning. **Keywords**: synthetic data generation, Unreal Engine, data ablation, deep learning, computer vision, dataset augmentation.

This paper introduces Neural Jump Stochastic Differential Equations, a novel framework that combines the strengths of neural networks and stochastic differential equations to model complex systems with jump discontinuities. The objective is to develop a more accurate and efficient method for simulating and analyzing systems that exhibit sudden changes, such as financial markets or biological systems. Our approach utilizes a neural network to learn the jump dynamics and integrates it with stochastic differential equations to capture the continuous evolution of the system. The results show that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Key findings include the ability to capture non-Gaussian distributions and non-linear relationships, as well as improved robustness to noise and uncertainty. The implications of this research are significant, enabling better modeling and prediction of complex systems, with potential applications in fields such as finance, biology, and engineering. Our contributions include the development of a new neural network architecture and a novel training algorithm, which can be used to improve the accuracy and efficiency of stochastic differential equation models. Keywords: Neural Jump SDEs, Stochastic Differential Equations, Neural Networks, Jump Processes, Monte Carlo Methods.

This paper addresses the challenge of leveraging offline data for meta-reinforcement learning (meta-RL) while maintaining adaptability to new tasks. Traditional meta-RL methods often require extensive online interaction, which can be impractical in real-world scenarios. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel framework that combines offline meta-reinforcement learning with online self-supervision. Our approach utilizes a pre-trained meta-RL model on offline datasets and introduces an online self-supervision mechanism to fine-tune the model with minimal interaction. This mechanism enables the model to adapt to new tasks by generating pseudo-labels and refining its policy through self-generated feedback. Experiments on benchmark environments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to fully online meta-RL approaches while significantly reducing the need for real-time interaction. The results highlight the potential of our framework for applications where offline data is abundant but online exploration is costly or constrained. This work contributes to advancing meta-RL by bridging the gap between offline learning and online adaptability, offering a practical solution for real-world deployment. **Keywords**: Meta-reinforcement learning, offline learning, self-supervision, adaptation, pseudo-labels, policy refinement.

This paper introduces ECGadv, a novel approach to generating adversarial electrocardiograms (ECGs) designed to misguide arrhythmia classification systems. The objective is to investigate the vulnerability of deep learning-based arrhythmia classification models to adversarial attacks. Our method utilizes a combination of generative adversarial networks (GANs) and gradient-based optimization techniques to craft subtle perturbations in ECG signals, resulting in misclassifications. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of ECGadv in deceiving state-of-the-art arrhythmia classification systems, with a significant reduction in classification accuracy. Our findings highlight the potential risks of relying solely on deep learning models for arrhythmia diagnosis and emphasize the need for developing more robust and secure classification systems. The contributions of this research include the development of a novel adversarial attack framework for ECGs and insights into the vulnerabilities of deep learning-based arrhythmia classification models, with implications for the development of more secure and reliable medical diagnosis systems. Key keywords: ECG, adversarial attacks, arrhythmia classification, deep learning, GANs, medical diagnosis security.

This paper investigates the robustness of Vision Transformers (ViT) to adversarial examples, a critical concern in deep learning-based computer vision. Our objective is to analyze the vulnerability of ViT models to carefully crafted input perturbations that can mislead their predictions. We employ a range of adversarial attack methods, including FGSM and PGD, to evaluate the robustness of ViT models against state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Our results show that ViT models exhibit unique robustness properties, with some architectures demonstrating increased resilience to adversarial examples compared to their CNN counterparts. We also identify key factors influencing ViT robustness, such as patch size and attention mechanisms. Our findings have important implications for the development of secure and reliable computer vision systems, highlighting the potential of ViT models in adversarial settings. This research contributes to the growing field of adversarial robustness, with applications in areas like autonomous driving, surveillance, and healthcare, and sheds light on the importance of considering robustness in Vision Transformer design. Key keywords: Vision Transformers, adversarial examples, robustness, computer vision, deep learning.

Objective: Adversarial patch attacks expose vulnerabilities in computer vision systems, but their conspicuous appearance and sensitivity to real-world distributional shifts limit practical evaluation of robustness. This paper introduces a novel transparent patch framework that simultaneously (1) maintains high attack strength under diverse distributional distortions and (2) minimizes visual obtrusiveness to human observers. Methods: We formulate transparent patch generation as a multi-objective optimization problem combining a classification-driven adversarial loss with a perceptual transparency loss derived from structural similarity metrics. To capture real-world variability, we train patches on a suite of simulated distributional shifts (e.g., noise, blur, weather effects) and augmentations. The optimization employs projected gradient descent with adaptive transparency weighting, yielding patches that remain effective under both clean and corrupted inputs. Results: On ImageNet and two common corruption benchmarks, our transparent patches achieve an average attack success rate of 82.5% under shift conditions—outperforming state-of-the-art opaque patches (68.3%) by 14.2%. Structural similarity (SSIM) scores indicate a 35% reduction in perceptual distortion compared to prior methods. A user study with 50 participants confirms that our patches are rated significantly less obtrusive (mean rating 2.1/5) than standard opaque attacks (3.8/5). Conclusion: Transparent patch attacks reveal persistent blind spots in modern image classifiers under distributional shift while preserving stealthiness. Our contributions include (i) a distribution-shift-aware transparent patch generation algorithm, (ii) a human-perception-guided transparency metric, and (iii) an open-source evaluation suite. This work underscores the need for defenses that address both adversarial robustness and practical stealth constraints. Keywords: Transparent adversarial patch, distributional shift, obtrusiveness, image classification, adversarial robustness.

The objective of this research is to enhance semantic segmentation of LiDAR point clouds in autonomous driving applications by introducing SalsaNext, an advanced model designed for fast and uncertainty-aware processing. Building on previous advancements in convolutional neural networks, our approach utilizes a lightweight architecture optimized for real-time applications without compromising accuracy. SalsaNext integrates an attention mechanism and a novel residual connection strategy, allowing the model to effectively handle the inherent challenges of sparse and irregular LiDAR data. Our experiments demonstrate that SalsaNext achieves superior segmentation performance on benchmark datasets, surpassing existing models in terms of both speed and accuracy. Through extensive testing, we highlight its robustness in various driving scenarios, showcasing significant improvements in handling edge cases and uncertainty quantification. The integration of uncertainty estimation enables more reliable predictions, essential for safety-critical applications in autonomous vehicles. The findings indicate that SalsaNext not only advances the state-of-the-art in point cloud segmentation but also introduces a framework that balances computational efficiency and predictive reliability. This research contributes to the field by offering a scalable and effective solution for real-time semantic understanding, paving the way for broader adoption in industry and further exploration of uncertainty-aware methodologies. Key keywords include LiDAR, semantic segmentation, uncertainty estimation, autonomous driving, and deep learning.

Phân vùng polyp trong ảnh nội soi là một nhiệm vụ quan trọng trong lĩnh vực y học, giúp phát hiện sớm các bệnh lý liên quan đến đường tiêu hóa. Việc áp dụng các phương pháp học máy, đặc biệt là học có giám sát, đã mở ra những hướng đi mới trong việc cải thiện độ chính xác và hiệu quả của quá trình phân tích hình ảnh y tế. Kiến trúc Transformer, với khả năng xử lý thông tin theo cách không tuần tự và chú trọng vào mối quan hệ giữa các phần của dữ liệu, đã chứng minh được tiềm năng vượt trội trong nhiều bài toán thị giác máy tính. Các bước thực hiện bao gồm thu thập và tiền xử lý dữ liệu hình ảnh, xây dựng mô hình học sâu dựa trên Transformer, và đánh giá hiệu suất của mô hình thông qua các chỉ số như độ chính xác, độ nhạy và độ đặc hiệu. Kết quả cho thấy mô hình không chỉ cải thiện đáng kể độ chính xác trong việc phân vùng polyp so với các phương pháp truyền thống mà còn giảm thiểu tỷ lệ sai sót trong chẩn đoán. Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown significant promise in solving complex continuous control tasks. However, its performance often degrades under model misspecification, where the learned policy fails to generalize due to discrepancies between the training environment and real-world conditions. This paper addresses the challenge of robust RL in continuous control settings by proposing a novel framework that enhances policy robustness against model uncertainties. Our approach integrates a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) technique with deep RL algorithms, enabling the agent to learn policies that are resilient to environmental variations. We evaluate the proposed method on a suite of benchmark continuous control tasks, including robotic manipulation and autonomous navigation, under varying levels of model misspecification. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing RL methods in terms of stability, generalization, and task performance. The key contributions of this work include a theoretically grounded robust RL formulation and a practical algorithm that bridges the gap between simulation and real-world deployment. This research advances the state-of-the-art in robust RL and provides a foundation for deploying RL-based systems in safety-critical applications where model uncertainties are prevalent. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Continuous Control, Model Misspecification, Robust Optimization, Deep RL, Generalization.

Breast cancer classification is a critical task in medical imaging, with significant implications for early diagnosis and treatment planning. This paper proposes an Attention Model Enhanced Network (AMEN) to improve the accuracy and robustness of breast cancer image classification. The proposed approach integrates an attention mechanism into a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, enabling the model to focus on diagnostically relevant regions within medical images while suppressing irrelevant features. The attention mechanism dynamically weights feature maps, enhancing the model's ability to capture subtle patterns indicative of malignancy. The network is trained and evaluated on a publicly available dataset of breast cancer images, including both benign and malignant cases. Experimental results demonstrate that AMEN outperforms traditional CNN-based methods, achieving higher classification accuracy and improved interpretability of decision-making processes. The model achieves an accuracy of 94.7%, surpassing state-of-the-art methods by 2.3%. Furthermore, the attention maps generated by the model provide valuable insights into the regions of interest, aiding clinicians in understanding the model's predictions. This research contributes to the field of medical image analysis by introducing a novel attention-enhanced architecture that improves both performance and interpretability, with potential applications in automated breast cancer diagnosis and other medical imaging tasks. **Keywords**: Breast cancer classification, attention mechanism, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, medical image analysis, interpretability.

Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) aims to localize the object referred to by a natural language expression in an image. Existing one-stage REC methods often struggle with complex scenarios requiring global contextual reasoning due to their limited receptive fields. This paper introduces a novel Real-time Global Inference Network (RGIN) for one-stage REC, designed to effectively capture global dependencies and facilitate accurate object localization. RGIN employs a hierarchical attention mechanism to aggregate contextual information from the entire image, enabling the model to reason about relationships between different regions and the referring expression. Furthermore, a cross-modal fusion module integrates visual and linguistic features, enhancing the alignment between the expression and the relevant image regions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg, demonstrate that RGIN achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining real-time processing speeds. The proposed model significantly improves accuracy in handling complex referring expressions that require global contextual understanding, offering a practical solution for real-world applications. Keywords: Referring Expression Comprehension, Global Inference, Attention Mechanism, Cross-modal Fusion, Real-time Object Localization.

This paper addresses the challenge of scene text recognition, a crucial task in computer vision, by introducing a novel approach from a two-dimensional perspective. The objective is to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of text recognition in images and videos, which is essential for various applications such as autonomous vehicles, robotics, and surveillance systems. Our method utilizes a deep learning-based architecture, incorporating convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to extract features from text regions and recognize characters. The proposed approach is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in recognition accuracy and speed compared to existing methods. Key findings include the effectiveness of our 2D perspective in handling text with varying orientations, fonts, and sizes. The contributions of this research lie in its ability to provide a more robust and efficient scene text recognition system, with potential applications in image and video analysis, document scanning, and optical character recognition (OCR). Relevant keywords for this study include scene text recognition, deep learning, CNN, RNN, 2D perspective, and OCR.

We present a unifying framework for designing and analysing distributional reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms in terms of recursively estimating statistics of the return distribution. Our key insight is that DRL algorithms can be decomposed as the combination of some statistical estimator and a method for imputing a return distribution consistent with that set of statistics. With this new understanding, we are able to provide improved analyses of existing DRL algorithms as well as construct a new algorithm (EDRL) based upon estimation of the expectiles of the return distribution. We compare EDRL with existing methods on a variety of MDPs to illustrate concrete aspects of our analysis, and develop a deep RL variant of the algorithm, ER-DQN, which we evaluate on the Atari-57 suite of games.

This paper introduces a novel gamut-mapping framework designed to enhance the color accuracy of high dynamic range (HDR) image reproduction on standard dynamic range (SDR) displays. The objective is to minimize color distortions and preserve perceptual fidelity during HDR-to-SDR conversion. Our approach integrates a perceptually-based color appearance model with a spatially adaptive gamut mapping algorithm. This algorithm selectively compresses colors based on local image content and human visual sensitivity, aiming to maintain hue and minimize clipping artifacts. We evaluate the performance of our framework through subjective and objective assessments, comparing it against state-of-the-art gamut mapping techniques. Results demonstrate that our method achieves superior color accuracy and visual quality, particularly in preserving fine details and vibrant colors, while effectively mitigating unwanted color shifts. The framework contributes to improved HDR image accessibility across a broader range of display technologies, facilitating a more faithful representation of the original scene. Keywords: HDR, SDR, gamut mapping, color appearance model, image reproduction, color accuracy.

Cao chiết vỏ quế (Cinnamomum verum) được nghiên cứu về tác động của nó đối với tăng trưởng và khả năng bảo vệ của cá rô phi (Oreochromis niloticus). Cụ thể, nghiên cứu đã chứng minh rằng cao chiết vỏ quế có thể tăng cường hoạt động của hệ miễn dịch của cá rô phi, giúp chúng chống lại các loại vi khuẩn và virus. Đồng thời, cao chiết vỏ quế cũng có thể giảm thiểu tác động của các chất ô nhiễm trong môi trường, giúp cá rô phi phát triển khỏe mạnh hơn. Kết quả nghiên cứu này có thể giúp phát triển các phương pháp bảo vệ và tăng trưởng cá rô phi hiệu quả hơn, góp phần vào sự phát triển bền vững của ngành nuôi trồng thủy sản.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) systems are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, but their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, particularly reward poisoning, poses significant risks. This paper addresses the critical challenge of defending RL agents against reward poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate reward signals to degrade learning performance or induce harmful behaviors. We propose a novel defense mechanism that leverages anomaly detection and robust optimization techniques to identify and mitigate malicious reward manipulations. Our approach integrates a dynamic reward filtering framework that distinguishes between legitimate and poisoned rewards, ensuring the integrity of the learning process. Through extensive experiments on benchmark RL environments, we demonstrate that our method significantly reduces the impact of reward poisoning attacks while maintaining high learning efficiency. Compared to existing defenses, our solution achieves superior robustness and scalability across diverse attack scenarios. The proposed framework not only enhances the security of RL systems but also provides a foundation for developing resilient learning algorithms in adversarial settings. This research contributes to advancing the field of secure RL by offering a practical and effective defense strategy against reward poisoning, with potential applications in autonomous systems, robotics, and cybersecurity. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Reward Poisoning, Anomaly Detection, Robust Optimization, Adversarial Attacks, Secure RL.

Các triệu chứng lâm sàng của MIS-C rất đa dạng, bao gồm sốt cao kéo dài, phát ban, đau bụng, tiêu chảy, và các dấu hiệu viêm như viêm kết mạc. Việc chẩn đoán sớm và điều trị kịp thời là rất quan trọng để giảm thiểu biến chứng và cải thiện tiên lượng cho bệnh nhi. Các nghiên cứu hiện tại đang tập trung vào việc hiểu rõ hơn về cơ chế bệnh sinh, cũng như tìm kiếm các phương pháp điều trị hiệu quả nhằm ứng phó với tình trạng này.

This paper introduces a novel approach for generating 3D visualizations from video frame sequences. The primary objective is to reconstruct a 3D representation of dynamic scenes captured in video, addressing the limitations of traditional multi-view stereo and structure-from-motion techniques when applied to monocular video. Our method employs a deep learning framework that combines convolutional neural networks for feature extraction with a differentiable rendering module to iteratively refine the 3D structure. Specifically, we train a model to predict depth maps from individual frames and subsequently fuse these depth maps into a consistent 3D point cloud using a learned volumetric representation. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of reconstruction accuracy and visual fidelity compared to existing methods. The resulting 3D visualizations exhibit improved temporal coherence and reduced artifacts, enabling more realistic and immersive experiences. This research contributes a robust and efficient solution for 3D video understanding, with potential applications in virtual reality, augmented reality, and autonomous navigation. Keywords: 3D reconstruction, video processing, deep learning, computer vision, differentiable rendering.

This paper introduces the Contextual Camouflage Attack (CCA), a novel approach to deceive object detection models by manipulating the surrounding context of the target object. The objective is to investigate the vulnerability of state-of-the-art object detection systems to contextual attacks, where the attacker camouflages the object by altering its background or nearby objects. Our approach utilizes a combination of computer vision and machine learning techniques to generate contextual camouflage patterns that can effectively evade object detection. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of CCA in reducing the detection accuracy of various object detection models, including YOLO and Faster R-CNN. The findings suggest that CCA can be a potent attack method, highlighting the need for more robust object detection systems. This research contributes to the development of more secure and reliable computer vision systems, with potential applications in areas such as surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and robotics. Key keywords: object detection, contextual camouflage attack, computer vision, machine learning, adversarial attack.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficient k-shot learning, where models must generalize effectively from limited labeled data. We propose a novel approach leveraging regularized deep networks to enhance learning performance in low-data regimes. Our method integrates a regularization framework that mitigates overfitting while preserving the model's ability to capture essential patterns from sparse datasets. The approach combines adaptive weight regularization with a modified loss function tailored for k-shot scenarios, ensuring robust feature extraction and improved generalization. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing k-shot learning techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Key findings reveal that the proposed regularization strategy significantly reduces model complexity without sacrificing predictive power, making it highly suitable for real-world applications with limited data availability. This research contributes to advancing k-shot learning by providing a scalable and efficient solution, with potential applications in domains such as medical imaging, natural language processing, and autonomous systems. Keywords: k-shot learning, deep networks, regularization, low-data regimes, generalization, adaptive learning.

We propose a novel method for unsupervised image-to-image translation, which incorporates a new attention module and a new learnable normalization function in an end-to-end manner. The attention module guides our model to focus on more important regions distinguishing between source and target domains based on the attention map obtained by the auxiliary classifier. Unlike previous attention-based method which cannot handle the geometric changes between domains, our model can translate both images requiring holistic changes and images requiring large shape changes. Moreover, our new AdaLIN (Adaptive Layer-Instance Normalization) function helps our attention-guided model to flexibly control the amount of change in shape and texture by learned parameters depending on datasets. Experimental results show the superiority of the proposed method compared to the existing state-of-the-art models with a fixed network architecture and hyper-parameters. Our code and datasets are available at https://github.com/taki0112/UGATIT or https://github.com/znxlwm/UGATIT-pytorch.

In the era of big data, effectively handling and modeling multidimensional datasets is an ongoing challenge. This paper introduces innovative tensor-train networks as a solution, aiming to enhance predictive modeling capabilities for complex, multidimensional data structures commonly encountered in various scientific and industrial applications. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel framework leveraging the tensor-train (TT) decomposition technique to model multidimensional datasets effectively. The approach utilizes tensor-train networks to compactly represent data, maintain structural integrity, and improve computational efficiency. We developed algorithms to train these networks, optimizing them for minimal dimensionality loss while ensuring accuracy in prediction tasks. Results/Findings: The proposed tensor-train networks demonstrate substantial improvements in both predictive accuracy and computational efficiency over traditional multidimensional data handling methods. Evaluations across multiple benchmark datasets reveal that our approach achieves superior performance metrics, including reduced error rates and faster processing times compared to existing models. We also highlight the scalability of our solution, as it adapts to varying sizes of data without significant degradation in performance. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a robust method for tackling the challenges of predictive modeling in multidimensional data space. The tensor-train network approach not only enhances prediction accuracy but also offers computational cost benefits, making it a viable tool for real-time applications in areas such as climate modeling, genomics, and image analysis. The work opens pathways for further exploration into tensor-based neural network architectures and their potential applications in diverse fields. Keywords: Tensor-Train Networks, Multidimensional Data, Predictive Modeling, Computational Efficiency, Data Decomposition, Neural Networks, Big Data Analysis.

Hình thái không gian công cộng khu vực lõi trung tâm TP.HCM đang trải qua sự thay đổi đáng kể. Khu vực này đã trở thành trung tâm kinh tế, văn hóa và xã hội của thành phố, thu hút hàng triệu người dân và du khách mỗi ngày. Không gian công cộng ở khu vực lõi trung tâm TP.HCM bao gồm các công viên, quảng trường, đường phố và các khu vực khác. Những không gian này không chỉ phục vụ nhu cầu sinh hoạt hàng ngày của người dân mà còn trở thành điểm đến hấp dẫn cho du khách. Tuy nhiên, sự phát triển nhanh chóng của thành phố đã dẫn đến sự thay đổi hình thái không gian công cộng. Các công trình kiến trúc hiện đại đã được xây dựng, nhưng cũng đã gây ra sự xáo trộn và mất đi tính chất truyền thống của khu vực. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, thành phố đã triển khai các dự án cải thiện không gian công cộng, bao gồm việc xây dựng các công viên mới, cải tạo các đường phố và quảng trường, và tạo ra các không gian công cộng đa dạng và linh hoạt. Mục tiêu của các dự án này là tạo ra một không gian công cộng hiện đại, an toàn, sạch sẽ và thân thiện với người dân và du khách. Đồng thời, cũng cần phải bảo vệ và tôn trọng tính chất truyền thống của khu vực, để giữ gìn giá trị văn hóa và lịch sử của thành phố.

Nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc xác định các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến hiệu suất chiết xuất, bao gồm nhiệt độ, thời gian chiết và tỷ lệ dung môi. Kết quả cho thấy quy trình này không chỉ hiệu quả trong việc chiết xuất mà còn có thể áp dụng rộng rãi trong nghiên cứu và phát triển các sản phẩm chức năng từ Vaccinium angustifolium. Việc xây dựng quy trình này góp phần nâng cao giá trị sử dụng của loại cây này trong ngành công nghiệp thực phẩm và dược phẩm.

Thiết kế của bục đài thường hướng đến việc tối ưu hóa không gian mở, tạo sự hài hòa giữa kiến trúc và cảnh quan xung quanh. Không gian phía trước tòa nhà, khi được thiết kế hợp lý, sẽ trở thành nơi giao lưu, tương tác xã hội, đồng thời nâng cao giá trị thẩm mỹ và chức năng của công trình. Deformable image registration and regression are important tasks in medical image analysis. However, they are computationally expensive, especially when analyzing large-scale datasets that contain thousands of images. Hence, cluster computing is typically used, making the approaches dependent on such computational infrastructure. Even larger computational resources are required as study sizes increase. This limits the use of deformable image registration and regression for clinical applications and as component algorithms for other image analysis approaches. We therefore propose using a fast predictive approach to perform image registrations. In particular, we employ these fast registration predictions to approximate a simplified geodesic regression model to capture longitudinal brain changes. The resulting method is orders of magnitude faster than the standard optimization-based regression model and hence facilitates large-scale analysis on a single graphics processing unit (GPU). We evaluate our results on 3D brain magnetic resonance images (MRI) from the ADNI datasets.

This paper introduces the Auto-Parsing Network (APNet), a novel approach aimed at enhancing performance in image captioning and visual question answering (VQA) tasks. The challenge addressed is the effective extraction and interpretation of visual and contextual information from images to generate accurate and contextually relevant captions and answers. Methods/Approach: APNet employs a hybrid deep learning architecture that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image feature extraction and transformers for context processing. The network incorporates an auto-parsing mechanism that dynamically segments elements of an image, assigning semantic roles to facilitate comprehensive understanding. This mechanism enables the model to effectively parse images and engage with multi-modal data, making it adept at generating detailed descriptions and answering complex questions related to images. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that APNet surpasses state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets such as MSCOCO for image captioning and VQA v2.0 for visual question answering. APNet shows significant improvements in evaluation metrics such as BLEU, METEOR, and CIDEr scores for caption generation and accuracy in VQA. The results suggest that the auto-parsing capability enhances the system’s ability to comprehend and synthesize visual information efficiently. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of the Auto-Parsing Network presents advancements in the fields of image captioning and visual question answering by improving the granularity and accuracy of image interpretation. The research contributes to the development of more intelligent visual AI systems, with potential applications spanning from accessibility technologies to advanced human-computer interaction. APNet lays the groundwork for future exploration into dynamic parsing methods in multi-modal AI frameworks. Key keywords include image captioning, visual question answering, auto-parsing, deep learning, CNN, transformer.

Do đó, việc thực hiện khảo sát một cách khoa học, khách quan, tuân thủ các tiêu chuẩn chuyên môn là vô cùng quan trọng. Bằng chứng khảo sát đáng tin cậy có thể giúp bên nguyên hoặc bị đơn chứng minh hoặc bác bỏ khả năng gây nhầm lẫn, từ đó ảnh hưởng lớn đến kết quả cuối cùng của vụ tranh chấp nhãn hiệu. Phương pháp LASSO (Hastie et al., 2015) ch ỉnh hóa các h ệ số hồi quy tuy ến tính bằng cách thêm vào tiêu chuẩn bình ph ương tối tiểu một đại lượng ph ạt chu ẩn 1. Gần đây, phương pháp này đư ợc sử dụng ph ổ biến để giải quy ết các bài toán h ồi quy s ố chiều cao trong các l ĩnh v ực thống kê, khai phá, h ọc máy cho d ữ liệu lớn. Trong bài báo này chúng tôi áp d ụng phương pháp LASSO để chỉnh hóa các h ệ số hồi quy phi tuy ến cho bài toán đ ịnh giá bất động sản. Định giá b ất động sản thư ờng ch ỉ dựa vào kho ảng vài ch ục thu ộc tính và rõ ràng m ối liên h ệ giữa giá bất động sản và các thu ộc tính này không ph ải tuyến tính (Król, 2015), nên chúng tôi ph ải sử dụng mô hình phi tuyến. Khi đó số hệ số cần xác đ ịnh trong mô hình này th ường rất lớn, vì v ậy chúng tôi áp d ụng phương pháp LASSO để chỉnh hóa các h ệ số này. Tuy nhiên phương pháp LASSO áp dụng như trên l ại thường khá nh ạy với tham số chỉnh hóa. Do đó chúng tôi đ ề xuất thuật toán kết tập hồi quy phi tuy ến LASSO để cộng hư ởng các hàm h ồi quy LASSO yếu thành hàm h ồi quy m ạnh, có phương sai nh ỏ hơn. Thu ật toán này đ ã được đánh giá trên các t ập dữ liệu giá b ất động sản thu th ập tại tỉnh Montreal, Canada (Noseworthy, 2014) và qu ận Long Biên, Hà N ội và cho k ết quả chính xác hơn các thu ật toán m ới nhất đã được đưa ra.

It is increasingly common in many types of natural and physical systems (especially biological systems) to have different types of measurements performed on the same underlying system. In such settings, it is important to align the manifolds arising from each measurement in order to integrate such data and gain an improved picture of the system. We tackle this problem using generative adversarial networks (GANs). Recently, GANs have been utilized to try to find correspondences between sets of samples. However, these GANs are not explicitly designed for proper alignment of manifolds. We present a new GAN called the Manifold-Aligning GAN (MAGAN) that aligns two manifolds such that related points in each measurement space are aligned together. We demonstrate applications of MAGAN in single-cell biology in integrating two different measurement types together. In our demonstrated examples, cells from the same tissue are measured with both genomic (single-cell RNA-sequencing) and proteomic (mass cytometry) technologies. We show that the MAGAN successfully aligns them such that known correlations between measured markers are improved compared to other recently proposed models.

Product embedding plays a crucial role in enhancing the performance of machine learning models for e-commerce applications, enabling personalized recommendations, product search, and customer behavior analysis. This paper delves into the theoretical underpinnings of product embedding techniques, aiming to provide a comprehensive understanding of their effectiveness and limitations. We investigate various embedding methodologies, including matrix factorization, deep learning architectures such as autoencoders and graph neural networks, and contrastive learning approaches, analyzing their mathematical properties and expressive power in capturing product relationships. Our theoretical analysis provides insights into the conditions under which specific embedding methods excel, considering factors like data sparsity, feature representation, and scalability. Furthermore, we explore the impact of different loss functions and regularization techniques on embedding quality and generalization performance. We present a theoretical framework to evaluate the robustness and stability of learned embeddings against adversarial attacks and data noise. The results of our theoretical analysis are validated through empirical experiments on real-world e-commerce datasets, demonstrating the practical implications of our findings. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of product embedding, offering guidance for selecting appropriate embedding techniques and improving the design of machine learning models for e-commerce. Keywords: Product Embedding, E-commerce, Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, Deep Learning, Theoretical Analysis.

Bên cạnh đó, việc đánh giá năng lực thẩm phán cần thực chất, khách quan, dựa trên kết quả công tác và phẩm chất đạo đức, từ đó có cơ sở để khen thưởng, kỷ luật, và có kế hoạch bồi dưỡng phù hợp. Ứng dụng này cung cấp một nền tảng đa phương tiện, bao gồm hình ảnh, video, thông tin chi tiết và các tính năng tương tác, giúp người dùng khám phá và học hỏi về các loài vật khác nhau. Với giao diện thân thiện và dễ sử dụng, Wild Explorer mang đến một trải nghiệm học tập thú vị và hấp dẫn, giúp học sinh, sinh viên phát triển kiến thức và kỹ năng về sinh học, bảo tồn và bảo vệ môi trường. Ứng dụng này cũng hỗ trợ giáo viên và nhà giáo dục trong việc giảng dạy và quản lý nội dung, giúp họ tạo ra một môi trường học tập hiệu quả và thú vị cho học sinh. Bằng cách kết hợp công nghệ và giáo dục, Wild Explorer hướng đến mục tiêu tạo ra một thế hệ học sinh, sinh viên hiểu biết và yêu thích thiên nhiên, đồng thời đóng góp vào việc bảo vệ và bảo tồn môi trường.

Cắt khối thân đuôi tụy và lách xuôi dòng là một phương pháp phẫu thuật quan trọng trong điều trị các bệnh lý liên quan đến tụy và lách. Phương pháp này không chỉ giúp loại bỏ các khối u hoặc tổn thương mà còn giảm thiểu nguy cơ tái phát bệnh. Thông báo lâm sàng về kỹ thuật này nhấn mạnh sự cần thiết của việc đánh giá kỹ lưỡng trước khi phẫu thuật, bao gồm các xét nghiệm hình ảnh và đánh giá chức năng gan, thận. Bên cạnh đó, việc theo dõi sau phẫu thuật cũng rất quan trọng để phát hiện sớm các biến chứng có thể xảy ra. Điểm lại y văn cho thấy rằng, mặc dù cắt khối thân đuôi tụy và lách xuôi dòng có thể mang lại nhiều lợi ích, nhưng cũng cần cân nhắc kỹ lưỡng giữa lợi ích và rủi ro cho từng bệnh nhân cụ thể. Các nghiên cứu gần đây đã chỉ ra rằng, sự phối hợp giữa các chuyên khoa trong quá trình điều trị sẽ nâng cao hiệu quả và an toàn cho bệnh nhân.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated remarkable success in modeling complex data distributions, particularly those with light-tailed characteristics. However, their ability to accurately represent heavy-tailed distributions, which are prevalent in real-world datasets such as financial data, natural phenomena, and network traffic, remains limited. This paper introduces Pareto GAN, a novel framework designed to extend the representational power of GANs to heavy-tailed distributions. The proposed approach leverages the Pareto distribution, a well-known model for heavy-tailed data, to enhance the generator's ability to capture extreme values and long-tail behavior. We present a modified loss function and training strategy that integrates Pareto principles into the adversarial learning process, ensuring stable convergence and improved performance. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that Pareto GAN outperforms traditional GANs in modeling heavy-tailed distributions, achieving higher fidelity in tail regions and better overall data representation. The framework's contributions include a new theoretical foundation for GANs in heavy-tailed settings and practical insights for applications in finance, risk analysis, and anomaly detection. This work advances the state-of-the-art in generative modeling by addressing a critical limitation of existing methods and opening new avenues for research in heavy-tailed data generation. **Keywords**: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), heavy-tailed distributions, Pareto distribution, extreme value modeling, generative modeling, anomaly detection.

Recent advancements in reinforcement learning (RL) have demonstrated remarkable success in solving complex tasks. However, many RL methods struggle with generalization, particularly in few-shot scenarios where agents must extrapolate to unseen environments or tasks. This paper addresses the challenge of few-shot extrapolation by proposing a novel approach based on structured maximum entropy (MaxEnt) RL. Our method leverages a probabilistic framework to encourage diverse policy exploration, enabling agents to discover multiple solutions to a given problem. By explicitly modeling the structure of the solution space, the approach facilitates robust generalization and adaptability to new contexts. We evaluate our method on a suite of benchmark tasks, including robotic manipulation and navigation, and demonstrate significant improvements in extrapolation performance compared to existing baselines. The results highlight the importance of diversity in policy learning and provide insights into how structured exploration can enhance few-shot generalization. This work contributes to the broader goal of developing RL systems that can efficiently adapt to real-world variability, with potential applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and beyond. **Keywords**: reinforcement learning, maximum entropy, few-shot learning, generalization, policy diversity, structured exploration.

This paper addresses the challenge of modeling tissue organization through the development of a novel supervised generative adversarial network (GAN) framework. The primary objective is to improve the understanding of complex biological structures, which is essential for various applications in biomedical research and regenerative medicine. Our proposed approach leverages a supervised learning mechanism to enhance the training of GANs, allowing for the generation of high-fidelity tissue architectures that closely resemble real biological samples. We present a comprehensive method that integrates multi-modal data inputs, ensuring robust learning of tissue features. Experiments demonstrate that our supervised GAN model outperforms traditional unsupervised GANs in terms of generative quality, structural fidelity, and realistic representation of tissue morphology. Notably, the generated tissue models exhibit superior alignment with experimental data, which underscores the effectiveness of our approach. The findings indicate significant implications for advancing tissue engineering and regenerative therapies, providing a promising tool for researchers to explore tissue dynamics and functionalities in silico. This work contributes to the field of computational biology by highlighting the potential of supervised GANs in generating biologically relevant architectures. Keywords: generative models, tissue organization, supervised GANs, computational biology, biomedical research.

Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms often face challenges in balancing exploration and exploitation, particularly in environments where safety and efficiency are critical. This paper addresses the problem of achieving fast and safe policy improvement by introducing a novel approach called Diverse Exploration (DE). The proposed method leverages diversity-driven exploration strategies to efficiently navigate the state-action space while minimizing risks associated with unsafe actions. DE integrates a multi-objective optimization framework that simultaneously maximizes reward and minimizes safety violations, ensuring robust policy updates. Experiments conducted on benchmark environments, including high-dimensional control tasks and safety-critical scenarios, demonstrate that DE outperforms traditional exploration methods in terms of convergence speed and safety compliance. The results highlight the method's ability to achieve superior performance with fewer unsafe interactions, making it particularly suitable for real-world applications such as autonomous systems and robotics. This work contributes to the advancement of RL by providing a scalable and practical solution for safe and efficient policy optimization. **Keywords**: reinforcement learning, exploration strategies, safe policy improvement, multi-objective optimization, autonomous systems, robotics.

**Abstract:** Forecasting the behavior of high-dimensional dynamical systems is a fundamental challenge in fields ranging from climate science to finance and engineering. Traditional approaches often rely on optimal embeddings of system states, which can be computationally expensive and impractical for systems with complex dynamics and partial observations. This paper proposes a novel framework for forecasting high-dimensional time series by exploiting suboptimal embeddings, which require less stringent reconstruction conditions and reduce computational overhead. We introduce an embedding selection algorithm that balances information preservation with embedding dimensionality, enabling the effective representation of system dynamics even when full observability is unattainable. Using both synthetic and real-world datasets, we evaluate the proposed approach against state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness to observational noise. Our results demonstrate that leveraging suboptimal embeddings not only maintains competitive forecasting performance but also enhances scalability and adaptability in high-dimensional settings. This research offers new insights into the efficient modeling of complex dynamical systems and provides practical guidelines for embedding selection in forecasting applications. Keywords: high-dimensional dynamics, time series forecasting, embedding theory, computational efficiency, complex systems, machine learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of editing textual content within images by leveraging multimodal affinities, connecting linguistic context with visual elements for enhanced text manipulation. Methods: We propose a novel approach that integrates language models with image processing techniques to learn and exploit affinities between textual and visual modalities. Our model utilizes a combination of natural language processing and computer vision algorithms, incorporating deep learning architectures to analyze and understand the contextual relationship between text and its surrounding visual environment. Results: The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in accurately identifying and editing text within images, outperforming existing techniques in terms of precision and adaptability. Experiments conducted on diverse datasets reveal that our approach provides robust results across various text-heavy images, exhibiting enhanced capabilities in maintaining semantic coherence and visual fidelity post-editing. Conclusion: This research contributes a new perspective on image text editing by harnessing the synergistic potential of multimodal learning. The developed model opens avenues for practical applications in digital content creation, augmented reality, and assistive technology, where precise text editing is essential. The novelty of our work lies in its ability to seamlessly integrate and manipulate textual data in images, setting a new benchmark for future studies in this domain. Keywords: Multimodal learning, text editing, image processing, language models, computer vision, deep learning, textual content manipulation.

Accurate estimation of forest biomass is critical for environmental monitoring and carbon stock assessment. This paper addresses the challenge of developing precise forest biomass prediction maps using radar backscatter data. The primary objective is to enhance prediction accuracy by integrating a sequential regression approach with a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN). Methods/Approach: We propose a novel method that leverages the strength of Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks to refine predictions from sequential regression models. Radar backscatter data serves as the primary input to the regression model, which sequentially adjusts its predictions using cGAN to capture complex relationships between the radar signals and biomass quantities. The cGAN architecture is designed to learn and correct prediction errors, providing more reliable biomass estimates. Results/Findings: The proposed approach was evaluated on forest areas with varying biomass densities. Results demonstrate that our method significantly improves prediction accuracy compared to traditional regression techniques and state-of-the-art machine learning models. Specifically, the integration of cGAN with sequential regression yielded more precise biomass maps, reducing prediction variance and enhancing spatial resolution. Conclusion/Implications: This research highlights the potential of combining advanced machine learning techniques, specifically Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks, with radar data for environmental applications. The improved accuracy of forest biomass predictions has significant implications for ecological management and climate change studies. Future work could explore expanding this framework to other forms of remote sensing data for broader environmental monitoring applications. Keywords: Forest biomass, radar backscatter, Conditional Generative Adversarial Network, sequential regression, environmental monitoring, machine learning.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of high variance in policy gradient methods within multi-agent reinforcement learning environments. The objective is to systematically analyze and characterize the variance arising in multi-agent policy gradient algorithms, which significantly impacts learning stability and convergence. We propose a novel theoretical framework that decomposes the sources of variance in multi-agent policy gradients, considering factors such as agent interactions, reward structures, and policy parameterizations. Furthermore, we introduce variance reduction techniques specifically tailored for multi-agent scenarios, including coordinated baselines and adaptive credit assignment strategies. Through a series of benchmark experiments on cooperative and competitive multi-agent tasks, our approach demonstrates substantial improvements in sample efficiency, stability, and overall performance compared to standard multi-agent policy gradient methods. The findings offer the first comprehensive treatment of variance issues in this domain, providing both theoretical insights and practical solutions. Our work advances the understanding of multi-agent policy optimization and lays the foundation for more robust and scalable learning in complex, dynamic systems such as autonomous robotics, distributed control, and multi-agent simulations. Keywords: multi-agent systems, policy gradient, variance reduction, reinforcement learning, sample efficiency.

Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (SNE) is a powerful dimensionality reduction technique widely used for visualizing high-dimensional data in lower dimensions. This paper presents a comprehensive tutorial and survey of SNE, focusing on its variants that utilize Gaussian and Student-t distributions. The objective is to provide a clear and accessible explanation of the underlying principles, mathematical formulations, and practical applications of these methods. We explore the original SNE algorithm, highlighting its strengths and weaknesses, and then delve into its Gaussian and Student-t based extensions, particularly focusing on t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE). The tutorial covers parameter selection, optimization strategies, and common pitfalls. The survey examines the theoretical underpinnings and empirical performance of each variant, comparing their ability to preserve local data structure and handle crowding problems. Furthermore, we discuss the computational complexity of each method and explore techniques for accelerating computation. Through detailed explanations, illustrative examples, and a comprehensive review of the literature, this paper offers a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners seeking to understand and apply SNE with Gaussian and Student-t distributions for effective data visualization and analysis. Keywords: Stochastic Neighbor Embedding, dimensionality reduction, visualization, Gaussian distribution, Student-t distribution, t-SNE, data analysis.

This paper addresses the challenge of few-shot segmentation of volumetric images, a crucial task in medical imaging and computer vision. Our objective is to develop an efficient and accurate approach for segmenting volumetric images with limited annotated data. We propose a novel 'Squeeze & Excite' guided framework, which leverages the power of attention mechanisms and few-shot learning techniques. Our approach utilizes a compact convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, combined with a 'Squeeze & Excite' block that selectively weighs the importance of features, allowing the model to focus on relevant regions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets with significant reductions in annotation requirements. The key findings of this research highlight the potential of 'Squeeze & Excite' guided few-shot learning for volumetric image segmentation, enabling accurate and efficient analysis of medical images with minimal labeled data. This work contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis, computer vision, and few-shot learning, with potential applications in clinical diagnosis, treatment planning, and personalized medicine, and is relevant to keywords such as few-shot learning, volumetric image segmentation, attention mechanisms, and medical imaging.

Deep neural network (DNN) weight pruning effectively reduces model size and computational cost, enabling deployment on resource-constrained mobile devices. However, existing pruning techniques often result in irregular sparsity patterns, hindering efficient hardware acceleration and real-time execution. This paper introduces PCONV, a novel pruning strategy that enforces a predefined, structured sparsity pattern characterized by contiguous blocks of zero weights within convolution filters. Our method optimizes a sparsity mask during training to maximize accuracy under this constraint, leveraging a differentiable approximation of the L0 norm. Experiments on various DNN architectures, including MobileNetV2 and ResNet-50, demonstrate that PCONV achieves comparable or superior accuracy compared to unstructured pruning methods at similar sparsity ratios. Furthermore, the structured sparsity enables significant speedups in inference time on mobile devices due to improved memory access patterns and reduced overhead in specialized convolution kernels. PCONV offers a practical solution for deploying high-performance DNNs on mobile platforms, bridging the gap between model compression and real-time execution. Keywords: DNN, weight pruning, sparsity, mobile devices, real-time execution, structured sparsity, hardware acceleration.

Scene text detection and recognition are critical for various applications, yet their performance often suffers due to the scarcity of annotated data and domain gaps between training and real-world images. This paper introduces a novel approach for generating verisimilar synthetic images to augment training datasets and improve the accuracy of text detection and recognition models. Our method leverages a combination of advanced rendering techniques, realistic texture synthesis, and contextual scene integration to create synthetic images that closely resemble real-world scenes. We employ a generative adversarial network (GAN)-based approach to refine the synthetic images, enhancing their realism and reducing the domain gap. Experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that training with our synthetically generated data significantly boosts the performance of state-of-the-art text detection and recognition models, achieving improvements of up to 15% in F1-score. The results highlight the effectiveness of our approach in creating high-quality synthetic data for scene text analysis, facilitating the development of more robust and accurate systems. Keywords: Scene Text Detection, Scene Text Recognition, Synthetic Data Generation, Image Synthesis, Generative Adversarial Networks, Domain Adaptation.

Bệnh viêm phế quản cấp là một tình trạng viêm nhiễm đường hô hấp phổ biến, thường gặp ở nhiều đối tượng, đặc biệt là trẻ em và người cao tuổi. Việc chẩn đoán và điều trị kịp thời là rất quan trọng để ngăn ngừa biến chứng và cải thiện sức khỏe cho bệnh nhân. Các phương pháp điều trị bao gồm sử dụng thuốc kháng viêm, thuốc giãn phế quản và các biện pháp hỗ trợ khác nhằm giảm triệu chứng và phục hồi chức năng hô hấp.

Thị trường chứng khoán đang ngày càng trở nên phức tạp và đa dạng, thu hút sự quan tâm của nhiều nhà đầu tư cá nhân. Tâm lý là một trong những yếu tố hành vi quan trọng nhất ảnh hưởng đến quyết định đầu tư. Nhà đầu tư cá nhân thường bị ảnh hưởng bởi cảm xúc như sợ hãi, hối tiếc, và niềm tin. Họ có thể đầu tư vào các công ty có tiềm năng cao nhưng lại sợ hãi khi thị trường biến động. Ngoài ra, họ cũng có thể đầu tư vào các công ty có kết quả kinh doanh tốt nhưng lại hối tiếc khi giá cổ phiếu giảm. Kinh nghiệm cũng là một yếu tố hành vi quan trọng ảnh hưởng đến quyết định đầu tư. Tuy nhiên, kinh nghiệm không phải lúc nào cũng chính xác và có thể dẫn đến các quyết định đầu tư sai lầm. Thông tin cũng là một yếu tố hành vi quan trọng ảnh hưởng đến quyết định đầu tư. Nhà đầu tư cá nhân thường dựa vào thông tin từ các nguồn khác nhau để đưa ra quyết định đầu tư. Họ có thể đọc báo cáo tài chính, xem xét các chỉ số kỹ thuật, và tham khảo ý kiến của các chuyên gia. Tuy nhiên, thông tin không phải lúc nào cũng chính xác và có thể dẫn đến các quyết định đầu tư sai lầm. Tóm lại, các yếu tố hành vi như tâm lý, kinh nghiệm, và thông tin có thể ảnh hưởng đến quyết định đầu tư của nhà đầu tư cá nhân trên thị trường chứng khoán. Nhà đầu tư cần phải hiểu rõ về các yếu tố hành vi này và áp dụng các chiến lược đầu tư phù hợp để đạt được kết quả tốt nhất.

This paper presents a novel approach to automatically designing Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures for medical image segmentation tasks. The objective is to develop an efficient and effective method for segmenting medical images, such as tumors, organs, and tissues, without requiring extensive manual architecture design. Our approach utilizes a reinforcement learning-based framework to search for optimal CNN architectures, leveraging a combination of convolutional and pooling layers to achieve state-of-the-art performance. The results demonstrate that our automatically designed architectures outperform manually crafted ones on several benchmark datasets, including BraTS and ISBI. Key findings include improved segmentation accuracy, reduced computational requirements, and enhanced robustness to variations in image quality. The contributions of this research lie in its ability to automate the design process, reducing the need for expert knowledge and enabling widespread adoption of deep learning-based medical image segmentation. This work has significant implications for clinical applications, including disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient monitoring, and paves the way for further innovations in medical imaging analysis using AI and deep learning techniques, particularly CNNs, reinforcement learning, and medical image segmentation.

This paper proposes a novel approach to economic forecasting by leveraging Error Correction Neural Networks (ECNNs). The objective is to improve the accuracy of economic predictions by integrating the strengths of error correction models with the learning capabilities of neural networks. Our approach utilizes a hybrid model that combines the error correction mechanism with a neural network architecture, enabling the capture of both short-term and long-term dependencies in economic time series data. The results show that the ECNN outperforms traditional forecasting methods, including ARIMA and vector autoregression, in terms of mean absolute error and mean squared error. The key findings highlight the importance of incorporating error correction mechanisms into neural network architectures for economic forecasting. This research contributes to the development of more accurate and reliable economic forecasting models, with potential applications in policy-making, financial planning, and risk management. The use of ECNNs offers a novel perspective on economic forecasting, leveraging the benefits of machine learning and error correction to improve prediction accuracy. Key keywords: Error Correction Neural Networks, Economic Forecasting, Time Series Analysis, Neural Networks, Machine Learning.

This study investigates the performance of keypoint detectors and binary descriptors under various photometric and geometric transformations, aiming to identify robust feature extraction methods for computer vision applications. A comprehensive evaluation framework is developed, incorporating state-of-the-art keypoint detectors and binary descriptors, to assess their sensitivity to changes in illumination, rotation, scale, and affine transformations. The results show that certain keypoint detectors and binary descriptors outperform others in handling specific types of transformations, with significant implications for tasks such as object recognition, tracking, and 3D reconstruction. Notably, the study reveals that the combination of a robust keypoint detector with an efficient binary descriptor can achieve superior performance under real-world conditions. The findings of this research contribute to the development of more reliable and efficient computer vision systems, with potential applications in fields like robotics, autonomous vehicles, and surveillance. Key keywords: keypoint detection, binary descriptors, photometric transformations, geometric transformations, computer vision, feature extraction, object recognition.

This paper presents a novel approach for representation learning of pedestrian trajectories by leveraging an actor-critic sequence-to-sequence autoencoder architecture. Our primary objective is to devise a robust method for encoding and reconstructing sequential trajectory data, which is essential for applications such as pedestrian behavior analysis, anomaly detection, and intelligent surveillance systems. The proposed model integrates an actor-critic framework with a sequence-to-sequence autoencoder, enabling the system to effectively capture both spatial and temporal dependencies within trajectory sequences. The actor network encodes the input trajectories, while the critic guides the optimization process, ensuring higher fidelity in the learned latent representations. Experimental evaluation was conducted on widely-used pedestrian trajectory datasets, where the method demonstrated superior performance in terms of reconstruction error and downstream task utility, outperforming conventional autoencoders and other baseline models. The results illustrate that our approach not only preserves critical information within pedestrian movement patterns but also yields compact and discriminative embeddings suitable for various trajectory analysis tasks. These findings suggest significant potential for enhanced context-awareness in intelligent transportation and public safety applications. Keywords: trajectory representation learning, sequence-to-sequence autoencoder, actor-critic model, pedestrian movement, spatiotemporal analysis.

This paper introduces *Synthesize-It-Classifier*, a novel generative classifier that leverages recurrent self-analysis to enhance classification performance. The primary objective of this work is to address the limitations of traditional discriminative classifiers by integrating generative modeling techniques, enabling the system to synthesize and analyze data iteratively for improved decision-making. The proposed approach employs a recurrent neural architecture that dynamically refines its understanding of data distributions through self-analysis, allowing it to adapt to complex and evolving datasets. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that *Synthesize-It-Classifier* achieves superior accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art discriminative models, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data or high-dimensional inputs. The results highlight the model's ability to generate synthetic samples that align closely with the underlying data distribution, thereby improving classification performance. This research contributes a new paradigm for classification tasks, offering a generative framework that combines synthesis and analysis for enhanced learning. The implications of this work extend to applications in domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, and anomaly detection, where generative capabilities can significantly augment classification systems. **Keywords**: generative classifier, recurrent self-analysis, synthetic data generation, neural networks, classification, adaptive learning.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of accurately forecasting time series data, which is prevalent in various fields such as finance, weather prediction, and inventory management. The research aims to develop innovative theoretical frameworks and algorithms that enhance the predictive capabilities of existing models. Methods/Approach: To achieve this, we propose a robust methodology that combines statistical techniques with novel machine learning approaches. Our framework introduces an integrated model leveraging deep learning architectures and traditional autoregressive methods, optimizing predictive performance and adaptability to non-linear patterns. Key algorithms were developed and implemented, including enhancements to recurrent neural networks and hybrid models that incorporate dynamic feature selection. Results/Findings: Our experimental analysis demonstrates that the proposed algorithms significantly outperform traditional time series forecasting models in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Across diverse datasets, our methods achieved a reduction in prediction error rates by an average of 15% compared to leading benchmarks. Furthermore, the models exhibited robust performance across varying time intervals and for both stationary and non-stationary data. Conclusion/Implications: The results confirm the potential of our theoretical advancements and algorithms to transform time series forecasting practices. The study contributes valuable insights into model adaptability and cross-domain applicability, offering substantial improvements for industries reliant on precise forecasting. Our approach sets the groundwork for future research into scalable machine learning solutions for time series analysis, opening avenues for practical applications in automated forecasting systems and decision support tools. Keywords: Time Series Forecasting, Machine Learning, Recurrent Neural Networks, Autoregressive Models, Predictive Analytics, Algorithm Development.
