Deep neural networks are known to be vulnerable to adversarial examples, i.e., images that are maliciously perturbed to fool the model. Generating adversarial examples has been mostly limited to finding small perturbations that maximize the model prediction error. Such images, however, contain artificial perturbations that make them somewhat distinguishable from natural images. This property is used by several defense methods to counter adversarial examples by applying denoising filters or training the model to be robust to small perturbations. In this paper, we introduce a new class of adversarial examples, namely "Semantic Adversarial Examples," as images that are arbitrarily perturbed to fool the model, but in such a way that the modified image semantically represents the same object as the original image. We formulate the problem of generating such images as a constrained optimization problem and develop an adversarial transformation based on the shape bias property of human cognitive system. In our method, we generate adversarial images by first converting the RGB image into the HSV (Hue, Saturation and Value) color space and then randomly shifting the Hue and Saturation components, while keeping the Value component the same. Our experimental results on CIFAR10 dataset show that the accuracy of VGG16 network on adversarial color-shifted images is 5.7%.

This paper addresses the challenges and considerations involved in deploying clinical machine learning models in real-world healthcare settings. The objective is to identify key factors that influence the successful integration of machine learning algorithms into clinical practice. A comprehensive approach is taken, combining insights from machine learning, healthcare policy, and clinical decision-making. The methods involve a mixed-methods analysis of existing literature, expert interviews, and case studies of successful deployments. The results highlight the importance of data quality, model interpretability, and clinical validation in ensuring the safe and effective use of machine learning in healthcare. The findings also emphasize the need for multidisciplinary collaboration, robust testing, and ongoing monitoring to address potential biases and errors. The conclusion underscores the potential of clinical machine learning to improve patient outcomes, while emphasizing the need for careful consideration of the complexities and challenges involved in deployment. Key contributions include a framework for evaluating the readiness of machine learning models for clinical deployment and recommendations for healthcare organizations seeking to leverage machine learning for improved patient care. Relevant keywords: clinical machine learning, deployment, healthcare, AI, model interpretability, data quality.

This paper presents a novel approach to object detection and tracking using a fully convolutional neural network (FCNN) with heatmap-based techniques. The primary objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of detecting and tracking objects in complex environments, particularly in scenarios with occlusions and dynamic backgrounds. The proposed method leverages a heatmap representation to localize objects, enabling precise detection and robust tracking across consecutive frames. The FCNN architecture is designed to process input images directly, eliminating the need for region proposal networks and reducing computational overhead. The approach was evaluated on benchmark datasets, including COCO and MOTChallenge, and compared against state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in detection accuracy and tracking robustness, with a notable reduction in false positives and computational latency. The heatmap-based framework also exhibits superior performance in handling occlusions and maintaining object identity over time. This research contributes to the field of computer vision by introducing a lightweight yet powerful solution for real-time object detection and tracking. The proposed method has potential applications in autonomous vehicles, surveillance systems, and robotics, where accurate and efficient object localization is critical. Key innovations include the integration of heatmap-based localization with FCNN, enabling end-to-end training and inference without compromising performance. **Keywords**: Object detection, object tracking, fully convolutional neural network, heatmap, computer vision, real-time systems.

We study the sample complexity of model-based reinforcement learning (henceforth RL) in general contextual decision processes that require strategic exploration to find a near-optimal policy. We design new algorithms for RL with a generic model class and analyze their statistical properties. Our algorithms have sample complexity governed by a new structural parameter called the witness rank, which we show to be small in several settings of interest, including factored MDPs. We also show that the witness rank is never larger than the recently proposed Bellman rank parameter governing the sample complexity of the model-free algorithm OLIVE (Jiang et al., 2017), the only other provably sample-efficient algorithm for global exploration at this level of generality. Focusing on the special case of factored MDPs, we prove an exponential lower bound for a general class of model-free approaches, including OLIVE, which, when combined with our algorithmic results, demonstrates exponential separation between model-based and model-free RL in some rich-observation settings.

This paper presents a novel approach to video scene graph generation, focusing on target adaptive context aggregation. The objective is to improve the accuracy of scene graph generation by effectively capturing contextual relationships between objects in videos. Our method employs a graph-based neural network that adaptively aggregates context from target objects, enabling more precise representation of complex scenes. The approach utilizes a multi-scale attention mechanism to weigh the importance of different contextual information. Experimental results demonstrate that our target adaptive context aggregation method outperforms existing state-of-the-art models, achieving significant improvements in scene graph generation accuracy. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a dynamic context aggregation mechanism and the application of a graph-based neural network to video scene graph generation. This work has important implications for various applications, including video understanding, object detection, and robotic vision. Key keywords: video scene graph generation, target adaptive context aggregation, graph-based neural networks, multi-scale attention, computer vision.

**Abstract** Regulatory compliance and model validation remain critical challenges for implementing ensemble machine learning methods such as bagging in the retail banking sector. This paper introduces XtracTree, a simple yet effective method designed to enhance the transparency and regulatory validation of bagging algorithms, such as Random Forests and Bagged Decision Trees, widely used for credit scoring and risk assessment. XtracTree enables interpretable model auditing by extracting a representative set of decision trees that accurately reflect the underlying ensemble’s predictive logic, while maintaining high model performance. We detail the XtracTree methodology, which systematically selects and analyzes trees using statistical measures of importance and diversity, providing clear, regulator-friendly documentation of ensemble behavior. Experimental evaluations on publicly available retail banking datasets demonstrate that XtracTree achieves regulatory validation objectives with minimal accuracy loss compared to the original bagging models, and significantly improves interpretability and auditability. The results suggest that XtracTree bridges the long-standing gap between model performance and regulatory transparency, enabling financial institutions to deploy robust machine learning models without compromising compliance requirements. This method holds promising implications for broader adoption of AI-driven decision-making in regulated environments. **Keywords:** bagging, interpretability, regulatory compliance, Random Forest, retail banking, explainability, model validation, ensemble learning.

Image super-resolution (SR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) images from low-resolution (LR) counterparts, playing a crucial role in applications such as medical imaging, surveillance, and computational photography. Traditional deep learning-based SR methods often rely on single-image inputs, limiting their ability to capture diverse structural and texture details. To address this limitation, we propose an Attention-based Multi-Reference Learning (AMRL) framework, which leverages multiple reference images to enhance SR performance. Our approach employs an attention-driven feature fusion mechanism that dynamically selects and integrates relevant information from multiple high-quality reference images. Specifically, we design a cross-reference attention module to align spatial and contextual features across different sources, ensuring effective transfer of fine-grained details. Furthermore, a multi-scale refinement strategy is introduced to progressively enhance high-frequency components while preserving image consistency. Extensive experiments on standard super-resolution benchmarks demonstrate that AMRL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics (PSNR, SSIM) and perceptual quality. The results highlight the effectiveness of multi-reference learning in improving texture reconstruction and fine detail preservation. Keywords: Image Super-Resolution, Multi-Reference Learning, Attention Mechanism, Feature Fusion, Deep Learning, High-Fidelity Image Reconstruction.

Kết quả: Sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thống kê giữa giá trị ADC đo tại trung tâm u và vùng thâm nhiễm (p < 0,05), với giá trị ADC của nhóm u bậc thấp cao hơn u bậc cao. Với giá trị điểm cắt ADC tại trung tâm u và vùng thâm nhiễm quanh u lần lượt là 0,99 x 10-3 mm2/s (độ nhạy = 73% và độ đặc hiệu = 91,7%) và 1,31 x 10-3 mm2/s (độ nhạy = 88,6% và độ đặc hiệu = 53,9%) có thể giúp phân bậc UTKĐ bậc cao và bậc thấp. Giá trị ADC ranh giới vùng thâm nhiễm - mô não bình thường và chất trắng bình thường đối bên không có sự khác biệt đáng kể giữa hai nhóm. Kết luận: Các giá trị ADC ở trung tâm u và vùng thâm nhiễm quanh u có thể giúp phân bậc UTKĐ, với giá trị ADC của nhóm u bậc thấp cao hơn u bậc cao. Giá trị ADC ranh giới vùng thâm nhiễm - mô não bình thường và chất trắng bình thường đối bên không có vai trò phân biệt UTKĐ bậc thấp và bậc cao.

Nghiên cứu đánh giá khả năng tự làm sạch của Hồ Tây, Hà Nội, tập trung vào các yếu tố thủy văn, chất lượng nước và trầm tích. Kết quả cho thấy hồ có khả năng tự làm sạch nhất định thông qua các quá trình vật lý, hóa học và sinh học. Tuy nhiên, mức độ ô nhiễm hữu cơ và phú dưỡng vẫn còn cao, đặc biệt là vào mùa khô. Cần có sự phối hợp giữa các cơ quan chức năng và cộng đồng để bảo vệ và phục hồi hệ sinh thái Hồ Tây một cách bền vững. Nghiên cứu cung cấp cơ sở khoa học cho việc đưa ra các quyết định quản lý và bảo tồn hồ.

This paper explores the critical landscape of interpretability and explainability within machine learning, offering a concise "mini-tour" of prominent techniques across diverse model types. We investigate methods for understanding how complex models, often considered "black boxes," arrive at their predictions. Our approach involves surveying a spectrum of interpretability techniques, ranging from model-agnostic methods like LIME and SHAP, applicable across various algorithms, to model-specific techniques tailored for linear models, decision trees, and neural networks. We comparatively analyze these techniques, focusing on their strengths, limitations, and applicability to different problem domains. The findings highlight the trade-offs between interpretability, accuracy, and computational cost associated with each method. Ultimately, this survey provides a valuable resource for practitioners seeking to enhance the transparency and trustworthiness of their machine learning deployments. Keywords: Interpretability, Explainability, Machine Learning, LIME, SHAP, Model-Agnostic, Transparency.

This paper presents a novel approach to gradient boosting by incorporating piece-wise linear regression trees as base learners, rather than the conventional piece-wise constant regression trees. The primary objective is to enhance the predictive accuracy and model expressiveness of gradient boosting algorithms, particularly in applications involving complex, non-linear relationships. The proposed method leverages trees whose leaf nodes represent linear models, allowing for a more flexible partitioning of the input space and improved fitting capabilities. To evaluate the effectiveness of this approach, extensive experiments were conducted on benchmark regression datasets. The results demonstrate that gradient boosting with piece-wise linear regression trees consistently outperforms traditional gradient boosted decision trees in terms of both root mean squared error and convergence speed. Comparative analyses highlight that the proposed method reduces overfitting and captures local trends within the data more effectively. Furthermore, an analysis of computational complexity shows that the overhead introduced by fitting linear models at the leaves is offset by faster convergence and improved generalization. This research advances the state-of-the-art in boosted ensemble methods by introducing a more powerful base learner while preserving the robustness and scalability of the gradient boosting framework. The findings have significant implications for fields such as machine learning, predictive analytics, and data mining, especially in scenarios demanding high model interpretability and performance. Future work will explore extensions to classification tasks and integration with distributed computing environments. Keywords: gradient boosting, regression trees, piece-wise linear models, ensemble learning, machine learning, predictive analytics

The exponential growth of the internet has seen a corresponding rise in malicious URLs, posing significant threats to users and organizations. This paper conducts a comprehensive survey of machine learning approaches for detecting malicious URLs, addressing the urgent need for effective and scalable detection methods. Methods/Approach: The paper reviews a wide array of machine learning models and techniques applied to the detection of malicious URLs. It explores supervised and unsupervised learning paradigms, including methods such as decision trees, support vector machines, neural networks, and ensemble methods. The survey evaluates different feature extraction techniques, highlighting those based on URL characteristics, host-based features, and content-based features. Results/Findings: Key findings indicate that machine learning models, especially those leveraging ensemble methods and neural networks, have shown promising results in terms of accuracy and adaptability in identifying malicious URLs. The survey identifies that feature engineering plays a critical role in enhancing model performance and that hybrid models combining multiple features and algorithms often yield superior detection rates. Conclusion/Implications: The paper underscores the significant contributions of machine learning to the field of cybersecurity, particularly in the automated detection of malicious URLs. It suggests potential areas for future research, emphasizing the importance of real-time detection capabilities and the integration of machine learning models with broader security systems. The findings aim to aid researchers and practitioners in developing more robust and effective solutions, enhancing the overall security of web platforms. Keywords: malicious URL detection, machine learning, cybersecurity, feature extraction, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, ensemble methods.

Ước lượng dòng điện phụ tải cho trạm điện kéo đường sắt đô thị là một yếu tố quan trọng trong việc đảm bảo hoạt động hiệu quả và an toàn của hệ thống giao thông công cộng. Việc xác định chính xác dòng điện cần thiết giúp tối ưu hóa thiết kế và vận hành trạm điện, từ đó nâng cao hiệu suất và giảm thiểu chi phí. Các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến dòng điện phụ tải bao gồm số lượng tàu hoạt động, tần suất di chuyển, và tải trọng của các đoàn tàu. Ngoài ra, việc phân tích các điều kiện môi trường và kỹ thuật cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc ước lượng chính xác. Kết quả của quá trình ước lượng này không chỉ giúp cải thiện chất lượng dịch vụ mà còn góp phần vào việc phát triển bền vững hệ thống giao thông đô thị.
Khả năng mở rộng (Scalability). Các tiến trình tương tự này cho phép mở rộng quy mô hệ thống một cách dễ dàng, theo chiều ngang hoặc theo chiều dọc.

Các công ty xây dựng tại tỉnh An Giang đang ngày càng chú trọng đến việc thực hiện trách nhiệm xã hội, không chỉ đóng góp vào sự phát triển kinh tế mà còn quan tâm đến các vấn đề môi trường và cộng đồng. Nhiều doanh nghiệp đã triển khai các dự án xây dựng xanh, sử dụng vật liệu thân thiện với môi trường và tiết kiệm năng lượng. Bên cạnh đó, các công ty cũng tích cực tham gia vào các hoạt động từ thiện, hỗ trợ giáo dục và y tế cho người dân địa phương. Việc thực hiện trách nhiệm xã hội không chỉ giúp nâng cao hình ảnh của doanh nghiệp mà còn góp phần tạo dựng niềm tin và sự gắn kết với cộng đồng. Tuy nhiên, vẫn còn một số thách thức như thiếu nguồn lực và nhận thức chưa đầy đủ về tầm quan trọng của trách nhiệm xã hội trong một số doanh nghiệp nhỏ.

Mục tiêu: Mô tả đặc điểm lâm sàng và hình ảnh nội soi phế quản của bệnh nhân u máu hạ thanh môn (UMHTM). Đối tượng nghiên cứu: 25 bệnh nhân được chẩn đoán và điều trị UMHTM tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương từ 1/6/2018 đến 30/5/2023. Phương pháp nghiên cứu: Mô tả cắt ngang hồi cứu và tiến cứu. Kết quả: Tuổi trung vị 2,7 tháng, dao động từ 20 ngày tuổi đến 20 tháng, tỷ lệ nữ/nam là 2,1/1. Tuổi khởi phát tiếng thở rít 30,7±20,6 ngày. Thời gian kéo dài triệu chứng thở rít trung bình 51,3±47,5 ngày. Đặc điểm lâm sàng: Thở rít (80%), co kéo hõm trên ức (76%), suy hô hấp (72%), ho (36%), u máu ngoài da (8%), ăn sặc (8%). Kết quả nội soi phế quản (NSPQ): 92% khối u có màu đỏ, thành nhẵn. Vị trí khối u: 36% bao quanh chu vi, 32% khối u xuất phát từ thành bên phải, 28% từ thành bên trái, 4% từ thành sau hạ thanh môn, 8% u lan xuống dưới khí quản 1 cm. Về kích thước khối u, chủ yếu hẹp độ III (60%) và độ II (32%). Kết luận: UMHTM là một trong những bệnh lý hiếm gặp, gây thở rít khởi phát sớm ở trẻ dưới 6 tháng, đặc điểm thở rít kéo dài, tái diễn, có thể gây khó thở thanh quản. Chẩn đoán chủ yếu dựa vào nội soi phế quản, quan sát màu sắc, đặc điểm hình thái, kích thước khối u.

Nghiên cứu về sự hài lòng của người nộp thuế tại Chi cục Thuế huyện Na Hang, tỉnh Tuyên Quang cho thấy mức độ hài lòng chung ở mức khá cao, tuy nhiên vẫn còn những khía cạnh cần được cải thiện. Các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến sự hài lòng bao gồm: thái độ phục vụ của cán bộ thuế, tính chuyên nghiệp, sự minh bạch trong quy trình, thủ tục, và cơ sở vật chất. Người nộp thuế đánh giá cao sự tận tình, chu đáo của cán bộ thuế, nhưng mong muốn rút ngắn thời gian giải quyết thủ tục, tăng cường ứng dụng công nghệ thông tin, và cải thiện cơ sở hạ tầng. Kết quả khảo sát là cơ sở để Chi cục Thuế huyện Na Hang đưa ra các giải pháp nâng cao chất lượng phục vụ, đáp ứng tốt hơn nhu cầu của người nộp thuế, góp phần tăng cường hiệu quả quản lý thuế trên địa bàn. Điều này đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc xây dựng hệ thống thuế công khai, minh bạch và hiệu quả, tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho người dân và doanh nghiệp thực hiện nghĩa vụ thuế.

El Niño, a complex climate phenomenon, has significant global impacts on weather patterns, agriculture, and economies. Traditional forecasting methods often struggle to capture the intricate spatial and temporal dependencies inherent in climate data. This paper proposes a novel approach to improve El Niño forecasts by modeling the Earth's climate system as a graph, leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to capture the relationships between geographically distributed climate variables. Our method represents climate data as nodes and edges in a graph, where nodes correspond to specific geographic locations and edges encode spatial relationships. We introduce a GNN-based architecture that integrates multi-modal climate data, including sea surface temperatures, atmospheric pressure, and wind patterns, to predict El Niño events with higher accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional statistical and machine learning models, achieving a 15% improvement in prediction accuracy over a 12-month forecast horizon. The proposed framework not only enhances the precision of El Niño forecasts but also provides interpretable insights into the underlying climate dynamics. This research highlights the potential of GNNs in advancing climate science and offers a scalable solution for other spatiotemporal prediction tasks. **Keywords**: El Niño, Graph Neural Networks, climate forecasting, spatiotemporal modeling, machine learning, climate dynamics.

Nghiên cứu về ảnh hưởng của các kỹ năng nghề nghiệp tới khả năng được tuyển dụng dựa trên cảm nhận của sinh viên cho thấy rằng, việc trang bị đầy đủ kỹ năng mềm và kỹ năng chuyên môn đóng vai trò quan trọng trong quá trình tìm kiếm việc làm. Sinh viên nhận thức rõ rằng các kỹ năng như giao tiếp, làm việc nhóm, quản lý thời gian và tư duy phản biện không chỉ giúp họ nổi bật trong mắt nhà tuyển dụng mà còn tăng cơ hội cạnh tranh trên thị trường lao động. Bên cạnh đó, kỹ năng chuyên môn vững vàng cũng được xem là yếu tố then chốt, đặc biệt trong các ngành nghề đòi hỏi kiến thức sâu rộng. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng, sinh viên có xu hướng đánh giá cao tầm quan trọng của việc liên tục cập nhật và trau dồi kỹ năng để đáp ứng yêu cầu ngày càng cao của thị trường việc làm hiện đại.

Phát triển ứng dụng meeting dựa trên video conferencing sử dụng công nghệ WebRTC là một hướng tiếp cận hiện đại nhằm đáp ứng nhu cầu giao tiếp trực tuyến ngày càng tăng trong các lĩnh vực như giáo dục, kinh doanh và làm việc từ xa. WebRTC, một công nghệ mã nguồn mở, cho phép truyền tải âm thanh, video và dữ liệu trực tiếp giữa các trình duyệt mà không cần phần mềm trung gian, mang lại hiệu suất cao và độ trễ thấp. Ứng dụng này tập trung vào việc tích hợp các tính năng cốt lõi như phòng họp ảo, chia sẻ màn hình, chat trực tuyến và quản lý người dùng, đồng thời đảm bảo tính bảo mật thông qua mã hóa dữ liệu đầu cuối. Quá trình phát triển bao gồm việc thiết kế giao diện người dùng thân thiện, tối ưu hóa hiệu năng để hỗ trợ đa nền tảng và xử lý các thách thức kỹ thuật như tương thích trình duyệt, cân bằng tải và quản lý băng thông. Do đó, việc lựa chọn vật liệu và thiết kế công tắc phù hợp là rất quan trọng để đạt được hiệu suất tốt nhất của động cơ điện.

Abstract Accurate forecasting and causal analysis of multivariate time series are essential in domains ranging from economics to neuroscience, yet classical vector autoregressions (VAR) struggle to capture nonlinear dependencies and complex dynamics. We propose Neural Vector Autoregressions (NVAR), a unified framework that integrates deep neural networks with autoregressive modeling to jointly address forecasting, causality inference, and impulse response estimation. NVAR employs a modular architecture that learns flexible, nonlinear interactions among variables while enforcing sparsity constraints for interpretable Granger-causal structures. To compute impulse responses, we derive a local linearization of the trained network around its operating point, enabling dynamic analysis of system shocks. Extensive experiments on synthetic data and real-world financial and neural recordings demonstrate that NVAR reduces forecasting error by up to 20% compared to linear VAR and kernel-based baselines, and achieves higher precision and recall in detecting causal links. Furthermore, the recovered impulse responses closely match ground-truth dynamics under diverse scenarios. Our results show that NVAR delivers both predictive accuracy and interpretability, offering a powerful tool for time series analysis. This approach opens new avenues for robust decision support in economics, epidemiology, climate science, and other fields that rely on understanding complex temporal interactions. Keywords: Neural VAR, multivariate time series forecasting, Granger causality, impulse response analysis, nonlinear dynamics, sparse modeling

Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) implement a specific form of multi-variate extrapolation and will generate an output for any input pattern, even when there is no similar training pattern. Extrapolations are not necessarily to be trusted, and in order to support safety critical systems, we require such systems to give an indication of the training sample related uncertainty associated with their output. Some readers may think that this is a well known issue which is already covered by the basic principles of pattern recognition. We will explain below how this is not the case and how the conventional (Likelihood estimate of) conditional probability of classification does not correctly assess this uncertainty. We provide a discussion of the standard interpretations of this problem and show how a quantitative approach based upon long standing methods can be practically applied. The methods are illustrated on the task of early diagnosis of dementing diseases using Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

This paper addresses the challenge of interpreting complex 3D point cloud data by introducing a novel approach to feature explanations using gradient-based methods. Our objective is to provide insights into the decisions made by deep learning models when processing 3D point clouds, which is crucial for applications such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and scene understanding. We employ a gradient-based explanation technique, adapted for 3D point cloud data, to highlight the most relevant points and features that contribute to the model's predictions. Our method utilizes a combination of gradient-based attribution and feature importance scores to generate explanations for 3D point cloud classifications. The results show that our approach can effectively identify the most salient points and features in the point cloud, leading to improved model interpretability and transparency. Our contribution is a significant step towards explainable 3D point cloud analysis, with potential applications in various fields, including computer vision, robotics, and geographic information systems. Key keywords: 3D point clouds, gradient-based explanations, deep learning, interpretability, feature attribution.

This paper revisits the concept of visual odometry, a crucial component in various computer vision and robotics applications. The objective is to investigate the key elements that should be learned to improve the accuracy and robustness of visual odometry systems. We propose a novel approach that leverages deep learning techniques to learn robust feature representations and motion models. Our method utilizes a combination of convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks to estimate camera poses from monocular image sequences. The results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of translation and rotation errors on benchmark datasets. We conclude that visual odometry can be significantly improved by learning informative features and motion patterns, and our work provides new insights into the design of more accurate and efficient visual odometry systems. The contributions of this research have important implications for applications such as autonomous vehicles, augmented reality, and robotics, where accurate visual odometry is essential. Key keywords: visual odometry, deep learning, computer vision, robotics, motion estimation.

Real-time physically-based rendering (PBR) on embedded devices presents a significant challenge due to limited computational resources. This paper introduces LumiPath, a novel rendering pipeline optimized for achieving high-fidelity visuals on resource-constrained platforms. LumiPath employs a hybrid approach combining path tracing with precomputed radiance transfer (PRT) to balance accuracy and performance. We leverage a spatially-aware sampling strategy and a customized material representation tailored for embedded systems to minimize computational overhead. The system is implemented using a custom rendering engine, allowing for fine-grained control over the rendering process. Performance evaluation demonstrates that LumiPath achieves interactive frame rates while maintaining visual quality comparable to offline PBR renderers. The results highlight the feasibility of implementing advanced rendering techniques on embedded devices, opening up new possibilities for mobile gaming, augmented reality, and other applications. Keywords: Physically-based rendering, path tracing, embedded systems, real-time rendering, mobile graphics, precomputed radiance transfer.

This paper introduces Neural Bellman-Ford Networks, a novel graph neural network framework designed for link prediction tasks. The objective is to develop a general and scalable approach that can effectively learn representations of nodes and edges in complex graphs. Our method leverages the Bellman-Ford algorithm as a foundation, incorporating neural network components to enhance its expressive power. The Neural Bellman-Ford Network is trained using a combination of unsupervised and supervised learning objectives, enabling it to capture both local and global graph structures. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art graph neural network models on several benchmark datasets. The key findings highlight the importance of integrating traditional graph algorithms with deep learning techniques, leading to improved performance and interpretability. This research contributes to the advancement of graph neural networks, with potential applications in recommendation systems, social network analysis, and knowledge graph completion. Key keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Link Prediction, Bellman-Ford Algorithm, Deep Learning, Node Representation Learning.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) achieved great cognitive performance at the expense of considerable computation load. To relieve the computation load, many optimization works are developed to reduce the model redundancy by identifying and removing insignificant model components, such as weight sparsity and filter pruning. However, these works only evaluate model components' static significance with internal parameter information, ignoring their dynamic interaction with external inputs. With per-input feature activation, the model component significance can dynamically change, and thus the static methods can only achieve sub-optimal results. Therefore, we propose a dynamic CNN optimization framework in this work. Based on the neural network attention mechanism, we propose a comprehensive dynamic optimization framework including (1) testing-phase channel and column feature map pruning, as well as (2) training-phase optimization by targeted dropout. Such a dynamic optimization framework has several benefits: (1) First, it can accurately identify and aggressively remove per-input feature redundancy with considering the model-input interaction; (2) Meanwhile, it can maximally remove the feature map redundancy in various dimensions thanks to the multi-dimension flexibility; (3) The training-testing co-optimization favors the dynamic pruning and helps maintain the model accuracy even with very high feature pruning ratio. Extensive experiments show that our method could bring 37.4% to 54.5% FLOPs reduction with negligible accuracy drop on various of test networks.

This paper addresses the challenge of predicting regression probability distributions when dealing with imperfect data, a common issue in real-world applications. Our objective is to develop a robust method that can effectively handle noisy, missing, or uncertain data. To achieve this, we propose an innovative approach based on optimal transformations, which enables the estimation of regression probability distributions with improved accuracy. Our method involves a novel transformation technique that adaptively adjusts to the underlying data characteristics, allowing for more reliable predictions. The results show that our approach outperforms existing methods, particularly in scenarios with high levels of data imperfection. Key findings indicate that the proposed optimal transformations can significantly reduce prediction errors and improve the overall quality of the estimated probability distributions. The implications of this research are substantial, as it contributes to the development of more robust and reliable predictive models in various fields, such as machine learning, artificial intelligence, and data science. By providing a novel solution to the problem of imperfect data, this study paves the way for more accurate and informative predictions, with potential applications in areas like uncertainty quantification, risk analysis, and decision-making under uncertainty. Keywords: regression probability distributions, imperfect data, optimal transformations, predictive modeling, uncertainty quantification.

Incremental Learning (IL) is an interesting AI problem when the algorithm is assumed to work on a budget. This is especially true when IL is modeled using a deep learning approach, where two com- plex challenges arise due to limited memory, which induces catastrophic forgetting and delays related to the retraining needed in order to incorpo- rate new classes. Here we introduce DeeSIL, an adaptation of a known transfer learning scheme that combines a fixed deep representation used as feature extractor and learning independent shallow classifiers to in- crease recognition capacity. This scheme tackles the two aforementioned challenges since it works well with a limited memory budget and each new concept can be added within a minute. Moreover, since no deep re- training is needed when the model is incremented, DeeSIL can integrate larger amounts of initial data that provide more transferable features. Performance is evaluated on ImageNet LSVRC 2012 against three state of the art algorithms. Results show that, at scale, DeeSIL performance is 23 and 33 points higher than the best baseline when using the same and more initial data respectively.

In recent years, the need for effective ranking of structured objects has emerged in various fields, including bioinformatics, information retrieval, and social network analysis. Traditional ranking algorithms often struggle to capture complex dependencies inherent in structured data. This paper addresses this challenge by exploring the potential of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to improve the ranking processes for such nuanced information structures. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel framework leveraging Graph Neural Networks for ranking structured objects, where objects and their relationships are represented in a graph format. Our approach involves constructing a graph model, where nodes represent structured objects and edges capture their interactions. A specialized GNN is then applied to extract and learn meaningful patterns from these graphs to generate effective rankings. The model incorporates propagation and aggregation techniques, optimizing the neural network's ability to discern complex relational patterns, which traditional methods fail to address. Results/Findings: The proposed GNN framework was tested on multiple datasets representing various structured data scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance in accuracy and ranking quality compared to existing state-of-the-art algorithms. Moreover, our methodology proved particularly beneficial in understanding the latent relationships and dependencies that affect the ranking outcomes critically. Conclusion/Implications: This study introduces a significant advance in the domain of ranking structured data through Graph Neural Networks. By effectively capturing intricate dependencies within data structures, the proposed model offers enhanced accuracy and efficiency. The results suggest potential applications in areas requiring sophisticated data interpretation and ranking, such as personalized recommendation systems and complex network analysis. With these findings, we open new avenues for leveraging the power of GNNs in various structured object ranking problems. Keywords: Graph Neural Networks, ranking, structured objects, data dependencies, algorithm performance, personalized recommendation systems.

Sự hài lòng của sinh viên khối cử nhân về học trực tuyến đồng bộ tại Trường Đại học Y khoa Phạm Ngọc Thảo đang trở thành chủ đề nóng được nhiều người quan tâm. Sinh viên cho biết, học trực tuyến đồng bộ giúp họ tiết kiệm thời gian và chi phí đi lại, đồng thời cũng có thể học tập tại bất kỳ nơi nào có kết nối internet. Tuy nhiên, cũng có một số sinh viên cho rằng, học trực tuyến đồng bộ còn hạn chế về mặt tương tác giữa sinh viên và giảng viên. Một số sinh viên còn cảm thấy khó khăn khi phải học tập trong môi trường không gian ảo. Mặc dù vậy, đa số sinh viên vẫn cho rằng, học trực tuyến đồng bộ là một phương thức học tập hiệu quả và cần được phát triển hơn nữa. Trường Đại học Y khoa Phạm Ngọc Thảo cũng đang nỗ lực để cải thiện và hoàn thiện phương thức học trực tuyến đồng bộ, nhằm mang lại trải nghiệm học tập tốt nhất cho sinh viên.

Structured Gaussian process (GP) models are widely used for modeling complex, high-dimensional data in various applications, such as spatiotemporal analysis and machine learning. However, traditional GP inference methods often struggle with scalability and computational efficiency, particularly when dealing with structured data. This paper introduces a novel gray-box inference approach that combines the interpretability of white-box models with the flexibility of black-box methods to address these challenges. Our approach leverages domain-specific knowledge to impose structure on the GP prior, enabling efficient inference while maintaining model accuracy. We propose a hybrid framework that integrates structured priors with scalable approximation techniques, such as sparse variational inference, to achieve significant computational savings without sacrificing predictive performance. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing GP inference techniques in terms of both computational efficiency and predictive accuracy. The proposed approach not only advances the state-of-the-art in structured GP modeling but also provides a practical solution for large-scale applications in areas such as environmental monitoring and time-series forecasting. This work highlights the potential of gray-box methods to bridge the gap between interpretability and scalability in probabilistic modeling. **Keywords**: Gaussian process, gray-box inference, structured models, scalable inference, spatiotemporal analysis, probabilistic modeling.

Short-term forecasting of passenger flow is critical for transit management and crowd regulation. Spatial dependencies, temporal dependencies, inter-station correlations driven by other latent factors, and exogenous factors bring challenges to the short-term forecasts of passenger flow of urban rail transit networks. An innovative deep learning approach, Multi-Graph Convolutional-Recurrent Neural Network (MGC-RNN) is proposed to forecast passenger flow in urban rail transit systems to incorporate these complex factors. We propose to use multiple graphs to encode the spatial and other heterogenous inter-station correlations. The temporal dynamics of the inter-station correlations are also modeled via the proposed multi-graph convolutional-recurrent neural network structure. Inflow and outflow of all stations can be collectively predicted with multiple time steps ahead via a sequence to sequence(seq2seq) architecture. The proposed method is applied to the short-term forecasts of passenger flow in Shenzhen Metro, China. The experimental results show that MGC-RNN outperforms the benchmark algorithms in terms of forecasting accuracy. Besides, it is found that the inter-station driven by network distance, network structure, and recent flow patterns are significant factors for passenger flow forecasting. Moreover, the architecture of LSTM-encoder-decoder can capture the temporal dependencies well. In general, the proposed framework could provide multiple views of passenger flow dynamics for fine prediction and exhibit a possibility for multi-source heterogeneous data fusion in the spatiotemporal forecast tasks.

We present a new method for forecasting systems of multiple interrelated time series. The method learns the forecast models together with discovering leading indicators from within the system that serve as good predictors improving the forecast accuracy and a cluster structure of the predictive tasks around these. The method is based on the classical linear vector autoregressive model (VAR) and links the discovery of the leading indicators to inferring sparse graphs of Granger causality. We formulate a new constrained optimisation problem to promote the desired sparse structures across the models and the sharing of information amongst the learning tasks in a multi-task manner. We propose an algorithm for solving the problem and document on a battery of synthetic and real-data experiments the advantages of our new method over baseline VAR models as well as the state-of-the-art sparse VAR learning methods.

In the domain of video action recognition, accurately identifying key actions over time remains a challenge due to dynamic scene changes and varying temporal relevance of visual cues. This research introduces Temporal Saliency Integration (TSI), a novel method designed to enhance the precision of action recognition by effectively aggregating salient temporal information. Methods/Approach: TSI leverages a specialized algorithm that integrates temporal saliency maps, highlighting the most relevant frames and sequences in a video segment. This approach improves upon traditional methods by employing an adaptive weighting mechanism that dynamically adjusts the focus on temporal elements exhibiting the highest indicative value for recognizing actions. The model was trained and validated using diverse video datasets to assess its adaptability and robustness across different action classes. Results/Findings: Experiments demonstrate that TSI significantly outperforms existing baseline models in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method achieved state-of-the-art results on benchmark video action recognition datasets, showcasing enhanced detection of subtle and complex actions. Furthermore, TSI's integration strategy reduced processing time while maintaining high accuracy, highlighting its practical applicability in real-time systems. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of TSI presents a breakthrough in video action recognition by addressing the temporal saliency challenge. This research contributes a scalable solution with potential applications in areas such as surveillance, sports analytics, and human-computer interaction. The success of TSI in improving action recognition performance underscores its value as a cornerstone for future advancements in video analysis technologies. Keywords: video action recognition, temporal saliency, TSI, adaptive weighting, real-time systems, video analysis technologies.

Design of cyber-physical systems (CPSs) is a challenging task that involves searching over a large search space of various CPS configurations and possible values of components composing the system. Hence, there is a need for sample-efficient CPS design space exploration to select the system architecture and component values that meet the target system requirements. We address this challenge by formulating CPS design as a multi-objective optimization problem and propose DISPATCH, a two-step methodology for sample-efficient search over the design space. First, we use a genetic algorithm to search over discrete choices of system component values for architecture search and component selection or only component selection and terminate the algorithm even before meeting the system requirements, thus yielding a coarse design. In the second step, we use an inverse design to search over a continuous space to fine-tune the component values and meet the diverse set of system requirements. We use a neural network as a surrogate function for the inverse design of the system. The neural network, converted into a mixed-integer linear program, is used for active learning to sample component values efficiently in a continuous search space. We illustrate the efficacy of DISPATCH on electrical circuit benchmarks: two-stage and three-stage transimpedence amplifiers. Simulation results show that the proposed methodology improves sample efficiency by 5-14x compared to a prior synthesis method that relies on reinforcement learning. It also synthesizes circuits with the best performance (highest bandwidth/lowest area) compared to designs synthesized using reinforcement learning, Bayesian optimization, or humans.

Space-time video super-resolution (STVSR) aims to increase the spatial and temporal resolutions of low-resolution and low-frame-rate videos. Recently, deformable convolution based methods have achieved promising STVSR performance, but they could only infer the intermediate frame pre-defined in the training stage. Besides, these methods undervalued the short-term motion cues among adjacent frames. In this paper, we propose a Temporal Modulation Network (TMNet) to interpolate arbitrary intermediate frame(s) with accurate high-resolution reconstruction. Specifically, we propose a Temporal Modulation Block (TMB) to modulate deformable convolution kernels for controllable feature interpolation. To well exploit the temporal information, we propose a Locally-temporal Feature Comparison (LFC) module, along with the Bi-directional Deformable ConvLSTM, to extract short-term and long-term motion cues in videos. Experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our TMNet outperforms previous STVSR methods. The code is available at https://github.com/CS-GangXu/TMNet.

Automotive Cyber-Physical Systems (ACPS) have attracted a significant amount of interest in the past few decades, while one of the most critical operations in these systems is the perception of the environment. Deep learning and, especially, the use of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) provides impressive results in analyzing and understanding complex and dynamic scenes from visual data. The prediction horizons for those perception systems are very short and inference must often be performed in real time, stressing the need of transforming the original large pre-trained networks into new smaller models, by utilizing Model Compression and Acceleration (MCA) techniques. Our goal in this work is to investigate best practices for appropriately applying novel weight sharing techniques, optimizing the available variables and the training procedures towards the significant acceleration of widely adopted DNNs. Extensive evaluation studies carried out using various state-of-the-art DNN models in object detection and tracking experiments, provide details about the type of errors that manifest after the application of weight sharing techniques, resulting in significant acceleration gains with negligible accuracy losses.

This paper presents a novel approach to point cloud colorization, leveraging a densely annotated 3D shape dataset to achieve high-fidelity results. The objective is to develop an effective method for assigning realistic colors to 3D point clouds, enhancing their visual appeal and usefulness in various applications. Our approach employs a deep learning-based model, utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to learn the complex relationships between 3D geometry and color information. The model is trained on a large-scale dataset of densely annotated 3D shapes, allowing it to capture subtle nuances in color distribution and texture. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our method, achieving significant improvements in colorization accuracy and visual coherence compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. The proposed approach has far-reaching implications for various fields, including computer vision, robotics, and 3D reconstruction, enabling the creation of more realistic and immersive 3D models. Key contributions include the introduction of a novel CNN-based architecture, a large-scale densely annotated 3D shape dataset, and a comprehensive evaluation framework for point cloud colorization. Relevant keywords: point cloud colorization, 3D shape dataset, deep learning, CNN, computer vision, 3D reconstruction.

The use of covariance kernels is ubiquitous in the field of spatial statistics. Kernels allow data to be mapped into high-dimensional feature spaces and can thus extend simple linear additive methods to nonlinear methods with higher order interactions. However, until recently, there has been a strong reliance on a limited class of stationary kernels such as the Matern or squared exponential, limiting the expressiveness of these modelling approaches. Recent machine learning research has focused on spectral representations to model arbitrary stationary kernels and introduced more general representations that include classes of nonstationary kernels. In this paper, we exploit the connections between Fourier feature representations, Gaussian processes and neural networks to generalise previous approaches and develop a simple and efficient framework to learn arbitrarily complex nonstationary kernel functions directly from the data, while taking care to avoid overfitting using state-of-the-art methods from deep learning. We highlight the very broad array of kernel classes that could be created within this framework. We apply this to a time series dataset and a remote sensing problem involving land surface temperature in Eastern Africa. We show that without increasing the computational or storage complexity, nonstationary kernels can be used to improve generalisation performance and provide more interpretable results.

In this paper, we introduce the , a nonconvex yet analytically tractable optimization program, in a quest to better understand deep neural networks that are trained for a sufficiently long time. As the name suggests, this new model is derived by isolating the topmost layer from the remainder of the neural network, followed by imposing certain constraints separately on the two parts of the network. We demonstrate that the Layer-Peeled Model, albeit simple, inherits many characteristics of well-trained neural networks, thereby offering an effective tool for explaining and predicting common empirical patterns of deep learning training. First, when working on class-balanced datasets, we prove that any solution to this model forms a simplex equiangular tight frame, which in part explains the recently discovered phenomenon of neural collapse \cite. More importantly, when moving to the imbalanced case, our analysis of the Layer-Peeled Model reveals a hitherto unknown phenomenon that we term , which fundamentally limits the performance of deep learning models on the minority classes. In addition, we use the Layer-Peeled Model to gain insights into how to mitigate Minority Collapse. Interestingly, this phenomenon is first predicted by the Layer-Peeled Model before being confirmed by our computational experiments.

This paper addresses the problem of digital image acquisition with the lowest possible sampling rate, leveraging Compressed Sensing (CS) and the Adaptive Sampling Based on Sparse Representation (ASBSR) method. The objective is to develop an efficient image sampling and reconstruction framework that minimizes the sampling rate while maintaining image quality. Our approach combines CS theory with the ASBSR method, which adaptively selects the most informative sampling locations based on sparse representation. The results show that the proposed framework achieves significant reductions in sampling rates, outperforming traditional uniform sampling methods. Key findings include improved image reconstruction quality and reduced sampling rates, making it suitable for applications where data acquisition is limited or costly. The contributions of this research lie in the development of a novel ASBSR-based CS method, which enables efficient digital image acquisition with low sampling rates, and has potential applications in areas such as image compression, surveillance, and medical imaging. Keywords: Compressed Sensing, Adaptive Sampling, Sparse Representation, Image Reconstruction, Digital Image Acquisition.

This paper aims to enhance motion cues for face anti-spoofing by proposing a novel CNN-LSTM architecture. The objective is to effectively distinguish between genuine and spoofed faces by analyzing subtle motion patterns. Our approach combines the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for temporal sequence modeling. The proposed model is trained on a large dataset of face videos with diverse spoofing attacks, including replay and mask attacks. Experimental results demonstrate that our CNN-LSTM architecture outperforms state-of-the-art face anti-spoofing methods, achieving a significant reduction in equal error rate. The key findings highlight the importance of motion cues in face anti-spoofing and the effectiveness of the proposed architecture in capturing these cues. This research contributes to the development of more robust and reliable face recognition systems, with potential applications in security, surveillance, and authentication. Key keywords: face anti-spoofing, CNN-LSTM, motion cues, deep learning, face recognition, security.

Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) are a powerful probabilistic framework widely used in sequence modeling tasks, such as natural language processing, computer vision, and bioinformatics. This paper provides an introduction to CRFs, focusing on their theoretical foundations and practical applications. The objective is to explain how CRFs address the limitations of traditional models like Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) by incorporating global dependencies and avoiding strong independence assumptions. We describe the mathematical formulation of CRFs, including their conditional probability distribution and feature functions, as well as the training process using maximum likelihood estimation. Additionally, we discuss inference techniques, such as the Viterbi algorithm, for predicting the most likely sequence of labels. The paper highlights the advantages of CRFs in handling complex, structured data and their superior performance in tasks like named entity recognition, part-of-speech tagging, and image segmentation. Finally, we explore recent advancements, including deep learning-based CRF variants, and their potential for improving accuracy and scalability. This work aims to serve as a foundational resource for researchers and practitioners seeking to understand and apply CRFs in real-world scenarios. **Keywords**: Conditional Random Fields, sequence modeling, probabilistic models, natural language processing, structured prediction, deep learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently classifying big data by introducing a novel method that enhances traditional decision tree algorithms. The primary aim is to improve the accuracy and processing speed when dealing with large-scale datasets. Methods/Approach: We propose an Augmented Decision Tree (ADT) approach that incorporates advanced feature selection and parallel processing techniques. This method optimizes the decision tree structure to handle vast volumes of data effectively. The ADT approach integrates data preprocessing, enhanced node splitting criteria, and parallel computing to expedite processing. Comparative analyses with standard decision tree models and other machine learning classifiers are conducted to underscore improvements. Results/Findings: The proposed ADT model demonstrates significantly improved classification accuracy and reduced processing time compared to classical decision tree approaches. Experiments on publicly available big data benchmarks illustrate a reduction in computational complexity by at least 30% while maintaining or improving accuracy rates. Additionally, ADT shows better scalability and resilience when applied to diverse datasets. Conclusion/Implications: The Augmented Decision Tree approach presents a robust alternative for big data classification, offering substantial enhancements over conventional methods in terms of efficiency and performance. This research contributes to the field by providing a scalable solution that can be applied in real-world big data environments, such as healthcare analytics, financial forecasting, and large-scale IoT data processing. Future work could explore further optimizations and adaptations of the ADT for specific big data applications. Keywords: big data, classification, decision trees, augmented decision trees, parallel processing, machine learning, scalability.

Chromosome segmentation, particularly in overlapping scenarios, remains a critical challenge in medical image analysis, with significant implications for genetic research and diagnostics. This paper introduces a novel adversarial multiscale feature learning framework designed to address the complexities of overlapping chromosome segmentation. The proposed approach leverages a generative adversarial network (GAN) architecture combined with multiscale feature extraction to enhance the model's ability to distinguish and separate overlapping chromosomes in high-resolution microscopy images. The multiscale feature learning component captures both fine-grained details and broader contextual information, while the adversarial training mechanism ensures robust and accurate segmentation outcomes. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios with high levels of chromosome overlap. The framework achieves a mean intersection-over-union (IoU) score of 0.92, surpassing state-of-the-art methods by 8%. This research contributes to the field by providing a scalable and efficient solution for overlapping chromosome segmentation, with potential applications in automated karyotyping and genetic disorder diagnosis. Key innovations include the integration of adversarial learning with multiscale feature extraction and the development of a loss function tailored to overlapping chromosome scenarios. **Keywords**: chromosome segmentation, adversarial learning, multiscale feature extraction, generative adversarial networks (GANs), medical image analysis, overlapping objects.

We propose a novel method for large-scale image stitching that is robust against repetitive patterns and featureless regions in the imagery. In such cases, state-of-the-art image stitching methods easily produce image alignment artifacts, since they may produce false pairwise image registrations that are in conflict within the global connectivity graph. Our method augments the current methods by collecting all the plausible pairwise image registration candidates, among which globally consistent candidates are chosen. This enables the stitching process to determine the correct pairwise registrations by utilizing all the available information from the whole imagery, such as unambiguous registrations outside the repeating pattern and featureless regions. We formalize the method as a weighted multigraph whose nodes represent the individual image transformations from the composite image, and whose sets of multiple edges between two nodes represent all the plausible transformations between the pixel coordinates of the two images. The edge weights represent the plausibility of the transformations. The image transformations and the edge weights are solved from a non-linear minimization problem with linear constraints, for which a projection method is used. As an example, we apply the method in a large-scale scanning application where the transformations are primarily translations with only slight rotation and scaling component. Despite these simplifications, the state-of-the-art methods do not produce adequate results in such applications, since the image overlap is small, which can be featureless or repetitive, and misalignment artifacts and their concealment are unacceptable.

Strategies for improving the training and prediction quality of weakly supervised machine learning models vary in how much they are tailored to a specific task or integrated with a specific model architecture. In this work, we introduce Knodle, a software framework that treats weak data annotations, deep learning models, and methods for improving weakly supervised training as separate, modular components. This modularization gives the training process access to fine-grained information such as data set characteristics, matches of heuristic rules, or elements of the deep learning model ultimately used for prediction. Hence, our framework can encompass a wide range of training methods for improving weak supervision, ranging from methods that only look at correlations of rules and output classes (independently of the machine learning model trained with the resulting labels), to those that harness the interplay of neural networks and weakly labeled data. We illustrate the benchmarking potential of the framework with a performance comparison of several reference implementations on a selection of datasets that are already available in Knodle. The framework is published as an open-source Python package knodle and available at https://github.com/knodle/knodle.

This paper presents a novel application of transfer learning techniques to enhance the automated detection of melanoma from dermoscopic images, as part of our participation in the ISIC 2017 Skin Lesion Classification Challenge. The study aims to address the critical challenge of accurately classifying malignant melanoma, thereby aiding in early detection and treatment. Methods/Approach: We adopted a transfer learning approach, utilizing pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) as a foundational model, specifically leveraging architectures such as VGG16 and ResNet50. These models were fine-tuned on the challenge dataset to adapt to the specific features of skin lesions. Data augmentation techniques were also employed to improve model robustness by expanding the diversity of input samples. Results/Findings: Our approach demonstrated significant improvements in accuracy and performance over baseline models. The fine-tuned CNNs achieved a higher classification accuracy and increased sensitivity in detecting melanoma compared to traditional machine learning methods. Our model ranked competitively in the ISIC 2017 challenge leaderboard, highlighting its efficacy. Conclusion/Implications: The study illustrates the potential of transfer learning in medical image analysis, particularly in enhancing the early detection of melanoma. The application of advanced CNN architectures for skin lesion classification presents a promising tool for improving diagnostic accuracy in dermatology. Further research could explore the integration of this approach in clinical settings, potentially contributing to automated diagnostic workflows. Key keywords include transfer learning, melanoma detection, convolutional neural networks, ISIC 2017, and skin lesion classification.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for learning representations on graph-structured data. This paper investigates the message passing mechanism inherent in GNNs, offering a novel perspective through the lens of power iteration clustering. We demonstrate that GNN message passing, under certain conditions, approximates a power iteration process aimed at identifying cluster structure within the graph. Our analysis reveals a connection between the spectral properties of the graph Laplacian and the convergence behavior of GNNs. Specifically, we show how the aggregation and combination functions within GNN layers influence the network's ability to discern clusters of varying densities and connectivity. Furthermore, we introduce a metric to quantify the alignment between GNN embeddings and the underlying cluster structure. Empirical evaluations on benchmark datasets validate our theoretical findings, highlighting the potential for improved GNN design and interpretability. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of GNN behavior and offers insights into optimizing their performance for tasks involving community detection and node classification. Keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Message Passing, Power Iteration, Clustering, Graph Laplacian, Spectral Analysis.

Object detection systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, posing a significant security risk. Existing attacks often lack transferability, limiting their effectiveness against unseen models. This paper introduces a novel framework for generating transferable adversarial attacks targeting both image and video object detection. Our approach leverages a combination of frequency-based perturbation and an ensemble of diverse detector architectures during attack generation to enhance transferability. We demonstrate that frequency-based perturbations improve the robustness of the attack across different datasets and model architectures. Furthermore, we introduce a temporal consistency loss for video object detection to ensure that the generated adversarial perturbations are smooth and visually plausible across video frames, leading to more effective attacks. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including COCO and ImageNet VID, show that our method achieves significantly higher transferability rates compared to state-of-the-art adversarial attack techniques, with minimal performance degradation on the source model. The proposed approach offers a robust defense evaluation tool and highlights the need for more resilient object detection models. Keywords: Adversarial Attacks, Object Detection, Transferability, Image Security, Video Security, Deep Learning.

Automatic image matting (AIM) refers to estimating the soft foreground from an arbitrary natural image without any auxiliary input like trimap, which is useful for image editing. Prior methods try to learn semantic features to aid the matting process while being limited to images with salient opaque foregrounds such as humans and animals. In this paper, we investigate the difficulties when extending them to natural images with salient transparent/meticulous foregrounds or non-salient foregrounds. To address the problem, a novel end-to-end matting network is proposed, which can predict a generalized trimap for any image of the above types as a unified semantic representation. Simultaneously, the learned semantic features guide the matting network to focus on the transition areas via an attention mechanism. We also construct a test set AIM-500 that contains 500 diverse natural images covering all types along with manually labeled alpha mattes, making it feasible to benchmark the generalization ability of AIM models. Results of the experiments demonstrate that our network trained on available composite matting datasets outperforms existing methods both objectively and subjectively. The source code and dataset are available at https://github.com/JizhiziLi/AIM.

Deep learning based approaches have achieved significant progresses in different tasks like classification, detection, segmentation, and so on. Ensemble learning is widely known to further improve performance by combining multiple complementary models. It is easy to apply ensemble learning for classification tasks, for example, based on averaging, voting, or other methods. However, for other tasks (like object detection) where the outputs are varying in quantity and unable to be simply compared, the ensemble of multiple models become difficult. In this paper, we propose a new method called Predictive Ensemble Learning (PEL), based on powerful predictive ability of deep neural networks, to directly predict the best performing model among a pool of base models for each test example, thus transforming ensemble learning to a traditional classification task. Taking scene text detection as the application, where no suitable ensemble learning strategy exists, PEL can significantly improve the performance, compared to either individual state-of-the-art models, or the fusion of multiple models by non-maximum suppression. Experimental results show the possibility and potential of PEL in predicting different models' performance based only on a query example, which can be extended for ensemble learning in many other complex tasks.

This research addresses the growing need for efficient learning mechanisms in temporal knowledge graphs, which encapsulate dynamic relationships and temporal attributes over time. Traditional methods require extensive data for training, often rendering them impractical for time-sensitive applications. Our aim is to introduce a one-shot learning approach tailored specifically for these temporal structures. Methods/Approach: We develop a novel model combining the principles of one-shot learning with temporal graph neural networks. This model leverages a minimal amount of temporal data while effectively generalizing to unseen scenarios. By incorporating context-aware temporal embeddings and an adaptable memory module, the approach is capable of capturing both the evolving and historical contextual nuances of the data. Results/Findings: The proposed one-shot learning framework demonstrates superior performance on benchmark temporal knowledge graph datasets compared to conventional multi-shot techniques. We observe significant improvements in prediction accuracy and processing speed, particularly under constraints of limited temporal data. The system efficiently learns new temporal dynamics with a fraction of the data that traditional methods would require. Conclusion/Implications: Our research contributes an innovative solution to the challenge of resource-efficient learning in temporal knowledge graphs. This one-shot framework offers potential applications in domains requiring real-time insights and adaptive modeling, such as event forecasting and dynamic network analysis. The findings underscore the feasibility of incorporating minimal data for robust temporal reasoning, setting a new direction for future research in knowledge graph management. Keywords: One-shot Learning, Temporal Knowledge Graphs, Graph Neural Networks, Context-aware Temporal Embeddings, Dynamic Networks.

This paper introduces IAN (Imaginative Adversarial Network), a novel framework for generating highly realistic and imaginative human faces by combining the strengths of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The primary objective of this research is to address the limitations of existing face generation models, such as lack of diversity and artifacts in synthesized images, while enabling the creation of unique, imaginative facial features. To achieve this, IAN integrates multiple GAN architectures with a custom-designed fusion mechanism that enhances feature representation and ensures smooth blending of diverse facial attributes. The proposed approach leverages advanced techniques in latent space manipulation and style transfer to produce high-quality, photorealistic images with improved diversity and creativity. Experimental results demonstrate that IAN outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of image quality, diversity, and perceptual realism, as validated by both quantitative metrics and human evaluations. The framework also exhibits robustness in generating faces across various demographics and artistic styles. The implications of this work extend to applications in digital art, virtual reality, and synthetic data generation for training AI systems. By combining innovation in GAN architectures with imaginative design, IAN sets a new benchmark for creative face generation in the field of computer vision. **Keywords**: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), face generation, imaginative design, latent space manipulation, style transfer, photorealistic synthesis.

Hue modification is the adjustment of hue property on color images. Conducting hue modification on an image is trivial, and it can be abused to falsify opinions of viewers. Since shapes, edges or textural information remains unchanged after hue modification, this type of manipulation is relatively hard to be detected and localized. Since small patches inherit the same Color Filter Array (CFA) configuration and demosaicing, any distortion made by local hue modification can be detected by patch matching within the same image. In this paper, we propose to localize hue modification by means of a Siamese neural network specifically designed for matching two inputs. By crafting the network outputs, we are able to form a heatmap which potentially highlights malicious regions. Our proposed method deals well not only with uncompressed images but also with the presence of JPEG compression, an operation usually hindering the exploitation of CFA and demosaicing artifacts. Experimental evidences corroborate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
