Nghiên cứu ảnh hưởng của liều lượng bón phân kali đến năng suất và chất lượng củ khoai lang đã chỉ ra rằng việc áp dụng phân kali một cách hợp lý có thể nâng cao đáng kể năng suất và cải thiện chất lượng sản phẩm. Thí nghiệm được thực hiện trên nhiều loại đất và điều kiện khí hậu khác nhau, cho thấy rằng liều lượng bón phân kali tối ưu không chỉ giúp củ khoai lang phát triển tốt hơn mà còn tăng cường hàm lượng dinh dưỡng, đặc biệt là vitamin và khoáng chất. Kết quả nghiên cứu cũng nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc điều chỉnh liều lượng phân bón phù hợp với từng giai đoạn sinh trưởng của cây, từ đó khuyến nghị các biện pháp canh tác hiệu quả nhằm nâng cao sản lượng và chất lượng khoai lang, đáp ứng nhu cầu thị trường ngày càng cao. Những phát hiện này có thể giúp nông dân tối ưu hóa quy trình sản xuất, góp phần vào sự phát triển bền vững của ngành nông nghiệp.
Ngoài ra, còn có những review điểm người dùng biết thêm thông tin khi ra quyết định lựa chọn.Tâm lý của người mua sản phẩm thì họ luôn mong muốn mua được sản phẩm với tiêu chí “ngonbore”.

Khu vực Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long đang đối mặt với nhiều thách thức trong công tác quản lý chất thải rắn sinh hoạt do tốc độ đô thị hóa nhanh và sự gia tăng dân số. Hiện nay, lượng chất thải rắn phát sinh ngày càng lớn, trong khi hệ thống thu gom, xử lý còn nhiều bất cập, dẫn đến tình trạng ô nhiễm môi trường nghiêm trọng. Các địa phương trong khu vực đang nỗ lực cải thiện quy trình quản lý bằng cách áp dụng công nghệ tiên tiến, tăng cường phân loại rác tại nguồn và khuyến khích tái chế. Xu hướng hiện nay là chuyển dịch từ phương pháp chôn lấp truyền thống sang các giải pháp bền vững hơn như đốt rác phát điện và ủ phân compost. Tuy nhiên, để đạt được hiệu quả cao, cần sự phối hợp chặt chẽ giữa chính quyền, doanh nghiệp và cộng đồng, cùng với nguồn đầu tư lớn cho cơ sở hạ tầng và nâng cao nhận thức người dân.

This paper investigates a discrete-time mean field control (MFC) problem where the environment's state influences the dynamics of a large population of agents. We formulate a novel framework where individual agents interact not only through the mean field distribution of agent states but also through a dynamically evolving environment state. This environment state, representing factors external to individual agents, impacts both the agent dynamics and the cost function. We derive the mean field equilibrium conditions, resulting in a system of coupled equations that characterize the optimal control strategy and the evolution of the environment state. Furthermore, we develop a policy iteration algorithm to approximate the solution of this MFC problem. The effectiveness of the proposed framework and algorithm is demonstrated through numerical experiments on a resource allocation problem, showing improved performance compared to traditional MFC approaches that neglect environment states. Key words: Mean Field Control, Discrete-Time Systems, Environment States, Policy Iteration, Large Population Games.

This paper introduces a novel dataset-level geometric framework designed to enhance the performance and robustness of ensemble classifiers. The objective is to improve the accuracy and reliability of classification tasks by leveraging geometric relationships between datasets. Our approach employs a unique combination of geometric transformations and manifold learning techniques to create a robust ensemble framework. The methodology involves representing each dataset as a geometric object, allowing for the identification of intrinsic patterns and relationships that can inform the ensemble classification process. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms traditional ensemble methods, particularly in scenarios with diverse or noisy datasets. Key findings include significant improvements in classification accuracy and reduced sensitivity to hyperparameter tuning. The proposed framework contributes to the field of machine learning by providing a innovative, geometry-driven approach to ensemble classification, with potential applications in areas such as data integration, anomaly detection, and multi-modal learning. Relevant keywords include ensemble learning, geometric deep learning, manifold learning, and classification algorithms.

Việc giữ chân nhân viên tại các công ty xây dựng nhỏ đang trở thành một thách thức lớn trong bối cảnh thị trường lao động cạnh tranh. Nghiên cứu cho thấy các yếu tố như lương thưởng không đủ hấp dẫn, cơ hội phát triển nghề nghiệp hạn chế, môi trường làm việc căng thẳng và thiếu sự công nhận đóng vai trò quan trọng dẫn đến tình trạng nhân viên rời bỏ công ty. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, các công ty cần xây dựng chính sách lương thưởng cạnh tranh, tạo điều kiện cho nhân viên nâng cao kỹ năng và kiến thức thông qua các khóa đào tạo, cải thiện môi trường làm việc bằng cách xây dựng văn hóa doanh nghiệp tích cực, tạo cơ hội thăng tiến và ghi nhận những đóng góp của nhân viên. Bên cạnh đó, việc tăng cường giao tiếp nội bộ, lắng nghe ý kiến của nhân viên và giải quyết kịp thời các vấn đề phát sinh cũng góp phần quan trọng vào việc xây dựng lòng trung thành và giữ chân nhân viên gắn bó lâu dài với công ty.

Đầu tư công đóng vai trò quan trọng trong thúc đẩy tăng trưởng kinh tế và hội tụ tại các vùng kinh tế trọng điểm. Tác động trực tiếp của đầu tư công thể hiện qua việc xây dựng cơ sở hạ tầng, nâng cao năng lực sản xuất và tạo việc làm, từ đó kích thích phát triển kinh tế địa phương. Bên cạnh đó, đầu tư công còn có tác động lan tỏa, thúc đẩy sự phát triển của các ngành công nghiệp phụ trợ, dịch vụ và thương mại, giúp thu hẹp khoảng cách phát triển giữa các vùng. Tuy nhiên, để đạt hiệu quả tối đa, cần có sự phân bổ hợp lý và quản lý chặt chẽ các nguồn lực đầu tư, đảm bảo tính bền vững và công bằng trong phát triển kinh tế - xã hội.

Nghiên cứu về ảnh hưởng của kali clorua (KCl) đến năng suất và phẩm chất hành hương (Allium fistulosum L.) cho thấy việc bón phân kali có vai trò quan trọng trong việc cải thiện các chỉ tiêu sinh trưởng và năng suất của cây. Thí nghiệm được thực hiện với nhiều mức bón KCl khác nhau, kết quả cho thấy việc tăng lượng kali bón thúc đẩy chiều cao cây, số nhánh, đường kính củ và năng suất củ. Đồng thời, KCl còn ảnh hưởng đến các thành phần dinh dưỡng trong củ hành, làm tăng hàm lượng chất khô, vitamin C và các khoáng chất quan trọng. Tuy nhiên, việc bón quá nhiều kali có thể gây ra tác động tiêu cực đến phẩm chất của hành hương. Do đó, cần xác định liều lượng KCl phù hợp để tối ưu hóa năng suất và chất lượng hành, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả kinh tế cho người trồng. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp cơ sở khoa học cho việc sử dụng phân bón kali hợp lý trong canh tác hành hương, hướng đến sản xuất bền vững và an toàn.

Gaussian Process (GP) models are powerful non-parametric methods widely used in machine learning for regression and classification tasks. Kernel selection significantly impacts GP performance; however, manually designing effective kernels is challenging. This paper introduces a novel approach to automatically evolve GP kernels from elementary mathematical expressions using genetic programming. The method explores the kernel space by combining functions such as addition, multiplication, exponentiation, and trigonometric operations to generate complex kernel structures. The fitness of each evolved kernel is evaluated based on its performance on a given dataset using a GP regression framework. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the evolved kernels often outperform hand-crafted kernels and kernels obtained through other automated kernel learning techniques. The evolved kernels provide interpretable functional forms, offering insights into the underlying data relationships. This automated kernel discovery approach offers a valuable tool for improving the accuracy and applicability of Gaussian Process models. **Keywords:** Gaussian Process, Kernel Learning, Genetic Programming, Kernel Evolution, Regression, Machine Learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of analyzing and classifying driving styles using primitive driving patterns and Bayesian nonparametric approaches. The objective is to develop a robust framework that can accurately identify and differentiate driving behaviors without relying on predefined categories or extensive labeled data. To achieve this, we propose a novel methodology that leverages unsupervised learning techniques, specifically Bayesian nonparametric models, to extract and cluster primitive driving patterns from raw sensor data. These patterns are then used to infer driving styles, enabling a more flexible and adaptive analysis compared to traditional rule-based or parametric methods. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showcasing its ability to accurately classify driving styles across diverse datasets. The framework outperforms existing methods in terms of adaptability and scalability, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data. The findings highlight the potential of Bayesian nonparametric approaches in driving behavior analysis, offering valuable insights for applications in autonomous driving, driver assistance systems, and transportation safety. This research contributes to the field by introducing a data-driven, unsupervised solution that enhances the understanding of driving styles and their underlying patterns. **Keywords**: driving style analysis, primitive driving patterns, Bayesian nonparametric models, unsupervised learning, autonomous driving, transportation safety.

This paper presents a novel approach to traffic control optimization by integrating a boosted genetic algorithm with machine learning techniques. Key keywords: traffic control optimization, genetic algorithm, machine learning, intelligent transportation systems, urban traffic management.

In this paper, we propose a fast and accurate coordinate regression method for face alignment. Unlike most existing facial landmark regression methods which usually employ fully connected layers to convert feature maps into landmark coordinate, we present a structure coherence component to explicitly take the relation among facial landmarks into account. Due to the geometric structure of human face, structure coherence between different facial parts provides important cues for effectively localizing facial landmarks. However, the dense connection in the fully connected layers overuses such coherence, making the important cues unable to be distinguished from all connections. Instead, our structure coherence component leverages a dynamic sparse graph structure to passing features among the most related landmarks. Furthermore, we propose a novel objective function, named Soft Wing loss, to improve the accuracy. Extensive experiments on three popular benchmarks, including WFLW, COFW and 300W, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance with fast speed. Our approach is especially robust to challenging cases resulting in impressively low failure rate (0% and 2.88%) in COFW and WFLW datasets.

Nowadays, as cameras are rapidly adopted in our daily routine, images of documents are becoming both abundant and prevalent. Unlike natural images that capture physical objects, document-images contain a significant amount of text with critical semantics and complicated layouts. In this work, we devise a generic unsupervised technique to learn multimodal affinities between textual entities in a document-image, considering their visual style, the content of their underlying text and their geometric context within the image. We then use these learned affinities to automatically cluster the textual entities in the image into different semantic groups. The core of our approach is a deep optimization scheme dedicated for an image provided by the user that detects and leverages reliable pairwise connections in the multimodal representation of the textual elements in order to properly learn the affinities. We show that our technique can operate on highly varying images spanning a wide range of documents and demonstrate its applicability for various editing operations manipulating the content, appearance and geometry of the image.

Our approach is evaluated on a range of benchmark tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in learning efficiency and policy performance compared to existing methods. The results show that our sequence modeling approach can effectively capture long-term dependencies and assign credit to actions in a more accurate and efficient manner. This research contributes to the development of more advanced reinforcement learning algorithms, with potential applications in areas such as robotics, game playing, and autonomous systems, and highlights the importance of temporal credit assignment in episodic reinforcement learning, with key keywords including reinforcement learning, sequence modeling, temporal credit assignment, and episodic learning.

This paper introduces a novel on-the-fly label learning framework for training robust image classification models. The approach addresses the challenge of noisy labels and limited labeled data by simultaneously learning and refining image labels during the training process. The proposed method leverages a combination of a classification network and a label correction module. Specifically, the classification network predicts class probabilities, while the label correction module estimates the reliability of existing labels and dynamically adjusts them based on the network's predictions and a consistency loss. This allows the model to iteratively improve its understanding of the data and correct erroneous labels, leading to more accurate and robust classification performance. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods for training with noisy labels, achieving significant improvements in classification accuracy and robustness against label noise. Furthermore, the on-the-fly nature of the learning process makes it adaptable to new data and changing label distributions without requiring retraining from scratch. The research contributes a practical and effective solution for training high-quality classification models in real-world scenarios with imperfect or limited annotations. Keywords: image classification, noisy labels, label correction, robust learning, on-the-fly learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning discriminative prototypes in the context of time-series classification using Dynamic Time Warping (DTW). The objective is to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of prototype-based learning methods by leveraging the strengths of DTW to measure similarities between time-series data. We propose an innovative approach that combines DTW with a prototype learning framework, facilitating the identification of representative examples that capture the underlying patterns within classes. Our method operates by dynamically adjusting prototype representations to better accommodate local variations in time-series sequences. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional techniques on various benchmark datasets, showcasing improved classification accuracy and robustness against noise and distortions in the data. The findings indicate that the integration of DTW not only helps in achieving higher performance metrics but also enriches the interpretability of the learned prototypes. In conclusion, this research contributes to the field of time-series analysis by providing a novel framework for learning prototypes that dynamically adapt to input sequences. The implications of our findings suggest practical applications in domains such as speech recognition, bioinformatics, and activity recognition, where accurate time-series classification is essential. Keywords: Dynamic Time Warping, time-series classification, discriminative prototypes, prototype learning, machine learning.

Bid rigging, a form of collusion in procurement auctions, poses significant challenges to market fairness and economic efficiency. Traditional detection methods often rely on manual analysis or rule-based systems, which are time-consuming and prone to errors. This paper proposes a novel deep learning-based approach to automatically detect bid rigging by identifying patterns indicative of cartel behavior. Leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs), we develop a model trained on historical bidding data to classify participants as either collusive or non-collusive. The model captures subtle irregularities in bid distributions, timing, and pricing strategies that are characteristic of cartel activities. Experimental results on real-world procurement datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving a detection accuracy of 92.3%, significantly outperforming conventional statistical approaches. The findings highlight the potential of deep learning in enhancing antitrust enforcement and ensuring competitive markets. This research contributes to the growing body of work applying artificial intelligence to regulatory challenges, offering a scalable and efficient solution for detecting bid rigging in large-scale procurement systems. **Keywords**: Bid rigging, cartel detection, convolutional neural networks, deep learning, procurement auctions, antitrust enforcement.

Few-shot learning aims to recognize new classes with limited labeled examples. This paper introduces Sparse Spatial Transformers (SST), a novel attention mechanism designed to improve feature alignment and reduce overfitting in few-shot classification tasks. SST leverages a sparse attention map to selectively focus on relevant spatial regions within feature maps, thereby enhancing discriminative feature extraction and reducing the influence of noisy background information. The proposed method is integrated into a meta-learning framework, where a spatial transformer network learns to align features between support and query images in an episodic training paradigm. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including miniImageNet and tieredImageNet, demonstrate that SST achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing few-shot learning approaches. Specifically, SST exhibits improved accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios with extremely limited training data. The results highlight the efficacy of sparse attention in learning transferable feature representations for few-shot learning. Key words: Few-shot learning, Meta-learning, Spatial Transformer, Attention Mechanism, Sparse Attention, Image Classification.

This paper addresses the challenge of action robustness in reinforcement learning (RL) for continuous control tasks. The objective is to develop RL agents that exhibit resilience to perturbations and uncertainties in action execution, a critical requirement for real-world deployment. We introduce a novel training framework, Action Robust Reinforcement Learning (ARRL), which explicitly models and mitigates the impact of action noise during the learning process. ARRL augments the standard RL objective with a regularization term that penalizes sensitivity to action variations, promoting policies that are inherently more robust. We evaluate ARRL across a suite of continuous control benchmarks, including tasks with simulated robotic manipulators and locomotion. Results demonstrate that ARRL agents significantly outperform standard RL algorithms and existing robustness-focused methods in the presence of action noise, achieving higher success rates and improved stability. Furthermore, we showcase the practical applicability of ARRL by deploying trained agents on a physical robot, demonstrating their ability to handle real-world uncertainties. The findings highlight the potential of ARRL for enabling reliable and safe RL-based control in complex and uncertain environments. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Robustness, Continuous Control, Action Noise, Robotics.

We present McAssoc, a deep learning approach to the as-sociation of detection bounding boxes in different views ofa multi-camera system. The vast majority of the academiahas been developing single-camera computer vision algo-rithms, however, little research attention has been directedto incorporating them into a multi-camera system. In thispaper, we designed a 3-branch architecture that leveragesdirect association and additional cross localization infor-mation. A new metric, image-pair association accuracy(IPAA) is designed specifically for performance evaluationof cross-camera detection association. We show in the ex-periments that localization information is critical to suc-cessful cross-camera association, especially when similar-looking objects are present. This paper is an experimentalwork prior to MessyTable, which is a large-scale bench-mark for instance association in mutliple cameras.

Object detection models traditionally require large quantities of accurately annotated data, making their deployment challenging in scenarios with limited labeling resources. This paper addresses the problem of training effective object detectors when only a small set of weakly-labeled images and a large collection of unlabeled images are available. We propose a novel semi-supervised learning framework that leverages weak labels—such as image-level tags or imprecise bounding boxes—combined with abundant unlabeled data. The method integrates a multi-stage training process: initial detector training with weak labels, pseudo-label generation on unlabeled images using the preliminary model, and iterative refinement through self-training. To mitigate the noise inherent to weak supervision, we introduce an adaptive pseudo-label filtering mechanism and confidence-based sample selection. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark object detection datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing weakly-supervised and semi-supervised methods in detecting challenging object categories, while requiring significantly less annotation effort. The results highlight the effectiveness of exploiting weak and unlabeled data, paving the way for scalable object detection in low-resource and real-world settings. Keywords: object detection, weakly-labeled data, semi-supervised learning, pseudo-labeling, deep learning.

This study addresses the challenge of accurately predicting multiphase flow dynamics, a critical problem in fields such as fluid dynamics, energy systems, and chemical engineering. Traditional methods for modeling multiphase flows often rely on computationally expensive simulations or simplified assumptions, limiting their accuracy and scalability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel deep neural network (DNN) framework designed to predict multiphase flow behavior with high precision and efficiency. Our approach leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture spatial and temporal dependencies in flow data, enabling the model to learn complex patterns and interactions between phases. The proposed framework is trained and validated on a comprehensive dataset generated from high-fidelity simulations, covering a wide range of flow regimes and conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that our DNN-based model achieves superior performance compared to traditional methods, with significant improvements in prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, the model exhibits strong generalization capabilities across diverse flow scenarios, highlighting its potential for real-world applications. This research contributes to the advancement of multiphase flow modeling by introducing a data-driven, AI-powered solution that bridges the gap between accuracy and computational feasibility. The proposed framework has broad implications for industries reliant on multiphase flow analysis, offering a scalable and cost-effective alternative to conventional approaches. **Keywords**: multiphase flow, deep neural networks, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, fluid dynamics, AI modeling.

Objective: Reinforcement learning (RL) agents often struggle to generalize to rare or adversarial scenarios, limiting their robustness and reliability in real-world applications. This paper introduces CoachNet, a novel adversarial sampling framework designed to systematically expose RL policies to challenging experiences during training. Methods: CoachNet comprises two coupled neural modules—a policy network and an adversarial sampler. The sampler learns to identify and generate high-impact state–action pairs that maximize the policy’s loss, while the policy network concurrently updates its parameters to minimize expected returns over both standard and adversarial samples. We implement CoachNet atop proximal policy optimization (PPO) and deep Q-learning (DQN), augmenting the replay buffer with adversarially selected transitions. Results: We evaluate CoachNet on a suite of benchmark tasks, including continuous-control environments (MuJoCo) and discrete-action domains (Atari 2600). Compared to baseline PPO and DQN agents, CoachNet achieves up to 35% faster convergence and improves out-of-distribution generalization by 20% under novel disturbance profiles. Ablation studies confirm that adversarial sampling, rather than increased data volume, drives gains in policy robustness and sample efficiency. Conclusion: By dynamically focusing training on the most informative and challenging experiences, CoachNet advances the state of the art in robust deep RL. Its adversarial sampling strategy yields policies that are both more resilient to perturbations and more data-efficient, with potential applications in autonomous robotics, strategic game playing, and safety-critical control systems. **Abstract:** Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides critical insights into brain functional connectivity by capturing spontaneous neural activity patterns. However, effective analysis of rs-fMRI data remains challenging due to the complex, graph-structured nature of brain networks. This paper explores the application and interpretability of Graph Isomorphism Networks (GINs) for rs-fMRI functional connectivity analysis. We design a framework that models brain regions as graph nodes and their connectivity as weighted edges, leveraging GINs to learn discriminative network representations. Our approach systematically evaluates GINs’ ability to capture key functional connectivity patterns relevant to neurological states. Experimental results on benchmark rs-fMRI datasets demonstrate that GINs outperform conventional graph neural network models in both accuracy and robustness for tasks such as subject classification and disease prediction. In addition, we perform interpretability studies to uncover how GINs encode topological information from brain networks, offering new insights into the network features critical for classification. The findings highlight the potential of GIN-based models for advancing automated, interpretable analysis of brain functional connectivity. This work establishes a solid foundation for future applications in neuroinformatics, brain disease diagnosis, and connectomics research. **Keywords:** Graph Isomorphism Network, GIN, rs-fMRI, functional connectivity, brain networks, graph neural networks, neuroinformatics, classification, interpretability, connectomics

Partial orders and directed acyclic graphs are commonly recurring data structures that arise naturally in numerous domains and applications and are used to represent ordered relations between entities in the domains. Examples are task dependencies in a project plan, transaction order in distributed ledgers and execution sequences of tasks in computer programs, just to mention a few. We study the problem of order preserving hierarchical clustering of this kind of ordered data. That is, if we have a < b in the original data and denote their respective clusters by [a] and [b], then we shall have [a] < [b] in the produced clustering. The clustering is similarity based and uses standard linkage functions, such as single- and complete linkage, and is an extension of classical hierarchical clustering. To achieve this, we define the output from running classical hierarchical clustering on strictly ordered data to be partial dendrograms; sub-trees of classical dendrograms with several connected components. We then construct an embedding of partial dendrograms over a set into the family of ultrametrics over the same set. An optimal hierarchical clustering is defined as the partial dendrogram corresponding to the ultrametric closest to the original dissimilarity measure, measured in the p-norm. Thus, the method is a combination of classical hierarchical clustering and ultrametric fitting. A reference implementation is employed for experiments on both synthetic random data and real world data from a database of machine parts. When compared to existing methods, the experiments show that our method excels both in cluster quality and order preservation.

This paper aims to investigate the application of deep learning techniques in X-ray security imaging for automatic threat detection. The increasing need for efficient and accurate security screening has driven research into leveraging deep learning models to enhance the detection of prohibited items in X-ray images. Our approach involves a comprehensive survey of recent advances in deep learning architectures, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning, tailored for X-ray image analysis. The results show that deep learning-based methods outperform traditional computer vision techniques in detecting threats, with improved accuracy and reduced false alarm rates. Key findings highlight the effectiveness of fine-tuning pre-trained models on X-ray image datasets and the importance of data augmentation techniques to address the limited availability of annotated data. This research contributes to the development of more reliable and automated X-ray security screening systems, with potential applications in aviation security, border control, and public safety. The study's novelty lies in its thorough examination of deep learning's role in X-ray threat detection, emphasizing the benefits of AI-driven security solutions. Relevant keywords: X-ray security imaging, deep learning, threat detection, CNNs, transfer learning, computer vision, AI security.

This paper addresses the critical need for effective benchmarks, algorithms, and metrics in the study of hierarchical disentanglement—a key challenge in machine learning and AI. Hierarchical disentanglement involves separating data into interpretable factors of variation that reflect underlying hierarchical relationships, yet a comprehensive evaluation framework remains lacking. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel suite of benchmarks specifically designed to rigorously assess hierarchical disentanglement. Our approach includes the development of innovative algorithms that prioritize the disentanglement of hierarchical structures within datasets. Additionally, we introduce robust metrics that quantitatively evaluate the performance and efficacy of these algorithms. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in disentangling hierarchical data when using our proposed framework, as compared to existing methods. Our benchmarks illustrate enhanced capability in extracting distinct hierarchical factors, while the new metrics provide superior insight into algorithmic performance. Findings suggest that our algorithms outperform traditional approaches in both accuracy and interpretability. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the AI community by providing essential tools for advancing the study of disentangled representations. The benchmarks, algorithms, and metrics developed can guide future research directions and drive innovations in various applications, including complex data interpretations and AI model transparency. Our work lays the groundwork for a standardized approach to evaluating hierarchical disentanglement, facilitating progress in the creation of more intelligent and trustworthy AI systems. Keywords: hierarchical disentanglement, machine learning, benchmarks, algorithms, metrics, AI transparency, data interpretation.

The generation of convincing bokeh effects in digital imagery has become increasingly important for both photography enthusiasts and modern imaging applications, particularly within computational photography and smartphone cameras. This paper presents a novel depth-aware image blending technique for generating high-quality bokeh effects by leveraging depth maps and advanced image smoothing methods. Our proposed approach first estimates the scene depth to accurately segment foreground and background regions. Subsequently, adaptive smoothing is applied to the background areas based on their depth values while retaining the sharpness of objects in the foreground. The final bokeh effect is produced by seamlessly blending the smoothed background with the untouched foreground using a depth-weighted fusion algorithm that minimizes visual artifacts and preserves natural edge transitions. Experimental results on a variety of synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional, depth-agnostic image blurring techniques in terms of both perceptual quality and edge preservation. The proposed framework is computationally efficient and easily adaptable for integration into real-time camera systems. These findings highlight the potential for depth-aware, smoothed image blending to enhance visual storytelling and improve the quality of digital images across diverse imaging platforms. Key keywords: bokeh effect, depth estimation, image blending, image smoothing, edge preservation, computational photography.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficient knowledge transfer in federated learning environments, where data is decentralized and privacy is a concern. Our objective is to develop a novel federated transfer learning framework that leverages dynamic gradient aggregation to improve model performance and adaptability. We propose a method that combines the benefits of transfer learning with the privacy-preserving aspects of federated learning, using a dynamic gradient aggregation approach to selectively update model parameters based on client contributions. Our results show that this approach outperforms traditional federated learning methods, achieving significant improvements in model accuracy and convergence speed. The key findings of this research highlight the potential of dynamic gradient aggregation in federated transfer learning, enabling more efficient and effective collaboration among clients. This work contributes to the development of more robust and adaptable federated learning systems, with potential applications in areas such as edge AI, IoT, and distributed machine learning. Key keywords: federated learning, transfer learning, dynamic gradient aggregation, edge AI, distributed machine learning.

The study addresses the challenge of efficiently representing and analyzing large collections of shapes in various applications such as computer graphics, computational geometry, and object recognition. Traditional shape analysis methods often struggle with alignment issues and high computational costs. This research proposes an innovative approach to model shape collections with alignment-aware linear models, enhancing representation accuracy and computational efficiency. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel alignment-aware linear model that incorporates alignment into the shape modeling process. This model leverages a combination of geometric feature extraction and linear transformation techniques to enable precise shape alignment and representation. The approach ensures that the variability within shape collections is captured effectively while minimizing alignment errors. Our study involved implementing the alignment-aware linear model on several benchmark shape datasets to evaluate its performance. Results/Findings: The proposed model demonstrated superior performance in both shape representation accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. Notably, our alignment-aware approach showed a significant reduction in shape misalignment, leading to improved fidelity of shape collections. Computational experiments indicated a marked improvement in processing times, making the model suitable for handling large-scale shape datasets. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes substantially to the field of shape analysis by introducing an alignment-aware linear model that combines efficiency with high accuracy. The findings have practical implications for applications involving 3D modeling, virtual reality, and other areas where shape representation is critical. The model's ability to handle large collections of shapes efficiently opens new avenues for real-time and large-scale shape analysis tasks. Keywords: Shape Collections, Alignment, Linear Models, Shape Analysis, 3D Modeling, Computational Geometry, Object Recognition.

This paper introduces DeeSIL, a novel Deep-Shallow Incremental Learning approach designed to efficiently adapt deep neural networks to evolving data streams. The objective is to address the challenge of catastrophic forgetting in incremental learning scenarios, where models must learn from a stream of data without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. DeeSIL achieves this by combining the strengths of deep and shallow learning techniques, leveraging the representational power of deep networks while incorporating the flexibility of shallow models to adapt to new data. Our approach utilizes a hybrid architecture that incrementally updates the model as new data arrives, ensuring a balance between knowledge retention and new information acquisition. Experimental results demonstrate that DeeSIL outperforms state-of-the-art incremental learning methods, exhibiting improved accuracy and reduced forgetting on several benchmark datasets. The proposed method has significant implications for real-world applications, such as continuous learning in autonomous systems, incremental data processing, and edge AI. Key contributions include the development of a novel deep-shallow incremental learning framework, improved performance on incremental learning tasks, and enhanced adaptability to changing data distributions. Relevant keywords: incremental learning, deep neural networks, shallow learning, catastrophic forgetting, edge AI, continuous learning.

Image-to-image translation is a critical task in computer vision, enabling the transformation of images from one domain to another while preserving essential features. This paper introduces U-GAT-IT, a novel unsupervised generative attentional network that leverages adaptive layer-instance normalization (AdaLIN) to enhance the quality and flexibility of image translation. The proposed framework incorporates attention mechanisms to focus on domain-specific regions, improving the translation of fine-grained details. AdaLIN dynamically adjusts normalization parameters, enabling the model to adaptively control the balance between style and content during the translation process. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that U-GAT-IT outperforms existing methods in terms of visual quality and structural consistency. The results highlight the effectiveness of attention mechanisms and adaptive normalization in unsupervised image-to-image translation. This work contributes to advancing generative models by providing a robust and versatile framework for domain adaptation tasks, with potential applications in image editing, style transfer, and data augmentation. **Keywords**: Image-to-image translation, unsupervised learning, generative networks, attention mechanisms, adaptive normalization, AdaLIN.

The paper presents a novel approach to imaginative face generation using a model called Imaginative Adversarial Network (IAN), which combines the principles of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to enhance creative outputs in facial imagery. This research addresses the challenge of generating diverse and imaginative facial features while maintaining the realism and coherence of generated images. Methods/Approach: The proposed IAN architecture integrates multiple GAN frameworks to leverage their distinct strengths for improved image generation. By incorporating adversarial training and a custom-designed creativity module that promotes feature exploration, IAN effectively generates high-quality, innovative facial images. The model is trained on a diverse dataset to ensure a broad range of expression and feature variability. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that IAN excels in generating highly realistic and creative faces compared to traditional GAN models. Quantitative measures show improved diversity and quality in facial feature generation, as assessed by various standard metrics. Qualitative analysis through user studies also indicates a preference for faces generated by IAN, highlighting its ability to produce both realistic and imaginative outcomes. Conclusion/Implications: The research introduces a significant advancement in face generation technology by combining GAN frameworks within the IAN model, contributing to both the fields of generative modeling and creative AI. This work opens new avenues for applications in entertainment, virtual reality, and digital art, providing tools for creating unique and expressive digital characters. Future research could extend IAN to other areas of creative media generation. Keywords: Imaginative Adversarial Network, face generation, GAN, creative AI, image synthesis, generative modeling.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated remarkable success in generating realistic data across various domains. However, estimating the likelihood of data under a GAN remains a significant challenge, hindering quantitative evaluation and comparison with other generative models. This paper introduces a novel approach for likelihood estimation in GANs by leveraging a learned auxiliary network. Our method trains a separate network to approximate the intractable density function implicitly defined by the generator. Specifically, we employ a variational inference framework, optimizing a lower bound on the log-likelihood using the auxiliary network as an approximation to the true posterior. The approach is validated on several benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and CelebA, demonstrating competitive performance in likelihood estimation compared to existing GAN evaluation metrics and other likelihood-based generative models. Furthermore, we explore the use of our likelihood estimates for anomaly detection and model selection. This work provides a practical and effective approach for quantifying the generative capability of GANs, facilitating their wider adoption and application. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, Likelihood Estimation, Variational Inference, Density Estimation, GAN Evaluation.

This paper presents InfographicVQA, a novel approach to visual question answering (VQA) specifically tailored for infographics. Infographics, which combine visual elements with textual information, pose unique challenges for traditional VQA systems. Our research aims to address these challenges and improve the interpretability and accuracy of VQA models when dealing with such complex visual-textual content. Methods/Approach: We propose a hybrid model that integrates both language and visual processing techniques to handle the intricacies of infographic data. By employing a multi-modal transformer-based architecture, our system effectively extracts and correlates textual and graphical information. The model leverages pre-trained language models, adapted for the visual domain, and employs fine-tuning strategies to enhance performance on infographic-specific datasets. Results/Findings: The InfographicVQA model demonstrates significant improvements over existing VQA methods, achieving higher accuracy in answering questions derived from infographics. Our approach outperforms baseline models on benchmark datasets, highlighting its superior ability to process and integrate multi-modal information. Comparative analyses show that our model reduces comprehension errors and increases reliability in generating precise responses. Conclusion/Implications: The InfographicVQA framework introduces a crucial advancement in the field of visual question answering, offering an effective solution for comprehending complex infographic content. The research contributes to expanding the capabilities of VQA systems, paving the way for applications in educational tools, data journalism, and automated report generation. Future developments could explore the integration of enhanced graphical detection techniques to further refine system performance. Keywords: InfographicVQA, visual question answering, multi-modal transformer, infographics, language models, dataset, fine-tuning, AI models.

This paper introduces a novel hierarchical representation learning framework for Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) aimed at improving sample efficiency and generalization in reinforcement learning. The approach learns a hierarchy of state representations, where higher levels capture more abstract and temporally extended features of the environment, enabling efficient planning and decision-making. We propose a deep neural network architecture trained end-to-end to extract these hierarchical features, using a combination of unsupervised and supervised learning techniques. Empirical evaluations on a suite of benchmark MDP environments demonstrate that our method achieves significant performance gains compared to state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms, particularly in complex and sparse-reward settings. The learned hierarchical representations also exhibit strong transferability across related tasks. These findings suggest that hierarchical representation learning can provide a powerful mechanism for scaling reinforcement learning to more complex and real-world applications. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Hierarchical Representation Learning, Markov Decision Processes, Deep Learning, Abstraction, Generalization.

Blockchain technology provides a decentralized and immutable platform for various applications. Analyzing the underlying graph structure of blockchains, however, presents unique challenges due to its scale and evolving nature. This paper introduces ChainNet, a novel graph neural network (GNN) framework specifically designed for learning on blockchain graphs by incorporating topological features. ChainNet integrates node-level attributes with graph-level topological properties, such as cycle bases and connectivity measures, to enhance representation learning. We propose a hierarchical aggregation scheme that captures both local neighborhood information and global structural characteristics. Experimental results on real-world blockchain transaction datasets demonstrate that ChainNet significantly outperforms existing GNN models in tasks such as fraud detection and transaction classification. The incorporation of topological features allows ChainNet to better identify complex patterns and relationships within the blockchain graph. This work offers a new approach to blockchain analytics, enabling more accurate and efficient insights for security and optimization. Keywords: Blockchain, Graph Neural Networks, Topological Features, Fraud Detection, Transaction Classification.

Monocular Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO) is a critical technology for enabling autonomous navigation in resource-constrained environments. However, achieving accurate and robust performance requires precise initialization and calibration of the sensor system, particularly in online scenarios where real-time operation is essential. This paper addresses the challenge of online initialization and extrinsic spatial-temporal calibration for monocular VIO systems. We propose a novel framework that integrates visual and inertial data to simultaneously estimate the initial state, including scale, gravity, and velocity, while calibrating the extrinsic parameters and time offsets between the camera and inertial measurement unit (IMU). Our approach leverages a sliding-window optimization technique to ensure computational efficiency and real-time applicability. Experimental results on public datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy in both initialization and calibration compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. The framework is robust to varying motion dynamics and sensor noise, making it suitable for practical applications in robotics and augmented reality. This work contributes to advancing the field of VIO by providing a reliable and efficient solution for online initialization and calibration, paving the way for improved performance in real-world deployments. **Keywords**: Monocular Visual-Inertial Odometry, Online Initialization, Extrinsic Calibration, Spatial-Temporal Calibration, Sensor Fusion, Real-Time Optimization.

Matrix Neural Networks (MNNs) represent a novel approach to deep learning, designed to address the limitations of traditional neural networks in handling high-dimensional structured data. This paper introduces a new architecture that leverages matrix-based operations to enhance feature extraction and representation learning, particularly for tasks involving image, graph, and sequence data. The proposed MNN framework integrates matrix-valued weights and activations, enabling more efficient parameter utilization and improved interpretability compared to conventional scalar-based networks. We present a comprehensive evaluation of MNNs across multiple benchmarks, demonstrating superior performance in tasks such as image classification, graph analysis, and time-series forecasting. Experimental results show that MNNs achieve state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing computational overhead by up to 30%. The findings highlight the potential of MNNs to advance the field of deep learning, offering a scalable and interpretable alternative for complex data structures. This research contributes to the growing body of work on structured neural networks, with implications for applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and network science. **Keywords**: Matrix Neural Networks, Deep Learning, Structured Data, Feature Extraction, Interpretability, High-Dimensional Data.

Mục tiêu: Nghiên cứu nhằm tìm hiểu mối liên quan giữa nồng độ pepsinogen huyết thanh và viêm teo niêm mạc dạ dày theo phân loại OLGA. Đối tượng và phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang được thực hiện tại khoa Tiêu hóa bệnh viện Bạch Mai từ tháng 3 – 12/2019 trên 95 đối tượng từ 40 tuổi được chẩn đoán viêm teo niêm mạc dạ dày. Tất cả bệnh nhân được xét nghiệm pepsinogen I, II và kháng thể Helicobacter Pylori. Kết quả: Nồng độ pepsinogen I trung bình theo phân loại OLGA I, II, III-IV là 74,2 ± 25,8 ng/ml, 53,1± 9,7 ng/ml và 26,6 ± 8,5 ng/ml (P < 0,05). Tỉ lệ pepsinogen I/II theo phân loại OLGA I, II, III-IV là 6,1 ± 1,9; 5,3 ± 1,5 và 4,1 ± 0,8 (P < 0,05). Có mối tương quan nghịch giữa nồng độ PGI, tỉ lệ PGI/II và mức độ viêm teo theo OLGA: r = -0,539 và r = -0,308 (P < 0,05). Với giá trị ngưỡng của Nhật Bản PGI < 70 ng/ml và PGI/II < 3 chưa thể phân biệt viêm teo niêm mạc dạ dày mức độ nặng III-IV và nhẹ I-II (P=0,536; 95% CI: 0,12-62,2). Kết luận: Nồng độ PGI và tỷ lệ PGI/II tương quan nghịch với mức độ viêm teo niêm mạc dạ dày. Nếu áp dụng giá trị ngưỡng pepsinogen của Nhật Bản thì chưa tìm ra được bệnh nhân viêm teo niêm mạc dạ dày mức độ nặng III-IV.

Tuyến phòng thủ ven biển tỉnh Phú Yên thế kỷ XIX là một hệ thống quân sự quan trọng, được xây dựng nhằm bảo vệ vùng duyên hải trước các mối đe dọa từ bên ngoài. Tuyến phòng thủ bao gồm các đồn binh, pháo đài và hệ thống canh gác, được bố trí chiến lược dọc bờ biển. This paper presents an innovative approach to unsupervised learning from narrated instruction videos, addressing the challenge of automatically understanding and extracting valuable information from unstructured video data. Our objective is to develop a system that can learn from instructional videos without manual annotation, enabling applications in areas such as robotic learning, task automation, and intelligent tutoring. We propose a novel framework that leverages computer vision and natural language processing techniques to jointly learn visual and linguistic representations from video and audio streams. Our approach utilizes a multimodal fusion strategy to integrate features from both modalities, allowing the model to discover underlying patterns and relationships between visual actions and narrative descriptions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in learning meaningful representations from instruction videos, outperforming existing unsupervised learning approaches. Our research contributes to the development of more intelligent and autonomous systems, with potential applications in human-robot interaction, education, and knowledge acquisition. Key keywords: unsupervised learning, instruction videos, multimodal fusion, computer vision, natural language processing, robotic learning.

Video action recognition is a fundamental task in computer vision with numerous applications. However, accurately identifying actions in videos remains challenging due to factors such as complex backgrounds, camera motion, and variations in action execution. This paper introduces Temporal Saliency Integration (TSI), a novel approach that leverages temporal saliency to enhance video action recognition performance. TSI integrates frame-level saliency maps across time, emphasizing important regions and suppressing irrelevant background clutter. We propose a recurrent neural network-based architecture to effectively model temporal dynamics and integrate saliency information. The model learns to focus on salient regions over time, improving feature representation for action classification. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including UCF101 and HMDB51, demonstrate that TSI achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods. The results also confirm that the proposed method is robust to noisy environments. The TSI method provides a robust and efficient approach to video action recognition and can be easily integrated into existing deep learning frameworks. Keywords: video action recognition, temporal saliency, recurrent neural network, deep learning, computer vision.

Binary Neural Networks (BNNs) offer significant advantages in terms of computational efficiency and memory footprint, making them attractive for resource-constrained devices. However, they often suffer from accuracy degradation compared to their full-precision counterparts. This paper introduces Structured Binary Neural Networks (SBNNs), a novel approach to enhance the performance of BNNs in image recognition tasks. SBNNs incorporate structured sparsity within the binary weights, allowing for a more refined representation of features and improved gradient flow during training. We employ a group-wise regularization technique to enforce structured sparsity, which encourages the network to learn more discriminative and robust binary patterns. Experiments conducted on benchmark image classification datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrate that SBNNs achieve significantly higher accuracy compared to conventional BNNs and other state-of-the-art binarization methods, while maintaining comparable computational benefits. The proposed structured binarization strategy effectively bridges the performance gap between binary and full-precision networks, offering a practical solution for deploying deep learning models on edge devices. Keywords: Binary Neural Networks, Structured Sparsity, Image Recognition, Model Compression, Deep Learning.

This paper addresses the computational bottleneck of the Softmax function in large-scale classification tasks within Tensorflow. The objective is to improve the efficiency of training deep learning models with extremely large output spaces. We propose an optimized implementation of Sampled Softmax tailored for Tensorflow, leveraging a novel sampling strategy and parallel computation techniques. Our approach reduces the computational complexity from O(N) to O(K), where N is the number of classes and K is the number of sampled classes (K << N). Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate a significant speedup in training time compared to the standard Softmax and existing Sampled Softmax implementations, while maintaining comparable accuracy. Specifically, we achieve a 2x to 5x reduction in training time with minimal impact on classification performance. This efficient Sampled Softmax implementation enables faster training of large-scale classification models in Tensorflow, facilitating research and applications in areas such as natural language processing and recommendation systems. Keywords: Sampled Softmax, Tensorflow, large-scale classification, deep learning, efficiency, optimization.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning relational representations within the realm of artificial intelligence, emphasizing the significant impact of incorporating logic-based methods into auto-encoding frameworks. The research aims to explore and advance the understanding of how auto-encoding logic programs can be effectively utilized to capture and model complex relational structures in data. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative method that integrates auto-encoders with logic programming techniques to form a novel auto-encoding logic program model. This approach leverages the strengths of both neural networks and logical reasoning, facilitating the learning of structured representations from relational datasets. Our framework applies a hybrid learning algorithm that combines symbolic logic rules with deep learning architectures, enabling the extraction of meaningful patterns and relationships. Results/Findings: The experimental results demonstrate the capability of our proposed model to outperform traditional neural architectures when dealing with relational data. The model achieved notable improvements in accuracy and generalization across a series of benchmarks and tasks, including knowledge graph completion and relational inference. Additionally, comparisons with existing methods highlight the superior efficiency and robustness of our approach in capturing complex relational dependencies. Conclusion/Implications: The integration of logic programming into auto-encoding mechanisms presents a promising avenue for advancing the field of relational learning. Our contributions offer a novel paradigm for relational representation, with potential applications spanning various domains, including knowledge management, semantic web technologies, and AI inferences. This study sets the foundation for future exploration into hybrid models that synergize symbolic and connectionist approaches, opening up opportunities for more interpretable and reliable AI systems. Keywords: relational representations, auto-encoders, logic programming, neural networks, hybrid learning, knowledge graph, AI inference.

This paper presents a novel approach for text-based person re-identification (Re-ID) by introducing a Dual-path Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture integrated with a Max Gated block. The primary objective is to bridge the semantic gap between visual data and textual descriptions for enhanced cross-modal retrieval performance in surveillance and security applications. Our method leverages two parallel pathways: one for processing image data and another for textual attributes, enabling efficient feature extraction from both modalities. The Max Gated block is introduced as a key module to adaptively select and fuse salient features, effectively mitigating noise and amplifying relevant information during feature interaction. Extensive experiments are conducted on benchmark datasets for text-based person Re-ID, demonstrating that the proposed model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of retrieval accuracy and computational efficiency. The results highlight significant improvements in cross-modal matching capability, robust feature representation, and scalability. In summary, this work contributes a powerful dual-path deep learning framework with an innovative gating mechanism, paving the way for more reliable and accurate person re-identification systems in real-world scenarios. Keywords: person re-identification, cross-modal retrieval, text-based Re-ID, dual-path CNN, Max Gated block, deep learning, feature fusion

Video Object Segmentation (VOS) is a critical task in computer vision, with applications ranging from video editing to autonomous systems. However, achieving accurate and efficient segmentation in dynamic and complex video sequences remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces ALBA, a novel reinforcement learning (RL)-based framework designed to address the limitations of existing VOS methods. ALBA leverages a deep Q-network (DQN) architecture to learn optimal segmentation policies by interacting with video frames, enabling adaptive and context-aware object tracking. The proposed approach integrates spatial-temporal features and reward mechanisms to refine segmentation masks over time, ensuring robustness against occlusions and appearance changes. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including DAVIS and YouTube-VOS, demonstrate that ALBA achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming traditional and deep learning-based methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The framework also exhibits superior generalization capabilities across diverse video scenarios. The results highlight the potential of RL in enhancing VOS by enabling dynamic decision-making and reducing dependency on large annotated datasets. In conclusion, ALBA represents a significant advancement in VOS by combining reinforcement learning with deep learning techniques, offering a scalable and adaptive solution for real-world applications. Its ability to handle complex video sequences with minimal supervision makes it a promising tool for future research and industry adoption. **Keywords**: Video Object Segmentation, Reinforcement Learning, Deep Q-Network, Spatial-Temporal Features, Adaptive Tracking, Computer Vision.

This paper addresses the challenges of optimizing image recognition systems using a structured approach to Binary Neural Networks (BNNs). BNNs have gained attention due to their potential for reduced computational complexity and energy efficiency. However, achieving competitive performance compared to full-precision networks remains a challenge. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel design of structured Binary Neural Networks that leverages enhanced weight representation techniques and network architecture modifications. The approach integrates binary-weight matrices with optimized connections to minimize information loss commonly observed in traditional BNNs. Furthermore, we introduce structured pruning and quantization strategies to retain essential features while condensing network sizes effectively. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed structured BNNs achieve state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark image recognition datasets. Notably, the modified BNNs exhibit a significant reduction in inference time and energy consumption compared to conventional BNN implementations, with accuracy levels comparably close to full-precision models. Comparative analysis with existing methods highlights the robustness and efficiency of our approach across varying image recognition tasks. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel perspective on designing Binary Neural Networks for high-performance image recognition, underscoring the potential of structured approaches in achieving efficiency without compromising accuracy. The findings suggest applicability in resource-constrained environments such as edge computing and mobile devices, where energy efficiency and speed are paramount. Our structured BNN model lays the groundwork for future exploration into scalable and efficient neural network solutions. Keywords: Binary Neural Networks, image recognition, structured pruning, quantization, computational efficiency, energy-efficient AI.

This paper aims to investigate the development of a personalized climate control system for assistant driving, focusing on mining individual preferences to enhance in-vehicle comfort. Our approach utilizes machine learning algorithms and sensor data to model driver behavior and climate settings, enabling the prediction of optimal temperature and air quality conditions. The results show a significant improvement in user satisfaction and reduced energy consumption, outperforming traditional one-size-fits-all climate control systems. Key findings include the identification of distinct climate preference patterns among drivers and the importance of incorporating real-time weather and traffic data into the prediction model. This research contributes to the advancement of intelligent transportation systems and smart vehicles, with potential applications in autonomous driving and eco-friendly transportation solutions. By leveraging data-driven insights and AI-powered climate control, our system provides a more comfortable, efficient, and personalized driving experience, highlighting the benefits of human-centered design in automotive technology. Keywords: personalized climate control, assistant driving, machine learning, intelligent transportation systems, smart vehicles, user-centric design.

We propose an attention-based method that aggregates local image features to a subject-level representation for predicting disease severity. In contrast to classical deep learning that requires a fixed dimensional input, our method operates on a set of image patches; hence it can accommodate variable length input image without image resizing. The model learns a clinically interpretable subject-level representation that is reflective of the disease severity. Our model consists of three mutually dependent modules which regulate each other: (1) a discriminative network that learns a fixed-length representation from local features and maps them to disease severity; (2) an attention mechanism that provides interpretability by focusing on the areas of the anatomy that contribute the most to the prediction task; and (3) a generative network that encourages the diversity of the local latent features. The generative term ensures that the attention weights are non-degenerate while maintaining the relevance of the local regions to the disease severity. We train our model end-to-end in the context of a large-scale lung CT study of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). Our model gives state-of-the art performance in predicting clinical measures of severity for COPD. The distribution of the attention provides the regional relevance of lung tissue to the clinical measurements.

Graph Attention Networks (GATs) have emerged as a powerful framework for learning representations of graph-structured data, leveraging attention mechanisms to capture node relationships. However, the extent to which GATs truly exploit attention mechanisms remains underexplored. This study investigates the effectiveness of attention in GATs, aiming to quantify their attentiveness and identify potential limitations. We propose a systematic evaluation framework to analyze the attention weights learned by GATs across diverse graph datasets. Our experiments reveal that, in many cases, GATs exhibit limited variability in attention weights, often approximating a uniform distribution. This suggests that the attention mechanism may not be fully utilized as intended. To address this, we introduce a modified attention mechanism that enhances the model's ability to focus on relevant node features, improving performance on benchmark tasks. Our findings highlight the importance of rigorously evaluating attention mechanisms in graph neural networks and provide insights into designing more effective architectures. This work contributes to the broader understanding of attention-based models in graph representation learning, offering practical implications for applications in social networks, recommendation systems, and bioinformatics. **Keywords**: Graph Attention Networks, attention mechanisms, graph neural networks, node representation, graph-structured data.

Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in face recognition, but their vulnerability to adversarial attacks poses a significant security concern, particularly in real-world scenarios. This paper investigates the robustness of deep learning-based face recognition systems against physical-world adversarial attacks. We propose a novel attack strategy, termed "Robust Physical Perturbation" (RPP), which generates adversarial perturbations that are resilient to variations in lighting, pose, and distance. RPP leverages a combination of 3D face modeling and differentiable rendering to synthesize robust adversarial examples. Our experiments demonstrate that RPP significantly degrades the performance of state-of-the-art face recognition models under various physical conditions. Specifically, RPP achieves a high success rate in evading recognition even when faces are captured from different angles and under varying illumination. We further analyze the transferability of RPP-generated perturbations across different face recognition architectures. The findings highlight the need for developing more robust face recognition models that are resilient to physical-world adversarial attacks. Keywords: Face Recognition, Adversarial Attacks, Physical World, Deep Learning, Robustness, 3D Modeling, Differentiable Rendering.

This paper addresses the critical issue of reward poisoning attacks in reinforcement learning (RL), which can severely compromise the decision-making capabilities of intelligent systems. The aim is to develop effective defense mechanisms that can identify and mitigate such attacks, ensuring the integrity of the learning process. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel framework that integrates anomaly detection techniques with robust RL algorithms. Our approach involves monitoring the reward signals for irregular patterns indicative of malicious interference. By leveraging statistical analysis and machine learning-based classifiers, the framework adapts to a wide range of attack vectors without requiring prior knowledge of potential threats. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed defense mechanism significantly enhances the resilience of RL systems against reward poisoning attacks. Our framework achieves a detection accuracy of over 95% across various benchmark environments, outperforming existing state-of-the-art solutions. Furthermore, it maintains high performance in the presence of attacks, with minimal impact on the learning process. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides a substantial contribution to the field of safe AI, presenting a robust solution to safeguard RL systems against reward manipulation. The proposed method not only fortifies the reliability of RL applications in critical domains such as autonomous vehicles and finance but also sets a foundation for future advancements in secure RL. Keywords include reinforcement learning, reward poisoning, anomaly detection, AI security, and algorithmic robustness.

This paper presents a novel approach to face age progression, incorporating attribute manipulation to generate realistic and diverse age-progression sequences. The objective is to develop a deep learning-based model that can accurately predict and visualize the aging process of a face while allowing for controlled manipulation of attributes such as facial expression, hair color, and accessories. Our method employs a combination of generative adversarial networks (GANs) and attribute editing techniques to produce high-quality, age-progressive images. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming existing methods in terms of visual realism and attribute control. The proposed model has significant implications for applications in forensic science, entertainment, and social media, enabling the creation of realistic age-progression simulations with fine-grained control over facial attributes. Key contributions include the introduction of a novel attribute manipulation module and a comprehensive evaluation framework for face age progression. Relevant keywords: face age progression, attribute manipulation, GANs, deep learning, facial analysis.

Medical image segmentation is crucial for computer-aided diagnosis, but its reliance on extensive labeled data poses a significant challenge, especially when dealing with rare diseases. This paper introduces a novel semi-supervised few-shot learning approach to address this challenge. Our method leverages a meta-learning framework coupled with a consistency regularization technique to effectively utilize both limited labeled data and abundant unlabeled data. Specifically, we train the model to rapidly adapt to new segmentation tasks with only a few labeled examples, while the consistency regularization ensures consistent predictions on unlabeled data under different perturbations. We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to existing few-shot and semi-supervised methods. The results show that our approach achieves superior performance with limited labeled data, enabling more accurate and efficient medical image segmentation. This work offers a promising direction for reducing the annotation burden in medical imaging and improving the applicability of AI in healthcare. **Keywords:** Semi-supervised learning, few-shot learning, medical image segmentation, meta-learning, consistency regularization, deep learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of training low-bit neural networks, which are critical for deploying efficient deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. We propose *Semi-Relaxed Quantization with DropBits*, a novel framework that combines bit-wise regularization with a semi-relaxed quantization approach to optimize the trade-off between model accuracy and computational efficiency. Our method introduces a stochastic bit-dropping mechanism, DropBits, which randomly deactivates bits during training to enhance robustness and generalization in low-bitwidth settings. The semi-relaxed quantization strategy allows for flexible bit-width adaptation, enabling the model to dynamically adjust its precision during training. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in low-bit neural network training, outperforming existing quantization methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed framework also exhibits improved robustness to bit-width reduction, making it suitable for applications in edge computing and IoT devices. This work contributes a scalable and effective solution for training low-bit neural networks, with potential implications for advancing energy-efficient AI systems. **Keywords**: Low-bit neural networks, quantization, bit-wise regularization, DropBits, semi-relaxed quantization, edge computing, efficient AI.

This research paper addresses the challenge of accurately segmenting cross-country scenes captured in the infrared (IR) spectrum. Traditional image segmentation techniques often struggle with variability and lack of discernible features in IR imagery, which is commonly used in night vision and surveillance applications. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel image segmentation framework designed specifically for IR images. This framework employs a hybrid approach, integrating deep learning models with spectral and spatial analysis techniques. A customized convolutional neural network (CNN) is developed, optimized for the unique characteristics of IR data, and combined with an adaptive threshold segmentation method to enhance boundary precision and feature delineation. Results/Findings: Our experimental evaluation on a diverse set of cross-country IR images demonstrates significant improvements over existing segmentation methods. The proposed framework consistently delivers higher accuracy and robustness in feature extraction, achieving up to 25% improvement in segmentation quality compared to leading edge detection techniques. Performance metrics, such as precision, recall, and F1-score, indicate superior adaptation to various environmental conditions and scene complexities. Conclusion/Implications: The research provides a significant contribution to the field by offering an advanced solution for IR image segmentation. This framework can be applied in numerous practical settings, including military surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and environmental monitoring. By refining segmentation capabilities in the IR spectrum, the proposed approach enhances the reliability and effectiveness of systems that rely on IR data for decision making. Keywords: Image segmentation, infrared spectrum, cross-country scenes, deep learning, convolutional neural network, adaptive threshold, feature extraction.

This paper presents a novel approach to active exploration, leveraging model-based techniques to efficiently discover and learn about unknown environments. The objective is to develop an autonomous system capable of adapting to new situations and making informed decisions about where to explore next. Our approach utilizes a combination of probabilistic modeling and reinforcement learning to guide the exploration process, allowing the system to balance the trade-off between exploiting known areas and exploring unknown regions. The results demonstrate significant improvements in exploration efficiency and knowledge acquisition compared to traditional methods, with applications in fields such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and environmental monitoring. Key contributions include the development of a flexible and scalable framework for model-based active exploration, as well as insights into the importance of incorporating uncertainty and adaptability into the exploration process. Relevant keywords: active exploration, model-based reinforcement learning, autonomous systems, probabilistic modeling, uncertainty-aware planning.
