Kết quả cho thấy, cà chua có khả năng chịu hạn tương đối tốt, đặc biệt là khi được trồng trong điều kiện thiếu nước. Các chỉ tiêu sinh lý như tỷ lệ nước, nồng độ đường và axit có thể thay đổi đáng kể khi cà chua chịu hạn. Tuy nhiên, hàm lượng prolin trong cà chua lại tăng lên đáng kể khi cây chịu hạn. Hàm lượng prolin cao có thể giúp cà chua chịu hạn tốt hơn, nhưng cũng có thể ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng và hương vị của quả. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp thông tin quan trọng về khả năng chịu hạn của cà chua và có thể giúp các nhà sản xuất và nông dân điều chỉnh phương pháp trồng trọt để tối ưu hóa khả năng chịu hạn của cây.

This paper introduces IAN, a novel framework that combines multiple Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to achieve advanced imaginative face generation. The primary objective of IAN is to expand the creative and structural diversity of synthesized facial images beyond the limitations of traditional GAN architectures. The proposed approach leverages a hybrid architecture in which several specialized GAN modules collaboratively generate and refine facial features, enabling the system to construct highly realistic as well as imaginative and unconventional face representations. Through a multi-stage training process, IAN encourages cross-network feature integration and creative synthesis, enhancing both the visual fidelity and originality of the generated faces. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark face image datasets demonstrate that IAN outperforms state-of-the-art GAN models in terms of visual quality, diversity, and novelty of generated outputs, as measured by quantitative metrics and human perceptual studies. In addition, the proposed system exhibits strong capabilities in controlled generation, allowing users to guide the imaginative aspects of face creation through adjustable parameters. The findings highlight IAN’s potential for applications in entertainment, digital arts, and data augmentation for facial recognition systems. Overall, this work significantly advances the field of generative face modeling by introducing a powerful architecture that balances realism and imagination in automated face synthesis. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, face generation, deep learning, creative AI, image synthesis, neural networks, computer vision.

Objective: To develop an effective and scalable individual-level patient cost prediction method by automatically learning hidden temporal patterns from multivariate time series data in patient insurance claims using a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture. Methods: We used three years of medical and pharmacy claims data from 2013 to 2016 from a healthcare insurer, where data from the first two years were used to build the model to predict costs in the third year. The data consisted of the multivariate time series of cost, visit and medical features that were shaped as images of patients' health status (i.e., matrices with time windows on one dimension and the medical, visit and cost features on the other dimension). Patients' multivariate time series images were given to a CNN method with a proposed architecture. After hyper-parameter tuning, the proposed architecture consisted of three building blocks of convolution and pooling layers with an LReLU activation function and a customized kernel size at each layer for healthcare data. The proposed CNN learned temporal patterns became inputs to a fully connected layer. Conclusions: Feature learning through the proposed CNN configuration significantly improved individual-level healthcare cost prediction. The proposed CNN was able to outperform temporal pattern detection methods that look for a pre-defined set of pattern shapes, since it is capable of extracting a variable number of patterns with various shapes. Temporal patterns learned from medical, visit and cost data made significant contributions to the prediction performance. Hyper-parameter tuning showed that considering three-month data patterns has the highest prediction accuracy. Our results showed that patients' images extracted from multivariate time series data are different from regular images, and hence require unique designs of CNN architectures.

This research addresses the challenge of enhancing semi-supervised transfer learning by introducing an innovative approach known as Adaptive Consistency Regularization (ACR). The goal is to improve model performance when labeled data is scarce, thereby exploiting the abundant unlabeled data efficiently. Methods/Approach: The proposed ACR method integrates adaptive consistency measures into the transfer learning framework to ensure robust learning across different domains. It leverages model predictions to enforce a regularization term that adapts dynamically based on the confidence of predictions. This nuanced regularization balances between labeled and unlabeled data during the learning process, promoting better generalization. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that the ACR approach significantly outperforms traditional methods, exhibiting improved accuracy and reduced error rates in semi-supervised learning scenarios. Compared to existing consistency regularization techniques, ACR shows enhanced adaptability and efficiency, as evidenced by tests across multiple datasets. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Adaptive Consistency Regularization offers a valuable advancement in the field of semi-supervised transfer learning, allowing for more effective utilization of unlabeled data. This method opens up new possibilities for applications requiring domain adaptation and knowledge transfer, particularly in environments where labeled data is limited. The adaptability of ACR paves the way for further research into dynamic consistency-based learning models, potentially transforming data-efficient learning strategies across various IT domains. Keywords: Adaptive Consistency Regularization, Semi-Supervised Learning, Transfer Learning, Unlabeled Data, Domain Adaptation, Model Generalization.

This paper investigates the vocabulary reliance in scene text recognition, a crucial aspect of computer vision and natural language processing. The objective is to analyze how the performance of scene text recognition systems is affected by the vocabulary used in training datasets. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in recognition accuracy, particularly for out-of-vocabulary words, achieving a 25% increase in accuracy compared to state-of-the-art models. The findings highlight the importance of vocabulary adaptation in scene text recognition and contribute to the development of more robust and flexible systems. Key contributions include the introduction of a vocabulary adaptation module and the demonstration of its effectiveness in improving recognition accuracy. Relevant keywords: scene text recognition, vocabulary reliance, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, vocabulary adaptation.

For continual learning, if the shape ( i.e.covariance) of the representation distribution of each old class does not change much after learning new tasks, the previous knowledge is well-preserved. Moreover, through the spectral analysis viewpoint, an eigenvector direction that is adjusted slightly after updating will have a small corresponding angle, and vice versa. Therefore, monitoring the corresponding angle can give helpful information about representation shift: eigenvectors that do not change much preserve knowledge well, while ones that significantly change do not carry helpful knowledge in terms of reducing catastrophic forgetting.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving the efficiency and scalability of model-based deep reinforcement learning (MBRL) in complex environments. Traditional MBRL methods often struggle with high computational costs and sample inefficiency, particularly when dealing with large state-action spaces. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel approach called Variational State Tabulation (VST), which integrates variational inference techniques with state abstraction to reduce the complexity of environment modeling. VST dynamically clusters states into a compact representation, enabling faster learning and more efficient policy optimization. Our method leverages a probabilistic framework to approximate the environment dynamics, ensuring robustness while minimizing computational overhead. Experimental results on benchmark environments demonstrate that VST significantly outperforms existing MBRL methods in terms of sample efficiency and computational speed, achieving up to a 30% reduction in training time without compromising performance. Furthermore, the proposed approach exhibits superior generalization capabilities in high-dimensional and partially observable settings. The findings highlight the potential of VST to advance the practical applicability of MBRL in real-world scenarios, such as robotics and autonomous systems, where efficiency and scalability are critical. This work contributes a scalable and efficient framework for MBRL, paving the way for future research in adaptive state abstraction and probabilistic modeling. **Keywords**: model-based reinforcement learning, variational inference, state abstraction, sample efficiency, probabilistic modeling, scalability.

We address the problem of estimating a high quality dense depth map from a single RGB input image. We start out with a baseline encoder-decoder convolutional neural network architecture and pose the question of how the global processing of information can help improve overall depth estimation. To this end, we propose a transformer-based architecture block that divides the depth range into bins whose center value is estimated adaptively per image. The final depth values are estimated as linear combinations of the bin centers. We call our new building block AdaBins. Our results show a decisive improvement over the state-of-the-art on several popular depth datasets across all metrics. We also validate the effectiveness of the proposed block with an ablation study and provide the code and corresponding pre-trained weights of the new state-of-the-art model.

This paper introduces PowerGym, a novel reinforcement learning environment designed to optimize volt-var control in power distribution systems. The objective is to develop an adaptive and efficient control strategy that minimizes energy losses and maintains voltage stability. PowerGym utilizes a model-based approach, integrating real-time data and simulations to train reinforcement learning agents. The environment is evaluated using various algorithms, including deep Q-networks and policy gradients, and demonstrates improved performance compared to traditional control methods. Results show significant reductions in energy losses and enhanced voltage regulation, highlighting the potential of PowerGym to transform the operation of power distribution systems. The contributions of this research lie in the development of a scalable and flexible environment that enables the application of reinforcement learning to complex power system control problems, with implications for smart grid development and grid modernization. Key aspects of this work include reinforcement learning, volt-var control, power distribution systems, and smart grid optimization.

Recommender systems are pivotal in enhancing user experience by providing tailored suggestions across various platforms. This paper addresses a critical challenge in recommender systems: efficiently identifying optimal input features to improve recommendation accuracy and system adaptability. We introduce a novel Differentiable Neural Input Search (DNIS) framework, which leverages gradient-based optimization to automatically and dynamically determine the most relevant input features for neural recommender models. Unlike traditional methods that rely on static feature selection, our approach integrates seamlessly into the training process, allowing for adaptive input adjustments in real-time. Experiments conducted on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that DNIS significantly improves recommendation accuracy, outperforming existing feature selection methods both in terms of precision and computational efficiency. The results indicate that DNIS not only enhances the performance of neural recommender systems but also reduces the complexity and manual effort associated with feature selection. This study provides new insights into the development of more intelligent and adaptable recommendation algorithms, paving the way for future advancements in personalized content delivery. Keywords: recommender systems, feature selection, neural networks, differentiable optimization, machine learning.

This paper introduces a novel approach for learning generative models of tissue organization using supervised Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The objective is to generate realistic and diverse synthetic tissue samples that mimic the complex structural arrangements observed in biological tissues. Our method employs a supervised GAN framework, where the discriminator is trained to distinguish between real and generated tissue samples, while simultaneously being guided by expert annotations of tissue components. This supervised learning approach ensures that the generated tissues not only exhibit visual realism but also accurately reflect the underlying biological structures. We evaluate our model on multiple datasets of histological images, demonstrating its ability to generate high-quality synthetic tissues with controlled variations in cellular density, spatial arrangement, and tissue morphology. Quantitative analysis, including Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and structural similarity (SSIM) metrics, reveals that our supervised GAN significantly outperforms unsupervised GANs and other generative models in capturing the intricate patterns of tissue organization. The generated synthetic tissues can be valuable for various applications, including training deep learning models for automated tissue analysis, simulating disease progression, and augmenting limited datasets for biomedical research. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, GAN, tissue organization, supervised learning, histological images, synthetic data, biomedical imaging.

This paper presents a novel approach to image inpainting, leveraging context-aware semantic understanding to restore missing regions in images. The objective is to develop an effective method that not only fills in missing pixels but also ensures the completed image is semantically coherent and visually pleasing. Our approach utilizes a deep learning-based model that integrates contextual information and semantic features to guide the inpainting process. The model is trained on a large dataset of images with varying levels of occlusion and damage. Experimental results demonstrate that our context-aware semantic inpainting method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving significant improvements in terms of visual quality and semantic accuracy. The proposed method has important implications for applications such as image editing, restoration, and computer vision. Key contributions include the introduction of a novel context-aware loss function and the development of a semantic feature extraction module. Our research highlights the potential of deep learning-based approaches for image inpainting and paves the way for future work in this area, with relevant keywords including image inpainting, semantic understanding, deep learning, computer vision, and context-aware modeling.

Accurate filling level classification is critical for applications in industrial automation, logistics, and waste management. However, existing methods often struggle with variability in object shapes, lighting conditions, and occlusions, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper proposes a novel approach to improve filling level classification by leveraging adversarial training techniques. We introduce a deep learning framework that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a generative adversarial network (GAN) to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of the classification model. The adversarial component is designed to generate challenging synthetic data, enabling the classifier to learn more discriminative features under diverse conditions. Experiments conducted on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that our method achieves a significant improvement in classification accuracy compared to traditional approaches, with a 12% increase in precision and a 9% reduction in error rates. Furthermore, the model exhibits superior performance in real-world scenarios with varying environmental factors. The results highlight the potential of adversarial training to address key challenges in filling level classification, offering a scalable and adaptable solution for industrial applications. This research contributes to advancing the state-of-the-art in automated monitoring systems and provides a foundation for future work in adversarial learning for classification tasks. **Keywords**: filling level classification, adversarial training, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, generative adversarial networks, industrial automation.

Recently, a new recurrent neural network (RNN) named the Legendre Memory Unit (LMU) was proposed and shown to achieve state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. Here we leverage the linear time-invariant (LTI) memory component of the LMU to construct a simplified variant that can be parallelized during training (and yet executed as an RNN during inference), thus overcoming a well known limitation of training RNNs on GPUs. We show that this reformulation that aids parallelizing, which can be applied generally to any deep network whose recurrent components are linear, makes training up to 200 times faster. Second, to validate its utility, we compare its performance against the original LMU and a variety of published LSTM and transformer networks on seven benchmarks, ranging from psMNIST to sentiment analysis to machine translation. We demonstrate that our models exhibit superior performance on all datasets, often using fewer parameters. For instance, our LMU sets a new state-of-the-art result on psMNIST, and uses half the parameters while outperforming DistilBERT and LSTM models on IMDB sentiment analysis.

In this paper, we develop a new approach of spatially supervised recurrent convolutional neural networks for visual object tracking. Our recurrent convolutional network exploits the history of locations as well as the distinctive visual features learned by the deep neural networks. Inspired by recent bounding box regression methods for object detection, we study the regression capability of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) in the temporal domain, and propose to concatenate high-level visual features produced by convolutional networks with region information. In contrast to existing deep learning based trackers that use binary classification for region candidates, we use regression for direct prediction of the tracking locations both at the convolutional layer and at the recurrent unit. Our extensive experimental results and performance comparison with state-of-the-art tracking methods on challenging benchmark video tracking datasets shows that our tracker is more accurate and robust while maintaining low computational cost. For most test video sequences, our method achieves the best tracking performance, often outperforms the second best by a large margin.

Disentangling latent factors from observed data remains a significant challenge, particularly in natural data where nonlinear relationships prevail. This paper introduces a novel approach, Temporal Sparse Coding (TSC), designed to achieve nonlinear disentanglement by leveraging temporal coherence. TSC encodes time-series data into sparse latent representations, enforcing temporal smoothness on disentangled factors. We propose a neural network architecture that integrates sparse coding principles with temporal constraints, allowing the model to learn disentangled representations without explicit supervision. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, including video sequences and motion capture data, demonstrate that TSC outperforms existing disentanglement methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy, factor interpretability, and downstream task performance. Furthermore, we show that TSC is robust to noise and occlusions commonly found in natural data. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of temporal sparsity as a powerful inductive bias for nonlinear disentanglement, offering a promising direction for representation learning in various domains. Keywords: Disentanglement, Sparse Coding, Temporal Modeling, Representation Learning, Nonlinear Dynamics.

This paper addresses the challenge of estimating feature importance in machine learning models under distribution shifts, where the training and testing data distributions differ. Our objective is to develop a robust method that accurately identifies crucial features in the presence of such shifts. We propose a novel approach that combines model-agnostic feature importance estimation with uncertainty quantification, allowing for reliable feature ranking even when the data distribution changes. Our method utilizes a combination of techniques, including permutation feature importance and Bayesian neural networks, to provide accurate and robust feature importance estimates. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of feature importance estimation accuracy and robustness under various distribution shifts. The key findings of this study highlight the importance of accounting for distribution shifts in feature importance estimation and demonstrate the potential of our approach in real-world applications, such as healthcare and finance, where data distributions often change over time. Our research contributes to the development of more reliable and trustworthy machine learning models, with key keywords including feature importance, distribution shifts, uncertainty quantification, and robust machine learning.

The dramatically growing availability of observational data is being witnessed in various domains of science and technology, which facilitates the study of causal inference. However, estimating treatment effects from observational data is faced with two major challenges, missing counterfactual outcomes and treatment selection bias. Matching methods are among the most widely used and fundamental approaches to estimating treatment effects, but existing matching methods have poor performance when facing data with high dimensional and complicated variables. We propose a feature selection representation matching (FSRM) method based on deep representation learning and matching, which maps the original covariate space into a selective, nonlinear, and balanced representation space, and then conducts matching in the learned representation space. FSRM adopts deep feature selection to minimize the influence of irrelevant variables for estimating treatment effects and incorporates a regularizer based on the Wasserstein distance to learn balanced representations. We evaluate the performance of our FSRM method on three datasets, and the results demonstrate superiority over the state-of-the-art methods.

Deep learning is ubiquitous across many areas areas of computer vision. It often requires large scale datasets for training before being fine-tuned on small-to-medium scale problems. Activity, or, in other words, action recognition, is one of many application areas of deep learning. While there exist many Convolutional Neural Network architectures that work with the RGB and optical flow frames, training on the time sequences of 3D body skeleton joints is often performed via recurrent networks such as LSTM. In this paper, we propose a new representation which encodes sequences of 3D body skeleton joints in texture-like representations derived from mathematically rigorous kernel methods. Such a representation becomes the first layer in a standard CNN network e.g., ResNet-50, which is then used in the supervised domain adaptation pipeline to transfer information from the source to target dataset. This lets us leverage the available Kinect-based data beyond training on a single dataset and outperform simple fine-tuning on any two datasets combined in a naive manner. More specifically, in this paper we utilize the overlapping classes between datasets. We associate datapoints of the same class via so-called commonality, known from the supervised domain adaptation. We demonstrate state-of-the-art results on three publicly available benchmarks.

Japanese comics (called manga) are traditionally created in monochrome format. In recent years, in addition to monochrome comics, full color comics, a more attractive medium, have appeared. Unfortunately, color comics require manual colorization, which incurs high labor costs. Although automatic colorization methods have been recently proposed, most of them are designed for illustrations, not for comics. Unlike illustrations, since comics are composed of many consecutive images, the painting style must be consistent. To realize consistent colorization, we propose here a semi-automatic colorization method based on generative adversarial networks (GAN); the method learns the painting style of a specific comic from small amount of training data. The proposed method takes a pair of a screen tone image and a flat colored image as input, and outputs a colorized image. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves better performance than the existing alternatives.

Adder Neural Networks (ANNs) which only contain additions bring us a new way of developing deep neural networks with low energy consumption. Unfortunately, there is an accuracy drop when replacing all convolution filters by adder filters. The main reason here is the optimization difficulty of ANNs using \ell_1-norm, in which the estimation of gradient in back propagation is inaccurate. In this paper, we present a novel method for further improving the performance of ANNs without increasing the trainable parameters via a progressive kernel based knowledge distillation (PKKD) method. A convolutional neural network (CNN) with the same architecture is simultaneously initialized and trained as a teacher network, features and weights of ANN and CNN will be transformed to a new space to eliminate the accuracy drop. The similarity is conducted in a higher-dimensional space to disentangle the difference of their distributions using a kernel based method. Finally, the desired ANN is learned based on the information from both the ground-truth and teacher, progressively. The effectiveness of the proposed method for learning ANN with higher performance is then well-verified on several benchmarks. For instance, the ANN-50 trained using the proposed PKKD method obtains a 76.8\% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet dataset, which is 0.6\% higher than that of the ResNet-50.

Safe exploration in reinforcement learning (RL) remains a critical challenge, particularly in environments where premature termination can lead to catastrophic outcomes. This paper addresses the problem of safe exploration by formulating it as an Early Terminated Markov Decision Process (ET-MDP), a novel framework designed to model and mitigate risks associated with early termination. The proposed approach integrates risk-aware policies with adaptive exploration strategies, enabling agents to learn optimal behaviors while minimizing the likelihood of unsafe states. We introduce a dynamic penalty mechanism that penalizes unsafe actions based on their proximity to termination conditions, ensuring a balance between exploration and safety. Experimental results on benchmark environments demonstrate that our method significantly reduces the occurrence of early terminations compared to traditional RL algorithms, while maintaining competitive performance in achieving task objectives. The framework is further validated in simulated robotic navigation tasks, showcasing its applicability to real-world scenarios. This research contributes a robust and scalable solution for safe exploration, with potential applications in autonomous systems, robotics, and safety-critical domains. **Keywords**: Safe exploration, reinforcement learning, early termination, Markov Decision Process, risk-aware policies, adaptive exploration.

Accurate forecasting of multivariate time series data presents a significant challenge in numerous applications, including finance, healthcare, and environmental science. This paper introduces Residual Recurrent Neural Networks (R2N2), a novel approach aimed at improving predictive accuracy for complex multivariate time series data. Methods/Approach: The R2N2 model integrates the strengths of recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures with a residual learning framework to address issues of vanishing gradients and to enhance information flow across time steps. By incorporating residual connections, the model effectively captures long-term dependencies and complex temporal patterns, resulting in more accurate and robust forecasting capabilities. Results/Findings: Our experimental evaluation on various benchmark multivariate time series datasets reveals that R2N2 outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Comparative analysis demonstrates a significant reduction in forecasting error rates and improvements in modeling dynamics of intricate data sequences compared to traditional RNNs and other sequential models. Conclusion/Implications: The research contributes a powerful tool for practitioners and researchers working with multivariate time series, offering enhanced predictive performance and scalability. The R2N2 model's ability to capture intricate dependencies and improve forecast accuracy makes it applicable to a broad range of domains, from financial market analysis to healthcare decision support systems. Future work may explore further adaptation for real-time applications and integration with hybrid forecasting systems. Keywords: multivariate time series, forecasting, residual learning, recurrent neural networks, R2N2, prediction accuracy, long-term dependencies.

The ability to reason effectively within large-scale theories is a critical challenge in artificial intelligence, particularly in domains requiring complex logical inference and decision-making. This paper addresses the problem of enabling AI systems to reason autonomously in large theories without relying on imitation learning or pre-existing human-generated reasoning traces. We propose a novel framework that combines reinforcement learning with symbolic reasoning techniques to guide the exploration of large theory spaces. Our approach leverages a dynamic reward mechanism to prioritize logical consistency and relevance, enabling the system to discover valid reasoning paths independently. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to imitation-based approaches, while significantly reducing reliance on annotated training data. The results highlight the potential of our framework to generalize across diverse domains and scale to increasingly complex theories. This work contributes to advancing autonomous reasoning capabilities in AI systems, with implications for applications in automated theorem proving, knowledge base construction, and decision support systems. **Keywords**: autonomous reasoning, reinforcement learning, symbolic reasoning, large theories, logical inference, AI systems.

Multivariate time series forecasting is crucial for various applications, including financial analysis, weather prediction, and anomaly detection. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated remarkable success in generating realistic data, but their training remains challenging due to issues like mode collapse and instability. This paper introduces a novel unified training framework for GANs leveraging self-labeling and self-attention mechanisms to address these limitations. Our approach incorporates a self-labeling module that assigns pseudo-labels to generated samples, providing additional supervisory signals to the discriminator. Furthermore, a self-attention mechanism is integrated within both the generator and discriminator to capture long-range dependencies and improve feature representation. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, CelebA, and LSUN, demonstrating significant improvements in image quality and training stability compared to existing GAN training techniques. Experimental results show that our unified approach achieves state-of-the-art Inception Score and FID scores, indicating enhanced generative performance. The proposed framework offers a robust and effective strategy for training GANs, leading to more stable convergence and higher-quality generated samples. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, GAN, Self-Labeling, Self-Attention, Image Generation, Unsupervised Learning.

This paper presents an end-to-end learning framework for 3D point cloud registration, utilizing the novel concept of virtual correspondences. The objective is to improve the accuracy and robustness of aligning two unstructured 3D point clouds, a critical task in fields such as autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. Unlike traditional methods that rely on hand-crafted features or explicit correspondence matching, our approach leverages deep neural networks to implicitly learn spatial relationships and generate virtual correspondences that guide the registration process. The proposed model integrates feature extraction, correspondence estimation, and transformation prediction into a unified pipeline, enabling joint optimization through supervised and unsupervised loss functions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in registration accuracy, outlier resistance, and computational efficiency compared to existing classical and learning-based techniques. Our method further exhibits strong generalization across diverse point cloud scenes without requiring extensive pre-processing or manual parameter tuning. The findings highlight the effectiveness of leveraging virtual correspondences within deep learning frameworks for 3D geometric learning. This approach opens new possibilities for efficient, scalable, and reliable 3D point cloud processing in real-world applications. Key topics addressed include 3D point cloud registration, virtual correspondences, end-to-end learning, deep learning for geometric matching, and spatial transformation networks.

Scene Graph Generation (SGG) is a critical task in computer vision, aiming to model the relationships between objects in an image as a structured graph. However, existing approaches often treat relation labels as flat categories, overlooking their inherent hierarchical structure, which can lead to suboptimal performance. This paper explores the hierarchical nature of relation labels in SGG and proposes a novel framework to leverage this hierarchy for improved relation prediction. Our approach introduces a hierarchical classification model that captures the dependencies and semantic relationships between different levels of relation labels, from coarse-grained to fine-grained. We evaluate our method on benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in relation prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art flat-label approaches. Additionally, our framework enhances interpretability by providing insights into the hierarchical structure of relations. The results highlight the importance of incorporating hierarchical information in SGG and open new avenues for research in structured visual understanding. Key contributions include a scalable hierarchical model, improved performance metrics, and a deeper understanding of relation label semantics. This work has implications for applications such as image captioning, visual question answering, and autonomous systems, where accurate and interpretable scene understanding is crucial. **Keywords**: Scene Graph Generation, Hierarchical Classification, Relation Prediction, Computer Vision, Structured Visual Understanding.

A micro-services architecture offers a modern approach to building applications by dividing the system into smaller, independent services, each handling a specific piece of functionality with its own logic and database. This paper investigates the vulnerability of speech command classification systems to universal adversarial examples, which are crafted perturbations that, when added to any input, can mislead a model to produce incorrect outputs. Understanding these vulnerabilities is crucial for enhancing the robustness and security of speech recognition technologies, widely used in voice-activated applications. Methods/Approach: We developed an innovative algorithm to generate universal adversarial examples for widely used speech command classification models. By employing a combination of gradient-based adversarial techniques and iterative optimization strategies, we crafted perturbations that remain effective across different inputs and models. The methodology was evaluated on various neural network architectures to assess the generalizability and efficacy of the adversarial examples. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrated that speech command classification models are highly susceptible to universal adversarial perturbations, with success rates exceeding 85% in misclassifying inputs when subjected to these crafted noises. Notably, the adversarial examples maintained their effectiveness under different levels of background noise, showcasing their robustness in diverse environmental conditions. Comparing our results with state-of-the-art adversarial strategies, our method showed superior performance in generating compact and efficient universal perturbations. Conclusion/Implications: This study reveals significant vulnerabilities in current speech command classification systems and emphasizes the need for stronger defensive measures to safeguard against adversarial attacks. The insights gained from our findings have important implications for the design of more robust and secure voice-activated systems. Future research could explore adaptive defense mechanisms that dynamically counteract adversarial influences to ensure reliable speech processing applications. Keywords: Universal adversarial examples, speech command classification, neural networks, adversarial attack, speech recognition, model robustness.

Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is a widely used probabilistic model for topic discovery in text corpora. This paper introduces a novel spectral algorithm for estimating the parameters of LDA models. Unlike traditional iterative methods, such as Gibbs sampling or Expectation-Maximization, our approach leverages spectral decomposition techniques to directly estimate topic-word distributions and document-topic distributions. The proposed algorithm offers provable guarantees for consistent parameter estimation under mild conditions. We demonstrate, through experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, that our spectral algorithm achieves comparable or superior accuracy to existing methods, while exhibiting significantly faster convergence rates. The results highlight the potential of spectral methods for large-scale topic modeling tasks, offering an efficient alternative to traditional inference algorithms. Keywords: Latent Dirichlet Allocation, Topic Modeling, Spectral Algorithms, Parameter Estimation, Text Analysis.

Constrained optimization in reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for ensuring that policies adhere to safety and operational constraints while maximizing performance. This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing policies under constraints by proposing a novel approach called Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO). The objective is to develop a robust and efficient algorithm that balances reward maximization with constraint satisfaction, particularly in environments where safety and feasibility are paramount. The proposed method builds on the foundation of policy gradient algorithms, integrating constraint-handling mechanisms directly into the optimization process. By leveraging Lagrangian duality and adaptive penalty methods, CPO ensures that constraints are respected throughout the learning process. The approach is evaluated on a range of benchmark tasks, including robotic control and autonomous navigation, where constraint violations can have significant real-world consequences. Experimental results demonstrate that CPO outperforms existing constrained RL methods in terms of both constraint satisfaction and cumulative reward. The algorithm achieves superior sample efficiency and stability, making it suitable for real-world applications with limited data availability. Furthermore, the method is shown to generalize well across diverse environments, highlighting its robustness. This research contributes a practical and scalable solution to constrained policy optimization, offering significant implications for safe and reliable deployment of RL systems in critical domains such as healthcare, robotics, and autonomous systems. The proposed framework opens new avenues for developing AI systems that operate safely and effectively in complex, constrained environments. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Constrained Optimization, Policy Gradient, Safety Constraints, Lagrangian Duality, Autonomous Systems.

Graph-based learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for analyzing structured data, with Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs) and Label Propagation (LP) being two prominent approaches. While GCNs excel in leveraging node features and graph structure, LP focuses on propagating labels across the graph based on connectivity. This paper proposes a novel framework that unifies GCNs and LP, addressing their individual limitations and combining their strengths. The proposed method integrates the feature-learning capabilities of GCNs with the label-smoothing properties of LP, enabling more robust and accurate predictions on semi-supervised node classification tasks. We introduce a hybrid model that jointly optimizes feature representation and label propagation through a unified loss function, ensuring seamless interaction between the two components. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms standalone GCN and LP methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and robustness. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining feature-based and structure-based learning, offering a promising direction for future research in graph-based machine learning. This work contributes to the growing field of graph representation learning by providing a scalable and interpretable framework with potential applications in social network analysis, recommendation systems, and bioinformatics. **Keywords**: Graph Convolutional Networks, Label Propagation, Semi-Supervised Learning, Graph Representation Learning, Node Classification.

This research addresses the need for more transparent and interpretable models in medical imaging by developing a framework for explainable disease classification that utilizes weakly-supervised segmentation techniques. The primary aim is to provide accurate disease diagnosis while offering insights into the decision-making process of the model. Methods/Approach: We introduce an innovative approach that leverages weakly-supervised segmentation to enhance the explainability of disease classification models. Our framework utilizes a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and attention mechanisms to highlight critical regions in medical images that influence classification decisions. The model is trained using only image-level labels, reducing the need for extensive pixel-wise annotations traditionally required for segmentation tasks. Results/Findings: The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in disease classification compared to traditional CNN-based approaches while providing clear visual explanations for its predictions. Our experiments on multiple benchmark datasets indicate that the model achieves high accuracy and robustness, with visualizations that effectively highlight medically relevant areas associated with disease presence. The weakly-supervised segmentation enhances the interpretability of the classification process substantially. Conclusion/Implications: This study provides a significant contribution to the domain of explainable artificial intelligence in medical imaging by presenting a method that balances prediction accuracy with interpretability. The integration of weakly-supervised segmentation expands the potential for clinicians to trust and adopt AI-driven diagnostic tools, potentially improving clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. Our framework sets a precedent for developing more explainable models in various medical applications. Key Keywords: explainable AI, disease classification, weakly-supervised segmentation, convolutional neural networks, medical imaging, interpretable models, attention mechanisms.

This study addresses the growing challenge of face spoofing attacks on biometric systems by introducing a novel approach for face anti-spoofing, termed as Physics-Guided Spoof Trace Disentanglement. The main objective is to enhance the robustness of face recognition systems against sophisticated spoofing attempts by disentangling spoof traces through a physics-informed methodology. Methods/Approach: We propose a model that incorporates physical properties of facial surfaces to distinguish between genuine human faces and spoofing artifacts. The approach employs advanced disentanglement techniques that leverage physics-based cues, effectively separating spoof traces from authentic facial features. The methodology is grounded in artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms, which are calibrated using a comprehensive dataset featuring diverse spoofing scenarios. Results/Findings: The proposed approach demonstrates significant improvements in face anti-spoofing performance, exceeding the accuracy of existing methods. The model achieves impressive results in accurately identifying spoofing attacks, with a marked reduction in false acceptance rates. Comparative analysis reveals that our technique effectively outperforms traditional face anti-spoofing methods under varying lighting conditions and attack types, establishing a new benchmark in the field. Conclusion/Implications: The research contributes a physics-guided model that not only advances the capabilities of face anti-spoofing technology but also provides a generalized solution applicable across different biometric systems. The implications of this work are significant for enhancing the security and reliability of face recognition platforms, potentially benefiting applications ranging from personal device unlocking to security in sensitive environments. Our approach paves the way for future research in physics-integrated face recognition solutions. Keywords: face anti-spoofing, spoof trace disentanglement, biometric security, physics-guided model, machine learning, facial recognition.

This graduation thesis introduces ARNav, an innovative Augmented Reality (AR) indoor navigation mobile application, addressing the growing need for intuitive and accurate navigation systems within complex indoor environments. The increasing complexity of modern buildings and the limitations of traditional navigation methods motivate this research, highlighting the importance of developing a user-friendly and efficient solution. The primary objectives of ARNav are to design and develop a mobile application that utilizes AR technology to provide users with a seamless and immersive indoor navigation experience, reducing navigation errors and enhancing overall user satisfaction. Specifically, this research aims to solve the problems of wayfinding and orientation within large indoor spaces, such as shopping malls, airports, and museums. To achieve this, a hybrid approach combining AR, computer vision, and mobile sensing technologies is employed. The system architecture of ARNav incorporates a markerless tracking algorithm, enabling users to navigate through indoor spaces using their mobile device's camera and sensor data. The results of this research demonstrate the effectiveness of ARNav in improving indoor navigation, with users experiencing reduced navigation time and increased satisfaction. The expected contributions of this research include the development of a novel AR-based indoor navigation system, providing a foundation for future research and real-world applications in various industries. In conclusion, ARNav offers a significant advancement in indoor navigation, leveraging the potential of AR technology to enhance user experience. Future developments may focus on integrating additional features, such as accessibility support and personalized routing, to further enhance the application's functionality and usability.

Although the construction and algorithm for granddaddy sequences have been known since around 1978, the discovery of a specialized decoder, DKRR, did not occur until 2016, thanks to Kociumaka, Radoszewski, and W. Rytter. DKRR is designed for granddaddy sequences of order k, and given any substring v of length k, it can efficiently locate the unique position of v in x. Remarkably, DKRR operates in O(k²log(q)) time on the word-RAM model and in O(k²) time under the unit-cost RAM model, offering significant computational efficiency.

– Classifier Chain (CC) : This approach considers label dependencies by creating a chain of binary classifiers, where each classifier is trained to predict the presence or absence of a label based on the input features aswell as the previously predicted labels in the chain. The chain is constructed in a specific order, typically determined by the label dependencies or a random permutation. During prediction, the classifiers are applied sequentially, with the output of each classifier being used as an additional input for the subsequent classifier. By incorporating the information from previously predicted labels, the Classifier Chain can capture label dependencies and improve the accuracy of multi-label classification. However, this approach is sensitive to label order, and errors made by early classifiers can propagate and affect subsequent predictions.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently learning CHARME (Contextual Hierarchical Attention-based Recurrent Memory Encoder) models, which are designed to capture complex temporal dependencies and hierarchical structures in sequential data. Traditional approaches often struggle with scalability and computational efficiency, particularly when dealing with large-scale datasets. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel neural network-based framework that integrates advanced attention mechanisms and memory-augmented architectures. Our approach leverages multi-layer recurrent neural networks (RNNs) combined with hierarchical attention layers to dynamically focus on relevant temporal and contextual features. We evaluate the proposed model on benchmark datasets for sequential prediction tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. The results highlight the model's ability to handle long-range dependencies and adapt to varying levels of data complexity. This research contributes to the advancement of sequential data modeling by introducing a scalable and interpretable framework, with potential applications in natural language processing, time-series analysis, and recommendation systems. Key innovations include the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms and memory-augmented RNNs, which enhance both performance and interpretability. Keywords: CHARME models, neural networks, attention mechanisms, sequential data, hierarchical modeling, memory-augmented architectures.

Tích hợp giảm thiểu rủi ro thiên tai trong quy hoạch đô thị là một vấn đề cấp thiết hiện nay. Để xây dựng các thành phố an toàn và bền vững, cần phải áp dụng các biện pháp tích hợp để giảm thiểu rủi ro thiên tai. Lý luận và kinh nghiệm cho thấy rằng, tích hợp giảm thiểu rủi ro thiên tai trong quy hoạch đô thị cần phải dựa trên các nguyên tắc sau: Đầu tiên, cần phải đánh giá và phân tích các rủi ro thiên tai tiềm ẩn trong khu vực quy hoạch. Điều này sẽ giúp xác định các khu vực có nguy cơ cao và cần phải có các biện pháp phòng ngừa và giảm thiểu rủi ro. Thứ hai, cần phải áp dụng các công nghệ và kỹ thuật hiện đại để xây dựng các công trình và hệ thống cơ sở hạ tầng an toàn và bền vững. Điều này bao gồm việc sử dụng các vật liệu và công nghệ có khả năng chống chịu với các tác động của thiên tai. Thứ ba, cần phải tích hợp các biện pháp giảm thiểu rủi ro thiên tai vào quy hoạch đô thị một cách toàn diện. Điều này bao gồm việc thiết kế các công trình và hệ thống cơ sở hạ tầng một cách an toàn và bền vững, cũng như việc lập kế hoạch và quản lý các nguồn lực và tài nguyên một cách hiệu quả. Cuối cùng, cần phải có sự tham gia và phối hợp của các bên liên quan, bao gồm chính quyền địa phương, cộng đồng và các tổ chức liên quan, để xây dựng các thành phố an toàn và bền vững.

Reinforcement learning (RL) in environments with high-dimensional or rich observations presents significant challenges in terms of sample efficiency and policy optimization. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing a provably efficient RL framework that leverages latent state decoding. The proposed approach utilizes representation learning to infer a compact latent state space from complex observational data, enabling the agent to operate in a lower-dimensional space while preserving essential environment dynamics. We develop a novel algorithm that integrates latent state inference with RL policy updates, ensuring accurate state estimation and efficient exploration. Our theoretical analysis establishes sample complexity bounds, demonstrating that the method achieves near-optimal learning performance under reasonable assumptions. Extensive experiments on benchmark environments with rich observations showcase superior performance compared to existing baselines, with notable improvements in convergence speed and policy effectiveness. This work contributes a principled methodology for scaling RL to more realistic settings with high-dimensional inputs and highlights the benefits of combining representation learning with sample-efficient policy optimization. Keywords: reinforcement learning, latent state decoding, rich observations, sample efficiency, representation learning, provable guarantees.

Đánh giá khuyết tật cọc khoan nhồi là một phần quan trọng trong việc đảm bảo an toàn và chất lượng của các công trình xây dựng. Cọc khoan nhồi là một loại cọc được sử dụng rộng rãi trong xây dựng, đặc biệt là trong các công trình có yêu cầu cao về độ ổn định và độ bền. Khuyết tật cọc khoan nhồi có thể xảy ra do nhiều nguyên nhân, bao gồm sự không đồng đều của vật liệu, quá trình sản xuất không đúng quy trình, hoặc do tác động của môi trường. Nếu không được phát hiện và xử lý kịp thời, khuyết tật cọc khoan nhồi có thể dẫn đến sự sụp đổ của công trình, gây thiệt hại nghiêm trọng về tài sản và tính mạng. Vận tốc sóng siêu âm là một phương pháp được sử dụng để đánh giá khuyết tật cọc khoan nhồi. Phương pháp này dựa trên nguyên tắc rằng sóng siêu âm sẽ bị ảnh hưởng bởi sự không đồng đều của vật liệu và khuyết tật trong cọc. Bằng cách đo lường vận tốc và cường độ của sóng siêu âm, có thể xác định được vị trí và mức độ nghiêm trọng của khuyết tật. Đánh giá khuyết tật cọc khoan nhồi theo vận tốc sóng siêu âm là một công nghệ hiện đại và hiệu quả, giúp đảm bảo an toàn và chất lượng của các công trình xây dựng. Phương pháp này không chỉ giúp phát hiện khuyết tật cọc khoan nhồi mà còn giúp xác định được nguyên nhân và mức độ nghiêm trọng của khuyết tật, từ đó giúp đưa ra các biện pháp xử lý phù hợp.

Điều này không chỉ cải thiện năng suất mà còn nâng cao chất lượng quả. Việc ổn định nền đất sau mố có chức năng riêng biệt là một vấn đề kỹ thuật quan trọng trong xây dựng, đặc biệt trong điều kiện địa chất phức tạp tại Việt Nam. Các giải pháp hiện nay tập trung vào việc sử dụng các phương pháp gia cố nền đất như cọc xi măng đất, cọc cát, hoặc các kỹ thuật xử lý nền móng khác nhằm đảm bảo độ ổn định và chịu tải của công trình. Đặc biệt, việc áp dụng công nghệ tiên tiến và vật liệu mới giúp nâng cao hiệu quả và giảm thiểu rủi ro trong quá trình thi công. Các nghiên cứu và thực tiễn cho thấy, việc kết hợp giữa kinh nghiệm truyền thống và công nghệ hiện đại là chìa khóa để giải quyết các thách thức về nền đất, đảm bảo an toàn và bền vững cho các công trình xây dựng trong tương lai.

Motif nghệ thuật trong tác phẩm của James Joyce và Franz Kafka thể hiện sự sâu sắc và đa dạng trong cách mà hai nhà văn này khám phá tâm lý con người và hiện thực xã hội. Joyce, với phong cách hiện đại, thường sử dụng các kỹ thuật như dòng ý thức và cấu trúc phi tuyến để thể hiện những suy nghĩ phức tạp của nhân vật, từ đó phản ánh sự hỗn loạn của cuộc sống đô thị. Ngược lại, Kafka lại nổi bật với những hình ảnh kỳ quái và tình huống phi lý, tạo nên cảm giác bất an và sự xa lạ trong thế giới mà nhân vật phải đối mặt. Cả hai tác giả đều khéo léo lồng ghép các motif như sự cô đơn, khát vọng tự do và sự tìm kiếm bản sắc, qua đó khắc họa những mâu thuẫn nội tâm và sự bế tắc của con người trong xã hội hiện đại. This paper investigates the generalization error behavior of generalized linear models (GLMs) when applied to high-dimensional data sets. Understanding the performance of GLMs in high dimensions is critical as these models are widely used in applications that involve large and complex data structures. Methods: We employ advanced statistical techniques to model the generalization error of GLMs, utilizing both theoretical analysis and empirical simulations. Our approach includes the derivation of asymptotic error bounds, taking into account the dimensionality of the data and the complexity of the model. We explore various parameter settings and sparsity conditions to evaluate the performance across different high-dimensional scenarios. Results: Our findings reveal that the generalization error of GLMs is significantly influenced by the ratio of dimensionality to sample size, as well as the sparsity level of the underlying data. Specifically, we identify critical thresholds where the generalization error transitions from manageable levels to more substantial increases. Comparisons with other commonly used models demonstrate the relative strengths and weaknesses of GLMs in handling high-dimensional data. Conclusion: The study provides new insights into the scalability and robustness of GLMs in high-dimensional contexts, contributing to more informed model selection and implementation in data-rich environments. The implications are particularly relevant for fields like bioinformatics, finance, and text processing, where GLMs are frequently employed. Our analysis highlights potential improvements in model formulation to enhance performance, paving the way for future research in high-dimensional statistics. Keywords: generalized linear models, high dimensionality, generalization error, statistical analysis, asymptotic bounds, sparsity, model performance.

Microwave imaging has emerged as a promising non-invasive technique for detecting brain anomalies, offering advantages such as portability and cost-effectiveness. However, traditional methods often struggle with reconstructing high-resolution images due to the complex nature of brain tissues and the ill-posed nature of the inverse problem. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging Graph Attention Networks (GATs) to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of microwave imaging for brain anomaly detection. The proposed method models the brain's electromagnetic properties as a graph, where nodes represent tissue regions and edges capture spatial relationships. By incorporating attention mechanisms, the GAT dynamically prioritizes relevant features, enabling robust feature extraction and improved image reconstruction. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms conventional methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency. The system achieves a 15% improvement in image resolution and a 20% reduction in processing time compared to state-of-the-art techniques. This research contributes a scalable and interpretable framework for microwave imaging, with potential applications in early diagnosis of brain disorders such as tumors and strokes. Key innovations include the integration of graph-based learning with attention mechanisms, offering a new direction for solving complex inverse problems in medical imaging. Keywords: Graph Attention Networks, Microwave Imaging, Brain Anomaly Detection, Inverse Problems, Non-Invasive Diagnostics.

This paper investigates the resilience of autonomous vehicle object category detection systems to universal adversarial perturbations. The objective is to analyze the vulnerability of these systems to subtle, yet malicious, input manipulations that can compromise their ability to accurately detect and classify objects. A deep learning-based approach is employed, utilizing a state-of-the-art object detection model and evaluating its performance under various universal adversarial perturbation attacks. The results show that even small perturbations can significantly degrade the detection accuracy, highlighting the need for robustness enhancements. Key findings indicate that the model's performance degrades by up to 30% under certain attack scenarios, emphasizing the importance of developing more resilient object detection systems. The research contributes to the understanding of adversarial vulnerabilities in autonomous vehicles and paves the way for the development of more secure and reliable object category detection systems, with potential applications in areas such as autonomous driving, robotics, and computer vision. Keywords: autonomous vehicles, object detection, universal adversarial perturbations, deep learning, robustness, computer vision, adversarial attacks.

Vừa qua, một công nghệ mới đã được áp dụng tại một nhà máy nhiệt điện, đó là việc sử dụng tro đá để thay thế cát trong quá trình xây dựng. Đây là một bước tiến quan trọng trong lĩnh vực xây dựng và công nghệ. Tro đá, còn được gọi là tro bay, là một loại vật liệu được tạo ra từ quá trình đốt cháy than đá. Nó có nhiều tính chất vật lý và cơ học tốt, bao gồm độ bền cao, độ giãn nở nhiệt thấp và khả năng chống chịu với các tác động bên ngoài. Khi sử dụng tro đá để thay thế cát trong xây dựng, các nhà thầu đã nhận thấy được nhiều lợi ích. Trước hết, tro đá có thể giúp giảm thiểu chi phí xây dựng do không cần sử dụng cát. Thứ hai, tro đá có thể giúp giảm thiểu tác động môi trường do không cần khai thác cát từ tự nhiên. Tuy nhiên, cũng cần lưu ý rằng việc sử dụng tro đá còn có một số hạn chế. Tuy nhiên, cũng cần phải xem xét kỹ lưỡng về các hạn chế và lợi ích của việc sử dụng tro đá.

Reward shaping is a critical technique in reinforcement learning (RL) to guide agents toward desired behaviors by incorporating additional rewards. However, existing methods often struggle with efficiently utilizing shaping rewards without compromising the original task objectives. This paper introduces a novel approach to reward shaping that dynamically learns to balance intrinsic and extrinsic rewards, enabling agents to better leverage shaping signals while preserving task performance. Our method employs a meta-learning framework to adaptively adjust the influence of shaping rewards based on the agent's learning progress and environmental context. Experiments conducted on benchmark RL environments demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves learning efficiency and final performance compared to traditional reward shaping techniques. The results highlight the method's ability to generalize across diverse tasks, offering a robust solution for complex RL scenarios. This work contributes to advancing reward shaping strategies, providing a scalable and adaptive framework for future RL applications. **Keywords**: reinforcement learning, reward shaping, meta-learning, adaptive learning, intrinsic rewards, extrinsic rewards.

Optical Braille Recognition (OBR) systems offer crucial accessibility for the visually impaired, yet challenges remain in accurately detecting and interpreting Braille dots from images. This paper introduces a novel OBR system leveraging the Circular Hough Transform (CHT) for robust dot detection. Our approach enhances traditional CHT by incorporating adaptive thresholding and spatial constraints to minimize false positives caused by noise and image artifacts. The system segments Braille cells, applies CHT to identify potential dot locations within each cell, and then validates these locations based on geometrical relationships inherent in Braille patterns. Experimental results, conducted on a diverse dataset of Braille images captured under varying lighting and quality conditions, demonstrate a significant improvement in dot detection accuracy compared to conventional methods. Specifically, our system achieves a recognition rate of 98.5%, a 10% increase over standard thresholding-based CHT implementations. The improved accuracy and robustness of this OBR system contribute to more reliable and accessible solutions for Braille users. Keywords: Optical Braille Recognition, Circular Hough Transform, Image Processing, Accessibility, Computer Vision.

Bin picking, a critical task in industrial automation, requires precise segmentation of workpieces to enable robotic systems to accurately identify and grasp objects. This paper addresses the challenge of deep workpiece region segmentation in cluttered and unstructured environments, where traditional methods often struggle with occlusion and varying object orientations. We propose a novel deep learning-based approach that leverages a multi-scale convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture enhanced with attention mechanisms to improve segmentation accuracy. The model is trained on a synthetic dataset generated using domain randomization techniques to ensure robustness across diverse real-world scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves a significant improvement in segmentation performance, with a mean Intersection-over-Union (IoU) score of 92.5%, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods by 8.2%. Furthermore, the proposed approach exhibits superior generalization capabilities when tested on unseen datasets with varying lighting conditions and object configurations. The findings highlight the potential of this method to enhance the efficiency and reliability of bin-picking systems in industrial applications, paving the way for more advanced automation solutions. **Keywords**: Bin picking, workpiece segmentation, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, attention mechanisms, industrial automation.

The objective of this research is to address the challenge of point cloud completion, a crucial task in 3D computer vision, which involves reconstructing missing parts of a point cloud to generate a complete 3D model. This paper introduces a novel Skip-attention Network with Hierarchical Folding (SHF-Net) designed to enhance the completion process of point clouds. The proposed SHF-Net leverages an innovative skip-attention mechanism that selectively attends to important features across varying scales, while the hierarchical folding approach incrementally reconstructs point clouds by utilizing intermediate deep representations. This combination aids in capturing both local and global structures, leading to more accurate and efficient reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate that SHF-Net outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency on benchmark datasets. The findings reveal significant improvements in system performance, particularly in dealing with dense and complex 3D structures. The novel architecture of SHF-Net not only advances theoretical understanding in 3D reconstruction but also offers potential applications in areas such as autonomous driving, augmented reality, and robotics, where quick and precise 3D environment mapping is essential. Key innovations include the integration of skip-attention and hierarchical processes to leverage symmetrical and contextual information, setting a new benchmark in the field of point cloud processing. Keywords: point cloud completion, 3D reconstruction, skip-attention, hierarchical folding, computer vision.

The classification of imbalanced datasets remains a significant challenge in machine learning, as traditional algorithms often exhibit bias toward the majority class, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper addresses this issue by proposing a novel approach using a Class Expert Generative Adversarial Network (CE-GAN) for effective imbalance data classification. The objective is to enhance the classification accuracy of minority classes by generating synthetic samples that better represent their distribution. The CE-GAN framework introduces a class-specific generator and discriminator architecture, enabling the model to focus on learning the unique characteristics of each class. The proposed method is evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets with varying degrees of class imbalance. Experimental results demonstrate that CE-GAN outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score, particularly for minority classes. Furthermore, the model exhibits robustness across different imbalance ratios, making it suitable for real-world applications such as fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and anomaly detection. The key contribution of this research lies in the integration of class-specific expertise within the GAN framework, offering a scalable and adaptable solution for imbalance data classification. This work advances the field of deep learning by providing a novel approach to address class imbalance, with potential implications for improving decision-making systems in diverse domains. **Keywords**: Imbalance data classification, Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), Deep learning, Class-specific learning, Synthetic data generation, Minority class enhancement.

High-dimensional data poses significant challenges for traditional machine learning model interpretability, limiting their adoption in critical applications where human understanding and transparency are vital. This paper introduces a novel framework for enhancing human-interpretable model explainability on high-dimensional datasets, such as those found in genomics, image analysis, and finance. The proposed approach combines dimensionality reduction techniques with feature attribution methods, enabling clear visualization and intuitive explanation of model behavior. Specifically, we integrate principal component analysis (PCA) and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) with model-agnostic explainers, including SHAP and LIME, to identify and present the most influential features driving model predictions. Extensive experiments conducted on publicly available benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method improves explanatory clarity without compromising predictive performance. Comparative analyses reveal substantial gains in human interpretability, as measured by empirical user studies and quantitative interpretability metrics, over conventional black-box models. The framework supports interactive visual tools, allowing users to explore, validate, and trust model outputs. Our results highlight the importance of fostering transparency for high-stakes decision-making and provide a scalable pathway for interpretable machine learning on complex, high-dimensional data. Key contributions include the integration of multi-modal dimensionality reduction, robust feature attribution, and end-user focused visualization. Keywords: model interpretability, explainable AI, high-dimensional data, dimensionality reduction, SHAP, LIME, visualization, transparency, machine learning.

Cây hành hướng (Allium fistulosum L.) là một loại thực vật quan trọng trong ẩm thực và y học. Tuy nhiên, việc sử dụng các loại phân bón có thể ảnh hưởng đến năng suất và phẩm chất của cây này. Trong nghiên cứu này, tác giả đã đánh giá ảnh hưởng của KCl (kali clorua) đến năng suất và phẩm chất của cây hành hướng. Kết quả cho thấy rằng việc sử dụng KCl đã tăng năng suất và phẩm chất của cây hành hướng. Cụ thể, cây trồng được KCl có chiều cao và trọng lượng cao hơn so với cây trồng không được KCl. Đồng thời, phẩm chất của cây hành hướng cũng được cải thiện, với tỷ lệ đường và chất xơ cao hơn. Tác giả cũng đã đánh giá ảnh hưởng của KCl đến các chỉ số sinh học của cây hành hướng, bao gồm tỷ lệ nước, tỷ lệ chất khô và tỷ lệ chất béo. Kết quả cho thấy rằng việc sử dụng KCl đã tăng tỷ lệ nước và giảm tỷ lệ chất khô và chất béo của cây hành hướng. Tổng kết, nghiên cứu này cho thấy rằng việc sử dụng KCl có thể cải thiện năng suất và phẩm chất của cây hành hướng. Tuy nhiên, cần phải thực hiện thêm nghiên cứu để đánh giá ảnh hưởng của KCl đến cây hành hướng trong điều kiện thực tế.

Bài viết tập trung vào việc xây dựng các dự án học tập nhằm phát triển năng lực viết văn thuyết minh cho sinh viên sư phạm ngữ văn. Nghiên cứu nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc trang bị cho sinh viên sư phạm khả năng viết thuyết minh hiệu quả, đáp ứng yêu cầu đổi mới của chương trình giáo dục phổ thông. Các dự án học tập được thiết kế theo hướng tích hợp kiến thức, kỹ năng và thái độ, tạo cơ hội cho sinh viên vận dụng lý thuyết vào thực tiễn. Đồng thời, nghiên cứu cũng đề xuất các tiêu chí đánh giá cụ thể, giúp sinh viên tự đánh giá và điều chỉnh quá trình học tập. Kết quả cho thấy việc áp dụng các dự án học tập đã giúp sinh viên sư phạm nâng cao đáng kể năng lực viết văn thuyết minh, đồng thời phát triển các kỹ năng mềm cần thiết cho nghề nghiệp trong tương lai.

Ứng dụng giải pháp thông gió thu hồi năng lượng (ERV) đang trở thành một trong những công nghệ hàng đầu trong việc nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng năng lượng. Công nghệ này cho phép thu hồi và tái sử dụng năng lượng đã bị lãng phí trong quá trình thông gió, giúp giảm thiểu sự tiêu thụ năng lượng mới và giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực đến môi trường. Với hệ thống ERV, không khí nóng và ẩm được thu hồi từ các phòng và tái sử dụng để làm mát và cung cấp không khí trong lành cho các khu vực khác trong tòa nhà. Điều này không chỉ giúp giảm thiểu sự tiêu thụ năng lượng mới mà còn giúp giảm thiểu lượng khí thải carbon và các chất gây ô nhiễm khác. Ứng dụng giải pháp thông gió thu hồi năng lượng (ERV) đang được áp dụng rộng rãi trong các tòa nhà thương mại, dân cư và công nghiệp, giúp giảm thiểu chi phí năng lượng và tăng cường hiệu suất sử dụng năng lượng.

Quảng Bình, vùng đất nổi tiếng với cảnh quan thiên nhiên hùng vĩ và di sản văn hóa phong phú, đang hướng đến phát triển loại hình du lịch văn hóa tâm linh. Với hệ thống đền chùa, di tích lịch sử và lễ hội truyền thống đa dạng, Quảng Bình có tiềm năng lớn để thu hút du khách tìm hiểu và trải nghiệm văn hóa tâm linh. Tuy nhiên, để khai thác hiệu quả, cần có những giải pháp đồng bộ như nâng cơ sở hạ tầng, đào tạo nguồn nhân lực chất lượng, và quảng bá hình ảnh du lịch một cách chuyên nghiệp. Việc kết hợp giữa bảo tồn giá trị văn hóa và phát triển kinh tế sẽ giúp Quảng Bình trở thành điểm đến hấp dẫn, góp phần thúc đẩy du lịch địa phương phát triển bền vững.

Dynamic textures—temporal sequences exhibiting consistent visual patterns, such as flowing water, smoke, or waving grass—present unique challenges for computer vision and graphics, especially in synthesizability assessment. This paper investigates the problem of automatically learning the synthesizability of dynamic texture samples, aiming to predict how well novel dynamic texture samples can be synthesized by computational models. We propose a learning-based approach that leverages deep neural networks to extract multi-scale spatio-temporal features from video sequences and build a regression model that estimates the synthesizability score for each sample. The method is trained and evaluated on a curated dataset of dynamic textures, annotated with ground-truth synthesizability ratings from human assessments. Experiments show that our approach outperforms existing hand-crafted and traditional feature-based methods, achieving higher correlation with human perception and improved generalization to unseen textures. The results provide deeper insights into the intrinsic properties that determine dynamic texture synthesizability and facilitate the automatic selection or filtering of suitable texture samples for synthesis tasks in computer graphics, animation, and vision-based simulation. Our findings advance the understanding of dynamic texture modeling and open new possibilities for intelligent content creation. Keywords: dynamic texture, synthesizability, deep learning, spatio-temporal features, video analysis, texture synthesis.

Rubella là bệnh truyền nhiễm qua đường hô hấp do virus rubella gây ra. Mặc dù phần lớn bệnh ở mức độ nhẹ nhưng khi phụ nữ mang thai mắc bệnh có thể gây ra những dị tật bẩm sinh nghiêm trọng đối với thai nhi, do đó việc sàng lọc, chẩn đoán phát hiện nhiễm virus rubella sớm là rất cần thiết. Với mục tiêu đó, các tác giả đã nghiên cứu phát triển khay thử chẩn đoán nhanh kháng nguyên virus rubella. Khay thử được phát triển dựa trên kỹ thuật sắc ký miễn dịch sử dụng hạt nano vàng. Nghiên cứu này nhằm xác định một số đặc tính của khay thử, bao gồm ngưỡng phát hiện, phản ứng chéo với một số tác nhân gây bệnh, độ lặp lại, độ nhạy và đặc hiệu. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy, khay thử có khả năng phát hiện được mẫu có chứa 105 PFU virus rubella; không có phản ứng chéo với các mẫu chứa các tác nhân gây bệnh như: Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, Candida albicans, virus sởi, virus cúm, Adenovirus, độ lặp lại của khay thử đạt 100% đối với mẫu âm tính và dương tính. Độ nhạy và độ đặc hiệu của khay thử đạt 98 và 99% tương ứng.

Giám sát sự thay đổi không gian xanh đô thị là một nhiệm vụ quan trọng trong bối cảnh phát triển bền vững và bảo vệ môi trường. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc sử dụng dữ liệu từ vệ tinh Sentinel-2 MSI để theo dõi và phân tích sự biến động của không gian xanh tại tỉnh Thái Nguyên. Qua việc thu thập và xử lý dữ liệu đa thời gian, nghiên cứu đã chỉ ra những thay đổi đáng kể trong diện tích và chất lượng không gian xanh, từ đó đánh giá tác động của các hoạt động đô thị hóa và biến đổi khí hậu. Kết quả cho thấy sự cần thiết phải có các biện pháp quản lý hiệu quả nhằm bảo tồn và phát triển không gian xanh, góp phần nâng cao chất lượng cuộc sống cho cư dân đô thị. Việc áp dụng công nghệ vệ tinh trong giám sát môi trường không chỉ mang lại thông tin chính xác mà còn hỗ trợ các quyết định quy hoạch đô thị bền vững hơn.
Ngoài ra, quản trị viên hệ thống có thể tùy chỉnh cấu hình cho hệ thống như cập nhật sản phẩm, phân quyền hoặc quản lý người dùng.
