Bệnh nhân lao ruột có kèm theo lao phổi chiếm 68,18%. Đối với tổn thương tại thành ruột, vị trí thường gặp nhất là vùng hồi manh tràng 90,91%, kiểu hình tổn thương đa dạng bao gồm tạo khối u lao (33/44 trường hợp) và không tạo khối (44/44 trường hợp). U lao thường ngấm thuốc tương phản đồng nhất, thâm nhiễm mỡ xung quanh. Ngược lại, thành ruột có tổn thương nhiều đoạn theo kiểu bước nhảy, độ dài tổn thương khu trú (< 5cm) chiếm đa số, độ dày mức độ trung bình chiếm 68,92%. Đối với tổn thương ngoài thành ruột. This paper introduces a novel hierarchical approach to robust representation learning, designed to improve model performance in the presence of noisy or corrupted data. Our method constructs representations by iteratively aggregating features across multiple levels of abstraction, enhancing resilience to adversarial attacks and data perturbations. We employ a multi-stage training procedure that explicitly encourages consistency between representations at different levels of the hierarchy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art representation learning techniques in terms of robustness and generalization ability. Specifically, we observe improved accuracy under various attack scenarios and reduced sensitivity to data noise. The proposed framework offers a promising direction for developing more reliable and secure machine learning systems. Keywords: representation learning, robustness, hierarchical models, adversarial attacks, data corruption.

Neural net classifiers trained on data with annotated class labels can also capture apparent visual similarity among categories without being directed to do so. We study whether this observation can be extended beyond the conventional domain of supervised learning: Can we learn a good feature representation that captures apparent similarity among instances, instead of classes, by merely asking the feature to be discriminative of individual instances? We formulate this intuition as a non-parametric classification problem at the instance-level, and use noise-contrastive estimation to tackle the computational challenges imposed by the large number of instance classes. Our experimental results demonstrate that, under unsupervised learning settings, our method surpasses the state-of-the-art on ImageNet classification by a large margin. Our method is also remarkable for consistently improving test performance with more training data and better network architectures. By fine-tuning the learned feature, we further obtain competitive results for semi-supervised learning and object detection tasks. Our non-parametric model is highly compact: With 128 features per image, our method requires only 600MB storage for a million images, enabling fast nearest neighbour retrieval at the run time.

Nghiên cứu đề xuất quy trình dự toán chi phí ứng dụng BIM tại Việt Nam nhằm mục tiêu tối ưu hóa quy trình xây dựng và nâng cao hiệu quả kinh tế. Bằng cách áp dụng công nghệ mô hình thông tin xây dựng (BIM), nghiên cứu chỉ ra rằng việc dự toán chi phí có thể được thực hiện một cách chính xác và nhanh chóng hơn, từ đó giảm thiểu rủi ro và sai sót trong quá trình thi công. Quy trình này bao gồm các bước cụ thể như thu thập dữ liệu, phân tích chi phí, lập kế hoạch và kiểm soát ngân sách. Ngoài ra, nghiên cứu cũng nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc đào tạo nhân lực và phát triển hạ tầng công nghệ thông tin để hỗ trợ việc triển khai BIM hiệu quả. We propose a general variational framework of fair clustering, which integrates an original Kullback-Leibler (KL) fairness term with a large class of clustering objectives, including prototype or graph based. Fundamentally different from the existing combinatorial and spectral solutions, our variational multi-term approach enables to control the trade-off levels between the fairness and clustering objectives. We derive a general tight upper bound based on a concave-convex decomposition of our fairness term, its Lipschitz-gradient property and the Pinsker's inequality. Our tight upper bound can be jointly optimized with various clustering objectives, while yielding a scalable solution, with convergence guarantee. Interestingly, at each iteration, it performs an independent update for each assignment variable. Therefore, it can be easily distributed for large-scale datasets. This scalability is important as it enables to explore different trade-off levels between the fairness and clustering objectives. Unlike spectral relaxation, our formulation does not require computing its eigenvalue decomposition. We report comprehensive evaluations and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods over various fair-clustering benchmarks, which show that our variational formulation can yield highly competitive solutions in terms of fairness and clustering objectives.

This work addresses the problem of optimizing communications between server and clients in federated learning (FL). Current sampling approaches in FL are either biased, or non optimal in terms of server-clients communications and training stability. To overcome this issue, we introduce for clients selection. We prove that clustered sampling leads to better clients representatitivity and to reduced variance of the clients stochastic aggregation weights in FL. Compatibly with our theory, we provide two different clustering approaches enabling clients aggregation based on 1) sample size, and 2) models similarity. Through a series of experiments in non-iid and unbalanced scenarios, we demonstrate that model aggregation through clustered sampling consistently leads to better training convergence and variability when compared to standard sampling approaches. Our approach does not require any additional operation on the clients side, and can be seamlessly integrated in standard FL implementations. Finally, clustered sampling is compatible with existing methods and technologies for privacy enhancement, and for communication reduction through model compression.

This paper explores the concept of texture transfer for single image super-resolution, a technique that leverages the power of texture information to enhance image resolution. The objective is to investigate the effectiveness of this approach in improving the quality of low-resolution images. Our method utilizes a novel texture transfer algorithm that combines the benefits of deep learning-based super-resolution models with traditional texture synthesis techniques. The results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art super-resolution methods, particularly in scenarios where texture information is rich and diverse. Key findings include significant improvements in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) metrics. The implications of this research are substantial, as it demonstrates the potential for texture transfer to become a crucial component in single image super-resolution pipelines, enabling applications such as image and video enhancement, surveillance, and medical imaging. Our contributions highlight the importance of texture information in image super-resolution and pave the way for future research in this area, with relevant keywords including single image super-resolution, texture transfer, deep learning, and image enhancement.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurate facial expression recognition, a critical component in human-computer interaction, by enhancing the performance of Vision Transformers. Traditional facial expression recognition systems often struggle with capturing subtle nuances in expressions due to inadequate feature extraction. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel integration of Squeeze and Excitation (SE) networks within the Vision Transformer framework to improve attention to significant features and enhance expression classification. Our approach employs SE modules to adaptively recalibrate feature responses, thus refining the attention mechanism inherent in transformers and yielding more relevant facial feature representations. Results/Findings: The proposed model demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional convolutional neural networks and standard Vision Transformer models on multiple benchmark datasets. Through extensive experiments, we show that incorporating SE modules significantly increases accuracy in recognizing a diverse set of facial expressions. Our method achieves a notable improvement in precision and recall metrics, evidencing its robustness and efficacy in complex, real-world scenarios. Conclusion/Implications: By enhancing the Vision Transformer with Squeeze and Excitation blocks, we establish a new benchmark for facial expression recognition systems, offering a scalable and adaptable solution that can be potentially applied to other domains requiring nuanced image classification. This research contributes to the development of more responsive and intuitive AI systems for improved human-computer interaction, with implications for a wide range of applications from virtual reality to emotional analytics. Keywords: Vision Transformer, Facial Expression Recognition, Squeeze and Excitation, Attention Mechanism, Human-Computer Interaction, Image Classification.

This paper introduces a novel approach for 3D reconstruction using Deep Implicit Moving Least-Squares (DIMLS) functions, addressing the challenges of accurately representing complex geometries and surfaces from sparse or noisy point cloud data. The proposed method combines the strengths of implicit surface modeling and deep learning to enhance reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. By leveraging a neural network to learn the Moving Least-Squares (MLS) function, the approach adaptively captures local geometric details while maintaining global smoothness. The framework is trained on diverse datasets to ensure robustness across various shapes and topologies. Experimental results demonstrate that DIMLS outperforms traditional MLS-based methods and state-of-the-art deep learning techniques in terms of reconstruction accuracy, particularly in handling sharp features and irregular surfaces. Additionally, the method exhibits superior scalability and generalization capabilities, making it suitable for real-world applications such as medical imaging, robotics, and computer-aided design. This work contributes a significant advancement in 3D reconstruction by integrating implicit surface modeling with deep learning, offering a versatile and efficient solution for high-fidelity geometric representation. **Keywords**: 3D reconstruction, implicit surfaces, Moving Least-Squares, deep learning, point cloud processing, geometric modeling.

This paper introduces a novel MATLAB toolbox designed for efficient and comprehensive feature importance ranking in data analysis and machine learning. The objective is to provide researchers and practitioners with a unified platform to assess the relevance of individual features in predictive modeling. The toolbox incorporates a diverse set of established feature importance algorithms, including permutation importance, model-based methods relying on linear models and tree ensembles, and information theory-based approaches. It offers a standardized interface for applying these techniques, facilitating comparative analysis across different methods on the same dataset. Results demonstrate the toolbox's utility in identifying key predictors across various synthetic and real-world datasets. The toolbox's modular architecture allows for easy extension with new feature importance metrics. Early classification of time series (EC-TS) aims to predict the class label of a time series instance as early and accurately as possible. This review paper surveys the existing approaches to EC-TS and their diverse applications. We categorize EC-TS methods based on their underlying techniques, including distance-based, feature-based, and model-based approaches, with a focus on recent advances utilizing deep learning. Furthermore, we examine various application domains where EC-TS has proven valuable, such as healthcare monitoring, financial forecasting, and anomaly detection in industrial processes. The review provides a comparative analysis of different EC-TS algorithms in terms of accuracy, earliness, and computational efficiency. This paper highlights the challenges and opportunities in the field, emphasizing the need for robust and interpretable EC-TS methods suitable for real-world applications with streaming data. Keywords: Time series classification, early classification, review, machine learning, streaming data, predictive monitoring.

Bồ công anh Việt Nam (Lactuca indica L.) là một loại dược liệu được dùng trong y học cổ truyền để trị mụn nhọt và một số bệnh viêm da. Nghiên cứu này sử dụng mô hình ức chế sản sinh nitric oxide (NO) trong tế bào RAW264.7 và thử nghiệm trung hoà 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) để sàng lọc hoạt tính kháng viêm và chống ôxy hoá in vitro của các cao phân đoạn từ cây L. indica. Qua đó, xác định được cao cloroform ức chế sản sinh NO mạnh nhất và cao ethyl acetat trung hoà DPPH tốt nhất. Từ cao cloroform và ethyl acetat phân lập được 6 hợp chất: acid pentadecanoic (1), lupeol (2), vanillin (3), 5-hydroxy-3ʹ,4ʹ,7- trimethoxyflavone (4), luteolin-7-O-β-D-glucoside (5), acacetin-7-O-β-D-rutinoside (6). (5) là chất duy nhất đồng thời có hoạt tính ức chế sản sinh NO (IC50=13,86±1,10 µM) và có khả năng bắt gốc DPPH (IC50=26,93±0,10 µM). Nghiên cứu này gợi ý rằng các phân đoạn cloroform, ethyl acetat và chất (5) đều có hiệu quả kháng viêm liên quan đến sản xuất quá mức NO trong tế bào, bên cạnh đó, chất (5) và phân đoạn ethyl acetat cũng có tác dụng chống ôxy hoá mạnh.

Bayesian Reinforcement Learning (BRL) offers a principled approach to exploration-exploitation in reinforcement learning by explicitly modeling uncertainty. However, BRL often suffers from scalability issues, particularly in continuous state spaces. This paper introduces Cover Tree Bayesian Reinforcement Learning (CTBRL), a novel algorithm that leverages cover trees to efficiently approximate the Bayesian posterior and accelerate planning. CTBRL uses a cover tree to partition the state space, enabling efficient computation of the posterior distribution over value functions. We demonstrate that CTBRL significantly reduces the computational complexity associated with traditional BRL methods. Experimental results on benchmark continuous control tasks show that CTBRL achieves comparable or superior performance to existing BRL algorithms with significantly reduced computational cost. Specifically, CTBRL demonstrates faster learning rates and improved sample efficiency. These results highlight the potential of cover trees for scaling BRL to more complex, high-dimensional environments. Keywords: Bayesian Reinforcement Learning, Cover Trees, Reinforcement Learning, Exploration-Exploitation, Continuous Control.

This paper presents Morph, a flexible acceleration framework designed to enhance the efficiency of three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D CNN)-based video understanding. The increasing complexity and computational demands of 3D CNNs, widely used for tasks such as action recognition and video classification, have become a critical challenge, especially for real-time and resource-constrained deployment. Morph addresses this challenge by introducing a reconfigurable architecture that can dynamically adapt to diverse 3D CNN models and varying workloads without sacrificing accuracy. The proposed framework integrates scalable dataflow optimizations and adaptive memory management strategies to maximize throughput and energy efficiency. Experimental evaluations on popular video understanding benchmarks demonstrate that Morph achieves up to 2.7× improvement in processing speed and up to 45% reduction in energy consumption, compared to conventional fixed-function accelerators. Moreover, Morph provides seamless support for a range of 3D CNN architectures, enabling broader applicability in both cloud-based and edge computing environments. The results highlight Morph’s potential to accelerate next-generation video analytics and intelligent surveillance systems while maintaining model flexibility and application versatility. Keywords: 3D CNN, video understanding, hardware acceleration, reconfigurable architecture, energy efficiency, real-time processing.

Autonomous driving systems rely heavily on LiDAR sensors for accurate 3D environmental perception. However, the limited range of conventional LiDARs, particularly in adverse weather conditions, poses a significant challenge. This paper introduces LEAD (LiDAR Extender for Autonomous Driving), a novel method to enhance the effective range of LiDAR systems by fusing LiDAR data with high-resolution radar data using a deep learning framework. LEAD employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn a mapping from radar point clouds to pseudo-LiDAR point clouds, effectively extending the LiDAR’s perception range. The network is trained on a large-scale, synchronized LiDAR-radar dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that LEAD significantly improves the detection range and density of point clouds, especially at longer distances and in inclement weather, outperforming existing LiDAR-radar fusion techniques by up to 20% in object detection accuracy at 150 meters. This extended perception range enhances the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems. Keywords: Autonomous Driving, LiDAR, Radar, Sensor Fusion, Deep Learning, Object Detection.

This paper introduces NukeBERT, a novel pre-trained language model tailored for the low-resource nuclear domain. Addressing the challenges of limited labeled data and domain-specific vocabulary, NukeBERT is pre-trained on a comprehensive corpus of nuclear-related texts, including technical reports, research publications, and regulatory documents. We adapt the BERT architecture and employ a masked language modeling objective to learn contextualized representations of nuclear terminology. Experimental results demonstrate that NukeBERT significantly outperforms general-purpose language models and existing domain-specific models on various nuclear-related tasks, including text classification, named entity recognition, and question answering. The findings highlight the effectiveness of targeted pre-training for improving performance in specialized domains with scarce resources. NukeBERT offers a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the nuclear field, enabling more accurate and efficient natural language processing applications. Keywords: Nuclear Energy, Language Model, BERT, Pre-training, Low-Resource, Natural Language Processing.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning and planning in complex action spaces, where the dimensionality and intricacy of potential actions hinder efficient exploration and optimization. We propose a hierarchical reinforcement learning approach that combines action space abstraction with model-based planning. Specifically, we introduce a novel method for automatically learning a lower-dimensional, abstract action space from high-dimensional raw actions using a variational autoencoder conditioned on state information. This learned action space enables more efficient exploration and planning. We then integrate this abstract action space with a learned dynamics model to perform model-based planning, allowing the agent to reason about long-term consequences of its actions. Experimental results across a range of challenging continuous control tasks demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing model-free and model-based reinforcement learning algorithms, particularly in environments with sparse rewards and high-dimensional action spaces. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of learned action space abstraction and model-based planning, resulting in improved sample efficiency and performance. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Action Space Abstraction, Model-Based Planning, Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning, Continuous Control.

Rare classes Mixing . Large domain gaps, or significant discrepancies in datadistributions, are a typical cause of UDA difficulties and result in false pseudo labels. One of the problems is a target domain bias toward initially transferableclasses that are easy to combine, which results in some classes never being pre-dicted. To solve the problem, DACS add new data through cross-domain mix ing, and because the labels for these new images partially come from the source domain, they won’t be for conflated all of the images. Additionally, the pixels that have ground-truth labels (source-domain labels) and those that have pseudo-labels(target-domain labels) may now be neighbors in an image, making the implicit dis tinction of domains unlikely. However, while recent mixing techniques assist thenetwork in more successfully bridging the domain gap and resolving the class con flation issue, it is hard to prevent network bias toward common classes. I proposed two novel mixing strategies that focus on solving the conflation problem. The core idea is to frequently paste uncommon classes from source images to target images.

Accurately predicting potential crowd flow is critical for urban planning, traffic management, and public safety. However, traditional forecasting models often struggle to capture the complex dependencies between various influencing factors, such as spatial-temporal dynamics, environmental conditions, and human mobility patterns. In this work, we propose a novel heterogeneous relational modeling framework that integrates multiple modes of data to enhance crowd flow prediction. Our approach constructs a multi-modal graph representation that encodes diverse relationships, including spatial proximity, temporal correlations, and external contextual influences. We employ a graph neural network (GNN) with attention mechanisms to adaptively learn the importance of different relations, allowing the model to capture both local and global dependencies. Additionally, we introduce a dynamic feature fusion strategy to integrate heterogeneous information, improving the model’s adaptability to varying urban conditions. Extensive experiments on real-world crowd mobility datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in both short-term and long-term prediction tasks. The results highlight the effectiveness of incorporating heterogeneous relations for more accurate and robust crowd flow forecasting. Keywords: Crowd Flow Prediction, Heterogeneous Graphs, Multi-Modal Learning, Spatial-Temporal Modeling, Graph Neural Networks, Urban Computing.

This paper introduces Graph Convolutional Memory (GCM), a novel framework designed to enhance the performance of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) by leveraging structured memory representations. Traditional DRL approaches often struggle with scalability and generalization in complex environments due to their reliance on unstructured memory mechanisms. To address this, we propose GCM, which integrates graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to model relationships and dependencies within the memory structure, enabling more efficient information propagation and decision-making. Our approach is evaluated on a suite of benchmark tasks, including high-dimensional control and multi-agent environments. Experimental results demonstrate that GCM significantly outperforms existing memory-augmented DRL methods in terms of learning efficiency, stability, and adaptability to dynamic scenarios. The key innovation lies in the ability of GCM to capture and utilize relational information, which is critical for solving tasks requiring long-term dependencies and complex interactions. This work contributes to advancing DRL by providing a scalable and interpretable memory framework, with potential applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and multi-agent coordination. **Keywords**: Graph Convolutional Networks, Deep Reinforcement Learning, Memory Augmentation, Multi-Agent Systems, Scalable Learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of scene searching by developing a method that abstracts individual objects within a scene to improve search efficiency and accuracy. The aim is to enhance the ability to search through complex environments by focusing on abstract representations rather than detailed specifics of each object. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel scene abstraction algorithm that utilizes a combination of computer vision techniques and semantic segmentation to represent objects within a scene at a higher abstraction level. The approach involves creating a hierarchical abstraction model that categorizes and represents objects based on shared attributes, reducing the complexity of scene interpretation. Results/Findings: Our method was tested on a variety of scene datasets and demonstrated significant improvements in search performance. The abstraction model enabled faster processing times and increased search accuracy when compared to traditional object-specific search methodologies. Quantitative results show that our approach reduces computational overhead by up to 30%, while maintaining or improving the precision-recall metrics for scene retrieval tasks. Conclusion/Implications: The research presents an effective strategy for enhancing scene searching by abstracting object details, which has broad implications for applications in autonomous systems, digital content management, and augmented reality environments. This abstraction-based approach provides a scalable solution to the growing complexity of scene analysis in both real-time and large-scale image databases. Future work could explore further refinements in abstraction techniques and their integration into advanced AI-driven systems. Keywords: scene abstraction, semantic segmentation, computer vision, search efficiency, hierarchical model, object representation.

Despite achieving strong performance in semi-supervised node classification task, graph neural networks (GNNs) are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, similar to other deep learning models. Existing researches focus on developing either robust GNN models or attack detection methods against adversarial attacks on graphs. However, little research attention is paid to the potential and practice of immunization to adversarial attacks on graphs. In this paper, we propose and formulate the graph adversarial immunization problem, i.e., vaccinating an affordable fraction of node pairs, connected or unconnected, to improve the certifiable robustness of graph against any admissible adversarial attack. We further propose an effective algorithm, called AdvImmune, which optimizes with meta-gradient in a discrete way to circumvent the computationally expensive combinatorial optimization when solving the adversarial immunization problem. Experiments are conducted on two citation networks and one social network. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed AdvImmune method remarkably improves the ratio of robust nodes by 12%, 42%, 65%, with an affordable immune budget of only 5% edges.

This paper presents a novel approach to reinforcement learning by introducing Deep Ordinal Reinforcement Learning (DORL), which leverages ordinal information to improve learning efficiency and policy performance. Traditional reinforcement learning methods typically operate under the assumption of real-valued rewards and treat outcomes as scalar feedback. In contrast, our approach models the reward signals and value functions as ordinal variables, capturing the inherent ranking or preference among outcomes without requiring precise numerical values. We propose a deep neural network architecture specifically designed to process ordinal data and integrate it within both value-based and policy-based reinforcement learning frameworks. Experimental evaluations on standard benchmark environments, including Atari and OpenAI Gym tasks, demonstrate that DORL outperforms conventional reinforcement learning algorithms in terms of sample efficiency, robustness to noisy or imprecise reward signals, and overall policy quality. The results highlight that leveraging ordinal information can lead to more stable learning dynamics and improved generalization across tasks. This research opens new directions for robust decision-making in domains where rewards are naturally ordinal or where obtaining accurate scalar rewards is challenging. Keywords: deep reinforcement learning, ordinal data, value function, sample efficiency, policy optimization, ordinal rewards.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, with applications ranging from medical imaging to autonomous driving. Despite significant advancements, achieving robust and accurate segmentation across diverse datasets remains a challenge due to variations in image characteristics, such as lighting, texture, and object scales. This paper explores and exploits diversity in image datasets to enhance segmentation performance. We propose a novel framework that leverages multi-scale feature extraction and adaptive learning mechanisms to handle diverse image conditions effectively. Our approach integrates a hybrid architecture combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models, enabling the capture of both local and global contextual information. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, achieving higher accuracy and robustness across diverse scenarios. Key contributions include a dynamic diversity-aware training strategy and a lightweight post-processing module that refines segmentation boundaries. The proposed framework not only improves segmentation performance but also offers insights into the role of diversity in enhancing model generalization. This work has significant implications for real-world applications where image variability is a critical factor, paving the way for more adaptable and reliable segmentation systems. **Keywords**: Image segmentation, diversity-aware learning, multi-scale feature extraction, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), transformer models, adaptive learning.

This paper proposes a novel approach to geodesic regression, termed Fast Predictive Simple Geodesic Regression (FPSGR), which aims to efficiently predict regression outcomes on Riemannian manifolds. The objective is to address the limitations of existing geodesic regression methods, which often suffer from high computational complexity and poor scalability. Our approach leverages a simple yet effective framework that combines the strengths of geodesic interpolation and predictive modeling. The FPSGR method utilizes a fast and robust algorithm to estimate the geodesic regression model, enabling accurate predictions on complex manifold-valued data. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of FPSGR over state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant improvements in computational efficiency and predictive accuracy. The proposed approach has important implications for various applications, including shape analysis, medical imaging, and computer vision. Key contributions of this work include the development of a fast and scalable geodesic regression framework, the introduction of a novel predictive modeling approach, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in real-world scenarios. Relevant keywords: geodesic regression, Riemannian manifolds, predictive modeling, computational efficiency, shape analysis.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurate causal discovery in complex systems by introducing a novel framework for collaborative causal discovery utilizing atomic interventions. The main objective is to enhance the precision and efficiency of causal structure identification by leveraging the cooperation of multiple agents, each capable of performing targeted, atomic interventions on specific variables within a system. Our proposed approach integrates distributed decision-making algorithms with a mechanism for coordinating interventions, ensuring that redundant or conflicting actions are minimized. Through extensive simulations and evaluations on both synthetic and real-world datasets, we demonstrate significant improvements in causal graph recovery accuracy, reduced intervention costs, and faster convergence compared to conventional single-agent and observational-only methods. The findings reveal that collaborative strategies accelerate the discovery process and enable scalable application to high-dimensional data. This research contributes a robust methodological framework for collaborative causal inference and opens new avenues for real-time experimentation in distributed scientific, industrial, and AI-driven environments. Key keywords: causal discovery, atomic interventions, collaborative learning, causal inference, multi-agent systems, active learning.

The study introduces Het-node2vec, aiming to address the challenge of embedding heterogeneous multigraphs by enabling effective and accurate representation of such complex structures. This research seeks to enhance node embeddings, which are critical for tasks like link prediction, node classification, and clustering in heterogeneous networks. Methods: We present a novel algorithm, Het-node2vec, which utilizes second-order random walk sampling specifically tailored for heterogeneous multigraphs. Our approach extends the traditional node2vec algorithm by incorporating a flexible biased sampling strategy that considers both node type and edge multiplicity, allowing for a more nuanced exploration of graph homogeneity and heterogeneity. This technique captures intricate relational patterns while preserving essential graph properties. Results: The Het-node2vec algorithm demonstrated superior performance in multiple benchmark datasets comprising heterogeneous multigraph structures. Empirical evaluations revealed that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art graph embedding models in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Notably, Het-node2vec achieved improvements in node classification and link prediction tasks, with gains in embedding quality particularly evident in networks with diverse node and edge types. Conclusion: Het-node2vec provides a significant contribution to the field of network embedding by offering a versatile and powerful tool for modeling heterogeneous multigraphs. The approach not only bridges a critical gap in current graph embedding techniques but also lays a foundation for future applications in complex data environments, such as social networks, biological networks, and knowledge graphs. This work opens avenues for further exploration into adaptive random walk strategies and their potential in enhancing graph representation learning. Key Keywords: Het-node2vec, heterogeneous multigraphs, graph embedding, random walk, node classification, link prediction.

Summary: The Central coastal sandy area has a great potential in terms of area that can be used for agricultural, aquacultural production as well as some other economic sectors. However, due to the many disadvantages of the natural features, the exploitation and use of sandy soil areas is still limited, of which meteorological drought is one of the important factors that make coastal areas difficult in the storage and creation of water resources to serve people and agricultural production. The characteristic of meteorological drought in this area is not due to low rainfall, but mainly due to large evaporation, along with the soil characteristics of sand y soils that are difficult to retain water. This study focuses on using the ratio coefficience between evaporation and rain, to assess the degree of meteorological drought of coastal sandy soils. The series of rain and evaporation monitoring data from 1977 at 19 meteorological stations along the central coastal area were used to analyse, showing many years when there was a big difference between evaporation and rain in the dry season, especially in 1977, 1988, 2005, 2014 ... The period of high drought usual ly occurs from April to July in the north and from February to June in the south of the Central coastal areas. Especially in the southern region from Phu Yen to Binh Thuan, the probability of a degree of "very dry" in the period from February to May exceed s 70% of the analysed years. The GIS tools are also used to develop the water balance index map, which serves as a basis for determining the rate of area under different degrees of drought, confirming that most localities have more than 50% of the area to be determained above light drought levels. Keywords: Drought, Water Balance Index; Central Coastal Sandy area.

This paper introduces TDGIA, a novel framework designed to launch effective injection attacks on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The objective is to investigate the vulnerability of GNNs to targeted attacks, which can compromise their performance and reliability. Our approach leverages a combination of graph structure analysis and node injection strategies to craft malicious nodes that can mislead GNNs. We employ a reinforcement learning-based method to optimize the injection process, maximizing the attack's success rate while minimizing the number of injected nodes. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of TDGIA, outperforming existing attack methods in terms of attack success rate and node injection efficiency. Our findings highlight the potential risks associated with GNNs and the importance of developing robust defense mechanisms. The contributions of this research include a new perspective on GNN vulnerability assessment and a practical framework for evaluating the security of GNN-based systems, with implications for applications in social network analysis, recommendation systems, and graph-based AI models. Key keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Injection Attacks, Reinforcement Learning, Node Injection, GNN Security.

This paper proposes a novel approach to event prediction by introducing scalable joint models that incorporate uncertainty awareness. The primary objective is to develop a reliable and efficient framework for predicting events in complex systems, where uncertainty is inherent. Our approach combines advances in machine learning and probabilistic modeling to create a robust and scalable joint model. The model is designed to capture complex relationships between variables and quantify uncertainty in predictions. We evaluate our model on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superiority over existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and reliability. Key findings include significant improvements in prediction performance and uncertainty estimation, particularly in scenarios with high levels of noise and ambiguity. The proposed framework has important implications for applications in risk management, decision-making, and event forecasting, where reliable uncertainty-aware predictions are crucial. Our contributions include the development of a scalable and efficient joint modeling approach, which can be applied to a wide range of event prediction tasks, including those involving complex and dynamic systems. Relevant keywords: uncertainty-aware prediction, joint models, scalable machine learning, event forecasting, probabilistic modeling.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have shown promise in face generation, but controlling specific attributes remains a challenge. This paper introduces an attribute-aware face generation framework based on GANs that enables fine-grained control over facial attributes during the generation process. Our approach incorporates attribute classifiers within the GAN architecture to provide feedback on the generated faces, guiding the generator to produce images that accurately reflect the desired attribute values. Specifically, we utilize a multi-task learning setup where the discriminator not only distinguishes between real and fake images but also predicts the attributes present in the generated faces. This encourages the generator to learn a disentangled representation of facial attributes. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance in generating faces with controlled attributes compared to existing GAN-based approaches. The generated images exhibit higher fidelity and more accurate attribute representation, as validated by quantitative metrics and qualitative evaluations. This research contributes to the field of controllable face generation and has potential applications in areas such as facial manipulation, data augmentation, and personalized avatar creation. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, Face Generation, Attribute Control, Deep Learning, Image Synthesis.

This paper addresses the critical issue of trustworthiness in classifier systems, a problem that has significant implications for the reliability and dependability of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications. The objective is to develop a framework for evaluating the trustworthiness of classifiers, which is essential for high-stakes decision-making. Our approach involves designing and implementing a novel trust metric that assesses the classifier's performance, robustness, and transparency. The results show that our trust metric outperforms existing methods in identifying trustworthy classifiers, with significant improvements in accuracy and reliability. The key findings highlight the importance of considering trustworthiness in classifier design and deployment, with potential applications in areas such as healthcare, finance, and cybersecurity. This research contributes to the development of more reliable and trustworthy AI systems, with a focus on explainability, robustness, and transparency. Key keywords: classifier trustworthiness, machine learning, artificial intelligence, reliability, transparency, explainability.

This paper addresses the challenge of color constancy in digital images, where the goal is to remove the effects of illumination and recover the true colors of objects. Our objective is to develop a novel approach to color constancy using a bag of color features, which can effectively capture the color distribution of an image. We propose a method that extracts a set of color features from an image and uses them to estimate the color of the illuminant, allowing for more accurate color constancy. Our approach utilizes a combination of color histograms and texture features to create a robust representation of the image's color content. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing color constancy algorithms, particularly in scenes with complex lighting conditions. The key findings of this research include the development of a new color feature extraction technique and the demonstration of its effectiveness in improving color constancy. This work contributes to the field of computer vision and has potential applications in image processing, object recognition, and color-based image retrieval, with relevant keywords including color constancy, bag of features, color histograms, and image processing.

This paper introduces Neural Knitworks, a novel approach to neural implicit representation networks that leverages a patched representation to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of 3D reconstruction tasks. The objective is to address the limitations of existing neural implicit representation methods, which often struggle with complex geometries and large-scale scenes. Our approach employs a modular architecture, where a scene is divided into smaller patches, each represented by a dedicated neural network. This allows for more effective capture of local details and improved handling of intricate structures. Experimental results demonstrate that Neural Knitworks outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. The key findings highlight the benefits of patched representations in neural implicit modeling, enabling more accurate and detailed 3D reconstructions. This research contributes to the advancement of neural implicit representation networks and has potential applications in fields such as computer vision, robotics, and computer-aided design. Key keywords: neural implicit representation, 3D reconstruction, patched representation, modular architecture, computer vision.

This paper investigates the vulnerability and robustness of reinforcement learning-based interactive recommender systems when subjected to adversarial attacks. These systems, which tailor user experiences by predicting preferences, are increasingly adopted in various domains; however, their susceptibility to adversarial perturbations poses significant security and reliability risks. Methods/Approach: We developed a comprehensive framework for generating adversarial attacks against reinforcement learning-based recommender systems and proposed novel detection mechanisms to identify such attacks. Our approach combines gradient-based methods to craft perturbations that manipulate system outputs subtly while exploring advanced anomaly detection techniques to safeguard the system. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our adversarial attack framework effectively compromises the performance of state-of-the-art reinforcement learning recommender systems, significantly degrading recommendation accuracy and user satisfaction. Conversely, the proposed detection methods successfully identify adversarial activities with high precision and recall, restoring the system's reliability and performance to near-original levels. Conclusion/Implications: The study highlights critical vulnerabilities in reinforcement learning-based recommender systems and underscores the importance of robust defense mechanisms against adversarial threats. Our findings contribute to the advancement of more resilient interactive systems, fostering safer deployment in real-world applications. Future research directions include enhancing attack defenses and extending the methodology to other AI-driven adaptive technologies. Keywords: reinforcement learning, recommender systems, adversarial attacks, anomaly detection, interactive systems, AI security.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving learning efficiency and convergence speed in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) systems, a domain where training times and computational costs often hinder practical deployment. We propose a suite of accelerated methods that integrate advanced optimization algorithms, adaptive exploration strategies, and efficient experience replay techniques to enhance the performance of DRL agents. Specifically, our approach incorporates momentum-based gradient updates, prioritized sampling, and dynamic adjustment of exploration rates to target slow-converging regimes in complex environments. Experimental evaluations were conducted across several standard benchmarks, including Atari and robotic control tasks, where our accelerated methods consistently achieved faster convergence and higher cumulative rewards compared to baseline DRL algorithms such as Deep Q-Networks (DQN) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The results demonstrate that the proposed techniques significantly reduce training epochs without compromising policy quality. This work contributes a novel framework for accelerating deep reinforcement learning, with practical implications for real-time decision-making, robotics, and large-scale autonomous systems. Key keywords include deep reinforcement learning, acceleration, optimization, experience replay, convergence speed, adaptive exploration, and policy improvement.

Single-image 3D photography aims to generate realistic depth-aware 3D effects from a single 2D image, enabling applications in VR, AR, and computational photography. However, existing methods often suffer from depth inconsistencies, occlusion artifacts, and unnatural layer transitions. To address these challenges, we propose SLIDE (Single Image 3D Photography with Soft Layering and Depth-aware Inpainting), a novel framework that reconstructs high-quality 3D views with improved occlusion handling and depth perception. SLIDE introduces a soft layering mechanism that decomposes an image into multiple depth-ordered layers with smooth transitions, reducing artifacts in synthesized novel views. Additionally, we employ a depth-aware inpainting module that predicts and fills occluded regions by leveraging context from surrounding depth and texture features. Our approach is trained in a self-supervised manner, ensuring generalization across diverse scenes without requiring ground-truth multi-view data. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SLIDE achieves state-of-the-art performance in single-image 3D view synthesis, outperforming existing methods in terms of depth consistency, visual realism, and occlusion handling. These results highlight the potential of soft layering and depth-aware inpainting for advancing 3D photography from monocular images. Keywords: 3D Photography, Single-Image 3D Reconstruction, Depth-aware Inpainting, Soft Layering, Novel View Synthesis, Computational Photography.

This paper presents a novel approach to evolving Gaussian Process (GP) kernels from elementary mathematical expressions, addressing the long-standing challenge of kernel design in machine learning. Our objective is to develop a flexible and automated framework for constructing kernels that can effectively capture complex patterns in data. We propose a method that utilizes evolutionary algorithms to search for optimal kernel combinations, leveraging a library of basic mathematical operations and functions. The results show that our approach can generate kernels that outperform traditional hand-designed kernels in various regression and classification tasks, demonstrating improved predictive accuracy and robustness. Our findings have significant implications for the development of more efficient and adaptive GP models, enabling their application to a broader range of problems in fields such as computer vision, natural language processing, and time-series forecasting. Key contributions include the introduction of a new kernel evolution framework, the demonstration of its effectiveness in real-world datasets, and the potential for automated kernel design in GP models, highlighting the importance of Gaussian Processes, kernel methods, and evolutionary algorithms in machine learning research.

This research addresses the challenge of synthesizing realistic face photos from simple line drawings, an application with significant potential in digital art and design. The study aims to enhance creative expression by allowing artists to control facial attributes directly from a basic sketch. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel approach that utilizes a deep learning framework capable of mapping line drawings to high-quality facial images with user-defined attributes such as age, gender, and expression. The core of our method is a generative adversarial network (GAN) specifically designed for attribute-controlled synthesis, supported by a feature-enhancement module to refine subtle details and artistic nuances. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method generates more realistic and semantically meaningful facial photos compared to existing approaches. The incorporation of an attribute control mechanism enables users to effectively guide the synthesis process, achieving personalized photorealism. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations show superior performance in maintaining consistency between the drawn attributes and the resulting image features. Conclusion/Implications: The insights gained from this research contribute to the growing field of AI-assisted artistic creation, offering a versatile tool for designers and illustrators. The proposed model not only advances the state-of-the-art in line drawing-to-photo synthesis but also broadens the potential for interactive and creative digital content generation. Future applications may include virtual reality avatar creation and interactive character design. Symmetric and hash-based cryptographic methods remain robust against quantum attacks, whereas common asymmetric cryptosystems such as RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography are vulnerable to powerful quantum computers capable of running Shor’s algorithm, which can efficiently break these schemes. In contemporary security protocols, public key cryptosystems play a crucial role in establishing shared secret keys between parties. However, the emergence of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) marks a significant advancement, as it enables two parties to securely generate and share a random secret key that is intrinsically protected against eavesdropping, even by adversaries equipped with quantum computational capabilities.

This paper addresses the challenge of deriving generalization guarantees in nonlinear metric learning without dependence on data dimensionality. Existing metric learning approaches often require strong assumptions on data structure or impose dimension-related constraints, making them impractical for high-dimensional applications such as image retrieval, natural language processing, and bioinformatics. We propose a novel theoretical framework that establishes dimension-free generalization bounds for a broad class of nonlinear metric learning algorithms, leveraging advances in Rademacher complexity and covering numbers. Our analysis encompasses both kernel-based and neural network-based metric learning models, demonstrating that their capacity to generalize is governed by intrinsic algorithmic properties rather than the ambient feature space size. Experimental evaluation on benchmark datasets validates the tightness of our bounds and the superior performance of nonlinear metrics in high-dimensional regimes compared to traditional linear methods. Our findings offer significant insights for the design of scalable and robust metric learning systems in data-rich environments. Keywords: metric learning, generalization bounds, kernel methods, neural networks, high-dimensional data, nonlinear models, Rademacher complexity.

This paper introduces *PowerGym*, a novel reinforcement learning (RL) environment designed to address the challenges of Volt-Var control in modern power distribution systems. The increasing integration of distributed energy resources (DERs) and the growing complexity of grid operations necessitate advanced control strategies to maintain voltage stability and optimize reactive power management. *PowerGym* provides a scalable and realistic simulation platform for training and evaluating RL-based control algorithms, enabling researchers to develop solutions for real-world power system challenges. The environment incorporates high-fidelity models of distribution networks, including dynamic load profiles, DERs, and controllable devices such as capacitor banks and voltage regulators. A deep reinforcement learning framework is employed to train agents that can autonomously manage Volt-Var control, ensuring compliance with operational constraints while minimizing energy losses and voltage deviations. Experimental results demonstrate that RL agents trained in *PowerGym* outperform traditional rule-based and optimization-based methods, achieving significant improvements in system efficiency and stability. The key contribution of this work lies in the development of a standardized, open-source RL environment tailored for power distribution systems, which bridges the gap between theoretical research and practical implementation. *PowerGym* not only advances the state-of-the-art in Volt-Var control but also serves as a valuable tool for accelerating the adoption of AI-driven solutions in the energy sector. **Keywords**: reinforcement learning, Volt-Var control, power distribution systems, distributed energy resources, deep learning, grid optimization.

The study explores the development and utilization of implicit deep latent variable models for enhancing text generation. The primary objective is to address the limitations of traditional text generation models through the integration of advanced latent variable techniques, aiming to achieve more coherent and contextually relevant text outputs. Methods/Approach: We introduce an innovative approach that leverages implicit modeling techniques in deep learning to construct latent variable models for text generation. This methodology entails embedding implicit generative mechanisms within a neural network architecture, facilitating the capture of complex data distributions without explicit likelihood approximations. The models are trained through a combination of variational inference and adversarial training strategies to optimize performance. Results/Findings: Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed implicit deep latent variable models significantly outperform existing benchmarks in text generation tasks. The generated text exhibits improved fluency, coherence, and diversity compared to conventional methods. The models also show robustness in handling diverse textual inputs and exhibit enhanced ability to generate contextually rich and semantically accurate content. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel framework for text generation by incorporating implicit latent variable models, which addresses key limitations in current methodologies. The findings suggest promising applications in areas such as natural language processing, AI communication systems, and automated content creation. The advanced text generation capabilities offered by this approach could be pivotal in developing more sophisticated AI-driven interactions and content generation platforms. Keywords: Implicit models, deep learning, latent variable models, text generation, variational inference, adversarial training, neural networks.

This paper introduces STEP, a novel framework that leverages Spatial Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (ST-GCNs) to recognize human emotions from gaits. The objective is to develop a deep learning model that can effectively capture the spatial and temporal dependencies in human walking patterns to infer emotional states. Our approach utilizes a graph-based representation of human skeletons, which are then fed into a ST-GCN to extract meaningful features. The results show that STEP outperforms existing methods in emotion recognition from gaits, achieving a significant improvement in accuracy. The key findings suggest that the spatial and temporal features extracted by the ST-GCN are essential for emotion perception. This research contributes to the field of affective computing and human-computer interaction, with potential applications in fields such as healthcare, psychology, and social robotics. The novelty of STEP lies in its ability to model complex human movements and emotions using a graph-based neural network architecture, making it a unique and innovative approach in the field of emotion recognition. Key keywords: ST-GCN, emotion recognition, gait analysis, affective computing, human-computer interaction.

This paper addresses the challenge of dataset bias in the field of visual emotion recognition, where the accuracy and fairness of predictive models are often compromised due to inherent biases in training data. The research seeks to understand these biases and proposes methods to mitigate their effects, thereby enhancing model reliability and performance. Methods/Approach: We conducted an in-depth analysis of existing visual emotion datasets to identify prevalent bias patterns, such as overrepresentation of specific demographics or emotional states. To address these biases, we developed a novel bias-mitigation framework that employs data augmentation and re-weighting techniques. Additionally, we introduce a fairness-aware model architecture that adjusts learning based on detected biases during training. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly reduces bias in visual emotion recognition models, leading to more equitable predictions across diverse demographic groups. Compared to baseline models, our approach achieved an improvement in accuracy and fairness metrics across multiple benchmark datasets. This highlights the effectiveness of our methods in overcoming dataset biases. Conclusion/Implications: Our research contributes to the field by providing a clearer understanding of the biases inherent in visual emotion datasets and offering practical solutions to address them. The innovations presented in this paper have the potential to be applied in various applications requiring emotion recognition, such as human-computer interaction, surveillance, and media analysis, ensuring that systems deliver unbiased and fair outcomes. Keywords: visual emotion recognition, dataset bias, fairness, bias mitigation, emotion datasets, machine learning.

Semi-supervised learning for volumetric medical image segmentation is crucial due to the scarcity of labeled data. This paper introduces a novel momentum contrastive voxel-wise representation learning framework to address this challenge. Our approach leverages unlabeled data by learning robust voxel-level feature representations through a contrastive loss, encouraging similar voxels to cluster together while dissimilar voxels are separated. Specifically, we utilize a momentum update strategy to maintain a consistent and stable feature bank for contrastive learning. This mitigates the noise inherent in training with limited labeled data. We evaluate our method on two publicly available datasets for abdominal organ segmentation and cardiac structure segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing semi-supervised segmentation methods, achieving comparable performance to fully supervised methods while using only a fraction of the labeled data. The learned voxel-wise representations also prove to be more generalizable and robust to variations in image acquisition parameters. Our findings highlight the potential of contrastive representation learning for improving medical image segmentation accuracy and reducing the reliance on extensive manual annotations. Keywords: Semi-supervised learning, medical image segmentation, contrastive learning, voxel-wise representation, momentum contrast, deep learning.

This paper addresses the intricate challenge of parameter inference in dynamic systems exhibiting bifurcations. These nonlinear dynamics are prevalent in many scientific domains and their accurate modeling is critical for system stability and prediction. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel approach leveraging bifurcation diagrams to enhance parameter inference. Our methodology systematically exploits the structural insights provided by bifurcation diagrams to refine parameter estimates in complex systems. This approach involves integrating bifurcation theory with advanced computational techniques to navigate the parameter space efficiently. Results/Findings: The application of our method demonstrates significant improvements in identifying and estimating parameters governing system behaviors. Our results show enhanced accuracy in capturing critical thresholds and transitions compared to traditional inference methods. The approach is validated on various dynamical systems, revealing robustness across different types of bifurcations. Conclusion/Implications: The research offers a substantial contribution to the field of dynamic systems by providing a more reliable and efficient framework for parameter inference. This has broad implications for models where bifurcations play a key role, such as climate modeling, biological systems, and engineering dynamics. Future work could extend this framework to integrate machine learning techniques for even more powerful inference and prediction capabilities. Keywords: parameter inference, bifurcation diagrams, nonlinear dynamics, dynamical systems, computational techniques.

Objective: Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) provides a principled way to extract and organize knowledge from binary relations by constructing concept lattices, but its combinatorial nature limits scalability and integration with modern machine‐learning pipelines. This paper introduces FCA2VEC, a novel embedding framework that transforms formal contexts and their derived concepts into continuous vector spaces while preserving lattice structure and semantic relationships. Methods: FCA2VEC adapts neural embedding techniques—drawing inspiration from skip‐gram models and graph representation learning—to generate low‐dimensional embeddings for objects, attributes, and concepts. We define sampling strategies over concept lattices and contextual windows in formal contexts, and employ negative sampling to optimize vector representations. The approach is evaluated on synthetic and real‐world datasets, including text corpora and knowledge‐base snapshots. Results: Experiments demonstrate that FCA2VEC embeddings achieve over 20% improvement in concept similarity correlation and 15% higher accuracy in concept membership prediction compared to baseline aggregation and matrix‐factorization methods. Qualitative analyses show that vector arithmetic captures lattice join and meet operations, and that clustering in embedding space recovers meaningful sublattices. Conclusion: FCA2VEC bridges classical FCA and contemporary representation learning, enabling efficient concept exploration, visualization, and downstream tasks such as classification and recommendation. By offering a scalable, trainable interface to concept lattices, FCA2VEC paves the way for real‐time knowledge discovery in large‐scale and dynamic datasets. Keywords: Formal Concept Analysis, embeddings, representation learning, concept lattices, neural vectors.

This paper addresses the challenge of few-shot learning, where the goal is to recognize new classes with only a few labeled examples. Traditional few-shot learning approaches often struggle to capture relationships among examples, limiting generalization capabilities. We introduce Relational Generalized Few-Shot Learning (RGFSL), which aims to enhance model understanding through relational representations, enabling better performance on a broader set of tasks with minimal data. Methods/Approach: The proposed RGFSL framework employs a relational module that constructs dynamic graphs to capture dependencies among input examples. Utilizing a graph neural network (GNN) architecture, this module effectively propagates information, allowing the model to make more informed predictions. This approach goes beyond static feature embedding methods by iteratively refining relationships during training and inference. To validate our approach, we conduct experiments using multiple benchmark datasets, comparing its performance against existing few-shot learning techniques. Results/Findings: Our findings demonstrate that RGFSL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models in few-shot tasks, achieving superior accuracy and robustness across different datasets. The model excels particularly in generalized settings, where class distributions and instance-level relationships are diverse. Notably, RGFSL shows marked improvements in both 5-way 1-shot and 5-way 5-shot tasks, confirming its capability to generalize from limited data effectively. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of relational processing in few-shot learning offers a promising direction for enhancing adaptability and generalization in AI models. By incorporating relational knowledge, RGFSL contributes to more versatile applications, including autonomous systems, personalized services, and other environments needing rapid adaptation with minimal input. This research outlines a novel pathway for advancing few-shot learning through relational understanding, setting the stage for future innovations in machine learning model design. Key Keywords: few-shot learning, relational learning, graph neural networks, few-shot classification, generalized few-shot tasks.

This paper addresses the challenge of detecting curve text in images, a problem that has garnered significant attention in the field of computer vision. The objective is to develop a robust method for curve text detection that can accurately locate and recognize text in images with complex backgrounds and varying font styles. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach based on conditional spatial expansion, which adaptively expands the spatial context of text regions to capture long-range dependencies and improve detection accuracy. Our method utilizes a deep learning framework that integrates a spatial expansion module with a text detection network, enabling the model to effectively handle curved text lines and irregular text layouts. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a conditional spatial expansion mechanism and the development of a robust curve text detection system that can be applied to various real-world applications, such as scene text recognition, document analysis, and autonomous driving. Keywords: curve text detection, conditional spatial expansion, deep learning, computer vision, scene text recognition.

The outcome of this work can be a cue to selection of algorithms as per requirement for automated blood cell classification.

Unsupervised Video Object Segmentation (UVOS) aims to identify and segment salient objects in a video without any manual annotation. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging instance embedding transfer to improve the performance of UVOS. Our method utilizes instance embeddings learned from static images to guide the segmentation process in videos. Specifically, we transfer the learned semantic understanding of objects from still images to the video domain, enabling the model to better distinguish between foreground objects and background clutter. This is achieved through a specifically designed loss function that encourages temporal consistency and semantic alignment of instance embeddings across video frames. Experimental results on standard UVOS benchmarks demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised methods. The proposed method achieves improved segmentation accuracy, robustness to motion blur, and better handling of complex scenes. The code will be publicly available. Keywords: Video Object Segmentation, Unsupervised Learning, Instance Embedding, Transfer Learning, Computer Vision.
