Recently, the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) graph isomorphism test was used to measure the expressive power of graph neural networks (GNN). It was shown that the popular message passing GNN cannot distinguish between graphs that are indistinguishable by the 1-WL test (Morris et al. 2018; Xu et al. 2019). Unfortunately, many simple instances of graphs are indistinguishable by the 1-WL test. In search for more expressive graph learning models we build upon the recent k-order invariant and equivariant graph neural networks (Maron et al. 2019a,b) and present two results: First, we show that such k-order networks can distinguish between non-isomorphic graphs as good as the k-WL tests, which are provably stronger than the 1-WL test for k>2. This makes these models strictly stronger than message passing models. Unfortunately, the higher expressiveness of these models comes with a computational cost of processing high order tensors. Second, setting our goal at building a provably stronger, simple and scalable model we show that a reduced 2-order network containing just scaled identity operator, augmented with a single quadratic operation (matrix multiplication) has a provable 3-WL expressive power. Differently put, we suggest a simple model that interleaves applications of standard Multilayer-Perceptron (MLP) applied to the feature dimension and matrix multiplication. We validate this model by presenting state of the art results on popular graph classification and regression tasks. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first practical invariant/equivariant model with guaranteed 3-WL expressiveness, strictly stronger than message passing models.

This paper proposes a novel semi-supervised deep kernel learning approach for regression tasks, leveraging unlabeled data to improve predictive performance by minimizing predictive variance. The objective is to develop a framework that effectively utilizes both labeled and unlabeled data to enhance model generalization. Our method employs a deep kernel learning architecture, combining the strengths of neural networks and kernel methods, to learn informative representations from both labeled and unlabeled datasets. By minimizing the predictive variance of the model, we encourage the learning of more consistent and accurate predictions. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, showing significant improvements in regression performance compared to state-of-the-art supervised and semi-supervised methods. The key contributions of this work include the development of a semi-supervised deep kernel learning framework, the introduction of a predictive variance minimization objective, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in leveraging unlabeled data for improved regression performance. This research has important implications for applications where labeled data is scarce or expensive to obtain, and highlights the potential of semi-supervised learning for improving model accuracy and robustness in real-world regression tasks, particularly in areas such as machine learning, kernel methods, and deep learning.

This research addresses the challenge of training deep action recognition networks, which require large and diverse labeled video datasets. Acquiring and annotating such data is time-consuming and labor-intensive. This study explores the use of procedural generation to create synthetic training videos, aiming to enhance the robustness and accuracy of action recognition models. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach leveraging procedural content generation techniques to produce a wide variety of synthetic video scenarios depicting different actions. These generated videos are used to train deep learning models for action recognition. The models are evaluated on their ability to recognize actions in both synthetic and real-world scenarios, underscoring the effectiveness of the generated content. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that models trained on procedurally generated videos perform on par with, and in some instances exceed, the performance of those trained on real-world datasets. The abundant diversity and controlled environment of the synthetic datasets enable the networks to generalize better to unseen real-world videos. Comparative analysis also shows a reduced requirement for manual labeling, significantly lowering costs and effort involved in curating training datasets. Conclusion/Implications: The study highlights the potential of procedural video generation as a viable solution to the data scarcity problem in training action recognition networks. This approach not only reduces the dependence on costly video collection and annotation processes but also improves model accuracy and robustness. The findings pave the way for broader applications in video analysis and surveillance systems, where real-time and precise action recognition is critical. Keywords: procedural generation, action recognition, deep learning, synthetic datasets, video analysis, AI models.

This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning (RL) approach leveraging Fenchel-Rockafellar duality to enhance policy optimization. We reformulate the RL problem within a convex optimization framework, enabling the derivation of dual policies and value functions that offer improved stability and convergence guarantees compared to traditional methods. Our approach replaces the standard Bellman equations with a dual representation, facilitating the use of efficient convex optimization algorithms. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method on a suite of benchmark RL tasks, including CartPole and MountainCar, showing significant improvements in sample efficiency and robustness to hyperparameter settings. Empirical results highlight the potential for scaling this method to more complex environments. Furthermore, we provide theoretical analysis ensuring convergence under mild assumptions. This work offers a new perspective on reinforcement learning by directly optimizing dual objectives and provides a foundation for developing more robust and efficient RL algorithms. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Fenchel-Rockafellar Duality, Convex Optimization, Policy Optimization, Dual Policies, Sample Efficiency.

Việc xây dựng bộ tiêu chí đánh giá tính hiệu quả và bền vững của cơ sở hạ tầng nông thôn tại Việt Nam là một yêu cầu cấp thiết trong bối cảnh phát triển kinh tế - xã hội hiện nay. Bộ tiêu chí này cần phản ánh được các yếu tố như chất lượng công trình, khả năng đáp ứng nhu cầu của người dân, tính thích ứng với biến đổi khí hậu, và hiệu quả sử dụng nguồn lực. Đồng thời, nó phải đảm bảo sự cân bằng giữa phát triển kinh tế và bảo vệ môi trường, hướng tới mục tiêu phát triển bền vững. **Abstract** Hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) is widely used for discovering data groupings, but traditional approaches often disregard the natural or original order of elements, which is crucial in domains such as time series analysis, genomics, and preference ranking. This paper introduces an order preserving hierarchical agglomerative clustering (OP-HAC) method that retains the sequential order of data while constructing the hierarchical clustering dendrogram. Our approach modifies traditional agglomerative strategies by restricting candidate cluster merges to adjacent clusters, thereby ensuring the global order is maintained throughout the clustering process. We present both an efficient algorithm for OP-HAC and a theoretical analysis of its computational complexity. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets, including temporal event streams and sorted lists, demonstrate that OP-HAC identifies meaningful clusters consistent with the underlying sequential structure, outperforming standard HAC when order preservation is essential. The proposed method also enhances interpretability in ordered data scenarios and reduces computational overhead by limiting merge possibilities. OP-HAC presents a significant advancement for clustering applications where structural ordering is intrinsic, with potential applications in time series segmentation, biological sequence analysis, and rank-based data mining. **Keywords:** hierarchical clustering, order preservation, agglomerative clustering, sequential data, time series, data mining.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing the performance of Adder Neural Networks (ANNs), which are known for reducing power consumption as compared to traditional neural networks while potentially sacrificing accuracy. The research focuses on developing a novel distillation approach to improve the accuracy of ANNs without significantly impacting their efficiency. Methods/Approach: We introduce a Kernel Based Progressive Distillation (KPD) method that leverages kernel functions to iteratively refine the knowledge transfer process from a pre-trained teacher model to an ANN student model. The proposed method progressively incorporates diverse kernel functions through multiple stages to enhance the learning capacity of the student network. This systematic distillation enables the student ANN to approximate the performance of its teacher while maintaining the computational advantages of adder networks. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our KPD approach significantly improves the accuracy of ANNs across various benchmark datasets, achieving results that are on par with, or surpass those of state-of-the-art models utilizing traditional neural networks. The KPD method proves effective in balancing the trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency, showing noteworthy enhancements in system performance with minimal additional resource consumption. Conclusion/Implications: The Kernel Based Progressive Distillation technique presents a substantial advancement in the field of efficient neural network models. By integrating kernel-based methods into the distillation process, this research offers a pathway to develop highly accurate yet energy-efficient ANNs. The implications of this study are vast, offering potential applications in edge computing and other resource-constrained environments where efficient yet powerful AI models are necessary. Keywords: Adder Neural Networks, Kernel Functions, Progressive Distillation, Energy Efficiency, Knowledge Transfer, Edge Computing.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing partitioning problems by leveraging a novel large-margin metric learning approach. Traditional partitioning methods often struggle with the discrimination of complex data structures, necessitating more sophisticated learning techniques to improve classification boundaries and partitioning efficiency. Methods/Approach: We propose a large-margin metric learning framework that optimizes a distance metric to better capture the intrinsic structure of data. By maximizing the margin between partition boundaries, our approach effectively differentiates between data clusters. This framework adopts a supervised learning paradigm that iteratively refines the metric based on labeled instances, facilitating more accurate and meaningful partitions. Results/Findings: Our experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over existing metric learning approaches in various partitioning tasks, both in terms of clustering accuracy and computational efficiency. Comparisons with state-of-the-art methods reveal that our large-margin strategy achieves superior performance across diverse datasets, highlighting its robustness and generality. Notably, the approach shows marked advancements in scenarios involving high-dimensional data and non-linear separations. Conclusion/Implications: The research presents a substantial contribution to the field of metric learning and partitioning problems by introducing a methodology that balances precision and adaptability. Its practical implications suggest the potential for enhanced data segmentation in applications such as image processing, network analysis, and more complex AI systems. Future work may explore the integration of this framework with unsupervised learning techniques to extend its applicability in broader contexts. Keywords: Metric Learning, Partitioning Problems, Large-Margin, Distance Metric, Clustering Accuracy, High-Dimensional Data.

This paper addresses the need for an improved gradient boosting method by integrating piece-wise linear regression trees to enhance predictive performance in various machine learning tasks. Traditional gradient boosting, while effective, is often limited by the use of constant values at each tree's leaves, potentially hindering accuracy and learning capacity. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel framework that incorporates piece-wise linear regression trees into the gradient boosting algorithm. This approach allows for each leaf of the tree to model linear relationships, providing more flexibility and precision in capturing the complexities of data. The methodology strengthens the predictive power by leveraging both the global features of the dataset and the localized linear patterns within tree leaves. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate a significant improvement in model accuracy and robustness across multiple benchmark datasets. When compared to standard gradient boosting methods, our approach consistently achieves lower error rates and faster convergence. The model's ability to adapt to nuanced data structures results in better performance, particularly in scenarios with complex decision boundaries. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a substantial advancement in the field of gradient boosting by incorporating piece-wise linear regression capabilities. The proposed model not only enhances prediction accuracy but also extends the applicability of gradient boosting methods to a broader range of complex data modeling problems. This innovation has the potential to be utilized in various applications where improved precision of predictions is crucial, such as in financial forecasting, healthcare diagnostics, and real-time data analysis. Keywords: gradient boosting, piece-wise linear regression trees, machine learning, predictive modeling, data structures.

The objective of this research is to address the challenge of multi-view clustering by developing a novel consistent multiple graph embedding framework. Multi-view clustering is critical for effectively analyzing data from different perspectives, yet traditional approaches often struggle with consistency and efficiency. Our proposed method leverages the power of consistent graph embeddings to integrate multiple views into a unified representation, enabling enhanced clustering performance. The approach relies on constructing a set of graph embeddings for each view and then aligning these into a consistent multi-view representation using advanced embedding techniques. Key findings indicate that this method not only improves clustering accuracy but also offers superior results in terms of computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art algorithms. Our results show its applicability to a range of domains that rely on multi-view data, such as image recognition, social network analysis, and bioinformatics. Conclusively, this research contributes to the field by providing a robust framework for consistent multi-view clustering, opening avenues for more dynamic data integration and analysis. Key keywords include multi-view clustering, graph embeddings, data integration, and clustering performance.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in healthcare, enabling precise diagnosis and treatment planning. However, designing effective Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures for this purpose often requires extensive expertise and manual tuning. This paper addresses the challenge by proposing an automated approach to design CNN architectures tailored for medical image segmentation. Our method leverages a neural architecture search (NAS) framework, which explores a diverse search space of convolutional operations, skip connections, and upsampling strategies to optimize segmentation performance. The proposed approach is evaluated on multiple medical imaging datasets, including MRI and CT scans, and demonstrates superior accuracy compared to manually designed architectures and existing NAS-based methods. Key findings reveal that the automatically generated architectures achieve higher Dice scores and improved boundary delineation, particularly in complex anatomical structures. The results highlight the potential of automated CNN design to reduce human effort while enhancing segmentation quality. This research contributes to the field by introducing a scalable and efficient NAS framework for medical imaging, paving the way for broader applications in clinical settings. **Keywords**: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Medical Image Segmentation, Neural Architecture Search (NAS), Automated Design, MRI, CT Scans.

In this paper user modeling task is examined by processing a gallery of photos and videos on a mobile device. We propose novel engine for user preference prediction based on scene recognition, object detection and facial analysis. At first, all faces in a gallery are clustered and all private photos and videos with faces from large clusters are processed on the embedded system in offline mode. Other photos may be sent to the remote server to be analyzed by very deep models. The visual features of each photo are obtained from scene recognition and object detection models. These features are aggregated into a single user descriptor in the neural attention block. The proposed pipeline is implemented for the Android mobile platform. Experimental results with a subset of Photo Event Collection, Web Image Dataset for Event Recognition and Amazon Fashion datasets demonstrate the possibility to process images very efficiently without significant accuracy degradation. The source code of Android mobile application is publicly available at https://github.com/HSE-asavchenko/mobile-visual-preferences.

This paper addresses the challenge of forecasting in multivariate time series data where observations are irregularly sampled and contain missing values, a common problem in various domains such as finance, healthcare, and environmental monitoring. We propose a novel deep learning model based on a temporal attention mechanism combined with a recurrent neural network, specifically designed to handle irregular sampling patterns and impute missing values simultaneously. The model learns temporal dependencies from observed data while adaptively weighting the importance of different time points and variables. We evaluate the proposed approach on several real-world datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in forecasting accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, including traditional imputation techniques and other deep learning models. Furthermore, we analyze the learned attention weights to gain insights into the temporal dynamics of the multivariate time series. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed model in capturing complex relationships and handling data irregularities, offering a robust and accurate solution for forecasting in challenging real-world scenarios. Keywords: time series forecasting, irregular sampling, missing values, deep learning, temporal attention, recurrent neural networks.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc điều chế vi cầu chứa bovine serum albumin (BSA) bằng phương pháp tạo gel ion sử dụng alginat và chitosan. Mục tiêu là tạo ra hệ vận chuyển thuốc tiềm năng, bảo vệ protein khỏi sự phân hủy và kiểm soát quá trình высвобождения. Các vi cầu được tạo ra với kích thước và hình thái khác nhau tùy thuộc vào tỷ lệ alginat và chitosan. Kết quả cho thấy sự tương tác tĩnh điện giữa alginat mang điện tích âm và chitosan mang điện tích dương đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc hình thành vi cầu. BSA được nạp thành công vào cấu trúc vi cầu, và tốc độ высвобождения của BSA có thể điều chỉnh bằng cách thay đổi thành phần của vi cầu. Objective: Continuous control in high-dimensional systems poses challenges in stability and sample efficiency for deep reinforcement learning (DRL). This paper introduces a hybrid framework that integrates deep RL with region-specific Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers to enhance learning stability and performance. Methods: We partition the state space into overlapping regions using a neural network classifier trained on state features. Within each region, a locally linearized dynamics model enables the synthesis of an LQR controller, yielding optimal feedback gains for that region. A deep actor-critic algorithm is then augmented to switch between region-specific LQR policies and a global DRL policy based on region membership. Policy updates incorporate both gradient-based deep network updates and closed-form LQR solutions to accelerate convergence toward high-performance control. Results: Experiments on standard continuous control benchmarks—including inverted pendulum, cart-pole swing-up, and three-link manipulator—demonstrate that the proposed method achieves up to 35% faster convergence and 20% higher average return compared to state-of-the-art model-free DRL baselines (PPO, DDPG). Stability analysis shows reduced variance in episodic returns and improved robustness under perturbations. Conclusion: By blending model-based LQR regions with model-free deep RL, our approach offers a novel pathway to reliable, sample-efficient learning in complex control tasks. This framework has potential applications in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and aerospace systems where safety and data efficiency are critical. Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Linear Quadratic Regulator, Hybrid Control, Actor-Critic, Continuous Control.

This paper introduces a novel approach to graph exploration, leveraging transfer learning to enable efficient and effective navigation of complex graph structures. The objective is to develop a framework that can learn transferable graph exploration strategies, applicable to various domains and graph types. Our method employs a graph neural network-based architecture, incorporating reinforcement learning and self-supervised learning techniques to learn generalizable exploration policies. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, outperforming existing methods in terms of exploration efficiency and node coverage. The key findings highlight the importance of transfer learning in graph exploration, enabling the model to adapt to new, unseen graphs with minimal additional training. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and scalable graph exploration algorithms, with potential applications in network analysis, recommendation systems, and graph-based machine learning. The proposed framework is particularly relevant to areas such as social network analysis, molecular graph exploration, and web graph crawling, where transferable graph exploration strategies can significantly improve performance and reduce computational costs. Key keywords: graph exploration, transfer learning, graph neural networks, reinforcement learning, self-supervised learning.

Traffic congestion in urban areas remains a critical challenge, necessitating efficient and adaptive traffic control systems. This paper proposes a novel approach to traffic control optimization by integrating a Boosted Genetic Algorithm (BGA) with Machine Learning (ML) techniques. The objective is to enhance the performance of traditional genetic algorithms in optimizing traffic signal timings, thereby reducing congestion and improving traffic flow. The proposed method leverages ML models to predict traffic patterns and dynamically adjust the fitness evaluation process within the BGA framework. This adaptive mechanism enables the algorithm to respond effectively to real-time traffic conditions. Experimental evaluations were conducted using simulated urban traffic scenarios, comparing the proposed BGA-ML approach with conventional genetic algorithms and other optimization methods. Results demonstrate significant improvements in traffic flow efficiency, with reductions in average waiting times and vehicle emissions. The study highlights the potential of combining evolutionary algorithms with ML for real-time traffic management, offering a scalable and adaptive solution for smart cities. Key contributions include the development of a hybrid optimization framework and its application to dynamic traffic control, showcasing its superiority over traditional methods. Keywords: Boosted Genetic Algorithm, Machine Learning, Traffic Control Optimization, Smart Cities, Real-Time Adaptation.

This paper addresses the challenge of safe exploration in identifying linear systems, a critical task in control theory and reinforcement learning. The objective is to develop a method that ensures system stability and safety while efficiently learning the system dynamics. To achieve this, we propose a robust optimization-based approach that integrates safety constraints directly into the exploration process. Our method leverages convex optimization techniques to formulate a constrained exploration problem, ensuring that the system remains within predefined safe operating limits during identification. We evaluate the proposed approach through extensive simulations and compare it with existing methods, demonstrating its ability to maintain safety while achieving accurate system identification. The results show significant improvements in both safety guarantees and exploration efficiency, particularly in high-dimensional and uncertain environments. This work contributes a novel framework for safe exploration in linear systems, with potential applications in autonomous systems, robotics, and adaptive control. Key innovations include the integration of robust optimization with exploration strategies and the development of safety-aware learning algorithms. Keywords: safe exploration, linear systems, robust optimization, system identification, control theory, reinforcement learning.

This paper presents a novel dataset for traffic accidents analysis. Our goal is to resolve the lack of public data for research about automatic spatio-temporal annotations for traffic safety in the roads. Through the analysis of the proposed dataset, we observed a significant degradation of object detection in pedestrian category in our dataset, due to the object sizes and complexity of the scenes. To this end, we propose to integrate contextual information into conventional Faster R-CNN using Context Mining (CM) and Augmented Context Mining (ACM) to complement the accuracy for small pedestrian detection. Our experiments indicate a considerable improvement in object detection accuracy: +8.51% for CM and +6.20% for ACM. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of accident forecasting in our dataset using Faster R-CNN and an Accident LSTM architecture. We achieved an average of 1.684 seconds in terms of Time-To-Accident measure with an Average Precision of 47.25%. Our Webpage for the paper is https://goo.gl/cqK2wE

Objective: Eye tracking has traditionally been confined to specialized labs by high-cost, closed‐source systems, limiting its adoption in ubiquitous and mobile applications. This paper introduces Pupil, an open‐source hardware and software platform designed to democratize pervasive eye tracking and gaze‐based interaction. Methods: Pupil combines a lightweight, 3D‐printed headset with commodity cameras and a cross‐platform software suite. The software employs a modular, plugin‐based architecture for real‐time pupil detection, gaze mapping, calibration, and scene annotation. Support for Linux, macOS, Windows, and mobile devices enables on‐device or streamed processing. Standard computer vision techniques are optimized for 60 Hz operation under varying lighting conditions. Results: Empirical evaluation demonstrates average gaze estimation accuracy of 0.6° of visual angle and precision of 0.2° at 60 Hz with end‐to‐end latency below 50 ms. The system maintains robust performance indoors and outdoors, and integrates seamlessly with AR/VR headsets and smartphones. A community‐driven plugin ecosystem has already yielded novel applications in assistive technology, behavioral research, and interactive gaming. Conclusion: By offering a low‐cost, extensible, and transparent platform, Pupil lowers barriers to eye‐tracking research and enables new mobile and pervasive applications. Its open‐source nature fosters collaboration, rapid prototyping, and educational use, positioning Pupil as a foundational tool for the next generation of gaze‐based human–computer interaction. Keywords: Eye tracking, Open source, Gaze interaction, Human–computer interaction, Mobile computing, Pupil.

The growing complexity of machine learning (ML) models has heightened the need for interpretability and explainability in decision-making processes. This paper provides a comprehensive mini-tour of interpretability and explainability techniques across a diverse range of ML models, referred to as the "Machine Learning Zoo." The objective is to systematically categorize and evaluate methods that enhance the transparency of ML systems, enabling users to understand and trust their outputs. We explore approaches such as feature importance analysis, rule-based explanations, and visualization techniques, tailored to specific model types including decision trees, neural networks, and ensemble methods. Our findings highlight the trade-offs between model complexity and interpretability, demonstrating that simpler models often provide more intuitive explanations, while advanced techniques like SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) offer robust solutions for complex models. The study concludes with practical insights into selecting appropriate interpretability tools based on application requirements, emphasizing the importance of balancing accuracy and transparency. This work contributes to the ongoing discourse on responsible AI by providing a structured overview of interpretability methods, aiding researchers and practitioners in building more trustworthy ML systems. **Keywords**: interpretability, explainability, machine learning, SHAP, LIME, transparency, responsible AI.

This paper explores the vulnerability of Google reCAPTCHA v3 to reinforcement learning (RL) based attacks. The objective is to demonstrate the feasibility of bypassing reCAPTCHA v3's bot detection mechanisms using an intelligent agent. We employ a deep Q-network (DQN) agent to learn an optimal interaction strategy with websites protected by reCAPTCHA v3. The agent is trained to mimic human-like browsing behavior, adjusting parameters such as mouse movements, click patterns, and navigation paths. Experimental results show that the DQN agent can achieve a high success rate in obtaining valid scores from reCAPTCHA v3, effectively bypassing the security system. This research highlights a critical weakness in reCAPTCHA v3, suggesting that current scoring algorithms are susceptible to sophisticated RL-based attacks. The findings emphasize the need for improved bot detection techniques that are resilient to adaptive adversarial strategies. Keywords: reCAPTCHA v3, Reinforcement Learning, Bot Detection, DQN, Security, Artificial Intelligence.

This paper addresses the challenge of small sample learning in the big data era, where traditional machine learning methods often struggle with limited training data. Our objective is to develop an effective approach to learn from small samples while leveraging the abundance of big data. We propose a novel framework that combines transfer learning and meta-learning to adapt pre-trained models to small sample tasks. Our method utilizes a few-shot learning paradigm, enabling the model to learn from a minimal number of examples. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our approach over state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency. The key findings of this research highlight the potential of small sample learning in big data applications, such as image classification, natural language processing, and recommender systems. Our contributions include a new perspective on small sample learning, a scalable and efficient algorithm, and empirical evidence of its effectiveness. This study has important implications for real-world applications where data is scarce or expensive to collect, and paves the way for further research in few-shot learning, meta-learning, and big data analytics, with relevant keywords including small sample learning, few-shot learning, transfer learning, meta-learning, and big data.

This study introduces CI-Net, a novel neural network architecture designed to simultaneously perform semantic segmentation and depth estimation by leveraging contextual information. The research aims to address the challenges of integrating these two tasks, which traditionally require separate models, to improve performance and efficiency in computer vision applications. Methods/Approach: CI-Net employs a dual-branch architecture that processes shared image features and extracts task-specific information. The model integrates a contextual information module to enhance the feature representations by capturing global and local context, facilitating improved task collaboration and accuracy. Advanced deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and attention mechanisms, are utilized to dynamically adapt to the diverse demands of both tasks. Results/Findings: The proposed CI-Net demonstrates superior performance over existing single-task models and conventional multi-task approaches, as evidenced by comprehensive evaluations on standard benchmark datasets. Notably, CI-Net achieves higher accuracy in semantic segmentation and more precise depth estimation, showcasing its ability to improve over competitive baselines. The model shows robustness across various scenarios, indicating its potential for real-world applications. Conclusion/Implications: CI-Net makes significant strides in joint task learning by effectively utilizing contextual information to enhance both semantic segmentation and depth estimation. This dual-task approach can lead to more efficient resource utilization and streamlined deployment in environments such as autonomous driving, augmented reality, and robotics. The research contributes to advancing multi-task learning frameworks and sets the stage for future explorations in integrating complex visual perception tasks within a unified framework. Keywords: CI-Net, semantic segmentation, depth estimation, contextual information, multi-task learning, computer vision, convolutional neural networks, attention mechanisms.

The rapid growth of large-scale brain imaging datasets presents significant challenges in analyzing and interpreting complex brain network data. This paper introduces an auto-encoding framework designed to efficiently model and analyze brain networks, enabling the extraction of meaningful patterns from high-dimensional neuroimaging data. Our approach leverages a deep learning-based auto-encoder architecture to encode brain network structures into low-dimensional latent representations, which are then decoded to reconstruct the original networks. This framework not only reduces computational complexity but also preserves critical topological features of brain connectivity. We evaluate the proposed method on multiple large-scale brain imaging datasets, demonstrating its ability to outperform traditional dimensionality reduction techniques in terms of reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, the latent representations generated by our model provide valuable insights into brain network organization, facilitating applications such as disease classification, biomarker discovery, and functional connectivity analysis. The results highlight the potential of auto-encoding brain networks as a powerful tool for advancing neuroimaging research and addressing the challenges posed by ever-growing datasets. **Keywords**: brain networks, auto-encoder, neuroimaging, deep learning, dimensionality reduction, functional connectivity.

Bài viết tập trung vào phương pháp đánh giá và quy trình xác định rủi ro thiên tai nước dâng do bão tại khu vực ven biển. Nghiên cứu sử dụng các mô hình toán học và dữ liệu lịch sử để dự báo mực nước dâng cao do bão, từ đó xác định các khu vực có nguy cơ ngập lụt cao. Các yếu tố như địa hình, độ cao, hệ thống đê điều và cơ sở hạ tầng ven biển được xem xét để đánh giá mức độ tổn thương. Quy trình bao gồm phân tích đặc điểm bão, xây dựng bản đồ ngập lụt, đánh giá thiệt hại tiềm tàng về kinh tế và xã hội. Kết quả đánh giá rủi ro là cơ sở quan trọng để xây dựng các kế hoạch phòng chống thiên tai, giảm thiểu tác động của nước dâng do bão đối với cộng đồng và môi trường ven biển, đồng thời đề xuất các giải pháp thích ứng và ứng phó hiệu quả, góp phần vào sự phát triển bền vững của khu vực.
